CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** James Miller, Donna Chant, Alistair K. Scott (Deputy Chief of the R.C.A.F. Ground Observer Corps)

**Date / Time:** October 8, 1967, between 10:00 p.m. and 11:00 p.m. (Additional reports of activity in the New Waterford area noted between October 13th and 14th, 1967).

**Location:** Glace Bay and New Waterford, Nova Scotia (specifically a parking area at the bottom of Blackett Street near the shoreline).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 8, 1967, James Miller and his girlfriend, Donna Chant, drove to a parking area near the shore at the bottom of Blackett Street in Glace Bay. While there, they observed a large, unidentified object hovering over the water. The witnesses reported that the object moved in an up-and-down motion near the shoreline. Mr. Miller became alarmed by the encounter and drove away from the scene. He later attempted to return to the location with his father, but his father declined to accompany him, choosing to watch a television program instead. A subsequent daylight visit to the area by Mr. Miller yielded no further sightings. Separately, reports surfaced via Radio Station C.H.E.R. Sydney regarding a UFO sighting in the New Waterford area between October 13th and 14th, 1967.

**Object:** The object was described as a large craft emitting a distinct blue glow, with some reports noting a blue or green hue. It featured a bright light on its top portion. The object’s movement was characterized by hovering and vertical oscillation over the water. Observers speculated that the object appeared to be interested in the local power infrastructure, specifically a nearby power sub-station carrying 6,600 volts.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Alistair K. Scott, Deputy Chief of the R.C.A.F. Ground Observer Corps, conducted a formal interview with James Miller on October 14, 1967. During the interview, Mr. Miller appeared visibly shaken. Mr. Scott inspected the Blackett Street site and noted the presence of a power sub-station equipped with mercury vapour lamps; however, Mr. Miller insisted that the object he witnessed was distinct from the sub-station lighting. Mr. Scott also surveyed the area using glasses (binoculars), noting that the shoreline provided a natural hiding place that could only be observed from the seaward side. The investigation included the use of a local map marking the sighting area, a D.N.D. (Army) map, and a reference to Chart 4367. The final report was received by the Maritime Command Commander on October 17, 1967.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯·米勒 (James Miller)、唐娜·钱特 (Donna Chant)、阿利斯泰尔·K·斯科特 (Alistair K. Scott，加拿大皇家空军地面观察团副团长)

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月8日，晚上10:00至11:00之间。（另有报告指出1967年10月13日至14日期间，新沃特福德地区也有相关活动。）

**地点：** 新斯科舍省格莱斯湾 (Glace Bay) 和新沃特福德 (New Waterford)（具体地点为布莱克特街 (Blackett Street) 尽头靠近海岸线的停车场）。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月8日晚，詹姆斯·米勒和他的女友唐娜·钱特开车前往格莱斯湾布莱克特街尽头靠近海岸的一个停车场。在那里，他们观察到一个巨大的不明物体悬浮在水面上。目击者称，该物体在海岸线附近做上下移动。米勒先生对此次遭遇感到惊恐，随即驾车离开现场。他后来试图带着父亲重返该地点，但他的父亲拒绝同行，选择留在家里看电视。米勒先生随后在白天再次前往该区域，但没有发现更多迹象。此外，悉尼市 C.H.E.R. 广播电台也收到了关于1967年10月13日至14日期间在新沃特福德地区出现UFO目击事件的报告。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一艘发出独特蓝色光芒的大型飞行器，也有报告称其带有蓝色或绿色色调。其顶部有一个明亮的灯光。该物体的运动特征是在水面上悬浮并进行垂直振荡。观察者推测，该物体似乎对当地的电力基础设施感兴趣，特别是附近一个承载6600伏电压的变电站。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家空军地面观察团副团长阿利斯泰尔·K·斯科特于1967年10月14日对詹姆斯·米勒进行了正式访谈。访谈期间，米勒先生显得明显惊魂未定。斯科特先生视察了布莱克特街现场，并注意到那里有一个配备汞蒸气灯的变电站；然而，米勒先生坚称他目击到的物体与变电站的灯光截然不同。斯科特先生还使用双筒望远镜对该区域进行了勘察，指出海岸线提供了一个天然的隐蔽处，只有从海面一侧才能观察到。调查工作包括使用标有目击区域的当地地图、国防部（陆军）地图以及参考4367号海图。最终报告于1967年10月17日呈交至海事司令部指挥官。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. John Cobel

**Date / Time:** October 9, 1967, between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM EST

**Location:** Near the Ricks farm, Curtis, Ontario (approximately three miles southeast of Oshawa)

**Sighting:**
On the morning of October 9, 1967, Mr. John Cobel observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the southeast sky. He reported that the object was initially positioned at an altitude of approximately 4,000 to 5,000 feet. As the object descended toward the ground, it appeared to increase in size. The sighting occurred under weather conditions characterized as cloudy with light fog in some areas. The object eventually disappeared from view.

**Object:**
The physical description of the object varies slightly between the narrative report and the supplementary questionnaire data, suggesting a complex or multi-part appearance. Mr. Cobel described the object as disk-shaped, noting that it made no sound during the observation. Its color shifted from red to a bright orange. 

Supplementary documentation (National Research Council of Canada file RG 77, Vol. 306) provides additional visual details: a sketch depicts three dark, oval-shaped objects stacked vertically. These components were labeled as emitting a "white light" and were described as being "orange in color, fading to red." The observer explicitly noted that the object did not possess a tail flame.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The documentation includes a formal questionnaire processed by the National Research Council of Canada (Conseil national de recherches du Canada). The file is cataloged under "RG 77, Vol. 306." The investigation materials consist of a narrative account provided by Mr. John Cobel, a handwritten questionnaire detailing environmental conditions and physical characteristics, and a sketch of the object’s configuration. No final explanation or official conclusion regarding the nature of the object is provided in the available records.

**目击者：** 约翰·科贝尔 (John Cobel) 先生

1967年10月9日上午，约翰·科贝尔先生在东南方天空中观察到一种不明空中现象。据他报告，该物体最初位于约4,000至5,000英尺的高度。随着物体向地面下降，其体积似乎有所增大。目击发生时的天气状况为多云，部分地区有轻雾。该物体最终消失在视野中。

关于该物体的物理描述在叙述报告和补充调查问卷数据之间略有出入，这表明其外观可能较为复杂或由多个部分组成。科贝尔先生将其描述为圆盘状，并指出在观察过程中该物体没有发出任何声音。其颜色从红色转变为明亮的橙色。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** J. Hallen (also referred to as J. Kallen), Mrs. J. Kallen, and their son.

**Date / Time:** October 8, 1967 (referenced as Oct 9 in some internal notes), between 1140Z and 1230Z.

**Location:** The witnesses' residence in Richmond, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On the night of October 8, 1967, the Kallen (Hallen) family observed three stationary objects from their home in Richmond, B.C. The weather conditions at the time were noted as cloudy in the north-east, while the south-east sky remained clear. The witnesses observed two objects positioned in the east and one object in the south-east. The two objects in the east were situated at approximately 45 degrees and 60 degrees above the horizon, respectively. The observer noted that the object at the 45-degree elevation appeared to be the closest to their position. The sighting lasted for nearly an hour, concluding around 1230Z.

**Object:** The three objects were described as lights that fluctuated in intensity, cycling from bright to zero. At the beginning of the observation period, the intensity varied every 3 to 4 minutes; by the end of the sighting, this frequency had slowed to 10-minute intervals. When the objects were at their largest and brightest, they emitted a silvery-white light. As they diminished in size and intensity, the color shifted to a yellowish hue. When the intensity was at its minimum, the objects appeared cylindrical in shape, resembling a long, bright star. While J. Hallen (Kallen) initially identified the objects as planets, the detailed report of their fluctuating intensity and specific geometric appearance was significant enough to warrant formal military intelligence review.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented as part of the CFOC (Canadian Forces Operational Command) UFO report. The report was initially processed by the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) in Vancouver and subsequently transmitted to CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters). Due to the nature of the report, CANFORCEHED requested that prints be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for photo intelligence analysis to determine the nature of the objects. The case remains filed under the Richmond, B.C. UFO reports for October 1967.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** J. 哈伦（J. Hallen，也被称为 J. 卡伦/J. Kallen）、J. 卡伦夫人以及他们的儿子。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月8日（部分内部记录中记为10月9日），格林威治标准时间（Z）11:40至12:30之间。

**地点：** 目击者位于不列颠哥伦比亚省列治文市的住所。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月8日晚，卡伦（哈伦）一家在他们位于不列颠哥伦比亚省列治文市的家中观察到了三个静止的物体。当时的天气状况显示，东北方向多云，而东南方向的天空则保持晴朗。目击者观察到两个物体位于东方，一个物体位于东南方。东方的那两个物体分别位于地平线上方约45度和60度处。观察者指出，位于45度仰角的物体看起来距离他们的位置最近。此次目击持续了近一个小时，于格林威治标准时间12:30左右结束。

**物体描述：** 这三个物体被描述为亮度会波动的光点，在明亮与熄灭之间循环。在观察初期，亮度变化的频率为每3到4分钟一次；到目击结束时，这一频率减慢至每10分钟一次。当物体处于最大、最亮的状态时，它们发出银白色的光；随着体积和亮度减小，颜色转变为黄色。当亮度降至最低时，物体呈现出圆柱形，看起来像一颗明亮的长星。尽管 J. 哈伦（卡伦）最初认为这些物体是行星，但关于其亮度波动和特定几何外观的详细报告引起了足够的重视，足以进行正式的军事情报审查。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件被正式记录在加拿大武装部队作战司令部（CFOC）的不明飞行物报告中。该报告最初由温哥华救援协调中心（RCC）处理，随后被转交给加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）。由于报告的性质，加拿大武装部队总部要求将照片副本转发给相关部门进行照片情报分析，以确定物体的性质。该案例目前仍归档在1967年10月列治文市的不明飞行物报告中。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:

**Aftermath:** The object disappeared between Texada Island and Comox, BC.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Russel (Russ) Hill (Department of Lands and Forest lookoutman), Bob Miller (Junction Lookout), Mr. Warren Smith, Mr. Grovue, a ranger’s son, and two unnamed gold prospectors.

**Date / Time:** July 3, 1967 (1700 hours); September 7, 1967; September 18, 1967 (0100 hours); October 7, 1967 (1945 hours); October 10, 1967 (1835 hours).

**Location:** Highwood/Nanton/Calgary, Alberta, specifically Raspberry Ridge Lookout, Junction Lookout, North Mist Mountain, Lost Creek, and areas 30 miles west of Nanton near the Highwood Ranger Station.

**Sighting:** The events involve multiple sightings over several months. On July 3, 1967, Warren Smith observed a circular object 30 miles west of Nanton. It banked, descended from 2,000–2,500 feet above him, and sped south behind trees. On September 18, Russ Hill reported a reddish object with a green light that hovered for three hours, causing power plant interference and a "queer sensation" from a pulsating sound, before ascending straight up; he believed it landed on a mountain plateau. A ranger’s son reportedly saw a similar object the previous year. On October 7, Hill observed an object at Raspberry Ridge, while Bob Miller at Junction Lookout reported lights and noise. On October 10, Hill observed a bright white glow moving west to east. Mr. Grovue was later involved in a search for debris, during which he became lost and recovered materials.

**Object:** Descriptions vary by encounter. The July 3 object was a shiny, aluminum, circular craft (25–50 feet in diameter, 11–14 feet deep). Photographic analysis suggested a torus (donut) or oblate ellipsoid shape with a 4:1 diameter-to-depth ratio. The September 18 object was large, reddish, and pitted like sandblasted automobile undercoating, featuring a green light and a pulsating, throbbing sound. The October 7 object was 75–80 feet across, resembling two bowls inverted (clam-shell style), with two light-colored exhaust flames, a green neon rim, and a rotating/pulsating yellow-green light on a top dome.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Warren Smith provided two photographs taken with an Olympus PEN EE camera. The Defence Photographic Interpretation Centre (Major K.J. Hope) could neither prove nor disprove the photos as fakes, noting they could be a 2-foot object at close range or a 40-foot object at altitude. The Department of National Defence (S/L E.B. Chase, S/L Morrison) requested the photos be sent to the University of Colorado for study. RCMP and forestry officials struggled to retrieve reports from the isolated Raspberry Ridge tower due to firefighting duties and lack of transport. Materials recovered by Mr. Grovue were analyzed by two labs; some were identified as aluminum, while others remained unidentified. Russ Hill expressed a desire to quit due to the stress of the sightings. No radar reports were confirmed.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 拉塞尔（拉斯）·希尔先生（Russel (Russ) Hill，土地与森林部瞭望员）、鲍勃·米勒（Bob Miller，枢纽瞭望台）、沃伦·史密斯先生（Warren Smith）、格罗夫先生（Mr. Grovue）、一名护林员的儿子，以及两名未具名的黄金勘探者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年7月3日（17:00）；1967年9月7日；1967年9月18日（01:00）；1967年10月7日（19:45）；1967年10月10日（18:35）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省海伍德（Highwood）/南顿（Nanton）/卡尔加里（Calgary），具体包括覆盆子岭瞭望台（Raspberry Ridge Lookout）、枢纽瞭望台（Junction Lookout）、北雾山（North Mist Mountain）、迷失溪（Lost Creek），以及南顿以西30英里靠近海伍德护林站的区域。

**目击经过：** 这些事件涉及数月内的多次目击。1967年7月3日，沃伦·史密斯在南顿以西30英里处观察到一个圆形物体。它在空中倾斜，从他上方2000至2500英尺处下降，随后加速向南飞入树林后方。9月18日，拉斯·希尔报告称看到一个带有绿光的红色物体，它悬停了三个小时，导致发电厂受到干扰，并因一种脉动声产生“怪异的感觉”，随后垂直升空；他认为该物体降落在了山顶高原上。据报道，一名护林员的儿子在前一年也见过类似的物体。10月7日，希尔在覆盆子岭观察到一个物体，而枢纽瞭望台的鲍勃·米勒报告了灯光和噪音。10月10日，希尔观察到一个从西向东移动的明亮白光。格罗夫先生后来参与了残骸搜寻工作，期间他一度迷路，并回收了一些材料。

**物体描述：** 描述因遭遇情况而异。7月3日的物体是一个闪亮的铝制圆形飞行器（直径25至50英尺，深11至14英尺）。照片分析显示其形状为圆环状（甜甜圈形）或扁椭球体，直径与深度的比例为4:1。9月18日的物体体积巨大，呈红色，表面有类似喷砂汽车底漆的凹坑，带有绿光，并发出脉动、跳动的声音。10月7日的物体直径为75至80英尺，类似于两个倒扣的碗（蛤壳式），带有两道浅色排气火焰、一个绿色霓虹边缘，以及顶部圆顶上旋转/脉动的黄绿色灯光。

**调查/后续：** 沃伦·史密斯提供了两张用奥林巴斯PEN EE相机拍摄的照片。国防摄影判读中心（K.J.霍普少校）无法证实或证伪这些照片的真伪，指出它们可能是近距离拍摄的2英尺物体，也可能是高空拍摄的40英尺物体。国防部（E.B.蔡斯中队长、莫里森中队长）要求将照片送往科罗拉多大学进行研究。由于消防任务和交通不便，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）和林业官员难以从偏远的覆盆子岭瞭望塔获取报告。格罗夫先生回收的材料经两家实验室分析；部分被鉴定为铝，其余则无法识别。拉斯·希尔因目击事件带来的压力表示想要辞职。未确认有雷达报告记录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The captain of a longliner (fishing vessel).

**Date / Time:** October 12, 1964; times reported vary between 2030 hours GMT and 2330 hours GMT.

**Location:** Gulf of Maine and Georges Banks area, approximately 30 miles South-Southwest (SSW) of the RCAF Station at Barrington, Nova Scotia (Position 1250 1075 SSW).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 12, 1964, the captain of a longliner was at the helm of his vessel returning from a fishing trip when he observed an unidentified object. The sky was clear at the time of the sighting. The witness reported that the object traveled in a straight line at a high rate of speed toward the southwest. The duration of the observation was estimated at 5 to 7 seconds. The witness noted that there was no sound associated with the object and no luminosity other than the flame at its rear. The position of the vessel was determined using a Loran set on board and correlated with chart C&GS 71 (Gulf of Maine and Georges Banks).

**Object:** The object was described as torpedo-shaped and black in color. It measured approximately 5 to 7 feet in length with a circumference of 8 to 10 inches. It maintained a steady altitude of approximately 150 feet above sea level. A distinct "purplish flame" was observed ejecting from the back end of the object, which the witness described as having a rocket-like thrust.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was subject to a formal investigation by the RCAF and the RCMP. F/L E.A. Rutherford conducted an interrogation of the captain on November 4, 1964, to verify the vessel's position and the details of the sighting. Additionally, an interrogation report was signed by Cpl. Parent of the AFP. F/L Collier of RCAF Station Barrington submitted the report to Air Defence Command (ADC) headquarters. Official documentation notes that the processing of the report was delayed because the information was initially received as casual civilian input and further hindered by the captain’s extended time at sea. Headquarters investigated the possibility that the sighting correlated with maritime trials or military exercises, though no impact was reported.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一艘延绳钓渔船的船长。

**日期 / 时间：** 1964年10月12日；报告时间在格林威治标准时间2030时至2330时之间不等。

**地点：** 缅因湾（Gulf of Maine）及乔治浅滩（Georges Banks）区域，位于新斯科舍省巴林顿（Barrington）加拿大皇家空军（RCAF）基地南-西南方向约30英里处（坐标位置 1250 1075 SSW）。

**目击经过：** 1964年10月12日晚，该延绳钓渔船船长在结束捕鱼作业返航途中掌舵时，观察到一个不明物体。目击时天空晴朗。据目击者报告，该物体以极高的速度沿直线向西南方向飞行。观测持续时间估计为5至7秒。目击者指出，该物体飞行时没有发出任何声音，除了尾部喷出的火焰外，没有其他光亮。船只的位置是通过船上的罗兰（Loran）导航仪测定的，并与C&GS 71号海图（缅因湾及乔治浅滩）进行了比对。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为鱼雷形状，呈黑色。长度约为5至7英尺，周长为8至10英寸。它保持在海平面上方约150英尺的稳定高度飞行。观察到该物体后端喷射出明显的“紫色火焰”，目击者形容其具有类似火箭的推力。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家空军（RCAF）和加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）进行了正式调查。1964年11月4日，E.A. 卢瑟福（E.A. Rutherford）空军上尉对船长进行了问询，以核实船只位置及目击细节。此外，加拿大联邦警察（AFP）的帕朗（Parent）下士签署了一份问询报告。巴林顿加拿大皇家空军基地的科利尔（Collier）空军上尉将报告提交给了防空司令部（ADC）总部。官方文件指出，该报告的处理过程有所延误，原因是信息最初被视为平民的随意反馈，且船长长期在海上作业也造成了进一步阻碍。总部调查了此次目击事件与海上试验或军事演习相关的可能性，但未收到任何撞击报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ron Morris (OPP), Crandle Childerhouse, Milton Pergeson, Roy Bavlis, and Roy Alyard.

**Date / Time:** October 13, 1967; 0045Z to 0055Z.

**Location:** Whitefish, Ontario (16 miles west of Sudbury).

**Sighting:** On October 13, 1967, a UFO sighting occurred in the vicinity of Whitefish and the northern Sudbury area. The event began at approximately 0045Z and lasted for a duration of five minutes. Witnesses Ron Morris (an OPP officer), Crandle Childerhouse, Milton Pergeson, Roy Bavlis, and Roy Alyard observed the object at a low altitude. While the object was considered too distant for fine-detail observation, it was noted for its ability to change direction with extreme speed. The witnesses reported the object moving away from their position during the observation period.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape, with estimated dimensions of two car lengths across and one car length in height. It appeared as bright as a standard house light and was self-luminous, though it did not illuminate the surrounding terrain. The object displayed a combination of green, red, and white lights. Regarding acoustics, the object emitted a sound similar to a bumblebee when at a distance, which transitioned into a loud, distinct whining sound as it drew closer to the observers.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation documented the event under the case title "Sudbury/Whitefish ON sightings Oct 1967." Official records note the weather conditions at the time of the sighting as cloudy, with high clouds present in the night sky. The file includes the names and addresses of the five primary witnesses involved in the Sudbury area. No further specific investigative findings or sketches were detailed in the provided documentation, other than the collection of witness identities and the recording of the atmospheric conditions.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗恩·莫里斯（Ron Morris，安大略省警察局警官）、克兰德尔·奇尔德豪斯（Crandle Childerhouse）、米尔顿·珀格森（Milton Pergeson）、罗伊·巴夫利斯（Roy Bavlis）以及罗伊·阿利亚德（Roy Alyard）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月13日；0045Z至0055Z。

**地点：** 安大略省怀特菲什（萨德伯里以西16英里处）。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月13日，怀特菲什及萨德伯里北部地区发生了一起不明飞行物（UFO）目击事件。事件始于格林威治标准时间（Z）0045左右，持续了五分钟。目击者罗恩·莫里斯（安大略省警察局警官）、克兰德尔·奇尔德豪斯、米尔顿·珀格森、罗伊·巴夫利斯和罗伊·阿利亚德观察到了该低空飞行的物体。尽管由于距离较远无法观察到精细细节，但该物体能够以极快的速度改变方向，这一点引起了目击者的注意。据目击者报告，在观察期间，该物体正远离他们的位置。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，估计尺寸为两辆汽车的长度宽，一辆汽车的长度高。它看起来像普通家用灯泡一样明亮，且自身发光，但并未照亮周围的地形。该物体显示出绿色、红色和白色交替的灯光。在声音方面，物体在远处时发出类似大黄蜂的嗡嗡声，当它靠近观察者时，声音转变为一种响亮且清晰的尖啸声。

**调查/后续：** 该调查将此事件记录在案，标题为“1967年10月萨德伯里/怀特菲什安大略省目击事件”。官方记录指出，目击时的天气状况为多云，夜空中存在高空云层。档案中包含了萨德伯里地区五名主要目击者的姓名和地址。除收集了目击者身份信息并记录了大气状况外，提供的文档中未详细说明进一步的具体调查结果或草图。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. W. Tibbs

**Date / Time:** October 13, 1967, at 11:30Z

**Location:** Highway 2A, south of Calgary, at the Sheep Creek Bridge, Alberta

**Sighting:**
On October 13, 1967, at 11:30Z, Mrs. W. Tibbs of High River, Alberta, was driving on Highway 2A when she encountered an unidentified aerial phenomenon at the Sheep Creek Bridge. According to her account, she observed an object descending from the sky directly toward the front of her vehicle. 

The encounter involved significant electromagnetic interference: as the object approached, Mrs. Tibbs reported that her car radio ceased functioning, her headlights extinguished, and her vehicle came to a complete, involuntary stop. During the period the object was in proximity, she noted a distinct physical sensation of feeling "extremely cold." She also reported hearing a slight whining sound. 

As the object departed, it appeared to tilt on one side before accelerating away at "tremendous speed." Immediately following the object's departure, the vehicle's electrical systems—the radio and headlights—resumed normal operation, and the car engine started again.

**Object:**
The object was described as oval-shaped and estimated to be between 20 and 30 feet in length. It hovered at an altitude of approximately 300 to 500 feet. Visually, the object was characterized by a large, extremely bright white light located at the tail, which reflected off the object's underside. Mrs. Tibbs specifically described the illumination as "the whitest white I have ever seen," noting that the light was intense yet produced no glare.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The documentation consists of typed NRC (National Research Council) file summaries. Official notes indicate that the location of this sighting was approximately 45 miles northeast of other reported sightings in the region. The records include the witness's personal account of the mechanical and electrical failures experienced during the event, as well as the specific physical characteristics of the object observed at the Sheep Creek Bridge. No further investigative actions or meteorological data were explicitly detailed in these specific pages.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** W. 蒂布斯夫人 (Mrs. W. Tibbs)

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月13日，11:30Z

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省卡尔加里以南，2A号公路，希普溪大桥 (Sheep Creek Bridge)

**目击经过：**
1967年10月13日11:30Z，居住在阿尔伯塔省海河镇 (High River) 的 W. 蒂布斯夫人在驾车行驶于2A号公路时，在希普溪大桥附近遭遇了不明空中现象。据她描述，她观察到一个物体从天而降，径直朝她的车头方向飞来。

此次遭遇伴随着明显的电磁干扰：当物体靠近时，蒂布斯夫人称她的车载收音机停止工作，车前灯熄灭，车辆也不受控制地完全停了下来。在物体靠近期间，她感到一种明显的身体不适，即“极度寒冷”。她还报告听到了一种轻微的嗡嗡声。

当物体离开时，它似乎向一侧倾斜，随后以“极快的速度”加速离去。在物体离开后，车辆的电气系统（收音机和前灯）立即恢复正常，引擎也重新启动了。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为椭圆形，估计长度在20至30英尺之间。它悬停在约300至500英尺的高度。从视觉上看，该物体的特征是尾部有一个巨大的、极其明亮的白光，光线反射在物体的底部。蒂布斯夫人特别形容这种光为“我所见过最纯净的白色”，并指出这种光虽然强烈，却并不刺眼。

**调查/后续：**
相关档案由加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 的打印文件摘要组成。官方记录显示，此次目击地点距离该地区其他已报告的目击事件地点约45英里。记录中包含了目击者关于事件期间车辆机械和电气故障的个人陈述，以及在希普溪大桥观察到的物体具体物理特征。在这些特定页面中，未详细说明进一步的调查行动或气象数据。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian reported the sighting to the unit.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on October 16 at dawn. The object appeared from behind a bush, climbing at a forty-five degree angle and flying east. The duration of the sighting was approximately 2 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as very bright, shaped like a curling stone, with the front half appearing aluminum and the back half engulfed in flame and smoke, leaving a 600-foot trail. No bursts were observed and no sound was heard.

**Aftermath:** The sighting was reported to the unit on November 17, 1967. The document is marked for the Meteor Centre NRC.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名平民向该单位报告了此次目击事件。

**目击：** 事件发生在10月16日黎明时分。物体从灌木丛后出现，以45度角爬升并向东飞行。目击持续时间约为2分钟。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为非常明亮，形状像冰壶，前半部分呈铝色，后半部分被火焰和烟雾吞没，留下了600英尺长的尾迹。未观察到爆炸，也未听到任何声音。

**后续：** 该目击事件于1967年11月17日报告给该单位。文件上标注了“Meteor Centre NRC”（加拿大国家研究委员会流星中心）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 史密斯夫人（居住于西第43大道145号）及其8岁的女儿。

**日期：** 1967年10月16日，1930Z（祖鲁时间）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian male who reported the incident to the RCMP office.

**Sighting:** On October 16, 1967, at approximately 10:50 PM, the witness was driving south on Highway 37 near the Swift Current Creek Bridge. He observed two lights through the upper right corner of his windshield. The lights appeared similar to car headlights, though one was slightly lower and smaller than the other. The witness reported no noise. The lights appeared to follow him up a hill, maintaining their position until he reached the top. At the top of the hill, the lights turned west and passed over some graineries.

**Object:** Two lights, similar to car headlights, with no further description provided by the witness.

**Aftermath:** The witness reported the incident to the RCMP at approximately 11:10 PM, appearing nervous and scared. Cpl. Crawford and the reporting officer visited the Swift Current Bridge but found nothing. The RCMP concluded that while the witness appeared sincere, no explanation for the sighting could be provided at the time.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）办公室报告此事的男性平民。

**日期：** 1967年10月16日

**地点：** 斯威夫特卡伦特溪（Swift Current Creek）大桥附近的37号高速公路。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月16日晚上约10点50分，目击者正驾车沿37号高速公路向南行驶，途经斯威夫特卡伦特溪大桥附近。他透过挡风玻璃的右上角观察到两道光束。这些光看起来类似于汽车前灯，尽管其中一道光比另一道略低、略小。目击者称现场没有任何声音。这两道光似乎跟随着他上坡，并保持着相对位置，直到他到达坡顶。在坡顶处，这两道光转向西面，并从一些粮仓上方掠过。

**物体描述：** 两道类似于汽车前灯的光束，目击者未提供进一步描述。

**调查/后续：** 目击者于晚上约11点10分向加拿大皇家骑警报告了此事，当时他表现得十分紧张和恐惧。克劳福德下士（Cpl. Crawford）与负责报告的警官前往斯威夫特卡伦特大桥进行了实地查看，但未发现任何异常。加拿大皇家骑警得出的结论是，尽管目击者表现得非常真诚，但当时无法对此次目击事件给出任何解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The pilot, Lt. Gallagher of the RCN, and the crew of an RCN Tracker aircraft.

**Sighting:** On October 17, 1967, while on exercise, the aircraft was positioned 100 nautical miles at 170 degrees magnetic from Shearwater. The crew observed 3 or 4 objects that appeared to be burning. The objects were visible for about two minutes at an elevation of approximately 30 degrees above the horizon.

**Object:** 3 or 4 objects described as appearing to be burning.

**Aftermath:** This is an interim report. The pilot is expected to submit a complete report upon returning to base, which will be forwarded as soon as possible. A handwritten note on the document states, "Strange! Will see what the crew reports."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 飞行员加拉格尔中尉（Lt. Gallagher，加拿大皇家海军）及一架加拿大皇家海军“追踪者”（Tracker）飞机的机组人员。

**日期：** 1967年10月17日。

**地点：** 位于希尔沃特（Shearwater）磁方位170度、距离100海里处。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月17日，该飞机在执行演习任务时，机组人员观察到3到4个看起来正在燃烧的物体。这些物体在地平线上方约30度的高度持续可见约两分钟。

**物体描述：** 3到4个被描述为看起来正在燃烧的物体。

**调查/后续：** 此为中期报告。预计飞行员在返回基地后将提交一份完整报告，该报告将尽快转交。文件上的一份手写笔记写道：“奇怪！看看机组人员会报告些什么。”

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:

**Sighting:** On October 17, 1967, at 170215 local time, an object was observed in cloudy conditions.

**Object:** The object was described as round, very bright, and red in color. It was observed flashing on and off for a duration of 2 or 3 minutes. No sound was observed, and the object was moving from east to west.

**Aftermath:** A handwritten note on the document indicates "No further action reqd. - our normal 'thanks' letter" dated 18 Oct.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 辛格先生（Mr. Singer），居住于蒙特利尔26区普拉蒙登街（Plamondon Street）4860号。

**调查/后续：** 文件上的一份手写备注显示“无需进一步行动——已寄出常规‘感谢’信”，日期为10月18日。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Russ Hill of the Raspberry Ridge Look-out Station.

**Sighting:** On the evening of 17 October 1967 at approximately 2100 hours local time, Mr. Hill was listening to his transistor radio when normal transmissions were interrupted by a Morse-type transmission. He reported hearing this on both his transistor and Forestry radio.

**Object:** The page describes an unusual radio transmission consisting of a series of repeated syllables including "ZEE GEE HEE FEE", "FEE AEE NEE NE", "LEE OEE ZEE CEE", "DEE MEE TREE SEE", and "OEEE XODEE".

**Aftermath:** Two other stations, Kananaskis and Moose Mountain, reported they had not heard this specific transmission but had periodically heard an unexplained carrier-type transmission.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 覆盆子岭（Raspberry Ridge）瞭望台的 Russ Hill 先生。

**目击：** 1967年10月17日晚约21:00（当地时间），Hill 先生在收听收音机时，正常的广播被一种莫尔斯电码式的传输中断。他表示在晶体管收音机和林业无线电上都听到了该传输。

**物体：** 页面描述了一段异常的无线电传输，包含一系列重复的音节，如“ZEE GEE HEE FEE”、“FEE AEE NEE NE”、“LEE OEE ZEE CEE”、“DEE MEE TREE SEE”以及“OEEE XODEE”。

**后续：** 卡纳纳斯基斯（Kananaskis）和驼鹿山（Moose Mountain）的另外两个站点报告称，他们没有听到这次特定的传输，但曾周期性地听到过无法解释的载波信号。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. R. Hill (also referred to as Russ Hill, Lands and Forest Lookout Man), Mr. OB Matson, Observer Brian Carnell.

**Date / Time:** October 18, 1967; various times recorded in Zulu (Z) between 0146Z and 2346Z.

**Location:** Raspberry Ridge (114° 38' W, 50° 18' N), Highwood Ranger Station, Mt. Fox, and the Crowsnest area, Alberta.

**Sighting:** 
The events of October 18, 1967, involved multiple observations across the Kananaskis region. 

At 0146Z, Mr. OB Matson observed two lights approximately 2.5 miles away on a bearing of 193° true. The lights were initially 100 yards apart, closed to 50 yards, and then separated, moving toward the east or southeast face of Mt. Fox. The sighting lasted approximately 2 minutes. At 0152Z, Mr. Matson observed a single light moving rapidly north from a bearing of 214° to 240°.

At 0151Z, Observer Brian Carnell, stationed at the Highwood Ranger Station (114° 38' W, 50° 24' N), reported a bright white flash. The object was observed approximately 0.5 miles from the witness, appearing below the treetops, and was last seen at a distance of just over 0.5 miles.

Later that day, Mr. Russ Hill, a lookout man for the Department of Lands and Forests at Raspberry Ridge, reported two separate sightings. At 2250Z, he observed a brown, disc-shaped object traveling north to south at approximately 150 knots, positioned below and between layers of cloud on a bearing of 272° T. This sighting lasted approximately 5 minutes. At 2346Z, Mr. Hill observed a dark, disc-shaped object at an altitude of 11,000 feet, positioned between broken cloud layers. This object traveled at an estimated speed of 150 to 200 knots, with the sighting lasting approximately one minute.

Additionally, a report was noted regarding a sighting in the Crowsnest area on the previous night, though no specific details were available at the time of the report.

**Object:** 
The objects varied in description. Mr. Matson observed lights that moved in proximity to one another before separating and moving rapidly. Mr. Carnell reported a bright white flash. Mr. Hill described a brown or dark, disc-shaped object. The objects were observed moving at speeds between 150 and 200 knots, often navigating between cloud layers. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The reports were processed by CANPERSUNIT Calgary and transmitted to RCCWC/CANFORCEHQ. Weather conditions at Raspberry Ridge were noted as scattered to broken layered clouds, with cloud bases between 9,000 and 10,000 feet. Regarding Mr. Hill’s reports, the investigating officer noted that the 2346Z incident was the observer's sixth sighting; Mr. Hill claimed to have witnessed four other objects in the preceding two weeks, though official documentation for those prior events had not been received. The documentation is labeled as "PAGE TWO RCWDDC 15 UNCLAS."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** R. 希尔先生（R. Hill，又称拉斯·希尔 Russ Hill，土地与森林资源瞭望员）、O.B. 马特森先生（O.B. Matson）、观测员布莱恩·卡内尔（Brian Carnell）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月18日；记录时间为祖鲁时间（Z），介于0146Z至2346Z之间。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省拉斯伯里岭（Raspberry Ridge，西经114° 38'，北纬50° 18'）、海伍德护林站（Highwood Ranger Station）、福克斯山（Mt. Fox）及克劳斯内斯特（Crowsnest）地区。

**目击经过：**
1967年10月18日发生的事件涉及卡纳纳斯基斯（Kananaskis）地区的多次观测。

0146Z时，O.B. 马特森先生在方位角193°真北方向约2.5英里处观测到两道光。这两道光最初相距100码，随后缩短至50码，接着分开并向福克斯山的东面或东南面移动。目击持续了约2分钟。0152Z时，马特森先生观测到一道单光从方位角214°向240°方向快速北移。

0151Z时，驻扎在海伍德护林站（西经114° 38'，北纬50° 24'）的观测员布莱恩·卡内尔报告看到一道明亮的白光闪烁。该物体在距离目击者约0.5英里处被观测到，出现在树梢下方，最后一次被观测到时距离刚超过0.5英里。

当天晚些时候，拉斯伯里岭土地与森林资源部的瞭望员拉斯·希尔先生报告了两次独立的目击事件。2250Z时，他观测到一个棕色、圆盘状的物体，以约150节的速度由北向南飞行，位于云层下方及云层之间，方位角为272°真北。此次目击持续了约5分钟。2346Z时，希尔先生在11,000英尺的高度观测到一个深色、圆盘状的物体，位于破碎的云层之间。该物体以估计150至200节的速度飞行，目击持续了约一分钟。

此外，报告中还提到前一天晚上在克劳斯内斯特地区也有一起目击事件，但报告时没有提供具体细节。

**物体描述：**
这些物体的描述各不相同。马特森先生观测到的光在靠近后分开并快速移动。卡内尔先生报告了一道明亮的白光闪烁。希尔先生描述了一个棕色或深色的圆盘状物体。这些物体的飞行速度在150至200节之间，经常在云层间穿行。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
这些报告由卡尔加里加拿大人员单位（CANPERSUNIT Calgary）处理，并转交给加拿大空军司令部（RCCWC/CANFORCEHQ）。拉斯伯里岭的天气状况记录为零散至破碎的层云，云底高度在9,000至10,000英尺之间。关于希尔先生的报告，调查官员指出2346Z的事件是该观测员的第六次目击；希尔先生声称在过去两周内还目击过其他四个物体，但尚未收到这些先前事件的官方文件。该文件被标记为“PAGE TWO RCWDDC 15 UNCLAS”。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A 17-year-old science hobbyist with an interest in astronomy and aircraft.

**Sighting:** On October 18, 1967, at 0608 GMT, the witness observed an object from the second-floor window and balcony of their residence while facing south. The weather was described as light broken cloud.

**Object:** The object appeared like a star diffraction photograph with a central yellow-silver glowing sphere and four points of bright silver. It was described as brighter than the moon, which was visible above and in the same direction. The object emitted a sound like an extremely low-flying jet aircraft. It was estimated to be at an altitude of about 400 feet and a distance of 1000 feet, moving from NNW to SSW. It featured red, yellow, and blue blinking lights, blinking approximately three times per second. The duration of the sighting was approximately seven seconds.

**Aftermath:** The witness checked with the Department of Transport (DOT), who stated only one DC8 was on takeoff at a right angle to the line of the UFO's course. The DOT suggested reporting the incident to the DND. The report was delayed because an adult associate derided the witness. The report was received at 2030 hours on the date of the sighting. The witness does not desire publicity.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名17岁的科学爱好者，对天文学和航空器颇感兴趣。

**日期：** 1967年10月18日，格林威治标准时间06:08。

**地点：** 目击者在自家住宅二楼的窗户和阳台，面向南方进行观测。当时天气状况为轻微的碎云。

**目击经过：** 该物体看起来像是一张恒星衍射照片，中心是一个黄银色的发光球体，带有四个明亮的银色光点。据描述，其亮度超过了当时在上方同一方向可见的月亮。该物体发出了类似超低空飞行喷气式飞机的声音。据估计，其高度约为400英尺，距离约为1000英尺，正从北西北（NNW）向南西南（SSW）方向移动。它带有红色、黄色和蓝色的闪烁灯光，闪烁频率约为每秒三次。目击持续时间约为七秒。

**调查/后续：** 目击者向交通部（DOT）进行了核实，交通部表示当时只有一架DC-8飞机正在起飞，其航线与该不明飞行物的航向呈直角。交通部建议将此事报告给国防部（DND）。由于一名成年同伴对目击者进行了嘲讽，导致报告有所延迟。该报告于目击当日20:30收到。目击者不希望公开此事。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Blair Gamble.

**Sighting:** The object was visible for five hours, starting at 210554Z. The location was reported as the Amherst Motel, 2 miles SSE of Amherst.

**Object:** The object was described as bright and apparently stationary in relation to other heavenly bodies, with a colour similar to a star or planet.

**Aftermath:** The sighting was reported to the Greenwood Tower. RCC Halifax attempted to contact the observer by telephone, but the attempt proved negative. The report concludes that the planet Venus was observed clearly in the Halifax area that morning.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 布莱尔·甘布尔 (Blair Gamble)。

**日期：** 协调世界时 210554Z。

**地点：** 阿默斯特汽车旅馆 (Amherst Motel)，位于阿默斯特东南偏南 2 英里处。

**目击经过：** 该物体可见时长达五个小时，始于 210554Z。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体非常明亮，相对于其他天体而言似乎处于静止状态，颜色与恒星或行星相似。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件已报告给格林伍德塔台 (Greenwood Tower)。哈利法克斯联合救援协调中心 (RCC Halifax) 曾尝试通过电话联系目击者，但未能成功。报告结论认为，当天早晨在哈利法克斯地区观测到的物体确为金星。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two Cominco Ltd. ore-truck drivers, a Euclid vehicle driver, A. Michalow (Cpl.), an unnamed supervisor, D.B. Kirkpatrick (Cst.), and additional unnamed witnesses.

**Date / Time:** October 21, 1967, with sightings reported between approximately 2:30 AM and 3:00 AM (and an earlier sighting at 8:15–8:20 PM).

**Location:** Pine Point, Northwest Territories, specifically in the vicinity of the ore pits and the X-15 road junction.

**Sighting:** On the night of October 21, 1967, multiple workers at the Pine Point ore pits reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon. Accounts vary significantly: some witnesses described a complex, multi-colored craft, while others reported a single stationary light. 

Two ore-truck drivers reported that at 3:00 AM, an object descended vertically from the southeast to a hover height of 20–30 feet, remaining for up to 15 minutes before departing rapidly to the southeast. A Euclid driver reported seeing a red light descend at 2:57 AM, hovering above a lowboy trailer near the X-15 junction. This witness shut off their vehicle, fearing it was a helicopter, and observed the object for 3–5 seconds before it ascended vertically. Cpl. A. Michalow provided a detailed account of the object dropping from a high altitude to approximately 400 yards away. Conversely, an unnamed supervisor reported seeing a bright white light at 8:15 PM and again at 2:30 AM, explicitly denying the presence of red or green lights, describing it only as a stationary light near a transformer. Another driver reported a yellowish, reddish-orange round light that remained stationary during two separate trips.

**Object:** Descriptions of the object were inconsistent. Several witnesses described a circular or elliptical craft, approximately 15 feet in diameter and 7–9 feet high, resembling two derby hats joined at the rims with a 3-foot center band. These witnesses reported a red flashing top half and a green flashing bottom half. Others described the lights as being the size of a desk or a police car light. Some witnesses noted the object was soundless, while others described it as moving like a shooting star before slowing to a hover. The supervisor and one driver described only a single, bright, stationary white or yellowish light, similar to a car headlight or the "midnight sun."

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews with the witnesses. One driver was considered reliable, while another’s account was questioned by police due to inconsistencies regarding when he first reported the event, leading to suspicions of a "community joke." Cpl. Michalow provided a sketch of the "derby hat" configuration. The Department of Transport in Fort Smith confirmed that the only aircraft in the area was a D.C. 6 that passed over at 1:00 AM, well before the primary sightings. RCMP investigations noted that witness statements regarding dates were corrected to include the night of October 20–21. No definitive explanation for the sightings was reached.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两名科明科有限公司（Cominco Ltd.）的矿石卡车司机、一名尤克里德（Euclid）重型车辆司机、A. 米哈洛（A. Michalow）下士、一名未具名的主管、D.B. 柯克帕特里克（D.B. Kirkpatrick）警员，以及其他未具名的目击者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年10月21日，目击报告时间约为凌晨2:30至3:00（另有一次较早的目击发生在晚上8:15至8:20）。

**地点：** 西北地区派恩波因特（Pine Point），具体位于矿坑及X-15公路交叉口附近。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月21日晚，派恩波因特矿坑的多名工人报告了不明空中现象。各方描述差异巨大：一些目击者称看到了一个复杂的、多色的飞行器，而另一些人则报告称只看到一个静止的光点。

两名矿石卡车司机报告称，凌晨3:00，一个物体从东南方向垂直下降，悬停在离地20至30英尺的高度，停留了长达15分钟，随后迅速向东南方向离去。一名尤克里德车辆司机报告称，在凌晨2:57看到一束红光下降，悬停在X-15交叉口附近的一辆平板拖车上方。该目击者因担心是直升机而熄灭了车辆引擎，观察了该物体3至5秒，随后物体垂直上升。A. 米哈洛下士详细描述了该物体从高空降落至距离其约400码处的过程。相反，一名未具名的主管报告称在晚上8:15和凌晨2:30分别看到了一束明亮的白光，他明确否认了红光或绿光的存在，仅将其描述为变压器附近的一个静止光点。另一名司机则报告称看到了一个黄中带红橙色的圆形光点，在两次往返途中该光点均保持静止。

**物体描述：** 对该物体的描述并不一致。几名目击者称其为一个圆形或椭圆形的飞行器，直径约15英尺，高7至9英尺，外观类似于两个边缘相连的圆顶硬礼帽，中间有一条3英尺宽的带状物。这些目击者报告称其上半部分闪烁红光，下半部分闪烁绿光。其他人则将这些光描述为书桌或警车警灯大小。一些目击者指出该物体没有发出声音，而另一些人则描述它像流星一样移动，随后减速并悬停。主管和其中一名司机仅描述了一个单一的、明亮的、静止的白色或黄色光点，类似于汽车前灯或“午夜太阳”。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对目击者进行了访谈。其中一名司机被认为可靠，而另一名司机的陈述因在首次报告时间上存在前后矛盾，受到警方的质疑，从而引发了关于这是否是“社区恶作剧”的怀疑。米哈洛下士提供了一份“圆顶硬礼帽”构型的草图。史密斯堡（Fort Smith）交通部证实，该地区当时唯一的飞行器是一架在凌晨1:00经过的DC-6飞机，远早于主要的目击时间。加拿大皇家骑警的调查指出，目击者关于日期的陈述已修正为包含10月20日至21日晚间。最终，这些目击事件未得出明确的解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miss [redacted], three unnamed youths, Cst. FERGUSON, an unnamed female student at Strasbourg High School, Mr. Delmar Canning (Vice-Principal), and an unnamed twelve-year-old girl.

**Date / Time:** October 24, 1967, at approximately 9:30 PM; October 25, 1967, at approximately 1:20 PM.

**Location:** Lumsden, Saskatchewan (valley two miles south-east) and Strasbourg, Saskatchewan (Strasbourg Public School).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 24, 1967, at approximately 9:30 PM, a group of youths, including Miss [redacted], observed an unidentified flying object hovering over a valley two miles south-east of Lumsden. The youths reported the object moved in a looping motion. While traveling on Highway 11, the group observed a second object that approached them rapidly before fading. The youths were found in a state of hysteria and crying. Simultaneously, a twelve-year-old girl in Lumsden reported seeing "Flying Saucers." Cst. FERGUSON, dispatched to the scene, observed a bright red light surrounded by smaller white lights flashing in unison at one-second intervals; he watched this object rise at a 45-degree angle into the cloud cover. The sighting lasted approximately three minutes with no audible sound.

On October 25, 1967, at 1:20 PM, a female student at Strasbourg Public School observed three bright white objects while in a ground-floor classroom. The objects hovered over the High School before disappearing in a south-westerly direction. The student was left in a state of shock.

**Object:** 
*   **Primary Object (Oct 24):** A small white light moving in a looping motion.
*   **Second Object (Oct 24):** A two-foot-long entity with a darker substance surrounding it.
*   **Officer’s Observation (Oct 24):** A bright red light surrounded by smaller white lights flashing at one-second intervals.
*   **Daytime Objects (Oct 25):** Three round, moon-shaped objects. One was the size of a silver dollar, and two were the size of 50-cent pieces. They were bright white, comparable to the lens of an illuminated flashlight or the sun in luminosity, though they cast no shadows. The last small object left a bright white trail.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Mr. Delmar Canning, Vice-Principal of Strasbourg Public School, reported the student's sighting to the RCMP after school hours. Cst. R. Serbanievich of the Strasbourg Detachment conducted inquiries in and around Strasbourg to locate further witnesses, but results were negative. Mr. John HODGES was notified of the initial sighting per Op. Man. "CO-Air." The file was concluded by Cst. Serbanievich, though a follow-up note from the Sub-Division requested clarification on whether to continue following "CO-Air" protocols for UFOs, noting that these sightings did not fit the criteria for fireballs or meteorites.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Donald Kowalski (age 13) and George Korol (age 14).

**Date / Time:** October 27, 1967, at 2130Z (initial sighting); December 12, 1967, at 1630 local time (subsequent observation).

**Location:** An empty lot near the corner of Jefferson and Sinclair in West Kildonan, Winnipeg, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On October 27, 1967, at 2130Z, Donald Kowalski and George Korol observed an object while in an empty lot in West Kildonan. The weather was described as cloudy and dull. George Korol later reported a second observation on December 12 at 1630 local time, lasting 8 to 10 minutes. During this event, the object was seen at an altitude of approximately 1500 feet, approaching from the east before moving in an "irregular manner" and eventually departing at a high rate of speed toward the southwest.

**Object:** The object’s appearance was dynamic. Initially described as elliptical, it appeared to change to a round shape as it passed overhead. Estimates of its size varied significantly; witnesses initially estimated a diameter of 20 to 30 feet. However, official photographic analysis by the Defence Photographic Interpretation Centre (DPIC) suggested the object was an oblate ellipsoid or "cigar" shaped, potentially rolling or yawing nearly 90 degrees. While witnesses perceived a large craft, the DPIC concluded the images were consistent with a 10-inch children’s balloon at a range of approximately 225 feet. The object was noted to be in "free flight" rather than controlled flight.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** George Korol took six photographs of the object using an Instamatic 104/Fixed Lens camera. The negatives and original prints were submitted to the Department of National Defence (DND) for analysis, and CFB Winnipeg created local enlargements. The investigation involved consultations with the Ottawa and Gimli meteorological offices and Ottawa Hydro to analyze wind data and potential balloon releases. 

While initial reports noted that the object’s movement against prevailing winds contradicted typical balloon behavior, the final DPIC report—signed by S/L C.R. Hallowell—concluded that the object was a 10-inch balloon. This conclusion was based on range calculations comparing the object's resolution to a nearby light standard (185 feet away) and a house (800 feet away). The report dismissed the possibility of a football or a large meteorological balloon, noting that no balloons were released from Winnipeg or Gimli during the relevant time frames. The investigation was officially closed by CFHQ under Colonel W.W. Turner. The boys were commended for their alertness, and the witness's parents requested that the matter remain private.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 唐纳德·科瓦尔斯基（Donald Kowalski，13岁）和乔治·科罗尔（George Korol，14岁）。

**日期/时间：** 1967年10月27日，21:30Z（首次目击）；1967年12月12日，当地时间16:30（后续观察）。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省温尼伯市西基尔多南区（West Kildonan），杰斐逊街（Jefferson）与辛克莱街（Sinclair）拐角处的一块空地。

**目击经过：** 1967年10月27日21:30Z，唐纳德·科瓦尔斯基和乔治·科罗尔在西基尔多南的一块空地上观察到了一个物体。据描述，当时天气阴沉。乔治·科罗尔随后报告称，在12月12日当地时间16:30又进行了第二次观察，持续了8到10分钟。在此次事件中，该物体出现在约1500英尺的高度，从东面靠近，随后以“不规则方式”移动，最终以极高的速度向西南方向飞离。

**物体描述：** 该物体的外观呈现动态变化。最初被描述为椭圆形，但在经过头顶时似乎变成了圆形。对其尺寸的估计差异很大；目击者最初估计其直径为20到30英尺。然而，国防摄影判读中心（DPIC）的官方摄影分析认为，该物体呈扁椭球体或“雪茄”状，可能发生了近90度的翻滚或偏航。尽管目击者认为这是一艘大型飞行器，但DPIC得出的结论是，这些图像与一个距离约225英尺、直径10英寸的儿童气球相符。该物体被指出处于“自由飞行”状态，而非受控飞行。

**调查/后续：** 乔治·科罗尔使用一台Instamatic 104型定焦相机拍摄了六张该物体的照片。底片和原始照片被提交给国防部（DND）进行分析，温尼伯加拿大空军基地（CFB Winnipeg）制作了局部放大照片。调查过程包括咨询渥太华和吉姆利（Gimli）的气象办公室以及渥太华水电局，以分析风力数据和潜在的气球释放情况。

尽管最初的报告指出该物体逆风移动的轨迹与典型气球的行为相矛盾，但由C.R.哈洛韦尔（C.R. Hallowell）中队长签署的DPIC最终报告结论认为，该物体就是一个10英寸的气球。这一结论是基于将物体的分辨率与附近的灯柱（185英尺远）和房屋（800英尺远）进行对比后的距离计算得出的。报告排除了它是橄榄球或大型气象气球的可能性，并指出在相关时间段内，温尼伯或吉姆利均未释放过气球。该调查由加拿大军队总部（CFHQ）的W.W.特纳（W.W. Turner）上校正式结案。两名男孩的警觉性受到了表扬，目击者的父母要求对此事保密。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:

**Witnesses:** James C. Moir, Edward Wonnocott, Ronald Nicol, and unidentified persons (responsible for the balsam wood structures).

**Date / Time:** October 31, 1968, at 9:30 PM MST.

**Location:** Cranbrook, British Columbia (specifically observed over Mount Baker, southwest of the city, moving toward the outskirts).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 31, 1968, under clear skies, James C. Moir observed an anomalous object from his backyard at 5 Alpine Trailer Court. He first spotted the craft over Mount Baker and watched as it traveled toward the outskirts of Cranbrook. Moir alerted Edward Wonnocott to the object, and both men utilized field glasses to observe it. Ronald Nicol also witnessed the object independently. Moir observed the craft for approximately 15 minutes, while Wonnocott and Nicol observed it for 5 to 10 minutes. The object appeared to clear the mountain top before moving to the outskirts of the city, where it appeared to land. 

Concurrent with this investigation (File CBK2327), RCMP members discovered that unidentified persons had been constructing "X"-shaped frames out of balsam wood. These frames were enclosed in plastic bags with candles attached to each end. RCMP officers noted that several of these makeshift devices were observed floating in the sky, with debris occasionally falling from them, suggesting a potential explanation for some aerial phenomena reported in the area.

**Object:** The primary object was described as cigar-shaped, measuring approximately 200 feet in length and 100 feet in width, with indentations at both ends. It featured bright orange flashes along its sides, a series of lights resembling portholes, and bright lights at each end. The object was observed turning end-for-end during the sighting. In contrast, the secondary objects identified by the RCMP were "X"-shaped balsam wood structures encased in plastic bags, propelled by candles attached to the frame ends.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Upon receiving the report, the Cranbrook RCMP detachment immediately dispatched patrols to the area where the object appeared to land. A thorough search of the surrounding terrain yielded no results. The sighting details were formally transmitted via teletype to the NRC Meteor Centre and other relevant agencies. The investigation concluded by documenting the local construction of the balsam wood and candle devices, which were observed by RCMP members to be floating in the sky, providing a terrestrial explanation for similar debris and sightings in the region.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯·C·莫伊尔 (James C. Moir)、爱德华·沃诺科特 (Edward Wonnocott)、罗纳德·尼科尔 (Ronald Nicol) 以及身份不明的人员（负责制作轻木结构装置）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年10月31日，山区标准时间 (MST) 晚上9:30。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省克兰布鲁克（具体观测点位于城市西南方的贝克山上方，并向郊区移动）。

**目击经过：** 1968年10月31日晚，在晴朗的天空下，詹姆斯·C·莫伊尔在他位于高山拖车营地 (Alpine Trailer Court) 5号的后院观察到一个异常物体。他最初在贝克山上空发现了该飞行器，并注视着它向克兰布鲁克郊区移动。莫伊尔提醒了爱德华·沃诺科特，两人随后使用双筒望远镜对其进行了观测。罗纳德·尼科尔也独立目击了该物体。莫伊尔观察该飞行器约15分钟，而沃诺科特和尼科尔观察了5至10分钟。该物体似乎飞越了山顶，随后移动到城市郊区，并看起来在那里降落。

在本次调查（档案编号 CBK2327）期间，加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 成员发现，有身份不明的人员一直在用轻木制作“X”形框架。这些框架被包裹在塑料袋中，并在每一端附有蜡烛。皇家骑警警官指出，曾观察到几个此类临时装置漂浮在空中，并不时有碎片从中掉落，这为该地区报告的部分空中现象提供了一种潜在的解释。

**物体描述：** 主要物体被描述为雪茄状，长约200英尺，宽约100英尺，两端有凹痕。其侧面闪烁着明亮的橙色光芒，有一系列类似舷窗的灯光，两端也有明亮的灯光。在目击过程中，该物体被观察到进行了首尾翻转。相比之下，皇家骑警确认的次要物体是包裹在塑料袋中的“X”形轻木结构，由附在框架末端的蜡烛提供动力。

**调查/后续：** 在接到报告后，克兰布鲁克皇家骑警分队立即派遣巡逻队前往该物体疑似降落的区域。对周边地形进行了彻底搜查，但未发现任何结果。目击详情已通过电传打字机正式传达给加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心及其他相关机构。调查最终记录了当地制作轻木和蜡烛装置的情况，皇家骑警成员曾观察到这些装置漂浮在空中，这为该地区类似的碎片和目击事件提供了地面解释。

**Witnesses:** W. Green (member of the Corps of Commissionaires), two unnamed officers at CFB Shilo.

**Date / Time:** November 2, 1967, at 11:00Z.

**Location:** Base Maintenance Section compound, CFB Shilo, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On November 2, 1967, at 11:00Z, W. Green was stationed at the Base Maintenance Section compound at CFB Shilo. He reported hearing a distinct noise described as a human-like cry, phonetically rendered as "HAW." Upon looking toward the northwest, he observed a bright golden object rising rapidly in a near-vertical trajectory, similar to a rocket. After the initial ascent, the object turned and proceeded in a southerly direction. During its flight, the object moved slowly, decelerating at intervals and occasionally speeding up slightly before eventually disappearing from view. The total duration of the sighting was estimated at two to three minutes. 

In a separate account involving Mr. Green and two other officers at the base, the event was discussed in the context of a weather balloon release. These individuals observed the release of a weather balloon under conditions they noted were similar to those of the reported UFO sighting. Following this observation, Mr. Green expressed his conviction that the object he had witnessed was, in fact, a weather balloon.

**Object:** The object was described as elliptical in shape with a faint red glow. It featured a distinct circle of six to ten twinkling lights located on its rim or bottom. Additionally, the object possessed protrusions resembling spikes on its top. While initially described as a bright golden object, subsequent official review suggested the object was a weather balloon.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report acknowledges that a weather balloon was released at CFB Shilo within ten minutes of the sighting. The proximity of this release led investigators to conclude that the balloon was the likely source of the observation. Mr. Green’s final assessment—that he was convinced the object was a balloon—was documented as part of the follow-up investigation into the incident.

**目击者：** W. 格林（W. Green，委任军官团成员），以及希洛加拿大军队基地（CFB Shilo）的两名匿名军官。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年11月2日，11:00Z（祖鲁时间）。

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省，希洛加拿大军队基地，基地维修区大院。

**目击经过：** 1967年11月2日11:00Z，W. 格林当时驻守在希洛加拿大军队基地的维修区大院。他报告称听到了一种独特的声音，听起来像人类的叫喊声，发音近似为“HAW”。当他向西北方向望去时，观察到一个明亮的金色物体正以近乎垂直的轨迹迅速上升，类似于火箭。在最初的上升之后，该物体转向并向南飞行。在飞行过程中，物体移动缓慢，间歇性减速，偶尔会轻微加速，最终消失在视野中。目击过程总时长估计为两到三分钟。

在涉及格林先生和基地另外两名军官的另一份叙述中，该事件是在气象气球释放的背景下进行讨论的。这些人观察到了一次气象气球的释放，并指出当时的环境条件与所报告的UFO目击事件相似。在此次观察之后，格林先生表示他确信自己目击到的物体实际上就是一个气象气球。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形，带有微弱的红光。其边缘或底部有一个明显的圆环，上面有六到十个闪烁的灯光。此外，该物体顶部还有类似尖刺的突起。虽然最初被描述为一个明亮的金色物体，但随后的官方审查认为该物体是一个气象气球。

**调查/后续：** 报告确认在目击事件发生后的十分钟内，希洛加拿大军队基地确实释放了一个气象气球。由于释放时间与目击时间非常接近，调查人员得出结论，认为该气球极有可能是此次目击事件的源头。格林先生最终的评估——即他确信该物体是一个气象气球——已被记录在该事件的后续调查报告中。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Victor McKee (Manager of the Robinson Department Store in Dauphin, Manitoba; former Infantryman with six years of military experience, 1940–1946).

**Date / Time:** December 3, 1967, at 2155Z.

**Location:** 202 Edgar Avenue, Dauphin, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** Mr. Victor McKee observed an unidentified object while looking out of his kitchen window under a clear sky. The object was first sighted north of Dauphin, traveling at a very high rate of speed in a north-northwest direction. The total duration of the observation was one minute, though the object disappeared from sight within five seconds of the initial sighting. During the event, Mr. McKee attempted to use eight-power binoculars to track the object, but he was unable to locate it through the lenses. The observed angle of the object was 50 degrees at the time of the first observation, decreasing to 40 degrees by the time it vanished.

**Object:** The object was described as definitely round in shape. Visually, it appeared as a spot of light with a luminosity and appearance comparable to one of the early large, bright stars seen at dusk on a summer evening. In terms of size, the witness compared it to the reflection from a nickel coin held at a distance of 10 feet. The altitude of the object was estimated by the witness to be 1,000 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Mr. McKee initially submitted an advisory note regarding the sighting to the Department of Transport (DOT) Headquarters in Winnipeg, which was subsequently forwarded to Training Command Headquarters. 

Military investigators conducted a cursory examination of potential aircraft in the area, but the results were negative, a failure they attributed to the difficulty of obtaining precise flight data at such a late date. The military assessment suggested that the sighting could be explained by the sun reflecting at a specific angle off a high-flying aircraft, creating the illusion of a round object; they posited that the change in the relative angle between the sun, the object, and the observer caused the reflection to disappear. Furthermore, officials noted that the described flight path was consistent with an aircraft at high or medium altitude overflying Dauphin along Amber Airway 11/Amber Route 9. Due to these conclusions, the military determined that no further action would be taken regarding the report.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 维克多·麦基先生（Victor McKee，曼尼托巴省多芬市罗宾逊百货公司经理；曾任步兵，拥有六年军旅经验，1940–1946年）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月3日，2155Z（格林威治标准时间）。

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省多芬市埃德加大道202号。

**目击经过：** 维克多·麦基先生在自家厨房窗前向外望去，在晴朗的天空中观察到一个不明物体。该物体最初在多芬市北部被发现，正以极高的速度向北-西北方向飞行。整个观察过程持续了一分钟，但该物体在最初发现后的五秒内便从视野中消失了。事件期间，麦基先生曾试图使用八倍双筒望远镜追踪该物体，但未能通过镜片定位到它。物体在首次观察时的仰角为50度，消失时降至40度。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为形状绝对呈圆形。从视觉上看，它表现为一个光点，其亮度和外观类似于夏日黄昏时分可见的早期大型亮星。在尺寸方面，目击者将其比作在10英尺距离处观察一枚镍币所产生的反光。目击者估计该物体的高度为1,000英尺。

**调查/后续：** 麦基先生最初就此次目击事件向位于温尼伯的交通部（DOT）总部提交了一份咨询说明，随后被转交至训练司令部总部。

军事调查人员对该地区潜在的飞行器进行了初步审查，但结果为阴性；他们将此归咎于在事发许久之后难以获取精确的飞行数据。军方的评估认为，此次目击事件可能是由于太阳在特定角度照射到高空飞行器上产生反射，从而造成了圆形物体的错觉；他们推测太阳、物体与观察者之间相对角度的变化导致了反射的消失。此外，官员们指出，所描述的飞行路径与一架沿琥珀航路11号/琥珀航线9号（Amber Airway 11/Amber Route 9）飞过多芬市上空的高空或中空飞行器相吻合。基于这些结论，军方决定不再对该报告采取进一步行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** WC RR Barber, SL De Weese, and LAC TM Stephens.

**Sighting:** On December 3, 1967, at 1930Z, the witnesses were traveling southbound on a highway ten miles south of Stettler, Alberta. They observed a bright, cigar-shaped object at about 40 degrees elevation, positioned ten degrees west of the north-south roadway. The object had clearly defined edges and was estimated to be at least twenty miles away.

**Object:** The object's axis changed from vertical to horizontal. It drifted east until it was positioned directly above the highway. When viewed with a finger and thumb held 18 inches from the face, the object measured about one-half inch in length. As the car traveled at 60 mph, the object moved away and its shape changed rapidly from a cigar shape to a round spot, described as the size of a bubble in a Kollsman sextant, with edges still clearly defined. The object then dimmed and was lost to view. The total observation time was twelve minutes.

**Aftermath:** The witnesses discussed the sighting and confirmed they were all seeing the same thing. They noted the object's elevation exceeded that of the sun. Because the object moved from west to east while the sun moved in the opposite direction, the witnesses discounted the theory that the object was associated with the sun. The report notes a regret for the delay in reporting due to unfamiliarity with CFAO 71-6.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** WC RR Barber, SL De Weese, 以及 LAC TM Stephens。

**目击：** 1967年12月3日1930Z，见证者们在阿尔伯塔省斯特特勒以南十英里的公路上向南行驶。他们观察到一个明亮的雪茄状物体，位于海拔约40度处，位置在南北向道路以西约10度。该物体边缘清晰，估计距离至少有二十英里。

**物体：** 该物体的轴线从垂直变为水平。它向东漂移，直到直接位于公路正上方。当用距离脸部18英寸的手指和拇指测量时，该物体长度约为半英寸。当汽车以60英里的时速行驶时，物体开始远离，其形状迅速从雪茄状变为圆形斑点（描述为Kollsman六分仪中气泡的大小），边缘依然清晰。随后物体变暗并消失。总观测时间为十二分钟。

**后续：** 见证者们讨论了此次目击事件，并确认他们看到的是同一个物体。他们指出该物体的高度超过了太阳。由于物体从西向东移动，而太阳向相反方向移动，见证者们排除了该物体与太阳有关的理论。报告提到由于不熟悉CFAO 71-6，对报告的延迟表示遗憾。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Evelyn Brown

**Date / Time:** December 18, 1967

**Location:** Regina, Saskatchewan

**Sighting:** 
On December 18, 1967, Mrs. Evelyn Brown captured photographs of an unidentified aerial object in Regina, Saskatchewan. Mrs. Brown reported the sighting and submitted the photographic evidence to the Department of National Defence for analysis. According to her account, she estimated the distance of the UFO to be approximately 400 yards from her position. The investigation focused heavily on the technical interpretation of the photographs to determine the nature of the object and the validity of the image.

**Object:** 
The object was captured using a Polaroid Swinger model 20 camera. Technical analysis of the photographs addressed specific features that appeared in the images. A "dark object" observed above the UFO in "Print #1" was identified by investigators as a 3-inch-long clothes pin. Furthermore, lines visible in the photographs were determined to be part of a clothesline, measured at heights ranging from 5 feet to 5 feet 9 inches above the ground. The object itself is primarily defined in the file by its estimated distance of 400 yards from the witness.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation was conducted by the Canadian Forces Recruiting Centre in Regina, which submitted detailed measurements and photographic analysis to the Chief of Defence Staff in Ottawa. The National Research Council of Canada was also involved in the institutional review of the case. 

To verify the scale and perspective of the photographs, investigators conducted a site survey. They measured the distance from the camera to the fence at 34 feet 3 inches. Additional measurements were taken of various environmental features to assist in the analysis, including the distance to an area where a tower had previously stood (154 yards), as well as dimensions for a wagon, the letter "O," and boards on an outhouse. The report confirms that the tower previously located in the background had been removed prior to the time the photographs were taken. The final technical report was signed by Lieutenant Commander Blair, the Commanding Officer.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 伊芙琳·布朗夫人 (Mrs. Evelyn Brown)

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月18日

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省里贾纳 (Regina, Saskatchewan)

**目击经过：** 
1967年12月18日，伊芙琳·布朗夫人在萨斯喀彻温省里贾纳拍摄到了一个不明飞行物。布朗夫人报告了此次目击事件，并将照片证据提交给国防部进行分析。据她描述，她估计该不明飞行物距离她所在位置约400码。调查重点在于对照片进行技术解读，以确定物体的性质及图像的真实性。

**物体描述：** 
该物体是使用宝丽来 (Polaroid) Swinger 20型相机拍摄的。对照片的技术分析针对图像中出现的特定特征进行了研究。调查人员认定，“照片1”中不明飞行物上方观察到的“暗色物体”实际上是一个3英寸长的晾衣夹。此外，照片中可见的线条被确定为晾衣绳的一部分，经测量，其离地高度在5英尺至5英尺9英寸之间。在档案中，该物体的主要特征被定义为距离目击者约400码。

**调查/后续：** 
此次调查由位于里贾纳的加拿大军队征兵中心进行，该中心将详细的测量数据和照片分析结果提交给了渥太华的国防参谋长。加拿大国家研究委员会也参与了该案件的机构审查。

为了核实照片的比例和透视关系，调查人员进行了现场勘测。他们测得相机到围栏的距离为34英尺3英寸。为了辅助分析，调查人员还对各种环境特征进行了额外测量，包括到曾经矗立过一座塔的区域的距离（154码），以及马车、字母“O”和厕所木板的尺寸。报告证实，背景中原有的塔在照片拍摄前已被拆除。最终技术报告由指挥官布莱尔 (Blair) 中校签署。

**Witnesses:** Several employees of the Department of Transport in Inuvik, N.W.T., and one student.

**Sighting:** On December 18, 1967, at 7:50 AM, observers reported a very bright, white, round light. The light was observed at an angle of about 30 degrees and appeared to move in an east to west direction, moving away from the observers. The light was not steady, but seemed to blink or flicker without a regular rhythm. The observation lasted until approximately 8:40 AM.

**Object:** The object was described as a round, bright white light, similar to the landing light of a large aircraft. No noise, heat, or other peculiarities were noted.

**目击者：** 西北地区伊努维克交通部的几名员工及一名学生。

**地点：** 西北地区伊努维克。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个圆形的明亮白光，类似于大型飞机的着陆灯。未发现噪音、热量或其他异常特征。

**调查/后续：** 一些观察者指出，在其他日子的同一时间，同一位置确实会出现一颗特定的恒星，但他们强调那颗恒星的亮度及大小均不及他们所目击到的光团。观察者们对该光团的成因未给出任何解释。

**Witnesses:** An unnamed civilian resident of New Minas, Miss Ethel Sandy (R.R. #3, Kentville, N.S.)

**Date / Time:** December 21, 1967, at approximately 5:00 A.M.

**Location:** New Minas / Kentville, Nova Scotia (specifically near the main highway of New Minas).

**Sighting:** On the morning of December 21, 1967, at 5:00 A.M., an unnamed civilian resident living near the main highway in New Minas observed an unidentified object positioned to the south. The object was described as being very low to the ground and in close proximity to the witness. The witness observed the object for approximately three minutes before it vanished. 

Separately, Miss Ethel Sandy of R.R. #3, Kentville, provided a brief written account regarding an observation. Her note emphasized that the object she witnessed remained stationary, stating, "it never moved, [it] stayed just the one place." While the provided documentation does not explicitly confirm if Miss Sandy and the unnamed resident witnessed the exact same phenomenon, both reports originate from the same geographic area and timeframe, and were compiled as part of the same official case file.

**Object:** The object was described by the unnamed resident as a large ball of light featuring a "neck" on the top and a distinct funnel shape. Regarding its behavior and appearance, the object underwent a color transformation during the three-minute sighting: it shifted from its initial state to red, then to pink and mauve, before finally extinguishing abruptly, "like a light being turned off." Miss Sandy’s account adds the detail that the object was stationary and did not exhibit any movement during her observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of two primary records preserved within the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) files. The first is a formal letter dated December 22, 1967, written by the unnamed New Minas resident. The witness was prompted to report the incident after reading a request in the local newspaper for reports regarding "strange objects." The second document is a handwritten note addressed to Miss Ethel Sandy (phone number 678-4535), which serves as a supplementary account of the event. No formal RCMP interrogation reports, official weather data, or final investigative conclusions are present in the provided pages.

**目击经过：** 1967年12月21日凌晨5:00，一名居住在新米纳斯主干道附近的匿名平民居民观察到一个位于南方的不明物体。据描述，该物体距离地面非常近，且与目击者距离很近。目击者观察了该物体约三分钟，随后它消失了。

此外，居住在肯特维尔 R.R. #3 的埃塞尔·桑迪小姐提供了一份关于此次目击事件的简短书面记录。她在笔记中强调，她所目击的物体保持静止状态，并写道：“它从未移动过，（它）一直停留在同一个地方。”虽然现有文件并未明确证实桑迪小姐与该匿名居民目击的是否为同一现象，但两份报告均来自同一地理区域和时间段，并被归入同一份官方档案中。

**物体描述：** 匿名居民将该物体描述为一个巨大的光球，顶部有一个“颈部”，呈明显的漏斗状。关于其行为和外观，该物体在三分钟的目击过程中发生了颜色变化：它从初始状态变为红色，随后转为粉色和淡紫色，最后突然熄灭，“就像关灯一样”。桑迪小姐的描述补充了一个细节，即该物体处于静止状态，在她的观察过程中没有任何移动。

**调查/后续：** 相关文档由保存在加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）档案中的两份主要记录组成。第一份是匿名新米纳斯居民于1967年12月22日写的一封正式信件。该目击者是在阅读了当地报纸关于征集“奇异物体”报告的请求后，决定报告此次事件的。第二份文件是一封写给埃塞尔·桑迪小姐（电话号码：678-4535）的手写便条，作为对该事件的补充说明。在提供的页面中，没有包含任何正式的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）审讯报告、官方气象数据或最终调查结论。

**Witnesses:** A civilian Justice of the Peace (Hafford, Saskatchewan).

**Date / Time:** December 25, 1967; two distinct times recorded: 3:15 PM CST and 6:15 PM MST.

**Location:** Hafford, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On December 25, 1967, a sighting occurred in Hafford, Saskatchewan, involving an unidentified aerial object. The documentation contains two conflicting time entries: one report notes the event at 3:15 PM CST, while the primary witness account—provided by a local Justice of the Peace—places the event at approximately 6:15 PM MST. 

The Justice of the Peace observed the object while looking through a picture window in his living room. Facing north, he watched the object for a duration of a few seconds as it traveled across the sky from east to west. The object maintained an altitude of approximately 10 degrees above the horizon. The witness initially interpreted the phenomenon as a meteor. The weather conditions at the time of the report were described as dark and clear.

**Object:** The object was described as round and white in color. Its apparent size was compared to that of a street lamp. It moved in a consistent trajectory from east to west at an altitude of 10 degrees off the horizon. The duration of the sighting was brief, lasting only a few seconds. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Justice of the Peace reported the sighting to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on December 27, 1967. The reporting officer evaluated the witness as reliable and noted that there were no other reports of similar sightings in the Hafford area at that time. 

The case file includes a priority communication regarding this event, which was transmitted to CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters) and F Division in Regina, with references made to the North Battleford Sub-Division. The documentation serves as an official record of the investigation into the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一位平民治安法官（萨斯喀彻温省哈福德）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月25日；记录了两个不同的时间：中部标准时间（CST）下午3:15和山区标准时间（MST）下午6:15。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省哈福德。

**目击经过：** 1967年12月25日，萨斯喀彻温省哈福德发生了一起涉及不明飞行物的目击事件。档案中包含两个相互矛盾的时间记录：一份报告指出事件发生在下午3:15（CST），而由当地治安法官提供的首要目击者陈述则将事件发生时间定在下午6:15（MST）左右。

这位治安法官是在透过客厅的落地窗向外看时观察到该物体的。他面向北方，观察了该物体几秒钟，当时它正从东向西横穿天空。该物体保持在地平线上方约10度的高度。目击者最初认为这一现象是流星。据报告，当时的天气状况为天色昏暗且晴朗。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，呈白色。其视大小被比作路灯。它以一致的轨迹从东向西移动，高度在地平线上方10度。目击持续时间很短，仅几秒钟。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 治安法官于1967年12月27日向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了此次目击事件。负责报告的警官评估认为该目击者是可靠的，并指出当时哈福德地区没有其他类似目击事件的报告。

该案卷包含一份关于此事件的优先通讯，已传达至加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）及位于里贾纳的F分部，并提及了北巴特尔福德分区。该文件作为此次目击事件调查的官方记录存档。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed observer, a three-man party from the unit, Major Bolduc, and the occupants of a moving car.

**Date / Time:** December 27, 1967, at 0238Z.

**Location:** St. Margarets, New Brunswick (specifically Highway Number 11, four miles northwest of the town).

**Sighting:** The event involved two distinct sets of observations. The occupants of a moving car reported seeing a "fireball" at 0238Z on Highway 11. This object moved from 20 degrees above the horizon, traveling through an arc of 340 degrees to 020 degrees, heading approximately 040 degrees. The sighting lasted three seconds and appeared to be a large, continuously burning object that may have disintegrated just above the horizon.

Separately, an observer reported watching an object that followed an arc before disappearing behind trees. This observer stopped to watch an intermittent, rotating beam of light emanating from an apparent landing site, aimed into the sky at a 75–80 degree angle for approximately 10 minutes. This sighting was noted to correspond almost exactly in description and movement to a sighting reported in the same general area two weeks prior by Major Bolduc.

**Object:** The descriptions of the objects varied significantly. The fireball seen by the car occupants was described as round, white, and continuously incandescent. It was estimated to be three times brighter than planets and one-fifteenth the size of a full moon. 

The object observed by the stationary witness was described as entirely luminous with a blue-green color and a profile resembling the bottom half of a cone. It emitted a very intense light that did not change in intensity. The intermittent beam associated with this sighting was later identified as a mechanical light source.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report of the stationary object, a three-man party from the unit snowshoed into the area to investigate a potential landing or near-landing. They discovered a natural explanation: a logging operation was underway involving a large log-loading machine and an 18-wheel truck. The investigation concluded that the trucks operated 24 hours a day and were equipped with rotating lights on their cabs. The "intermittent beam" observed by the witness was determined to be the movement of the loader crane passing over the cab. Regarding the fireball reported by the car occupants, a handwritten note on the official document states: "fireball no further action."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名未具名的观察者、一支三人小组、博尔杜克少校（Major Bolduc）以及一辆行驶中汽车的乘员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月27日，02:38Z（祖鲁时间）。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省圣玛格丽特（St. Margarets）（具体位于该镇西北四英里处的11号高速公路上）。

**目击经过：** 该事件涉及两组截然不同的观察记录。一辆行驶中汽车的乘员报告称，于02:38Z在11号公路上看到一个“火球”。该物体从地平线上方20度处出现，沿340度至020度的弧线移动，航向约为040度。目击过程持续了三秒钟，该物体看起来是一个巨大的、持续燃烧的物体，可能在地平线上方解体。

另有一名观察者报告称，看到一个物体划过一道弧线后消失在树丛后。该观察者停下脚步，观察到从一个疑似着陆点射出一道间歇性的旋转光束，光束以75至80度的角度射向天空，持续了约10分钟。据记录，此次目击事件在描述和移动轨迹上，与两周前博尔杜克少校在同一大片区域报告的目击事件几乎完全吻合。

**物体描述：** 对物体的描述存在显著差异。汽车乘员看到的火球被描述为圆形、白色且持续发光。据估计，其亮度是行星的三倍，大小约为满月的十五分之一。

静止观察者看到的物体被描述为通体发光，呈蓝绿色，轮廓类似于圆锥体的下半部分。它发出的光非常强烈，且亮度没有变化。与此次目击相关的间歇性光束后来被确认为是一种机械光源。

**调查/后续：** 在收到关于静止物体的报告后，一支三人小组穿上雪鞋进入该区域，调查是否存在潜在的着陆或近距离着陆事件。他们发现了一个自然的解释：当时该地正在进行伐木作业，现场有一台大型原木装载机和一辆18轮卡车。调查结论显示，这些卡车24小时作业，驾驶室上装有旋转灯。观察者所看到的“间歇性光束”被确定为装载机吊臂经过驾驶室上方时产生的。关于汽车乘员报告的火球，官方文件上的一份手写笔记写道：“火球，无需进一步行动。”

**Witnesses:** LAC JJP Berube (Radar Technician, Group 1, age 22)

**Date / Time:** December 28, 1967, at 0245Z (also recorded as 250245Z)

**Location:** Highway 54 / 54A, approximately 7 to 8 miles south of the CFS Mont Apica guardhouse, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On December 28, 1967, at 0245Z, LAC JJP Berube, a 22-year-old Radar Technician with two years and three months of service, was driving alone heading north on Highway 54A. The weather conditions were clear with no moon, visible stars, and negligible wind. While driving, the witness’s attention was drawn to a single bright light high in the sky at the 2 o'clock position. Over a duration of approximately 3 to 4 seconds, the object descended in an arc toward the 1 o'clock position. During this descent, the witness observed the object exhibit a distinct pattern of slowing down and re-accelerating. The object appeared to perform a gradual descent before seemingly landing. Following the object's disappearance from view, a beam of light was observed, which the witness described as being similar to a rotating searchlight on a control tower. This was the witness's first UFO sighting, and he noted that he did not believe in such phenomena prior to this event.

**Object:** The object was described as a luminous blue-green light. In terms of shape, it was characterized as resembling the bottom half of a cone. It was observed at an intermittent, relatively low altitude. The movement was described as a gradual, arcing descent characterized by a slowing down and subsequent re-acceleration. The duration of the sighting was brief, lasting approximately 3 to 4 seconds.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official documentation includes a formal sighting report and internal handwritten notes regarding the incident. The report notes that the witness was a trained Radar Technician, which added weight to the observation. Internal military commentary on the file states: "Most interesting, if we had time & means I'm sure that many of the UFO sightings could be explained. However, this does not readily explain the object & its movement as observed from the vehicle." Handwritten queries were made regarding whether any radar returns were captured at the time of the sighting. Ultimately, the military concluded that further investigation was not feasible or desired, noting that "further investigation is not believed to be possible."

**目击者：** JJP·贝鲁比（JJP Berube）空军一等兵（雷达技术员，第1组，22岁）

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月28日，0245Z（亦记录为250245Z）

**地点：** 54号/54A号公路，魁北克省蒙阿皮卡（CFS Mont Apica）警卫室以南约7至8英里处。

**目击经过：** 1967年12月28日0245Z，22岁的雷达技术员JJP·贝鲁比空军一等兵（服役两年零三个月）独自驾车沿54A号公路向北行驶。当时天气晴朗，无月光，星光可见，几乎无风。行驶途中，目击者的注意力被天空中2点钟方向的一道明亮光点所吸引。在约3至4秒的时间内，该物体呈弧线状向1点钟方向下降。在下降过程中，目击者观察到该物体表现出明显的减速和再次加速的规律。物体似乎在进行缓慢下降，随后看似着陆。在物体消失在视野中后，目击者观察到一道光束，他将其描述为类似于控制塔上的旋转探照灯。这是该目击者的首次UFO目击经历，他表示在此事件之前并不相信此类现象。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一道发光的蓝绿色光芒。形状上，它被描述为类似于圆锥体的下半部分。它出现在间歇性的、相对较低的高度。其运动轨迹被描述为一种缓慢的弧线下降，并伴有减速和随后的再次加速。目击持续时间很短，约为3至4秒。

**调查/后续：** 官方档案包括一份正式的目击报告以及关于该事件的内部手写记录。报告指出，目击者是一名训练有素的雷达技术员，这增加了其观察结果的分量。军方内部评论写道：“非常有趣，如果我们有时间和手段，我相信许多UFO目击事件都能得到解释。然而，这并不能轻易解释从车内观察到的该物体及其运动方式。”针对当时是否捕捉到任何雷达回波，军方进行了手写问询。最终，军方得出结论，认为进一步调查既不可行也不必要，并指出“认为进一步调查已无可能”。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Wendy Hanson, Mr. John Hanson, David Fay, Dennis Hentrian

**Date / Time:** August 29, 1966, at 9:30 PM MST (Hanson account); August 22, 1968, at 10:30 PM (Fay/Hentrian account)

**Location:** Dixonville, Alberta (specifically NW 31-87-23 W5, approximately 2 miles north of Dixonville for the 1968 sighting)

**Sighting:** 
The case file documents two distinct sightings reported in the Dixonville area. On August 29, 1966, at 9:30 PM MST, Wendy Hanson and Mr. John Hanson observed an object while standing in their yard. They described the object as moving at a high rate of speed, characterized by a counter-clockwise, rotating, and flashing motion.

Two years later, on August 22, 1968, at 10:30 PM, David Fay and Dennis Hentrian observed a "fireball" while located approximately 2 miles north of Dixonville (NW 31-87-23 W5). The weather conditions at the time of this second sighting were reported as clear. Fay and Hentrian observed the object moving from the West to the East, positioned high in the sky.

**Object:** 
The descriptions of the objects vary significantly between the two reports. The 1966 object observed by the Hansons was described as a silver, cylinder-shaped object resting within a saucer-like dish, featuring pulsing red lights. It was reported as silent and remained visible for 5 minutes before disappearing from view, even when tracked with binoculars.

The 1968 object observed by Fay and Hentrian was described as a round, red fireball. Unlike the 1966 sighting, this object was observed for a duration of 3 to 4 minutes. No sounds were reported in association with the 1968 fireball.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Both reports were processed by the RCMP. The 1966 report was filed by T.C. Cadieux of Peace River, Alberta, on August 30, 1966. The 1968 report was filed by J.C. Cadieux of Peace River, Alberta, on August 30, 1968. The 1968 documentation specifically noted the clear weather conditions at the time of the sighting.

***

*Note: While the provided case file headers grouped these under a single "Dixonville AB fireball" event title dated 1968-08-22, the internal documentation clearly distinguishes between two separate incidents occurring two years apart (1966 and 1968) involving different sets of witnesses and distinct object descriptions.*
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 温迪·汉森 (Wendy Hanson)、约翰·汉森先生 (Mr. John Hanson)、大卫·费伊 (David Fay)、丹尼斯·亨特里安 (Dennis Hentrian)

**日期 / 时间：** 1966年8月29日，晚上9:30（山区标准时间，汉森夫妇的陈述）；1968年8月22日，晚上10:30（费伊/亨特里安的陈述）

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省迪克森维尔 (Dixonville)（具体坐标为 NW 31-87-23 W5，1968年目击事件发生于迪克森维尔以北约2英里处）

**目击经过：**
该案卷记录了在迪克森维尔地区报告的两起不同目击事件。1966年8月29日晚上9:30（山区标准时间），温迪·汉森和约翰·汉森先生在自家院子里观察到了一个物体。他们描述该物体以极高的速度移动，并伴有逆时针旋转和闪烁的动作。

两年后的1968年8月22日晚上10:30，大卫·费伊和丹尼斯·亨特里安在迪克森维尔以北约2英里处（NW 31-87-23 W5）观察到了一个“火球”。据报告，第二次目击时的天气状况晴朗。费伊和亨特里安观察到该物体位于高空，由西向东移动。

**物体描述：**
两份报告对物体的描述存在显著差异。汉森夫妇在1966年观察到的物体被描述为一个银色的圆柱体，静置于一个碟状物中，并带有脉冲式的红光。据报告，该物体全程无声，可见时长为5分钟，即便使用双筒望远镜追踪，最终也消失在视野中。

费伊和亨特里安在1968年观察到的物体被描述为一个圆形的红色火球。与1966年的目击事件不同，该物体的观测时长为3到4分钟。报告称1968年的火球未伴随任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
两份报告均由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 处理。1966年的报告由阿尔伯塔省皮斯河镇 (Peace River) 的 T.C. 卡迪厄 (T.C. Cadieux) 于1966年8月30日提交。1968年的报告由阿尔伯塔省皮斯河镇的 J.C. 卡迪厄 (J.C. Cadieux) 于1968年8月30日提交。1968年的文档特别记录了目击时晴朗的天气状况。

***

*注：尽管提供的案卷标题将这些事件归类为1968年8月22日的单一“迪克森维尔火球”事件，但内部文档清楚地将其区分开来，指出这是两起相隔两年（1966年和1968年）发生的独立事件，涉及不同的目击者群体和截然不同的物体描述。*

**Witnesses:** Cst Luchak, L.R., Cst Maudsley, C., Cst Barter, and Cst Davidson, DC, all of RCMP Burnaby.

**Sighting:** On January 1, 1968, at 7:23 PM PST, the witnesses observed an object from the top of Burnaby Mountain, Burnaby, BC. The weather conditions were clear with a slight haze up to approximately 1000 feet and darkness.

**Object:** The object appeared as one red pulsating light, twice as bright as stars. It was first sighted just at the top of the haze above the horizon. The light moved in a vertical direction, taking approximately 10 minutes to rise three times its original altitude. The duration of the sighting was 10 to 12 minutes.

**Aftermath:** Moments before the object's light went out, it released what appeared to be a bright white molten material that burnt itself out as it fell toward the earth. This substance was emitted on three occasions at about three-second intervals. A full report was to follow from the Burnaby Detachment.

**Additional pages:** This incident is also documented on 1 other page of the FOIA release.
