**目击者：** 汉斯·韦塞尔（Hans Wessel）、帕蒂·格林（Patti Greene）、约翰·奥尔森（John Olsen）、威尔玛·奥尔森（Wilma Olsen）、乔治·豪夫妇（Mr. and Mrs. George Howe）、阿诺德·莫恩（Arnold Moen）、阿特·赫林（Art Helin）、卡罗尔·赫林（Carol Helin）、萨克斯·杜多沃德（Sax Dudoward）、吉尔·卢西亚（Jill Lussiar）、安妮特·卢西亚（Annette Lussiar）、警员 K.E. 艾伦（Cst. K.E. Allen）、警员 D.W. 布朗（Cst. D.W. Brown）、警员 D.D. 法雷尔（Cst. D.D. Ferrel）、辅助警员 M. 麦克劳德（Aux. Cst. M. McLeod）、辅助警员 A. 斯蒂尔（Aux. Cst. A. Steel）以及一名未透露姓名的士兵。

**日期/时间：** 1968年7月27日（午夜过后不久）及1968年7月28日（晚上11:20）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省鲁珀特王子港（包括富尔顿街、海斯山以及公园边汽车旅馆/拖车营地）。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月的最后一个周末，鲁珀特王子港发生了一系列目击事件。7月27日午夜过后不久，包括汉斯·韦塞尔、约翰·奥尔森、赫林夫妇、豪夫妇、阿诺德·莫恩及一名士兵在内的多名目击者，在海斯山和富尔顿街附近观察到一个物体。交通部（DOT）员工韦塞尔报告称，该物体在山上盘旋了20至30秒，随后下降并消失。其他目击者描述该物体从东南方向靠近，盘旋长达30分钟，并无声地缓慢移动。一些观察者注意到该物体是逆风移动的。

7月28日晚上11:20，第二次重大目击事件发生在公园边汽车旅馆/拖车营地。警员 K.E. 艾伦、D.W. 布朗、D.D. 法雷尔，辅助警员 M. 麦克劳德、A. 斯蒂尔以及多位平民目击了此次事件。目击者报告称，该物体向西缓慢移动了2至3分钟，喷射出火花，随后爆发出更大规模的火花并消失。帕蒂·格林和另外七名女孩也在周六报告了目击情况，描述为一个带有红点的明亮橙色光团。一些目击者报告看到13个较小的物体从一个较大的物体中分离出来，而另一些人则推测周日的目击事件可能是一个带有照明弹的气象气球。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被一致描述为圆形且呈橙色，但亮度各异；有人将其强度比作七八盏路灯。一名目击者注意到物体顶部有一个圆顶状结构。这些物体飞行时保持静默，移动缓慢，并表现出独特的飞行模式：一些以估计1,800至4,300英尺的高度向西北或东北方向飞行，另一些则以高速垂直向上冲去。目击持续时间从20秒到30分钟不等，其中7月28日的物体被特别指出在解体前喷射出了火花。

**调查/后续：** 鲁珀特王子港皇家骑警（RCMP）进行了广泛的访谈，并将报告提交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心。官方后续调查包括核查气象数据（记录显示当时天空多云）以及收集目击者证词。汉斯·韦塞尔曾试图拍摄该物体，但因缺乏设备未能成功。这些目击事件引发了公众的广泛讨论，一些目击者（如乔治·豪）主动站出来讲述了此前未曾公开的经历。皇家骑警表示，后续将会有来自鲁珀特王子港分局的更多报告。

**Witnesses:** Cst. H. Richard (Shediac Town Police), several local residents of Shediac, N.B., and several unknown persons.

**Date / Time:** July 6, 1968, at approximately 9:30 P.M. (Note: Page 195 lists the date as July 8, while Page 197 lists the date as July 6; the official report transmitted to the RCMP and NRC confirms the July 6 date).

**Location:** Shediac, New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On the evening of July 6, 1968, under clear sky conditions, Cst. H. Richard of the Shediac Town Police, along with several local residents and other unknown persons, observed an unidentified object in the northeast sky. Cst. Richard monitored the object for approximately 15 minutes using binoculars. During this time, the object remained stationary at an estimated altitude of between 2,000 and 10,000 feet (specifically cited as 7,000 feet in the formal report). Following the 15-minute observation period, the object performed a rapid vertical ascent, disappearing from view in approximately one minute.

**Object:** The object was described as egg-shaped. Its surface featured a distinct pattern consisting of three lengthwise (vertical) bars and one horizontal bar. The bars were colored yellow and blue, while the remainder of the object’s body was white. The object did not display any lights.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting generated significant public interest, with the Department of Transport Meteorology Centre at Moncton Airport reporting that they received numerous calls from the public regarding the object. Airport tower staff also observed the object through binoculars. Based on their observations, the Meteorology Centre suggested that the object was a weather balloon that had drifted into the area from Portland or Caribou, Maine, U.S.A., concluding that it was "almost definitely" a weather balloon. The official report of the incident was transmitted via telecommunications to the RCMP Commissioner in Ottawa and the Commanding Officer of J Division in Fredericton, N.B. A copy of the report was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) on July 10, 1968.

**目击者：** H. 理查德警官（谢迪亚克镇警察局）、几位谢迪亚克当地居民以及几名身份不明的人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月6日，大约晚上9:30。（注：第195页将日期列为7月8日，而第197页列为7月6日；提交给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）和国家研究委员会（NRC）的正式报告确认日期为7月6日。）

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省，谢迪亚克。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月6日晚，在天空晴朗的条件下，谢迪亚克镇警察局的 H. 理查德警官与几位当地居民及其他不明身份者，在东北方天空中观察到一个不明物体。理查德警官使用双筒望远镜对该物体进行了约15分钟的监测。在此期间，该物体保持静止，估计高度在2,000至10,000英尺之间（正式报告中具体标注为7,000英尺）。在15分钟的观察结束后，该物体进行了快速的垂直上升，并在约一分钟内消失在视野中。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为蛋形。其表面具有独特的图案，由三条纵向（垂直）条纹和一条横向条纹组成。条纹呈黄色和蓝色，而物体其余部分为白色。该物体未显示任何灯光。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件引起了公众的极大关注，蒙克顿机场交通部气象中心报告称，他们接到了大量关于该物体的公众来电。机场塔台工作人员也通过双筒望远镜观察到了该物体。根据他们的观察，气象中心推测该物体是从美国缅因州波特兰或卡里布漂流至此的气象气球，并得出结论认为它“几乎可以肯定”是气象气球。该事件的正式报告通过电信传达给了渥太华的加拿大皇家骑警专员以及新不伦瑞克省弗雷德里克顿的 J 分部指挥官。报告副本随后于1968年7月10日被转发给国家研究委员会（NRC）。

**Witnesses:** Cst. B. Richard (Shediac Town Police), Mrs. Dorothy Goguen (wife of the Chief of Police), Mrs. Bernard Richard, Mr. and Mrs. Omer Goguen, and several other unnamed persons.

**Date / Time:** July 8, 1968 (with one report erroneously citing July 5, 1968), at approximately 9:30 P.M.

**Location:** Shediac, West County, New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On the evening of July 8, 1968, at approximately 9:30 P.M., a UFO sighting occurred in the north-east sky over Shediac, N.B. The event was witnessed by Cst. B. Richard of the Shediac Town Police, who observed the object for 15 minutes using binoculars. Other witnesses present included Mrs. Dorothy Goguen (wife of the Chief of Police), Mrs. Bernard Richard, Mr. and Mrs. Omer Goguen, and several other unidentified individuals. The sky was reported as clear during the observation. The object remained stationary for the duration of the sighting at an estimated altitude ranging between 2,000 and 10,000 feet (with specific reports citing 7,000 feet). Following the 15-minute observation period, the object disappeared by ascending vertically at a high rate of speed, completing its departure in approximately one minute.

**Object:** The object was described as egg-shaped. Its surface featured a distinct pattern consisting of three vertical bars and one horizontal bar. The bars were colored yellow and blue, while the remainder of the object appeared white. The object displayed no lights and made no audible sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented and filed by the RCMP Moncton Sub-Division. On July 9, 1968, the RCMP contacted the Department of Transport Meteorology Centre at the Moncton Airport to investigate potential explanations. The Meteorology Centre reported receiving numerous calls from the public regarding the object. While the Centre suggested that the planet Venus might be visible in the north-west sky, they acknowledged that the witnesses had reported the object in the north-east. Staff at the airport tower observed the object through binoculars and concluded that it was a weather balloon. They hypothesized that the object originated from Portland or Caribou, Maine, U.S.A., noting that such balloons are routinely released four times daily. Despite the discrepancy in the date recorded on one of the file pages (July 5 vs. July 8), the consistent description of the object and the 15-minute duration confirms that all reports refer to the same event.

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月8日，晚上约9:30（有一份报告错误地记录为1968年7月5日）。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省西县谢迪亚克。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月8日晚约9:30，新不伦瑞克省谢迪亚克东北方向的天空中出现了不明飞行物（UFO）。谢迪亚克镇警察局的B. 理查德警官目击了这一事件，并使用双筒望远镜对该物体进行了长达15分钟的观察。其他在场的目击者包括多萝西·戈根夫人（警察局长夫人）、伯纳德·理查德夫人、奥默·戈根夫妇以及其他几位身份不明的人士。据报告，观测期间天空晴朗。该物体在目击期间保持静止，估计高度在2,000至10,000英尺之间（具体报告称约为7,000英尺）。在15分钟的观察结束后，该物体以极高的速度垂直上升并消失，整个离开过程大约持续了一分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为蛋形。其表面具有独特的图案，由三条垂直条纹和一条水平条纹组成。条纹呈黄色和蓝色，而物体的其余部分呈白色。该物体没有显示任何灯光，也没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）蒙克顿分部记录并归档。1968年7月9日，加拿大皇家骑警联系了蒙克顿机场的交通部气象中心，以调查可能的解释。气象中心报告称，他们接到了大量公众关于该物体的来电。虽然中心建议称金星可能在西北天空可见，但他们承认目击者报告的物体位于东北方向。机场塔台的工作人员通过双筒望远镜观察了该物体，并断定它是一个气象气球。他们推测该物体可能来自美国缅因州的波特兰或卡里布，并指出此类气球通常每天释放四次。尽管其中一份档案页上的日期存在差异（7月5日与7月8日），但对物体描述的一致性以及15分钟的持续时间证实，所有报告均指向同一事件。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. H.D. WATTS, Cpl. A.A. MATHESON, Cst. S. CLARK, Mr. John DOUGLAS (Geological Survey of Canada), Cpl. D.J.L. WEIN, and various local residents of Sydney Mines (including a neighbor from Diggin St.).

**Date / Time:** July 12, 1968; sightings reported at approximately 3:00 P.M. and 8:00 P.M.

**Location:** Sydney Mines, Nova Scotia (specifically near Tobin Road and Diggin St.).

**Sighting:** The event involved reports of an aerial object observed over Sydney Mines. Accounts vary slightly regarding the time, with some reports citing 3:00 P.M. and others 8:00 P.M. Witnesses described a round, white light, similar in appearance to a car headlight, traveling from east to west. The object was seen descending from an unknown altitude toward the ground. One witness noted the object trailing flames as it moved from the direction of Sydney Harbour. The sighting lasted approximately 15 seconds. As the object passed over or struck power lines, it caused a loud bang, a blue flash, and the emission of blue smoke. The impact resulted in a momentary power failure at a local substation and caused a grass fire in a circular area approximately three feet in diameter. Local residents extinguished the fire.

**Object:** The object was described as a round, headlight-sized white light. It emitted a roaring noise and trailed flames as it descended. Upon impact with the power lines and ground, it left behind a heavy, rock-like substance (described as the size of an orange, or approximately three inches long by two inches wide).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP (North Sydney Detachment) conducted an investigation, noting that Eastern Light and Power Company inspected the power lines, finding them pitted and shiny for a length of 10 to 20 feet from the impact point. Cst. H.D. WATTS, Cpl. A.A. MATHESON, and Cst. S. CLARK were involved in the initial response. Physical evidence, including the rock-like object, samples of the burnt grass, and dirt, were collected. These materials were forwarded to Mr. John DOUGLAS of the Geological Survey of Canada for analysis. Following the investigation, Mr. Douglas determined the object was a meteorite rather than a U.F.O. The file was subsequently closed by Cpl. D.J.L. WEIN of the North Sydney Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** H.D. 瓦茨警员 (Cst. H.D. WATTS)、A.A. 马西森下士 (Cpl. A.A. MATHESON)、S. 克拉克警员 (Cst. S. CLARK)、约翰·道格拉斯先生 (Mr. John DOUGLAS，加拿大地质调查局)、D.J.L. 温下士 (Cpl. D.J.L. WEIN)，以及悉尼矿区 (Sydney Mines) 的多位当地居民（包括一名来自迪金街 (Diggin St.) 的邻居）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月12日；目击报告分别出现在下午3:00左右和晚上8:00左右。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省悉尼矿区（具体位于托宾路 (Tobin Road) 和迪金街附近）。

**目击经过：** 该事件涉及多起关于悉尼矿区上空出现不明飞行物的报告。关于时间的描述略有出入，部分报告称在下午3:00，另一些则称在晚上8:00。目击者描述称，一个圆形的白光物体（外观类似于汽车前灯）由东向西移动。该物体从未知高度向地面降落。一名目击者指出，该物体从悉尼港方向移动时尾部拖着火焰。目击过程持续了约15秒。当物体经过或撞击电线时，引发了巨大的响声、蓝色闪光并冒出蓝色烟雾。撞击导致当地变电站瞬间断电，并在地面上造成了一个直径约三英尺的圆形草地火灾。当地居民随后将火扑灭。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个圆形、前灯大小的白光。它在下降时发出轰鸣声并拖着火焰。在撞击电线并坠地后，留下了一种沉重的、类似岩石的物质（据描述大小如橙子，长约三英寸，宽约两英寸）。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（北悉尼分局）进行了调查，指出东部电力公司 (Eastern Light and Power Company) 对电线进行了检查，发现从撞击点起，长达10至20英尺的电线表面出现了凹痕且呈现光亮状。H.D. 瓦茨警员、A.A. 马西森下士和S. 克拉克警员参与了初步响应。包括岩石状物体、烧焦的草样和泥土在内的物理证据被收集起来，并转交给加拿大地质调查局的约翰·道格拉斯先生进行分析。调查结束后，道格拉斯先生认定该物体为陨石而非不明飞行物。该档案随后由北悉尼分局的D.J.L. 温下士结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Jody Knipple, Howard (bus driver), Vcernia (Vigenia) Stridfel, and Marcella.

**Date / Time:** July 13, 1978; sighting occurred at approximately 0430Z; reported by Jody Knipple’s father at 1452Z (with a secondary notation of 145Z).

**Location:** Argyle Street, near Regent Park, Regina, Saskatchewan (while returning from the North Gate Mall).

**Sighting:** On July 13, 1978, at approximately 0430Z, a group of passengers aboard a Tele-A-Bus observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The bus driver, identified as Howard, stopped the vehicle and extinguished the bus lights to allow the occupants—Jody Knipple, Vcernia (also recorded as Vigenia) Stridfel, and Marcella—to exit and observe the object more clearly. The witnesses watched the object for a total duration of approximately ten minutes. The sighting was later reported to authorities by Jody Knipple’s father, who emphasized that his daughter was very certain of her observations and maintained that the event was "definitely out of the ordinary."

**Object:** The object was described as dome-shaped with two distinct ends. Its color was noted as red on the top portion and a "dirty chrome" color on the remainder of the craft. The structure featured square windows along its sides. Regarding movement, the object exhibited erratic, jerky motions, traveling sideways, up and down, and back and forth. During its departure, the object displayed a unique behavior: it disappeared while trailing a plume of pure black smoke, only to return shortly thereafter. Accounts vary slightly regarding the speed of this departure, with reports citing either a 3-second or 15-second disappearance time.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was formally reported at 1452Z by the father of witness Jody Knipple. The official record highlights the witness's high level of certainty regarding the sighting. While the provided documentation notes the specific details of the craft and the actions taken by the bus driver to facilitate the observation, there is no mention of further physical evidence or meteorological data beyond the witness testimonies provided in the case file.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. P. Pertson, Cst. G. Flake, and one unnamed local resident of Yellowknife.

**Date / Time:** July 15–16, 1968, at 12:20 AM. (Note: Reports vary between July 15 and July 16, likely due to the early morning hour).

**Location:** Yellowknife, Northwest Territories (near the Old Stope Hotel and the COMINCO mine).

**Sighting:** On July 15/16, 1968, at 12:20 AM, two RCMP officers, Cst. P. Pertson and Cst. G. Flake, were on patrol near the Old Stope Hotel when they observed a single object moving rapidly across the sky from south to north. The officers first noticed the object at an elevation of 45 degrees above the northern horizon; it traveled until it reached 10 degrees, at which point it disappeared near a cloud bank. The transit across the sky lasted approximately seven seconds. Simultaneously, a local resident near the COMINCO mine reported observing an identical object.

**Object:** The object appeared to be disintegrating and burning in the air, with witnesses describing it as resembling a fireworks display. It left a distinct, double vapour trail along its flight path that remained visible in the sky for 50 minutes after the sighting. While the observers estimated the object’s altitude to be approximately 50,000 feet, the Department of Transport (DOT) noted that cloud cover in the area was at 10,000 feet, suggesting the object may have been at a lower altitude than initially estimated.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally reported by the Yellowknife RCMP Detachment. Following the event, the Department of Transport (DOT) was contacted and confirmed that there were no missing aircraft in the area at the time of the sighting. The report was subsequently reviewed by the Officer Commanding (O.C.) of the Fort Smith Sub-Division, who noted that the report had been submitted late. No further official explanation for the object was provided.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** P. 珀森警官 (Cst. P. Pertson)、G. 弗莱克警官 (Cst. G. Flake) 以及一名未具名的耶洛奈夫当地居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月15日至16日，凌晨12:20。（注：由于时间处于凌晨，报告日期在7月15日和16日之间存在差异）。

**地点：** 西北地区耶洛奈夫（靠近老斯托普酒店 (Old Stope Hotel) 和科明科 (COMINCO) 矿区）。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月15日/16日凌晨12:20，两名加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警官 P. 珀森和 G. 弗莱克在老斯托普酒店附近巡逻时，观察到一个物体正从南向北在天空中快速移动。警官们最初在北地平线上方45度角处发现了该物体；它持续飞行直至降至10度角，随后在云层附近消失。整个穿越天空的过程持续了约七秒钟。与此同时，科明科矿区附近的一名当地居民也报告观察到了一个相同的物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体看起来像是在空中解体并燃烧，目击者将其描述为类似于烟花表演。它在飞行路径上留下了明显的双重尾迹，在目击事件发生后，这些尾迹在天空中持续可见了50分钟。虽然观察者估计该物体的高度约为50,000英尺，但交通部 (DOT) 指出，该地区的云层高度为10,000英尺，这表明该物体的实际高度可能比最初估计的要低。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件由耶洛奈夫加拿大皇家骑警分队正式报告。事件发生后，交通部 (DOT) 获悉并确认当时该地区没有失踪的飞机。该报告随后由史密斯堡 (Fort Smith) 分区的指挥官 (O.C.) 进行审查，指挥官指出该报告提交时间较晚。此后，官方未再对该物体提供进一步的解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Three local women, a civilian male (Forestry employee), Miss [redacted], [redacted], three additional civilians, and unspecified observers in Fort Smith and Fort Resolution, NWT.

**Date / Time:** July 16, 1968, between 12:00 a.m. and 1:00 a.m.

**Location:** Fort Smith and Fort Resolution, Northwest Territories.

**Sighting:** Multiple sightings occurred over the course of one hour. At 12:15 a.m., three women in a parked vehicle observed an object traveling rapidly in a rising arc from South to North. Between 12:30 a.m. and 1:00 a.m., several other groups of witnesses observed an object (or objects) moving in a straight line from the southwest toward the northeast, or in a westerly direction. Observers in Fort Resolution estimated the altitude between 7,000 and 10,000 feet. While most witnesses reported silence, one witness reported a sound like two shots or a car backfire after the object entered the clouds. Witnesses were noted by the RCMP to be sober, reliable, and familiar with aircraft. One witness compared the object to a B-61 or Matador pilotless aircraft, noting the primary difference was the intense light at the rear.

**Object:** Descriptions varied, likely due to viewing angles or multiple objects. Shapes reported included round, oval, disc-like, and elongated/pointed (rocket-shaped). The object was described as having a dark, oval front end and a bright, luminous light at the rear, colored white, blue, red, green, and purple. It emitted sparks, smoke (described as "curly" or like fireworks), and a vapor trail up to one mile long. The light was compared to an acetylene torch. It moved faster than a jet, with durations ranging from 4–5 seconds to 60 seconds. Some witnesses noted lights that resembled windows.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews and concluded the witnesses were credible. Sketches were obtained from observers depicting disc-like and elongated, pointed shapes with trailing sparks and smoke. The Department of Transport (D.O.T.) Aeradio reported weather conditions as 1,200 ft. scattered cumulus and 12,000 ft. alto stratus. A Pacific Western Airlines Convair flight passed over earlier at 9:10 p.m., but witnesses insisted the UFO was larger and lower. The case was documented via RCMP reports, hand-drawn sketches, and internal correspondence, with some portions later redacted under the Access to Information Act.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 三名当地女性、一名男性平民（林业局员工）、[已涂黑]小姐、[已涂黑]、三名其他平民，以及在西北地区史密斯堡（Fort Smith）和雷索卢申堡（Fort Resolution）的其他未具名观察者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月16日，凌晨12:00至1:00之间。

**地点：** 西北地区，史密斯堡和雷索卢申堡。

**目击经过：** 在一小时内发生了多次目击事件。凌晨12:15，三名坐在停放车辆内的女性观察到一个物体以弧线从南向北快速升起。凌晨12:30至1:00之间，其他几组目击者观察到一个（或多个）物体从西南向东北方向，或向西移动。雷索卢申堡的观察者估计其高度在7,000至10,000英尺之间。虽然大多数目击者称现场寂静无声，但有一名目击者报告称，在物体进入云层后，听到了类似两声枪响或汽车回火的声音。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）指出，目击者均神志清醒、可靠，且熟悉飞行器。一名目击者将该物体比作B-61或“斗牛士”（Matador）无人驾驶飞机，并指出其主要区别在于尾部有强烈的亮光。

**物体描述：** 描述各不相同，这可能是由于观察角度不同或存在多个物体所致。报告的形状包括圆形、椭圆形、盘状以及细长/尖头状（火箭形）。该物体被描述为前端呈深色椭圆形，尾部带有明亮的强光，颜色包括白色、蓝色、红色、绿色和紫色。它会喷射火花、烟雾（被描述为“卷曲状”或类似烟花），并留下一条长达一英里的尾迹。其光芒被比作乙炔焊炬。它的移动速度比喷气式飞机快，持续时间从4-5秒到60秒不等。一些目击者注意到其上有类似窗户的灯光。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警进行了访谈，并得出结论认为目击者是可信的。警方从观察者处获得了草图，描绘了带有拖曳火花和烟雾的盘状及细长尖头形状。交通部（D.O.T.）航空无线电部门报告称，当时的天气状况为1,200英尺处有零散积云，12,000英尺处有高层云。太平洋西部航空公司（Pacific Western Airlines）的一架康维尔（Convair）客机曾于当晚9:10飞过，但目击者坚称该不明飞行物更大且飞行高度更低。此案通过加拿大皇家骑警报告、手绘草图和内部通信进行了记录，部分内容后来根据《信息获取法》进行了涂黑处理。

**Witnesses:** Lyette Bastien, Anne Robillard, and Mrs./Mme Page. The two principal letter-writers (Bastien and Robillard) both reside at C.P. 122, Saint-Jovite, Quebec.

**Date / Time:** Sighting on the morning of 5-6 July 1968, between approximately 1:30 and 2:00 A.M. Witness letters were composed on 5 July 1968 in both French and English versions. CFS La Macaza forwarded the letters to the Chief of the Defence Staff on 10 July 1968. NRC Peter M. Millman replied to both witnesses on 1 August 1968. File reference N68/085.

**Location:** Saint-Jovite, Quebec, Canada. The witnesses observed the object from a fifth-storey balcony in the town centre.

**Sighting:** In the early hours of the morning, Lyette Bastien and her friend (Anne Robillard) observed a bright, luminous, star-like object in the sky over Saint-Jovite. Mme Page joined the witnesses, and at one point left to fetch binoculars; during her brief absence the object stopped, appeared to dim, and ultimately disappeared. Anne Robillard's account adds that her aunt also briefly came outside and observed the UFO before going back in for binoculars; the object never returned. Both witnesses described the object as "unlike a falling star or a satellite" — point-like but with motion that could not be explained by either. A radio bulletin shortly afterward referenced a parallel UFO sighting in Joliette, mentioned in the Bastien letter postscript dated Saturday 6 July 1968.

**Object:** A bright, luminous, star-like point of light, motionless or slow-moving in the sky, eventually fading and disappearing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Lt.-Col. P.J. Roy, Commanding Officer of CFS La Macaza, forwarded both witness letters to the Chief of the Defence Staff in Ottawa via cover memo dated 10 July 1968. Peter M. Millman of the NRC's Meteor Centre / Astrophysical Branch sent personal reply letters dated 1 August 1968 to both Anne Robillard and Lyette Bastien (file marked N68/085), advising that "the object was undoubtedly a satellite." The case file was retained at NRC.

**File-structure note:** Prior indexing fragmented this single packet into six separate events ("St-Jovite QC sighting", "Bright luminous object letter", "Joliette sighting", "St Boniface letter", "Handwritten UFO note", and a partial assignment of pp.51-53 to the unrelated O'Chiese Alberta Logan case). gpt-5.5 vision audit of pp.51-60 confirmed all ten pages belong to this one Saint-Jovite multi-witness wave.

**Witnesses:** Lauchlin MacKinnon (45), Margaret MacKinnon (20), John MacKinnon (22), Rose MacKinnon (24), other unnamed family members, and Cst. C.M. Campbell of the RCMP Inverness Detachment.

**Date / Time:** July 20, 1968, 11:15 PM to July 21, 1968, 12:30 AM.

**Location:** Deepdale, Inverness County, Nova Scotia (MacKinnon farm).

**Sighting:** On the night of July 20, 1968, the MacKinnon family observed two unidentified aerial phenomena. One object was positioned on the horizon, while a second object was observed directly above the MacKinnon farm. The sighting lasted for approximately one hour and fifteen minutes. According to the family, the light emitted from the object directly overhead was intense enough to illuminate the roof of their barn. A second object, located to the east of the farm, was observed illuminating a nearby field before it disappeared. 

Cst. C.M. Campbell of the RCMP Inverness Detachment arrived at the scene during the event. He personally observed a bright object at a high altitude several miles away, which remained stationary for ten minutes. The RCMP officer interviewed the family and noted that they appeared sincere and were not under the influence of alcohol, leading him to conclude that the sighting was quite reliable.

**Object:** The objects were described as round, brilliant, and silent. They displayed shifting layers of red, green, and white colors. Estimates placed the objects at an altitude between 8,000 and 10,000 feet. Regarding movement, the objects were initially stationary; they later moved in a northerly direction at a high rate of speed before stopping again. The objects eventually disappeared at approximately 12:30 AM on July 21, 1968, departing at a "terrific rate of speed." Lauchlin MacKinnon noted that the appearance of these objects was consistent with a saucer-shaped object he had observed near his farm on a previous occasion.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by Cst. C.M. Campbell and filed by the RCMP Sydney Subdivision. The weather at the time of the sighting was reported as clear. Cst. Campbell conducted follow-up inquiries at other farms in the immediate area to determine if there were additional witnesses; however, all inquiries yielded negative results, and no other reports were received regarding the event.

**目击经过：** 1968年7月20日晚，麦金农一家观察到了两个不明空中现象。其中一个物体位于地平线上，另一个则位于麦金农农场的正上方。目击过程持续了约一小时十五分钟。据该家庭描述，正上方物体发出的光芒极其强烈，足以照亮他们谷仓的屋顶。另一个位于农场东侧的物体在消失前曾照亮了附近的一片田地。

加拿大皇家骑警因弗内斯分局的C.M.坎贝尔警官在事件期间抵达现场。他亲眼目睹了数英里外高空处有一个明亮的物体，该物体保持静止状态长达十分钟。坎贝尔警官对该家庭进行了访谈，并指出他们看起来非常真诚，且未受酒精影响，这使他得出结论：此次目击事件相当可靠。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为圆形、光芒四射且无声。它们呈现出红色、绿色和白色交替变换的层次。据估计，这些物体的高度在8,000至10,000英尺之间。在移动方面，物体起初处于静止状态；随后以极高的速度向北移动，之后再次停下。这些物体最终于1968年7月21日凌晨12:30左右消失，离开时速度“极快”。劳克林·麦金农指出，这些物体的外观与他之前在农场附近观察到的碟状物体一致。

**调查/后续：** 调查由C.M.坎贝尔警官进行，并由加拿大皇家骑警悉尼分区归档。据报告，目击时的天气状况晴朗。坎贝尔警官对附近地区的其他农场进行了后续询问，以确定是否有其他目击者；然而，所有询问均无结果，且未收到有关该事件的其他报告。

**Witnesses:** Captain A. Schulte.

**Sighting:** The report describes an observation made on July 24, 1968, at 1625Z. The weather conditions were clear with broken cumulus and cirrus clouds.

At approximately 9:30 p.m., while driving near Belliveau’s upholstery shop, the witnesses observed an unidentified object appearing from behind the shop. Because the witnesses were inside a moving car with the windows closed, no sound was heard.

**Object:** The object was described as being similar in both shape and size to the top of a small car. It exhibited a distinct bluish-white color. Regarding its movement, the object was observed at a "fast drift" in a north-westerly direction. Its altitude was recorded as 50 degrees at the time of the initial sighting, descending to 40 degrees by the time it was last seen.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally reported to the National Research Council of Canada. Documentation includes a report filed under section "10. Other information and narrative report," which lists a return address for Professor R. H. MacNeill of Acadia University in Wolfville, N.S., suggesting his involvement in the collection or forwarding of the report. No further official investigation results or atmospheric explanations were provided in the available documentation.

**目击经过：** 1968年7月25日晚，弗雷德和莉娜（雷娜）·格雷厄姆夫妇在晴朗的天气下驱车前往沃尔夫维尔。晚上9:30左右，当车行驶至贝利沃装潢店附近时，目击者看到一个不明物体从该店后方出现。据描述，当时目击者正驾车上坡，他们在越过坡顶时首次发现了该物体。当目击者到达坡顶时，该物体已消失不见。据记录，整个目击过程持续了1/4到1/2分钟。由于目击者当时身处车窗紧闭的行驶车辆内，因此未听到任何声音。

**Witnesses:** Irene L. Logan, Mr. M. Braithwaite, Mrs. M. Braithwaite, Mrs. David Nance.

**Date / Time:** July 30, 1968, at 11:00 PM (Logan sighting); July 31, 1968, at 0815 GMT (Braithwaite/Nance sighting).

**Location:** O’Chiese / Codner area, Alberta (Logan); Red Deer, Alberta (Braithwaite/Nance).

**Sighting:** 
On the night of July 30, 1968, at 11:00 PM, Irene L. Logan was driving in extreme darkness approximately 1/2 mile north of Codner/O’Chiese, Alberta. She initially observed a light in the sky, which she mistook for an airplane. The object suddenly appeared directly in front of her vehicle at approximately the height of the windshield. The object proceeded to circle her car four or five times at a very high speed. Each time the object passed the windshield, its tail made contact with the vehicle, producing a distinct sound described as the crack of a whip. Following these maneuvers, the object departed vertically at a high rate of speed. Mrs. Logan, noted as a non-drinker, was reported to be extremely upset by the encounter.

Separately, on July 31, 1968, at 0815 GMT, Mr. and Mrs. M. Braithwaite and Mrs. David Nance observed an object over the city of Red Deer, Alberta. The witnesses reported the object traveling in an upward easterly direction. The duration of this sighting was approximately three minutes under cloudy weather conditions.

**Object:** 
The object observed by Irene L. Logan was described as a brilliant red disc, resembling two pie plates joined together. It measured approximately 4–5 feet in diameter and 1–3 feet in depth. It featured a 3–4 foot long, grey, rope-like tail. 

The object observed by the Braithwaites and Mrs. Nance was described as a bright red light, approximately three times the size of a star.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP Red Deer sub-division handled the initial report regarding Irene L. Logan. Due to the nature of the incident, the report was forwarded to authorities in Ottawa, CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters), and the NRC (National Research Council) Meteor Centre for further advice and investigation. No further information was provided regarding the sighting reported by the Braithwaites and Mrs. Nance.

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省奥奇斯 (O’Chiese) / 科德纳 (Codner) 地区（洛根）；阿尔伯塔省红鹿市 (Red Deer)（布雷斯韦特夫妇及南斯夫人）。

**目击经过：**
1968年7月30日晚上11:00，艾琳·L·洛根正驾车行驶在阿尔伯塔省科德纳/奥奇斯以北约半英里处，当时夜色极深。她起初观察到天空中有一个光点，误以为是飞机。该物体突然出现在她车辆的正前方，高度大约与挡风玻璃齐平。随后，该物体以极高的速度绕着她的车盘旋了四到五圈。每当物体经过挡风玻璃时，它的尾部都会接触到车辆，发出一种类似于鞭子抽打的清脆声响。完成这些动作后，该物体以极高的速度垂直升空离去。据记录，洛根夫人从不饮酒，且在遭遇此事后情绪极度不安。

另一起事件中，1968年7月31日格林威治标准时间08:15，M·布雷斯韦特夫妇和大卫·南斯夫人在阿尔伯塔省红鹿市上空观察到了一个物体。目击者称该物体正向东上方飞行。在多云的天气条件下，此次目击持续了约三分钟。

**物体描述：**
艾琳·L·洛根观察到的物体被描述为一个明亮的红色圆盘，看起来像两个扣在一起的派盘。其直径约为4至5英尺，厚度约为1至3英尺。它带有一条3至4英尺长、灰色的绳状尾巴。

布雷斯韦特夫妇和南斯夫人观察到的物体被描述为一个明亮的红光，大小约为恒星的三倍。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 红鹿市分局处理了关于艾琳·L·洛根的初步报告。由于事件的性质，该报告被转交给渥太华当局、加拿大武装部队总部 (CANFORCEHED) 以及加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心，以寻求进一步的建议和调查。关于布雷斯韦特夫妇和南斯夫人报告的目击事件，未提供进一步信息。

**Witnesses:** One female civilian residing in Rocky Mountain House, Alberta.

**Date / Time:** July 30, 1968, at 11:00 PM.

**Location:** One-half mile north of Codner, Alberta (driving south).

**Sighting:** On the night of July 30, 1968, the witness was driving south in extreme darkness when she observed a light in the sky, which she initially mistook for an airplane. Suddenly, the object appeared directly in front of her vehicle at approximately the height of the windshield. The object proceeded to circle the car four or five times at a very high rate of speed. During each pass, the object’s tail made physical contact with the vehicle, producing a sound described as the crack of a whip. Following these maneuvers, the object ascended straight upward at a high rate of speed. The entire sighting lasted approximately five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a brilliant red disc, resembling two pie plates joined together. It measured approximately 4–5 feet in diameter and 1–3 feet in depth. Attached to the object was a 3–4 foot long, grey, rope-like tail. The object exhibited rapid, circling movement and high-speed vertical acceleration.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation into the incident. The witness was noted to be a non-drinker and was described as being extremely upset by the encounter. Despite the witness's distress, character enquiries conducted by the RCMP included a statement from a friend who referred to the witness as a "silly woman." The RCMP performed follow-up enquiries with other individuals in the Codner area to determine if there were any additional sightings or corroborating evidence, but these efforts yielded no further information. Consequently, the RCMP file on the matter was closed.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** William Prochner, Kenneth Julius Prochner, Julius Prochner, and Mrs. Anton (Elizabeth) Eberts.

**Date / Time:** August 4, 1968, at approximately 4:00 a.m. – 4:15 a.m.

**Location:** A farmyard 1.5 miles south of Qu'Appelle, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On the morning of August 4, 1968, Kenneth Prochner observed an illuminated object hovering approximately 200 feet above his house and alerted his father, William Prochner. The witnesses observed the object for 3–4 minutes from a distance of approximately 150 yards before eventually taking cover. Kenneth described the object moving in an oval or circular pattern, moving away, and returning. William observed the object hovering over a barn; he noted it was spinning and appeared quite large. Julius Prochner also witnessed the event, reporting that the object hovered over the barn for about one minute, stopped spinning, moved 50–100 feet to the southeast, hovered again, and then departed. Julius noted the object darted at right angles from point to point. Mrs. Elizabeth Eberts, located approximately 1/4 mile to the northeast, reported hearing a distinct whirling or whining noise at 4:00 a.m., though she did not see the object.

**Object:** The object was described as saucer-shaped, greyish-white in color, and approximately 20–30 feet in diameter. It hovered at an altitude of 80–100 feet. Observations regarding its illumination varied: some accounts described it as an illuminated, circular object with a "quite dull" light, while others noted a brightly lit bottom that revolved quickly. It produced no light rays and did not cast light onto the ground or the barn. While some witnesses reported no noise, others noted a whirling or whining sound. The object’s movement was characterized by spinning, hovering, and darting at right angles.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Indian Head detachment of the RCMP, including Cpl. R.D. Anderson and Cst. Cassidy of the Identification Section, investigated the site. They discovered circular marks in the pasture near the barn. While initial reports mentioned six marks, subsequent official documentation focused on four marks, each approximately 4.5 to 5 feet in diameter, which were clear of grass except for the center. Although the marks were initially thought to form a square pattern, measurements could not confirm a definitive geometric arrangement. These marks were eventually obliterated by rain. Cst. F.W. Pushka obtained formal statements from the witnesses on August 9, 1968. Meteorological data for the area confirmed cloudy conditions with thunder and lightning between 2:30 a.m. and 4:55 a.m. The RCMP concluded that the witnesses appeared sincere and reliable, though some internal reports listed the reliability of the incident as "unknown." No photographs or diagrams were preserved, as the physical marks were ultimately deemed of no significance.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威廉·普罗克纳 (William Prochner)、肯尼斯·朱利叶斯·普罗克纳 (Kenneth Julius Prochner)、朱利叶斯·普罗克纳 (Julius Prochner) 以及安东·埃伯茨夫人（伊丽莎白·埃伯茨，Mrs. Anton (Elizabeth) Eberts）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月4日，凌晨约4:00至4:15。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省夸佩尔 (Qu'Appelle) 以南1.5英里处的一个农场。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月4日清晨，肯尼斯·普罗克纳观察到一个发光物体悬停在他家上方约200英尺处，并提醒了他的父亲威廉·普罗克纳。目击者在约150码的距离外观察了该物体3至4分钟，随后躲避起来。肯尼斯描述该物体呈椭圆形或圆形运动，先是飞离，随后又返回。威廉观察到该物体悬停在谷仓上方；他注意到它在旋转，且体积相当大。朱利叶斯·普罗克纳也目击了这一事件，他报告称该物体在谷仓上方悬停了约一分钟，停止旋转，向东南方向移动了50至100英尺，再次悬停，然后离开。朱利叶斯指出，该物体在各点之间呈直角快速移动。位于东北方向约1/4英里处的伊丽莎白·埃伯茨夫人报告称，她在凌晨4:00听到了明显的旋转声或呜呜声，但她并未看到该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为碟状，呈灰白色，直径约20至30英尺。它悬停在80至100英尺的高度。关于其照明情况的描述各不相同：一些说法称其为一个发光的圆形物体，光线“相当暗淡”，而另一些说法则指出其底部有快速旋转的明亮灯光。它没有产生光束，也没有将光投射到地面或谷仓上。虽然一些目击者称没有听到声音，但另一些人注意到了旋转声或呜呜声。该物体的运动特征包括旋转、悬停以及呈直角快速移动。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 印第安角 (Indian Head) 分队，包括R.D. 安德森下士 (Cpl. R.D. Anderson) 和身份鉴定部门的卡西迪警官 (Cst. Cassidy) 对现场进行了调查。他们在谷仓附近的牧场发现了圆形痕迹。虽然最初的报告提到了六个痕迹，但随后的官方文件重点记录了四个痕迹，每个直径约4.5至5英尺，除中心外，痕迹内的草地均已消失。尽管最初认为这些痕迹形成了方形图案，但测量结果无法证实其具有明确的几何排列。这些痕迹最终被雨水冲刷消失。F.W. 普什卡警官 (Cst. F.W. Pushka) 于1968年8月9日获得了目击者的正式陈述。该地区的气象数据显示，凌晨2:30至4:55期间天气多云，伴有雷电。加拿大皇家骑警得出的结论是，目击者看起来真诚且可靠，尽管一些内部报告将该事件的可靠性列为“未知”。由于物理痕迹最终被认为没有意义，因此没有保留任何照片或图表。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michael St Amour (age 18), Mr. Romeo Thibault (also spelled Thibeault), Mrs. Romeo Thibault, Miss Thibault, and Mr. and Mrs. Ceie.

**Date / Time:** August 12, 1968, at 12Z (12:00 Zulu).

**Location:** Hull, Quebec (PQ).

**Sighting:** On August 12, 1968, at 12Z, a group of witnesses—including Mr. Michael St Amour, Mr. and Mrs. Romeo Thibault, Miss Thibault, and Mr. and Mrs. Ceie—observed an unidentified object in the sky over Hull, Quebec. The sky conditions at the time were reported as cloudy. The observation lasted for a duration of a few minutes. 

The witnesses provided varying perspectives on the object's trajectory and altitude. Some accounts described the object traveling from east to west, while others specified the path as moving from the direction of Ottawa toward Aylmer. Regarding altitude, reports differed, with estimates placed at approximately 90 degrees in one account and 65 degrees in another. The witnesses noted that the object was not positioned at a very high altitude.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape and red in color. There was a discrepancy in the reported size, with estimates ranging from 6 inches to 2 feet in diameter. The object moved in a distinct zig-zag course. Regarding speed, it was described as moving "very fast" in one account, while another report compared its speed to being slightly faster than a piston-engine aircraft. The object was observed to be silent, making no noise during the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation for this event was signed by Captain R. Hutton, DOPSO. Official notes indicate that the primary observer, Mr. Romeo Thibault, preferred to express himself in French during the investigation process. No further relevant information or physical evidence was recorded in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 迈克尔·圣阿穆尔先生（Michael St Amour，18岁）、罗密欧·蒂博先生（Romeo Thibault，拼写亦作Thibeault）、罗密欧·蒂博夫人、蒂博小姐，以及塞伊夫妇（Mr. and Mrs. Ceie）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月12日，12Z（祖鲁时间12:00）。

**地点：** 魁北克省赫尔（Hull, Quebec）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月12日12Z，一群目击者——包括迈克尔·圣阿穆尔先生、罗密欧·蒂博夫妇、蒂博小姐以及塞伊夫妇——在魁北克省赫尔上空观测到一个不明飞行物。据报告，当时天空多云。观测持续了几分钟。

目击者对该物体的飞行轨迹和高度的描述各不相同。一些描述称物体由东向西飞行，另一些则指出其路径是从渥太华方向朝艾尔默（Aylmer）移动。关于高度，报告存在差异，有的估计约为90度，有的则估计为65度。目击者指出，该物体所处的高度并不算太高。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，呈红色。关于其尺寸的报告存在出入，直径估计从6英寸到2英尺不等。该物体以独特的之字形路线移动。关于速度，一份报告称其移动“非常快”，而另一份报告则将其速度比作略快于活塞式发动机飞机。据观测，该物体在目击过程中保持静默，未发出任何声响。

**调查/后续：** 该事件的文档由DOPSO（作战参谋部行动处）的R·赫顿（R. Hutton）上尉签署。官方记录显示，主要观察者罗密欧·蒂博先生在调查过程中倾向于使用法语表达。提供的档案中未记录其他相关信息或实物证据。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** D. John Martell, Wendy Martell, John Mantle (Note: John Mantle is the resident of 17 Hillside Ave and likely the same individual as D. John Martell).

**Date / Time:** September 13, 1968; between 11:53 PM and 12:04 AM.

**Location:** 17 Hillside Ave, Wolfville, Nova Scotia (with observations directed toward the Cape Blomidon, Evangeline Beach, and Dyke Land areas).

**Sighting:** On the night of September 13, 1968, the witnesses observed two unidentified objects through a glass window under cloudy sky conditions. The first object was observed for approximately 30 seconds, while the second object was observed for approximately 1 minute. The first object moved in a south-east direction, then south-west, then back to south-east. The second object appeared in the same location as the first, traveled straight toward the observers, and then turned to follow the same path as the first object. As the second object departed, its light was observed to pulsate. One of the two objects was noted to hover for approximately 45 seconds.

**Object:** The objects were described as saucer-shaped, bright yellow with a reddish tint. While the distance made size estimation difficult, they were compared to the size of a penny held at a distance of approximately 5 miles. The altitude was recorded between 20 and 40 degrees above the horizon. The objects exhibited extreme acceleration, covering an estimated 2 to 3 miles in approximately 10 seconds. No sounds were heard during the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the National Research Council of Canada. A formal report form was utilized, which included a return address to Professor R. H. MacNeill at Acadia University, Wolfville, N.S. A handwritten sketch was included in the documentation, mapping the relative positions of Cape Blomidon, Evangeline Beach, and Dyke Land. The sketch utilizes arrows to trace the flight paths of both objects, marking the initial sighting point, the path of the first object, the path of the second object, and the final sighting point. The sketch also denotes a "Point A" and indicates a 60-degree angle relative to a north line. No final identification or official conclusion was recorded in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** D. 约翰·马特尔 (D. John Martell)、温迪·马特尔 (Wendy Martell)、约翰·曼特尔 (John Mantle)（注：约翰·曼特尔是希尔赛德大道17号的住户，很可能与 D. 约翰·马特尔为同一人）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月13日；晚上11:53至凌晨12:04之间。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省沃尔夫维尔市希尔赛德大道17号（观测方向指向布洛米顿角、伊万杰琳海滩及堤岸地区）。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月13日晚，目击者透过玻璃窗在多云的天气条件下观测到了两个不明物体。第一个物体观测时长约30秒，第二个物体观测时长约1分钟。第一个物体先向东南方向移动，随后转向西南，最后又回到东南方向。第二个物体出现在与第一个物体相同的位置，径直朝观测者方向飞来，随后转向并沿用了第一个物体的飞行路径。当第二个物体离开时，观察到其灯光呈脉冲式闪烁。其中一个物体被记录到悬停了约45秒。

**物体描述：** 物体被描述为碟状，呈亮黄色并带有微红色调。由于距离较远，难以估算其大小，目击者将其比作在约5英里距离处观察一枚硬币的大小。记录显示其高度位于地平线上方20至40度之间。这些物体表现出了极高的加速度，在约10秒内飞行了估计2至3英里的距离。整个目击过程中未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已报告给加拿大国家研究委员会。报告采用了正式表格，其中包括寄回给新斯科舍省沃尔夫维尔市阿卡迪亚大学 R. H. 麦克尼尔 (R. H. MacNeill) 教授的地址。文档中包含一份手绘草图，标绘了布洛米顿角、伊万杰琳海滩和堤岸地区的相对位置。草图使用箭头描绘了两个物体的飞行路径，标记了初始目击点、第一个物体的路径、第二个物体的路径以及最终目击点。草图还标注了一个“A点”，并指出了相对于北向线的60度角。所提供的文档中未记录最终的辨识结果或官方结论。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Richard A. Skewes (age 25), Mrs. Ann Marie Skewes (age 29), and Miss Gail Yemm (age 17).

**Date / Time:** August 15, 1968, at approximately 11:30 PM.

**Location:** Highway 4, between Truro and Springhill, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** While traveling by car from Halifax toward Springhill, the three witnesses observed a group of 5 to 7 unidentified flying objects. The encounter lasted between 5 and 10 minutes. The objects were observed hovering and circling the witnesses' vehicle in an "irrational manner" at an altitude of 30 to 100 feet above the ground and nearby trees. 

Mr. Richard Skewes, a former member of the Royal Canadian Navy with professional experience in identifying objects from a lookout position, stated he had never seen anything like these craft and expressed significant fear regarding how close they came to the vehicle. One object specifically approached the car at high speed, moved directly toward it, then "reared up" and passed over the vehicle. Despite the proximity, the witnesses reported that the objects made no engine or mechanical noise, even when the car windows were opened to listen. The witnesses were too frightened to stop the vehicle, fearing a collision.

**Object:** The objects were described as dark in color, approximately 20 feet in length and 6 to 10 feet in depth. One craft was noted to have white spots across its surface. They were covered in numerous brilliant yellow and green lights, which Mrs. Skewes compared to the brightness of a Christmas tree. One larger object featured a prominent yellow light at the front. Anne Marie Skewes remarked that the appearance of the craft reminded her of a World War II-era plane on display at the CNE grounds. The objects maneuvered with ease and appeared to hover and circle the area even as the witnesses drove away.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Mr. Skewes initially hesitated to report the sighting due to a fear of being perceived as mentally unstable, but after discussing the event with his wife and the babysitter (Miss Yemm) while passing through Toronto on August 17, he decided to proceed. Mrs. Skewes subsequently contacted the Department of National Defence (DND) and the RCMP. 

The report was formally filed by Sgt. R. I. Evans of the Hamilton Detachment. The RCMP conducted interviews with the witnesses on August 19, 1968, to obtain official statements. Due to the time lapse between the sighting and the report, no telex was sent to the National Research Council (N.R.C.) Meteor Centre. The witnesses explicitly requested a follow-up reply from authorities to help ease their minds regarding the nature of the encounter.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 理查德·A·斯丘斯先生（Richard A. Skewes，25岁）、安·玛丽·斯丘斯夫人（Ann Marie Skewes，29岁）以及盖尔·耶姆小姐（Gail Yemm，17岁）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月15日，晚上约11:30。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省特鲁罗（Truro）与斯普林希尔（Springhill）之间的4号公路。

**目击经过：** 三名目击者在驾车从哈利法克斯前往斯普林希尔的途中，观察到一组5至7个不明飞行物。此次遭遇持续了5到10分钟。这些物体在距离地面及附近树木上方30至100英尺的高度盘旋，并以“不合常理的方式”环绕目击者的车辆飞行。

理查德·斯丘斯先生曾是加拿大皇家海军成员，具备从瞭望岗位识别物体的专业经验。他表示从未见过此类飞行器，并对它们距离车辆如此之近感到极度恐惧。其中一个物体以极高速度冲向汽车，径直逼近后又突然“昂起”并从车顶上方掠过。尽管距离极近，但目击者称这些物体没有发出任何引擎或机械噪音，即使他们摇下车窗倾听也是如此。目击者因担心发生碰撞，不敢停车。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为深色，长约20英尺，厚约6至10英尺。其中一个飞行器表面带有白色斑点。它们覆盖着许多明亮的黄色和绿色灯光，斯丘斯夫人将其亮度比作圣诞树。其中一个较大的物体前端有一个显眼的黄色灯光。安·玛丽·斯丘斯提到，这些飞行器的外观让她想起了在加拿大国家展览会（CNE）展出的一架二战时期的飞机。这些物体机动灵活，即便在目击者驾车离开时，它们似乎仍在该区域盘旋。

**调查/后续：** 斯丘斯先生起初因担心被视为精神不稳定而犹豫是否要报告此次目击事件，但在8月17日途经多伦多时，与妻子及保姆（耶姆小姐）讨论后，他决定上报。随后，斯丘斯夫人联系了加拿大国防部（DND）和加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）。

该报告由汉密尔顿分局的R. I. 埃文斯（R. I. Evans）警官正式归档。加拿大皇家骑警于1968年8月19日对目击者进行了访谈，以获取正式陈述。由于目击事件与报告时间之间存在间隔，当局未向国家研究委员会（N.R.C.）流星中心发送电传。目击者明确要求当局给予后续回复，以帮助缓解他们对此次遭遇性质的担忧。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月15日，23:30至01:00之间。

**目击经过：** 三名目击者在驾车从哈利法克斯前往斯普林希尔的途中，观察到一组5至7个不明飞行物。此次遭遇持续了约5至10分钟。这些物体在低空盘旋或飞行，距离树梢和地面约30至100英尺。目击者描述称，这些物体以“不合常理”的方式机动，环绕车辆飞行，并不断变换队形。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Dr. [redacted], Cst. L.J. Lavoie, 3/Cst. J.P. Eagan, Cst. R.A. Peers, Cst. J.L. Miles, Cst. C.H. Bishop, Cst. W.J. Whyte, and Mrs. Whyte.

**Date / Time:** July 18, 1968 (1:05 AM and 1:10 AM); August 16, 1968 (10:00 PM – 11:00 PM).

**Location:** Truro, Nova Scotia (3 North St); Onslow Mountain, Colchester County, Nova Scotia; and a farm near Truro.

**Sighting:** 
The case file documents multiple sightings occurring on two separate dates. On July 18, 1968, Cst. W.J. Whyte and his wife reported two distinct events. At 1:05 AM, while at 3 North St, Truro, they observed a circular, yellow object moving from west to east. Cst. Whyte, a licensed aerial navigator, noted the object’s speed was comparable to North Atlantic Strategic Air Command flights but at a higher altitude; it appeared larger and brighter than the brightest star and turned reddish before disappearing. At 1:10 AM, at Onslow Mountain, they observed a second object: a large, circular, rosy-red light that hovered stationary above the treetops for 10–15 minutes before accelerating rapidly out of sight.

On August 16, 1968, at approximately 10:00 PM, a doctor (name redacted) contacted the RCMP to report a UFO near his farm. He described a bright orange or yellow light at an elevation of 20 degrees that shifted to red. He insisted the object was moving. RCMP members from the Truro detachment (Csts. Lavoie, Eagan, Peers, Miles, and Bishop) arrived at the scene to investigate. While the doctor maintained the object was in motion, the officers observed the light as a bright, twinkling star. They noted the object cycled through colors, including blue, green, white, and red. By 11:00 PM, Cst. Lavoie observed the object again and concluded it was a star, noting that it had shifted position higher in the sky while continuing to twinkle and change colors.

**Object:** 
The objects were consistently described as circular or light-based. The July 18 objects were yellow (turning red) and rosy-red, estimated to be twice the size of the brightest star. The August 16 object was described as a bright light that shifted between orange, yellow, blue, green, white, and red. Movement varied from stationary hovering with rapid acceleration (July 18) to perceived movement versus stationary twinkling (August 16). Durations ranged from 2–3 minutes for the first July sighting to 10–15 minutes for the second, and approximately one hour for the August observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP conducted an on-site investigation for the August 16 report, with five officers responding to the doctor’s farm. The official conclusion of the responding officers was that the August 16 object was a star, citing its twinkling nature and the fact that it appeared to move only in accordance with the rotation of the sky. No further physical evidence or sketches were noted in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删节] 医生、L.J. 拉瓦伊（Lavoie）警员、J.P. 伊根（Eagan）三级警员、R.A. 皮尔斯（Peers）警员、J.L. 迈尔斯（Miles）警员、C.H. 毕晓普（Bishop）警员、W.J. 怀特（Whyte）警员及怀特夫人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月18日（凌晨1:05及1:10）；1968年8月16日（晚上10:00 – 11:00）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省特鲁罗（北街3号）；新斯科舍省科尔切斯特县昂斯洛山；特鲁罗附近的一个农场。

**目击经过：**
该档案记录了发生在两个不同日期的多次目击事件。1968年7月18日，W.J. 怀特警员及其妻子报告了两次不同的事件。凌晨1:05，在特鲁罗北街3号，他们观察到一个从西向东移动的圆形黄色物体。怀特警员是一位持证空中领航员，他指出该物体的速度与北大西洋战略空军司令部的飞行速度相当，但高度更高；它看起来比最亮的恒星还要大且亮，在消失前转变为红色。凌晨1:10，在昂斯洛山，他们观察到了第二个物体：一个巨大的圆形玫瑰红色光团，在树梢上方悬停了10至15分钟，随后迅速加速消失。

1968年8月16日晚上10:00左右，一位医生（姓名已删节）联系加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP），报告其农场附近出现不明飞行物。他描述称，一个仰角为20度的明亮橙色或黄色光团转变成了红色。他坚称该物体在移动。来自特鲁罗分局的皇家骑警成员（拉瓦伊、伊根、皮尔斯、迈尔斯和毕晓普警员）抵达现场进行调查。尽管该医生坚持认为物体在移动，但警员们观察到该光点表现为一颗明亮、闪烁的恒星。他们注意到该物体会循环变换颜色，包括蓝色、绿色、白色和红色。到晚上11:00，拉瓦伊警员再次观察该物体并得出结论认为它是一颗恒星，并指出它在天空中位置的偏移是由于地球自转，且它持续闪烁并变换颜色。

**物体描述：**
这些物体被一致描述为圆形或光团状。7月18日的物体为黄色（转为红色）和玫瑰红色，估计大小为最亮恒星的两倍。8月16日的物体被描述为在橙色、黄色、蓝色、绿色、白色和红色之间变换的明亮光团。运动方式各异，从悬停后迅速加速（7月18日）到被感知到的移动与静止闪烁（8月16日）不等。持续时间方面，7月的第一次目击约为2至3分钟，第二次为10至15分钟，8月的观察则持续了约一小时。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警针对8月16日的报告进行了现场调查，五名警员前往该医生的农场。出警警员的官方结论是，8月16日的物体是一颗恒星，理由是其具有闪烁特性，且其移动轨迹仅符合天空的旋转规律。所提供的文档中未记录任何进一步的物证或草图。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** MAJ (N) WJ Draper, LT Montgomery, PTE Burr, CPL Remple, PTE Vernon, the Officer of the Watch (OOW), lookouts, and unspecified personnel aboard HMCS *Yukon* and HMCS *Mackenzie*.

**Date / Time:** 21 August 1968; initial sighting at 1258Z, duration of 13 minutes until 1311Z.

**Location:** Pacific Ocean; ship position at 1300Z was 33° 32' N, 135° W (with objects sighted at 33° 24' N, 134° 57' W).

**Sighting:** On 21 August 1968, a formation of objects was observed by personnel aboard the HMCS *Yukon* and HMCS *Mackenzie*. The sighting began at 1258Z when a group of lights appeared at an altitude of 10 degrees, bearing 070 degrees true, positioned immediately above the moon. The formation moved across the sky, reaching a maximum elevation of 85 degrees at bearing 265 degrees true by 1303Z. By 1309Z, the formation had shifted to an altitude of 45 degrees at bearing 265 degrees true, eventually fading from view at 1311Z. The formation was observed by eye, through binoculars, and using negative filters. Despite the clear weather conditions, there were no corresponding contacts on the ships' SPS-10 or SPS-12 radar systems.

**Object:** The phenomenon consisted of a group of approximately 20 bright, white lights resembling stars or satellites. The formation subtended an arc of 5 degrees. One light, located in the center of the formation, was notably brighter than the others and exhibited a distinct white glow. The brightness of the objects was compared to the magnitude of Venus. The formation moved at a velocity described as faster than an average satellite but slower than a meteor shower; notably, no meteor tails were observed. Some reports described the visual appearance as a "cloud" or "formation" on the horizon.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The event was documented in a formal UFO report filed by CANFORCENED for CFOC. The report was transmitted as an unclassified priority message to the National Research Council (Radio and Electrical Engineering Division), CANMARPAC, and CANINFO Victoria. Meteorological data recorded at 1300Z included a barometer reading of 1021.5, a wet bulb temperature of 18.1°C, a dry bulb temperature of 21.1°C, and a sea temperature of 23.9°C. The ships were maintaining a course of 065 degrees true at a speed of 16 knots during the observation. No photographs were taken.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 海军少校 W.J. Draper、Montgomery 中尉、Burr 列兵、Remple 下士、Vernon 列兵、值更官（OOW）、瞭望员，以及加拿大皇家海军“育空”号（HMCS *Yukon*）和“麦肯齐”号（HMCS *Mackenzie*）上的其他未具名人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月21日；首次目击时间为 1258Z（祖鲁时间），持续时间为13分钟，至 1311Z 结束。

**地点：** 太平洋；1300Z 时舰船位置为北纬 33° 32'，西经 135°（物体目击位置为北纬 33° 24'，西经 134° 57'）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月21日，加拿大皇家海军“育空”号和“麦肯齐”号上的船员观测到了一组飞行物体。目击事件始于 1258Z，当时一群光点出现在高度角10度、真方位角070度的位置，正好位于月球上方。该编队在天空中移动，至 1303Z 时达到最大仰角85度，方位角为真方位265度。到 1309Z，编队移动至高度角45度、真方位角265度的位置，并最终于 1311Z 从视野中消失。目击者通过肉眼、双筒望远镜以及负片滤镜进行了观测。尽管当时天气晴朗，但舰船上的 SPS-10 和 SPS-12 雷达系统均未探测到相应的回波。

**物体描述：** 该现象由约20个明亮的白色光点组成，类似于恒星或卫星。编队覆盖了5度的弧度。位于编队中心的一个光点明显比其他光点更亮，并散发出独特的白光。这些物体的亮度被比作金星的视星等。编队的移动速度被描述为比普通卫星快，但比流星雨慢；值得注意的是，未观察到任何流星尾迹。一些报告将该视觉外观描述为地平线上的一团“云”或“编队”。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被记录在由加拿大武装部队司令部（CANFORCENED）为加拿大海军司令部（CFOC）提交的正式 UFO 报告中。该报告以非机密优先电文形式发送至加拿大国家研究委员会（无线电与电气工程部）、加拿大太平洋海事司令部（CANMARPAC）以及维多利亚加拿大信息中心（CANINFO Victoria）。1300Z 记录的气象数据显示：气压为 1021.5 百帕，湿球温度为 18.1°C，干球温度为 21.1°C，海水温度为 23.9°C。观测期间，舰船保持真航向065度，航速16节。现场未拍摄任何照片。

**Witnesses:** Edward D. Robichaud, Don Robichaud, Al Robichaud, Bob Robichaud, and an unidentified reporter (residing at Box 15, Coldbrook, Kings Co.).

**Date / Time:** August 23, 1968.

**Location:** Sackville Downs Race Track, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On August 23, 1968, the Robichaud group (Edward, Don, Al, and Bob) observed an unidentified object at the Sackville Downs Race Track under a clear sky. The sighting lasted for approximately three to four minutes. The object was initially seen hovering in the north before it began moving slowly toward the south at a consistent, slow speed. 

In a separate account associated with the same event, an unidentified reporter from Coldbrook, N.S., provided a narrative describing a reactive interaction with an object. This witness noted that the object would "swoop down" specifically when they turned their lights off. Furthermore, this witness claimed to be able to see "images behind the windows" of the craft.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped. Its lighting configuration was complex, featuring three or four white lights, a red light on top, and at least one green light. The object emitted a bright flash during the observation. Regarding sound, the Robichaud witnesses reported hearing a low hum, which they explicitly noted did not sound like a helicopter. The unidentified witness’s account confirms the presence of windows and suggests the object was capable of controlled, reactive flight maneuvers (swooping).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** This case file is part of the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) records. The documentation includes a report form directed to Professor R. H. MacNeill at Acadia University in Wolfville, N.S. The file contains the contact information for the Coldbrook witness (Box 15, Coldbrook, Kings Co., including a phone number). The investigation notes confirm that the object maintained a very slow speed throughout the duration of the sighting with no observed acceleration or deceleration.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 爱德华·D·罗比肖（Edward D. Robichaud）、唐·罗比肖（Don Robichaud）、阿尔·罗比肖（Al Robichaud）、鲍勃·罗比肖（Bob Robichaud），以及一名身份不明的记者（居住于科尔布鲁克国王县15号信箱）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月23日。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省，萨克维尔唐斯赛马场（Sackville Downs Race Track）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月23日，罗比肖一行人（爱德华、唐、阿尔和鲍勃）在晴朗的天空下，于萨克维尔唐斯赛马场观测到一个不明物体。目击过程持续了约三到四分钟。该物体最初悬停在北方，随后开始以恒定的慢速向南方移动。

在与此次事件相关的另一份陈述中，一名来自新斯科舍省科尔布鲁克的身份不明记者描述了该物体与其产生的互动反应。该目击者指出，每当他们关掉灯光时，物体就会“俯冲下来”。此外，该目击者声称能够看到飞行器“窗户后的影像”。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形。其灯光配置复杂，包括三到四个白灯、一个顶部红灯以及至少一个绿灯。在观测过程中，该物体发出了一道明亮的闪光。关于声音，罗比肖一行人报告称听到了低沉的嗡嗡声，并明确指出这听起来不像直升机。身份不明目击者的陈述证实了窗户的存在，并暗示该物体具备受控的反应性飞行机动能力（俯冲）。

**调查/后续：** 该档案属于加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的记录。相关文件包括一份寄往新斯科舍省沃尔夫维尔阿卡迪亚大学 R. H. 麦克尼尔（R. H. MacNeill）教授的报告表。档案中包含了科尔布鲁克目击者的联系方式（科尔布鲁克国王县15号信箱，含电话号码）。调查记录证实，该物体在整个目击过程中保持着极慢的速度，未观察到加速或减速现象。

**Witnesses:** Cpl. D.W. Tribble, Mrs. B. White

**Date / Time:** August 25, 1968, at 0502 GMT

**Location:** Sampson St, Ottawa

**Sighting:** On the morning of August 25, 1968, at 0502 GMT, Cpl. D.W. Tribble and his neighbor, Mrs. B. White, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon directly overhead. The witnesses reported that the object traveled in a path that was generally straight, yet it notably deviated from a standard trajectory by failing to follow the curvature of the earth. Instead, the object exhibited slight, irregular zig-zagging motions as it traversed the sky. 

There is a minor discrepancy in the recorded direction of travel between the initial observations: while one account notes the object moving from west to east, another record indicates it was moving in a westerly direction. Regardless of the directional heading, both witnesses agreed that the sighting lasted for approximately two minutes. The event concluded as the object faded into the eastern sky, eventually blending into the background of the stars. The witnesses noted that the surrounding environment was "dead silent" during the observation, which allowed them to clearly distinguish the specific sound associated with the object.

**Object:** The object appeared as a singular white light, estimated to be approximately twice the intensity of the brightest star visible in the sky. The light did not remain constant; it flashed intermittently with no discernible or regular pattern. The object emitted a distinct, audible sound described as being similar to a medium-speed electric motor. This sound was faint, but loud enough for the witnesses to confirm that the noise moved in direct conjunction with the light, indicating the sound originated from the object itself.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, an official report was generated and transmitted from CANFORBASE UPLANDS. The documentation was forwarded to the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCCWC) and Canadian Forces Headquarters (CANFORCEHED). Additionally, the report was submitted to the National Research Council (NRC) for review by the Radio and Electrical Engineering Division to determine if the sighting could be attributed to known aerial phenomena or technical anomalies.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** D.W. 特里布尔下士 (Cpl. D.W. Tribble)、B. 怀特夫人 (Mrs. B. White)

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月25日，格林威治标准时间 05:02

**地点：** 渥太华，桑普森街 (Sampson St)

**目击经过：** 1968年8月25日清晨，格林威治标准时间 05:02，D.W. 特里布尔下士和他的邻居 B. 怀特夫人观察到了头顶上方出现的不明空中现象。目击者报告称，该物体行进路径总体呈直线，但值得注意的是，它并未遵循地球曲率，而是偏离了标准轨迹。相反，该物体在穿越天空时表现出轻微且不规则的“之”字形运动。

关于物体行进方向的初始记录存在细微出入：一份记录指出物体由西向东移动，而另一份记录则显示其向西移动。尽管航向存在争议，但两位目击者一致认为目击过程持续了约两分钟。事件结束时，物体逐渐消失在东方的天空中，最终与背景星空融为一体。目击者指出，观察期间周围环境“死一般寂静”，这使他们能够清晰地辨别出与该物体相关的特定声音。

**物体描述：** 该物体表现为一个单一的白光点，亮度估计约为天空中最亮恒星的两倍。光线并不恒定，而是以无规律、不可辨识的模式间歇性闪烁。该物体发出一种独特且可听见的声音，被描述为类似于中速运转的电动机。声音虽然微弱，但足以让目击者确认其与光点同步移动，表明声音正是源自物体本身。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，加拿大武装部队厄普兰基地 (CANFORBASE UPLANDS) 生成并传达了一份正式报告。该文件被转交至救援协调中心 (RCCWC) 和加拿大武装部队总部 (CANFORCEHED)。此外，报告还提交给了加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC)，由无线电与电气工程部门进行审查，以确定此次目击事件是否可归因于已知的空中现象或技术异常。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Armand Charbonneau 先生。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Robert Gerald Robichaud (also referred to as Robert Rabidau), Don (Donald) Robichaud, Al (Albert) Robichaud, and Ed (Edward) Robichaud.

**Date / Time:** August 28, 1968; sighting occurred between 9:02 p.m. and 9:05 p.m.

**Location:** Sackville Downs Race Track, Middle Sackville, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of August 28, 1968, four witnesses—Robert, Don, Al, and Ed Robichaud—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while at the Sackville Downs Race Track. The sky conditions were reported as clear. According to the accounts, the object was first spotted hovering in the north. One narrative notes the object appeared stationary for approximately two minutes before the light initially went out. As the object approached the witnesses, it began to display a complex array of lights. The witnesses observed the object move slowly from the north toward the south, and eventually toward the east. While one account suggests the sighting lasted five minutes and another suggests four, the consensus is that the object remained in view for a short duration. Regarding sound, reports vary slightly: some witnesses stated the object was entirely soundless, while others noted that any potential noise from the object might have been masked by the ambient noise of the crowd at the race track. The witnesses expressed a strong conviction that the object was a "flying saucer."

**Object:** The object was described as large, round, and wider than an airplane, though not as long. Its appearance was dynamic: it began as a bright, steady white light before transitioning into a display of flashing red, green, and white lights. Specifically, observers noted red and green lights "floating" with additional white lights positioned above them, creating the impression of a circular craft. The object’s movement was characterized by an initial hover followed by a very slow, steady-speed transit from north to south, and finally to the east. No change in speed was noted during its transit.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation includes a formal narrative report and a return address for Professor R. H. MacNeill of Acadia University in Wolfville, N.S., indicating academic interest in the sighting. The report identifies Robert Rabidau (Robichaud) of 3622 Barrington St., Halifax, as the primary reporter. While the files contain detailed witness accounts and descriptions of the object's behavior, there is no record of a formal RCMP conclusion or a final investigative determination provided in these pages. The files serve as a collection of witness statements and narrative reports regarding the event.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗伯特·杰拉德·罗比肖（Robert Gerald Robichaud，亦被称为罗伯特·拉比多 Robert Rabidau）、唐（唐纳德）·罗比肖（Don (Donald) Robichaud）、阿尔（阿尔伯特）·罗比肖（Al (Albert) Robichaud）以及埃德（爱德华）·罗比肖（Ed (Edward) Robichaud）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月28日；目击时间发生在晚上9:02至9:05之间。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省米德尔萨克维尔（Middle Sackville），萨克维尔唐斯赛马场（Sackville Downs Race Track）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月28日晚，四名目击者——罗伯特、唐、阿尔和埃德·罗比肖在萨克维尔唐斯赛马场观察到一种不明空中现象。据报告，当时天空晴朗。根据描述，该物体最初被发现悬停在北方。其中一份叙述指出，该物体在灯光熄灭前似乎静止了约两分钟。当物体靠近目击者时，开始展现出一系列复杂的灯光。目击者观察到该物体从北向南缓慢移动，最终转向东方。虽然有一份报告称目击持续了五分钟，另一份则称四分钟，但一致的看法是该物体在视野中停留的时间很短。关于声音，报告略有出入：一些目击者称物体完全无声，而另一些则指出，物体可能产生的任何噪音可能被赛马场人群的嘈杂声掩盖了。目击者坚信该物体是一架“飞碟”。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为大型、圆形，宽度超过飞机，但长度不及飞机。其外观具有动态变化：起初是一个明亮、稳定的白光，随后转变为闪烁的红、绿、白灯光组合。具体而言，观察者注意到红光和绿光在“漂浮”，上方还有额外的白光，营造出一种圆形飞行器的视觉印象。该物体的运动特征是先悬停，随后以非常缓慢、稳定的速度从北向南移动，最后转向东方。在移动过程中未观察到速度变化。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案包含一份正式的叙述报告，以及阿卡迪亚大学（Acadia University）R. H. 麦克尼尔（R. H. MacNeill）教授（位于新斯科舍省沃尔夫维尔）的回信地址，表明学术界对此次目击事件的关注。报告将居住在哈利法克斯巴林顿街3622号的罗伯特·拉比多（罗比肖）列为主要报告人。尽管档案中包含了详细的目击者陈述和对物体行为的描述，但这些文件中并未记录加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的正式结论或最终调查定论。这些文件主要作为关于该事件的目击者陈述和叙述报告的汇编。

**Witnesses:** Sgt Thomas H Sisco (USAF) and AB Philip J Molno (USAF).

**Sighting:** On 4 September 1968, in clear blue skies with no clouds, witnesses observed an object near Goose Bay (Military Grid Ref 722095). The object was described as approximately round, silver, and metallic in color. It traveled from north to south with no sound and no vapor trail. The sighting lasted approximately 5 minutes.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Four employees of the Greater Winnipeg Water District (G.W.W.D.) railway (names redacted), Cst. L.R. Stright, and a civilian resident of 15 Lenora St, Winnipeg.

**Date / Time:** September 11, 1968 (Note: Page 134 contains a typographical error citing 1953; the context of the RCMP investigation confirms 1968). Times reported vary between 7:25 p.m., 7:30 p.m., and 10:00 p.m. CST.

**Location:** Waugh, Manitoba, specifically near "Mile 91" on the Greater Winnipeg Water District (G.W.W.D.) railway line.

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 11, 1968, four G.W.W.D. railway employees were traveling on a railway track car when they observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. Accounts place the object 4–6 miles northwest of Waugh. While some reports suggest the sighting occurred during daylight hours (7:25–7:30 p.m.), others place the event at 10:00 p.m. The witnesses observed the object positioned above the tree line. It traveled in a horizontal line at an extremely high rate of speed, moving from the south toward the west. The sighting lasted for approximately one minute before the object disappeared behind trees or out of view.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as a round, very bright white light. Estimates of its diameter ranged from 13 to 20 inches. Witnesses reported that the object moved at a high rate of speed with no irregular movements. No windows, vapor trails, or sounds were associated with the object.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was reported to the RCMP by a witness from Waugh. On September 12, 1968, at 6:45 p.m., Cpl. G.R. Granger conducted formal interviews with the four G.W.W.D. employees. During the investigation, the RCMP specifically questioned the witnesses regarding potential alcohol consumption; the witnesses denied this, and the RCMP noted that they appeared to be responsible men with no apparent motive to fabricate the report. Cst. L.R. Stright was also involved in the documentation of the event. The Falcon Beach RCMP detachment transmitted the details via telex to the Winnipeg detachment. Despite the investigation, authorities were unable to provide a satisfactory explanation for the object, and the case file notes that further reporting was anticipated.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 大温尼伯水区（G.W.W.D.）铁路的四名员工（姓名已删减）、L.R. 斯特莱特（L.R. Stright）警员，以及温尼伯市莱诺拉街（Lenora St）15号的一名平民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月11日（注：第134页存在排版错误，误写为1953年；加拿大皇家骑警的调查背景证实应为1968年）。报告的时间在中部标准时间（CST）晚上7:25、7:30和10:00之间不等。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省沃（Waugh），具体位于大温尼伯水区（G.W.W.D.）铁路线的“91英里”处附近。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月11日晚，四名大温尼伯水区铁路员工在乘坐轨道车时，观察到一种不明空中现象。据描述，该物体位于沃西北方向4至6英里处。虽然一些报告称目击发生在白天（晚上7:25至7:30），但另一些报告则称事件发生在晚上10:00。目击者观察到该物体悬停在树线之上。它以极高的速度沿水平方向移动，从南向西飞行。目击持续了大约一分钟，随后物体消失在树木后或视野之外。

**物体描述：** 该物体被一致描述为一个圆形、非常明亮的白光。对其直径的估计在13到20英寸之间。目击者报告称，该物体以高速移动，没有不规则的动作。该物体没有窗户、尾迹，也没有伴随任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由沃的一名目击者报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）。1968年9月12日晚上6:45，G.R. 格兰杰（G.R. Granger）下士对四名大温尼伯水区员工进行了正式访谈。在调查过程中，加拿大皇家骑警专门询问了目击者是否饮酒；目击者予以否认，且警方指出他们看起来是负责任的人，没有明显的动机去编造报告。L.R. 斯特莱特警员也参与了此次事件的记录工作。猎鹰海滩（Falcon Beach）的加拿大皇家骑警分队通过电传将详细信息发送给了温尼伯分队。尽管进行了调查，当局仍无法对该物体给出令人满意的解释，案件档案中注明预计会有进一步的报告。

**Witnesses:** Three civilians (residents of Waller St. and Barker Ave.), one individual at 4526 Halley Street, and one individual at 4533 Barker Street.

**Date / Time:** September 25, 1968 (Note: Page 130 contains a typographical error citing 1963; the event is confirmed as 1968), at approximately 9:15 P.M. PDT.

**Location:** Burnaby, British Columbia (vicinity of Moseron St., Barker Ave., and Halley St.).

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 25, 1968, multiple witnesses located in the residential area of Burnaby, B.C., observed an unusual aerial phenomenon in the northwesterly sky. While standing near the intersection of Moseron St. and Barker Ave., and at their respective residences on Halley St. and Barker St., the witnesses observed two bright, yellowy-orange lights. The witnesses noted that the lights appeared similar in appearance to distant street lights, though they were significantly brighter than a star. 

The movement of the objects was described as a distinct "swaying" motion. One of the two lights remained stationary, while the second light performed an anti-clockwise rotation before coming to a stop directly beneath the stationary light. The objects were observed to be approximately four feet apart (or, as noted in one account, 1/2 diameter apart). The entire sighting lasted between 5 to 10 minutes, concluding when the lights faded away in a westerly direction. All witnesses confirmed that there was a complete absence of sound, which led them to rule out the possibility of the objects being aircraft.

**Object:** The objects consisted of two bright, yellowy-orange lights, each approximately one and one-half feet in diameter. They were positioned roughly four feet apart. Their movement was characterized by a swaying motion, with one light remaining fixed while the other executed an anti-clockwise rotation to position itself vertically below the first. No sound was emitted by the objects during the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, the witnesses contacted the Vancouver International Airport control tower to inquire about potential aircraft or other reports; the tower confirmed that no UFO reports had been received. The Burnaby detachment of the RCMP subsequently followed up by contacting the airport tower, which reiterated that no other reports had been logged. The reporting officer interviewed the witnesses and noted that all parties appeared to be responsible and sincere in their accounts. On September 26, 1968, a telex regarding the incident was officially dispatched to the R.C. Meteor Centre and other relevant authorities for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 三名平民（沃勒街和巴克大道居民）、哈雷街4526号的一位人士，以及巴克街4533号的一位人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月25日（注：第130页有印刷错误，误写为1963年；该事件已确认为1968年），太平洋夏令时间晚上9:15左右。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比（莫塞隆街、巴克大道和哈雷街附近）。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月25日晚，位于不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比住宅区的多名目击者在西北方向的天空中观察到一种异常的空中现象。目击者们当时分别站在莫塞隆街与巴克大道的交叉口附近，以及位于哈雷街和巴克街的各自住所处，他们观察到了两道明亮的黄橙色光芒。目击者指出，这些光芒看起来类似于远处的路灯，但比星星要明亮得多。

这些物体的移动方式被描述为一种明显的“摇摆”运动。其中一道光保持静止，而第二道光则进行了逆时针旋转，随后停在静止光芒的正下方。据观察，这两个物体相距约四英尺（或如其中一份记录所述，相距半个直径的距离）。整个目击过程持续了5到10分钟，最终光芒向西消散。所有目击者都确认现场完全没有声音，这使他们排除了这些物体是飞机的可能性。

**物体描述：** 这些物体由两道明亮的黄橙色光芒组成，每道光的直径约为一英尺半。它们彼此相距约四英尺。其运动特征为摇摆式移动，其中一道光保持固定，而另一道光则执行逆时针旋转，将自身定位在第一道光的正下方。在整个目击过程中，这些物体没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，目击者联系了温哥华国际机场控制塔，询问是否有关于飞机或其他飞行物的报告；塔台确认未收到任何不明飞行物（UFO）报告。随后，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）本拿比分局跟进联系了机场塔台，塔台重申没有记录到其他相关报告。负责的警官采访了目击者，并指出所有当事人在陈述时表现得负责且真诚。1968年9月26日，一份关于此事件的电传被正式发送至加拿大皇家气象中心及其他相关部门进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. [redacted], his wife, and a second civilian from Great Falls, Manitoba (employed by a telephone company).

**Date / Time:** September 27, 1968, at approximately 10:20 PM – 10:30 PM Central Time.

**Location:** Highway 12 and 15, approximately 5 miles north of Anola, Manitoba, traveling toward Beausejour, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On the night of September 27, 1968, the witnesses were traveling in a private vehicle when the wife first noticed a light in the sky. The witnesses observed a large, greyish-colored light positioned just above their car, seemingly tracking along the nearby telephone lines. The object followed the witnesses' vehicle for a distance of 15 to 20 miles as they drove toward Beausejour. The witnesses noted that the object remained visible even after they turned off their vehicle's headlights. 

Upon reaching the outskirts of Beausejour, the witnesses stopped the car and exited the vehicle to gain a better view. At this point, the object was observed hovering between two houses at a distance of approximately 15 to 20 yards away. After hovering, the object moved away slowly and eventually disappeared behind the houses. The total duration of the sighting was estimated at 20 to 25 minutes. Following the encounter, the witnesses proceeded to the RCMP office to file a formal report with Cst. T.E. Driver.

**Object:** The object was described as a flat, round, greyish-colored craft. Estimates of its size varied slightly between 10 to 15 feet and 10 to 15 yards in diameter. It featured "turning lights" and maintained an altitude of approximately 30 to 50 feet throughout the encounter. No specific sound was reported, and the object demonstrated the ability to follow the vehicle at a consistent pace before hovering and moving away slowly.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was reported to Cst. T.E. Driver at the RCMP office. An RCMP patrol was dispatched to the reported location to scan the area, but the search yielded negative results. Additional patrols were conducted along the highway, and other motorists in the area were questioned, all with negative results. A formal statement was obtained from the primary witness and attached to the official report as Appendix A. The RCMP noted that the witness appeared calm during the interview, though they qualified that the witness's reliability could not be fully assessed as he was not previously known to the detachment. Weather conditions at the time of the sighting were noted as cloudy.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]先生、其妻子，以及一名来自曼尼托巴省大瀑布城（Great Falls）的平民（受雇于一家电话公司）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月27日，中部时间晚上10:20至10:30左右。

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省阿诺拉（Anola）以北约5英里的12号和15号公路交汇处，当时正驱车前往曼尼托巴省博塞茹（Beausejour）。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月27日晚，目击者一行人正乘坐私家车行驶，其妻子首先注意到天空中出现了一道光。目击者观察到一个巨大的灰白色光体悬停在他们车子上方，似乎正沿着附近的电话线移动。当他们驱车前往博塞茹时，该物体跟随他们的车辆行驶了15到20英里。目击者指出，即使在他们关闭车灯后，该物体依然清晰可见。

抵达博塞茹郊区后，目击者停车并走出车外以便观察。此时，他们看到该物体悬停在两座房屋之间，距离约15到20码。悬停片刻后，该物体缓慢移开，最终消失在房屋后方。整个目击过程估计持续了20到25分钟。事发后，目击者前往加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）办公室，向T.E. 德赖弗（T.E. Driver）警官提交了正式报告。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个扁平、圆形、灰色的飞行器。对其尺寸的估计略有差异，直径约为10至15英尺或10至15码。它配有“转向灯”，在整个接触过程中保持在约30至50英尺的高度。据报告，该物体没有发出任何特定声音，并展现出以恒定速度跟随车辆，随后悬停并缓慢移开的能力。

**调查/后续：** 该事件已向RCMP办公室的T.E. 德赖弗警官报告。RCMP派遣了一支巡逻队前往报告地点进行搜寻，但未发现任何异常。随后，警方沿公路进行了额外的巡逻并询问了该地区的其他驾驶员，均无任何发现。警方获取了主要目击者的正式陈述，并将其作为附录A附在正式报告中。RCMP指出，目击者在接受采访时表现冷静，但同时也说明，由于该目击者此前与该分局并无接触，其可靠性无法完全评估。目击时的天气状况记录为多云。

Approximately 30 minutes after the initial disappearance, a jet aircraft flew through the area, and the object reappeared, following the exact same flight path and disappearance procedure. The total duration of the sighting was estimated at two to three minutes. It was further noted that Mr. Freeman MacDonald had witnessed this same phenomenon on several previous occasions, though he had not formally reported those prior sightings.

**Object:** The object was described as a large, egg-shaped amber light. It exhibited rapid, jet-like movement and the ability to vanish instantly. No physical structure or sound was reported by the witnesses.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented as a formal UFO report directed to Canadian Forces Headquarters (CFHQ) in Ottawa, Ontario, and the National Research Council (NRC) Radio and Electrical Engineering Division. The weather at the time of the sighting was reported as clear with visible stars. The information regarding the sighting was transmitted via Canadian Pacific Telegram to Professor R.H. Macneil at Acadia University in Wolfville, Nova Scotia, for further review. No final identification or official conclusion regarding the nature of the object is recorded in the provided files.

**Witnesses:** Roderick B. Mattatall (also identified as Rodrick B. Mottett)

**Date / Time:** 1968-09-28

**Location:** Sackville, New Brunswick (inferred from return address)

**Sighting:**
On the night of September 28, 1968, Roderick B. Mattatall observed an unidentified object from his front yard. The sighting occurred during a night characterized by cloudy conditions with occasional clear intervals. Using a 240x refractor telescope, Mattatall observed the object for a duration of 20 minutes, until the moon was completely obscured by cloud cover. 

Mattatall, who noted that he has been an amateur sky observer for over a year, expressed significant skepticism regarding the existence of "flying saucers." He emphasized that he had never witnessed anything similar to this event previously. To ensure the accuracy of his observations, he utilized different eyepieces on his telescope to confirm that the shifting colors were not an optical error or a byproduct of his equipment. He noted that the colors were definitely reflected through the telescope. Regarding the object's position, Mattatall reported that it remained stationary, hovering over or near the moon's "center of darkness." He noted that he could not definitively determine if the object was positioned close to the lunar surface or many miles above it. However, he concluded that for the object to be visible at that distance, it would necessarily have to be "considerably large."

**Object:**
The object was described as resembling a star in appearance, roughly the size of a 3rd magnitude star. Its color was dynamic, shifting between red-orange, pale yellow, and blue. The object remained stationary throughout the duration of the sighting, with no noticeable change in speed or movement.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The report was filed with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) and is cataloged under file reference RG 77, Vol. 306. The documentation includes a continuation page (labeled "10. Other information and narrative report") intended to be returned to Professor R. H. MacNeill at Acadia University in Wolfville, Nova Scotia. No formal conclusion or official investigation result was recorded in the provided files.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of two separate reports (Page 149 and Page 150) detailing the event. While the accounts of the object’s movement, the interaction with the approaching aircraft, and the physical description are identical, the reports provide conflicting dates and times (October 10 at 0125Z versus October 11 at 0215Z). **目击者：** 罗伯特·施鲁斯伯里-吉先生（Robert Shrewsbury-Gee，也被称为奥伯特·施鲁斯伯-吉先生，Mr. Orbert Shrewsbur-Gee）及其他五人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年10月10日 0125Z 和 1968年10月11日 0215Z。

**地点：** 多伦多国际机场。

**目击经过：** 该档案包含两份独立的报告，记录了在多伦多国际机场上空观察到的一致空中现象。在这两起事件中，目击者均观察到一个物体从东向西飞行，并专门在南北向跑道的尽头盘旋。观察期间，一架飞机正准备进场降落；该不明物体被目击到从进场飞机的上方掠过，向南飞行后消失在视野中。报告指出，尽管有这些目击记录，但多伦多国际机场的任何管制机构均未探测或记录到相应的活动。

**物体描述：** 该物体是通过望远镜观察到的。据描述，其视觉星等与恒星相当，且显著特征是没有任何航行灯。在整个目击过程中，它始终保持在地平线低空，仰角在5到10度之间。

**调查/后续：** 相关文档由两份详细记录该事件的独立报告（第149页和第150页）组成。虽然关于物体运动轨迹、与进场飞机的互动以及物理特征的描述完全一致，但报告在日期和时间上存在冲突（10月10日0125Z与10月11日0215Z）。官方后续记录证实，调查人员曾向多伦多国际机场的管制机构进行过问询，但未发现任何能够支持目击者所报告的视觉观测结果的佐证数据或雷达确认信息。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Keith Martin, Mearle Haurie

**Date / Time:** October 14, 1968, at 7:35 PM MST

**Location:** Highway 95, approximately 24 miles north of Kimberley, BC, near Skookumchuck, BC.

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 14, 1968, Keith Martin (of 2385 Warren Ave., Kimberley, BC) and Mearle Haurie (of Invermere, BC) were traveling south on Highway 95 in separate private vehicles when they encountered an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sky was reported as clear at the time of the sighting. Both witnesses observed the object for approximately two minutes. Mearle Haurie utilized 10-power binoculars to gain a closer look at the object during the encounter. According to the witnesses, the object hovered for a short duration before executing an extreme burst of speed, traveling toward the east. It moved over the mountain peaks and eventually disappeared over the horizon.

**Object:** The object was described as a spherical ball of white light. A distinct feature noted by the witnesses was the presence of two square-shaped "windows" on the surface of the sphere. The light emitted by the object was observed to be pulsating. The object was estimated to be hovering at an altitude of approximately 500 feet above the ground surface before it accelerated away. No specific sound was reported during the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by the Kimberley Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Official notes from the RCMP indicate that both Keith Martin and Mearle Haurie were interviewed and deemed to be sound and reliable sources. The investigation remained active following the initial report, with a follow-up report scheduled to be filed by the Cranbrook Detachment of the RCMP.

**目击者：** 基思·马丁 (Keith Martin)、米尔·豪里 (Mearle Haurie)

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年10月14日，晚上7:35（山区标准时间）

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省金伯利以北约24英里处的95号高速公路，靠近同省的斯库库姆查克 (Skookumchuck)。

**目击经过：** 1968年10月14日晚，基思·马丁（居住于不列颠哥伦比亚省金伯利市沃伦大道2385号）和米尔·豪里（居住于不列颠哥伦比亚省因弗米尔）分别驾驶私家车沿95号高速公路向南行驶时，遭遇了不明空中现象。据报告，目击当时天空晴朗。两位目击者观察该物体约两分钟。在遭遇过程中，米尔·豪里使用了10倍双筒望远镜以近距离观察该物体。据目击者称，该物体在短暂停留后突然以极快的速度向东飞去，越过山峰，最终消失在地平线上。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 金伯利分队记录在案。加拿大皇家骑警的官方记录显示，基思·马丁和米尔·豪里均接受了访谈，被认为是可靠的信息来源。初步报告提交后，调查仍在继续，并计划由加拿大皇家骑警克兰布鲁克分队提交后续报告。
