CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lyndia Arychuk, A. Goller (Mackenzie River School Principal), W. Garolitz, J. Bonnetrouge, Phillip Davies, and an unknown observer.

**Date / Time:** December 19, 1968, at 7:15 PM MST.

**Location:** Three miles east of Fort Providence, Northwest Territories.

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 19, 1968, multiple witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon under clear, dark sky conditions. The event began at approximately 7:15 PM MST. The witnesses, including Lyndia Arychuk, A. Goller, W. Garolitz, J. Bonnetrouge, Phillip Davies, and an unknown observer, monitored the object for a duration of twenty minutes. 

Phillip Davies, who was driving south on the highway toward Fort Providence, reported that the object hovered directly over his vehicle before moving to hover over trees located to the west of the highway. Other observers watched the object from a stationary position three miles east of the town. The witnesses utilized a thirty-power telescope to gain a closer look at the object, which remained approximately 300 feet above the ground. Despite its hovering behavior, the object did not remain in one fixed spot for the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** The object was initially described as a red ball, which subsequently changed color to white. Through the thirty-power telescope, observers noted that the object featured dark spots or craters on its surface and appeared to discharge gases, which seemed to facilitate its movement. Regarding its structural form, Phillip Davies described the object as having a stubby, cigar-shaped bottom section topped with a shorter, rectangular upper section.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The object remained unidentified by all observers present. The documentation notes that the main body of the object was visible for twenty minutes. Official follow-up actions were initiated, with the RCMP in Fort Smith tasked with filing a formal report on the incident.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 琳迪亚·阿里丘克 (Lyndia Arychuk)、A. 戈勒 (A. Goller，麦肯齐河学校校长)、W. 加罗利茨 (W. Garolitz)、J. 博内特鲁日 (J. Bonnetrouge)、菲利普·戴维斯 (Phillip Davies) 以及一名身份不明的观察者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月19日，山区标准时间 (MST) 晚上7:15。

**地点：** 西北地区，普罗维登斯堡 (Fort Providence) 以东三英里处。

**目击经过：** 1968年12月19日晚，在晴朗黑暗的天空下，多名目击者观察到了一种不明空中现象。事件始于山区标准时间晚上7:15左右。包括琳迪亚·阿里丘克、A. 戈勒、W. 加罗利茨、J. 博内特鲁日、菲利普·戴维斯以及一名身份不明的观察者在内的目击者对该物体进行了长达二十分钟的观测。

当时正驾车沿公路向普罗维登斯堡方向南行的菲利普·戴维斯报告称，该物体曾直接悬停在他的车辆上方，随后移动并悬停在公路西侧的树木上方。其他观察者则在距离小镇以东三英里的固定位置进行了观测。目击者使用了一台30倍望远镜近距离观察该物体，当时它距离地面约300英尺。尽管该物体表现出悬停行为，但在整个目击过程中，它并未固定在某一个位置。

**物体描述：** 该物体最初被描述为一个红色的球体，随后颜色变为白色。通过30倍望远镜，观察者注意到该物体表面有黑点或陨石坑，并似乎在排放气体，这些气体似乎有助于其移动。关于其结构形态，菲利普·戴维斯描述称，该物体底部呈短粗的雪茄状，顶部则是一个较短的矩形部分。

**调查/后续：** 在场的所有观察者均无法识别该物体。记录显示，该物体的主体可见时间持续了二十分钟。官方已启动后续行动，由史密斯堡 (Fort Smith) 的加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 负责就此事件提交正式报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A local Justice of the Peace, one unnamed resident (operator of a D-6 cat vehicle), Mr. [Name Redacted], his son, his wife, and other unnamed individuals.

**Date / Time:** December 11, 1968 (5:00 P.M. – 8:00 P.M.); December 22, 1968 (approx. 9:00 A.M.); December 27, 1968 (5:00 P.M.).

**Location:** Fort Norman, NWT (specifically 15 miles west of the settlement and near the Mackenzie River/McKay Mountain Range).

**Sighting:** 
The case file documents a series of sightings in the Fort Norman area during December 1968. On December 11, between 5:00 P.M. and 8:00 P.M., a resident, his wife, his son, and others observed 10 objects moving in continuous straight lines across the sky in various directions. 

On December 22 at approximately 9:00 A.M., a more localized event occurred 15 miles west of Fort Norman. A resident operating a D-6 cat vehicle with his headlights on was startled by a sudden, intense brightness. He looked up to see an object for 5 to 6 seconds and immediately alerted a second witness—a local Justice of the Peace—who was standing nearby. The Justice of the Peace observed the object for 2 to 3 seconds before it disappeared behind the tree line. 

On December 27 at 5:00 P.M., a group of observers witnessed a UFO across the Mackenzie River near the McKay Mountain Range. This object remained in view for 3 to 5 minutes until the observers moved indoors.

**Object:** 
The December 11 objects were described as star-sized and at a very high altitude. The December 22 object was described as a round, pinkish-colored fireball, approximately 2 feet in diameter, with an 8-foot tail of fire. It traveled in a southerly direction at an estimated altitude of 100 feet above the trees before making an abrupt descent behind the tree line. The witnesses explicitly stated it did not resemble a meteor. The December 27 object appeared as a large star, shifting in color from white to red, hovering over the mountain tops at an approximate altitude of 2,000 feet and moving slowly.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP conducted investigations into these reports. Regarding the December 22 sighting, the reporting officer deemed both witnesses (including the Justice of the Peace) to be reliable and not prone to fabrication; however, no definitive conclusion was reached. Regarding the December 11 sightings, the RCMP concluded the 10 objects were likely meteors or satellites. The December 27 sighting was initially linked to the December 11 report (file 68-400-15) and theorized to be a bright planet or satellite. While the official record acknowledges that some sightings remained unexplained, the RCMP determined that no further investigation was warranted, and the file was concluded.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一位当地治安法官、一名未具名的居民（D-6型推土机操作员）、[姓名已删除]先生及其妻子和儿子，以及其他未具名人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月11日（下午5:00 – 晚上8:00）；1968年12月22日（约上午9:00）；1968年12月27日（下午5:00）。

**地点：** 西北地区诺曼堡（Fort Norman）（具体位于定居点以西15英里处，靠近马更些河/麦凯山脉）。

**目击经过：**
该案卷记录了1968年12月期间在诺曼堡地区发生的一系列目击事件。12月11日下午5点至晚上8点之间，一名居民及其妻子、儿子和其他人观察到10个物体在天空中沿直线持续向不同方向移动。

12月22日上午9点左右，在诺曼堡以西15英里处发生了一起更为局部的事件。一名正在驾驶D-6型推土机的居民在开启车头灯时，被突如其来的强烈光亮惊吓到。他抬头看到一个物体持续了5到6秒，并立即提醒了附近的一名目击者——一位当地的治安法官。治安法官观察了该物体2到3秒，随后它消失在树线后方。

12月27日下午5点，一群观察者在马更些河对岸靠近麦凯山脉的地方目击了一个不明飞行物。该物体在观察者进入室内前，持续可见了3到5分钟。

**物体描述：**
12月11日的物体被描述为星体大小，且处于极高的高度。12月22日的物体被描述为一个圆形的粉红色火球，直径约2英尺，拖着一条8英尺长的火尾。它以约100英尺的高度在树木上方朝南飞行，随后突然下降至树线后方。目击者明确表示它看起来不像流星。12月27日的物体看起来像一颗大星星，颜色在白色和红色之间变换，悬停在山顶上方约2000英尺的高度，并缓慢移动。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对这些报告进行了调查。关于12月22日的目击事件，负责警官认为两名目击者（包括治安法官）均非常可靠，且不会编造事实；然而，调查并未得出明确结论。关于12月11日的目击事件，加拿大皇家骑警得出结论，认为那10个物体很可能是流星或卫星。12月27日的目击事件最初被归入12月11日的报告（档案号68-400-15），并被推测为一颗明亮的行星或卫星。尽管官方记录承认部分目击事件仍无法解释，但加拿大皇家骑警认定无需进一步调查，该档案随之结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cpl. Hawboldt, Cst. W.S. King, Cst. A.F. Hatchette, and unnamed civilians.

**Date / Time:** December 28, 1968; initial sighting at 7:30 PM NST (Cst. Hatchette), primary event from 7:55 PM to 8:10 PM NST.

**Location:** Grand Falls, Newfoundland; specifically the Exploits River, Bishops Falls, Jumpers Brook, the TCH bridge over the Exploits River, and the CJCN-TV (also referred to as OCN-TV) transmitter at Grenfell Heights.

**Sighting:** The event began earlier in the evening when Cst. A.F. Hatchette observed a light moving west out of Exploits Bay at 7:30 PM NST. The primary sighting commenced at 7:55 PM NST, involving Cpl. Hawboldt, Cst. W.S. King, and Cst. A.F. Hatchette, alongside reports from civilians. The object was first observed at an altitude of approximately 1,000 feet, traveling along the head of the Exploits River toward Bishops Falls. 

At Jumpers Brook, the object came to a stop near the Price Newfoundland Ltd. powerhouse, remaining stationary for two to three minutes. It was subsequently observed from the TCH bridge over the Exploits River, appearing to maintain an altitude of less than 1,000 feet. The object then moved northwest toward the CJCN-TV (OCN-TV) transmitter at Grenfell Heights, Grand Falls, where it hovered stationary for another two to three minutes. Following this, the object moved rapidly in a northeasterly direction and disappeared over the horizon. While an initial report incorrectly stated the object disappeared in the northeast, a subsequent correction clarified that the final movement and disappearance occurred in the northwest (though later reports reconcile this by noting a complex path: moving northwest, then north, then finally northeast).

**Object:** The object was described as a single, bright white light with an amber tinge. It exhibited the ability to brighten and dim slowly. In terms of movement, it initially traveled at a speed comparable to a helicopter; however, during its final departure, it was noted to move very rapidly. The total duration of the primary observation was 15 minutes (7:55 PM to 8:10 PM NST).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported and documented by the Grand Falls Highway Patrol. The RCMP St. John’s sub-division initiated an investigation into the incident, which included the collection of civilian reports to corroborate the observations made by the officers. Official documentation includes a correction regarding the final trajectory of the object to ensure accuracy in the flight path records.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 霍博尔特下士 (Cpl. Hawboldt)、金警官 (Cst. W.S. King)、哈切特警官 (Cst. A.F. Hatchette) 以及多名未具名的平民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月28日；首次目击时间为纽芬兰标准时间 (NST) 晚上7:30（哈切特警官），主要事件发生于晚上7:55至8:10。

**地点：** 纽芬兰大瀑布镇 (Grand Falls)；具体涉及埃克斯普洛伊茨河 (Exploits River)、毕晓普斯瀑布 (Bishops Falls)、詹珀斯布鲁克 (Jumpers Brook)、横跨埃克斯普洛伊茨河的跨加拿大公路 (TCH) 大桥，以及位于格伦费尔高地 (Grenfell Heights) 的 CJCN-TV（亦称 OCN-TV）发射塔。

**目击经过：** 事件始于当晚较早时分，哈切特警官于纽芬兰标准时间晚上7:30观察到一个光点从埃克斯普洛伊茨湾向西移动。主要目击事件始于晚上7:55，参与者包括霍博尔特下士、金警官和哈切特警官，此外还有多名平民的报告。该物体最初在约1,000英尺的高度被发现，沿埃克斯普洛伊茨河源头向毕晓普斯瀑布方向移动。

在詹珀斯布鲁克，该物体在普莱斯纽芬兰有限公司 (Price Newfoundland Ltd.) 的发电厂附近停下，并保持静止状态两到三分钟。随后，人们从横跨埃克斯普洛伊茨河的 TCH 大桥上观察到它，其高度似乎保持在1,000英尺以下。接着，该物体向西北方向移动至大瀑布镇格伦费尔高地的 CJCN-TV (OCN-TV) 发射塔，并在该处再次悬停静止了两到三分钟。此后，该物体迅速向东北方向移动并消失在地平线上。虽然最初的一份报告错误地称该物体在东北方向消失，但随后的更正说明其最终移动方向和消失位置是在西北方（尽管后来的报告通过指出其复杂的飞行路径——先向西北，再向北，最后向东北——调和了这一矛盾）。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个带有琥珀色光晕的明亮白光。它表现出缓慢变亮和变暗的能力。在移动方面，它最初的飞行速度与直升机相当；但在最后离开时，其移动速度极快。主要观测过程的总持续时间为15分钟（纽芬兰标准时间晚上7:55至8:10）。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件由大瀑布镇公路巡警队报告并记录。加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 圣约翰斯分部对该事件展开了调查，其中包括收集平民报告以佐证警官们的观察结果。官方文档中包含了一份关于该物体最终轨迹的更正说明，以确保飞行路径记录的准确性。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A female civilian, two CBC employees, Mrs. [Name Redacted] (a licensed astronomer), and Cst. D.J. Morrison (RCMP).

**Date / Time:** December 30, 1968; sightings reported around 5:30 p.m.

**Location:** Corner Brook, Deer Lake, and St. John’s, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 30, 1968, multiple reports of unidentified objects in the sky were filed across Newfoundland. A female civilian reported observing a large object hovering over the Blomidon Golf Course for approximately one hour before it disappeared. Conversely, two CBC employees in Corner Brook reported seeing a jet aircraft pass over the area; they observed a yellowish glow that shifted into red and blue, creating a rainbow-like effect that lasted for twenty minutes before dissolving. They explicitly noted the absence of any metal object or unusual noise. 

Other reports from the region described objects that appeared to be "jumping" or "vibrating" in the sky. One report (SD4054), following up on an initial report (SD4046), noted that at its closest point, the object appeared to be the size of a large helicopter. Observers noted that there was no noise discernible from the object above the ambient level of local vehicle traffic.

**Object:** Descriptions varied significantly by witness. The female civilian described a large, reddish metal object with a revolving light beneath it. The CBC employees described a glowing, multi-colored (yellow, red, blue) light effect. Other reports characterized the object as being the size of a large helicopter. Movement was described by some as hovering, while others perceived a "jumping" or "vibrating" motion.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation into the various reports. Cst. D.J. Morrison of the Corner Brook City Detachment submitted the final findings for information purposes. The investigation concluded that many of the sightings were attributable to a bright star visible in the Western sky from sunset until 9:00 p.m. and later, which was corroborated by members of the police force. 

Furthermore, a licensed astronomer from Deer Lake was consulted regarding the reports of "vibrating" objects. She identified the source as the planet Venus, explaining that the perceived movement was an optical illusion caused by high atmospheric pressure and heavy atmospheric conditions, including haze, clouds, and smoke. The CBC employees' observation was attributed to a jet aircraft leaving a vapor trail, which created an optical illusion when refracted by the sun's rays. The RCMP ultimately classified the incident as the planet Venus, while noting that such reports are often categorized as meteors, fireballs, or UFOs.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名女性平民、两名加拿大广播公司（CBC）员工、[姓名已删除]女士（持证天文学家）以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员 D.J. 莫里森（D.J. Morrison）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月30日；目击报告时间约为下午5:30。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省的科纳布鲁克（Corner Brook）、鹿湖（Deer Lake）及圣约翰斯（St. John’s）。

**目击经过：** 1968年12月30日傍晚，纽芬兰全省各地接连收到多起关于空中不明物体的报告。一名女性平民报告称，她观察到一个大型物体在布洛米登高尔夫球场（Blomidon Golf Course）上空盘旋了约一小时后消失。与此同时，科纳布鲁克的两名CBC员工报告称看到一架喷气式飞机飞过该地区；他们观察到一种黄色的光芒，随后转变为红色和蓝色，产生了类似彩虹的效果，持续了二十分钟后消散。他们明确指出，现场没有任何金属物体，也没有听到异常噪音。

该地区的其他报告描述称，空中的物体看起来在“跳跃”或“振动”。一份后续报告（SD4054，针对初始报告SD4046）指出，该物体在最近距离时，看起来有大型直升机大小。观察者指出，除了当地车辆交通的背景噪音外，无法从该物体上辨别出任何声音。

**物体描述：** 不同目击者的描述差异很大。该女性平民描述为一个大型的、红色的金属物体，下方有旋转的灯光。CBC员工则描述为一种发光的、多色（黄色、红色、蓝色）的光学效应。其他报告将该物体描述为大型直升机大小。运动方式方面，有人描述为盘旋，而另一些人则观察到“跳跃”或“振动”的动作。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对这些报告进行了调查。科纳布鲁克市分局的 D.J. 莫里森警员提交了最终调查结果以供参考。调查结论认为，许多目击事件可归因于一颗在日落后至晚上9点及之后可见于西方天空的明亮恒星，这一结论得到了警队成员的证实。

此外，调查组就“振动”物体的报告咨询了一位来自鹿湖的持证天文学家。她指出该现象的源头是金星，并解释称所谓的运动是由高气压及浓重的气象条件（包括霾、云层和烟雾）所导致的视觉错觉。CBC员工的观察结果则被归因于喷气式飞机留下的凝结尾迹，在阳光折射下产生了视觉错觉。加拿大皇家骑警最终将该事件归类为金星，并指出此类报告常被误认为是流星、火球或不明飞行物（UFO）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Walter Webster (salesman), Arlene Webster, Ernest Webster (Assistant Manager, Civic Properties Commission), Donald Cook (B.C. Bearing and Engineering / service station attendant), Grant Magnuson (B.C. Bearing and Engineering / customer), Mr. and Mrs. Victor Imhoff, Mr. William McLeod, Mr. Martin Pearson, Mr. William Dow, Geoff Richmond (postal clerk) and his wife and three children.

**Date / Time:** January 1, 1969, between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM PST (with subsequent reports through January 5, 1969).

**Location:** Prince George, B.C., specifically observed while traveling on 5th Avenue near Alward and Burden Streets.

**Sighting:** On January 1, 1969, at approximately 5:20 PM, Walter Webster observed an object while traveling on 5th Avenue and alerted Donald Cook and Grant Magnuson at a service station. Geoff Richmond reported observing an object at approximately 5:30 PM while driving on the same street. Later that evening, between 6:30 PM and 7:00 PM, Ernest Webster and his family observed the object. Mr. and Mrs. Victor Imhoff reported seeing a dull orange object approximately 200 feet off the ground while traveling in a taxi on January 1. Additional reports were received from Mr. William McLeod and Mr. Martin Pearson. The sightings occurred in clear weather conditions, with the duration of the initial observations lasting between 1 and 1.5 hours.

**Object:** The object was generally described as round or spherical, emitting a radiant yellowish-orange glow. Walter Webster described it as one-eighth the size of the moon, featuring a square attachment on the bottom and diagonal straps across the top. While Cook and Magnuson corroborated the general appearance, they did not observe the square attachment. Arlene Webster noted the object appeared to fluctuate between dull and bright. Ernest Webster observed a radiant orange glow that would disappear and reappear much fainter. Geoff Richmond described the object as one-twentieth the size of the moon. The object moved straight up, gaining altitude estimated between 2,000 and 10,000 feet, with no audible sound reported by any witness.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP collected statements from the witnesses and documented the complaints. Initial inquiries with the Department of Transport Radio Sound suggested the object could have been a floating weather balloon. However, on January 4, 1969, an object was recovered in the backyard of Mr. William Dow. It was identified as a plastic laundry bag constructed with a circular frame made of drinking straws. A cross made of straws held birthday candles attached with straight pins, and the bag was sealed at the top with Scotch Tape. The RCMP concluded that the sightings were likely these "hot air" devices—plastic bags lifted by candle heat—or floating balloons, potentially constructed by children. The investigating officer determined that the reports from the Websters, Cook, Magnuson, Richmond, and the Imhoffs were consistent with these homemade devices.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 沃尔特·韦伯斯特（Walter Webster，推销员）、阿琳·韦伯斯特（Arlene Webster）、欧内斯特·韦伯斯特（Ernest Webster，市政资产委员会助理经理）、唐纳德·库克（Donald Cook，不列颠哥伦比亚轴承与工程公司员工/加油站服务员）、格兰特·马格努森（Grant Magnuson，不列颠哥伦比亚轴承与工程公司客户）、维克多·伊姆霍夫夫妇（Mr. and Mrs. Victor Imhoff）、威廉·麦克劳德先生（Mr. William McLeod）、马丁·皮尔逊先生（Mr. Martin Pearson）、威廉·道先生（Mr. William Dow）、杰夫·里士满（Geoff Richmond，邮政职员）及其妻子和三个孩子。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月1日，太平洋标准时间下午5:00至7:00之间（后续报告持续至1969年1月5日）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省乔治王子城，具体观测点位于靠近阿尔沃德街（Alward Street）和伯登街（Burden Street）的第五大道（5th Avenue）沿线。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月1日下午5:20左右，沃尔特·韦伯斯特在第五大道行驶时发现了一个物体，并提醒了加油站的唐纳德·库克和格兰特·马格努森。杰夫·里士满报告称，他在下午5:30左右驾车经过同一条街道时也观察到了该物体。当晚6:30至7:00之间，欧内斯特·韦伯斯特及其家人也观察到了该物体。维克多·伊姆霍夫夫妇报告称，1月1日他们乘坐出租车时，看到一个距离地面约200英尺的暗橙色物体。此外，威廉·麦克劳德先生和马丁·皮尔逊先生也提交了报告。目击事件发生时天气晴朗，最初的观测持续时间在1至1.5小时之间。

**物体描述：** 该物体通常被描述为圆形或球形，散发着耀眼的黄橙色光芒。沃尔特·韦伯斯特将其描述为月球大小的八分之一，底部有一个方形附件，顶部有对角线状的带子。库克和马格努森证实了其大致外观，但并未观察到方形附件。阿琳·韦伯斯特指出，该物体的亮度在暗淡和明亮之间波动。欧内斯特·韦伯斯特观察到一种耀眼的橙色光芒，它会消失并再次出现，但亮度要暗得多。杰夫·里士满则描述该物体的大小约为月球的二十分之一。物体垂直向上移动，飞行高度估计在2,000至10,000英尺之间，所有目击者均表示未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）收集了目击者的证词并记录了投诉。交通部无线电探测部门的初步调查认为，该物体可能是一个漂浮的气象气球。然而，1969年1月4日，威廉·道先生的后院发现了一个物体。经鉴定，这是一个由吸管制作的圆形框架支撑的塑料洗衣袋。十字形的吸管架上用大头针固定着生日蜡烛，袋子顶部用透明胶带密封。加拿大皇家骑警得出结论，目击事件很可能是由这些“热气”装置（由蜡烛热量升空的塑料袋）或漂浮气球引起的，可能是由儿童制作的。调查警官认定，韦伯斯特一家、库克、马格努森、里士满以及伊姆霍夫夫妇的报告与这些自制装置的特征相符。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. Roland Johnston (also recorded as Johnson)

**Date / Time:** January 30, 1969, at approximately 9:30 PM – 9:35 PM MST

**Location:** Crossfield, Alberta area; specifically identified as 4 miles west and 1.5 miles south of Crossfield, and near the witnesses' farm 14 miles south of Crossfield.

**Sighting:** On the night of January 30, 1969, Mr. and Mrs. Roland Johnston observed an unidentified object while in their truck near their farm. The weather was clear with no haze, though temperatures were approximately thirty degrees below zero. Mrs. Johnston, an amateur astronomer, initially mistook the object for a meteorite, but upon closer inspection, both witnesses observed windows along the object's contour. The object traveled from west to east at an estimated speed exceeding 500 mph. The witnesses, who were at their farmhouse at the time of the report, noted that the area is isolated, with no other occupied residences within a one-mile radius. Mr. Johnston, a foreman at a local petrochemical plant, explicitly ruled out the possibility that the sighting was an optical illusion caused by the plant’s smoke, steam, or the nearby flare pit located to the northwest. The sighting lasted between five and ten seconds before the object and its lights disappeared suddenly. No noise was heard during the event.

**Object:** The craft was described as dark and disc-shaped. Estimates of its size varied slightly in the reports, ranging from the length of a large aeroplane window to the length of a large aeroplane. It featured glowing yellow lights along its sides and a long, pointed bright yellow light or exhaust stream trailing from the rear. The object was estimated to be at an altitude of 2,000 to 3,000 feet and approximately one mile away from the observers. The witnesses noted the presence of windows along the object's contour.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by Corporal R.H.W. Pyper of the RCMP Calgary Sub-Division. Cpl. Pyper, who had known Mr. Johnston for two years, characterized him as a reliable, level-headed, and sincere individual. The report notes that neither witness consumes alcohol. Cpl. Pyper concluded that the Johnstons were credible and had witnessed a genuine event, noting that the account provided was the best possible description given the brief duration of the sighting. The incident was documented in Crossfield Message 69/2 and forwarded to the Calgary Sub-Division. No other UFO reports were received from the surrounding area. The investigating officer requested a formal correction to the spelling of the witnesses' surname, noting it had been incorrectly recorded as "Johnson" in earlier telexes.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗兰·约翰斯顿先生和夫人（Roland and Mrs. Roland Johnston，曾被记录为 Johnson）

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月30日，大约晚上9:30至9:35（山区标准时间）

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省克罗斯菲尔德（Crossfield）地区；具体位置为克罗斯菲尔德以西4英里、以南1.5英里处，靠近目击者位于克罗斯菲尔德以南14英里的农场。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月30日晚，罗兰·约翰斯顿夫妇在农场附近的卡车内观察到一个不明物体。当时天气晴朗，没有雾霾，但气温约为零下30度。约翰斯顿夫人是一位业余天文学家，起初误以为该物体是陨石，但经过仔细观察，两人都发现物体轮廓上有窗户。该物体由西向东飞行，估计速度超过每小时500英里。目击者在报告时身处农舍，他们指出该地区非常偏僻，方圆一英里内没有其他住户。约翰斯顿先生是当地一家石油化工厂的领班，他明确排除了该目击事件是由工厂烟雾、蒸汽或西北方附近的火炬坑引起的视错觉的可能性。目击过程持续了五到十秒，随后物体及其灯光突然消失。事件过程中未听到任何声音。

**物体描述：** 该飞行器被描述为深色、圆盘状。报告中对其尺寸的估计略有差异，从大型飞机窗户的长度到大型飞机的长度不等。其侧面有发光的黄色灯光，尾部拖着一道长而尖的明亮黄色光束或尾气流。据估计，该物体飞行高度在2,000至3,000英尺之间，距离观察者约一英里。目击者注意到物体轮廓上有窗户。

**调查/后续：** 调查由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）卡尔加里分局的R.H.W.派珀（R.H.W. Pyper）下士负责。派珀下士认识约翰斯顿先生已有两年，他形容对方是一位可靠、冷静且真诚的人。报告指出，两位目击者均不饮酒。派珀下士得出结论，认为约翰斯顿夫妇是可信的，且确实目击了一起真实事件，并指出鉴于目击时间短暂，他们提供的描述已是尽可能详尽的。该事件被记录在“克罗斯菲尔德消息 69/2”（Crossfield Message 69/2）中，并转交至卡尔加里分局。周边地区未收到其他UFO报告。调查警官要求对目击者的姓氏拼写进行正式更正，指出该姓氏在早期的电传中被错误地记录为“Johnson”。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Marrieann Emelise Castle, a Grade 12 student from Hamiota, Manitoba, and a companion named Bill. The statement was taken by Cst. J.A. Coagie. The case file also references Gerald Richard Grattan.

**Sighting:** The event occurred at approximately 9:45 P.M. while the witnesses were driving west on Provincial Road #469, about two miles west of Hamiota. Although the witness could not recall the specific calendar day during the interview, the case is filed under a 1969 reference number. The sky conditions at the time were not remembered, but it was dark.

**Object:** The object was described as a huge, circular, reddish-orange glowing craft. It was first spotted on the south side of the road and moved away in a south-westerly direction. The witness stated it was "brighter than the moon" and appeared to be twice the size of the moon from their vantage point. It was positioned much higher than the trees and was observed for three to four minutes before it moved away and was obscured by trees. No sounds, bursts, or trails of smoke/color were observed.

**Aftermath:** The document records a formal statement and a detailed question-and-answer session conducted by the RCMP. The witness provided specific details regarding the object's size, color, and movement, despite being unable to pinpoint the exact date of the occurrence.

**Additional pages:** This same incident is also recorded on 2 other pages (p.161, 163) of the same file. Cluster confirmed by shared FOIA record number N69/171.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Marrieann Emelise Castle，一名来自曼尼托巴省哈米奥塔（Hamiota）的12年级学生，以及一名叫作比尔（Bill）的同伴。该陈述由警员 J.A. Coagie 记录。案卷中还提到了 Gerald Richard Grattan。

**目击：** 事件发生在大约晚上9:45，当时目击者正沿着469号省道向西行驶，位于哈米奥塔以西约两英里处。尽管目击者在接受询问时表示记不清具体的日期，但该案卷是以1969年的编号归档的。目击者不记得当时的天气状况，但确认当时天色已黑。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的、圆形的、发出红橙色光芒的飞行器。它最初出现在道路南侧，随后向西南方向飞离。目击者称其“比月亮还亮”，且从他们的视角看，大小是月亮的两倍。物体的位置远高于树木，在飞离并被树木遮挡前，观察时间持续了三到四分钟。目击过程中没有发现任何声音、爆发光或烟雾/颜色拖尾。

**后续：** 该文件记录了一份正式陈述以及由皇家骑警（RCMP）进行的一系列详细问答。尽管目击者无法确定事件发生的准确日期，但她就物体的大小、颜色和运动轨迹提供了详尽的细节。

**其它相关页面：** 本事件在同一档案的其它 2 页（第 161, 163 页）中亦有记录（由共同的 FOIA 编号 N69/171 确认）。

**Witnesses:** William Briant MacMeekin, Tessie Audrey MacMeekin, and Morse Parker Patton.

**Date / Time:** January 5, 1969, at 8:15 PM and 8:30 PM Atlantic Time.

**Location:** Hilden and North River, Colchester County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** The event began when the primary witness (referred to as the "subject") observed significant television interference, characterized by silver streaks appearing across the bottom of the screen and the picture beginning to roll. Prompted by this disturbance, the subject went outside to investigate, initially suspecting that an airplane might be passing overhead. Upon looking toward the western horizon, the subject, accompanied by Tessie Audrey MacMeekin and Morse Parker Patton, observed a mysterious aerial object. The witnesses watched the object for a duration of approximately 25 to 30 minutes, though they did not observe it until the moment of its final disappearance. The object moved very slowly in a north-westerly direction, descending at an oblique angle toward the horizon.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape with a distinct, though not clearly defined, projection on its underside. Its luminosity was exceptionally bright and intense; witnesses compared its brilliance and size to a neighbor’s daylight lamp located approximately 7/10 of a mile away. The object’s color was initially white, but it underwent a gradual transition, shifting through shades of orange before turning red. It was estimated to be at an altitude of approximately 2 miles above the horizon.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The case was documented by the Truro Sub-Division (RCMP). The records consist of multiple sighting reports and interrogation summaries that consistently detail the television interference, the specific color-shifting sequence of the object, and the comparative brightness analysis. No other individuals were reported to have witnessed the event, and the investigation notes conclude with the administrative designation "TRURO S/DIV."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威廉·布莱恩特·麦克米金 (William Briant MacMeekin)、泰西·奥黛丽·麦克米金 (Tessie Audrey MacMeekin) 和莫尔斯·帕克·巴顿 (Morse Parker Patton)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月5日，大西洋时间晚上8:15及8:30。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省科尔切斯特县希尔登 (Hilden) 和北河 (North River)。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，底部有一个明显但不甚清晰的突出物。其亮度异常强烈；目击者将其亮度和大小与约0.7英里外邻居家的日光灯进行了对比。物体的颜色起初为白色，随后逐渐发生变化，在转为红色之前经历了橙色的色调过渡。据估计，该物体位于地平线上方约2英里处。

**调查/后续：** 该案件由特鲁罗 (Truro) 分局（加拿大皇家骑警，RCMP）记录在案。档案包含多份目击报告和审讯摘要，其中详细记录了电视干扰情况、物体特定的变色顺序以及亮度对比分析。据报告，没有其他人目击到此次事件，调查记录以行政代号“TRURO S/DIV”结尾。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** D.H. Oldershaw (Assistant Provincial Apiarist), Dal Heservy (also referred to as D. Meservy), and J. Meservy.

**Date / Time:** December 14, 1968, between 6:45 a.m. and 6:53 a.m.

**Location:** Mile 22, Alaska Highway, British Columbia (c/o Farmington P.O.).

**Sighting:** The three men were positioned on a hill overlooking two meadows, observing the sky in clear, star-visible conditions with a surface temperature of -20°F. D.H. Oldershaw, who noted his professional background in photography, microscopy, and optics, emphasized that observations were made in the open with no obstructions between the observers and the subject. Distances were calculated using known landmarks and tree lines.

The object was first spotted through the silhouettes of a first line of trees, with a second range of trees beyond. The witnesses observed the light moving in a series of straight-line, non-accelerated maneuvers. Initially, it moved in a westerly direction before stopping for one full minute. It then dropped approximately 3,500 feet in a south-westerly direction, stopping abruptly. The object’s flight path included traveling northwest parallel to the earth’s surface, shifting to an almost due east course, moving southwesterly, and finally heading due north until it diminished in size. At one point, the object moved upward vertically, dropped lower than its original position, rose to a midpoint, and remained stationary. 

When Dal Heservy flashed the car headlights at the object, it moved toward the witnesses, stopping between the first line of trees and the car at a distance of approximately one mile. After remaining there briefly, it sped away into the northern sky, disappearing in about two seconds.

**Object:** The witnesses reported seeing only a light, with no solid form visible. The light was described as being the size of a 3/8-inch disc, exhibiting constant brightness rather than the beam of a conventional aircraft. It displayed two distinct color phases: a pure pale green and a bright transparent white. The object remained in critical focus throughout the sighting, never appearing fuzzy or diffused, and produced no audible noise.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was submitted by D.H. Oldershaw to the Radio & Electrical Engineering division of the National Research Council in Ottawa. The documentation includes a section titled "Points of Scientific Interest" and is cataloged with the file reference "M45-1-101." Oldershaw explicitly stated his qualifications in optics to preemptively address potential concerns regarding optical artifacts or aberrations.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** D.H. 奥尔德肖（D.H. Oldershaw，省助理养蜂专家）、达尔·赫瑟维（Dal Heservy，亦被称为 D. 梅瑟维 D. Meservy）以及 J. 梅瑟维（J. Meservy）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月14日，上午6:45至6:53之间。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省，阿拉斯加公路22英里处（法明顿邮局转交）。

**目击经过：** 三名男子当时位于俯瞰两片草地的小山上，在天空晴朗、星光可见、地表温度为华氏零下20度（约摄氏零下29度）的环境下进行观测。D.H. 奥尔德肖特别提到他在摄影、显微镜学和光学方面的专业背景，并强调观测是在开阔地带进行的，观察者与目标之间没有任何遮挡物。距离是通过已知的地标和树线计算得出的。

该物体最初是在第一排树木的轮廓中被发现的，其后方还有第二排树木。目击者观察到该光点进行了一系列直线、非加速的机动飞行。起初，它向西移动，随后停顿了整整一分钟。接着，它向西南方向下降了约3500英尺，并突然停止。该物体的飞行路径包括：平行于地表向西北方向飞行，转向几乎正东方向，向西南方向移动，最后向正北方向飞去，直到其尺寸变小直至消失。在某一时刻，该物体垂直向上移动，随后降至低于其原始位置的高度，又升至中点，并保持静止。

当达尔·赫瑟维用汽车前灯向该物体闪烁示意时，它向目击者方向移动，停在第一排树木与汽车之间，距离约为一英里。在短暂停留后，它加速飞向北方天空，并在约两秒钟内消失。

**物体描述：** 目击者报告称只看到了光，没有看到任何固体形态。该光点被描述为大小如一枚3/8英寸的圆盘，呈现出恒定的亮度，而非传统飞行器的光束。它表现出两种截然不同的颜色阶段：纯淡绿色和明亮的透明白色。在整个目击过程中，该物体始终保持清晰对焦，从未显得模糊或弥散，且未产生任何可听见的噪音。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由 D.H. 奥尔德肖提交给渥太华国家研究委员会的无线电与电气工程部门。文件包含一个名为“科学兴趣点”的章节，并被编入档案，参考编号为“M45-1-101”。奥尔德肖明确陈述了他的光学资质，以预先回应关于光学伪影或像差的潜在质疑。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Jack (Edith) Rose, Jerome Rose, Aux. Member Reginald Parsons, S/Sgt F.J.H. Gorrell, Cpl. D. Sear, Csts. C.A. Stewart (V. Stewart), J.W. Trenholm, D.J. Barrett, L.P. Marshall, K.B. MacDougall, J.H. MacNeil (Mackeil), G.D.T. Clark, and C.F. Parlee.

**Date / Time:** January 9, 1969; sighting duration from 7:30 PM to 8:24 PM NST.

**Location:** Northwest of Harbour Grace and Bell Island, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 9, 1969, a significant UFO event occurred northwest of Harbour Grace, involving multiple RCMP officers and civilian witnesses. Mrs. Jack Rose and Jerome Rose were among the primary observers. At approximately 7:30 PM, the object was first sighted under weather conditions described as cloudy with infrequent clear intervals. 

Accounts of the object’s behavior varied among the witnesses. Some observers reported the object as stationary, while others noted it moving alternately north and south, or moving west and then back to the northwest several times. One RCMP officer, while driving on No. 2 Road at 7:55 PM, observed the object moving at a downward angle of approximately 45 degrees toward the west at a speed faster than an aircraft but slower than a falling star. This officer noted the object would periodically fade to a point before reappearing three to four seconds later. The sighting lasted for approximately 40 to 54 minutes, with the object eventually disappearing near the western horizon around 8:24 PM. No sound, smoke, or vapor trails were reported by any witnesses.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright light, significantly brighter than the North Star, the moon, and other surrounding stars. Its shape was a subject of debate, with witnesses describing it as alternating between circular and triangular. It emitted a bright orange color that shifted to red at frequent or infrequent intervals. Mr. Rose and Cst. MacDougall attempted to view the object through 7x50 power binoculars, though they reported it remained impossible to see clearly.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted a multi-detachment investigation involving members from Harbour Grace, Bell Island, and St. John’s. Despite the number of official witnesses, the RCMP concluded that no specific shape could be definitively established and that no further action was necessary. A formal report was transmitted to the NRC Meteor Centre by the RCMP. Subsequent internal correspondence, including a memorandum from the O.C. St. John’s dated February 14, 1969, and a final file note dated February 27, 1969, confirmed that the investigation was closed with no further action to be taken.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 杰克·罗斯夫人（伊迪丝·罗斯）、杰罗姆·罗斯、辅助警员雷金纳德·帕森斯、参谋军士F.J.H.戈雷尔、下士D.西尔、警员C.A.斯图尔特（V.斯图尔特）、J.W.特伦霍姆、D.J.巴雷特、L.P.马歇尔、K.B.麦克杜格尔、J.H.麦克尼尔（麦克伊尔）、G.D.T.克拉克以及C.F.帕利。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月9日；目击持续时间为纽芬兰标准时间（NST）晚上7:30至8:24。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省海港格雷斯（Harbour Grace）及贝尔岛（Bell Island）西北部。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月9日晚，海港格雷斯西北部发生了一起重大的不明飞行物事件，多名加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员及平民目击了该过程。杰克·罗斯夫人和杰罗姆·罗斯是主要观察者。晚上7:30左右，该物体首次被发现，当时天气状况为多云，间或有晴朗间隙。

目击者对该物体行为的描述各不相同。一些观察者称该物体处于静止状态，而另一些人则注意到它交替向北和向南移动，或向西移动后又多次返回西北方向。一名加拿大皇家骑警警员在晚上7:55驾车行驶在2号公路上时，观察到该物体以约45度的向下角度向西移动，速度比飞机快，但比流星慢。该警员指出，物体会周期性地变暗至消失，三到四秒后又重新出现。目击过程持续了约40至54分钟，最终该物体于晚上8:24左右在西地平线附近消失。没有任何目击者报告听到声音、看到烟雾或尾迹。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一团明亮的光，亮度显著超过北极星、月亮及周围的其他恒星。其形状存在争议，目击者称其在圆形和三角形之间交替变换。它发出明亮的橙色光，并频繁或不定期地转变为红色。罗斯先生和麦克杜格尔警员曾尝试用7x50倍双筒望远镜观察该物体，但报告称仍无法看清其细节。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警进行了跨分局调查，涉及海港格雷斯、贝尔岛和圣约翰斯分局的成员。尽管有众多官方目击者，但骑警最终认定无法确定其具体形状，且无需采取进一步行动。加拿大皇家骑警向国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心提交了正式报告。随后的内部通信，包括圣约翰斯指挥官于1969年2月14日发出的备忘录以及1969年2月27日的最终档案记录，确认调查已结案，不再采取进一步行动。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月9日，纽芬兰标准时间晚上7:30至8:24。

**地点：** 纽芬兰哈伯格雷斯（Harbour Grace，特别是基琴斯山 Kitchens Hill 一带）及贝尔岛（Bell Island，2号公路）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Fred Lincoln (a Native Indian employee at the North Pacific Fish Cannery).

**Date / Time:** January 13, 1969, at 5:00 PM PST; and January 14, 1969, at approximately 5:30 PM PST.

**Location:** North Pacific Fish Cannery, near Port Edward, BC.

**Sighting:** There is a discrepancy in the provided records regarding the date of the sighting, with reports citing both January 13 and January 14, 1969. Fred Lincoln, the sole witness, observed an unidentified flying object in clear weather conditions. On the 13th, the object was sighted over the North Pacific near Port Edward. On the 14th, the witness observed the object traveling from South to North directly over the North Pacific Fish Cannery. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately five minutes, during which the object moved at an estimated speed of 50 to 100 mph before disappearing slowly.

**Object:** The object was described as a dirigible-shaped balloon, approximately 20 feet in diameter and 30 to 40 feet in length. It was grey in color and featured small stabilizer fins on the rear. Notably, the object had no lights and produced no motor sound. A distinct feature noted by the witness was a trailing object at the leading end, described as a mooring cable or rope approximately 5 feet in length. The object maintained an altitude estimated between 1,000 and 3,000 feet throughout the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the Prince Rupert Sub-Division of the RCMP. Initial suspicions suggested the object might be a weather balloon; however, official follow-up inquiries were conducted to verify this hypothesis. The Meteorological Station at Digby Island, BC, confirmed that no weather balloons had been released in the area at the time of the sighting. Furthermore, the Air Sea Rescue Coordinator and the Air Transport Command in Vancouver were contacted; both agencies advised that the object’s description did not match that of a standard weather balloon. Following these negative identifications, the official investigation was discontinued.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 弗雷德·林肯（Fred Lincoln，北太平洋鱼类罐头厂的一名原住民员工）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月13日下午5:00（太平洋标准时间）；以及1969年1月14日下午约5:30（太平洋标准时间）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省爱德华港附近的北太平洋鱼类罐头厂。

**目击经过：** 现有记录中关于目击日期的记载存在出入，报告中同时提到了1969年1月13日和1月14日。唯一的目击者弗雷德·林肯在天气晴朗的情况下观测到了一个不明飞行物。13日，该物体出现在爱德华港附近的北太平洋上空。14日，目击者观察到该物体从南向北直接飞越了北太平洋鱼类罐头厂。目击过程持续了约五分钟，期间该物体以估计每小时50至100英里的速度移动，随后缓慢消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个飞艇形状的气球，直径约20英尺，长30至40英尺。它呈灰色，尾部带有小型稳定鳍。值得注意的是，该物体没有灯光，也没有发出任何引擎声。目击者注意到的一个显著特征是其前端拖着一个物体，被描述为一根约5英尺长的系泊缆绳或绳索。在整个观测过程中，该物体保持在估计1,000至3,000英尺的高度。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件已报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）鲁珀特王子港分部。最初的怀疑认为该物体可能是一个气象气球；然而，官方随后进行了后续调查以核实这一假设。位于不列颠哥伦比亚省迪格比岛的气象站证实，在目击事件发生时，该地区并未释放任何气象气球。此外，温哥华的海空救援协调中心和航空运输司令部也受到了联络；这两个机构均表示，该物体的描述与标准气象气球不符。在这些否定性鉴定结果出炉后，官方调查宣告终止。

**Witnesses:** An unnamed female, Augustus Kenny, and Ross Rendell (both employees of C.B.C., Corner Brook), and members of the RCMP.

No alarm was reported among the public.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Four unnamed employees of Mount Nansen Mines (including a driver and two passengers in one vehicle), an unnamed civilian employee of Nansen Mines Ltd., an unnamed civilian (witness to the Dec 1968 event), and one additional unnamed individual. RCMP officers involved include Cst. G.J. Jared and Cpl. M.D. Walker.

**Date / Time:** January 20, 1969, between 9:00 p.m. and 9:45 p.m. (Additional sighting reported December 17, 1968, at 8:00 p.m., and late November 1968 at 6:00 p.m.).

**Location:** Mount Nansen Road, Carmacks, Yukon (specifically between Mile 5, Mile 15, and near Victoria Creek).

**Sighting:** On January 20, 1969, a wave of sightings occurred along Mount Nansen Road. At 9:00 p.m., a driver and two passengers observed a blue light hovering above the tree line at Mile 5. It moved slowly toward Mount Nansen before reappearing on a ridge near Victoria Creek, where it shot away with a red trail. Simultaneously, two other employees observed a light south of the road that pulsed, moved back and forth, turned red, and departed rapidly over a hill. At 9:45 p.m., another employee observed two objects descending into a valley 6 miles from Carmacks; these hovered and emitted light beams. Upon reaching Mile 15, the same witness observed four additional lights in a line that moved side-by-side, merged into one, and faded. 

Historical context provided by witnesses includes a November 1968 incident where a pulsating yellowish light moved up and down near the road, accompanied by a second light that followed the witnesses' vehicle. Additionally, on December 17, 1968, a witness at a fuel tank observed a stationary light near Tit Mountain for 15 minutes, which changed colors before disappearing as the witness moved their truck.

**Object:** Descriptions varied but generally featured luminous, color-changing phenomena. Objects were described as round, ranging from the size of a 45-gallon drum top to large, bright lights. Colors included light blue, turquoise, yellow, white, red, and green. The objects exhibited complex movement: hovering, pulsating, moving in lines, merging, and rapid, high-speed departure. Some emitted distinct beams of light or left red trails/flashes of fire. No sound was reported. Durations ranged from one minute to 15 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Carmacks Detachment investigated the January 20 sightings. Cst. G.J. Jared and Cpl. M.D. Walker collected signed statements from multiple employees. The RCMP assessed three of the primary witnesses as highly reliable, while one was unknown to the detachment. The Yukon Sub/Division forwarded the file on February 3, 1969, noting that while several individuals witnessed the events, others declined to provide statements due to fear of public ridicule. The official status of the January 20 event was filed as an "unconfirmed sighting." No further physical evidence was recovered.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 南森山矿业公司（Mount Nansen Mines）的四名匿名员工（包括一辆车上的司机及两名乘客）、南森矿业有限公司的一名匿名文职员工、一名匿名平民（1968年12月事件的目击者），以及另外一名匿名人士。参与调查的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警官包括 G.J. 杰瑞德（G.J. Jared）警员和 M.D. 沃克（M.D. Walker）下士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月20日，晚上9:00至9:45之间。（另有报告称1968年12月17日晚上8:00，以及1968年11月下旬下午6:00亦有目击事件）。

**地点：** 育空地区卡马克斯（Carmacks）的南森山路（Mount Nansen Road）（具体位于5英里处、15英里处以及维多利亚溪附近）。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月20日，南森山路沿线发生了一系列目击事件。晚上9:00，一名司机和两名乘客在5英里处观察到一个悬浮在树线上的蓝光。它缓慢向南森山移动，随后出现在维多利亚溪附近的山脊上，并带着红色的尾迹疾驰而去。与此同时，另外两名员工观察到路南侧有一个光点，它不断脉动、来回移动、变红，随后迅速越过山丘消失。晚上9:45，另一名员工观察到两个物体降落在距离卡马克斯6英里处的一个山谷中；它们悬浮着并发出光束。当到达15英里处时，同一名目击者观察到另外四个排成一行的光点，它们并排移动、合并为一个光点，随后消失。

目击者提供的历史背景包括1968年11月发生的一起事件：一个脉动的黄色光点在路附近上下移动，并伴有第二个光点跟随目击者的车辆。此外，1968年12月17日，一名在油罐处的目击者观察到提特山（Tit Mountain）附近有一个静止的光点持续了15分钟，该光点在目击者移动卡车时变换了颜色并消失。

**物体描述：** 描述各不相同，但通常表现为发光且会变色的现象。物体被描述为圆形，大小从45加仑油桶盖大小到巨大的明亮光团不等。颜色包括浅蓝色、绿松石色、黄色、白色、红色和绿色。这些物体表现出复杂的运动方式：悬浮、脉动、排成直线移动、合并以及高速离去。一些物体发出了明显的光束或留下了红色的尾迹/火光。未报告有任何声音。持续时间从一分钟到15分钟不等。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警卡马克斯分局对1月20日的目击事件进行了调查。G.J. 杰瑞德警员和 M.D. 沃克下士收集了多名员工的签名陈述。皇家骑警评估认为其中三名主要目击者非常可靠，而另一名目击者身份不明。育空分部于1969年2月3日转发了该档案，并指出尽管有多人目击了这些事件，但其他人因担心遭到公众嘲笑而拒绝提供陈述。1月20日事件的官方状态被归档为“未经证实的目击事件”。未发现任何进一步的实物证据。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], Mr. and Mrs. [redacted], Cpl. A.D. Clearwater, Cst. B.M. Hurst, Cst. R.F. Mattson, and multiple unnamed civilian residents of Valleyview.

**Date / Time:** January 20, 1969 (8:15 P.M. – 8:20 P.M.) and January 21, 1969 (8:45 P.M. – 9:30 P.M.); follow-up observation on January 28, 1969, at 10:00 P.M.

**Location:** Valleyview, Alberta.

**Sighting:** The events in Valleyview involved multiple sightings over several days. On January 20, 1969, between 8:15 P.M. and 8:20 P.M., residents observed an object south of town. One witness, using field glasses, described it as an orange ball that initially appeared to be a plane on fire; it hovered over the town for approximately one minute before departing directly east. 

On January 21, 1969, between 8:45 P.M. and 9:30 P.M., a second, more extensive series of sightings occurred under clear, cold conditions. Mrs. [redacted] reported a "pinkish" light appearing from the southwest, traveling southeast, disappearing, and reappearing to hover over town before dropping and moving north. Mr. [redacted] observed a "yellowish-orange" light to the southwest that moved south, disappeared, and reappeared lower and brighter; he noted it hovered and moved side-to-side before descending behind buildings. Mr. and Mrs. [redacted] corroborated the 8:45 P.M. to 9:30 P.M. timeline, noting the object appeared as a round, reddish light that hovered, disappeared behind a building, and then appeared quite high before heading due north. Cst. B.M. Hurst and Cst. R.F. Mattson also observed the object; Cst. Hurst described it as a "pinkish" light north of town that changed intensity, resembling a star moving northeast. 

A final observation was recorded on January 28, 1969, at 10:00 P.M., when RCMP members witnessed a pinkish-red light to the west of Valleyview that shifted intensity to white before disappearing after five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described variously as a brilliant light, a round reddish light, a "pinkish" light, and a "yellowish-orange" light. On January 20, it was estimated to be an orange ball approximately 2 feet in diameter, later appearing to be 1 foot in diameter. The object displayed high-speed movement, hovering capabilities, and side-to-side motion. Despite appearing close to witnesses, no sound was reported. The duration of the January 21 sighting was described as a fifteen-minute sporadic appearance.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was handled by the RCMP Valleyview Detachment, specifically Cpl. A.D. Clearwater, Cst. B.M. Hurst, and Cst. R.F. Mattson. Cst. Hurst personally observed the object after receiving initial calls. A Telex message (VV15) was dispatched regarding the details. Cpl. Clearwater filed a formal report, which was forwarded to the Commissioner in Ottawa on February 4, 1969. Weather conditions on January 21 were noted as clear and cold. Mrs. [redacted] provided information linking the January 21 sightings to similar reports made by residents on the night of January 20.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]女士、[已删除]先生、[已删除]夫妇、A.D. 克利尔沃特（A.D. Clearwater）下士、B.M. 赫斯特（B.M. Hurst）警员、R.F. 马特森（R.F. Mattson）警员，以及多名未具名的瓦利维尤（Valleyview）平民居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月20日（晚上8:15 – 8:20）及1969年1月21日（晚上8:45 – 9:30）；1969年1月28日晚上10:00有后续观测。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省瓦利维尤。

**目击经过：** 瓦利维尤发生的事件涉及多日内的多次目击。1969年1月20日晚上8:15至8:20之间，居民们观察到镇子南侧出现了一个物体。一名使用双筒望远镜的目击者将其描述为一个橙色的球体，起初看起来像是一架着火的飞机；它在镇子上空盘旋了约一分钟，随后径直向东飞离。

1969年1月21日晚上8:45至9:30之间，在晴朗寒冷的天气条件下，发生了第二次、规模更大的系列目击事件。[已删除]女士报告称，一道“粉红色”的光从西南方向出现，向东南方向移动，消失后又重新出现，在镇子上空盘旋，随后下降并向北移动。[已删除]先生观察到西南方有一道“黄橙色”的光，它向南移动，消失后又在更低的位置重新出现，且亮度增加；他注意到该物体在降落到建筑物后方之前，曾进行过盘旋和左右移动。[已删除]夫妇证实了晚上8:45至9:30的时间线，指出该物体表现为一道圆形的微红色光芒，它曾盘旋、消失在建筑物后，随后又出现在高空，最后径直向北飞去。B.M. 赫斯特警员和R.F. 马特森警员也观察到了该物体；赫斯特警员将其描述为镇子北侧一道“粉红色”的光，其亮度会发生变化，看起来像是一颗向东北方向移动的星星。

1969年1月28日晚上10:00记录了最后一次观测，当时加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）成员目击到瓦利维尤西侧有一道粉红色的光，其亮度转变为白色，五分钟后消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为多种形态：一道耀眼的光、一道圆形的微红色光、一道“粉红色”的光以及一道“黄橙色”的光。1月20日，据估计它是一个直径约2英尺的橙色球体，后来看起来直径约为1英尺。该物体表现出高速移动、盘旋能力以及左右摇摆的动作。尽管目击者感觉物体距离很近，但并未报告任何声音。1月21日的目击事件被描述为持续了十五分钟的零星出现。

**调查/后续：** 此案由加拿大皇家骑警瓦利维尤分局负责调查，具体调查人员为A.D. 克利尔沃特下士、B.M. 赫斯特警员和R.F. 马特森警员。赫斯特警员在接到最初的报警电话后亲自观察了该物体。当局发送了一份关于详细情况的电传信息（VV15）。克利尔沃特下士提交了一份正式报告，该报告于1969年2月4日被转交给渥太华的专员。[已删除]女士提供了相关信息，将1月21日的目击事件与1月20日晚居民们的类似报告联系了起来。1月21日的天气状况被记录为晴朗且寒冷。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A local resident, his sister, a local service station owner (who is also a pilot), two civilians (at a barn), and three additional unnamed civilians from Blaeberry, B.C. (interviewed by D.R. Strobel).

**Date / Time:** January 22, 1969, at approximately 7:30 PM and 9:30 PM; with historical sightings reported in mid-September 1968, early October 1968, and September 15, 1968.

**Location:** Blaeberry area (approximately 13 miles northwest of Golden, B.C.), Willow Bank Mountain, and Highway 1 near the Columbia River.

**Sighting:** On January 22, 1969, at 7:30 PM, a local resident and his sister were at a barn in Blaeberry to feed horses. The horses exhibited signs of distress, refusing to approach the barn. Following a loud crash in the nearby bush, one witness armed themselves with a rifle and flashlight. Looking West, they observed two bright white lights descending at a 45-degree angle in a Northerly direction. The lights were estimated to be four miles away at an altitude of 500 feet before they extinguished simultaneously. The witness noted they had seen similar lights five or six times in the previous year.

Separately, on the same evening at 9:30 PM, a local service station owner (a pilot) observed a fairly large white light traveling horizontally near the mountain range across the Columbia River while driving on Highway 1. Additional reports collected by D.R. Strobel on January 24, 1969, included sightings of a large round light with a tail of light traveling south, followed by a grey cigar-shaped object moving in the opposite direction near Willow Bank Mountain. Historical reports from the same area included a large yellowish ball (size of the moon) seen in mid-September 1968 moving south-westerly, and a large round object (twice the size of a star) seen in early October 1968 moving East to West for 5 to 10 seconds.

**Object:** The objects were described as bright white lights (estimated 10 feet in diameter), a large round light with a tail, a grey cigar-shaped object, a large yellowish ball, and a round object twice the size of a star. Movement varied from horizontal travel at high speed to 45-degree descents and sudden accelerations. No sound was reported other than a "loud crash" heard in the bush during the 7:30 PM event.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** On January 23, 1969, Search and Rescue Headquarters were contacted to check for missing aircraft; none were reported. A telex was sent to the NORAD Meteor Centre. On January 24, 1969, an RCMP patrol visited the Blaeberry area to conduct interviews. The reporting officer noted that the witnesses appeared sincere but had previously withheld reports due to fear of adverse local opinion. D.R. Strobel documented the additional civilian statements regarding the cigar-shaped object and historical sightings. Witnesses explicitly stated their belief that these phenomena were not planes, flares, or shooting stars.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名当地居民及其妹妹、一名当地加油站站长（同时也是一名飞行员）、两名平民（在谷仓处），以及另外三名来自不列颠哥伦比亚省布莱伯利（Blaeberry, B.C.）的匿名平民（由 D.R. 斯特罗贝尔进行访谈）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969 年 1 月 22 日，约晚上 7:30 和 9:30；此外还有 1968 年 9 月中旬、1968 年 10 月上旬及 1968 年 9 月 15 日的历史目击报告。

**地点：** 布莱伯利地区（位于不列颠哥伦比亚省戈尔登西北约 13 英里处）、柳岸山（Willow Bank Mountain）以及哥伦比亚河附近的 1 号公路。

**目击经过：** 1969 年 1 月 22 日晚上 7:30，一名当地居民和他的妹妹在布莱伯利的谷仓喂马。马匹表现出不安，拒绝靠近谷仓。在附近丛林传来一声巨响后，其中一名目击者持步枪和手电筒进行查看。向西望去，他们观察到两道明亮的白光以 45 度角向北下降。据估计，这些光点在熄灭前距离他们约 4 英里，高度为 500 英尺。目击者指出，在过去的一年中，他们曾五六次看到类似的光点。

同日晚上 9:30，另一位当地加油站站长（飞行员）在 1 号公路上驾车时，观察到一道相当大的白光在哥伦比亚河对岸的山脉附近水平移动。D.R. 斯特罗贝尔于 1969 年 1 月 24 日收集的其他报告包括：有人看到一个带有光尾的大型圆形光点向南移动，随后在柳岸山附近出现一个灰色雪茄状物体向相反方向移动。同一地区的历史报告还包括：1968 年 9 月中旬看到的一个大型黄色球体（月球大小）向西南方向移动，以及 1968 年 10 月上旬看到的一个大型圆形物体（两倍于恒星大小）由东向西移动，持续了 5 到 10 秒。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为明亮的白光（估计直径 10 英尺）、带有光尾的大型圆形光点、灰色雪茄状物体、大型黄色球体，以及两倍于恒星大小的圆形物体。其运动方式多样，包括高速水平飞行、45 度角下降以及突然加速。除 7:30 事件中丛林里传出的“巨响”外，未报告有其他声音。

**调查/后续：** 1969 年 1 月 23 日，搜救总部接到联系以核查是否有失踪飞机；结果显示并无此类报告。一份电传被发送至北美防空司令部（NORAD）流星中心。1969 年 1 月 24 日，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）巡逻队前往布莱伯利地区进行访谈。负责警官指出，目击者看起来很真诚，但此前因担心当地舆论的不利影响而未报告。D.R. 斯特罗贝尔记录了其他平民关于雪茄状物体和历史目击事件的陈述。目击者明确表示，他们相信这些现象既不是飞机、照明弹，也不是流星。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian (known to the RCMP as a stable and reliable source), Esterbrook, and an unidentified employee of a nearby seismic camp.

**Date / Time:** January 24, 1969, at 7:15 PM PST.

**Location:** Willow Lake, Northwest Territories (190 miles northeast of Fort Simpson, NWT).

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 24, 1969, multiple witnesses observed an unidentified flying object in the vicinity of Willow Lake. A civilian witness, while sitting in his cabin at the west end of the lake, observed the object traveling in a northerly direction at a high rate of speed. He watched the object for approximately 1.5 to 2 minutes until it disappeared over a hill roughly 10 miles away. Simultaneously, an employee of a nearby seismic camp reported observing the object at an estimated altitude of 3,000 feet. This witness also reported that the object traveled until it went over a hill and disappeared, noting a sighting duration of two to three minutes. Both the civilian witness and the seismic camp employee explicitly stated that they had seen meteors in the past and were certain that this object was not a meteorite.

**Object:** The object was described as a dark or black-fronted craft with a distinct, bright appearance, likened to the ignition of an acetylene torch. It featured a black rear section emitting a blue-green flame that trailed behind the object for 150 to 200 feet. The object produced a continuous, loud "screaming" noise, described as being similar to an uneven jet engine. A diagram provided by a witness depicted the object traveling in a westward direction (noting a discrepancy with the northerly direction reported by the cabin witness) and confirmed the length of the flame/body as 150 to 200 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The event was reported to the RCMP, and the file was handled by the Fort Smith Sub-Division. The RCMP contacted the Department of Transport (D.O.T.) aeradio to check for any missing aircraft, but none were reported. A rough sketch and a diagram of the object were submitted by witnesses (one name redacted). While the RCMP detachment initially concluded that the object was in all probability a fireball or meteorite, they were unable to conduct further investigation and subsequently closed the file. A copy of the report was forwarded to the Providence detachment in the event they had contact with Esterbrook’s company.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名平民（加拿大皇家骑警 RCMP 认定其为稳定可靠的消息来源）、埃斯特布鲁克（Esterbrook），以及附近一个地震勘探营地的一名身份不明的员工。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969 年 1 月 24 日，太平洋标准时间下午 7:15。

**地点：** 西北地区威洛湖（Willow Lake）（位于西北地区辛普森堡东北 190 英里处）。

**目击经过：** 1969 年 1 月 24 日傍晚，多名目击者在威洛湖附近观察到一个不明飞行物。一名平民目击者当时正坐在湖西端的木屋里，观察到该物体正以极高的速度向北飞行。他注视了该物体约 1.5 到 2 分钟，直到它消失在约 10 英里外的一座小山后。与此同时，附近一个地震勘探营地的一名员工报告称，观察到该物体飞行高度约为 3,000 英尺。该目击者也报告说，物体一直飞行直到越过小山消失，并指出目击持续时间为两到三分钟。平民目击者和地震勘探营地员工都明确表示，他们过去曾见过流星，并确信该物体绝非陨石。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一艘前端呈深色或黑色的飞行器，外观特征鲜明且明亮，类似于乙炔焊枪点火时的光芒。其后部为黑色，喷射出蓝绿色的火焰，火焰在物体后方拖曳出 150 到 200 英尺长。该物体发出持续且巨大的“尖啸”声，被描述为类似于不平稳的喷气发动机声。一名目击者提供的示意图显示该物体向西飞行（与木屋目击者报告的向北方向存在出入），并确认了火焰/机身的长度为 150 到 200 英尺。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP），并由史密斯堡（Fort Smith）分部处理。RCMP 联系了交通部（D.O.T.）航空无线电部门以核查是否有失踪飞机，但未收到相关报告。目击者提交了一份草图和一份物体示意图（其中一个名字被涂黑）。尽管 RCMP 分队最初断定该物体极有可能是火球或陨石，但由于无法进行进一步调查，随后结案。报告副本被转发给普罗维登斯（Providence）分队，以备他们与埃斯特布鲁克所在公司取得联系时参考。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** C. Perrault, Perrault (father)

**Date / Time:** January 27, 1969; duration of 2 hours.

**Location:** 6 Erick St, Winnipeg, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On January 27, 1969, two witnesses, C. Perrault and his father, both residing at 6 Erick St in Winnipeg, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for a duration of two hours. Both witnesses reported seeing a bright light in the sky, which they characterized as the brightest light visible at that time. The object exhibited flashing red and green lights and was observed moving in a southwesterly direction.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright light, noted by the witnesses as the brightest light in the sky. It featured distinct flashing red and green lights. Regarding its movement, the object traveled in a southwesterly direction. The total duration of the sighting was recorded as two hours.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official follow-up inquiries were conducted with the local air traffic control tower. Upon checking the sky in response to the report, the tower personnel stated that they could see nothing in the area except for the planet Venus. No further anomalous objects were confirmed by official observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** C. 佩罗 (C. Perrault)、佩罗先生（父亲）

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月27日；持续时间为2小时。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省温尼伯市埃里克街6号 (6 Erick St, Winnipeg, Manitoba)。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月27日，居住在温尼伯市埃里克街6号的两名目击者——C. 佩罗及其父亲，观测到了一种不明空中现象。此次目击持续了两个小时。两位目击者均报告称，天空中出现了一道明亮的光，他们将其描述为当时天空中可见的最亮光源。该物体闪烁着红绿相间的光芒，并被观测到正向西南方向移动。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一道明亮的光，目击者称其为天空中最亮的光源。它具有明显的红绿闪烁灯光。在移动轨迹方面，该物体向西南方向飞行。目击总时长记录为两小时。

**调查/后续：** 相关部门向当地空中交通管制塔台进行了后续问询。塔台工作人员在接到报告后对天空进行了核查，表示除金星外，该区域未见任何异常。官方观测未证实存在其他异常物体。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. D.R. Gaeta (RCMP), Cst. T.A. Lamond (RCMP), Mrs. W.R. Biggar, and Mr. Joseph A. Smith.

**Date / Time:** January 30, 1969, at 10:00 PM Mountain Time (recorded as 0300Z on January 31, 1969).

**Location:** Beaverlodge, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the night of January 30, 1969, Mr. Joseph A. Smith contacted the RCMP detachment in Beaverlodge to report an unusual aerial phenomenon. Following this report, Constable David Gaeta exited the detachment and personally confirmed the observation. The sighting, which occurred under clear sky conditions, lasted for approximately 10 minutes. The object was initially spotted west of Beaverlodge and was observed traveling in a westerly direction until it eventually moved out of sight. Constable Gaeta continued to monitor the object until it disappeared completely. Mrs. W.R. Biggar and Constable T.A. Lamond were also identified as witnesses to the event.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, round entity. Its color was initially noted as a bright orangy-red (or bright red), which then transitioned to an off-white color. Observers noted that the color change occurred without a set pattern or timing, leading to the suggestion that the object may have been revolving. The object did not possess a trailing tail. It maintained an estimated altitude of 1,000 feet throughout the duration of the sighting. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was officially documented by the RCMP Beaverlodge Detachment. Following the observation, the Canadian Forces Station (CFS) Beaverlodge radar facility was contacted to determine if the object had been tracked; however, the base reported no corresponding sightings on their radar equipment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** D.R. 加埃塔警官（加拿大皇家骑警）、T.A. 拉蒙德警官（加拿大皇家骑警）、W.R. 比格夫人以及约瑟夫·A·史密斯先生。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月30日，山区时间晚上10:00（记录为1969年1月31日0300Z）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省比弗洛奇（Beaverlodge）。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月30日晚，约瑟夫·A·史密斯先生联系了比弗洛奇的加拿大皇家骑警分局，报告了一起异常的空中现象。接到报告后，大卫·加埃塔警官走出分局，亲自证实了这一观测结果。此次目击事件发生在晴朗的天空下，持续了约10分钟。该物体最初在比弗洛奇以西被发现，并被观察到向西飞行，最终消失在视野之外。加埃塔警官持续监视该物体，直到它完全消失。W.R. 比格夫人和 T.A. 拉蒙德警官也被确认为该事件的目击者。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的圆形实体。其颜色最初被记录为明亮的橙红色（或亮红色），随后转变为灰白色。观察者指出，颜色变化没有固定的模式或时间规律，这暗示该物体可能在旋转。该物体没有拖尾。在整个目击过程中，它保持在约1,000英尺的估计高度。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警比弗洛奇分局正式记录。观测结束后，相关人员联系了加拿大武装部队比弗洛奇雷达站，以确定该物体是否被追踪到；然而，该基地报告称其雷达设备上没有相应的观测记录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Bill Seman.

**Sighting:** On January 30, 1969, at 0400Z, a sighting occurred west of the town of Boharm, Saskatchewan. The sky conditions were reported as scattered cloud.

**Object:** The object appeared as a white and red light low on the western horizon. When viewed through binoculars, it appeared as a round ball, red on one side. The lights changed very slowly, with the red color changing to white every 3 to 4 seconds. The object remained in one spot for 10 minutes.

**Aftermath:** The object was initially believed to be an aircraft, but the lack of motion and the slowness of the color changes disqualified this conclusion.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Bill Seman 先生。

**目击：** 1969 年 1 月 30 日 0400Z，在萨斯喀彻温省 Boharm 镇以西发生了一起目击事件。当时的天气状况为零散云层。

**物体：** 该物体表现为西方地平线上低空的白色和红色光点。通过双筒望远镜观察，它呈现为一个圆球状，一侧为红色。灯光变化非常缓慢，红色每 3 到 4 秒变为白色。该物体在同一位置停留了 10 分钟。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. [Redacted]

**Date / Time:** January 30, 1969, at approximately 9:30 p.m. – 9:35 p.m. MST

**Location:** A farm located 4 miles west and 1.5 miles south of Crossfield, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the night of January 30, 1969, the witnesses were in their truck near their farmhouse when they observed an unidentified object. The wife, an amateur astronomer, first spotted the object and initially mistook it for a meteorite; she alerted her husband, who was driving. The wife observed the object for approximately 10 seconds, while the husband observed it for about 5 seconds. The witnesses noted that the sky was very clear with no haze, mist, or Northern Lights, and that Venus had already set. The object moved from west to east at an estimated distance of one mile. The witnesses reported that the object disappeared suddenly and that no noise was heard during the event.

**Object:** The object was described as a dark, disc-shaped craft, estimated to be the size of a large airplane. It featured windows along its contour that emitted a bright, glowing yellow light. Additionally, a long, pointed object or exhaust stream—also glowing bright yellow—was observed trailing from the rear of the craft. The witnesses estimated the altitude to be between 2,000 and 3,000 feet. Both witnesses acknowledged that their estimates regarding size and distance might be inaccurate due to the short duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was investigated by Corporal R.N.W. Pyper of the RCMP Crossfield Detachment. The investigating officer, who had known the husband for two years, described him as a reliable, level-headed foreman at a local petrochemical plant; both witnesses were characterized as sincere, non-drinkers. 

The investigation considered local environmental factors: a flare pit is located to the northwest of the farm, and a large petrochemical plant emitting smoke and steam is situated to the east. However, the husband explicitly stated that neither of these familiar landmarks could have caused the visual phenomenon he observed. The temperature at the time of the sighting was approximately 30 degrees below zero. No other occupied farmhouses were within a one-mile radius, and no other UFO reports were received from the area. The RCMP concluded that the couple did witness an event and provided the most accurate description possible under the circumstances. The incident was formally documented via a telex (Crossfield Message 69/2) sent to the Calgary Sub Division.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除] 夫妇

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月30日，约晚上9:30 – 9:35（山区标准时间）

**地点：** 位于艾伯塔省克罗斯菲尔德（Crossfield）以西4英里、以南1.5英里处的一处农场。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月30日晚，目击者正坐在农舍附近的卡车内，此时他们观察到了一个不明物体。身为业余天文学家的妻子最先发现了该物体，起初误以为是陨石；她随即提醒了正在开车的丈夫。妻子观察该物体约10秒，丈夫则观察了约5秒。目击者指出，当时天空非常晴朗，没有雾霾、薄雾或极光，且金星已经落下。该物体由西向东移动，估计距离约为一英里。目击者报告称，该物体突然消失，且在整个过程中未听到任何声音。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一艘深色的圆盘状飞行器，估计大小相当于一架大型飞机。其轮廓上分布着窗户，散发出明亮的黄色光芒。此外，在飞行器后方还观察到一条长而尖的物体或排气流，同样发出明亮的黄光。目击者估计其高度在2,000至3,000英尺之间。两位目击者均承认，由于目击时间较短，他们对尺寸和距离的估算可能存在误差。

**调查/后续：** 此事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）克罗斯菲尔德分局的 R.N.W. 派珀（Pyper）下士进行调查。负责调查的警官与该丈夫相识两年，称其为当地一家石油化工工厂可靠且头脑冷静的领班；两位目击者都被评价为真诚且不饮酒的人。

调查考虑了当地的环境因素：农场西北方有一个火炬坑，东面则有一家排放烟雾和蒸汽的大型石油化工工厂。然而，丈夫明确表示，这些熟悉的地理标志都不可能造成他所观察到的视觉现象。目击发生时的气温约为零下30度。方圆一英里内没有其他有人居住的农舍，该地区也没有收到其他UFO报告。加拿大皇家骑警得出结论：这对夫妇确实目击了一起事件，并在当时的情况下提供了尽可能准确的描述。该事件已通过发送至卡尔加里分部的电传（克罗斯菲尔德消息 69/2）正式记录在案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Peter Pawluk, Myra Pawluk, Harry Demko, and John Andries.

**Date / Time:** February 1, 1969, at 9:50 PM Mountain Standard Time (Note: Page 106 contains a clerical error citing January 2, 1969, which is corrected by the subsequent pages to February 1, 1969).

**Location:** The Pawluk residence, located 8 to 8 1/2 miles north of Berwyn, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the night of February 1, 1969, at approximately 9:50 PM, four witnesses—Peter Pawluk, Myra Pawluk, Harry Demko, and John Andries—observed an unidentified flying object while at the Pawluk residence. The sky was reported as clear at the time of the sighting. The witnesses collectively observed the object for a duration of 5 to 8 minutes before it disappeared from view.

**Object:** The object was described as having no definite shape. Visually, it appeared orangish-red in color with a distinct bluish-green hue on the top. The object exhibited a rhythmic brightening and fading effect and performed minor up-and-down movements. Both the altitude and the distance of the object remained indeterminate throughout the duration of the sighting. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to and investigated by the Peace River Sub-Division of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Following the report, the RCMP conducted an immediate patrol to the scene to investigate the circumstances and question the witnesses. The reporting officer, N.T. Martin, formally noted that Peter Pawluk appeared to be in a sober state of mind and is considered a reputable member of the community. Based on the investigation, the RCMP concluded that no further action was required regarding the incident.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 彼得·帕卢克 (Peter Pawluk)、迈拉·帕卢克 (Myra Pawluk)、哈里·登科 (Harry Demko) 和约翰·安德里斯 (John Andries)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月1日，山区标准时间晚上9:50（注：第106页存在笔误，写成了1969年1月2日，后续页面已更正为1969年2月1日）。

**地点：** 位于艾伯塔省伯温 (Berwyn) 以北8至8.5英里处的帕卢克住所。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月1日晚约9:50，四名目击者——彼得·帕卢克、迈拉·帕卢克、哈里·登科和约翰·安德里斯——在帕卢克家中观察到一个不明飞行物。据称当时天空晴朗。目击者共同观察该物体持续了5至8分钟，随后物体消失在视野中。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为没有明确的形状。从视觉上看，它呈橙红色，顶部带有明显的蓝绿色调。该物体呈现出有节奏的明暗变化效果，并伴有轻微的上下移动。在整个目击过程中，物体的海拔高度和距离均无法确定。未报告有任何声音。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Multiple employees of Geophysical Service Incorporated (G.S.I.) Party No. 422 (including the second-in-charge, a mechanic, and other personnel), an unnamed civilian employee of G.S.I., an unnamed employee of Pan American Oil Co., and an unnamed individual residing in Edmonton.

**Date / Time:** February 6, 1969 (2:00 a.m.); February 15/18, 1969 (11:00 p.m. M.S.T.); March 1, 1969 (12:30 a.m.); March 7, 1969 (approx. midnight); March 8, 1969 (11:00 p.m. – 1:00 a.m.).

**Location:** Vicinity of Fort Liard, N.W.T., and Fort Nelson, B.C. Specific coordinates noted include 60° 8' N, 123° 31' W and 60° 10' N, 123° 30' W / 123° 15' W.

**Sighting:** Between February 6 and March 8, 1969, multiple seismic and oil company personnel reported a series of anomalous aerial phenomena. The G.S.I. Party #422 reported three distinct sightings (Feb 6, March 1, March 7) under clear, starry skies. Witnesses were initially reluctant to report due to fear of ridicule but came forward after hearing of similar sightings in Fort Simpson and Fort Nelson. 

On February 15/18, a G.S.I. employee observed an object moving East to West for 15 minutes, tracked via a 27-power transit at 225 degrees azimuth. On March 8, a Pan American Oil Co. employee observed an object 19 miles southeast of Fort Liard. This object approached the witness, receded, and vanished, only to reappear 2–5 minutes later from the same direction, repeating this cycle of color changes and movement before finally disappearing.

**Object:** Descriptions were consistent across multiple sightings. The object was generally described as the bottom half of a globe, flared on top as if surrounded by a round disc. Size was estimated at 50 to 70 feet across. Colors shifted rapidly between very bright red and a greyish blue; when red, the shape was indiscernible, but it became clear when greyish blue. The Pan American witness also noted a misty green/blue phase. Movement was erratic: the object would remain stationary, move rapidly, or drift slowly in a southerly direction. Altitudes were estimated between 500 and 1,000 feet above ground, observed at distances of approximately 20 miles.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** RCMP Cpl. D.F. Watt interviewed witnesses at the Fort Nelson detachment on April 1, 1969, noting that the witnesses were "definite, clear, and very reliable." Observations were aided by 27-power and 40-power transit instruments. An RCMP officer also conducted inquiries at the Pointed Mountain airstrip on March 20, 1969. The RCMP concluded that further investigation was difficult because the area was largely unpopulated and the seismic crews had vacated the region by the end of March 1969. A second witness in Edmonton was identified but remained unavailable for interview.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 地球物理服务公司（G.S.I.）第422勘探队的多名员工（包括二把手、一名机械师及其他人员）、一名未具名的G.S.I.文职员工、一名未具名的泛美石油公司（Pan American Oil Co.）员工，以及一名居住在埃德蒙顿的未具名人士。

**日期/时间：** 1969年2月6日（凌晨2:00）；1969年2月15日/18日（山区标准时间晚上11:00）；1969年3月1日（凌晨12:30）；1969年3月7日（午夜左右）；1969年3月8日（晚上11:00至次日凌晨1:00）。

**地点：** 西北地区利亚德堡（Fort Liard）及不列颠哥伦比亚省纳尔逊堡（Fort Nelson）附近。记录的具体坐标包括北纬60°8'、西经123°31'以及北纬60°10'、西经123°30'/123°15'。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月6日至3月8日期间，多名地震勘探和石油公司人员报告了一系列异常空中现象。G.S.I.第422勘探队在晴朗的星空下报告了三次明确的目击事件（2月6日、3月1日、3月7日）。目击者起初因担心遭到嘲笑而不愿上报，但在听闻辛普森堡（Fort Simpson）和纳尔逊堡也有类似目击事件后，才决定站出来。

2月15日/18日，一名G.S.I.员工观察到一个物体由东向西移动了15分钟，并通过27倍经纬仪在方位角225度处进行了追踪。3月8日，一名泛美石油公司的员工在利亚德堡东南19英里处观察到一个物体。该物体靠近目击者后退去并消失，随后在2至5分钟后从同一方向再次出现，重复着颜色变化和移动的循环，最终彻底消失。

**物体描述：** 多次目击事件的描述基本一致。该物体通常被描述为半球体，顶部向外扩张，仿佛被一个圆盘环绕。估计直径为50至70英尺。颜色在极亮的红色和灰蓝色之间快速切换；当呈现红色时，形状难以辨认，但在灰蓝色时则清晰可见。泛美石油公司的目击者还注意到该物体存在朦胧的绿/蓝色阶段。其移动方式不规则：物体时而静止，时而快速移动，或缓慢向南漂移。据估计，其高度在地面以上500至1000英尺之间，观测距离约为20英里。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）下士D.F. 瓦特（D.F. Watt）于1969年4月1日在纳尔逊堡分局采访了目击者，并指出这些目击者“态度明确、思路清晰且非常可靠”。观测过程借助了27倍和40倍的经纬仪。一名皇家骑警警官还于1969年3月20日在尖山（Pointed Mountain）简易机场进行了问询。皇家骑警得出结论，由于该地区人烟稀少，且地震勘探队已于1969年3月底撤离，进一步调查存在困难。埃德蒙顿的第二名目击者已被确认身份，但未能接受采访。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:

The other two witnesses, located in Berwyn and Dawson Creek, B.C., corroborated the sighting. The object remained visible for the duration of the event before disappearing from view.

**Object:** The object was described as having no definite shape. Its coloration was distinct, featuring an orangish-red body with a bluish-green top. The object exhibited a pulsating effect, characterized by brightening and fading, and performed slight up-and-down movements. Its altitude and distance from the observers remained indeterminate throughout the sighting. No specific sound was reported.

Following the initial report, the RCMP conducted a patrol to the scene and performed an interrogation of the primary witness. The reporting officer documented that the primary witness appeared to be in a sober state of mind and was considered a reputable member of the community. Based on the investigation, the RCMP concluded that no further action was necessary regarding the incident.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of 107-2nd Ave S, Weyburn, Saskatchewan.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名居住在萨斯喀彻温省韦伯恩市南第二大道107-2号的平民。

**日期：** 1969年2月2日

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省韦伯恩市（Weyburn）以北8英里处。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月2日晚上7点25分，一名目击者在公路上向南行驶时，观察到一个火球由北向南飞行。据报告，当时天空为多云天气。该物体出现在韦伯恩市以北8英里处。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为比满月更亮，未观察到阴影。它看起来比满月稍小，呈蓝白色，没有留下任何尾迹。它以极高的速度飞行，且高度看起来很低。目击过程中没有听到任何声音。目击持续时间为2到3秒，随后物体就像关灯一样瞬间熄灭。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. G.J. Jared (RCMP), Mrs. Gloria Jared, George Kolla (truck driver), and Stuart White (mentioned as a separate observer of a similar event).

**Date / Time:** February 3, 1969, from approximately 8:30 PM to 10:00 PM.

**Location:** Carmacks, Yukon (Klondike Highway #2, specifically between Mile 96 and Mile 107, Mt. Nansen mine area, and Five Finger Rapids).

**Sighting:** On February 3, 1969, at 10:00 PM, Cst. G.J. Jared, his wife Gloria Jared, and truck driver George Kolla observed an unusual aerial phenomenon. Cst. Jared first spotted the light while driving north toward Carmacks; he observed it for five minutes before it moved behind hills. After reaching Coal Mine Hill, he observed it for an additional five minutes. Simultaneously, George Kolla, who had departed Pelly Crossing at 8:30 PM driving south, reported seeing a light on his right side. Kolla observed the light again at Five Finger Rapids at 9:45 PM. At Mile 107, Kolla stopped his truck for two minutes to watch the object, which grew very bright before disappearing over the mountains at approximately 10:00 PM. The witnesses noted the weather was clear with thin scattered clouds and a full moon, which remained visible during the sighting. Kolla also reported seeing a similar phenomenon two weeks prior while traveling from Clinton Creek, and Stuart White was noted to have observed a similar event on January 24, 1969.

**Object:** The object was described as a white ball or light, sometimes appearing with a "bit of haze." It glowed with a pulsating intensity, shifting from a bright to a dull milky color. Its size was estimated to be approximately one-eighth the size of the full moon, or comparable to a street lamp at a distance. The object appeared stationary at an estimated distance of 15 miles northwest of the observers and one mile high, though its movement was difficult to judge due to the witnesses' own travel. No noise, movement (other than fading and disappearing behind terrain), or colors other than white were reported. The object eventually faded in intensity and size until it vanished.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation, with Cst. G.J. Jared documenting the statements of himself, his wife, and George Kolla. The report was forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre. Local investigation by the RCMP yielded no plausible explanation for the occurrence. Despite the collection of statements and the documentation of the sighting, no definitive identification of the object was made.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
