**Witnesses:** Two civilians (Melville Cove/Purcell’s Cove), a civilian resident of 2775 Devlin Drive, a second individual at the Devlin Drive address, and a civilian resident of Melville Cove.

**Date / Time:** June 13, 1970, at approximately 10:15 P.M. to 10:30 P.M. ADST.

**Location:** Halifax, Nova Scotia (specifically Melville Cove, Purcell’s Cove, and 2775 Devlin Drive).

**Sighting:** On the night of June 13, 1970, multiple witnesses across Halifax County observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sightings began around 10:15–10:30 P.M. and lasted between 20 and 40 minutes. Witnesses reported the object traveling in a northwesterly direction toward the Bedford Basin. One witness noted that the sky, initially cloudy, cleared during the observation. The object moved at a great height and speed, appearing to slow down at intervals before increasing speed as it moved toward and eventually disappeared over the horizon. Multiple witnesses, including a resident at 2775 Devlin Drive and a resident of Melville Cove, utilized binoculars to observe the object. One observer noted that through binoculars, the object appeared as a steady, bright white light for approximately 30 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as being the size of a large star and possessing a brightness comparable to the Evening Star or the North Star. It exhibited a distinct sequence of color changes: it began as a star-like light, transitioned to a bright flickering orange (for 4–5 minutes), shifted to a bright flickering red (for approximately 1 minute), and finally turned light green (for approximately 10 seconds) before vanishing. The object produced no noise, left no trail, and had no discernible physical form or structure associated with it.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews with the witnesses on June 14, 1970. The reporting officer characterized the witness from Devlin Drive as a polite, sensible, and reliable individual; it was noted that this witness had previously consulted with Rev. M.W. Burke-Gaffney of the National Research Council Associate Committee regarding satellite sightings. Official inquiries were made with radar operators at the Halifax International Airport, who confirmed that no UFOs were detected on their monitors during the time of the sightings. The investigation concluded that the object was not a falling star or a comet.

**目击者：** 两名平民（梅尔维尔湾/珀塞尔湾）、一名居住在德夫林大道 2775 号的平民、该地址的第二名个人，以及一名梅尔维尔湾的平民居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970 年 6 月 13 日，大西洋夏令时间（ADST）晚上 10:15 至 10:30 左右。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省哈利法克斯（具体为梅尔维尔湾、珀塞尔湾及德夫林大道 2775 号）。

**目击经过：** 1970 年 6 月 13 日晚，哈利法克斯县的多名目击者观察到一种不明空中现象。目击事件始于晚上 10:15 至 10:30 之间，持续了 20 到 40 分钟。目击者报告称，该物体正向西北方向的贝德福德盆地移动。一名目击者指出，天空最初多云，但在观察过程中转为晴朗。该物体在高空以极快速度移动，时而减速，随后又加速向地平线方向移动并最终消失。包括德夫林大道 2775 号居民和一名梅尔维尔湾居民在内的多名目击者使用了双筒望远镜进行观察。其中一名观察者指出，通过双筒望远镜观察时，该物体呈现为持续的明亮白光，持续了约 30 分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一颗大恒星大小，亮度与长庚星（金星）或北极星相当。它表现出明显的颜色变化序列：起初像恒星一样发光，随后转变为明亮的闪烁橙色（持续 4-5 分钟），接着变为明亮的闪烁红色（持续约 1 分钟），最后变为浅绿色（持续约 10 秒），随后消失。该物体没有发出任何声音，没有留下任何尾迹，也没有观察到任何明显的物理形态或结构。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）于 1970 年 6 月 14 日对目击者进行了访谈。负责警官将德夫林大道的目击者描述为一名礼貌、理智且可靠的人；并指出该目击者此前曾就卫星观测事宜咨询过国家研究委员会联合委员会的 M.W. 伯克-加夫尼牧师（Rev. M.W. Burke-Gaffney）。官方对哈利法克斯国际机场的雷达操作员进行了询问，他们证实目击期间雷达监视器上未探测到任何不明飞行物。调查结论认为，该物体并非流星或彗星。

**Witnesses:** James Vincent Young, Mr. Gordon Deal, and Vivian MacDonald.

**Date / Time:** June 13, 1970, at approximately 10:30 P.M. – 10:39 P.M. ADST.

**Location:** Melville Cove and Purcells Cove, Halifax, Nova Scotia (Lat 44° 37' N, Long 63° 37' W).

**Sighting:** On the night of June 13, 1970, multiple witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon over the Halifax area. Mr. Gordon Deal first spotted the light from his home in Melville Cove at approximately 10:30 P.M. James Vincent Young, located in nearby Purcells Cove, observed the object beginning at 10:39 P.M. The sky, initially cloudy, cleared during the observation period. Estimates of the sighting duration varied between 20 and 40 minutes. The object traveled in a northwesterly direction at a great height and speed, with witnesses noting that it would occasionally slow down before increasing speed again as it eventually disappeared over the horizon. Vivian MacDonald, who observed the object through binoculars, corroborated the accounts provided by Deal and Young.

**Object:** The object was described as appearing as bright as the evening star or the North Star. It lacked any distinct physical form, trail, or associated sound. Through binoculars, the object appeared bright white for approximately 30 minutes. Following this, it underwent a series of color changes: it shifted to a bright flickering orange (observed for 4–5 minutes), then to a bright flickering red (observed for approximately 1 minute), and finally to a light green (visible for approximately 10 seconds) before vanishing. Witnesses explicitly stated the object was not a falling star or a comet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews with all three witnesses on June 14, 1970. Investigating officers S/Sgt. J.H. Carroll and Cst. R.L. Smith characterized the witnesses as reliable, honest, and sensible individuals, despite noting that Mr. Deal had been drinking at the time of the sighting. Mr. Deal had previously been in contact with M.W. Burke-Gaffney of the National Research Council (NRC) Associate Committee regarding satellite sightings. The RCMP checked with radar operators at the Halifax International Airport, who reported no corresponding UFO tracks on their monitors. The official RCMP conclusion suggested the object might have been a fireball. The case file was formally documented by the RCMP in Halifax and forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre in Ottawa for further assessment.

Burke-Gaffney）有过联系。加拿大皇家骑警向哈利法克斯国际机场的雷达操作员进行了核实，对方报告称雷达监视器上未发现相应的UFO轨迹。加拿大皇家骑警的官方结论认为该物体可能是一颗火流星。该案卷由哈利法克斯的加拿大皇家骑警正式记录，并转交至渥太华的加拿大国家研究委员会流星中心进行进一步评估。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cpl. J. G. Foster, Csts. P.S. Robbins, M.R. Lester, G.W. Coolen (all of Gander RCMP Detachment), Mr. Bell Kornick (ATC Controller), Capt. Sarks (Operations Officer, CFS Gander), and various unnamed members of the Gander Meteorological Office.

**Date / Time:** June 26, 1970; initial sightings reported between 11:00 A.M. and 11:20 A.M. NDT (1320Z), continuing until approximately 1:00 P.M. NDT.

**Location:** Gander, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On the morning of June 26, 1970, a UFO was observed over Gander under partly cloudy skies with slight haze. RCMP officers Cpl. J. G. Foster, Csts. P.S. Robbins, M.R. Lester, and G.W. Coolen observed the object for an initial 10-minute period, followed by a secondary 10-minute observation using 7x50 binoculars from 169 Sullivan Avenue. Simultaneously, members of the Gander Meteorological Office and other RCMP personnel tracked the object as it drifted. ATC Controller Mr. Bell Kornick and CFS Gander Operations Officer Capt. Sarks also provided observations. The object remained visible until approximately 1:00 P.M. NDT, at which point it disappeared into a bank of cirrus clouds. The sighting was widespread, with RCMP detachments in Grand Falls, Glovertown, Lewisporte, and Botwood reporting that they had received similar accounts from the public.

**Object:** Descriptions of the object varied slightly by observer. The RCMP and Meteorological staff described it as round, transparent, and colourless, drifting with the wind in a north-westerly direction at an estimated altitude of 25,000 to 30,000 feet. When viewed through binoculars, the top portion appeared "belled out" by the wind. Meteorological staff specifically reported observing an antenna attached to the object. Conversely, Mr. Bell Kornick and Capt. Sarks described the object as a tear-drop shaped, clear plastic, coloured balloon, estimating its altitude at 10,000 to 12,000 feet with a diameter of 4 to 5 feet. No sound or independent movement was reported; the object’s trajectory was attributed entirely to wind drift.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally reported to Air Traffic Control and the Gander Meteorological Office. While the Meteorological Office confirmed they had received multiple reports of the object, they verified that it was not one of their own weather balloons. Despite this, the consensus among the reporting RCMP officers and Meteorological staff was that the object was a weather balloon. The investigation noted that the object’s behavior and appearance were consistent with previous experiences involving high-altitude weather balloons, leading to the conclusion that the sighting was likely a balloon of unknown origin.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** J. G. 福斯特下士（Cpl. J. G. Foster）、P. S. 罗宾斯警员（Cst. P.S. Robbins）、M. R. 莱斯特警员（Cst. M.R. Lester）、G. W. 库伦警员（Cst. G.W. Coolen）（均为甘德皇家加拿大骑警分队成员）、贝尔·科尼克先生（Bell Kornick，空中交通管制员）、萨克斯上尉（Capt. Sarks，甘德加拿大武装部队基地作战官），以及甘德气象局的多名未具名成员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年6月26日；首次目击报告时间为纽芬兰夏令时间（NDT）上午11:00至11:20（协调世界时1320Z），持续至当日下午约1:00。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省甘德（Gander）。

**目击经过：** 1970年6月26日上午，在部分多云且有轻微雾霾的天气下，甘德上空出现了一个不明飞行物。皇家加拿大骑警（RCMP）的J. G. 福斯特下士、P. S. 罗宾斯、M. R. 莱斯特和G. W. 库伦警员在沙利文大道169号（169 Sullivan Avenue）对该物体进行了最初10分钟的观察，随后又使用7x50双筒望远镜进行了第二次10分钟的观察。与此同时，甘德气象局的工作人员及其他骑警人员也对该物体的漂移轨迹进行了追踪。空中交通管制员贝尔·科尼克先生和甘德加拿大武装部队基地作战官萨克斯上尉也提供了观测记录。该物体一直可见至下午约1:00，随后消失在卷云层中。此次目击事件影响广泛，大瀑布城（Grand Falls）、格洛弗敦（Glovertown）、刘易斯波特（Lewisporte）和博特伍德（Botwood）的骑警分队均表示收到了公众类似的报告。

**物体描述：** 不同目击者对该物体的描述略有差异。骑警和气象人员将其描述为圆形、透明且无色，随风向西北方向漂移，估计高度在25,000至30,000英尺之间。通过双筒望远镜观察时，其顶部呈现出被风吹出的“钟形”。气象人员特别报告称观察到物体上附有天线。相反，贝尔·科尼克先生和萨克斯上尉则将其描述为一个泪滴状、透明塑料材质的彩色气球，估计高度为10,000至12,000英尺，直径约为4至5英尺。报告中未提及任何声音或自主运动；该物体的轨迹完全归因于风力漂移。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已正式报告给空中交通管制部门和甘德气象局。虽然气象局确认收到了多份关于该物体的报告，但他们证实这并非他们释放的气象气球。尽管如此，报告此事的骑警和气象人员一致认为该物体是一个气象气球。调查指出，该物体的行为和外观与以往高空气象气球的经验相符，因此结论认为此次目击事件很可能是一个来源不明的气象气球。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Walter Judson Vincent (also recorded as Walter Judon Vincent)

**Date / Time:** June 30, 1970, at 4:10 AM Yukon Standard Time

**Location:** 604 Strickland St., Whitehorse, Yukon Territory (observed from the doorway of a workshop)

**Sighting:**
On the morning of June 30, 1970, Walter Judson Vincent, a sign painter and former R.C.A.F. Safety Equipment Technician (with 10 years of Air Force service), observed an unidentified flying object. At 4:10 AM, while standing in the doorway of his workshop at 604 Strickland St., Vincent witnessed an object moving in a northerly direction, positioned to the west of his address. The sky conditions at the time were described as light overcast. The entire sighting lasted for a duration of 2 to 3 seconds before the object disappeared. Despite the proximity to the city, no other persons were reported to have observed the event.

**Object:**
The object was described as having a saucer-shaped bottom with a distinct squarish structure on top. Its color was compared to that of a red-hot electric element on a stove. Regarding its dimensions, reports vary slightly in the documentation: some accounts estimate the length to be twice that of a Boeing 737, while others describe it as being the size of a Boeing 737 in length, with a height comparable to the aforementioned stove element. The object was completely noiseless and left no vapour trail. It was observed at an estimated altitude of 500 feet, traveling at a high velocity estimated to be two to three times the speed of a Voodoo jet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The RCMP conducted an investigation into the sighting. During the interview process, the witness was assessed as rational and normal, though official documentation later listed the reliability of the report as "unknown." 

Official follow-up measures included:
*   **Aviation Check:** The Whitehorse Airport control tower confirmed that no aircraft had landed or taken off during the time of the sighting.
*   **Meteorological Check:** The meteorological station confirmed that no weather balloons had been released in the area during that period.
*   **Reporting:** A telex regarding the sighting was dispatched via RCMP telecommunications to the National Research Council (NRC) of Canada and the NRC Meteor Centre.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 沃尔特·贾德森·文森特（Walter Judson Vincent，亦有记录为 Walter Judon Vincent）

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年6月30日，育空标准时间凌晨4:10

**地点：** 育空地区怀特霍斯市斯特里克兰街604号（从一间工作室的门口观测）

**目击经过：**
1970年6月30日清晨，身为招牌画师、曾任加拿大皇家空军（R.C.A.F.）安全设备技术员（拥有10年空军服役经验）的沃尔特·贾德森·文森特观测到了一个不明飞行物。凌晨4:10，文森特站在其位于斯特里克兰街604号的工作室门口时，目击到一个物体正位于他所在位置的西侧，并向北移动。当时的天空状况被描述为轻微阴天。整个目击过程持续了2到3秒，随后物体消失。尽管该地点靠近市区，但据报道并无其他人目击到该事件。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为底部呈碟状，顶部有一个明显的方形结构。其颜色被比作炉子上烧红的电热元件。关于其尺寸，文档中的记录略有出入：一些记录估计其长度是波音737的两倍，而另一些则描述其长度与波音737相当，高度则与上述电热元件相当。该物体完全静音，且未留下任何尾迹。据估计，该物体飞行高度约为500英尺，以估计为“巫毒”（Voodoo）喷气式战斗机两到三倍的高速飞行。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对此次目击事件进行了调查。在访谈过程中，目击者被评估为理智且正常，尽管官方文件随后将该报告的可靠性列为“未知”。

官方后续措施包括：
*   **航空核查：** 怀特霍斯机场控制塔确认，在目击事件发生期间没有飞机起降。
*   **气象核查：** 气象站确认，在此期间该地区没有释放过气象气球。
*   **报告：** 关于此次目击事件的电传已通过加拿大皇家骑警电信系统发送至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）及NRC气象中心。

**Witnesses:** Mr. D. Banister, his children, and neighbours.

**Date / Time:** July 9, 1970, at 0245Z (also recorded as 090245Z).

**Location:** Winnipeg, MB.

**Sighting:** On July 9, 1970, at 0245Z, a sighting occurred in clear daylight conditions. The event was witnessed by Mr. D. Banister, his children, and several neighbours. The children observed the object for a duration of 15 minutes, while Mr. Banister—noted as an ex-Air Force member—observed the object for approximately 5 minutes. All witnesses observed the object flying due west. The object maintained a position of 45 degrees from the horizon throughout the encounter.

This specific maneuver was repeated several times, with the object varying its altitude by approximately 1,000 feet during its flight path.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report, an inquiry was made with the Winnipeg control tower. The tower confirmed that there were no aircraft in the area at the time of the sighting. The documentation notes the background of the primary witness, Mr. Banister, as an ex-Air Force individual, which is included as a relevant detail regarding the credibility of the observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:

**Location:** Chicoutimi and Kenogami, Quebec.

Trambley, his wife, his son, and a neighbor observed an object positioned 40 degrees northeast of Chicoutimi. The group monitored the object for 45 minutes, utilizing field glasses to assist their observation. Simultaneously, in the nearby area of Kenogami, Mr. Roger Vaillancourt reported observing an aerial phenomenon. His observation lasted for a duration of 15 minutes.

**Object:** The descriptions of the object varied based on the vantage point and the equipment used. The group in Chicoutimi described the object as a stationary entity featuring blinking green and red lights. They reported that the object made no sound throughout the 45-minute duration of their observation. Conversely, Mr. Vaillancourt, observing from Kenogami, described the object as a bright light resembling a fireball that maintained a slow, steady movement from south to north.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official records for the event note that weather conditions at the time of the sightings consisted of thin, scattered clouds with no obstructions to visibility. The reports were filed as part of the official documentation for the Chicoutimi/Kenogami sighting event. No further specific investigative actions, such as formal RCMP interrogations or detailed sketches, were explicitly noted in the provided documentation beyond the initial witness reports and weather data.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯·B·特兰布雷先生（Mr. James B. Trambley）、特兰布雷夫人（妻子）、詹姆斯·B·特兰布雷先生的儿子、一名未具名的邻居，以及罗杰·瓦扬古先生（Mr. Roger Vaillancourt）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年7月14日，0450Z（协调世界时）。

**地点：** 魁北克省希库蒂米（Chicoutimi）和凯诺加米（Kenogami）。

**目击经过：** 1970年7月14日清晨0450Z，希库蒂米/凯诺加米地区报告了两组截然不同的观测记录。詹姆斯·B·特兰布雷先生及其妻子、儿子和一名邻居观察到一个位于希库蒂米东北方向40度处的物体。该群体利用双筒望远镜对该物体进行了长达45分钟的观测。与此同时，在附近的凯诺加米地区，罗杰·瓦扬古先生报告观察到了一种空中现象。瓦扬古先生将该物体描述为一团明亮的光，类似于火球，正以未知高度从南向北缓慢移动。他的观测持续了15分钟。

**物体描述：** 根据观测点和所用设备的不同，对该物体的描述也存在差异。希库蒂米的观测群体将该物体描述为一个静止的实体，带有闪烁的红绿灯。他们报告称，在45分钟的观测过程中，该物体未发出任何声音。相反，在凯诺加米进行观测的瓦扬古先生则将该物体描述为一团类似于火球的明亮光体，并保持着从南向北缓慢而稳定的移动。

**调查/后续：** 该事件的官方记录指出，目击发生时的天气状况为稀疏的薄云，能见度未受阻碍。这些报告被归档为希库蒂米/凯诺加米目击事件的官方文件。除初步的目击者报告和气象数据外，提供的文件中未明确提及进一步的具体调查行动，如加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的正式审讯或详细的草图绘制。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unnamed resident of Holmesville, N.B.; Unnamed store owner in Holmesville, N.B.; Unnamed local resident and his son; Two unnamed individuals (witnesses in the vicinity of Holmesville and Upper Kent, N.B.).

**Date / Time:** May 10, 1970 (approx. 1:30 PM – 2:15 PM ADT) and May 11, 1970 (1:30 PM).

**Location:** Johnville, Carleton County, and Holmesville/Upper Kent, New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On May 10, 1970, at approximately 1:30 PM ADT, two witnesses in the vicinity of Holmesville and Upper Kent observed an object for five minutes moving in a southeasterly direction under overcast skies with a low ceiling. One witness described the object as a "ball of fire," while the other noted it appeared to project outward, simulating the wings of an aircraft. Both reported a dense trail of black smoke and noted the object made no noise and appeared to burn out before hitting the ground. 

Later that day, at approximately 2:15 PM, a resident of Holmesville reported a suspected plane crash in the Johnville area, describing an object falling from the sky trailing heavy black smoke. The following day, May 11, 1970, at 1:30 PM, a store owner in Holmesville observed an object descending at a 45-degree angle in a gliding fashion. This witness described the object as having a tail section, being covered in flames, and emitting dense black smoke. The object nosed toward the ground and disappeared from sight near Shepherd's Hill, approximately five to six miles away. The witness reported no noise or explosion, but noted a distinct gunpowder-like smell lingering after the object vanished.

**Object:** The object was described variously as a ball of fire, an aircraft-like structure with wings or a tail section, and a rocket. It was characterized by flames, a dense trail of black smoke, and a gliding, descending motion. It made no noise, though a gunpowder-like odor was reported at the site of disappearance. The object was later identified by authorities as a distress signal rocket, likely salvaged from a ship that had gone ashore in Saint John, N.B.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted extensive patrols and searches of the woods in Johnville with negative results. Official inquiries were made with private aircraft owners, local airports, and the Maine State Police regarding missing aircraft, all of which yielded no reports of missing planes. 

Following rumors, the RCMP investigated a local resident’s home and confirmed that the resident's son had ignited a rocket in the backyard on May 10, 1970. The RCMP determined the son had likely salvaged the distress rocket and ignited it without realizing the potential consequences. At the time of the report, the RCMP intended to obtain a formal statement from the son, who was working at Dartmouth Salvage in Dartmouth, N.S. The RCMP contacted his parents, but they were uncertain of his return date. The case was forwarded to the Doaktown Detachment for further action and remained marked as "STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION" pending the interview.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 新不伦瑞克省霍姆斯维尔（Holmesville）的一名匿名居民；霍姆斯维尔的一名匿名店主；一名当地居民及其儿子；两名匿名人士（霍姆斯维尔及上肯特（Upper Kent）附近的目击者）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年5月10日（约下午1:30 – 2:15，大西洋夏令时间）及1970年5月11日（下午1:30）。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省卡尔顿县（Carleton County）的约翰维尔（Johnville），以及霍姆斯维尔/上肯特地区。

**目击经过：** 1970年5月10日下午约1:30（大西洋夏令时间），两名在霍姆斯维尔和上肯特附近的目击者观察到一个物体，该物体在阴天低云层下向东南方向移动，持续了五分钟。一名目击者将其描述为“火球”，另一名则指出该物体似乎向外延伸，看起来像飞机的机翼。两人均报告称其拖着浓重的黑烟，且物体在飞行过程中没有发出任何声音，在坠地前似乎已燃尽。

当天晚些时候，约下午2:15，一名霍姆斯维尔居民报告称约翰维尔地区可能发生了飞机坠毁事件，描述有一个物体拖着浓重的黑烟从空中坠落。次日，即1970年5月11日下午1:30，霍姆斯维尔的一名店主观察到一个物体以45度角滑翔下降。该目击者描述该物体带有尾部结构，全身被火焰覆盖，并散发出浓重的黑烟。物体机头朝下坠向地面，在距离约五到六英里外的谢泼德山（Shepherd's Hill）附近消失。目击者报告称没有听到任何噪音或爆炸声，但注意到物体消失后空气中残留着一种类似火药的独特气味。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为火球、带有翼或尾部的飞行器结构，以及火箭。其特征包括火焰、浓重的黑烟轨迹，以及滑翔下降的动作。它没有发出声音，但在消失地点附近有人闻到了类似火药的气味。该物体后来被当局认定为一枚求救信号火箭，很可能是从圣约翰（Saint John）搁浅的一艘船上打捞出来的。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对约翰维尔的树林进行了广泛的巡逻和搜查，但未发现任何结果。官方还向私人飞机拥有者、当地机场以及缅因州警方询问了有关失踪飞机的情况，但均未收到任何失踪报告。

在流言传出后，加拿大皇家骑警调查了一名当地居民的住所，证实该居民的儿子曾在1970年5月10日在后院点燃了一枚火箭。警方认定，该儿子很可能是打捞到了这枚求救火箭，并在未意识到潜在后果的情况下将其点燃。在报告撰写时，警方打算从该男子处获取正式陈述，当时他正在新斯科舍省达特茅斯（Dartmouth）的达特茅斯打捞公司（Dartmouth Salvage）工作。警方联系了他的父母，但他们无法确定他的归期。此案被移交给多克敦（Doaktown）分局作进一步处理，在访谈完成前，案件状态仍标记为“调查中”。

**Witnesses:** J.M. Dyke (Assistant Chief Engineer), Mrs. Dyke

**Date / Time:** July 31, 1970, at approximately 11:55 PM (EDT)

**Location:** Galt, Ontario

**Sighting:** 
On the night of July 31, 1970, J.M. Dyke and his wife were present together when they observed an unusual aerial phenomenon. Mr. Dyke, an Assistant Chief Engineer, alerted his wife to the event by exclaiming "look up." The witnesses observed the object while looking toward the north. 

Accounts regarding the trajectory and duration vary slightly across the documentation. One account describes the object moving from north to south over a duration of 15 seconds, passing below the star Vega. Other documentation from the same event indicates the object traveled from east to west at a very high speed, with a much shorter duration of 1.5 to 3.0 seconds. During this brief window, the witnesses noted that the object maneuvered violently at least twice.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a grouping of 10 to 12 distinct points of light, all reddish in color. Collectively, these lights formed a shape described as a "thin football" or a "banana." The object was observed at a considerable range and exhibited high-speed, erratic movement.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was formally documented and filed with the National Research Council of Canada under file number N70/048. The investigation file includes a hand-drawn sketch provided by the witnesses, which maps the trajectory of the lights relative to the star Vega. Additionally, the file contains a directional compass diagram confirming the observation was made while looking toward the north.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_04_-_Pages_90.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** J.M. 戴克（J.M. Dyke，助理总工程师）、戴克夫人

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年7月31日，约晚上11:55（东部夏令时间）

**地点：** 安大略省加尔特（Galt, Ontario）

**目击经过：** 
1970年7月31日晚，J.M. 戴克与其妻子共同目击了一起异常的空中现象。身为助理总工程师的戴克先生惊呼“快看上面”，提醒妻子注意这一事件。目击者在朝北望去时发现了该物体。

关于物体轨迹和持续时间的记录略有出入。一份记录描述该物体由北向南移动，持续时间为15秒，并从织女星（Vega）下方掠过。而同一事件的其他文档则显示，该物体以极高速度由东向西飞行，持续时间仅为1.5至3.0秒。在这短暂的时间内，目击者注意到该物体至少进行了两次剧烈的机动飞行。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为由10到12个独立的红光点组成。这些光点整体呈现出“细长橄榄球”或“香蕉”状。目击者在相当远的距离外观察到了该物体，并注意到其呈现出高速且不规则的运动轨迹。

**调查/后续：** 
此次目击事件已被正式记录并归档至加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council of Canada），档案编号为 N70/048。调查档案中包含一份由目击者手绘的草图，标绘了这些光点相对于织女星的运动轨迹。此外，档案中还附有一张方向罗盘图，证实了目击者是在朝北观察时发现该物体的。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Residents of Little Hearts Ease and St. Jones, Mr. Ernest Norris and his family, Mr. and Mrs. William Robbins (local Post-Mistress and her husband).

**Date / Time:** August 14, 1970; sightings reported between 8:45 PM and 9:00 PM.

**Location:** Little Hearts Ease and St. Jones, Trinity Bay, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On the evening of August 14, 1970, multiple residents across the communities of Little Hearts Ease and St. Jones observed a significant aerial event. At approximately 8:45 PM to 9:00 PM, witnesses—including the Norris family and Mr. and Mrs. William Robbins—observed a fireball descending from the sky. The object was noted to be relatively close to the earth when first sighted, traveling in a northeasterly direction at an altitude of approximately one-quarter mile. 

The object’s luminosity was intense enough to illuminate the surrounding hills and the settlement itself, casting distinct shadows across the landscape. Observers reported that the object exhibited a noticeable "wobbling" motion as it traversed the sky. As it passed directly over the settlement of Little Hearts Ease, witnesses observed the object shedding pieces before it ultimately crashed into the water near the mouth of the harbour. The sighting lasted for approximately five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, blood-red fireball. It measured approximately eight to ten feet in length, with a tail of a lighter shade of red extending several feet beyond the main body. The width of the object was estimated at four feet. During its transit, the object produced a distinct rushing noise, accompanied by the sound of burning.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the reports, the RCMP Clarenville Detachment initiated an investigation. Sgt. G.R. Dorken oversaw the file, which included conducting an RCMP patrol of the area and a boat search of the harbour mouth; however, no physical evidence or debris was recovered. 

Official inquiries were made with the Air Terminal in Gander, which confirmed that no aircraft were missing or overdue in the Newfoundland region. The RCMP concluded that the event was a genuine fireball sighting. Documentation of the incident, including Clarenville Message #124, was forwarded on August 19, 1970, to the RCMP St. John’s Division, the Communication Squadron in Ottawa, and Rev. M.W. Burke-Gaffney at St. Mary’s University for further review. The file was subsequently marked as concluded by the Clarenville Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 小心易（Little Hearts Ease）和圣琼斯（St. Jones）的居民，欧内斯特·诺里斯（Ernest Norris）先生及其家人，威廉·罗宾斯（William Robbins）夫妇（当地邮政局长及其丈夫）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年8月14日；目击报告时间在晚上8:45至9:00之间。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省三一湾（Trinity Bay）的小心易和圣琼斯。

**目击经过：** 1970年8月14日晚，小心易和圣琼斯社区的多名居民目击了一起重大的空中事件。大约在晚上8:45至9:00之间，包括诺里斯一家和威廉·罗宾斯夫妇在内的目击者观察到一个火球从天而降。据记录，该物体初次被发现时距离地面相对较近，正以约四分之一英里的高度向东北方向飞行。

该物体的亮度极高，足以照亮周围的山丘和整个定居点，并在地表投下清晰的阴影。观察者报告称，该物体在穿越天空时呈现出明显的“摇晃”运动。当它直接飞过小心易定居点上空时，目击者看到该物体在坠入港口入口附近的水域之前，不断有碎片脱落。整个目击过程持续了约五分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的血红色火球。其长度约为八到十英尺，主体后方拖着一条延伸数英尺、颜色较浅的红色尾迹。据估计，该物体的宽度为四英尺。在飞行过程中，该物体发出明显的呼啸声，并伴有燃烧的声音。

**调查/后续：** 事件发生后，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）克拉伦维尔分局展开了调查。G.R. 多肯（G.R. Dorken）警长负责处理此案，包括对该地区进行巡逻以及对港口入口进行船只搜寻；然而，并未发现任何实物证据或残骸。

官方已向甘德（Gander）航空站进行查询，对方确认纽芬兰地区没有飞机失踪或逾期未归。加拿大皇家骑警最终认定该事件为一起真实的火球目击事件。包括克拉伦维尔第124号信息在内的事件记录已于1970年8月19日转发给加拿大皇家骑警圣约翰斯分部、渥太华通信中队以及圣玛丽大学的 M.W. 伯克-加夫尼（M.W. Burke-Gaffney）牧师进行进一步审查。此后，该档案被克拉伦维尔分局标记为结案。

At times, the object appeared almost stationary, while at other times it exhibited an up-and-down motion, which was specifically described by witnesses as being similar to the movement of a kite.

**Object:** The object was consistently described by both witnesses as round in shape and red in color. It was noted to be flashing throughout the duration of the sightings.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Prince George City Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation into the reports. As part of the follow-up process, the RCMP contacted the Canadian Forces Base (CFB) at Baldy Hughes. Military personnel at the base confirmed that they were actively tracking the object. **Witnesses:** Mr. Donald W. Golding

**Date / Time:** September 22, 1970; 5:45 AM EST and 5:50 AM EST

**Location:** Oshawa, Ontario

**Sighting:** 
The event involved two distinct observations occurring in the early morning hours of September 22, 1970, reported by Mr. Donald W. Golding. The first sighting occurred at 5:45 AM EST. During this observation, an object was seen positioned 40 degrees above the eastern horizon. It traveled from the northwest toward the southeast (with a conflicting note in the file suggesting a northwest to northeast trajectory) over a duration of approximately 3 to 4 seconds. The estimated altitude of this object was 120 miles.

A second sighting occurred five minutes later, at 5:50 AM EST. This object appeared in the northeast sky. Unlike the first object, this one was observed moving slowly, appearing to transition from the position of one star to another.

**Object:** 
The objects displayed different characteristics:
*   **First Object (5:45 AM):** Described as ball-shaped and dull white in color. It featured a bright white flash that pulsed at regular intervals. It moved with significant speed, traversing its path in only 3 to 4 seconds.
*   **Second Object (5:50 AM):** Described as a dark yellowish-orange color. Its movement was characterized as slow and deliberate, shifting between star positions. 

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation into this case (N70/064) was initiated following a letter sent by the witness, Mr. Donald W. Golding, to the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa. The case file includes a sketch illustrating the path of the second object relative to the surrounding stars to document its slow, star-to-star movement. No further official investigation notes or meteorological data were provided in the summary documents.

该事件涉及唐纳德·W·戈尔丁先生于1970年9月22日清晨报告的两次独立观测。第一次目击发生在上午5:45（东部标准时间）。观测期间，一个物体位于东方地平线上方40度处。它从西北向东南方向移动（档案中有一处矛盾的记录显示其轨迹为西北至东北方向），持续时间约为3至4秒。该物体的估计高度为120英里。

这些物体表现出不同的特征：
*   **第一个物体（上午5:45）：** 描述为球形，呈暗白色。它发出的明亮白光呈规律性脉冲闪烁。其移动速度极快，仅用3至4秒便完成了整个路径的飞行。

针对此案（编号 N70/064）的调查始于目击者唐纳德·W·戈尔丁先生致信渥太华国家研究委员会 (NRC) 之后。案卷中包含一张草图，展示了第二个物体相对于周围恒星的路径，以记录其缓慢的、从一颗恒星移动到另一颗恒星的过程。摘要文件中未提供进一步的官方调查记录或气象数据。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Fred Bradley and his family.

**Sighting:** On September 25, 1970, at 0835Z, the observer reported seeing what he believed to be a jet aircraft glowing reddish, located eight miles west of Port Alberni, BC. The object was moving slowly in a south-easterly direction toward Victoria. The observer could not confirm the sound due to nearby pulp mills.

**Object:** After three minutes, flames broke out and the object began to descend rapidly while changing direction to the north. During the descent, there were periods where no flames were visible, but black smoke was seen coming from the object. A piece of material broke off during the descent and fell in flames along with the main object, landing near the south shore of Sproat Lake. There was no explosion at any time. The duration of the sighting was approximately four minutes.

**Aftermath:** The observer reported the sighting to the RCMP in Port Alberni. The RCMP checked the area but found nothing. They reported the sighting to the control tower at CFB Comox, who relayed it to RCC Victoria. RCC Victoria conducted a communications check for overdue aircraft, but none were reported; therefore, the report is being considered a UFO.

The witnesses provided accounts noting the event duration as approximately five minutes. According to the observers, the object was first noted moving in a southward direction. A significant detail of the sighting involved the appearance of an unidentified aircraft. After the UFO had finished hovering and began its rapid northward departure, an aircraft appeared in the vicinity and seemed to follow the object. The witnesses noted that the UFO moved at a speed significantly faster than that of the aircraft. Despite the proximity of the aircraft, the witnesses reported that no sound was heard from either the UFO or the aircraft. The observers were unable to identify the specific type of aircraft, noting they could not determine if it was jet or propeller-driven.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, round, bright red ball. It was estimated to be at an altitude of 30,000 to 40,000 feet above sea level. In terms of visual size, the witnesses estimated the object to be one-quarter the diameter of a full moon. The object exhibited complex flight characteristics, including southward travel, circling, hovering, and a rapid northward departure. No sound was emitted by the object during any phase of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and processed through official channels. The report was transmitted from the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) in Victoria to RCCWC/CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters). Additionally, the report was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) Radio and Electrical Engineering Division for further review. The discrepancy in the recorded times (0220Z and 0402Z) appears within the official documentation, though both entries pertain to the same event witnessed by the Templetons.

**目击者：** J. 坦普尔顿夫人 (Mrs. J. Templeton)、J. 坦普尔顿先生 (Mr. J. Templeton)

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年10月4日；报告时间包括 0220Z 和 0402Z

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华

**目击经过：** 1970年10月4日，J. 坦普尔顿夫妇在不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华上空观测到一种不明空中现象。据目击者描述，整个事件持续了约五分钟。据观察者称，该物体最初向南移动，随后盘旋并悬停在原地，持续了五分钟。悬停阶段结束后，该物体迅速向北飞离。

此次目击事件的一个重要细节是出现了一架不明飞行器。在不明飞行物（UFO）结束悬停并开始迅速向北离开时，附近出现了一架飞机，似乎在跟踪该物体。目击者指出，UFO的飞行速度明显快于该飞机。尽管飞机距离很近，但目击者称未听到UFO或飞机发出的任何声音。观察者无法识别该飞机的具体型号，并表示无法确定它是喷气式还是螺旋桨驱动的。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个圆形的、明亮的红色球体。据估计，其飞行高度在海拔30,000至40,000英尺之间。在视觉大小方面，目击者估计该物体的直径约为满月的四分之一。该物体表现出复杂的飞行特征，包括向南移动、盘旋、悬停以及迅速向北离开。在目击过程的任何阶段，该物体均未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已通过官方渠道正式记录并处理。报告由维多利亚的救援协调中心（RCC）传达至加拿大武装部队总部（RCCWC/CANFORCEHED）。此外，报告还被转发至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）无线电与电气工程部进行进一步审查。官方文件中出现了记录时间上的差异（0220Z 和 0402Z），尽管这两项记录均指代坦普尔顿夫妇目击的同一事件。

**Witnesses:** Robert Manuel, Mrs. Dorothy Dauphone, Mr. Graham Walker, M/CPL Walker.

**Date / Time:** October 5, 1970, at 0900Z (050910Z for radar observation).

**Location:** Halifax/Shearwater, Nova Scotia (specifically near the TV towers at Fairview, Halifax; radar position 4443N 6336W).

**Sighting:** On October 5, 1970, at 0900Z, multiple witnesses reported anomalous aerial activity in the Halifax area. Robert Manuel (Tantallon, NS) and Mrs. Dorothy Dauphone (Halifax, NS) observed an object for fifteen minutes under partially cloudy conditions. They estimated the range to be approximately 3 nautical miles. Simultaneously, Mr. Graham Walker reported a sighting near the TV towers in Fairview, Halifax. He observed a circular object that remained visible for 5 minutes, accompanied by a streamer that remained visible for 20 minutes. 

Separately, at 050910Z, M/CPL Walker observed a stationary target on precision radar at coordinates 4443N 6336W. The target was at an estimated altitude of 2500 feet ASL and provided a strong radar return on both azimuth and elevation indicators, exhibiting characteristics consistent with a large aircraft. M/CPL Walker monitored the target for approximately ten minutes before discontinuing surveillance to prepare for an aircraft recovery. He noted that he did not initially take the sighting seriously until he heard reports of similar sightings on a radio news broadcast, which prompted him to file his official report.

**Object:** The descriptions of the object varied significantly by witness. Robert Manuel and Mrs. Dorothy Dauphone described the object as having a "flatfish" appearance with a tail; it moved at a slow speed and left a lingering glow in the sky after its departure. Mr. Graham Walker described the object as circular with bright beams emanating from the center, featuring colors around the circular body. He also noted a greenish, bright object at the end of a streamer and described the overall appearance as "star-shaped," noting that it traveled at a high speed in an eastward direction. M/CPL Walker’s radar observation identified a stationary target that possessed the physical radar signature of a large aircraft.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The official investigation into these reports includes a consistent notation across all documentation regarding a barium rocket launch. Records indicate that a barium rocket was fired from a rocket range in West Virginia on October 5, 1970, at 09:00 Z, which is cited as the likely explanation for the sightings. Contact information for witnesses Robert Manuel and Mrs. Dorothy Dauphone was recorded as 826-2235 and 826-2725, respectively. M/CPL Walker’s report was filed after he cross-referenced his radar data with public news reports of the event.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗伯特·曼努埃尔 (Robert Manuel)、多萝西·多芬夫人 (Mrs. Dorothy Dauphone)、格雷厄姆·沃克先生 (Mr. Graham Walker)、沃克下士 (M/CPL Walker)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年10月5日，0900Z（雷达观测时间为050910Z）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省哈利法克斯/希尔沃特（具体位于哈利法克斯费尔维尤的电视塔附近；雷达坐标为北纬44度43分，西经63度36分）。

**目击经过：** 1970年10月5日0900Z，多名目击者报告在哈利法克斯地区观测到异常空中活动。罗伯特·曼努埃尔（新斯科舍省坦塔隆）和多萝西·多芬夫人（新斯科舍省哈利法克斯）在局部多云的天气下观测该物体长达十五分钟，估计距离约为3海里。与此同时，格雷厄姆·沃克先生报告在哈利法克斯费尔维尤的电视塔附近看到了一个圆形物体，该物体可见时长为5分钟，并伴有一条可见时长达20分钟的流光。

此外，在050910Z，沃克下士在精密雷达上观测到一个位于北纬44度43分、西经63度36分坐标处的静止目标。该目标估计高度为海拔2500英尺，在方位角和仰角指示器上均显示出强烈的雷达回波，其特征与大型飞机一致。沃克下士对该目标进行了约十分钟的监控，随后因准备飞机回收任务而停止监视。他指出，起初并未将此次观测当回事，直到听到广播新闻中关于类似目击事件的报道，才促使他提交了正式报告。

**物体描述：** 不同目击者对物体的描述差异显著。罗伯特·曼努埃尔和多萝西·多芬夫人描述该物体外观呈“比目鱼”状，带有尾部；它以缓慢的速度移动，并在离开后在天空中留下了持久的余辉。格雷厄姆·沃克先生则描述该物体为圆形，中心射出明亮光束，圆形主体周围带有颜色。他还注意到流光末端有一个绿色的明亮物体，并将其整体外观描述为“星形”，指出它以高速向东飞行。沃克下士的雷达观测则显示该静止目标具备大型飞机的物理雷达特征。

**调查/后续：** 针对这些报告的官方调查在所有文件中均包含了一项一致的记录，即关于钡云火箭的发射。记录显示，1970年10月5日09:00 Z，西弗吉尼亚州的一个火箭发射场发射了一枚钡云火箭，这被认为是造成此次目击事件的可能原因。目击者罗伯特·曼努埃尔和多萝西·多芬夫人的联系电话分别记录为826-2235和826-2725。沃克下士是在将雷达数据与该事件的公开新闻报道进行交叉比对后提交的报告。

**Witnesses:** Two civilian women (residing in Lorette and Dugald), Mrs. [redacted], and a neighbour.

**Date / Time:** October 8, 1970, at approximately 11:00 PM – 11:15 PM Central Time.

**Location:** Springfield/Lorette, Manitoba area (specifically near the intersection of Highway #1 and P.R. #206, and municipal roads one mile east and one mile south and one-half mile east of Highway 1 East and Highway 207).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 8, 1970, multiple witnesses reported anomalous aerial activity. At approximately 11:00 PM, a witness in Dugald observed a light of a light yellow color in the sky. Shortly thereafter, at 11:15 PM, a second witness driving south of Highway #1 and P.R. #206 observed strange lights. Initially mistaking the object for a vehicle, she realized it was at an altitude too high for a car. This object approached her vehicle, hovered directly over it, and subsequently departed while emitting a noise similar to an airplane. 

Simultaneously, Mrs. [redacted] and a neighbour, while driving on a municipal road (one mile east, one mile south, and one-half mile east of Highway 1 East and Highway 207), observed three round, bright red objects in the cloudy sky. These objects were described as being approximately the size of a car. They were initially observed at a high altitude before dropping toward the witnesses' vehicle. The objects hovered over the top of the car for several seconds before accelerating away. The entire event lasted for a few minutes.

**Object:** The accounts describe two distinct visual experiences. One object was described as large, featuring two bright outer lights and a small red light at the rear, producing a noise similar to an airplane. The second account describes three distinct round objects, bright red in color, each roughly the size of a car. Movement for both accounts involved high-altitude positioning, a descent toward the witnesses, a hovering phase, and a rapid departure.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews with the witnesses involved in the first sighting and formally assessed them as mentally stable and reliable. The investigating officer concluded that the witnesses likely observed an aircraft, citing recent reports of planes flying at low altitudes with landing lights engaged. Consequently, no further official action was taken regarding that report. A separate report was initiated for the sighting involving Mrs. [redacted] and her neighbour, with documentation noting that a follow-up report was to follow.

**目击者：** 两名平民女性（分别居住在洛雷特和杜加尔德）、[已删除姓名]女士及其一位邻居。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年10月8日，中部时间晚上约11:00至11:15。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省斯普林菲尔德/洛雷特地区（具体位于1号公路与206号省级公路交叉口附近，以及1号公路东段与207号公路交叉口以东一英里、以南一英里及以东半英里的市政道路上）。

**目击经过：** 1970年10月8日晚，多名目击者报告了异常的空中活动。晚上约11:00，一名杜加尔德的目击者观察到天空中出现一束浅黄色的光。此后不久，即晚上11:15，另一名在1号公路与206号省级公路以南驾车的目击者也观察到了奇怪的光源。她起初误以为那是车辆，但随后意识到其高度远超汽车所能达到的范围。该物体靠近她的车辆，直接悬停在上方，随后发出类似飞机的噪音并飞离。

与此同时，[已删除姓名]女士和她的邻居在市政道路上（1号公路东段与207号公路交叉口以东一英里、以南一英里及以东半英里处）驾车时，观察到多云的天空中出现了三个圆形的亮红色物体。据描述，这些物体大约有汽车大小。它们起初在高空被发现，随后向目击者的车辆俯冲。这些物体在车顶上方悬停了几秒钟，然后加速离去。整个事件持续了几分钟。

**物体描述：** 描述中包含了两种截然不同的视觉体验。其中一个物体被描述为体积庞大，带有两个明亮的外部灯光和一个位于后部的小红灯，并发出类似飞机的噪音。第二种描述涉及三个独立的圆形物体，呈亮红色，每个大约有汽车大小。两起事件中物体的运动轨迹均包括：高空定位、向目击者俯冲、悬停阶段以及快速离去。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对第一起目击事件的当事人进行了访谈，并正式评估认为她们精神状态稳定且证词可靠。调查警官得出结论，认为目击者看到的很可能是飞机，并援引了近期关于飞机在开启着陆灯的情况下低空飞行的报告。因此，针对该报告未采取进一步的官方行动。针对[已删除姓名]女士及其邻居的目击事件，警方启动了一份单独的报告，记录显示后续将会有进一步的调查报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lawrence Charles Smith (also referred to as Lawrence Chas Smith), Manus Eugene Smith (also referred to as Manns Eugene Smith), Timothy Daniel Neilson (Cpl.), Cathelene Mary Smith, Carole June Smith, and unnamed men engaged in "jacklighting" deer.

**Date / Time:** November 25, 1970, between 9:30 PM and 9:50 PM AST. (Note: Some documents contain clerical errors citing November 26 or December 25, but the primary investigation confirms the event date as Nov 25).

**Location:** Shelburne County, Nova Scotia, specifically near Lower Shag Harbour, Smithville, Port LaTour, and the No. 3 Highway near Bear Point.

**Sighting:** Multiple witnesses reported a series of reddish-orange lights appearing in the night sky. Lawrence and Manus Smith, while driving toward Shag Harbour, observed five to six lights suspended 30–50 feet in the air, approximately 150 feet from their vehicle. They reported that their car stopped while traveling at 45 M.P.H. and their tape player ceased functioning. Lawrence Smith reported a "blank" in his memory of approximately 10 minutes. Simultaneously, in Smithville and Port LaTour, Cpl. Timothy Daniel Neilson, Cathelene Mary Smith, and Carole June Smith observed four lights in a straight line at a 20-degree downward angle. These witnesses noted that one of the center lights would periodically extinguish and reappear. The lights were observed for 20–60 seconds before sinking below the tree line or disappearing. Unnamed men "jacklighting" deer also reported their vehicle stalling and tape player failing upon encountering five lights.

**Object:** The objects were described as perfectly round, reddish-orange or fiery orange lights, ranging from 16 to 30 inches in diameter. They appeared solid with no reflecting rays. The lights were observed in formations of four, five, or six, sometimes in a straight line at a 20-degree slant, and other times in staggered formations (with some lights positioned 4–8 feet above others). The objects were silent and remained stationary or moved slowly before disappearing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP (Cst. R.E. Keeping and Cpl. C.M.D.) conducted an extensive investigation, interviewing witnesses separately and patrolling the wooded areas, finding no physical evidence. Col. Rushton of CFS Barrington confirmed that one of his personnel had witnessed a similar event. The RCMP concluded the witnesses were credible, reliable, and not prone to superstition or alcohol. The reports were forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) Radio and Electrical Engineering Division. Investigators noted the potential for a strong magnetic field affecting the vehicles and tape players, though no definitive scientific explanation was found. Diagrams were produced by witnesses to illustrate the specific, non-linear arrangement of the lights.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 劳伦斯·查尔斯·史密斯（Lawrence Charles Smith，又称 Lawrence Chas Smith）、马努斯·尤金·史密斯（Manus Eugene Smith，又称 Manns Eugene Smith）、蒂莫西·丹尼尔·尼尔森（Timothy Daniel Neilson，下士）、凯瑟琳·玛丽·史密斯（Cathelene Mary Smith）、卡罗尔·琼·史密斯（Carole June Smith），以及几名正在进行“夜间探照捕鹿”（jacklighting）的匿名男子。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年11月25日，大西洋标准时间（AST）晚上9:30至9:50之间。（注：部分文档因笔误记录为11月26日或12月25日，但初步调查确认事件发生日期为11月25日）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省谢尔本县（Shelburne County），具体位于下沙格港（Lower Shag Harbour）、史密斯维尔（Smithville）、拉图尔港（Port LaTour）以及靠近熊点（Bear Point）的3号公路附近。

**目击经过：** 多名目击者报告称夜空中出现了一系列红橙色的光团。劳伦斯·史密斯和马努斯·史密斯在开车前往沙格港的途中，观察到五个到六个光团悬浮在距离地面30至50英尺的空中，距离他们的车辆约150英尺。他们报告称，当车辆以每小时45英里的速度行驶时突然熄火，车载磁带播放器也停止了工作。劳伦斯·史密斯称自己有约10分钟的记忆“空白”。与此同时，在史密斯维尔和拉图尔港，蒂莫西·丹尼尔·尼尔森下士、凯瑟琳·玛丽·史密斯和卡罗尔·琼·史密斯观察到四个呈直线排列、向下倾斜20度的光团。这些目击者注意到，其中一个中间的光团会周期性地熄灭并重新出现。这些光团被观察了20至60秒，随后沉入树线以下或消失。几名正在“夜间探照捕鹿”的匿名男子也报告称，他们在遇到五个光团时，车辆熄火且磁带播放器失灵。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为完美的圆形、红橙色或火橙色的光团，直径在16至30英寸之间。它们看起来是实心的，没有反射光线。这些光团以四个、五个或六个一组的队形出现，有时呈20度倾斜的直线排列，有时呈交错队形（部分光团位于其他光团上方4至8英尺处）。这些物体保持静默，在消失前保持静止或缓慢移动。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP，由 R.E. Keeping 警员和 C.M.D. 下士负责）进行了广泛的调查，分别采访了目击者并巡逻了林区，但未发现任何物理证据。巴林顿加拿大武装部队基地（CFS Barrington）的拉什顿上校（Col. Rushton）证实，他的一名下属也目击了类似的事件。加拿大皇家骑警得出结论，认为目击者可信、可靠，且不易受迷信影响或受酒精干扰。报告被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）无线电与电气工程部。调查人员指出，强磁场可能对车辆和磁带播放器产生了影响，但未找到确切的科学解释。目击者绘制了图表，以说明这些光团特殊的非线性排列方式。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Gerald Lloyd Adams, Donna Martin (referred to as his girlfriend).

**Date / Time:** October 24, 1970, at approximately 1:00 A.M. CDT (also noted as 0700Z to 0900Z).

**Location:** MacGregor/Bagot, Manitoba. The initial sighting occurred two miles north and one mile west of MacGregor; a second sighting occurred two miles northwest of the first location.

**Sighting:** Gerald Adams and Donna Martin were sitting in a truck parked on a trail road 3–4 miles north of MacGregor when they observed a bright light. Initially mistaking it for an approaching car, they realized the object was hovering in a field approximately one-half mile away. Adams decided to approach the object on foot; Martin, initially scared, accompanied him. They observed a humanoid figure approximately one-half mile from the craft, walking northward with difficulty. The figure was described as 4 feet tall, possessing a head, arms, and legs, and wearing a silver metallic uniform with a helmet. Adams reported being within 50 feet of this entity. After returning home, Adams observed the object had relocated further northwest, remaining low to the ground before it eventually lifted vertically and departed rapidly, disappearing within 30 seconds. The night was clear with visible stars, Northern Lights, and light clouds. Martin also observed falling stars during the event.

**Object:** The craft was described as an oblong or disc-shaped object, approximately 5 feet high and 8 feet in diameter, with a tapered, bowl-shaped bottom. It was orange-yellow in color. The top featured nine rods (2 feet high) arranged in three clusters of three, each topped with a red light. A dark flange or structure encircled the center, exhibiting a wavering motion and extending about a foot from the body. Above this flange, there was a window approximately one foot high emitting a bright yellow light. The object was noted to be bright enough to illuminate the sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP in Carberry, Manitoba, interviewed Adams, though the report was not initially forwarded to the CFOC or NRC, necessitating a reminder regarding standard reporting procedures. Adams engaged in correspondence with Peter M. Millman of the National Research Council (NRC) regarding file M45-1-101. Adams explicitly rejected the NRC’s official conclusion that the sighting was a mirage of tower lights from Neepawa, arguing the distance was too great and such a phenomenon had never been observed there before. Millman and Halliday noted that the moon rose at 2:04 A.M. CDT, contradicting the witnesses' claims that the moon was shining at 1:00 A.M. Adams provided a hand-drawn sketch of the craft and expressed a strong desire for further information regarding the "little silver man."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 杰拉尔德·劳埃德·亚当斯 (Gerald Lloyd Adams)、唐娜·马丁 (Donna Martin，据称为其女友)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年10月24日，大约凌晨1:00（中部夏令时间，CDT；亦记录为0700Z至0900Z）。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省麦格雷戈 (MacGregor) / 巴戈特 (Bagot) 地区。首次目击发生在麦格雷戈以北两英里、以西一英里处；第二次目击发生在距离首个地点西北两英里处。

**目击经过：** 杰拉尔德·亚当斯和唐娜·马丁当时坐在麦格雷戈以北3至4英里处一条林间小路上停放的卡车里，这时他们观察到了一道亮光。起初他们误以为是迎面驶来的汽车，随后意识到该物体正悬停在约半英里外的一片田野上。亚当斯决定步行靠近该物体；马丁起初感到害怕，但随后也陪同前往。他们在距离飞行器约半英里处观察到一个类人生物，正步履蹒跚地向北走去。据描述，该生物身高约4英尺，拥有头部、手臂和腿，身穿银色金属制服并戴着头盔。亚当斯报告称，他曾靠近至距离该实体不到50英尺的地方。回到家后，亚当斯观察到该物体已移动到更偏西北的位置，保持在低空，随后垂直升起并迅速离开，在30秒内消失不见。当晚天空晴朗，可见星星、北极光和少量云层。马丁在事件过程中还观察到了流星。

**物体描述：** 该飞行器被描述为一个长方形或圆盘状物体，高约5英尺，直径约8英尺，底部呈锥形碗状，颜色为橙黄色。顶部设有九根杆子（高2英尺），分为三组，每组三根，每根顶端都有一个红灯。一个深色的凸缘或结构环绕在中心，呈现出摇摆的运动状态，并从主体向外延伸约一英尺。在该凸缘上方，有一个约一英尺高的窗户，发出明亮的黄光。据记录，该物体亮度极高，足以照亮天空。

**调查/后续：** 马尼托巴省卡伯里 (Carberry) 的加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 对亚当斯进行了询问，但该报告最初并未转发给加拿大不明飞行物中心 (CFOC) 或加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC)，因此需要提醒其遵守标准报告程序。亚当斯就档案 M45-1-101 与国家研究委员会 (NRC) 的彼得·M·米尔曼 (Peter M. Millman) 进行了通信。亚当斯明确拒绝了 NRC 关于该目击事件是尼帕瓦 (Neepawa) 塔灯海市蜃楼的官方结论，理由是距离太远，且该地区此前从未观察到此类现象。米尔曼和哈利迪 (Halliday) 指出，月亮是在凌晨2:04（CDT）升起的，这与目击者称凌晨1:00时月光明亮的说法相矛盾。亚当斯提供了该飞行器的手绘草图，并表示强烈希望获得有关“银色小人”的更多信息。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ms. F.R. Woodward, Mr. F.R. Woodward (referred to as "Fred" and "the husband"), and an unnamed writer/author.

**Date / Time:** October 31, 1970, approximately 10:00 p.m.

**Location:** 440 Albert St, Windsor, N.S. (with additional reports of sightings in the Mount Dennis and Weston areas).

**Sighting:** On the evening of Halloween, the Woodwards were in their living room when the author heard a strange noise, causing their cat to react and look toward the window. Upon looking out, the author observed that the shadows of a tree and a house addition were illuminated clearly. Initially, Mr. Woodward (Fred) was skeptical and refused to look. However, approximately 10 to 12 minutes later, he observed the object and called the author to witness it. The object was positioned across the street, hovering above a playground directly opposite the living room window. The sky was clear at the time of the observation. The witnesses watched the object for 5 to 10 minutes before it faded away. Other reports from the Mount Dennis and Weston areas suggest the object was seen by others, though their identities remain unknown. One witness noted that after the object displayed a "pink colour," it disappeared; they went outside immediately but could neither see nor hear anything, leading them to conclude the object must have been traveling at a very high speed to vanish and return in such a short window.

**Object:** The object was described as round, resembling a "ball of fire" with small yellowish lights. It appeared to be shining, emitting sparks, and was compared to a sharp light. It was estimated to be 500 to 600 feet from the home. During the observation, it gradually dimmed, described as "just like a fire going out," before fading completely. It was observed moving in a northerly direction. No specific sound was identified by the Woodwards due to ambient noise in the house, though the initial sighting was triggered by a "strange noise."

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The file contains documentation processed by the National Research Council of Canada. The report includes specific location data (440 Albert St) and weather conditions (clear sky). The investigation notes the discrepancy between the Woodwards' account and the reports from the Mount Dennis and Weston areas, where witnesses noted a "pink colour" and high-speed movement. The file serves as a collection of personal accounts and correspondence regarding these "unusual experiences."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** F.R. 伍德沃德女士 (Ms. F.R. Woodward)、F.R. 伍德沃德先生 (Mr. F.R. Woodward，文中称为“弗雷德”及“丈夫”)，以及一位未具名的作家。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年10月31日，晚上10:00左右。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省温莎市阿尔伯特街440号（另有报告称在丹尼斯山和韦斯顿地区也有目击记录）。

**目击经过：** 万圣节当晚，伍德沃德夫妇正在客厅里，这时那位作家听到了一种奇怪的声音，导致他们的猫产生反应并看向窗外。作家向外望去，发现树木和房屋扩建部分的影子被清晰地照亮了。起初，伍德沃德先生（弗雷德）持怀疑态度，拒绝查看。然而，大约10到12分钟后，他也观察到了该物体，并叫作家一同观看。该物体位于街对面，悬停在客厅窗户正对面的操场上方。观测时天空晴朗。目击者观察了该物体5到10分钟，随后它逐渐消失。来自丹尼斯山和韦斯顿地区的其他报告表明，该物体也被其他人看到，尽管他们的身份不明。其中一位目击者指出，该物体在呈现出“粉红色”后消失了；他们立即走到室外，但既没看到也没听到任何动静，因此推断该物体一定是以极高的速度移动，才能在如此短的时间内消失并返回。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，类似于一个带有黄色小光的“火球”。它看起来闪闪发光，不断喷射火花，被比作一道刺眼的光芒。据估计，它距离住宅约500到600英尺。在观测过程中，它逐渐变暗，被形容为“就像火熄灭了一样”，随后完全消失。观测显示它向北移动。由于屋内环境噪音，伍德沃德夫妇没有辨认出任何特定的声音，尽管最初的目击是由一种“奇怪的声音”引发的。

**调查/后续：** 该档案包含由加拿大国家研究委员会处理的文件。报告包括具体的地点数据（阿尔伯特街440号）和天气状况（晴空）。调查指出，伍德沃德夫妇的描述与丹尼斯山和韦斯顿地区目击者的报告存在差异，后者提到了“粉红色”和高速移动。该档案汇集了关于这些“异常经历”的个人陈述和信件。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of Courtenay (redacted in some records), Cst. W. E. Anderson, and Cst. Caughill.

**Date / Time:** November 27, 1970, at 9:15 p.m. PST.

**Location:** 19th Street, Courtenay, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 27, 1970, a civilian resident of Courtenay reported a UFO sighting near 19th Street. Following this report, Cst. W. E. Anderson and Cst. Caughill conducted a patrol of the area. The officers observed the object in clear skies with good visibility. The witnesses tracked the object as it traveled in an easterly direction for a duration of approximately 30 seconds before it disappeared from view. The altitude of the object was estimated to be approximately 6,000 feet.

**Object:** The object was described as round or oval in shape and light orange in color. It did not emit any sound during the observation. Subsequent investigation identified the object as a homemade device—specifically, a dry cleaning plastic bag attached to a light-gauge wire hoop. A piece of cotton soaked in solvent was suspended in the center of the hoop and ignited; the resulting hot air filled the bag, causing it to elevate and drift.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Courtenay Detachment filed an official report regarding the sighting. Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Comox was notified of the event during the investigation. It was ultimately determined that a local boy was responsible for constructing and launching the device. The incident was formally reported to the National Research Council (N.R.C.) Meteor Centre via telex. Following the identification of the object as a homemade hot-air balloon, no further investigation was conducted.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名考特尼（Courtenay）的平民居民（部分记录中已隐去姓名）、W. E. 安德森警官（Cst. W. E. Anderson）以及考希尔警官（Cst. Caughill）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年11月27日，太平洋标准时间晚上9:15。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省考特尼市第19街。

**目击经过：** 1970年11月27日晚，一名考特尼的平民居民报告称在第19街附近目击到一个不明飞行物。接到报告后，W. E. 安德森警官和考希尔警官对该区域进行了巡逻。在能见度良好的晴朗夜空中，警官们观察到了该物体。目击者追踪了该物体的飞行轨迹，它向东飞行了约30秒后消失在视野中。据估计，该物体的飞行高度约为6,000英尺。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形或椭圆形，呈浅橙色。在观察过程中，它没有发出任何声音。随后的调查确认该物体为一个自制装置，具体来说，是一个连接在轻型金属丝环上的干洗店塑料袋。在金属丝环的中心悬挂着一块浸过溶剂的棉花并将其点燃；产生的热空气充满塑料袋，使其升空并随风飘移。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）考特尼分局就此次目击事件提交了正式报告。调查期间，科莫克斯加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Comox）也接到了相关通知。最终确定该装置是由当地一名男孩制作并放飞的。该事件通过电传正式报告给了加拿大国家研究委员会（N.R.C.）流星中心。在确认该物体为自制热气球后，未再进行进一步调查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The crew of the CCGS Narwhal.

**Sighting:** A report was received regarding an object sighted at a bearing of 137 degrees and approximately 20 degrees high. The object was observed moving very slowly in a westward direction to a position 10 miles west of Egg Island.

**Object:** The object was described as saucer-shaped. While it was suggested that the object could be a weather balloon, observers using field glasses maintained that it appeared saucer-shaped.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted via teletype to the National Research Council for Radio and Electrical Engineering Division.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_05_-_Pages_12.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** CCGS Narwhal 号船员。

**目击：** 接到一份关于在方位角 137 度、高度约 20 度处发现物体的报告。该物体被观察到以非常缓慢的速度向西移动，最终到达蛋岛（Egg Island）以西 10 英里处的位置。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为碟形。虽然有人提出该物体可能是气象气球，但使用双筒望远镜的观察者坚持认为它看起来是碟形的。

**后续：** 该报告通过电传打字机发送至加拿大国家研究委员会无线电与电气工程部。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. [Name redacted] (residents of Haines Junction), and several civilian residents of MacIntosh Lodge, Destruction Bay, and Haines Junction, Y.T.

**Date / Time:** November 30, 1970, at approximately 9:00 P.M. (Follow-up observations occurred December 1–3, 1970).

**Location:** Haines Junction, Destruction Bay, and MacIntosh Lodge, Yukon Territory.

**Sighting:** On the night of November 30, 1970, at approximately 9:00 P.M., multiple witnesses across the Yukon region observed a significant aerial phenomenon. Mr. and Mrs. [Name redacted] reported seeing a large ball of blue light traveling from the south at an enormous rate of speed. They estimated the object’s altitude at 35,000 to 40,000 feet, moving at a 45-degree angle toward the earth. The sighting lasted approximately 30 seconds, during which the light was so intense that the countryside was illuminated brighter than natural daylight. 

Other civilian witnesses in MacIntosh Lodge, Destruction Bay, and Haines Junction described the event as an instantaneous, very white flash, comparable to a fluorescent light, which also illuminated the surrounding countryside. Following the disappearance of the object over the northern or northwestern horizon, witnesses reported a loud, boom-like explosion occurring approximately 30 seconds later. This was followed by sounds described as resembling underground mine rumblings or thunder-like rumbles originating from the north/northwest. Mr. and Mrs. [Name redacted] estimated that the object made contact with the earth approximately 75 miles from their sighting location.

**Object:** The object was described as a large ball of blue light, slightly smaller than a full moon, featuring a trailing blue streak or tail that covered half the visible sky. The light was compared to an acetylene torch in color and intensity. Other reports characterized the phenomenon simply as a bright, white flash, with official documentation categorizing the event as a "Meteor or Fireball."

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted interviews with Mr. and Mrs. [Name redacted] on December 1, 1970, and formally noted that the couple possessed a favorable reputation in the community and were considered reliable witnesses. Regarding the aftermath, one witness reported observing vapour clouds rising from the suspected crash site during the daylight hours of December 1st and 2nd. These clouds were no longer visible by December 3rd, 1970. The RCMP detachment noted that no additional reports regarding these vapour clouds were received, and no further official investigation details were provided.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [姓名已删除] 夫妇（海恩斯章克申居民），以及麦金托什旅馆、毁灭湾和育空地区海恩斯章克申的多位平民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年11月30日，约晚上9:00。（后续观察发生在1970年12月1日至3日）。

**地点：** 育空地区海恩斯章克申、毁灭湾和麦金托什旅馆。

**目击经过：** 1970年11月30日晚约9:00，育空地区的众多目击者观察到了一起重大的空中现象。[姓名已删除] 夫妇报告称，看到一个巨大的蓝色光球从南方以极高的速度飞过。他们估计该物体高度在35,000至40,000英尺之间，正以45度角向地面移动。目击过程持续了约30秒，期间光芒极其强烈，将乡村照得比自然日光还要明亮。

麦金托什旅馆、毁灭湾和海恩斯章克申的其他平民目击者将此次事件描述为一次瞬间的、非常耀眼的白色闪光，类似于荧光灯，同样照亮了周围的乡村。在物体消失于北部或西北部地平线后，目击者报告称约30秒后听到了一声巨大的、类似爆炸的轰鸣声。随后，从北/西北方向传来了类似地下矿井震动或雷鸣般的隆隆声。[姓名已删除] 夫妇估计，该物体在距离他们目击地点约75英里处与地面发生了接触。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的蓝色光球，略小于满月，拖着一条覆盖了半个可见天空的蓝色尾迹。其颜色和强度被比作乙炔焊炬。其他报告则简单地将其描述为明亮的白色闪光，官方文件将此次事件归类为“流星或火球”。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）于1970年12月1日对 [姓名已删除] 夫妇进行了访谈，并正式记录称这对夫妇在社区中享有良好声誉，被认为是可靠的目击者。关于后续情况，一名目击者报告称在12月1日和2日的白天观察到疑似坠毁地点有蒸汽云升起。到1970年12月3日，这些云已不再可见。加拿大皇家骑警分局指出，未收到关于这些蒸汽云的其他报告，也没有提供进一步的官方调查细节。

**见证者：** 一名居住在哈夫洛克（Havelock）R.R. #2 Fork Stream Road 的平民，以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员 G.R. Bambury 和 L.G. Myra。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted], Cst. M.B. O'NEIL, Cst. S.W. Slade, and the reporting officer (unnamed).

**Date / Time:** December 19, 1970; sightings occurred at 6:30 PM, 8:05 PM, and approximately 8:30 PM.

**Location:** St. Charles, Prince Edward Island (PEI).

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 19, 1970, under dark and snowy weather conditions, Mrs. [redacted] reported a series of three UFO sightings in St. Charles, PEI. The first sighting occurred at 6:30 PM, the second at 8:05 PM, and a third at approximately 8:30 PM. Mrs. [redacted] observed the objects moving in a south to southeasterly direction. She described the objects as appearing like stars that emitted flashes of fire or light. Each sighting lasted between 5 and 10 minutes. During the events, the objects produced a distinct noise described as "SHHHHHH" or similar to air escaping from a balloon. Mrs. [redacted] noted that while one object landed in her yard, the other two landed in a nearby wooded area. Upon contact with the snow, the objects extinguished themselves. The RCMP Souris Detachment was contacted regarding the final sighting, and officers arrived to investigate the scene in an open field.

**Object:** The recovered object was identified as a large, off-white, plastic item measuring approximately 4 feet in length and 2 feet in width, resembling a large plastic garbage bag. Physical examination revealed it featured a cardboard rim, a piece of wire, a wire coil, some cloth fabric, and a thin wire covered with paper at the open end. The object appeared scorched, contained soot inside, and emitted a smell of burning.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Members of the RCMP Souris Detachment, including Cst. M.B. O'NEIL and Cst. S.W. Slade, conducted an investigation at the scene and recovered the object from the field. The item was initially held at the Souris Detachment for examination. On December 23, 1970, the object was transferred to the custody of personnel from CFB Summerside, PEI, at which point the official file was considered closed.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]女士、M.B. O'NEIL警官、S.W. SLADE警官，以及报告警官（姓名未详）。

**日期/时间：** 1970年12月19日；目击时间分别为下午6:30、晚上8:05及约晚上8:30。

**地点：** 爱德华王子岛（PEI）圣查尔斯（St. Charles）。

**目击经过：** 1970年12月19日晚，在阴暗多雪的天气条件下，[已删除]女士报告在爱德华王子岛圣查尔斯发生了三起不明飞行物目击事件。第一次目击发生在下午6:30，第二次在晚上8:05，第三次在晚上8:30左右。[已删除]女士观察到这些物体向南至东南方向移动。她描述这些物体看起来像闪烁着火光或亮光的星星。每次目击持续时间在5到10分钟之间。在事件过程中，这些物体发出了一种独特的噪音，被描述为“嘶嘶”声，类似于气球漏气的声音。[已删除]女士注意到，其中一个物体降落在她的院子里，另外两个则降落在附近的林区。当接触到积雪时，这些物体便熄灭了。针对最后一次目击事件，她联系了加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）苏里斯（Souris）分遣队，警官随后抵达现场，对一片开阔地进行了调查。

**物体描述：** 经回收的物体被确认为一个大型的灰白色塑料制品，长约4英尺，宽约2英尺，外观类似于一个大型塑料垃圾袋。物理检查显示，该物体具有一个纸板边缘、一段金属丝、一个金属线圈、一些布料，以及开口处覆盖着纸张的细金属丝。该物体表面有灼烧痕迹，内部含有煤烟，并散发出烧焦的气味。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警苏里斯分遣队的成员，包括M.B. O'NEIL警官和S.W. SLADE警官，在现场进行了调查并从田野中回收了该物体。该物品最初被存放在苏里斯分遣队进行检查。1970年12月23日，该物体被移交给爱德华王子岛萨默赛德（Summerside）加拿大空军基地的相关人员，随后该官方档案被视为结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of Havelock R.R. #2 (Fork Stream Road), residents of Scoth Road R.R. #2 (Coles Island), RCMP Constable G.R. Bambury, and RCMP Constable L.G. Myra.

**Date / Time:** December 1, 1970, at 8:30 P.M. A.S.T. (initial sighting); sightings continued daily between 8:00 P.M. and 6:00 A.M. for two weeks. A specific observation occurred on December 22, 1970, at approximately 9:00 P.M.

**Location:** Canaan Forks, Queens County, New Brunswick (including sightings from Havelock R.R. #2, Fork Stream Road, Scoth Road R.R. #2, Coles Island, and Chipman).

**Sighting:** The event began on December 1, 1970, at 8:30 P.M. A.S.T., when residents of the Canaan Forks area reported a strange phenomenon in the sky. The object remained visible for two weeks, appearing daily between 8:00 P.M. and 6:00 A.M. It was consistently observed at an altitude of approximately one mile, located in the eastern sky, roughly 1/2 mile from Canaan Forks, and traveling in a southerly direction. 

On December 17, 1970, Cst. G.R. Bambury patrolled the Havelock area and confirmed observing the object at a high altitude. On December 18, 1970, Csts. Bambury and L.G. Myra returned to the area to investigate. A separate incident occurred on December 22, 1970, at 9:00 P.M., when a civilian pointed out a bright object to an RCMP officer under clear skies. The civilian, using a rifle telescope, reported seeing shifting colors, while the officer, using binoculars, observed only a bright, steady white light. This specific object was also visible from Chipman.

**Object:** The primary object was described as circular in shape. It featured a large red light on top that emitted a distinct glow, a band of greenish-colored lights around the middle, and a white light on the bottom. Witnesses reported that fire appeared to shoot out of four or five "legs" located on the bottom of the craft. During the December 22 sighting, the object appeared as a bright star or planet, significantly brighter than any other celestial body in the sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Petitcodiac detachment deemed the civilian observers to be reliable. Reports were formally forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre and RCMP "J" Division in Fredericton, as well as the Chipman Detachment. Regarding the December 22 sighting, the investigating RCMP officer concluded that the varying colors reported by the civilian through the rifle telescope were likely optical artifacts caused by reflections within the rifle lens. No further official action was taken by the RCMP following these investigations.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 哈夫洛克（Havelock）R.R. #2（福克溪路）的一名平民居民、斯科思路（Scoth Road）R.R. #2（科尔斯岛）的居民、加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警官 G.R. 班伯里（G.R. Bambury）以及加拿大皇家骑警警官 L.G. 迈拉（L.G. Myra）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年12月1日，大西洋标准时间（A.S.T.）晚上8:30（首次目击）；此后两周内，每天晚上8:00至次日凌晨6:00持续出现目击事件。1970年12月22日晚上约9:00发生了另一次特定观测。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省皇后县迦南福克斯（Canaan Forks）（包括从哈夫洛克 R.R. #2、福克溪路、斯科思路 R.R. #2、科尔斯岛和奇普曼等地点的目击报告）。

**目击经过：** 事件始于1970年12月1日大西洋标准时间晚上8:30，当时迦南福克斯地区的居民报告称天空中出现了奇异现象。该物体在两周内持续可见，每天晚上8:00至次日凌晨6:00出现。观测显示其高度始终保持在约一英里处，位于迦南福克斯以东约半英里处的天空中，并向南移动。

1970年12月17日，G.R. 班伯里警官在哈夫洛克地区巡逻时，证实观测到了该高空物体。1970年12月18日，班伯里警官与 L.G. 迈拉警官返回该地区进行调查。1970年12月22日晚上9:00发生了另一起独立事件：在晴朗的天空下，一名平民向一名加拿大皇家骑警警官指出了一个明亮的物体。该平民通过步枪瞄准镜观察，报告称看到了不断变化的颜色；而该警官通过双筒望远镜观察，仅看到了一道明亮且稳定的白光。该特定物体在奇普曼地区也清晰可见。

**物体描述：** 主要物体被描述为圆形。其顶部有一个发出独特光芒的大红灯，中部环绕着一圈绿色的灯光，底部则有一个白灯。目击者报告称，飞行器底部有四到五个“支腿”，并有火焰从中喷出。在12月22日的目击事件中，该物体看起来像一颗明亮的恒星或行星，比天空中任何其他天体都要明亮得多。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警佩蒂科迪亚克（Petitcodiac）分遣队认为这些平民目击者是可靠的。报告被正式转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心、位于弗雷德里克顿的加拿大皇家骑警“J”分部以及奇普曼分遣队。关于12月22日的目击事件，负责调查的警官得出结论：平民通过步枪瞄准镜观察到的颜色变化，很可能是步枪镜片内部反射引起的光学伪影。在此次调查之后，加拿大皇家骑警未再采取进一步的官方行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** RCMP Constables Graham J.H., Wilson W.A., and Taylor A.G.; Department of Transport (DOT) employees Trevor Worobo and Bailey Holte.

**Date / Time:** December 27, 1970, from approximately 5:20 A.M. MST to 8:00 A.M. MST.

**Location:** Fort McMurray, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the morning of December 27, 1970, a group of RCMP officers and DOT employees observed two distinct objects in the sky over Fort McMurray. The sighting began at 5:20 A.M. and lasted for nearly three hours, concluding at 8:00 A.M. The observers reported that the objects appeared to move slightly and exhibited a synchronized rising and falling motion. Throughout the duration of the event, the sky was noted as being clear.

**Object:** Two oval-shaped objects were observed, both moving in a northwesterly direction. 
*   **Object No. 1:** Described as a bright white, bluish oval, positioned at an elevation of 75 miles above the horizon.
*   **Object No. 2:** Described as a dull, hazy, reddish-brown oval, positioned at an elevation of 50 miles above the horizon.
Both objects maintained their relative positions while rising and falling in tandem. No sound was reported in association with the objects.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation involved both RCMP personnel and the Department of Transport. To gain precise data on the objects' positions, the observers utilized a theodolite to take formal readings at 6:07 A.M. and 6:16 A.M. 

Following the initial report, the RCMP conducted a check with the local DOT weather station, which confirmed that there were no aircraft in the vicinity at the time of the sighting. The matter was referred to the Edmonton DOT office for further analysis. The Edmonton DOT initially suggested that the objects might be a "Morning Star." Upon further review and consultation, DOT officials concluded that the objects were, in fact, the two "Morning Stars" (Venus). The official determination was that the sighting was a natural astronomical phenomenon and that there was no cause for further concern or investigation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员格雷厄姆·J.H.（Graham J.H.）、威尔逊·W.A.（Wilson W.A.）和泰勒·A.G.（Taylor A.G.）；交通部（DOT）员工特雷弗·沃罗博（Trevor Worobo）和贝利·霍尔特（Bailey Holte）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年12月27日，约凌晨5:20（山区标准时间）至上午8:00（山区标准时间）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省麦克默里堡（Fort McMurray）。

**目击经过：** 1970年12月27日清晨，一群加拿大皇家骑警警员和交通部员工在麦克默里堡上空观察到了两个独特的物体。目击事件始于凌晨5:20，持续了近三个小时，于上午8:00结束。观察者报告称，这些物体似乎有轻微移动，并表现出同步的升降运动。在整个事件过程中，天空晴朗无云。

**物体描述：** 观察到了两个椭圆形物体，均向西北方向移动。
*   **物体1号：** 被描述为一个明亮的白色带蓝色调的椭圆体，位于地平线上方75英里处。
*   **物体2号：** 被描述为一个暗淡、模糊的红褐色椭圆体，位于地平线上方50英里处。
两个物体在同步升降的同时保持了它们的相对位置。据报告，这些物体没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 调查工作由加拿大皇家骑警和交通部共同参与。为了获取物体位置的精确数据，观察者使用经纬仪在凌晨6:07和6:16进行了正式读数。

在初步报告之后，加拿大皇家骑警向当地交通部气象站进行了核实，确认目击当时附近没有任何飞行器。此事被转交至埃德蒙顿交通部办公室进行进一步分析。埃德蒙顿交通部最初认为这些物体可能是“晨星”。经过进一步审查和咨询，交通部官员得出结论，这些物体实际上就是两颗“晨星”（金星）。官方最终认定，此次目击事件属于自然天文现象，无需进行进一步的关注或调查。

**Witnesses:** An announcer at CJFB Television Station, an employee of the Success Compressor Station, B. [redacted], a maintenance man at the Success Compressor Station, Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], [redacted], a civilian witness, Cst. C.A. Lentowicz (RCMP), and Mr. and Mrs. [unclear].

**Date / Time:** January 9, 1971; sightings occurred between approximately 7:45 A.M. and 9:10 A.M., with a follow-up report made to the RCMP at 6:00 P.M. that evening.

**Location:** Success, Saskatchewan; specifically the area surrounding the Saskatchewan Power Corp Compressor Station and the road between Cantuar and Success.

**Sighting:** On the morning of January 9, 1971, multiple witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon near the Success Compressor Station. One witness, driving from Cantuar toward Success, observed the object moving ahead of them, performing an arc maneuver, meeting them at a corner two miles west of the highway, turning right, moving north around buildings, and heading south toward the station tanks. Another witness, observing from the northwest of the station, watched the object remain in a fixed position for ten minutes before it faded and moved away with a slight "bobbing" motion. When witnesses attempted to approach the object by car, it vanished. 

Accounts describe the object’s appearance as highly mutable. Initially, it was seen as a long, narrow, flat-surfaced horizontal bar of dull white light traveling at speeds estimated over 100 mph. It then transitioned into a disc shape with a smaller disc underneath, emitting a yellow light. Near Caswell’s farm, it shifted into an irregular shape resembling a "deep wall" of mixed colors with vertically moving lights similar to the Northern Lights. Finally, it manifested as a dark red ball or mass, comparable in size to a full moon, which hovered near the compressor station tanks for approximately 15 minutes. Some witnesses initially feared the tanks were on fire due to the object's red glow.

**Object:** The object was described as a shape-shifter, transitioning from a flat, dull white bar to a dual-disc configuration (yellow light), then to an irregular, multi-colored light display, and finally to a dull red, spherical mass. It lacked a distinct outer line, appeared hazy, and exhibited a bobbing motion. It made no audible sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Swift Current detachment received reports on January 9 and formally documented the event in telex # SC 8. Cst. C.A. Lentowicz interviewed several witnesses and witnessed their statements. The RCMP noted that the witnesses appeared responsible and reliable, though they requested anonymity to avoid publicity. One witness was unavailable for an interview as they were away on a course, but their account was reported to be consistent with their spouse’s statement. Weather conditions were described as overcast, hazy, and frosty, with clear, peaceful air. A physical search of the area by a witness later that afternoon yielded no evidence. The RCMP investigation concluded that the witnesses were credible, though the object remained unidentified.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** CJFB电视台的一名播音员、萨塞克斯（Success）压缩站的一名员工、B. [已涂黑]（萨塞克斯压缩站的一名维修工）、[已涂黑]夫人、[已涂黑]先生、[已涂黑]（一名平民目击者）、C.A. 伦托维奇（C.A. Lentowicz）警官（加拿大皇家骑警），以及[不详]夫妇。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年1月9日；目击事件发生在上午7:45至9:10之间，当晚6:00向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）提交了后续报告。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省萨塞克斯；具体区域为萨斯喀彻温电力公司压缩站周边，以及坎图尔（Cantuar）与萨塞克斯之间的道路。

**目击经过：** 1971年1月9日上午，多名目击者在萨塞克斯压缩站附近观察到一种不明空中现象。一名目击者在从坎图尔开车前往萨塞克斯的途中，观察到该物体在前方移动，并做出了弧线机动，在距离公路两英里处的一个拐角处与他们相遇，随后右转，绕过建筑物向北移动，最后向南飞向压缩站的储油罐。另一名从压缩站西北方观察的目击者看到该物体在固定位置停留了十分钟，随后逐渐变淡并伴随着轻微的“上下起伏”动作移开。当目击者试图开车靠近该物体时，它消失了。

据描述，该物体的外观极具多变性。起初，它被看作是一条长而窄、表面平坦的暗白色水平光带，飞行速度估计超过每小时100英里。随后，它转变为圆盘状，下方带有一个较小的圆盘，并发出黄光。在卡斯韦尔（Caswell）农场附近，它变成了一种不规则形状，类似于混合颜色的“深墙”，并带有类似北极光的垂直移动光束。最后，它呈现为一个深红色的球体或团块，大小与满月相当，在压缩站储油罐附近盘旋了约15分钟。由于物体发出的红光，一些目击者起初担心储油罐着火了。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一种“变形体”，从平坦的暗白色光带转变为双圆盘结构（发出黄光），接着变为不规则的多色光展示，最后变为暗红色的球状团块。它没有明显的轮廓，看起来模糊不清，并表现出上下起伏的运动。整个过程中未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警斯威夫特卡伦特（Swift Current）分局于1月9日接到报告，并以电传 # SC 8 正式记录了该事件。C.A. 伦托维奇警官采访了几位目击者并记录了他们的陈述。加拿大皇家骑警指出，目击者看起来负责且可靠，尽管他们要求匿名以避免公众关注。其中一名目击者因参加培训课程而无法接受采访，但据称其陈述与配偶的说法一致。当时的天气状况被描述为阴天、有雾且有霜，空气清冷平静。当天下午，一名目击者对该区域进行了实地搜寻，但未发现任何证据。加拿大皇家骑警的调查结论认为目击者是可信的，但该物体仍未被识别。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted] (school bus driver), one school teacher, and approximately fifteen students.

**Date / Time:** March 17, 1971, at 8:00 A.M. Mountain Standard Time.

**Location:** Hawk Hills District, approximately 22 miles North East of Manning, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the morning of March 17, 1971, at 8:00 A.M. MST, a school bus driver (Mrs. [redacted]) was operating a school bus in the Hawk Hills District, northeast of Manning, Alberta, when she and her passengers—a school teacher and approximately fifteen students—observed an unusual object in the sky. The weather conditions at the time of the sighting were reported as clear. The witnesses observed the object hovering in the air for a duration of approximately three minutes. Following this period of stationary hovering, the object moved away. No specific direction of travel was determined by the observers, and the altitude of the object remained undetermined.

**Object:** The object was consistently described by all witnesses as round in shape and silver in color. It remained stationary (hovering) for approximately three minutes before departing. No sound or mechanical features were reported, and no specific direction of travel was noted upon its departure.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally investigated by the Manning Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). The primary witness, Mrs. [redacted], was identified as a long-time resident of the Manning area and a school bus driver for the Manning School Division; both she and the accompanying school teacher were deemed reliable witnesses by local authorities. As of March 22, 1971, the RCMP confirmed that no other sightings had been reported to the detachment regarding this event. The official report was filed by the Manning RCMP and subsequently transmitted to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre and the Canadian Forces Headquarters for further review.

**目击者：** [已删除]女士（校车司机）、一名学校教师以及约十五名学生。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年3月17日，山区标准时间上午8:00。

**地点：** 艾伯塔省曼宁市东北约22英里处的霍克山地区（Hawk Hills District）。

**目击经过：** 1971年3月17日上午8:00（山区标准时间），一名校车司机（[已删除]女士）正在艾伯塔省曼宁市东北部的霍克山地区驾驶校车。当时，她与车上的乘客——一名学校教师和约十五名学生——观察到了天空中出现了一个异常物体。据报告，目击时的天气状况晴朗。目击者观察到该物体在空中悬停了约三分钟。在这一段静止悬停后，该物体随即离开。观察者未能确定其具体的飞行方向，物体的飞行高度也无法确定。

**物体描述：** 所有目击者对该物体的描述一致：呈圆形，银色。它在离开前保持静止（悬停）状态约三分钟。据报告，该物体没有发出任何声音，也未观察到任何机械特征，其离开时的具体方向也未被记录。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）曼宁分局对此次目击事件进行了正式调查。主要目击者[已删除]女士被确认为曼宁地区的长期居民，也是曼宁学区的校车司机；当地当局认为她和随行的学校教师均为可靠的目击者。截至1971年3月22日，加拿大皇家骑警确认，该分局未收到有关此事件的其他目击报告。官方报告由曼宁加拿大皇家骑警存档，并随后转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心及加拿大武装部队总部进行进一步审查。

**目击：** 1971年3月23日晚上9:50（大西洋标准时间），目击者在爱德华王子岛省福琼（Fortune）的2号公路上行驶，当时天气阴天并伴有小雪。目击者观察到一个圆形的亮红色物体，高度约为1500英尺，从东向西移动，并有轻微的下降运动。观察持续了三到四分钟。

**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of Rollo Bay, P.E.I. (also referred to as a civilian observer)

**Date / Time:** March 23, 1971 (reported as March 25, 1971, in some records), at approximately 9:50 PM AST

**Location:** Highway #2, Fortune area, Rollo Bay, P.E.I.

**Sighting:** On the night of the incident, the witness was traveling east on Highway #2 in the Fortune area. Weather conditions were noted as overcast with light snow. The witness observed a round, bright red object at an altitude of approximately 1,500 feet, moving from east to west with a slight downward motion. The observation lasted for three to four minutes. 

As the witness traveled, the object disappeared briefly when the vehicle entered a dip in the road, but the witness regained sight of it upon reaching higher elevation. The witness observed the object appearing to rest on the ground approximately one-quarter mile from the main highway. As the snowfall intensified, the witness noted that the object appeared to lose its brilliance. The witness parked the car to observe the light, which remained stationary on the ground, before contacting the Souris RCMP detachment at 10:15 PM to report the sighting.

**Object:** The object was described as a round, bright red light. It was initially seen at an altitude of 1,500 feet before descending to the ground. It remained stationary once it landed. The object’s brilliance appeared to diminish as the intensity of the snowstorm increased.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Constable O'Neill of the Souris RCMP detachment responded to the report on the night of the sighting. The officer attempted to search the fields near the highway, but the search was negative due to poor visibility caused by the ongoing snowstorm. 

On March 26, 1971, the officer returned to the area to conduct a follow-up investigation. Upon further inspection, the RCMP identified the "object" as a red warning light belonging to a newly constructed radio tower located at Bear River, P.E.I. The tower had only recently been connected to electrical power, making the night of the sighting the first time the red light was visible to the public. With this identification, the file was officially concluded.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 爱德华王子岛省（P.E.I.）罗洛湾（Rollo Bay）的一名平民居民（也被称为平民观察员）

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年3月23日（部分记录显示为1971年3月25日），大西洋标准时间（AST）晚上9:50左右

**地点：** 爱德华王子岛省罗洛湾，福琼（Fortune）地区，2号公路

**目击经过：** 事发当晚，目击者正驾车沿2号公路向东行驶，途经福琼地区。当时天气阴沉，伴有小雪。目击者观察到一个圆形、明亮的红色物体，高度约为1500英尺，正从东向西移动，并伴有轻微的下降动作。观察过程持续了三到四分钟。

当目击者继续行驶时，车辆进入一段低洼路面，物体曾短暂消失，但当车辆到达高处时，目击者再次看到了它。目击者观察到该物体似乎停在距离主干道约四分之一英里处的地面上。随着降雪增强，目击者注意到物体的光芒似乎减弱了。目击者将车停下观察这道光，它在地面上保持静止。随后，目击者于晚上10:15联系了苏里斯（Souris）皇家骑警（RCMP）分局报告了此次目击事件。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个圆形的明亮红光。起初它出现在1500英尺的高空，随后降落至地面。着陆后，它保持静止状态。随着暴风雪强度的增加，物体的亮度似乎有所减弱。

**调查/后续：** 苏里斯皇家骑警分局的奥尼尔（O'Neill）警官在目击当晚接报后进行了响应。该警官试图搜寻公路附近的田野，但由于暴风雪导致能见度极差，搜寻未果。

1971年3月26日，该警官返回现场进行后续调查。经进一步检查，皇家骑警确认该“物体”实际上是位于爱德华王子岛省熊河（Bear River）的一座新建无线电塔上的红色警示灯。该塔当时刚接通电源，因此目击当晚是该红灯首次向公众展示。随着这一身份的确认，该档案被正式结案。

**Witnesses:** RCMP officers on patrol.
