CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Wilbur Kennedy, the Kennedy family, the Charsley family, and the Horner family.

**Date / Time:** September 3 and 4, 1973; follow-up report dated September 5, 1973, at 0130Z.

**Location:** Skead, Ontario.

**Sighting:** The sightings in Skead, Ontario, involved multiple families—the Kennedys, Charsleys, and Horners—who observed anomalous aerial phenomena over the course of two nights. According to the primary reports, the witnesses observed the activity for approximately one hour on the nights of September 3 and 4. A subsequent report filed on September 5, 1973, at 0130Z, noted a sighting under clear weather conditions that lasted for 15 minutes. The witnesses reported that the objects appeared to originate from the east.

**Object:** There is a discrepancy in the number of objects reported across the documentation. Initial reports indicated a single object, but a correction note explicitly clarified that there were 11 objects observed in total. The objects were consistently described as having the shape and appearance of a star. They were noted to be very bright, almost white in color, and were positioned at a very high altitude. Regarding movement, the objects were described as traveling at a very high rate of speed, moving erratically in all directions. No specific sound was recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was formally documented by the Commanding Officer of Canadian Forces Station (CFS) Falconbridge. Official reports were forwarded to the National Defence Headquarters and the National Research Council for review. The documentation includes a record of the weather conditions at the time of the September 5th sighting, which were noted as clear. No further investigative details or sketches were provided in the available file pages.

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年9月3日和4日；后续报告日期为1973年9月5日，0130Z（协调世界时）。

**地点：** 安大略省斯基德（Skead, Ontario）。

**物体描述：** 关于所报告的物体数量，档案记录中存在出入。最初的报告显示只有一个物体，但一份更正说明明确指出总共观察到了11个物体。这些物体被一致描述为具有恒星的形状和外观。据记录，它们非常明亮，颜色近乎白色，且处于极高的高度。在运动方面，这些物体被描述为以极高的速度飞行，并向各个方向不规则地移动。未记录到任何特定的声音。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Donald Grossland, Don Boue, and two unidentified female companions.

**Date / Time:** September 30, 1973, 9:30 PM to October 1, 1973, 12:30 AM.

**Location:** Four and one-half miles east and one mile south of Nipawin, Saskatchewan, near the Carrot River.

**Sighting:** On October 9, 1973, Donald Grossland provided a report to the RCMP regarding an encounter that occurred nine days prior. Grossland stated that he, Don Boue, and two female companions were driving in the countryside when they observed three unidentified flying objects. The witnesses were parked in the area when they first noticed the objects hovering nearby. When the group attempted to leave their parking spot, the three objects began to follow their vehicle. The witnesses reported that the objects pursued them for approximately five miles, maintaining a distance of one-quarter mile intervals from the vehicle. After the five-mile pursuit, the objects gained altitude and disappeared into the night sky.

**Object:** The three objects were described as having a greenish-red glow. Each object was approximately four feet in diameter and was observed to be revolving. They maintained a consistent hovering altitude of approximately eight to ten feet above the ground during the initial encounter and the subsequent pursuit.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was reported to the RCMP Carrot River Detachment. During the interview, Donald Grossland admitted to consuming beer while observing the objects. He explained that he had delayed reporting the sighting until October 9 because he feared that others would perceive him as "crazy." He also declined to identify the two female companions who were present during the event. The RCMP initiated an investigation and transmitted the details via telex (#CRVR-15) to the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa. Subsequent efforts by the RCMP to locate Don Boue were unsuccessful, as he had relocated to British Columbia without leaving a forwarding address. Similarly, the RCMP was unable to establish the current whereabouts of Donald Grossland, who also moved to British Columbia without providing a forwarding address. Due to the inability to contact the primary witnesses, the investigation was officially concluded.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 唐纳德·格罗斯兰（Donald Grossland）、唐·布伊（Don Boue）以及两名身份不明的女性同伴。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年9月30日晚上9:30至1973年10月1日凌晨12:30。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省尼帕温（Nipawin）以东4.5英里、以南1英里处，靠近胡萝卜河（Carrot River）。

**目击经过：** 1973年10月9日，唐纳德·格罗斯兰向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了一起发生于九天前的遭遇事件。格罗斯兰称，当时他与唐·布伊及两名女性同伴驾车行驶在乡间，突然观察到三个不明飞行物。目击者一行人当时正将车停在路边，随后注意到这些物体在附近盘旋。当他们试图驾车离开时，这三个物体开始尾随他们的车辆。据目击者描述，这些物体追踪了他们约五英里，并始终与车辆保持四分之一英里的距离。在五英里的追逐后，这些物体升高并消失在夜空中。

**物体描述：** 这三个物体被描述为散发着红绿色的光芒。每个物体的直径约为四英尺，且在旋转。在最初的遭遇和随后的追逐过程中，它们始终保持在离地约八到十英尺的高度盘旋。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被报告给了加拿大皇家骑警胡萝卜河分局。在接受采访时，唐纳德·格罗斯兰承认在观察这些物体时曾饮用过啤酒。他解释说，之所以推迟到10月9日才报告，是因为担心别人会认为他“疯了”。他还拒绝透露当时在场的两名女性同伴的身份。加拿大皇家骑警启动了调查，并通过电传（#CRVR-15）将详细信息发送至位于渥太华的国家研究委员会（NRC）。随后，加拿大皇家骑警试图寻找唐·布伊，但未能成功，因为他已搬迁至不列颠哥伦比亚省且未留下转寄地址。同样，警方也无法确定唐纳德·格罗斯兰目前的下落，他也已搬至不列颠哥伦比亚省且未提供联系地址。由于无法联系到主要目击者，该调查正式宣告结束。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unnamed subject (September 29 sighting), unspecified additional witnesses (October 4 sighting).

**Date / Time:** September 29, 1973, at 6:30 AM MDT; October 4, 1973, at 10:20 PM MDT.

**Location:** South city limits of Edmonton, Alberta.

**Sighting:** 
The case file documents two distinct sightings in the south Edmonton area. On September 29, 1973, at 6:30 AM MDT, an unnamed subject observed an object in the sky south of the city. The subject utilized binoculars to view the object and verified the time by checking their watch. The object moved west before executing a turn to the north at a high rate of speed. The observation lasted for 10 minutes, concluding when the object moved behind a tree branch.

On October 4, 1973, at 10:20 PM MDT, a second sighting occurred in the south city limits. This event was observed under cloudy conditions. The object was tracked for 5–10 minutes as it traveled in a south-west direction. The sighting ended when the object disappeared into the horizon, appearing to drop downward.

**Object:** 
The September 29 object was described as a red light with no discernible shape, noted for its ability to travel at great speed. The October 4 object was described as a bright, fiery, round ball. It maintained an approximate altitude of 1,000 feet and emitted a distinct humming sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP Edmonton detachment handled the documentation of these events. Regarding the September 29 sighting, the report was officially transmitted to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre and the CANFORCEHED Commissioner. Regarding the October 4 sighting, the RCMP noted that the identities of additional witnesses were being ascertained and that further contact with these individuals was pending. A follow-up report for the October 4 incident was expected to be filed. Weather conditions were recorded as "light cloud" for the September 29 sighting and "cloudy" for the October 4 sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 匿名人士（9月29日目击事件），其他未具名目击者（10月4日目击事件）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年9月29日，山地夏令时间（MDT）上午6:30；1973年10月4日，山地夏令时间（MDT）晚上10:20。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省埃德蒙顿市南郊。

**目击经过：**
该档案记录了埃德蒙顿南部地区发生的两次独立目击事件。1973年9月29日山地夏令时间上午6:30，一名匿名人士观察到城市南部的天空中出现了一个物体。该目击者使用双筒望远镜观察该物体，并通过查看手表确认了时间。该物体先向西移动，随后以极高的速度转向北面。观察过程持续了10分钟，最终因物体移动到树枝后方而结束。

1973年10月4日山地夏令时间晚上10:20，在城市南郊发生了第二次目击事件。此次事件是在多云的天气条件下观察到的。该物体被追踪了5至10分钟，当时它正向西南方向飞行。目击过程在物体消失在地平线并似乎向下坠落时结束。

**物体描述：**
9月29日的物体被描述为一个没有明显形状的红光，其高速移动的能力引人注目。10月4日的物体被描述为一个明亮、炽热的圆球。它保持在大约1000英尺的高度，并发出明显的嗡嗡声。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）埃德蒙顿分局负责了这些事件的记录工作。关于9月29日的目击事件，报告已正式提交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心及加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）专员。关于10月4日的目击事件，加拿大皇家骑警指出，其他目击者的身份正在核实中，并等待与这些人进行进一步接触。预计将针对10月4日的事件提交一份后续报告。气象条件记录显示，9月29日目击时为“薄云”，10月4日目击时为“多云”。

**Witnesses:** Capt. Ruddick DGA, Pte. Cabana JP

**Date / Time:** August 11, 1973, at 0419Z

**Location:** CFS Moosonee, Ontario

**Sighting:** 
On August 11, 1973, at 0419Z, a UFO sighting occurred at the Canadian Forces Station (CFS) in Moosonee. The event was witnessed by Capt. Ruddick DGA and Pte. Cabana JP. According to the official reports, the atmospheric conditions at the time of the sighting were cloudy. Both witnesses observed a single, distinct object that appeared in the sky and moved in a southerly direction. The witnesses noted the object’s position at an angle of 35 degrees from the horizon. The duration of the sighting was described as instantaneous, meaning the object appeared and disappeared or completed its observed movement in a near-momentary fashion.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a single yellow-orange ball. Regarding its movement, it traveled in a southerly direction at an elevation of 35 degrees from the horizon. The duration of the sighting was recorded as instantaneous. No sound or specific size dimensions were provided in the documentation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was treated as an official military report. Immediately following the event, the sighting was reported via telephone to NORAD (North American Aerospace Defense Command). Subsequently, the incident was formally documented and transmitted through a series of official communications, including a teletype report identified as TMO 405. This report was disseminated to the National Research Council (NRC) and National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) to ensure proper record-keeping and investigation by the relevant Canadian authorities.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 鲁迪克上尉 (Capt. Ruddick DGA)、卡巴纳列兵 (Pte. Cabana JP)

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年8月11日，0419Z（协调世界时）

**地点：** 安大略省穆索尼加拿大武装部队基地 (CFS Moosonee)

**目击经过：** 
1973年8月11日0419Z，穆索尼加拿大武装部队基地发生了一起不明飞行物目击事件。鲁迪克上尉和卡巴纳列兵目睹了这一过程。根据官方报告，目击时的天气状况为多云。两位目击者观察到一个出现在天空中的单一、清晰的物体，该物体向南移动。目击者指出，该物体位于地平线上方35度角的位置。目击持续时间被描述为“瞬间”，意味着该物体出现并消失，或是在极短时间内完成了其观测到的运动。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为一个单一的黄橙色球体。关于其运动轨迹，它在地平线上方35度的高度向南飞行。目击持续时间记录为瞬间。文档中未提及该物体的声音或具体尺寸。

**调查/后续：** 
此次目击事件被作为官方军事报告处理。事件发生后，目击者立即通过电话向北美防空司令部 (NORAD) 进行了报告。随后，该事件被正式记录并通过一系列官方通讯渠道进行传达，其中包括编号为 TMO 405 的电传报告。该报告被分发至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 和国防部总部 (NDHQ)，以确保相关加拿大当局进行妥善的记录与调查。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Denis Bilodeau (also recorded as Denniy/Denise/Dennis Dilodeau), Mr. Michael Reid, Mr. Paquin (also recorded as Baquin), Dr. Bernard Richer, Mr. and Mrs. Claude Girard (also recorded as Giard), Mr. Michel Guy (QPP), Pte. Marriott, Agent Gauthier (St. Agathe Municipal Police), and Mrs. Ernest Plouffe (also recorded as E. Plauff).

**Date / Time:** October 5, 8, 9, and 10, 1973. Various times recorded between 0000Z and 0900Z, with additional sightings reported during the afternoon of October 9.

**Location:** Ste Agathe, Quebec, specifically near Lac des Sables and Lac Carre.

**Sighting:** The Ste Agathe sighting wave involved multiple reports over several days. On October 8, witnesses observed three groups of objects at an estimated altitude of 10,000 feet, remaining stationary for a period before moving. A single object was observed performing fast, zig-zag maneuvers; Mrs. Claude Girard reported this object fired two projectiles (described as rockets) upward before the object descended into the woods. The stationary groups subsequently gained altitude and departed to the northwest. 

Other accounts from October 8 and 9 describe objects at lower altitudes (300–500 feet) circling slowly for durations ranging from 1 hour 15 minutes to 2 hours 20 minutes. On October 10, witnesses reported objects descending from the north accompanied by a buzzing sound, followed by a second object appearing from the northeast. Mrs. Ernest Plouffe reported an oval object over Lac Carre on the afternoon of October 9, and Pte. Marriott observed lights rising between mountains toward Ste Agathe at 0815Z on October 10.

**Object:** Descriptions vary but consistently feature bright, multi-colored lights. Objects were described as having red, blue, and green spots, or red, blue, and yellow lights, often encircled by a bright, flashing light. One object was estimated at 100 feet in diameter and another was described as oval-shaped. Most witnesses reported no engine sound, though one report noted a "buzzing sound." Movement ranged from slow, circular hovering to high-speed zig-zagging and rapid vertical ascent.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Reports were filed by Canadian Forces Station Lac St. Denis, North Bay, and the Quebec Provincial Police (QPP). Documentation was transmitted to the National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ), the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa, and the National Defence Operations Centre (NDOC). The weather during the primary sightings was noted as clear with high visibility. Official records include witness statements, transmission logs between military/police agencies, and references to the objects' flight paths and behaviors.

**日期/时间：** 1973年10月5日、8日、9日及10日。记录时间多集中在格林威治标准时间（Z）00:00至09:00之间，10月9日下午亦有额外目击报告。

**地点：** 魁北克省圣阿加特（Ste Agathe），具体位于萨布勒湖（Lac des Sables）和卡雷湖（Lac Carre）附近。

**目击经过：** 圣阿加特目击浪潮涉及多日的多起报告。10月8日，目击者观察到三组物体，估计高度为10,000英尺，它们在移动前曾保持静止状态。其中一个物体被观察到进行了快速的“之”字形机动；克劳德·吉拉德夫人报告称，该物体向上发射了两枚射弹（描述为火箭），随后坠入树林。静止的物体群随后升高并向西北方向离去。

10月8日和9日的其他描述显示，物体在较低高度（300至500英尺）缓慢盘旋，持续时间从1小时15分钟到2小时20分钟不等。10月10日，目击者报告称有物体伴随着嗡嗡声从北方降下，随后第二个物体从东北方出现。欧内斯特·普卢夫夫人报告称10月9日下午在卡雷湖上空看到一个椭圆形物体；马里奥特列兵则于10月10日格林威治标准时间08:15观察到有光点在山间升起，向圣阿加特方向移动。

**物体描述：** 描述各异，但均一致提到明亮的多色光。物体被描述为带有红色、蓝色和绿色的光点，或红色、蓝色和黄色的灯光，通常被一圈明亮的闪光包围。其中一个物体估计直径为100英尺，另一个被描述为椭圆形。大多数目击者称没有听到引擎声，但有一份报告提到有“嗡嗡声”。物体的运动方式包括缓慢的环形盘旋、高速的“之”字形移动以及快速的垂直上升。

**调查/后续：** 报告由圣丹尼斯湖（Lac St. Denis）加拿大武装部队基地、北湾（North Bay）基地以及魁北克省警察局（QPP）提交。相关文件被传送到渥太华的国防总部（NDHQ）、国家研究委员会（NRC）以及国防作战中心（NDOC）。主要目击期间天气晴朗，能见度高。官方记录包括目击者证词、军事/警察机构之间的通信日志，以及关于物体飞行路径和行为的参考资料。

**Witnesses:** Mr. William Keller (Assistant District Biologist, Department of Environment), Mr. Antonio Gegin.

**Date / Time:** 1973-10-23, 0200Z.

**Location:** Goulet, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On October 23, 1973, at 0200Z, two distinct reports were filed regarding aerial phenomena over Goulet, Ontario. Mr. William Keller, an Assistant District Biologist with the Department of Environment, observed an object while utilizing high-powered binoculars. He described the object as a large light moving slowly in an eastward direction. Simultaneously, Mr. Antonio Gegin reported observing two round objects that were hovering and circling the town. According to Mr. Gegin, who also utilized field glasses for his observation, the objects appeared orange when viewed from a distance. However, upon closer inspection, the color shifted to red with visible green spots. Mr. Keller’s account corroborates the presence of red and green coloration, describing his single observed object as a large red light surrounded by green.

**Object:** The event involved at least two round objects. Descriptions provided by the witnesses indicate that the objects were capable of hovering, circling, and slow eastward movement. The visual appearance of the objects was dynamic: they appeared orange at a distance, but transitioned to a red color featuring green spots when viewed at closer range through optical aids (binoculars/field glasses). The duration of the sighting was sufficient for the witnesses to track the movement and color changes of the objects. No specific sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation indicates that the investigation into the Goulet, Ontario sighting remains in progress. No further details regarding RCMP involvement, specific weather data, or finalized sketches were provided in the current file pages.

**目击者：** 威廉·凯勒先生（William Keller，环境部助理区域生物学家）、安东尼奥·格金先生（Antonio Gegin）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年10月23日，0200Z（协调世界时）。

**地点：** 安大略省古莱（Goulet, Ontario）。

**目击经过：** 1973年10月23日0200Z，安大略省古莱上空出现了两起关于空中现象的独立报告。环境部助理区域生物学家威廉·凯勒先生在使用高倍望远镜观测时发现了一个物体。他描述该物体是一个缓慢向东移动的大型光源。与此同时，安东尼奥·格金先生报告称观察到了两个盘旋并环绕该镇飞行的圆形物体。据同样使用双筒望远镜进行观测的格金先生所述，这些物体在远距离观察时呈橙色；然而在近距离观察时，颜色转变为红色，并带有可见的绿色斑点。凯勒先生的描述证实了红绿色彩的存在，他称自己观察到的那个物体是一个被绿色包围的大型红光。

**Witnesses:** Hugh Malcolm, Richard Aetknes, Daren Dick

**Date / Time:** October 24–25, 1973. Specific recorded times include: 230005Z (Oct 23/24), 240030Z (Oct 24), 250015Z (Oct 25), and 0400Z (Oct 25).

**Location:** St. Vital, Winnipeg, Manitoba (specifically referencing Victoria Road and Homer Street).

**Sighting:** 
The event involves multiple sightings reported by three witnesses in the St. Vital area of Winnipeg. 

Richard Aetknes (of 4 Homer) and Daren Dick (of 16 Homer) reported three distinct sightings from their homes. The first occurred at 230005Z with a duration of 20 minutes; the second at 240030Z lasting 12 minutes; and the third at 250015Z lasting 10 minutes. During these events, they observed the object moving up and down and traveling in a south-westerly direction before it was eventually lost from view.

Hugh Malcolm (of 3 Victoria Road) reported a separate sighting on October 25, 1973, at 0400Z. While traveling along St. Vital toward River Road, he observed a light in the sky. He noted the object moved at a 45-degree downward angle, traveled along the skyline, leveled off, and came to a complete stop. The duration of Mr. Malcolm’s sighting was between 45 and 60 seconds, ending when the object disappeared behind clouds or trees.

**Object:** 
The descriptions vary by witness and time. Richard Aetknes and Daren Dick described the object as round and white, noting that it sometimes appeared as a "little white ball" in the center. Hugh Malcolm described his sighting as a yellowish light. Regarding movement, the witnesses reported a range of behaviors: vertical movement (up and down), south-westerly travel, and a controlled descent at a 45-degree angle followed by a sudden stop. The duration of the sightings ranged from short bursts of 45–60 seconds to extended periods of up to 20 minutes. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The documentation consists of official sighting reports filed within the Canadian FOIA case file for the St. Vital area. The records categorize the events by witness location and specific Z-time (Zulu/UTC) timestamps. The reports track the progression of the sightings across the specified dates in October 1973, noting the witnesses' residential addresses and the specific flight paths observed. No further meteorological data or physical evidence recovery was noted in these specific pages.

**Witnesses:** Shayne Senton (also identified as Shayne Kevin Fenton), an 11-year-old boy.

**Date / Time:** November 4, 1973, at approximately 9:00 PM Atlantic Time (also recorded as 05/0100Z Nov 73).

**Location:** Surry/Hillsborough, Albert County, New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** The event was reported by an 11-year-old boy, who claimed to be the sole witness to the sighting. According to the initial report, the object approached the witness's dwelling from an easterly direction. The object banked quickly to the right, hovered, and then departed at a high rate of speed. The duration of the sighting was estimated at 5–10 seconds. While one account notes the object was at tree-top level, another specifies it was hovering approximately 4 feet off the ground and 50–60 feet from the house. The witness reported a "large crack" sound during the departure.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped, approximately 15–20 feet in length, and larger than a motor car. Its physical appearance was bright silver. Key features included a lit cockpit at the front, rear fins, and a yellow/orange light positioned on the bottom (roughly halfway between the front and center). The object emitted a humming sound while hovering. Upon departure, it was observed emitting a red glow from the rear as it accelerated in a northeasterly/northerly direction.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Hillsborough Detachment conducted an investigation into the report. While the witness was initially considered reliable due to his emotional state following the event, the subsequent official investigation concluded that no UFO sighting had actually occurred. The RCMP determined that the entire account was a fabrication created by the child. Consequently, the case was closed, and no further action was taken by the authorities. Weather conditions at the time of the reported event were noted as having scattered clouds.

**目击者：** 谢恩·森顿（Shayne Senton，也被记录为谢恩·凯文·芬顿 Shayne Kevin Fenton），一名11岁男孩。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年11月4日，大西洋时间晚上9:00左右（也被记录为1973年11月7日 05/0100Z）。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省阿尔伯特县，萨里/希尔斯伯勒（Surry/Hillsborough）。

**目击经过：** 该事件由一名11岁男孩报告，他声称是此次目击事件的唯一目击者。根据初步报告，该物体从东方向目击者的住所靠近。物体迅速向右倾斜、悬停，随后高速离去。目击持续时间估计为5至10秒。虽然有一份记录称物体处于树梢高度，但另一份记录指出它悬停在离地约4英尺、距离房屋50至60英尺的位置。目击者报告称，物体离开时发出了一声“巨大的爆裂声”。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形，长度约为15至20英尺，比汽车大。其外观呈亮银色。主要特征包括前部有一个发光的驾驶舱、后部有鳍状物，底部（大致位于前部和中心之间）有一个黄/橙色的灯。物体在悬停时发出嗡嗡声。离开时，观察到其后部发出红光，并向东北/北方向加速离去。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）希尔斯伯勒分局对该报告进行了调查。尽管目击者在事件发生后的情绪状态使其最初被认为可靠，但随后的官方调查得出结论：并未发生任何UFO目击事件。加拿大皇家骑警认定，整个叙述是该儿童编造的。因此，案件被结案，当局未采取进一步行动。据记录，报告事件发生时的天气状况为零散云层。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Barbara Alice Reynolds, her three children (ages 12, 10, and 8), and Mr. and Mrs. Curtis Sanford.

**Date / Time:** November 6, 1973, at 7:10 P.M. A.S.T.

**Location:** Falmouth, Hants County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 6, 1973, at approximately 7:10 P.M. A.S.T., a group of six individuals—Mrs. Barbara Alice Reynolds, her three children, and neighbors Mr. and Mrs. Curtis Sanford—observed an unidentified aerial object while at the Reynolds residence. The sky was reported as very clear at the time of the sighting. The object was initially spotted at an altitude of approximately 100 feet and at a distance of about one-quarter mile from the Reynolds home. 

The object remained stationary for approximately 20 minutes. Following this period of hovering, the object began to travel around the Windsor-Falmouth area. Specifically, it was observed moving toward Avondale, Hants County, before returning in a southwesterly direction toward Windsor. After remaining stationary for a few additional minutes, it continued in a southwesterly direction until it was eventually lost from sight. The total duration of the observation was approximately 30 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped, with a physical appearance likened to a bathtub, and was estimated to be approximately five feet in length/diameter. It featured two distinct reddish-colored lights that exhibited a rhythmic change in brightness, where one light would dim as the other became brighter. Additionally, the object emitted a light green glow while in motion. Throughout the entire duration of the sighting, no sound was reported by any of the witnesses.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation into the event, which included checking with local business firms to determine if any helicopters or light aircraft were operating in the area at the time; all such inquiries yielded negative results. The witnesses were assessed as appearing reliable. The official report regarding the incident was subsequently forwarded to the Astrophysics Branch of the Upper Atmosphere Research Section at the National Research Council in Ottawa for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 芭芭拉·爱丽丝·雷诺兹（Mrs. Barbara Alice Reynolds）夫人、她的三个孩子（分别为12岁、10岁和8岁），以及柯蒂斯·桑福德（Mr. Curtis Sanford）夫妇。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年11月6日，大西洋标准时间（A.S.T.）晚上7:10。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省汉茨县法尔茅斯（Falmouth, Hants County, Nova Scotia）。

**目击经过：** 1973年11月6日晚约7:10（大西洋标准时间），六人小组——芭芭拉·爱丽丝·雷诺兹夫人、她的三个孩子以及邻居柯蒂斯·桑福德夫妇——在雷诺兹家中观察到了一个不明飞行物。据称，目击时天空非常晴朗。该物体最初被发现时位于约100英尺的高度，距离雷诺兹家约四分之一英里。

该物体保持静止状态约20分钟。悬停结束后，它开始在温莎-法尔茅斯（Windsor-Falmouth）地区移动。具体而言，它被观察到向汉茨县的埃文代尔（Avondale）方向移动，随后又折返向西南方向的温莎移动。在又静止了几分钟后，它继续向西南方向飞行，直至最终消失在视野中。整个观察过程持续了约30分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形，外观类似于浴缸，估计长度/直径约为五英尺。它具有两个独特的红光，呈现出有节奏的亮度变化，即一盏灯变暗时另一盏灯变亮。此外，该物体在移动时会发出淡绿色的光芒。在整个目击过程中，没有任何目击者报告听到声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对该事件进行了调查，包括向当地商业公司核实当时是否有直升机或轻型飞机在附近作业；所有此类查询结果均为否定。目击者被评估为可靠。关于此事件的正式报告随后被转交至渥太华国家研究委员会高层大气研究部门的天体物理分部，以作进一步审查。

**Witnesses:** Ruth Carruthers, Sandra Harris

**Date / Time:** November 11, 1973, at 0715Z

**Location:** Morin Heights, Quebec

**Sighting:** On the morning of November 11, 1973, at 0715Z, witnesses Ruth Carruthers and her sister, Sandra Harris, observed an aerial phenomenon from inside a residence in Morin Heights, Quebec, while looking out through a living room window. The sighting lasted for a total duration of 20 minutes. 

According to the witnesses, the event began with the appearance of a small, oval-shaped white object at an estimated altitude of 100 feet. This object exhibited a distinct zig-zag movement pattern. After moving in this manner, the small white object disappeared from view for several minutes. It subsequently reappeared in the company of a second, larger object. The witnesses observed the smaller white object merge with the larger, bright yellow object. Following this merger, the combined entity moved toward the south, leaving behind a bright, blueish-colored trail or glow.

**Object:** The event involved two distinct objects. The first was described as small, oval-shaped, and white, characterized by a zig-zag flight path. The second object was larger and bright yellow in color. Upon the merger of the two objects, the resulting entity moved southward, emitting a bright blueish trail or glow. The objects were observed at an estimated altitude of 100 feet, and the entire encounter lasted for 20 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and reported through military and defense channels. The report was transmitted from Canadian Forces Station Lac St. Denis and 22 NORAD Region Headquarters in North Bay to the National Defence Headquarters in Ottawa and the National Research Council for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 露丝·卡鲁瑟斯 (Ruth Carruthers)、桑德拉·哈里斯 (Sandra Harris)

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年11月11日，0715Z（协调世界时）

**地点：** 魁北克省莫林高地 (Morin Heights)

**目击经过：** 1973年11月11日上午0715Z，目击者露丝·卡鲁瑟斯及其姐妹桑德拉·哈里斯在魁北克省莫林高地的一处住宅内，透过客厅窗户观察到了一种空中现象。此次目击事件总持续时间为20分钟。

据目击者称，事件开始时，一个小型椭圆形白色物体出现在约100英尺的空中。该物体呈现出明显的“之”字形移动轨迹。在以这种方式移动后，该小型白色物体消失了几分钟。随后，它与第二个较大的物体一同出现。目击者观察到较小的白色物体与较大的亮黄色物体发生了融合。融合后，合并后的实体向南方移动，并留下了一条明亮的淡蓝色轨迹或光晕。

**物体描述：** 事件涉及两个不同的物体。第一个被描述为小型、椭圆形、白色，飞行轨迹呈“之”字形。第二个物体较大，呈亮黄色。当两个物体融合后，形成的实体向南移动，并散发出明亮的淡蓝色轨迹或光晕。这些物体被观测到的高度约为100英尺，整个接触过程持续了20分钟。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已通过军事和国防渠道正式记录并上报。报告由圣丹尼斯湖加拿大武装部队基地 (Canadian Forces Station Lac St. Denis) 和位于北湾 (North Bay) 的北美防空司令部 (NORAD) 第22区域总部，传达至渥太华的国防部总部及加拿大国家研究委员会，以供进一步审查。

**Date / Time:** November 11, 1973, at 9:10 PM AST.

**Location:** Lot 5, Robin Village, RR 1, Lincoln (Fredericton area), New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 11, 1973, under clear sky conditions, the three witnesses were outside their trailer at Robin Village when they observed an unidentified object at a high altitude. The object was traveling at a fast rate of speed, moving from west to east. The witnesses reported that the object left a distinct white vapor trail that remained visible for approximately 3 to 5 minutes. Mrs. Jane Wambolt, who is employed as an E.L.M. (Electronic) Technician at CFB Gagetown, and her husband, Allen Russell Wambolt, also an E.L.M. Technician at CFB Gagetown, were noted by investigators as having a better-than-average knowledge of air transport and were considered highly reliable witnesses.

**Object:** The witnesses were unable to discern a specific shape for the object due to its high altitude. The visual display consisted of two neon-bright white lights that moved in unison. These lights flashed together in bursts of 4, 5, or 6 flashes, followed by a distinct pause. During these intervals of darkness, a small, glowing red light—described by the witnesses as resembling the appearance of a cigarette lighter—was visible on the right-hand side of the object. The object made no sound throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, Mrs. Wambolt contacted the Fredericton Airport control tower to report the event. The incident was subsequently investigated by Cst. Fred Shaw of the airport and Sgt. W. Weiss of the RCMP. Official follow-up included a check of all air traffic records for that time period; however, the investigation yielded no results, as no known aircraft were in the vicinity. Based on the testimony of the witnesses—particularly the technical background of the Wambolts—the investigating officers officially concluded that the witnesses had observed an unknown object.

**Location:** Robbin Village Trailer Court, Lincoln, Sunbury Co., New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 11, 1973, at approximately 9:10 P.M., three witnesses located at the Robbin Village Trailer Court in Lincoln, N.B., observed an unidentified object high in the sky. The witnesses were outside their trailer when they spotted the object moving from west to east at a fast rate of speed. The sky was noted as being clear at the time of the sighting. The object produced a distinct white vapour trail, yet it emitted no sound throughout the duration of the observation, which lasted between 3 to 5 minutes. 

Mrs. [redacted] initially contacted the Fredericton Airport tower, fearing the object might be an aircraft in distress. While the airport advised that a DC-9 was departing from runway 15, Mrs. [redacted] remained convinced that the object she observed was not that aircraft. One of the witnesses, who possessed better-than-average knowledge of aeronautical transport, also believed the object appeared to be an aircraft in distress; however, they were unable to identify or explain the unusual flashing light pattern exhibited by the craft. All three witnesses concluded that they had observed something unknown.

**Object:** The physical shape of the object could not be determined by the witnesses. It featured bright, neon-like white lights that flashed in rhythmic groups of 4, 5, or 6, followed by a pause, before repeating the sequence. During these pauses in the white flashing, a small, steady red light—described as resembling the glow of a cigarette lighter—was visible on what appeared to be the right side of the object. The object left a white vapour trail in its wake.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the initial report to the Fredericton Airport, Cst. Fred Shaw of the Fredericton Airport was notified and subsequently reported the incident to the RCMP. Cst. Shaw conducted a follow-up investigation, which included a patrol to the witnesses' residence to conduct formal interviews. A secondary check of the airport’s flight logs confirmed that no other transport aircraft were passing through the area at the time of the sighting. Despite the investigation and the input of a witness with aeronautical expertise, the object remained officially unidentified at the time the report was filed.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Winifred E. Rees, an unnamed civilian witness (the son of the civilian witness was also mentioned as a confidant).

**Date / Time:** Monday, October 15, 1973; early morning (at "barely dawn").

**Location:** Ottawa, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the early morning of October 15, 1973, two separate accounts describe an aerial phenomenon observed in the clear, indigo sky over Ottawa. Winifred E. Rees observed the object while looking out of her kitchen window at dawn, noting that the sky was cloudless with a few stars still visible. A second civilian witness also observed the object in the early morning hours. This second witness tracked the object for more than ten minutes as it moved at a very slow pace toward the North West, following the path of the Ottawa River. The second witness noted that the object was entirely soundless. Due to a fear of public ridicule, the second witness did not report the sighting officially at the time, only disclosing the event to their 43-year-old married son during a trip to Iroquois on Saturday, October 20, 1973.

**Object:** The object was consistently described by both witnesses as a bright, silvery "stick." Winifred E. Rees described it as being approximately the size of a piece of ordinary school-board chalk, positioned at an extremely high altitude. The second witness similarly described it as a silvery stick of chalk, comparing its appearance to a silver cigar, though noting it was significantly shorter in length than a Zeppelin. Both accounts emphasize that the object possessed no wings, no tail, and left no vapour trail in its wake.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, Winifred E. Rees took the initiative to write a formal letter to the UFO Department of the National Research Council of Canada. Her motivation for reporting the incident stemmed from reading an article in the *Ottawa Journal* that requested information from the public regarding UFO sightings. There is no record of an official RCMP interrogation or formal weather report included in these specific pages, though the witnesses provided consistent environmental data regarding the clear, indigo sky conditions at the time of the observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威妮弗雷德·E·里斯（Winifred E. Rees），一名未具名的平民目击者（该平民目击者的儿子也被提及为知情者）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年10月15日，星期一；清晨（“黎明时分”）。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华。

**目击经过：** 1973年10月15日清晨，有两份独立的报告描述了在渥太华清澈的靛蓝色天空中观察到的空中现象。威妮弗雷德·E·里斯在黎明时分从厨房窗户向外望去时发现了该物体，她注意到当时天空万里无云，还能看到几颗星星。第二位平民目击者也在清晨时分观察到了该物体。这位目击者跟踪了该物体十多分钟，它沿着渥太华河的走向，以非常缓慢的速度向西北方向移动。第二位目击者指出，该物体全程没有任何声音。由于担心遭到公众嘲笑，该目击者当时并未正式报告此次目击事件，直到1973年10月20日星期六在前往伊罗夸（Iroquois）的途中，才向其43岁的已婚儿子透露了此事。

**物体描述：** 两位目击者对该物体的描述一致，均称其为一个明亮的银色“棍状物”。威妮弗雷德·E·里斯将其描述为大约普通学校粉笔大小，位于极高的高度。第二位目击者也将其描述为一根银色的粉笔，并将其外观比作一支银色雪茄，但指出其长度明显短于齐柏林飞艇。两份报告都强调，该物体没有机翼，没有尾翼，且身后没有留下任何尾迹。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，威妮弗雷德·E·里斯主动致信加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council of Canada）的UFO部门。她报告此事的动机源于她在《渥太华日报》（*Ottawa Journal*）上读到的一篇文章，该文章向公众征集有关UFO目击事件的信息。在这些特定记录中，没有关于加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）正式审讯或正式天气报告的记录，尽管目击者提供了关于当时清澈的靛蓝色天空状况的一致环境数据。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Guy Roux

**Date / Time:** December 7, 1973, at approximately 2:30 A.M. (AST)

**Location:** 490 Parck Site, Bathurst, New Brunswick

**Sighting:** 
On the morning of December 7, 1973, at approximately 2:30 A.M., Mrs. Guy Roux, a resident of 490 Parck Site in Bathurst, observed an unidentified flying object from her residence. The sighting occurred under clear weather conditions and lasted for a duration of approximately 10 minutes. Mrs. Roux, noted in official documentation as a well-respected lady in the city, observed the object moving very slowly across the sky in an east-to-west direction. She estimated the object's altitude to be approximately 1,500 feet.

**Object:** 
The object was described as cigar-shaped and appeared larger than the moon from the witness's vantage point. It featured two distinct light-colored spots on the front. Initially, the object appeared black, but it noticeably became lighter in color as Mrs. Roux continued to observe it. No sound was reported, and the movement was characterized as very slow.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Following the report, the Bathurst RCMP detachment conducted an investigation and subsequently forwarded the findings to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch at the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa. 

Official follow-up measures included:
*   **Local Inquiries:** A check with the Bathurst Canadian Pacific (C.P.) office was conducted, which yielded negative results regarding any unusual activity or reports.
*   **Military Verification:** The RCMP contacted Canadian Forces Base (C.F.B.) Chatham to determine if any military aircraft were in the vicinity at the time of the sighting. C.F.B. Chatham confirmed that no aircraft were in the area at 2:30 A.M.
*   **General Reporting:** The RCMP noted that no other sightings were reported to their office regarding this event.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Dr. Roberts-Pichette (Department of the Environment), A.G. McNamara (National Research Council) and members of his car pool, Mr. Vernon (Department of the Environment), E.G. Baker.

**Date / Time:** December 7, 1973. Observations occurred at various intervals: 16:35–16:50 EST (McNamara), 02:30 UT (Baker), 21:00 Z (Vernon), and 21:10–21:50 (Dr. Roberts-Pichette).

**Location:** Ottawa, Ontario (NRC Building M-50, downtown, Alta Vista Drive, 1125 Castledill Cres.) and Hull, Quebec (Place Vincent Massey, Fontaine Building).

**Sighting:** 
The events of December 7, 1973, involved multiple sightings across the Ottawa-Hull region. A.G. McNamara and his car pool observed a high-flying jet traveling west at 16:35 EST. As the jet passed into the sunlight above the shadow line, its contrail transformed into a brilliant orange fan, eventually appearing as a stationary orange oval and finally a bright orange "blob" against the sunset sky. McNamara correctly predicted this would generate UFO reports.

Later that evening, other witnesses reported distinct phenomena. At 21:00 Z, Mr. Vernon observed objects from Place Vincent Massey in Hull; he described a stationary object resembling an airplane contrail catching the sunset, accompanied by two low-flying objects—one comet-like and one appearing as a small dot. 

At 21:10, Dr. Roberts-Pichette, viewing from the 9th floor of the Fontaine Building, observed two lights in the north. The larger was saucer-shaped and twice the size of an aircraft, while the smaller vanished instantly. A third light appeared to the west, growing larger over 20 minutes before moving west and elongating to four times the size of an aircraft. At 21:50, a red light appeared, four times the size of an aircraft, remaining stationary for over 30 minutes before shrinking to a dot. Separately, E.G. Baker reported a "Non-Meteoritic Sighting" at 02:30 UT in downtown Ottawa.

**Object:** 
Descriptions varied significantly:
*   **Jet/Contrail:** Initially a jet plane with a short contrail, evolving into an orange fan, comet shape, oval, and finally a bright orange blob.
*   **Lights:** Yellow and red lights, saucer-shaped or elongated, ranging from the size of a dot to four times the size of an aircraft.
*   **Movement:** Stationary, slow-moving, or vanishing instantly.
*   **Sound:** No sound reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The reports were funneled through the Meteor Centre via telephone between December 10 and 11, 1973. E.G. Baker’s report was officially classified as a "Non-Meteoritic Sighting" (Serial No. N231478). Documentation references further investigation notes on page 176 of the original file. The sightings are collectively categorized as IFOs (Identified Flying Objects), with the primary explanation being the visual distortion of high-altitude jet contrails illuminated by the setting sun.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗伯茨-皮切特博士（Dr. Roberts-Pichette，环境部）、A.G. 麦克纳马拉（A.G. McNamara，国家研究委员会）及其拼车同事、弗农先生（Mr. Vernon，环境部）、E.G. 贝克（E.G. Baker）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年12月7日。观测发生于不同时段：16:35–16:50 EST（麦克纳马拉）、02:30 UT（贝克）、21:00 Z（弗农）以及21:10–21:50（罗伯茨-皮切特博士）。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华（国家研究委员会M-50大楼、市中心、阿尔塔维斯塔大道、卡斯尔迪尔新月街1125号）及魁北克省赫尔（文森特·梅西广场、方丹大楼）。

**目击经过：**
1973年12月7日发生的事件涉及渥太华-赫尔地区的多次目击报告。A.G. 麦克纳马拉及其拼车同事于东部标准时间16:35观测到一架向西飞行的高空喷气式飞机。当飞机进入阴影线以上的阳光照射区时，其尾迹变成了一个明亮的橙色扇形，最终看起来像一个静止的橙色椭圆形，并在日落的天空中呈现为一个明亮的橙色“斑点”。麦克纳马拉当时准确预言这将会引发不明飞行物（UFO）报告。

当晚晚些时候，其他目击者报告了不同的现象。21:00 Z，弗农先生在赫尔的文森特·梅西广场观测到物体；他描述了一个类似于飞机尾迹在夕阳下发光的静止物体，并伴有两个低空飞行的物体——一个呈彗星状，另一个表现为一个小点。

21:10，罗伯茨-皮切特博士在方丹大楼9楼观测到北方的两道光。较大的光呈碟状，体积是飞机的两倍，而较小的光瞬间消失。西方出现了第三道光，在20分钟内逐渐变大，随后向西移动并拉长至飞机体积的四倍。21:50，出现了一道红光，体积是飞机的四倍，在静止超过30分钟后缩小为一个点。此外，E.G. 贝克于02:30 UT在渥太华市中心报告了一起“非流星目击事件”。

**物体描述：**
描述差异显著：
*   **喷气式飞机/尾迹：** 最初为带有短尾迹的喷气式飞机，随后演变为橙色扇形、彗星状、椭圆形，最后变为明亮的橙色斑点。
*   **光点：** 黄色和红色的光，呈碟状或拉长状，大小从一个点到飞机体积的四倍不等。
*   **运动：** 静止、缓慢移动或瞬间消失。
*   **声音：** 未报告任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
这些报告于1973年12月10日至11日期间通过电话汇集至流星中心。E.G. 贝克的报告被正式归类为“非流星目击事件”（序列号 N231478）。相关文档提及原始档案第176页有进一步的调查记录。这些目击事件被统称为IFO（已识别飞行物体），主要解释为高空喷气式飞机尾迹在夕阳照射下产生的视觉畸变。

**日期 / 时间：** 1973年12月17日，凌晨12:50（大西洋标准时间）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省北悉尼，圣伊丽莎白医院附近（具体位置标注为医院以南约200英尺处）。

**目击经过：** 1973年12月17日凌晨，一名目击者观察到一种不明空中现象，持续时间总计五分钟。目击发生时天气晴朗，有高云。目击者当时位于北悉尼的圣伊丽莎白医院附近，最初观察到该物体保持静止状态约两分钟。在此静止期过后，物体开始向内陆移动。目击者估计该物体距离其约4至5英里，位置似乎在悉尼的雷达基地和机场附近。据描述，该物体的移动速度与正在进行进场降落的飞机相当。

**物体描述：** 在观察过程中，该物体的外观发生了明显的转变。起初，它被描述为半月形（具体为下半部分），呈现出明亮的火焰黄色。当开始向内陆移动时，物体的形态似乎转变为三角形，其顶部有一个红灯。该物体飞行时的估计高度在2,000至3,000英尺之间。

**调查/后续：** 报告提交后，相关部门进行了官方调查，以排除常规飞行器或雷达异常的可能性。经核查当地雷达基地，确认在目击发生时，雷达屏幕上未检测到任何异常。此外，调查人员还联系了机场以确定是否有任何空中交通可以解释该现象；官方确认该地区的最后一次航班发生在1973年12月16日晚上11:45，远早于凌晨12:50的目击时间。尽管目击者对不明飞行物现象表现出明显的兴奋，但调查人员仍认为该目击者是可靠的。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 雷金纳德·贝内特（Reginald Bennett）先生、他的妻子以及唐娜·奥奎因（Donna O'Quinn）。

**调查/后续：** 目击过程持续了约20分钟。1973年12月19日的一份后续报告指出，该物体实际上是当地一家飞行服务公司的直升机，当时该直升机在附近区域放下了一名乘客后再次起飞。此后未采取进一步行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Carl Nicholson (15 years old)

**Date / Time:** January 5–6, 1974, at approximately 11:30 PM Atlantic Time. (Note: Reports vary between January 5 and January 6; the witness reported the sighting to the RCMP at 12:30 AM on January 7, 1974).

**Location:** Park Crest Drive, Upper Lawrencetown, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** Carl Nicholson, a 15-year-old who was babysitting at his parents' house, observed a UFO after being alerted by his dog barking. He watched the object for approximately one hour as it moved back and forth across the skyline and hovered above the tree line. The sighting occurred on a night described as having excellent visibility, with a bright moon and partly cloudy skies. The witness observed the object from his residence, estimating the landing site to be in a wooded area approximately two to three miles away. Despite the duration of the sighting, no other persons reported observing the object.

**Object:** The witness could not discern a specific shape for the object. Its primary visual features consisted of four flashing colored lights—red, blue, yellow, and green—arranged in a horizontal line. Prior to the object descending into the wooded area, a large white light appeared beneath the horizontal row of colored lights. The object exhibited movement by hovering above the tree line and traveling back and forth across the sky before its eventual landing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the RCMP Dartmouth detachment at 12:30 AM on January 7, 1974. An investigating officer arrived at the scene, but the object was no longer visible, and a search of the wooded area failed to locate any physical evidence or the object itself. The RCMP conducted inquiries with CFB Shearwater and the Halifax International Airport controller; neither facility had any radar or visual reports corresponding to the sighting. 

The RCMP noted that while the witness’s reliability was officially categorized as "unknown," the investigating officer remarked that the youth appeared sincere. The case file was processed by the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre on January 7, 1974, and subsequently forwarded to the NRC in Ottawa. No further action was taken by the RCMP, and the investigation was concluded with no definitive explanation for the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 卡尔·尼科尔森（Carl Nicholson，15岁）

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年1月5日至6日，大西洋时间晚上11:30左右。（注：报告日期在1月5日和1月6日之间存在出入；目击者于1974年1月7日凌晨12:30向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了此次目击事件。）

**地点：** 新斯科舍省，上劳伦斯镇（Upper Lawrencetown），公园冠道（Park Crest Drive）。

**目击经过：** 15岁的卡尔·尼科尔森当时正在父母家中照看房子，在听到狗叫声后，他发现了一个不明飞行物（UFO）。他观察该物体长达约一小时，目睹它在天际线来回移动，并悬停在树梢上方。目击当晚能见度极佳，月光明亮，天空局部多云。目击者从住所进行观察，估计其降落地点位于约两到三英里外的一片林区。尽管目击持续时间较长，但没有其他人报告看到该物体。

**物体描述：** 目击者无法辨认出该物体的具体形状。其主要的视觉特征是由红、蓝、黄、绿四种闪烁的灯光组成，呈水平排列。在物体降落到林区之前，水平排列的彩色灯光下方出现了一道巨大的白光。该物体表现出的运动方式包括悬停在树梢上方，以及在降落前于天空中来回穿梭。

**调查 / 后续：** 该目击事件于1974年1月7日凌晨12:30报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）达特茅斯分局。调查警官抵达现场时，物体已不见踪影，对林区的搜寻也未能发现任何物理证据或物体本身。加拿大皇家骑警向希尔沃特加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Shearwater）及哈利法克斯国际机场管制中心进行了询问；两处设施均无任何与此次目击事件相符的雷达或目击报告。

加拿大皇家骑警指出，虽然目击者的可靠性被官方归类为“未知”，但调查警官评论称该青年看起来很真诚。该案卷于1974年1月7日由国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心处理，随后被转交至渥太华的国家研究委员会。加拿大皇家骑警未采取进一步行动，调查最终在没有明确解释的情况下结束。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ronald Louisseize, 6 unnamed individuals, and Mme Hélène Turgeon.

**Date / Time:** February 14, 1974; 02:45 (Louisseize group) and 04:30 (Turgeon).

**Location:** Clarence Creek and the road between Curran and Bourget, Ontario.

**Sighting:** 
The event involved two distinct observations occurring in the early morning hours of February 14, 1974. At 02:45, Ronald Louisseize and six others were traveling on a snowmobile in the woods near Clarence Creek. They observed a white light suspended in the air, which they likened to a searchlight. Suddenly, the light intensified and directed itself toward the witnesses with such density that the surrounding snow appeared completely white. Following this, the light vanished.

At 04:30, Mme Hélène Turgeon, while driving from Curran toward Bourget, observed an object for approximately 7 minutes. She noted the object moving slowly from right to left at a fixed altitude. Initially, the object was stationary; it then crossed the road while its lights were extinguished. Once the lights reactivated, the object proceeded toward a wooded area. Mme Turgeon remained in her vehicle throughout the duration of the sighting, noting that her car was moving very slowly during the observation.

**Object:** 
The descriptions provided by the witnesses suggest a large, silent craft. The Louisseize group described a machine passing approximately 100 feet above them, featuring four lights (yellow, green, blue, and red) arranged in a 40-foot square formation. They noted the object traveled westward at a speed of 5 mph. 

Mme Turgeon described a large white light positioned on the side of the object, accompanied by four fixed red lights. She specified that there were no flashing lights on the craft. Both accounts emphasize that the object made no noise during the sightings.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Official reports were filed via telephone on February 19, 1974. The Louisseize report was directed to the National Research Council, while Mme Turgeon’s report was transmitted to the centre for meteor and meteorite studies. Weather conditions at the time of the first sighting were noted as cloudy.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗纳德·路易塞兹 (Ronald Louisseize)、6名未具名人士以及海伦·特琼女士 (Mme Hélène Turgeon)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年2月14日；02:45（路易塞兹一行）及 04:30（特琼女士）。

**地点：** 安大略省克拉伦斯溪 (Clarence Creek) 以及库兰 (Curran) 至布尔热 (Bourget) 之间的公路。

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及1974年2月14日凌晨发生的两次独立观测。凌晨02:45，罗纳德·路易塞兹和其他六人正驾驶雪地摩托在克拉伦斯溪附近的树林中行驶。他们观察到空中悬浮着一道白光，并将其比作探照灯。突然，光线增强并以极高的密度射向目击者，导致周围的积雪看起来一片惨白。随后，光线消失了。

凌晨04:30，海伦·特琼女士在从库兰开车前往布尔热的途中，观察到一个物体约7分钟。她注意到该物体在固定高度从右向左缓慢移动。起初，该物体处于静止状态；随后它在熄灭灯光的情况下横穿了公路。当灯光重新亮起后，物体向一片树林方向驶去。特琼女士在整个目击过程中一直留在车内，并注意到她在观察时车辆行驶得非常缓慢。

**物体描述：**
目击者提供的描述表明这是一个大型、无声的飞行器。路易塞兹一行人描述称，一个机器从他们头顶约100英尺处经过，其上装有四个灯（黄色、绿色、蓝色和红色），排列成一个40英尺见方的阵列。他们指出该物体以每小时5英里的速度向西飞行。

特琼女士描述称，该物体侧面有一个巨大的白光，并伴有四个固定的红灯。她特别指出该飞行器上没有闪烁的灯光。两份报告都强调，该物体在目击过程中没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
官方报告于1974年2月19日通过电话提交。路易塞兹的报告被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会 (National Research Council)，而特琼女士的报告则被传达至流星与陨石研究中心。据记录，第一次目击时的天气状况为多云。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Al Smith, Mr. Al Smith’s mother

**Date / Time:** May 27, 1974, at 0340Z

**Location:** Pakenham/Almont, Ontario

**Sighting:** 
On May 27, 1974, at 0340Z, Mr. Al Smith and his mother observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the Almont area. According to the witnesses, the event involved a large craft that appeared twice during the sighting. Throughout the duration of the encounter, the witnesses reported hearing a distinct crackling sound emanating from the object. The sighting was significant enough to prompt the witnesses to report the incident to the local Ontario Provincial Police (OPP).

**Object:** 
The object was described as a large craft. Its lighting configuration consisted of clear, bright white lights at the front, which the witnesses likened to aircraft landing lights, and three green lights positioned at the rear of the craft. The object was noted for its size and the audible crackling sound associated with its presence.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The incident was formally reported to the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) for the Almont/Pakenham area. As part of the official follow-up investigation, authorities conducted radar checks for the vicinity to determine if any conventional aircraft or anomalous targets were present at the time of the sighting. The radar investigation concluded that there were no radar paints recorded in the area during the time of the incident.

**Witnesses:** James Michael John Kolenz, Loretta Lillian Thompson, Robert John Kolenz

**Date / Time:** September 17, 1974, between 8:45 PM and 9:00 PM CST

**Location:** Roche Percee, Saskatchewan

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 17, 1974, three witnesses—James Michael John Kolenz, Loretta Lillian Thompson, and Robert John Kolenz—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the village of Roche Percee, Saskatchewan. The sighting occurred under clear sky conditions and lasted for a duration of approximately 5 to 10 minutes. According to the collective account provided to the RCMP, the object was initially observed floating directly overhead at an estimated altitude of several thousand feet. The witnesses reported that the object exhibited complex flight patterns, including moving in circles and traveling in a zig-zag motion while heading in an easterly direction. Subsequently, the object changed its trajectory and proceeded due north over the nearby town of Bienfait, Saskatchewan, before finally disappearing from the witnesses' view.

**Object:** The object was described as being egg-shaped and featured a short, pointed "tail." It emitted a distinct yellowish-green light that blinked on and off throughout the duration of the sighting. The object appeared to be floating at an altitude of several thousand feet and demonstrated unconventional movement, characterized by circular motions and zig-zagging flight paths. No specific sound was reported by the witnesses.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was investigated by Cpl. A.T. Myshrall of the RCMP Estevan Detachment. Following his interviews with the witnesses, Cpl. Myshrall formally documented his assessment of their credibility. He concluded that James Michael John Kolenz, Loretta Lillian Thompson, and Robert John Kolenz were reliable, honest individuals of good character within their community. No further atmospheric or conventional explanations were noted in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯·迈克尔·约翰·科伦兹 (James Michael John Kolenz)、洛蕾塔·莉莲·汤普森 (Loretta Lillian Thompson)、罗伯特·约翰·科伦兹 (Robert John Kolenz)

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年9月17日，中部标准时间 (CST) 晚上8:45至9:00之间

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省，罗什珀塞 (Roche Percee)

**目击经过：** 1974年9月17日晚，三名目击者——詹姆斯·迈克尔·约翰·科伦兹、洛蕾塔·莉莲·汤普森和罗伯特·约翰·科伦兹——在萨斯喀彻温省罗什珀塞村时观察到一种不明空中现象。目击事件发生在晴朗的天空下，持续时间约为5至10分钟。根据他们向加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 提供的集体陈述，该物体最初被观察到悬浮在正上方，估计高度为几千英尺。目击者报告称，该物体表现出复杂的飞行模式，包括盘旋飞行以及在向东移动时呈“之”字形轨迹运动。随后，该物体改变了航向，径直向北飞越了附近的萨斯喀彻温省比恩费特 (Bienfait) 镇，最终从目击者的视野中消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为蛋形，带有一个短而尖的“尾巴”。它发出一种独特的黄绿色光，在整个目击过程中不断闪烁。该物体似乎悬浮在几千英尺的高空，并表现出非传统的运动方式，其特征为圆周运动和“之”字形飞行轨迹。目击者未报告听到任何特定的声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警埃斯特万 (Estevan) 分队的 A.T. 迈什拉尔 (A.T. Myshrall) 下士负责调查。在采访目击者后，迈什拉尔下士正式记录了他对目击者可信度的评估。他得出结论认为，詹姆斯·迈克尔·约翰·科伦兹、洛蕾塔·莉莲·汤普森和罗伯特·约翰·科伦兹是社区中可靠、诚实且品行端正的人。提供的文档中未提及任何进一步的大气或常规解释。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Robert Hagell (also referred to as Hagel), his wife, and his father.

**Date / Time:** September 25, 1974, at 9:10 P.M. (Note: Page 283 records the event as 0010Z on September 26, which corresponds to the same timeframe).

**Location:** Philip Street, Truro, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** The sighting occurred under a clear sky. Mr. Robert Hagell, along with his wife and father, observed an anomalous aerial phenomenon. According to Mr. Hagell, who was standing on Philip Street, the sighting lasted between 4 to 5 minutes (Page 283 notes 3 to 4 minutes). The object was observed moving from a South to an Easterly direction. During the event, the object exhibited erratic movement, traveling both up and down and from side to side (port to starboard). A significant detail noted by the witnesses was the observation of pieces or parts falling from the object. Mr. Hagell suggested that these falling fragments may have landed in the vicinity of Brookfield or Hilden, Nova Scotia. After the debris was shed, the object moved upward and eventually disappeared.

**Object:** The object was described as ball-shaped with a bright reddish tinge (Page 283 describes it as a large white light). It was positioned under the "star of the East." The estimated elevation of the object was between 10,000 and 15,000 feet. No sound was reported. The duration of the observation was approximately 3 to 5 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Mr. Robert Hagell, who serves as the supervisor of electrical services at Halifax International Airport, formally reported the incident to the RCMP in Truro and to Mr. Campbell, the chief controller at Halifax International Airport. The official RCMP report was filed by Constable H. M. Pike of the Truro Detachment on September 30, 1974.

**Witnesses:** Mary Issabel MacIssac (25 years old, of Dunvagin, Inverness County) and CST G J E P Pharanb of the RCMP Arichat detachment.

**Sighting:** The event occurred at 10 P.M. AST on October 6, 1974, at a roadside park on Highway 19, 1.2 miles west of the South West Margaree River Bridge. The sky was clear and moonlit. The object was first noted when its brightness attracted the witness's attention.

**Object:** The object appeared as a circular sphere with a horizontal plain around the perimeter. It was capable of revolving, rising, and descending. The color changed from white to red, though the brightness remained constant. There was no sound and no shadow. The elevation was approximately 300 feet. The first exposure lasted 10-15 minutes, followed by a 20-30 minute interval. A second exposure appeared suddenly within 100 feet, appearing white only, and disappeared upon the approach of a west-bound motor vehicle on the highway.

**Aftermath:** No apparent landing occurred. The witness has not yet been interviewed.

**后续：** 没有明显的着陆迹象。目击者尚未接受采访。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** John Breen (Air Traffic Controller/Pilot), Janice Gould, Robert Lawrence (Supervising Controller), Edward Duhany (Supervising Controller), the Captain and crew of a Capital Airlines DC-8 (N-490C).

**Date / Time:** October 10, 1974, at approximately 10:10 p.m. (Atlantic Time) through October 11, 1974, at approximately 4:15 a.m. (Atlantic Time).

**Location:** Gander, Newfoundland (vicinity of Grand Falls, Deer Lake, and Gander International Airport).

**Sighting:** The events began on October 10 at 10:10 p.m. when John Breen, an Air Traffic Controller piloting a Cessna (C-GLCF) with passenger Janice Gould, observed a greenish, luminous light while flying between Deer Lake and Gander. The object exhibited controlled, intelligent movement, matching the Cessna’s altitude of 3,000–5,000 feet. It repeatedly repositioned itself, speeding ahead, slowing down, following behind, or flying underneath the aircraft. The encounter lasted 25 minutes, ending at 10:35 p.m. when the object changed from a north-westerly to a westerly course and descended to treetop level.

On October 11 at 4:15 a.m., the crew of a Capital Airlines DC-8 (N-490C) reported a second encounter while descending toward Gander International Airport at 7,500 feet and 290 mph. The object pulled alongside the airliner and maintained a parallel course for 5 to 7 minutes. Like the previous sighting, the object displayed controlled flight, occasionally speeding ahead of the DC-8 before returning to its position alongside. When the airliner reached a point 5 miles west of Gander, the object entered a cloud formation and disappeared. The DC-8 crew descended to 2,000 feet, but the object was not seen again.

**Object:** The object observed by Breen was a solitary, greenish, luminous light. The object observed by the DC-8 crew was described as having an indistinguishable shape and size, but was clearly marked by flashing red and white lights. Both sets of witnesses explicitly stated their belief that the object was not a conventional aircraft.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** During the Cessna encounter, Supervising Controller Robert Lawrence attempted to track the object on radar. A target was detected within 6 miles of the aircraft, but it did not appear as a standard aircraft; it was tracked for two sweeps before disappearing, likely due to its descent to treetop level. During the DC-8 encounter, Supervising Controller Edward Duhany confirmed that no other aircraft were reported in the area and that Gander radar monitors failed to detect any targets other than the DC-8. CFS Gander radar installations similarly reported no other aircraft. The incident was reported to the Early Warning defensive system at Goose Bay, and the official report was forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section, Astrophysics Branch, NRC, Ottawa.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·布林（John Breen，空中交通管制员/飞行员）、珍妮丝·古尔德（Janice Gould）、罗伯特·劳伦斯（Robert Lawrence，主管管制员）、爱德华·杜哈尼（Edward Duhany，主管管制员），以及一架首都航空（Capital Airlines）DC-8客机（注册号 N-490C）的机长及机组人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月10日约晚上10:10至1974年10月11日约凌晨4:15（大西洋时间）。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省甘德（Gander）（大瀑布城、鹿湖及甘德国际机场附近）。

**目击经过：** 事件始于10月10日晚上10:10，当时身为空中交通管制员的约翰·布林正驾驶一架塞斯纳（Cessna）飞机（C-GLCF），载着乘客珍妮丝·古尔德在鹿湖与甘德之间飞行，期间观察到一个绿色的发光体。该物体表现出受控的智能运动，与塞斯纳飞机保持在3,000至5,000英尺的相同高度。它反复变换位置，时而加速超前，时而减速，时而尾随，或是在飞机下方飞行。这次接触持续了25分钟，于晚上10:35结束，当时该物体从西北方向转向西，并下降至树梢高度。

10月11日凌晨4:15，一架首都航空DC-8客机（N-490C）的机组人员在以290英里/小时的速度下降至甘德国际机场、高度为7,500英尺时，报告了第二次接触。该物体飞至客机侧面，并保持平行航线飞行了5至7分钟。与前一次目击类似，该物体表现出受控飞行状态，偶尔会加速超过DC-8，随后又回到侧面位置。当客机到达甘德以西5英里处时，该物体进入云层并消失。DC-8机组人员随后下降至2,000英尺，但未再发现该物体。

**物体描述：** 布林观察到的物体是一个单一的、绿色的发光体。DC-8机组人员观察到的物体形状和大小无法辨认，但有明显的红色和白色闪烁灯光。两组目击者均明确表示，他们认为该物体并非传统飞行器。

**调查/后续：** 在塞斯纳飞机的接触事件中，主管管制员罗伯特·劳伦斯试图通过雷达追踪该物体。在距离飞机6英里范围内探测到了一个目标，但它看起来不像标准飞行器；雷达对其进行了两次扫描后目标便消失了，这很可能是因为它下降到了树梢高度。在DC-8的接触事件中，主管管制员爱德华·杜哈尼确认该区域没有其他飞行器报告，且甘德雷达监视器除DC-8外未探测到任何目标。加拿大武装部队（CFS）甘德雷达站同样报告没有其他飞行器。该事件被上报至鹅湾（Goose Bay）的预警防御系统，官方报告随后被转交至渥太华加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）天体物理分部的高层大气研究部门。

**Witnesses:** Nicholas JAY, Derrick JAY (reporting party), W.N. HOLDEN (Principal)

**Date / Time:** October 12/13, 1974; witness reported waking at approximately 12:00 midnight, with subsequent documentation noting the observation occurring around 1:00 A.M.

**Location:** Red Streak Campground, Radium Hot Springs, B.C.

**Sighting:** While sleeping in a station wagon at the Red Streak Campground, Nicholas Jay (a student at John Ware Junior High School, born August 10, 1961) observed a group of unidentified objects. The witness reported waking up and looking in a northeasterly direction, where he saw the objects emerge from behind a mountain. He observed between three and four objects in total. The objects moved in a northeasterly direction, traveling upwards before slowly vanishing. The total duration of the sighting was approximately 40 seconds.

**Object:** The objects were described as white-shining and oblong in shape. Each featured a circle around the main body, with a line running through the center that terminated in a point at each end. The witness noted that the objects made no sound and did not resemble an aircraft. He estimated the objects were approximately four miles away and appeared to be roughly the size of a 13-foot trailer.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was reported to the RCMP by the witness’s father, Mr. Derrick Jay. As part of the official follow-up, the RCMP contacted Mr. W.N. Holden, the Principal of the school attended by Nicholas Jay. Mr. Holden provided a character assessment of the witness, stating that while the student could occasionally be vague, he was not the type of child to seek attention, act maliciously, or intentionally cause problems with false reports.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 尼古拉斯·杰伊 (Nicholas JAY)、德里克·杰伊 (Derrick JAY，报告人)、W.N. 霍尔顿 (W.N. HOLDEN，校长)

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月12日至13日；目击者称于午夜12:00左右醒来，后续记录显示观测时间发生在凌晨1:00左右。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省，镭温泉镇 (Radium Hot Springs)，红纹露营地 (Red Streak Campground)

**目击经过：** 当时，尼古拉斯·杰伊（约翰·威尔初中学生，1961年8月10日出生）正在红纹露营地的一辆旅行车内睡觉，期间他观察到了一组不明飞行物体。目击者称自己醒来后向东北方向望去，看到这些物体从山后出现。他总共观察到了三到四个物体。这些物体向东北方向移动，向上飞行后缓慢消失。目击过程持续了约40秒。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为散发着白光、呈长方形。每个物体的主体周围都有一个圆环，中间有一条贯穿的线条，两端呈尖状。目击者指出，这些物体没有发出任何声音，也不像任何飞行器。他估计这些物体距离约四英里，看起来大约有13英尺长的拖车那么大。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由目击者的父亲德里克·杰伊先生报告给了加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP)。作为官方后续调查的一部分，加拿大皇家骑警联系了尼古拉斯·杰伊所在学校的校长 W.N. 霍尔顿先生。霍尔顿先生对该目击者进行了品行评估，称虽然该学生有时说话可能比较模糊，但他并非那种会寻求关注、心怀恶意或故意编造虚假报告来制造麻烦的孩子。

**Witnesses:** Thomas Edwards (12-year-old student), Mrs. Natalie Edwards, Mr. Ray Matheson (Principal of St. Annes School).

**Date / Time:** October 19, 1974, between 7:00 A.M. and 7:30 A.M.

**Location:** Calgary, Alberta; specifically observed from a residence looking toward the Gulf Oil Refineries in the Ogden area, near the Inglewood Bird Sanctuary.

**Sighting:** On the morning of October 19, 1974, Thomas Edwards, a 12-year-old grade 8 student, observed an unidentified aerial object while looking out his bedroom window. His mother, Mrs. Natalie Edwards, was also present for the sighting. The sky was noted as being clear with some stars still visible. The object was initially spotted hovering over the Gulf Oil Refineries in Ogden, appearing to be positioned in the vicinity of the Inglewood Bird Sanctuary. The object remained stationary for approximately five seconds before accelerating rapidly in a northerly direction.

**Object:** The object was described as a large, round, bright light characterized by a surrounding halo and "sparkly things." The witness noted that the object exhibited a dynamic appearance, seemingly changing shape—at times appearing thin and tall, and at other times round—a phenomenon the witness described as "like breathing." As the object began to move, the bright light dimmed, revealing a solid, disc-shaped craft resembling a frisbee with no sharp edges. Throughout the duration of the observation, the object produced no noise.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The official report was filed by S/Sgt. J.R. Galbraith of the Calgary Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) following an interview with Thomas Edwards. As part of the follow-up investigation, the RCMP contacted Mr. Ray Matheson, the principal of St. Annes School, to verify the credibility of the witness. Mr. Matheson provided a character reference for Thomas, describing him as a quiet student who is not a dreamer, thereby supporting the reliability of the account provided to the authorities.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 托马斯·爱德华兹（Thomas Edwards，12岁学生）、娜塔莉·爱德华兹夫人（Mrs. Natalie Edwards）、雷·马西森先生（Mr. Ray Matheson，圣安妮学校校长）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月19日，上午7:00至7:30之间。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省卡尔加里；具体观测点位于一处住宅，朝奥格登（Ogden）地区的湾石油炼油厂（Gulf Oil Refineries）方向望去，靠近英格尔伍德鸟类保护区（Inglewood Bird Sanctuary）。

**目击经过：** 1974年10月19日清晨，12岁的八年级学生托马斯·爱德华兹透过卧室窗户观察时，发现了一个不明飞行物。他的母亲娜塔莉·爱德华兹夫人当时也在场。据记录，当时天空晴朗，仍可见几颗星辰。该物体最初被发现悬停在奥格登的湾石油炼油厂上方，位置似乎在英格尔伍德鸟类保护区附近。物体保持静止约五秒钟，随后迅速向北加速离去。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的圆形亮光，周围环绕着光晕和“闪烁物”。目击者指出，该物体呈现出动态外观，似乎在不断变换形状——有时看起来又细又高，有时又呈圆形——目击者将其描述为“像在呼吸”。当物体开始移动时，亮光变暗，显露出一个坚固的圆盘状飞行器，类似于飞盘，没有尖锐的边缘。在整个观测过程中，该物体未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 官方报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）卡尔加里分局的J.R.加尔布雷斯（J.R. Galbraith）高级警长在采访托马斯·爱德华兹后提交。作为后续调查的一部分，加拿大皇家骑警联系了圣安妮学校校长雷·马西森先生，以核实目击者的可信度。马西森先生为托马斯提供了品行证明，称他是一名安静、不爱幻想的学生，从而支持了其向当局所提供证词的可靠性。

**Witnesses:** A group of ten children, aged 9 to 13 years.

**Sighting:** On October 19, 1974, at 9:30 PM, the witnesses observed an object while standing on a hill approximately 2 1/2 miles south of the town of Cochrane, Alberta. The sky was clear.

**Object:** The object was described as disc-shaped, ten to twenty feet in diameter, with an apparent superstructure. It displayed red and white flashing lights. **Witnesses:** Unnamed female witness, anonymous source.

**Date / Time:** October 19, 1974, at 2:50 AM MDT; October 20, 1974, at approximately 9:10 PM.

**Location:** Priddis, Alberta (including 1 mile south of Priddis and Southeast Quarter Section 15-22-3-W5).

**Sighting:** This case file documents two distinct sightings reported in the Priddis, Alberta area. The first event occurred on October 19, 1974, at 2:50 AM MDT, when an unnamed female witness located one mile south of Priddis observed a UFO while using a telescope. She reported that the sky was very clear with no cloud cover. She observed the primary object hovering approximately 100 feet off the ground, accompanied by two other objects that remained at a greater distance.

The second event occurred on October 20, 1974, at approximately 9:10 PM. An anonymous source observed an object near the Southeast Quarter Section 15-22-3-W5. The witness noted that the sky was clear to the east with some clouds to the west. The object was observed for approximately 30 seconds as it moved in a south-to-north direction, approximately 150–200 yards west of the witness's dwelling.

**Object:** Both reports describe an object of identical dimensions: approximately 60 feet in length/width and 25 feet in height. 

In the October 19 sighting, the object emitted a "very white light" and exhibited a zig-zag movement pattern while maintaining a general hovering position for several seconds. 

In the October 20 sighting, the object was described as a "brilliant light" with no specific color, featuring red clearance lights positioned above and below a window. Its movement was described as a "sweeping motion" at an altitude of approximately 100 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The October 19 report was processed via radio records and transmitted to the National Research Council Meteor Centre in Ottawa, with information copies distributed to the Calgary S/Div and the Turner Valley Detachment. 

The October 20 report was formally filed by the Turner Valley RCMP. Official follow-up notes indicate that there were no similar reports from other sources regarding the second sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_07_-_Pages_18.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名未具名的女性目击者，一位匿名消息来源。

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月19日，凌晨2:50（山区夏令时间）；1974年10月20日，约晚上9:10。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省普里迪斯（Priddis）（包括普里迪斯以南1英里处及第15-22-3-W5号区域东南四分之一地块）。

**目击经过：** 本案卷记录了在阿尔伯塔省普里迪斯地区报告的两起独立目击事件。第一起事件发生在1974年10月19日凌晨2:50（山区夏令时间），一名位于普里迪斯以南1英里的未具名女性目击者在使用望远镜时观察到了一个不明飞行物（UFO）。她报告称当时天空非常晴朗，没有云层覆盖。她观察到主要物体悬停在离地约100英尺的高度，并伴有两个保持在较远距离的其他物体。

第二起事件发生在1974年10月20日晚上约9:10。一名匿名消息来源在第15-22-3-W5号区域东南四分之一地块附近观察到了一个物体。目击者指出，当时东部天空晴朗，西部有少量云层。该物体被观察了约30秒，它在目击者住所西侧约150至200码处由南向北移动。

**物体描述：** 两份报告描述的物体尺寸相同：长/宽约60英尺，高约25英尺。

在10月19日的目击事件中，该物体发出“非常白的光”，并呈现出锯齿状的移动模式，同时保持了几秒钟的悬停状态。

在10月20日的目击事件中，该物体被描述为一团“耀眼的光”，没有特定的颜色，窗户上方和下方装有红色指示灯。其移动方式被描述为“扫掠式运动”，飞行高度约为100英尺。

**调查/后续：** 10月19日的报告通过无线电记录进行处理，并传送至位于渥太华的国家研究委员会流星中心，同时将副本分发给卡尔加里分部（Calgary S/Div）和特纳谷（Turner Valley）分遣队。

10月20日的报告由特纳谷皇家骑警（RCMP）正式立案。官方后续记录显示，没有收到其他来源关于第二次目击事件的类似报告。

**Witnesses:** Cst. F.S. Creasor (also spelled Creaser), Cst. Storie (also spelled Storey), Cst. Humphrey (all of the Strathmore Highway Patrol), and members/units of the Calgary City Police.

**Date / Time:** October 23, 1974; initial report at 3:22 AM, observations occurring between 3:45 AM and 6:30 AM.

**Location:** Shepard area, southeast of Calgary, Alberta.

**Sighting:** The event began when the Calgary Sub/Division Message center reported a U.F.O. over the Shepard area at 3:22 AM. Cst. Creasor patrolled the location and rendezvoused with other officers, including Cst. Storie, Cst. Humphrey, and three units of the Calgary City Police. Between 3:45 AM and 6:30 AM, the officers observed a singular, exceptionally bright light in an otherwise clear, star-filled sky. The object was positioned high in the sky, southeast of Calgary, near the base of the Big Dipper constellation. At 4:00 AM, a CFCN Radio helicopter arrived to investigate the area; the helicopter reported flying at altitudes reaching 11,000 feet, yet the witnesses observed the light to be at an even higher altitude, appearing to be in outer space.

**Object:** The object was described as a very bright white light, significantly more luminous than any other star in the sky—estimated to be twice the size of a standard star. It exhibited a twinkling or flickering effect, emitting flashes of violet, blue, and red light. While the object appeared stationary for periods, it demonstrated a distinct change in location toward the west over a 20-minute interval. No sound was emitted by the object throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was officially filed by Cst. F.S. Creasor of the Strathmore Detachment of the RCMP. The investigation involved a collaborative effort between the RCMP Strathmore Highway Patrol and the Calgary City Police. A key component of the follow-up was the utilization of a CFCN Radio helicopter to provide a point of reference for altitude; by comparing the object’s position to the helicopter’s flight path at 11,000 feet, officers confirmed the object was at a significantly higher elevation. The sky conditions were noted as clear with no cloud cover, ensuring the object was the only light of its nature visible in the vicinity.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** F.S. 克里瑟警官（Cst. F.S. Creasor，亦拼作 Creaser）、斯托里警官（Cst. Storie，亦拼作 Storey）、汉弗莱警官（Cst. Humphrey，以上三人均隶属斯特拉斯莫尔高速公路巡逻队），以及卡尔加里市警察局的成员/单位。

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月23日；初步报告时间为凌晨3:22，观测持续时间为凌晨3:45至6:30。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省卡尔加里东南部的谢泼德（Shepard）地区。

**目击经过：** 事件始于凌晨3:22，当时卡尔加里分区信息中心报告称谢泼德地区上空出现不明飞行物。克里瑟警官前往该地点巡逻，并与其他警官会合，其中包括斯托里警官、汉弗莱警官以及卡尔加里市警察局的三个单位。在凌晨3:45至6:30之间，警官们观察到在晴朗且繁星点点的夜空中，有一个异常明亮的单一光源。该物体位于卡尔加里东南部的高空，靠近大熊星座（北斗七星）底部。凌晨4:00，一架CFCN电台的直升机抵达该区域进行调查；直升机报告其飞行高度达到11,000英尺，但目击者观察到该光源的高度更高，看起来仿佛位于外太空。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一团非常明亮的白光，其亮度远超天空中任何其他恒星，估计大小是普通恒星的两倍。它呈现出闪烁的效果，并发出紫、蓝、红色的光芒。虽然该物体在一段时间内看起来是静止的，但在20分钟的时间间隔内，它表现出了明显的向西位移。在整个目击过程中，该物体未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）斯特拉斯莫尔分队的 F.S. 克里瑟警官正式提交。调查工作由加拿大皇家骑警斯特拉斯莫尔高速公路巡逻队与卡尔加里市警察局协作完成。后续调查的一个关键部分是利用CFCN电台的直升机提供高度参考点；通过将该物体的位置与直升机在11,000英尺处的飞行路径进行对比，警官们确认该物体处于明显更高的高度。据记录，当时天空晴朗无云，确保了该物体是附近唯一可见的此类光源。

**Witnesses:** James (Jim) Pearce, Etta Pearce

**Date / Time:** October 22, 1974, at approximately 5:28 PM CST (Note: Page 12 records the time as 6:28 PM; Page 13 records 5:28 PM CST).

**Location:** A field north of the Pearce farmyard, near Wilcox, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 22, 1974, James and Etta Pearce observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while located in a field north of their farm. James Pearce first spotted a bright light in the East, which proceeded to move West toward their farm. Both witnesses observed the object at an estimated altitude of 400–600 feet. The object traveled from east to west at a slow rate of speed for approximately ten minutes before disappearing to the West at a high rate of speed. 

Following the disappearance of the primary object, a second event occurred a few minutes later. James Pearce observed a bright light in the western horizon, from which at least several bright, colored objects were emitted. These smaller objects were observed emitting light toward the south before they also disappeared.

**Object:** The primary object was described as saucer-shaped and covered in numerous, various-colored lights. It emitted a sound described by the witnesses as a "muffled down big motor." Regarding its movement, the witnesses noted it traveled faster than a small plane, despite the initial slow-speed observation period. The secondary objects observed later were described as bright and colored.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the RCMP, who noted that the witnesses appeared earnest and sober. James Pearce, who is a former member of the Air Force, stated that the object resembled nothing he had seen during his service. Pearce provided a hand-drawn sketch of the objects to the investigating officers. The report was officially forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the National Research Council (NRC). The NRC conducted a follow-up investigation and noted that CFB Moose Jaw was conducting military exercises in the area at the time of the sighting, which officials suggested may account for the observations. The sky conditions at the time of the event were reported as clear.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯（吉姆）·皮尔斯 (James (Jim) Pearce)、埃塔·皮尔斯 (Etta Pearce)

**日期 / 时间：** 1974年10月22日，中部标准时间 (CST) 下午约5:28（注：第12页记录时间为下午6:28；第13页记录为下午5:28）。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省威尔科克斯 (Wilcox) 附近，皮尔斯农场北侧的一片田地。

**目击经过：** 1974年10月22日傍晚，詹姆斯·皮尔斯和埃塔·皮尔斯在自家农场北侧的田地里目击到一种不明空中现象。詹姆斯·皮尔斯首先发现东方出现一道亮光，随后该光点向西朝着他们的农场移动。两位目击者观察到该物体的高度估计在400至600英尺之间。该物体以缓慢的速度自东向西飞行了约十分钟，随后以极高的速度向西消失。

在主物体消失几分钟后，发生了第二次事件。詹姆斯·皮尔斯观察到西侧地平线上出现一道亮光，从中射出了至少几个明亮的彩色物体。这些较小的物体被观察到向南方发出光芒，随后也消失了。

**物体描述：** 主物体被描述为碟状，表面覆盖着许多不同颜色的灯光。它发出的声音被目击者形容为“沉闷的大型引擎声”。关于其运动方式，目击者指出，尽管初期观察时速度缓慢，但其飞行速度比小型飞机还要快。随后观察到的次要物体被描述为明亮的彩色光点。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件被报告给了加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP)，警方指出目击者表现得诚恳且清醒。曾为空军成员的詹姆斯·皮尔斯表示，该物体与他在服役期间见过的任何东西都不像。皮尔斯向调查警官提供了他手绘的物体草图。该报告被正式转交至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 的高层大气研究部门。NRC进行了后续调查，并指出当时加拿大穆斯乔空军基地 (CFB Moose Jaw) 正在该地区进行军事演习，官方认为这或许可以解释此次目击事件。据报告，事件发生时天空状况晴朗。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Mary Harris

**Date / Time:** October 28, 1974, at 280000Z (00:00 Zulu time)

**Sighting:**
On October 28, 1974, Mrs. Mary Harris observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon from her residence in Alliston, Ontario. The sighting was sustained, lasting for a total duration of one and one-half hours. According to Mrs. Harris’s account, the object was positioned in the sky and appeared to move away from the moon. Throughout the duration of the event, only one object was reported by the witness.

**Object:**
The object was described as having an elongated spherical shape with pointed ends. A distinct feature of the craft was an "orbital center" containing a red ball. Additionally, a bright bar of light was observed running through the entire length of the object. The altitude of the object remained undetermined throughout the observation. No sound or specific flight maneuvers beyond the movement away from the moon were noted in the documentation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The sighting was formally documented and processed through military and scientific channels. The report was initially handled by the Base Commander of Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Borden. From there, the documentation was officially transmitted to the National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa. Furthermore, the report was forwarded to the National Research Council in Ottawa and the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada for their records and potential review.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Tom Clark, Ruth Tobin

**Date / Time:** January 26, 1975, at 1:00 AM

**Location:** Bay Bulls, Newfoundland

**Sighting:** On the night of January 26, 1975, at approximately 1:00 AM, witnesses Tom Clark (of Petty Harbour) and Ruth Tobin (of Witless Bay) observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the Bay Bulls area. The sky conditions were reported as clear at the time of the sighting. According to the initial reports provided by the witnesses, they observed a round object hovering above the ground at a distance of approximately 200 feet. The object was noted for its distinct color changes, shifting between bright red and bright white. The witnesses observed this object for a duration of approximately 30 minutes before it departed the area at a high rate of speed.

**Object:** The object was described as round in shape and was observed hovering at an altitude of roughly 200 feet. It exhibited a color-changing property, alternating between bright red and bright white. While the initial observation suggested an anomalous aerial phenomenon, subsequent investigation identified the object as a small private aircraft. The aircraft was operating in the vicinity of Bay Bulls at the time of the sighting, with its landing lights activated while the pilot was reportedly checking his cabin.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally reported through the St. John's Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). The RCMP forwarded the details of the report to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre in Ottawa for further review. Following the investigation into the circumstances of the event, authorities concluded that the "UFO" was a small private aircraft. The investigation established that the pilot was conducting operations in the Bay Bulls area and that the visual characteristics reported by the witnesses—specifically the hovering motion and the bright, color-changing lights—were consistent with the aircraft’s landing lights and flight path during the pilot's cabin check.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 汤姆·克拉克 (Tom Clark)、露丝·托宾 (Ruth Tobin)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年1月26日，凌晨1:00

**地点：** 纽芬兰省，贝布尔斯 (Bay Bulls)

**目击经过：** 1975年1月26日凌晨1点左右，目击者汤姆·克拉克（来自佩蒂港）和露丝·托宾（来自威特利斯湾）在贝布尔斯地区观察到一种不明空中现象。据报告，当时天空晴朗。根据目击者提供的初步报告，他们观察到一个圆形物体悬浮在离地约200英尺（约61米）的空中。该物体颜色变化明显，在亮红色和亮白色之间交替闪烁。目击者观察了该物体约30分钟，随后它以极高的速度离开了该区域。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，悬浮在约200英尺的高度。它具有变色特性，在亮红色和亮白色之间交替。虽然初步观察显示这是一种异常的空中现象，但随后的调查确认该物体是一架小型私人飞机。事发时，该飞机正在贝布尔斯附近飞行，飞行员在检查机舱时开启了着陆灯。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件通过加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 圣约翰分局正式上报。加拿大皇家骑警将报告详情转交至位于渥太华的国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心进行进一步审查。在对事件情况进行调查后，当局得出结论，该“不明飞行物”是一架小型私人飞机。调查确定，飞行员当时正在贝布尔斯地区进行飞行作业，目击者所报告的视觉特征——特别是悬停动作以及明亮的变色灯光——与飞行员在进行机舱检查时的着陆灯和飞行轨迹相吻合。

**Witnesses:** George Bartzs, Gerald Reynolds, and RCMP officers Cst. McCartney and Cst. Pilszek.

**Sighting:** On February 16, 1975, between 7 PM and 8 PM, four unidentified objects were observed near Mildred Lake, north of Fort McMurray. The sky was clear with a first-quarter moon. Bartzs and Reynolds first saw three lights while driving into town; the lights appeared to remain steady. They were later joined by RCMP officers who patrolled to a hill southwest of town.

**Object:** The witnesses observed four lights of great intensity, red and blue-green, flashing at an elevation of approximately 30 degrees to the southeast, estimated to be 50 to 100 miles away. Another light of lesser intensity was seen to the northwest at an altitude of 20 degrees. Additionally, two bright orange, triangular-shaped lights were observed in the southwest, one above the other, moving up and down from an altitude of 5 degrees to below the horizon.

**Aftermath:** All lights were in sight for over one hour and were viewed through binoculars.

**Additional pages:** This same incident is also recorded on 1 other page (p.148) of the same file. Cluster confirmed by shared FOIA record number N75/017.

**Witnesses:** David W. Goudy and his wife.

**Sighting:** On Tuesday, March 4, at approximately 10 PM, the witness observed a small bright light from a window facing North. The object traveled from west to east at approximately 15 degrees above the horizon at considerable speed. It stopped directly opposite the window for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, then moved again across the horizon, stopped for another 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, and finally disappeared behind a hill to the North-East.
