**Witnesses:** Two civilians (residing on Simcoe St and Macdonald St, Moose Jaw), Cpl. Ferguson RC, Cst. Monaghan JK, Cst. Mann DJ, and Cst. Woodward RC (all of the Moose Jaw Detachment RCMP).

**Date / Time:** April 10, 1975 (noted as April 18, 1975, in secondary documentation), between 9:30 PM and 11:45 PM CST.

**Location:** Township 19, Range 28, West of the 2nd Meridian, situated between the towns of Tuxford and Marquis, Saskatchewan, northwest of Moose Jaw.

**Sighting:** On the night of the incident, a high-intensity white light was observed by two civilians and four RCMP officers. The sighting lasted approximately two hours, during which the object moved from the west of Moose Jaw to a position approximately 30 miles northwest of the city. The sky conditions were reported as clear with scattered clouds. The object’s altitude was observed to be dynamic, shifting from below cloud level to above cloud level throughout the duration of the event. The sighting concluded when an Air Canada flight, traveling from Regina to Edmonton, reached the approximate location of the object. Witnesses observed the aircraft lights and the unidentified light in the same general area immediately prior to the object’s disappearance.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, high-intensity white light with no discernable shape or structure. It exhibited significant movement across the sky, transitioning between altitudes above and below the cloud layer. No sound was reported, and the duration of the observation was approximately two hours.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Moose Jaw Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation involving four officers (Cpl. Ferguson, Cst. Monaghan, Cst. Mann, and Cst. Woodward). Official inquiries were made with Regina Air Traffic Control (ATC) to determine if the object had been tracked; ATC reported no radar contact with the object. The investigation noted that the object remained visible until the arrival of an Air Canada flight, at which point it vanished from sight.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两名平民（分别居住在穆斯乔市的西姆科街和麦克唐纳街），以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）穆斯乔分局的弗格森下士（Cpl. Ferguson）、莫纳汉警员（Cst. Monaghan JK）、曼恩警员（Cst. Mann DJ）和伍德沃德警员（Cst. Woodward RC）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年4月10日（部分辅助文档记录为1975年4月18日），中部标准时间（CST）晚上9:30至11:45之间。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省穆斯乔西北部，塔克斯福德镇与马奎斯镇之间的第19乡区，西经第2子午线第28测区。

**目击经过：** 事件当晚，两名平民和四名加拿大皇家骑警警员观察到一束高强度的白光。目击过程持续了约两个小时，期间该物体从穆斯乔以西移动至该市西北约30英里处的位置。据报告，当时天空晴朗，有零星云层。观察发现该物体的高度处于动态变化中，在整个事件过程中，它在云层下方和上方之间来回穿梭。当一架从里贾纳飞往埃德蒙顿的加拿大航空航班抵达该物体所在的大致区域时，目击事件结束。在物体消失前，目击者观察到飞机灯光与该不明光源处于同一大致区域。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为单一的高强度白光，没有可辨认的形状或结构。它在天空中表现出明显的移动，并在云层上方和下方的高度之间转换。据报告，现场没有任何声音，观察持续时间约为两小时。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警穆斯乔分局对此展开了调查，四名警员（弗格森下士、莫纳汉警员、曼恩警员和伍德沃德警员）参与其中。官方曾向里贾纳空中交通管制中心（ATC）进行查询，以确定该物体是否被追踪；空中交通管制中心报告称，雷达并未探测到该物体。调查指出，该物体一直处于可见状态，直到一架加拿大航空公司的航班抵达，随后该物体便消失在视野中。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Norman Prince

**Date / Time:** April 13, 1975, at 1810Z

**Location:** Fort St James, specifically over Hunguay Island on Stuart Lake

**Sighting:** 
On April 13, 1975, at 1810Z, witness Norman Prince observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon over Hunguay Island, located on Stuart Lake in Fort St James. The sighting lasted for a total duration of 20 minutes. During this period, the witness observed the object hovering or remaining in the vicinity of the island. The account provided by the witness consistently describes the object’s appearance as changing in both color and intensity throughout the duration of the event.

**Object:** 
The object was described as being round in shape. Its visual characteristics were dynamic, appearing bright and yellow at certain times, and shifting to a red, dim appearance at other times. No specific sound or complex movement patterns were reported beyond its presence over the island for the 20-minute duration.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was formally documented and transmitted from the Canadian Forces Station (CFS) Baldy Hughes to the National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa. The report was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) for further review and analysis as part of the official Canadian UFO reporting process.

该物体被描述为圆形。其视觉特征具有动态性，有时呈现明亮的黄色，有时又转变为暗淡的红色。除在岛屿上空停留了20分钟外，未报告有任何特定的声音或复杂的运动模式。

此次目击事件被正式记录在案，并由加拿大武装部队巴尔迪休斯站 (CFS Baldy Hughes) 传达至位于渥太华的国防部总部 (NDHQ)。随后，作为加拿大官方不明飞行物报告程序的一部分，该报告被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 进行进一步的审查与分析。

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP officers conducted the observation directly from the City Hall location in response to public reports. Following the conclusion of the sighting, the official report was formally transmitted from CFS (Canadian Forces Station) Kamloops to the National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa. CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Phillip Burkinshaw (also recorded as Phil Burkinshaw), Lois Stewart

**Date / Time:** May 15, 1975, at approximately 0045–0051 hours (Mountain Standard Daylight Saving Time)

**Location:** Red Deer, Alberta

**Sighting:** On the night of May 15, 1975, witnesses Phillip Burkinshaw and Lois Stewart were outdoors in Red Deer, Alberta, engaged in identifying constellations in a clear, unobstructed sky. At approximately 0045 hours, they observed three unidentified objects traveling at an extremely high rate of speed. Initially, the objects were moving in a southbound direction. The witnesses observed the objects performing erratic maneuvers, specifically turning around and proceeding in a north-northeasterly (N.N.E.) direction. During this time, the objects were not flying in a standard formation; instead, they were observed passing one another and crisscrossing paths. The total duration of the observation was estimated to be between one and two minutes.

**Object:** The three objects were described as boomerang-shaped and emitted a distinct orange glow. They were observed at a very high altitude. The movement was characterized as erratic and high-speed, involving complex, non-linear flight paths. No sound was reported by the witnesses.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Red Deer City Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation into the report. The reporting officer noted that the complainant (Burkinshaw) appeared sober and earnest, and explicitly stated there was no reason to doubt the credibility of the witnesses. A check with other RCMP members on patrol confirmed that no other sightings were reported to the office at that time. Following the initial report, a telex was forwarded to the National Research Council at 0109 hours on May 15, 1975. Additionally, the case was slated for a follow-up report to be sent to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 菲利普·伯金肖（Phillip Burkinshaw，亦记录为 Phil Burkinshaw）、洛伊斯·斯图尔特（Lois Stewart）

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月15日，约00:45–00:51（山区标准夏令时间）

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省红鹿市（Red Deer, Alberta）

**目击经过：** 1975年5月15日晚，目击者菲利普·伯金肖和洛伊斯·斯图尔特在阿尔伯塔省红鹿市户外观察并辨认星座，当时天空晴朗无遮挡。约00:45，他们观察到三个不明物体以极高的速度飞行。起初，这些物体向南移动。目击者观察到这些物体进行了不规则的机动飞行，具体表现为掉头并转向北北东（N.N.E.）方向行进。在此期间，这些物体并未保持标准编队，而是相互交错穿行。整个观察过程持续时间估计在一到两分钟之间。

**物体描述：** 这三个物体被描述为回旋镖形状，并发出明显的橙色光芒。它们被观察时处于极高的高度。其运动特征为不规则且高速，涉及复杂的非线性飞行路径。目击者称未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）红鹿市分局对该报告进行了调查。负责警官指出，举报人（伯金肖）看起来清醒且诚恳，并明确表示没有理由怀疑目击者的可信度。经向其他巡逻的皇家骑警成员核实，当时办公室未收到其他目击报告。在初步报告之后，一份电传于1975年5月15日01:09发送至加拿大国家研究委员会。此外，该案件已被列入后续报告计划，将提交至高层大气研究部门。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Henry Francois, Mrs. Sawatzky

**Date / Time:** June 4, 1975, at approximately 7:40 A.M. (Daylight Saving Time)

**Location:** A municipal road near Holland, Manitoba; specifically noted as being approximately 3/4 of a mile east of the junction of P.T.H. #34 and #22 (also referenced as the junction of P.T.H. #34 and #2).

**Sighting:** On the morning of June 4, 1975, Henry Francois was driving east on a municipal road near Holland, Manitoba, when he encountered an unidentified object. At the time of the sighting, the sky was reported as cloudy. Mr. Francois observed the object for approximately two minutes. During this time, he left the immediate vicinity to drive to the residence of Mr. Henry Sawatzky to request that Mrs. Sawatzky accompany him back to the site to witness the object. Upon returning to the location with Mrs. Sawatzky, the object was no longer present.

**Object:** The object was described as an oval, disc-shaped craft measuring approximately 30 feet in diameter and 10 feet in height. It was positioned hovering approximately 2 feet above the ground in the center of the municipal road. The craft was a brilliant silvery-white color and featured a very brilliant light located near the top and center. This light was observed flashing on and off at regular intervals of approximately one second. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Treherne RCMP detachment conducted an investigation into the sighting. At approximately 4:30 P.M. on the day of the event, an RCMP officer accompanied Mr. Francois to the site to inspect the area for physical evidence; however, none was found. The RCMP noted that Mr. Francois is considered a reliable and mentally stable citizen. The official report was subsequently forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch at the National Research Council in Ottawa, as well as the National Research Council Meteor Center.

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月4日，约上午7:40（夏令时间）

**地点：** 马尼托巴省荷兰镇 (Holland, Manitoba) 附近的一条市政道路；具体位置标注为距离34号和22号省道 (P.T.H. #34 and #22) 交汇处以东约3/4英里处（亦有记录称其为34号和2号省道交汇处）。

**目击经过：** 1975年6月4日上午，亨利·弗朗索瓦驾车在马尼托巴省荷兰镇附近的一条市政道路上向东行驶时，遇到了一个不明物体。据报告，当时天空多云。弗朗索瓦先生观察该物体约两分钟。在此期间，他离开了现场，驱车前往亨利·萨瓦茨基 (Henry Sawatzky) 先生的住所，请求萨瓦茨基夫人随他一同返回现场见证该物体。当他与萨瓦茨基夫人回到该地点时，物体已不见踪影。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个椭圆形、圆盘状的飞行器，直径约30英尺，高约10英尺。它悬停在市政道路中央，距离地面约2英尺。飞行器呈明亮的银白色，顶部中心附近有一个非常耀眼的光源。据观察，该光源以约一秒的固定间隔闪烁。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 特雷赫恩 (Treherne) 加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 分队对此次目击事件进行了调查。事发当天下午约4:30，一名皇家骑警警官陪同弗朗索瓦先生前往现场检查是否有物理证据，但未发现任何痕迹。皇家骑警指出，弗朗索瓦先生被认为是一位可靠且精神稳定的公民。官方报告随后被转交至渥太华国家研究委员会天体物理分部的高层大气研究部门，以及国家研究委员会流星中心。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst J.R. Brault (also referred to as J.P. Brault), Cst W.F. Joyce, and Cst R.J. Howe of the RCMP Brandon Detachment.

**Date / Time:** June 20, 1975, at approximately 11:10 PM, continuing until 12:30 AM on June 21, 1975.

**Location:** Kirkham's Bridge, Manitoba; Grand Valley Road; PTH 21; and a final location approximately 3 miles southeast of Hamiota, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On the night of June 20, 1975, at approximately 11:10 PM, Cst J.R. Brault was on patrol near Kirkham's Bridge and Grand Valley Road when he observed an illuminated object. At 11:30 PM, Csts W.F. Joyce and R.J. Howe, who were patrolling in a separate police vehicle, also sighted the same light in the Kirkham's Bridge area. 

Cst Brault attempted to close in on the object but was unable to reach it. He pursued the light toward Hamiota, Manitoba. Simultaneously, Csts Joyce and Howe followed the object while traveling on PTH 21 toward Hamiota. The officers maintained visual contact with the object until it finally vanished at 12:30 AM on June 21, 1975, at a location approximately 3 miles southeast of Hamiota.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright white light suspended approximately 200 to 300 feet above the ground. It remained stationary for the duration of the observation, though it periodically increased in brightness on several occasions. Just before the object vanished at 12:30 AM, a distinct red flash was observed within the white light. No sound was reported, and the object displayed no conventional aircraft characteristics.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the initial sighting at 11:30 PM, the officers contacted the Brandon Airport Tower to inquire about air traffic in the vicinity. The tower confirmed that there were no aircraft in the area at that time. After the object disappeared, the officers conducted a search of the immediate area to determine if the light could have been a star or a terrestrial object, but they found nothing that could account for the sighting. Based on the lack of identifiable aircraft, the behavior of the light, and the inability to explain the phenomenon, the reporting officers (Csts Brault, Joyce, and Howe) officially concluded that the object should be classified as a UFO.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）布兰登分局的 J.R. 布罗（J.R. Brault，亦被称为 J.P. 布罗）、W.F. 乔伊斯（W.F. Joyce）以及 R.J. 豪（R.J. Howe）警官。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月20日，约晚上11:10，持续至1975年6月21日凌晨12:30。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省柯克汉姆桥（Kirkham's Bridge）；格兰德谷路（Grand Valley Road）；21号省道（PTH 21）；以及马尼托巴省哈米奥塔（Hamiota）东南约3英里处。

**目击经过：** 1975年6月20日晚约11:10，J.R. 布罗警官在柯克汉姆桥和格兰德谷路附近巡逻时，观察到一个发光的物体。晚上11:30，在另一辆警车上巡逻的 W.F. 乔伊斯警官和 R.J. 豪警官也在柯克汉姆桥区域看到了同样的亮光。

布罗警官试图靠近该物体，但未能成功。他驱车向马尼托巴省哈米奥塔方向追逐该光源。与此同时，乔伊斯和豪警官也在21号省道上向哈米奥塔方向行驶，并跟随该物体。警官们保持着对该物体的目视接触，直到它最终于1975年6月21日凌晨12:30在哈米奥塔东南约3英里处消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个悬浮在离地约200至300英尺高空的明亮白光。在整个观察过程中，它保持静止，但曾多次周期性地增强亮度。在凌晨12:30物体消失前，白光中出现了一次明显的红色闪光。据报告，现场没有任何声音，且该物体未表现出任何常规飞行器的特征。

**调查/后续：** 在晚上11:30首次目击后，警官们联系了布兰登机场塔台，询问该区域的空中交通情况。塔台确认当时该区域没有任何飞行器。物体消失后，警官们对周边区域进行了搜查，以确定该光源是否可能是一颗恒星或地面物体，但他们没有发现任何可以解释此次目击事件的线索。基于无法识别飞行器、光源的行为表现以及无法解释该现象，报告警官（布罗、乔伊斯和豪）正式得出结论：该物体应被归类为不明飞行物（UFO）。

**Witnesses:** Norman Robertson (age 21), Mrs. Archie Robertson (age 45), Cst. E. G. White (Rosetown Detachment RCMP).

**Date / Time:** July 29, 1975; 1:35 AM to 2:07 AM.

**Location:** Zealandia, Saskatchewan (specifically the Robertson farm).

**Sighting:** On July 29, 1975, at 1:35 AM, Norman Robertson and his mother, Mrs. Archie Robertson—both noted by authorities as very reliable witnesses—observed a strange object in the sky located west-northwest of their farm. The witnesses utilized a pair of small field glasses to track the object. Over a 12-minute period, the object descended from a fairly high position in the sky to a point just above the horizon. 

The witnesses reported that the object moved in short, quick bursts with no discernible pattern. At 2:07 AM, the object disappeared instantly, described by the witnesses as being "as if a light had been turned out." It subsequently reappeared, faded, and reappeared again before finally fading away entirely. The observers noted a buildup of thunderclouds to the north, which were moving toward the direction of the object.

**Object:** The object was observed at a great distance. It was described as having a definite green color, accompanied by a red light. This red light was predominantly positioned on the bottom of the object but was observed moving to other positions around the green light; at times, the red light appeared to rotate around the green center. The object’s movement was characterized by quick, short-distance shifts. No photographs were taken, as the witnesses determined the object was too far away for their equipment.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was documented by Cst. E. G. White of the Rosetown Detachment of the RCMP. Official notes indicate that the sky was generally clear, though there was a notable thundercloud buildup in the northwest. Investigators remained uncertain as to whether the object's final disappearance was caused by the encroaching cloud cover or by the object itself. The witnesses were formally interviewed, and their reliability was noted in the official file.

**目击者：** 诺曼·罗伯逊（Norman Robertson，21岁）、阿奇·罗伯逊夫人（Mrs. Archie Robertson，45岁）、加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）罗斯敦分局警员 E. G. 怀特（Cst. E. G. White）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年7月29日；凌晨1:35至2:07。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省西兰迪亚（Zealandia）（具体地点为罗伯逊农场）。

**目击经过：** 1975年7月29日凌晨1:35，诺曼·罗伯逊及其母亲阿奇·罗伯逊夫人——两人均被当局认定为非常可靠的目击者——在农场西北偏西方向的天空中观察到一个奇怪的物体。目击者使用一副小型野外望远镜对该物体进行了追踪。在12分钟的时间里，该物体从高空下降至地平线附近。

目击者称，该物体以短促、快速且无明显规律的方式移动。凌晨2:07，物体瞬间消失，目击者形容其过程“就像关掉了一盏灯”。随后它又重新出现、变暗，再次出现，最后彻底消失。观察者注意到北面有雷雨云堆积，并正向该物体所在的方向移动。

**物体描述：** 该物体在极远距离被观察到。据描述，它呈现出明显的绿色，并伴有一道红光。这道红光主要位于物体底部，但也被观察到会移动到绿色光源周围的其他位置；有时，红光似乎围绕着绿色的中心旋转。该物体的移动特点是快速、短距离的位移。由于目击者认为物体距离太远，无法用现有设备拍摄，因此未留下照片。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警罗斯敦分局的 E. G. 怀特警员记录在案。官方记录显示，当时天空总体晴朗，但西北方向有明显的雷雨云堆积。调查人员无法确定该物体最终消失是因为被逼近的云层遮挡，还是物体本身的原因。目击者接受了正式访谈，官方档案中特别注明了他们的可靠性。

**Witnesses:** The author, his wife, a friend, and an unnamed man in Ontario.

**Date / Time:** October 12, 1975, at 8:00 p.m. (with historical reference to a 1947 sighting).

**Location:** Ontario, Canada.

**Sighting:** The primary account involves the author, his wife, and a friend who were in their living room on October 12, 1975, at 8:00 p.m. watching television when the screen suddenly went blank, displaying only white snow. According to a handwritten account, two beings emerged directly from the television receiver. These entities were dressed in "silvery bluish-brown suits" and wore complete, round, clear plastic helmets through which their faces were clearly visible. The entities did not speak audibly; instead, the witness experienced a "mind/voice-like influence," feeling that the beings were communicating through thought. The entities assured the witness they would not cause harm and claimed they would help the witness make the sighting "fit" a spacecraft. 

The author also links this event to a broader narrative, claiming he received information on October 12 regarding scientists discussing the dangers of nuclear power and its impact on a 200-mile radius. He further references a newspaper article from *The Sun* (dated October 14, 1975) titled "Growth of reactors threatens oceans," which he connects to warnings about mercury pollution and poisoned lakes. Additionally, the author recounts a 1947 sighting in western Ontario where he witnessed a strip of lumber being cut and burned before his eyes, an event he reported to the local police at the time.

**Object:** 
*   **The 1975 Object:** A television receiver that functioned as a portal for the entities. The witness also refers to a "space ship" that was mentally linked to the experience, described as being "built" or constructed in a specific manner.
*   **The 1947 Object:** A cigar-shaped craft, approximately 30 feet wide, emitting a burning bluish light described as resembling a welding torch.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The author claims to have studied UFOs for 32 years, beginning with observations during World War II. He notes that a separate sighting by an unnamed man in Ontario was reported in *The Sun* newspaper on October 14, 1975. The author’s documentation includes a mix of personal testimony, references to environmental concerns (nuclear power and mercury pollution), and historical accounts of his own long-term interest in the phenomenon. No formal RCMP or meteorological reports were provided in the summary, though the author notes he reported his 1947 sighting to an Ontario police station.

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年10月12日晚8:00（并提及1947年的一次目击事件作为历史参考）。

**地点：** 加拿大安大略省。

**目击经过：** 主要事件发生在1975年10月12日晚8:00，当时作者、其妻子和一位朋友正在客厅看电视，电视屏幕突然变黑，随后只显示出雪花点。根据一份手写记录，两个生命体直接从电视接收器中显现出来。这些实体身穿“银蓝棕色套装”，戴着完整的圆形透明塑料头盔，透过头盔可以清晰地看到他们的脸。这些实体没有发出声音，但目击者感受到了一种“类似思维/声音的影响”，认为这些生命体是通过意念进行交流的。他们向目击者保证不会造成伤害，并声称会帮助目击者将这次目击经历与一艘宇宙飞船“联系起来”。

作者还将此事件与更广泛的叙述联系起来，声称他在10月12日获悉科学家们正在讨论核能的危险及其对半径200英里范围的影响。他进一步引用了1975年10月14日《太阳报》（*The Sun*）上题为《反应堆的增长威胁海洋》的文章，并将其与关于汞污染和湖泊中毒的警告联系在一起。此外，作者还讲述了1947年发生在安大略省西部的一次目击事件，当时他亲眼目睹了一块木材被切割并燃烧，他当时已向当地警方报告了此事。

**物体描述：**

**Witnesses:** One individual residing at Beaverbank Villa (civilian).

**Date / Time:** October 17, 1975.

**Location:** Beaverbank Villa, Lower Sackville, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 17, 1975, a civilian resident of Beaverbank Villa observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The weather conditions at the time of the sighting were noted as clear and cool. The witness observed a single light positioned at an approximate altitude of 5,000 feet. According to the witness account, the object exhibited rapid, erratic movement, shifting quickly from one location to another in the sky. During the course of the observation, the object appeared to develop or display a white tail.

**Object:** The object was described as a single light. Its primary characteristics included a high rate of speed and the ability to move quickly between different points in the sky. At one point during the sighting, the object appeared to have a white tail. The estimated altitude of the object was 5,000 feet. No specific sound or duration beyond the observation of the movement was recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was formally reported to the Bedford Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Following the report, an investigation was conducted to determine if other sightings had occurred in the area; however, the RCMP concluded that there were no other reports of the observation, and the case remained an isolated incident.

**目击者：** 一名居住在比弗班克别墅（Beaverbank Villa）的平民。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的光点。其主要特征包括极高的速度，以及在天空中不同点之间快速移动的能力。在目击过程中的某个时刻，该物体似乎带有一条白色的尾迹。该物体的估计高度为5000英尺。除对其运动轨迹的观察外，未记录到特定的声音或持续时间。

**调查/后续：** 该事件已正式报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）贝德福德分局。报告提交后，警方展开了调查，以确定该地区是否还发生过其他目击事件；然而，加拿大皇家骑警最终认定没有其他相关报告，该案件被视为一起孤立事件。

**Witnesses:** OPP Constables Gay and Bradshaw, a civilian radio operator named Douglas, and employees from a radio station and the Northern Telephone Company.

**Sighting:** On November 3, 1975, at 0945Z, observers reported a round, bright white light the size of a street lamp hovering northeast of Haileybury. Emanating from this object were fingers of white light. A second, larger light was observed just north of the first object, displaying red, white, and green colors.

**Object:** The objects were described as being approximately 50 times larger and brighter than a star. After about one hour, the objects began moving slowly south and appeared to climb higher, though altitude was difficult to estimate.

**Aftermath:** The objects were still being observed at 1100Z.

**Additional pages:** This incident is also documented on 3 other pages of the FOIA release.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_09_-_Pages_24.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** OPP警官Gay和Bradshaw，一名名为Douglas的平民无线电操作员，以及来自广播电台和北方电话公司的员工。

**目击：** 1975年11月3日0945Z，观察者报告在海利伯里（Haileybury）东北方向发现一个路灯大小的圆形明亮白光，并从中发出白光。在第一个物体北侧还观察到另一个大型光源，发出红色、白色和绿色光芒。

**物体：** 这些物体被描述为比星星大50倍且更亮。大约一小时后，这些物体开始缓慢向南移动，并似乎在爬升，尽管高度难以估计。

**后续：** 截至1100Z，观察仍在继续。

**其它相关页面：** 本事件在 FOIA 解密档案的其它 3 页中亦有记录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_09_-_Pages_24.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst J Olson, Cst R Platz, and Cst Calvert of the RCMP Grimshaw Detachment.

**Sighting:** On November 6, 1975, between 2:30 AM and 3:00 AM MST, with clear skies, RCMP officers located on Highway 2, approximately four miles east of Brownvale, Alberta, observed unidentified flying objects. Cst Olson reported the shape as round, while Cst Platz reported the shape as oval with a half-moon shape at the top. The color was white, changing to red and blue. The altitude was estimated between two and three thousand feet. The object moved to the right or south and appeared to increase altitude while remaining in the same area.

**Object:** The object was described as round or oval with a half-moon top, changing colors between white, red, and blue.

**Aftermath:** At 4:45 AM, Cst Platz observed a similar object to the west in the vicinity of Hines Creek, Alberta. Upon viewing it through binoculars, he stated it was identical to the previously sighted object. This object remained stationary and disappeared at 4:45 AM.

**见证者：** 皇家骑警 (RCMP) Grimshaw 分队的 Cst J Olson, Cst R Platz 和 Cst Calvert。

**目击：** 1975年11月6日凌晨2:30至3:00（山区标准时间），在天空晴朗的情况下，位于阿尔伯塔省布朗维尔 (Brownvale) 以东约四英里处2号公路上的皇家骑警观察到了不明飞行物。Cst Olson 报告物体形状为圆形，而 Cst Platz 报告形状为椭圆形，顶部呈半月形。颜色为白色，并会变为红色和蓝色。高度估计在两千到三千英尺之间。物体向右或向南移动，在保持在同一区域的同时，高度似乎有所增加。

**Witnesses:** Two individuals operating a tractor trailer, and several other subjects in the Whitehorse area.

**Sighting:** At approximately 4:20 AM on November 16, 1975, while traveling south on the Whitehorse-Carmacks Highway at Mile 31 near Fox Lake, witnesses observed an object descend like a helicopter over the rear of their trailer. The sky at the time was thin overcast.

**Object:** The object was described as much larger than the truck. It was very bright, hurting the eyes, with a center of light that was very white and edges that were bluish. It illuminated the entire area for about one mile in all directions like daylight. The object traveled in the same direction as the vehicle at a slightly greater speed than the truck, which was moving at 55 mph. It then rose at a fantastic speed and moved to the north over some hills in an arc.

**Aftermath:** The subjects observed the object for no more than 25 seconds. Several other subjects in the Whitehorse area reported seeing brightness in the sky for a few seconds but did not actually see the object.

**物体：** 该物体被描述为比卡车大得多。它非常明亮，刺眼，中心光芒呈亮白色，边缘呈蓝色。它将周围约一英里的区域照亮得如同白昼。该物体以略高于卡车（时速55英里）的速度沿相同方向行驶，随后以极快的速度上升，并呈弧线向北飞越山丘。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Louise Litwin, Lori Heward

**Date / Time:** October 21, 1976, at approximately 0300Z

**Location:** Chaplin, Saskatchewan (specifically near the Esso Bulk Dealer)

**Sighting:** 
On October 21, 1976, at approximately 0300Z, witnesses Louise Litwin and Lori Heward observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the town of Chaplin, Saskatchewan. The witnesses were positioned near the Esso Bulk Dealer when they first spotted the object. The sighting lasted for a total duration of 10 to 15 minutes. 

During the encounter, the witnesses exited their vehicle to obtain a better view of the object as it hovered over the Esso bulk dealer site. After observing the craft, the witnesses returned to their car and drove two blocks to a nearby house to retrieve a camera. Upon returning to the location of the sighting, the witnesses observed the object departing the area, heading in a southerly direction. 

In addition to the primary event, Louise Litwin provided follow-up information regarding a separate, unreported sighting. She noted that on the night of Monday, October 18, 1976, a local farmer in the area had also observed a UFO, though that individual chose not to file an official report at the time.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a single, disc-shaped craft featuring a dome on its top. It was equipped with two bright lights, which displayed green and red colors. Throughout the 10 to 15-minute duration of the observation, the witnesses reported that the object made no noise. Its movement was characterized by an initial hovering phase over the Esso bulk dealer, followed by a departure toward the south.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The documentation consists of witness accounts provided by Louise Litwin and Lori Heward regarding the October 21 event. The records note the specific location of the sighting (the Esso Bulk Dealer) and the witnesses' attempt to document the object via camera. The file also includes the anecdotal report provided by Louise Litwin concerning a previous, unreported sighting by a local farmer on October 18, 1976, which serves as contextual background for the activity in the Chaplin area during that week.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 路易丝·利特温 (Louise Litwin)、洛里·休厄德 (Lori Heward)

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年10月21日，约 0300Z（协调世界时）

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省查普林 (Chaplin, Saskatchewan)（具体位于埃索 (Esso) 散装经销商附近）

**目击经过：**
1976年10月21日约 0300Z，目击者路易丝·利特温和洛里·休厄德在萨斯喀彻温省查普林镇观察到一种不明空中现象。目击者最初是在埃索散装经销商附近发现该物体的。整个目击过程持续了约10到15分钟。

在目击过程中，目击者走下车，以便更清楚地观察悬停在埃索散装经销商上方的物体。观察完飞行器后，目击者回到车内，驱车前往两个街区外的一处住宅取相机。当她们返回目击地点时，发现该物体正向南方飞离。

除此次主要事件外，路易丝·利特温还提供了关于另一起未公开目击事件的后续信息。她提到，1976年10月18日星期一晚上，当地的一位农场主也观察到了一个不明飞行物，但该当事人当时选择不提交正式报告。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为一个圆盘状的飞行器，顶部有一个圆顶。它配备了两盏明亮的灯，分别显示出绿色和红色。在10到15分钟的观察过程中，目击者称该物体没有发出任何声音。其运动特征表现为先在埃索散装经销商上方悬停，随后向南方离去。

**调查/后续：**
相关档案包含路易丝·利特温和洛里·休厄德关于10月21日事件的证词。记录指出了目击的具体地点（埃索散装经销商）以及目击者试图用相机记录该物体的过程。档案中还包括路易丝·利特温提供的轶事报告，内容涉及当地农场主在1976年10月18日的一次未公开目击事件，这为该周查普林地区的活动提供了背景参考。

**目击者：** 拉尔夫·张伯伦 (Ralph Chamberlain)。

**地点：** 密歇根州迪尔伯恩市，福特汽车公司。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. M. Ritchie

**Date / Time:** January 21, 1976, at 2100 hours local time; observation lasted until 2120 hours; object disappeared by 2200 hours.

**Location:** 19 miles west of Grande Prairie, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 21, 1976, at approximately 2100 hours, Mrs. M. Ritchie observed an unidentified object while located 19 miles west of Grande Prairie, Alberta. The object was positioned due east of the observer’s location. Throughout the duration of the sighting, which lasted from 2100 hours until 2120 hours, the object remained stationary. In addition to the primary object, Mrs. Ritchie observed an aircraft landing from the north. The object was no longer visible to the observer by 2200 hours.

**Object:** The object was described as a stationary entity that exhibited a pulsating effect and continuously changed colors. While the report distinguishes between the "object" and an "aircraft" observed landing from the north, both were noted during the same observation window.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official documentation of the event includes a CIRVIS (Communication Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report. Following the investigation into the details provided by Mrs. Ritchie, the official assessment noted a suspicion that the sighting was likely a satellite observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** M. 里奇夫人 (Mrs. M. Ritchie)

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年1月21日，当地时间21:00；观测持续至21:20；物体于22:00消失。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省大草原城 (Grande Prairie) 以西19英里处。

**目击经过：** 1976年1月21日晚约21:00，M. 里奇夫人在阿尔伯塔省大草原城以西19英里处观测到一个不明物体。该物体位于观测者正东方。在21:00至21:20的整个观测期间，该物体保持静止状态。除该主要物体外，里奇夫人还观察到一架飞机从北面降落。至22:00时，观测者已无法再看到该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个静止的实体，呈现出脉动效果并不断变换颜色。虽然报告将该“物体”与从北面降落的“飞机”进行了区分，但两者均在同一观测窗口内被记录。

**调查/后续：** 该事件的官方记录包含一份 CIRVIS（重要情报目击报告通信指令）报告。在对里奇夫人提供的细节进行调查后，官方评估指出，该目击事件极有可能是对卫星的观测。

**Witnesses:** The author and a neighbor, Mr. Evans of 1658 Grant.

**Sighting:** On the 26th at 8:45 PM, a disk was observed over Lake St. Clair. When viewed through a telescope, it appeared as a 'K type' (round clock face looking) object, blue and white, moving into space. Mr. Evans observed blinking lights on a regular disk with rotating lights, which he described as a saucer. On March 31, the author observed an object toward Monroe over Wyandotte, initially appearing as an evening star. When viewed through a 700mm telescope, it appeared as a small reddish-colored dot moving in short circles. It was later identified as an 'E type' saucer, round and bluish with white lights.

**Object:** Described as 'K type' and 'E type' saucers, featuring rotating lights, blue/white colors, and reddish dots.

**Aftermath:** The report includes handwritten notes regarding telescope focal length and particle movement, and bears a received stamp from the N.R.C. Records Services dated April 8, 1976.

**Additional pages:** Inherited-stamp cluster — pages 12 of the same file fall between FOIA record stamps and belong to **N76/026**.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 作者本人及住在Grant街1658号的邻居Evans先生。

**目击：** 26日晚8点45分，圣克莱尔湖上空出现一个圆盘状物体。通过望远镜观察，它呈现为“K型”（类似钟面），呈蓝白色，正向太空移动。Evans先生观察到该圆盘带有旋转灯光，并称其为飞碟。3月31日，作者观察到怀恩多特（Wyandotte）方向门罗（Monroe）上空有一个物体，起初看起来像一颗晚星。当使用700毫米望远镜观察时，它表现为一个在短圆周内移动的小红点。该物体随后被识别为“E型”飞碟，呈圆形，带有蓝色和白色灯光。

**物体：** 被描述为“K型”和“E型”飞碟，具有旋转灯光、蓝白色外观及红色光点。

**后续：** 报告包含关于望远镜焦距和粒子运动的手写笔记，并盖有加拿大国家研究委员会（N.R.C.）记录服务处1976年4月8日的收件章。

**其它相关页面：** 依据 FOIA 编号传递规则，本文件第 12 页位于两个 N 编号戳之间，归属于记录 **N76/026**。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Guthro and 12 unnamed individuals.

**Date / Time:** July 23, 1976, at 11:25 local time.

**Location:** Ben-Eion Beach, looking towards Big Pond.

**Sighting:** On July 23, 1976, at 11:25 local time, a sighting occurred at Ben-Eion Beach. Mr. Guthro, acting as the primary observer, was situated on the beach looking in the direction of Big Pond. He was accompanied by 12 other individuals who also witnessed the event. The sighting took place on a clear day and lasted for a total duration of one and a half hours. According to the accounts provided by the group, the object was observed at a very high altitude, heading in a northward direction. The witnesses reported that the object performed maneuvers, specifically circling around the perimeter of the area, and exhibited a behavior described as "coming and going" throughout the duration of the sighting before eventually departing.

**Object:** The object was described as being reddish-blue in color. It maintained a very high altitude throughout the observation. Regarding its movement, the object traveled northward, circled the perimeter of the observation area, and displayed a pattern of "coming and going." The total duration of the sighting was one and a half hours.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report regarding the Ben-Eion Beach sighting was formally documented and transmitted from CFS (Canadian Forces Station) Sydney to the National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa. Additionally, the report was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 古思罗（Guthro）先生及12名未具名人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年7月23日，当地时间11:25。

**地点：** 本-伊恩海滩（Ben-Eion Beach），朝大池塘（Big Pond）方向望去。

**目击经过：** 1976年7月23日当地时间11:25，本-伊恩海滩发生了一起目击事件。古思罗先生作为主要观察者，当时正位于海滩上，面向大池塘方向。与他同行的还有其他12名目击者。目击事件发生在一个晴朗的日子，持续时间总计一个半小时。据该群体描述，该物体处于极高空，正向北飞行。目击者报告称，该物体执行了机动动作，具体表现为在区域周边盘旋，并在整个目击过程中呈现出“来回往复”的行为，最终离开。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为呈红蓝色。在整个观测过程中，它始终保持在极高的高度。关于其运动轨迹，该物体向北飞行，绕着观测区域周边盘旋，并表现出“来回往复”的移动模式。目击持续时间总计一个半小时。

**调查/后续：** 关于本-伊恩海滩目击事件的报告已正式记录，并由悉尼加拿大武装部队基地（CFS Sydney）传达至位于渥太华的国防总部（NDHQ）。此外，该报告还被转交至渥太华的国家研究委员会（NRC）进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Howard Trotter (age 18), Reginald Trotter, Elmer Trotter, and unnamed neighbours.

**Date / Time:** May 2, 1976 (discovery of the site); May 12, 1976 (reporting and official investigation).

**Location:** A field north of the Trotter farm, Madoc, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On May 2, 1976, Howard Trotter discovered three large, anomalous holes in a pasture field located north of the family farmhouse while moving cattle. The discovery was subsequently inspected by Reginald Trotter, Elmer Trotter, and several neighbours, none of whom could provide a logical explanation for the markings. On May 12, 1976, Elmer Trotter formally reported the findings to CFB Trenton. An official investigation conducted that same day confirmed the presence of the three holes. The site was noted for its isolation; the field had not been plowed for five years, there were no vehicle tracks in the vicinity, and the lack of roads or neighboring farms to the north made vehicular access to the site effectively impossible.

**Object:** The physical evidence consisted of three distinct holes in the ground. Detailed measurements recorded during the investigation were as follows: one hole measured 11' x 3'7", a second measured 3'9" x 2'9", and the third measured 4' x 4'4". The holes ranged from 8 to 10 inches in depth. A notable feature of the site was that the sod removed from the holes appeared completely intact, as if it had been cleanly lifted out. Furthermore, investigators observed that neither the sod itself nor the soil at the bottom of the holes showed any signs of depression or compression, suggesting the material had been removed without the application of heavy downward pressure.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented in an Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) Supplementary Report. Official follow-up included the creation of a diagram detailing the relative positions and specific dimensions of the three holes. Photographs were taken of each individual hole, including close-ups of the removed sod sections and general location shots to document the surrounding terrain. Following the investigation, Major Karess of Base Operations at CFB Trenton, Ontario, requested a formal copy of the report for official review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 霍华德·特罗特（Howard Trotter，18岁）、雷金纳德·特罗特（Reginald Trotter）、埃尔默·特罗特（Elmer Trotter）及几位未具名的邻居。

**日期：** 1976年5月2日（发现现场）；1976年5月12日（报告及官方调查）。

**地点：** 安大略省马多克（Madoc），特罗特农场北侧的一片田地。

**目击经过：** 1976年5月2日，霍华德·特罗特在转移牛群时，发现自家农舍北侧的牧场上有三个巨大的异常坑洞。随后，雷金纳德·特罗特、埃尔默·特罗特及几位邻居对现场进行了查看，但无人能对这些痕迹给出合理的解释。1976年5月12日，埃尔默·特罗特正式向特伦顿加拿大军队基地（CFB Trenton）报告了这一发现。当天进行的官方调查证实了这三个坑洞的存在。该地点位置偏僻，这片田地已五年未曾耕种，附近没有任何车辆行驶的痕迹，且由于北面没有道路或邻近农场，车辆实际上根本无法到达该现场。

**物体描述：** 实物证据为地面上的三个明显坑洞。调查期间记录的详细尺寸如下：第一个坑洞为11英尺 x 3英尺7英寸，第二个为3英尺9英寸 x 2英尺9英寸，第三个为4英尺 x 4英尺4英寸。坑洞深度在8到10英寸之间。该现场的一个显著特征是，从坑洞中取出的草皮看起来完好无损，仿佛是被整齐地提走了一样。此外，调查人员观察到，无论是草皮本身还是坑底的土壤，都没有任何下陷或受压的迹象，这表明这些物质是在没有施加巨大向下压力的情况下被移除的。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被记录在安大略省省警（OPP）的补充报告中。官方后续行动包括绘制了一份详细说明三个坑洞相对位置和具体尺寸的图表。调查人员对每个坑洞进行了拍照，包括被移除草皮部分的特写以及记录周围地形的现场全景照。调查结束后，安大略省特伦顿加拿大军队基地作战部的卡雷斯少校（Major Karess）索要了一份正式报告副本，以供官方审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Rachelle Pilon (also referred to as Rachel Pilon), Marcel Poliquin

**Date / Time:** May 15, 1976, at 20:15 hours EDT

**Location:** Roadside near Napierreville, Quebec

**Sighting:** On the evening of May 15, 1976, Rachelle Pilon and Marcel Poliquin were stopped on the side of a roadway near Napierreville, Quebec, when they observed an unidentified object in the clear night sky. The sighting lasted for approximately 20 minutes. According to the accounts provided by the witnesses, the object moved in circular patterns and traveled in a southerly direction toward the United States border. 

**Object:** The object was described as having the shape of an inverted pail. It displayed red and green coloration. While initial reports placed the object at an altitude of approximately 5,000 feet, subsequent follow-up documentation corrected this estimate to an approximate height of 500 feet. The object made no sound during the duration of the sighting. The witnesses were unable to provide a specific description of the object's physical size.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** This case was initiated following a telex dated May 16, 1976. The witnesses, Rachelle Pilon (DOB 28-2-55) and Marcel Poliquin (DOB 23-12-52), were interviewed by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). During the interrogation, the RCMP specifically noted that the subjects stated they do not use alcohol or drugs. The investigating officer remarked that while the witnesses appeared frank and sincere in their belief that they had observed an anomalous phenomenon, the investigator personally concluded that the incident remained questionable. No further physical evidence or sketches were noted in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 拉谢尔·皮隆（Rachelle Pilon，亦作 Rachel Pilon）、马塞尔·波利坎（Marcel Poliquin）

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年5月15日，东部夏令时间 20:15

**地点：** 魁北克省纳皮耶维尔（Napierreville）附近路边

**目击经过：** 1976年5月15日晚，拉谢尔·皮隆和马塞尔·波利坎在魁北克省纳皮耶维尔附近的路边停车时，在晴朗的夜空中观察到一个不明物体。目击过程持续了约20分钟。据目击者描述，该物体呈圆形轨迹移动，并向南方的美国边境方向飞去。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为倒置的桶状，呈现红色和绿色。虽然最初的报告称该物体高度约为5000英尺，但后续的记录文件将此估算值修正为约500英尺。在整个目击过程中，该物体未发出任何声音。目击者无法提供该物体具体物理尺寸的描述。

**调查/后续：** 本案始于1976年5月16日的一份电传。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对目击者拉谢尔·皮隆（出生日期：1955年2月28日）和马塞尔·波利坎（出生日期：1952年12月23日）进行了访谈。在问询过程中，加拿大皇家骑警特别记录了当事人声明他们不饮酒也不吸毒。调查警官指出，虽然目击者在坚信自己观察到了异常现象时表现得坦率且真诚，但调查员个人认为该事件仍存疑。所提供的档案中未记录任何进一步的物证或草图。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** One civilian observer (name redacted), Edouard Montpetit.

**Date / Time:** May 15, 1976, at 20:15 EDT.

**Location:** Roadside near Napierville, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On the evening of May 15, 1976, at approximately 20:15 EDT, two witnesses—a civilian observer (whose name is redacted) and Edouard Montpetit—were stopped on the side of a roadway near Napierville, Quebec. Both witnesses reported observing a singular unidentified aerial phenomenon under clear sky conditions. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately 20 minutes. According to the accounts, the object performed circular motions in the sky before eventually traveling in a southerly direction toward the United States border.

**Object:** The object was described as being shaped like an inverted pail. It featured a color scheme of red and green. The witnesses estimated the object’s altitude to be approximately 5,000 feet. The object was noted for its silent flight, as it did not emit any noise during the observation. While the witnesses were able to provide details regarding the object's shape, color, and movement, they were unable to provide a specific estimate regarding its physical size.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of two separate reports (Page 225 and Page 226) detailing the same event. Both reports confirm the clear weather conditions at the time of the sighting and corroborate the specific details regarding the object's appearance, altitude, and flight path. No further official investigation notes, sketches, or RCMP follow-up actions were provided in the provided pages.

**目击经过：** 1976年5月15日傍晚，约东部夏令时间 20:15，两名目击者——一名平民观察员（姓名已删减）和爱德华·蒙佩蒂特，在魁北克省纳皮尔维尔附近的路边停车。两位目击者均报告称，在晴朗的天空下观察到了一个单一的不明空中现象。目击过程持续了大约20分钟。据描述，该物体在天空中进行了圆周运动，随后向南朝着美国边境方向飞去。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为形状像一个倒置的桶。其配色方案为红色和绿色。目击者估计该物体的高度约为5,000英尺。值得注意的是，该物体飞行时保持静默，在观察期间未发出任何声音。虽然目击者能够提供有关物体形状、颜色和运动的细节，但无法对其具体物理尺寸做出估计。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案由两份详细记录同一事件的独立报告（第225页和第226页）组成。两份报告均证实了目击发生时天气状况晴朗，并相互印证了关于物体外观、高度和飞行路径的具体细节。所提供的页面中未包含进一步的官方调查记录、草图或加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 的后续行动信息。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Barbara McPherson, John Walker, Karl Halloran, Fred Phillips, Gerald Brown, Sandy Morrison.

**Date / Time:** May 18, 1976; sightings reported at 22:00 GMT and 23:00 GMT.

**Location:** Sydney, Nova Scotia (specific locations noted: 297 Rotary Drive, 555 Esplanade St, 226 Rockdale Avenue, Westmount Road towards Point Edward).

**Sighting:** Two distinct observation windows were recorded regarding the event on May 18, 1976. The first group of witnesses, Barbara McPherson and John Walker, observed an object for 45 minutes starting at 22:00 GMT. They reported the object remained stationary at a very high altitude. When a nearby aircraft approached the object, it reacted by moving straight up and out of sight. 

A second group of witnesses—Karl Halloran, Fred Phillips, Gerald Brown, and Sandy Morrison—observed an object at 23:00 GMT. This group reported the object moving north on Westmount Road toward Point Edward. Their observation lasted for approximately 5 minutes. During this time, the object remained stationary in the air, exhibiting a tipping motion back and forth before eventually departing in a straight line.

**Object:** The descriptions of the object vary between the two witness groups. McPherson and Walker described a single object shaped like four round discs joined together, black in color, and surrounded by a grey mist. 

Halloran, Phillips, Brown, and Morrison described the object as an aluminum disc with a ball in the center. They noted that the object changed color, turning orange several times before reverting to its original aluminum color. The object was described as stationary, tipping back and forth, and capable of rapid, straight-line departure.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was formally documented and transmitted from CFS Sydney to the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCCWC) at NDHQ Ottawa. The report was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) for the Radio and Electrical Engineering Division for further review. Weather conditions at the time of the 23:00 GMT sighting were recorded as clear with few clouds.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 芭芭拉·麦克弗森 (Barbara McPherson)、约翰·沃克 (John Walker)、卡尔·哈洛兰 (Karl Halloran)、弗雷德·菲利普斯 (Fred Phillips)、杰拉德·布朗 (Gerald Brown)、桑迪·莫里森 (Sandy Morrison)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年5月18日；目击报告时间分别为格林威治标准时间 (GMT) 22:00 和 23:00。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省悉尼市（具体地点包括：Rotary大道297号、Esplanade街555号、Rockdale大道226号，以及通往爱德华角 (Point Edward) 的韦斯特蒙特路 (Westmount Road)）。

**目击经过：** 1976年5月18日的事件记录了两个不同的观察窗口。第一组目击者芭芭拉·麦克弗森和约翰·沃克从格林威治标准时间22:00开始观察到一个物体，持续了45分钟。他们报告称，该物体在高空保持静止。当附近一架飞机靠近该物体时，它做出反应，径直向上移动并消失在视野中。

第二组目击者——卡尔·哈洛兰、弗雷德·菲利普斯、杰拉德·布朗和桑迪·莫里森在格林威治标准时间23:00观察到了一个物体。该组报告称，物体沿韦斯特蒙特路向北朝爱德华角方向移动。他们的观察持续了约5分钟。在此期间，物体在空中保持静止，呈现出前后倾斜的动作，随后沿直线离开。

**物体描述：** 两组目击者对物体的描述有所不同。麦克弗森和沃克描述该物体为一个由四个圆形圆盘连接而成的单一物体，呈黑色，周围环绕着灰色雾气。

哈洛兰、菲利普斯、布朗和莫里森则将该物体描述为一个中心带有球体的铝制圆盘。他们注意到该物体会变色，多次变为橙色，随后又恢复为原来的铝色。该物体被描述为处于静止状态，会前后倾斜，并能够进行快速的直线飞行离开。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被正式记录，并由悉尼加拿大武装部队基地 (CFS Sydney) 传达至渥太华国防总部 (NDHQ) 的救援协调中心 (RCCWC)。报告随后被转发至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 的无线电与电气工程部门进行进一步审查。据记录，格林威治标准时间23:00目击事件发生时的天气状况为晴朗，少云。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lionel Botte, J.C. Hotte, Sandra Bourque, Claudette Saberge, and two additional anonymous individuals.

**Date / Time:** June 1, July 6, and July 7, 1976, between 3:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. (with a possible additional sighting on August 21, 1976).

**Location:** Ottawa, Ontario. Sightings were reported in two specific areas: above the Rideau Canal between Parliament and the Chateau Laurier (near the former railway site) and over the Rideau River between Sussex and St. Patrick streets, near the Minto bridges.

**Sighting:** A series of recurring aerial phenomena were observed by multiple witnesses over the course of the summer of 1976. Lionel Botte and two anonymous witnesses reported observing an object hovering over the Rideau Canal area during the afternoon hours. Simultaneously, J.C. Hotte, Sandra Bourque, and Claudette Saberge reported observing a strange phenomenon over the Rideau River near the Minto bridges. While the witnesses provided varying accounts, the consensus among the group was that the objects did not conform to conventional aircraft or natural phenomena. The author of the report (J.C. Hotte) expressed caution in labeling the objects as "flying saucers" or "extraterrestrial," yet maintained that no conventional explanation could account for the sightings.

**Object:** The object was described as having a distinct shell-like, elongated almond shape. It featured a pattern of stripes and was marked by lighter, circular features resembling portholes. The color scheme was noted as black and white, and the object exhibited a high degree of brightness. Regarding movement and sound, the reports emphasize the object's presence in the sky during the mid-afternoon, though specific details regarding propulsion or auditory output were not explicitly recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The events gained public attention following an open letter published in the newspaper *Le Droit* on July 2, 1976, written by J.C. Hotte. Following the public discourse, a formal report was filed by Annie Claude on August 5, 1976, at 11:30 a.m. to document the accounts of Lionel Botte and the other witnesses. The investigation notes that while multiple witnesses were involved, their accounts differed slightly in detail, though they remained consistent regarding the timeframe and the general nature of the observed phenomena.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 莱昂内尔·博特（Lionel Botte）、J.C. 霍特（J.C. Hotte）、桑德拉·布尔克（Sandra Bourque）、克劳黛特·萨伯格（Claudette Saberge），以及另外两名匿名人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年6月1日、7月6日及7月7日，下午3:00至5:00之间（8月21日可能还有一次目击）。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华。目击报告集中在两个特定区域：国会大厦与劳里埃城堡酒店（Chateau Laurier）之间的里多运河上方（靠近原铁路遗址），以及萨塞克斯街（Sussex）与圣帕特里克街（St. Patrick）之间、靠近明托桥（Minto bridges）的里多河上方。

**目击经过：** 1976年夏季，多名目击者观察到了一系列反复出现的空中现象。莱昂内尔·博特和两名匿名目击者报告称，在午后时分观察到一个物体悬停在里多运河区域上空。与此同时，J.C. 霍特、桑德拉·布尔克和克劳黛特·萨伯格报告称，在靠近明托桥的里多河上空观察到了奇怪的现象。尽管目击者提供的描述各不相同，但该群体的共识是，这些物体不符合常规飞行器或自然现象的特征。报告作者（J.C. 霍特）在将这些物体标记为“飞碟”或“外星飞行器”时持谨慎态度，但坚称没有任何常规解释可以说明这些目击事件。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为具有独特的壳状、细长的杏仁形状。其表面带有条纹图案，并有类似舷窗的较亮圆形特征。配色方案为黑白相间，且物体表现出极高的亮度。关于运动和声音，报告强调了该物体在午后出现在天空中的情况，但未明确记录有关推进方式或声音输出的具体细节。

**调查/后续：** 1976年7月2日，J.C. 霍特在《权利报》（Le Droit）上发表了一封公开信，使这些事件引起了公众关注。在引发公众讨论后，安妮·克劳德（Annie Claude）于1976年8月5日上午11:30提交了一份正式报告，记录了莱昂内尔·博特及其他目击者的陈述。调查指出，尽管涉及多名目击者，但他们的陈述在细节上略有出入，不过在时间范围和所观察现象的一般性质上保持了一致。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mark Kopecky and his daughter Kristy.

**后续：** Kopecky 将这张宝丽来照片带到了《Record-Herald》报社。文章还提到了威斯康星州 Elmwood 发生的另一起目击事件，涉及一名名为 George Wheeler 的警官。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Cliff Bennett, a salesman, along with two other employees of Suburban Motors, Douglas Murphy and Michael McKenna.

**Sighting:** On June 7, 1976, at 2010 GMT, Mr. Bennett observed objects while at Suburban Motors in Victoria. The objects appeared at an altitude of 500-1000 feet, performing random maneuvers in both vertical and horizontal planes. They were described as having a khaki-colored underside with minimal reflective properties, while the top was highly reflective like chrome. The objects appeared to be the size of large birds with a swept-back gull wing configuration, featuring rows of vents and what appeared to be a nozzle or jet exhaust. A second object, a perfect sphere with a white corona, was sighted at 2020 GMT, remaining stationary for 45 minutes before moving NW by W.

**Object:** The primary objects were described as having no fuselage, thin wings, and vents. The secondary object was a sphere with the reflective index of a bright moon.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 销售员克里夫·贝内特（Cliff Bennett）先生，以及另外两名郊区汽车公司（Suburban Motors）的员工道格拉斯·墨菲（Douglas Murphy）和迈克尔·麦肯纳（Michael McKenna）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Art McKay (residing at 12 Gilbert St., Belleville, Ontario)

**Date / Time:** June 17, 1976, at 1559Z

**Location:** Near Thomasburg, Ontario, on Highway 37

**Sighting:** On June 17, 1976, at 1559Z, Mr. Art McKay was traveling on Highway 37 near Thomasburg when he observed an unidentified object. The weather conditions at the time were reported as partly cloudy. Upon spotting the object, Mr. McKay stopped his vehicle to get a better look and to listen for any auditory cues. He remained stationary to observe the object’s behavior as it traversed his field of vision. Despite his proximity and the object's low altitude, he reported hearing absolutely no noise emanating from it. Furthermore, he noted that the object left no exhaust or vapor trails behind it during its transit. The entire observation lasted approximately 35 seconds from the moment the object entered his field of vision until it disappeared.

**Object:** The object was described as being approximately the size of a Piper Cub aircraft. It was silvery in color and appeared very bright, effectively reflecting the sunlight. The object was flying at a very low altitude and was moving at an extremely high rate of speed—notably appearing to travel faster than any jet aircraft flights the witness had previously observed. The object maintained a consistent appearance throughout the 35-second duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of multiple reports detailing the account of Mr. Art McKay. Official records confirm the date, time, and location of the sighting, as well as the specific environmental conditions (partly cloudy). The investigation notes emphasize the witness's specific observations regarding the lack of engine noise and the absence of any propulsion trails, as well as the comparative speed of the object against known jet aircraft. No further official follow-up or identification of the object was recorded in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 阿特·麦凯先生（Art McKay，居住于安大略省贝尔维尔市吉尔伯特街12号）

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年6月17日，15:59Z（协调世界时）

**地点：** 安大略省托马斯堡（Thomasburg）附近的37号高速公路

**目击经过：** 1976年6月17日15:59Z，阿特·麦凯先生在托马斯堡附近的37号高速公路上行驶时，观察到一个不明物体。据报告，当时的天气状况为局部多云。发现该物体后，麦凯先生停下车以便更仔细地观察，并试图听取是否有任何声音信号。他保持静止状态，观察该物体穿过其视野时的动态。尽管距离很近且物体飞行高度较低，但他报告称完全没有听到该物体发出任何声音。此外，他还注意到该物体在飞行过程中没有留下任何尾气或蒸汽轨迹。从物体进入视野到消失，整个观察过程持续了约35秒。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为大约有一架派珀幼兽（Piper Cub）飞机大小。它呈银色，看起来非常明亮，能有效反射阳光。该物体以极低的高度飞行，且移动速度极快——据目击者称，其飞行速度明显快于他此前观察过的任何喷气式飞机。在35秒的目击过程中，该物体的外观始终保持一致。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案包含多份详细记录阿特·麦凯先生陈述的报告。官方记录证实了目击事件的日期、时间和地点，以及当时具体的环境状况（局部多云）。调查记录强调了目击者关于该物体没有引擎噪音、没有推进轨迹，以及与已知喷气式飞机相比其速度极快的具体观察结果。在提供的文件中，未记录到针对该物体的进一步官方后续调查或身份确认。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Rick Lean, located at 925 2nd Ave, NE, Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on June 19, 1976. The observer reported an object with a red light on the top and bottom. The lights pulsated, becoming brighter, and then turned green. The object moved very slowly, covering approximately 20-30 miles in 15-20 minutes. The total duration of the sighting was 20 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as being 30 or 40 feet off the ground.

**Aftermath:** The observer stated there was no known aircraft in the vicinity at the time of the sighting.

**Additional pages:** This incident is also documented on 1 other page of the FOIA release.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Toulain Sabian, Mr. John Oconner, Miss Francine Hall, Mr. Walter Farrell.

**Date / Time:** June 21, 1976, at 0330Z (Sabian, Oconner, Hall); June 23, 1976, at 2152Z (Farrell).

**Location:** Gillis Lake, 16 miles east of Sydney, Nova Scotia, off the Coxheath Highway; Sydney, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** 
The case file documents two distinct sighting events reported in the Sydney, Nova Scotia area during June 1976. 

The first event occurred on June 21, 1976, at 0330Z near Gillis Lake, 16 miles east of Sydney, off the Coxheath Highway. Witnesses Mr. Toulain Sabian, Mr. John Oconner, and Miss Francine Hall reported observing an unidentified object under clear weather conditions. The witnesses observed the object hovering approximately 100 yards above the ground for a duration of one and a half hours. During this time, the object was noted to flash on and off.

The second event occurred on June 23, 1976, at 2152Z in Sydney, Nova Scotia. Witness Mr. Walter Farrell reported observing an object that appeared similar to a star. The object was positioned at a very high altitude and was observed moving in a trajectory from north to south. The duration of this sighting was approximately 2 minutes.

**Object:** 
The objects described in these two reports differ significantly in appearance and behavior. 

The Gillis Lake object (June 21) was described as blue in color and oval-shaped. It measured approximately 30 feet across. Its primary movement was hovering, and it exhibited a flashing light pattern (on and off) while remaining stationary for 90 minutes. 

The Sydney object (June 23) was described as looking like a star. It was observed at a very high altitude and maintained a steady movement from north to south. No sound was reported for either object.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Following the June 21 sighting, the report was formally transmitted from CFS Sydney to NDHQ (National Defence Headquarters) in Ottawa and the National Research Council for the Radio and Electrical Engineering Division. 

Regarding the June 23 sighting reported by Mr. Walter Farrell, official follow-up confirmed that there was no corresponding radar sighting recorded at the time of the observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 图兰·萨比安先生 (Mr. Toulain Sabian)、约翰·奥康纳先生 (Mr. John Oconner)、弗朗辛·霍尔小姐 (Miss Francine Hall)、沃尔特·法雷尔先生 (Mr. Walter Farrell)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年6月21日，0330Z（萨比安、奥康纳、霍尔）；1976年6月23日，2152Z（法雷尔）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省悉尼市以东16英里处，考克斯希思公路 (Coxheath Highway) 旁的吉利斯湖 (Gillis Lake)；新斯科舍省悉尼市。

**目击经过：**
该档案记录了1976年6月在新斯科舍省悉尼地区报告的两起截然不同的目击事件。

第一起事件发生在1976年6月21日0330Z，地点位于悉尼以东16英里、考克斯希思公路旁的吉利斯湖附近。目击者图兰·萨比安先生、约翰·奥康纳先生和弗朗辛·霍尔小姐报告称，在天气晴朗的情况下观察到了一个不明物体。目击者观察到该物体在离地约100码（约91米）的高度悬停了一个半小时。在此期间，该物体被注意到在不断地闪烁。

第二起事件发生在1976年6月23日2152Z，地点位于新斯科舍省悉尼市。目击者沃尔特·法雷尔先生报告称观察到一个看起来像星星的物体。该物体位于极高空，并被观察到沿南北轨迹移动。此次目击持续时间约为2分钟。

**物体描述：**
这两份报告中描述的物体在外形和行为上存在显著差异。

吉利斯湖物体（6月21日）被描述为蓝色、椭圆形。其直径约为30英尺（约9米）。其主要运动方式为悬停，并在保持静止的90分钟内呈现出闪烁（开/关）的光模式。

悉尼物体（6月23日）被描述为看起来像一颗星星。它在极高空被观察到，并保持着从北向南的稳定移动。两起目击事件中均未报告有声音。

**调查/后续：**
在6月21日的目击事件发生后，该报告由悉尼加拿大武装部队基地 (CFS Sydney) 正式转交至渥太华的国防总部 (NDHQ) 以及国家研究委员会无线电与电气工程部门。

关于沃尔特·法雷尔先生报告的6月23日的目击事件，官方后续调查确认，在观察当时并未记录到相应的雷达回波。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_10_-_Pages_27.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Samual Robichaud.

**Sighting:** The witness reported an object observed on June 28, 1976, at 0210Z. The weather conditions were cloudy. The witness observed the object through binoculars.

**Object:** The object displayed bright white lights at both the front and back, creating a headlight effect. There was a smaller white light in the center that emitted a lesser glow. The approximate size was comparable to a large passenger plane. The object made no sound and remained stationary in the sky for over 20 minutes.
