CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p014.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian witness (referenced in both reports)

**Date / Time:** December 11, 2011, at 1000z; December 24, 2011, at 1000z; and January 1, 2012, at 0113z.

**Location:** Quebec City, Quebec.

**Sighting:** The documentation consists of reports relayed via telephone from the Montreal Area Control Centre (ACC) regarding a civilian witness who observed anomalous aerial phenomena over Quebec City. The witness reported observing three bright, stationary lights in the sky on three separate occasions. The first reported sighting occurred on December 11, 2011, at 1000z. A subsequent report from the same witness indicates a sighting on December 24, 2011, at 1000z. A final sighting was reported by the same individual on January 1, 2012, at 0113z. In all instances, the witness described the objects as remaining stationary in the sky.

**Object:** The object is described consistently across all reports as "three bright lights." The lights were noted for their lack of movement, remaining stationary in the sky during each observation. No specific size, color (other than "bright"), sound, or structural details were provided in the logs.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The reports were formally logged as part of the daily operations records. The information was received by the reporting agency via a phone call from the Montreal ACC. The January 1, 2012, entry specifically notes that the report was logged as part of the daily operations log on that date. There is no mention of further investigation, RCMP involvement, or meteorological analysis in the provided pages.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p014.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名平民目击者（两份报告中均有提及）

**日期 / 时间：** 2011年12月11日 1000z；2011年12月24日 1000z；以及2012年1月1日 0113z。

**地点：** 魁北克省魁北克市。

**目击经过：** 相关文档包含通过蒙特利尔区域管制中心（ACC）电话转达的报告，内容涉及一名平民目击者在魁北克市上空观测到的异常空中现象。该目击者报告称，在三个不同的时间点观测到了天空中出现三个明亮且静止的光点。第一次目击报告发生在2011年12月11日 1000z。同一目击者随后的报告指出，在2011年12月24日 1000z再次观测到该现象。最后一次目击由该个人于2012年1月1日 0113z报告。在所有案例中，目击者均描述这些物体在天空中保持静止状态。

**物体描述：** 在所有报告中，该物体被一致描述为“三个明亮的光点”。这些光点的显著特征是缺乏移动，在每次观测期间都保持在天空中静止不动。记录中未提供关于其具体尺寸、颜色（除“明亮”外）、声音或结构细节的信息。

**调查/后续：** 这些报告作为日常运营记录的一部分被正式归档。报告机构通过蒙特利尔区域管制中心的电话接收了相关信息。2012年1月1日的条目特别注明，该报告已作为当日日常运营日志的一部分进行了登记。所提供的文档中未提及任何进一步的调查、加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的介入或气象分析。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p012.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two aircraft crews (as reported by the Winnipeg Area Control Centre Shift Manager).

**Date / Time:** December 15, 2011, at 0530Z (initial sighting); 0738Z (reporting follow-up).

**Location:** Northwest of Winnipeg, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** At 0530Z, the Winnipeg Area Control Centre (Wpg ACC) Shift Manager received a CIRVIS (Communication Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report concerning an aerial phenomenon observed by two separate aircraft crews. Both crews reported witnessing a meteorite or fireball while flying in the airspace northwest of Winnipeg. The reports were treated as official intelligence sightings, necessitating formal documentation and escalation to military authorities.

**Object:** The object was described by the flight crews as a meteorite or a fireball. No further details regarding the object's specific shape, size, color, sound, movement, or duration were recorded in the provided documentation beyond this classification.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation process was handled through standard aviation reporting protocols. Following the receipt of the CIRVIS report from the Winnipeg ACC Shift Manager at 0530Z, the information was processed and subsequently faxed to the Canadian NORAD Region (CANR) at 0738Z for further review and military awareness. No additional sketches, weather data, or RCMP interrogation notes were included in the provided pages.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p012.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两组机组人员（据温尼伯区域管制中心值班经理报告）。

**日期 / 时间：** 2011年12月15日，0530Z（首次目击）；0738Z（后续报告）。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省温尼伯西北部。

**目击经过：** 0530Z，温尼伯区域管制中心（Wpg ACC）值班经理收到一份关于两组不同机组人员所观察到的空中现象的CIRVIS（报告重要情报目击事件的通信指令）报告。两组机组人员均报告称，在飞越温尼伯西北部空域时目击了一颗陨石或火球。这些报告被视为官方情报目击事件，需要进行正式记录并上报至军事当局。

**物体描述：** 机组人员将该物体描述为陨石或火球。除此分类外，提供的文档中未记录关于该物体具体形状、大小、颜色、声音、运动方式或持续时间的进一步细节。

**调查/后续：** 调查过程按照标准航空报告规程进行处理。在0530Z收到温尼伯区域管制中心值班经理提交的CIRVIS报告后，相关信息经过处理，并于0738Z传真至加拿大北美防空司令部区域（CANR）以供进一步审查及军事知悉。所提供的页面中未包含任何额外的草图、气象数据或加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的问询记录。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p028.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Anonymous (Montreal Area Control Centre staff)

**Date / Time:** June 22, 2013, at 0201z

**Location:** Montreal, Quebec

**Sighting:** 
On June 22, 2013, at 0201z, the Montreal Area Control Centre (ACC) received a report regarding an unidentified flying object. The sighting was documented by anonymous staff members at the ACC. According to the report, the object consisted of three distinct floating lights. These lights were observed performing complex aerial maneuvers, moving from east to west and subsequently reversing direction to travel from west to east. During the observation, the lights were seen separating into three individual entities before converging back together. The event concluded when the object disappeared over the horizon. The altitude of the object remained unknown throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** 
The object was described as three floating lights, characterized by orange, red, and white colors. The lights exhibited dynamic movement, specifically traveling east to west and west to east, with the ability to separate and rejoin. The duration of the sighting was sufficient for the witnesses to observe these distinct phases of movement and formation changes before the object vanished over the horizon. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The report of the sighting was formally forwarded to the Canadian Air Defence Sector (CADS) by the shift manager of the Montreal ACC via fax. The original documentation was submitted in French and subsequently translated into English by WO Passley and Capt Grignon. 

Meteorological data for the time and location of the event was recorded as follows: METAR CYQB 220200z 000000kt 15 sm SCT 250 17/10 A3018 RMK C12. This indicates calm wind conditions (000000kt), 15 statute miles of visibility, and scattered clouds at 25,000 feet, suggesting that the sighting occurred under clear, stable atmospheric conditions.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p028.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 匿名（蒙特利尔区域管制中心工作人员）

**日期 / 时间：** 2013年6月22日，02:01（协调世界时）

**地点：** 魁北克省蒙特利尔

**目击经过：**
2013年6月22日02:01（协调世界时），蒙特利尔区域管制中心（ACC）收到一份关于不明飞行物的报告。该目击事件由ACC的匿名工作人员记录。据报告称，该物体由三个明显的漂浮光点组成。这些光点被观察到进行了复杂的空中机动，先是从东向西移动，随后改变方向由西向东飞行。在观察过程中，这些光点被看到先是分离成三个独立的个体，随后又重新汇聚在一起。事件以该物体在地平线上消失而告终。在整个目击过程中，该物体的高度始终未知。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为三个漂浮的光点，呈现橙色、红色和白色。这些光点表现出动态的移动，具体表现为由东向西及由西向东的往返飞行，并具备分离和重组的能力。目击持续时间足够长，使目击者能够观察到这些明显的移动阶段和队形变化，随后物体在地平线上消失。报告中未提及任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
该目击报告由蒙特利尔区域管制中心的值班经理通过传真正式转发给加拿大防空部门（CADS）。原始文件以法语提交，随后由帕斯利准尉（WO Passley）和格里尼翁上尉（Capt Grignon）翻译成英语。

事件发生时当地的气象数据记录如下：METAR CYQB 220200z 000000kt 15 sm SCT 250 17/10 A3018 RMK C12。这表明当时风力平静（000000kt），能见度为15英里，25,000英尺高空有零散云层，说明目击事件发生时处于晴朗、稳定的大气条件下。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p032.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Toronto Control Centre shift manager, Unspecified witnesses (reporting parties)

**Date / Time:** 2013-10-02 at 0205z

**Location:** Toronto, Ontario

**Sighting:** At 0205z, the Toronto Control Centre shift manager received a report regarding an aerial sighting over Toronto. The report originated from unspecified witnesses who observed two distinct objects in the sky. The objects were seen moving at an extremely slow speed in a northwesterly direction. The witnesses noted that the objects maintained an altitude below 1000ft throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** The objects were described as two orange balls. When viewed together, they appeared to form a triangle or star shape. While the event was categorized in official documentation as a "meteorite/fireball," the description of the objects moving slowly at a low altitude (below 1000ft) distinguishes the account from typical high-velocity meteor activity.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Upon receiving the report from the reporting parties, the Toronto Control Centre shift manager initiated standard protocol. The information was formally documented and subsequently faxed to Transport Canada in strict accordance with Check list #16. No further investigative steps or physical evidence (such as sketches or weather data) were noted in the provided file pages beyond the initial reporting and inter-agency notification.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p032.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 多伦多控制中心值班经理，未具名目击者（报告方）

**日期 / 时间：** 2013年10月2日，02:05z

**地点：** 安大略省多伦多

**目击经过：** 02:05z，多伦多控制中心值班经理收到一份关于多伦多上空出现不明飞行物的报告。该报告来自观察到天空中出现两个独特物体的未具名目击者。据观察，这些物体以极慢的速度向西北方向移动。目击者指出，在整个目击过程中，这些物体始终保持在1000英尺以下的高度。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两个橙色的球体。当它们同时出现时，看起来像是一个三角形或星形。尽管该事件在官方文件中被归类为“陨石/火球”，但关于物体在低空（低于1000英尺）缓慢移动的描述，使其与典型的高速流星活动有所区别。

**调查/后续：** 在收到报告方的报告后，多伦多控制中心值班经理启动了标准程序。相关信息被正式记录，并随后严格按照第16号检查清单传真至加拿大交通部。在提供的文件页面中，除了初步报告和机构间通知外，未记录任何进一步的调查步骤或实物证据（如草图或气象数据）。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p034.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An individual and their wife.

**Date / Time:** October 12, 2013, at 20:27 local time (logged officially as October 13, 2013, at 01:15z).

**Location:** Keswick, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 12, 2013, at approximately 20:27 local time, an individual and their wife were at their residence in Keswick, Ontario, while watching the news. During this time, they observed an unidentified aerial object traveling across the sky. The witnesses reported that the object moved in a trajectory from the South to the North. The witnesses noted that the object maintained an elevation of 50–60 degrees from their viewpoint. Furthermore, the reporting party indicated that this event was not an isolated incident, noting a previous sighting in the same general area that occurred in July of the same year. The witnesses described the July event as being similar in nature to the October sighting, though the earlier object was observed to be lower in altitude and moving at a slower speed.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape and appeared entirely bright orange in color. It lacked any standard navigation lights. Regarding its flight characteristics, the object made no sound and traveled at an estimated speed of 500–600 mph, which the witnesses characterized as "jet speed." The physical size and exact distance of the object from the observers remain unknown.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report of the sighting was formally logged into the system at 01:15z on October 13, 2013. Following standard protocol for such reports, the documentation regarding the Keswick event was processed and transmitted via fax. No further investigative details, such as radar correlation or physical evidence, were noted in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p034.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一位男士及其妻子。

**日期 / 时间：** 2013年10月12日，当地时间20:27（官方记录时间为协调世界时2013年10月13日01:15）。

**地点：** 安大略省凯斯威克（Keswick）。

**目击经过：** 2013年10月12日晚约20:27，一位男士及其妻子在安大略省凯斯威克的家中观看新闻时，观察到一个不明飞行物体掠过天空。目击者称，该物体沿由南向北的轨迹飞行。据目击者观察，该物体保持在仰角50至60度的高度。此外，报告人指出这并非孤立事件，并提到同年7月在同一区域曾有过一次目击经历。目击者描述称，7月的事件与10月的目击情况性质相似，但当时观察到的物体飞行高度更低，速度也更慢。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，通体呈现明亮的橙色。它没有任何标准的航行灯。在飞行特性方面，该物体飞行时没有发出任何声音，估计速度为每小时500至600英里，目击者将其形容为“喷气式飞机的速度”。该物体的实际大小及其与观察者的确切距离尚不明确。

**调查/后续：** 该目击报告于2013年10月13日协调世界时01:15正式录入系统。按照此类报告的标准流程，有关凯斯威克事件的文档已进行处理并通过传真发送。所提供的档案中未记录雷达比对或实物证据等进一步的调查细节。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p040.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The Vancouver ACC shift manager reported information from two separate aircraft pilots.

**Sighting:** At 0550z, a CIRVIS report was filed regarding two separate aircraft. The first aircraft, departing Victoria, reported seeing a bright flash of light "hi" to the northwest over the Georgia Strait. A second aircraft, taking off from Vancouver, reported a bright flash of light "hi" approximately 30 miles northwest of YVR.

**Object:** A bright flash of light.

**Aftermath:** The report was sent via secure fax to CANR at 0500z, and CANR was to be notified of the second sighting.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p040.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 温哥华航空交通管制中心（ACC）值班经理报告了来自两名不同飞行员的信息。

**目击经过：** 协调世界时（z）05:50，一份关于两架不同飞机的CIRVIS（民用航空飞行员目击报告）被提交。第一架从维多利亚起飞的飞机报告称，在乔治亚海峡西北方向的高空看到一道明亮的闪光。第二架从温哥华起飞的飞机报告称，在温哥华国际机场（YVR）西北约30英里处的高空看到一道明亮的闪光。

**物体描述：** 一道明亮的闪光。

**调查/后续：** 该报告于协调世界时05:00通过安全传真发送至加拿大北美防空司令部（CANR），并已通知CANR关于第二次目击事件的情况。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p044.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pilot of JAZZ281

**Date / Time:** 2016-09-20; initial sighting reported at 0343Z, with the official CIRVIS report received by ATC at 0404Z.

**Location:** 5305N 12845W (Airspace monitored by CYVR ATC)

**Sighting:** On September 20, 2016, the pilot of flight JAZZ281 was operating an aircraft heading south at an altitude of 25,000 feet. At 0343Z, the pilot observed three distinct red lights positioned approximately 3,000 feet above their aircraft. The pilot noted that these lights were moving at a speed slower than that of the JAZZ281 aircraft. The incident was subsequently reported to the CYVR (Vancouver) ATC shift manager, who formally documented the event as a CIRVIS (Communication Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report at 0404Z.

**Object:** The object(s) were described as three red lights. They maintained an altitude 3,000 feet above the reporting aircraft and exhibited a flight speed slower than the JAZZ281 aircraft. No further physical characteristics, such as shape, size, or sound, were reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the receipt of the CIRVIS report, CYVR ATC conducted an immediate check and confirmed there were no other known aircraft or radar contacts in the vicinity of the sighting. A formal radar playback was conducted by AST/CADS, which confirmed the presence and location of JAZZ281 at the time of the report; however, the playback verified that there were no other radar contacts within a 100-nautical-mile radius of the aircraft. The official CIRVIS report was subsequently faxed to Transport Canada and the Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance Division (ISRD) for further processing.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p044.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** JAZZ281 航班飞行员

**日期 / 时间：** 2016年9月20日；首次目击报告于协调世界时（Z）0343时，空中交通管制（ATC）于0404时收到正式的 CIRVIS 报告。

**地点：** 北纬53度05分，西经128度45分（由温哥华国际机场（CYVR）空管监控的空域）

**目击经过：** 2016年9月20日，JAZZ281 航班的飞行员正驾驶飞机向南飞行，高度为25,000英尺。0343时，飞行员观察到在飞机上方约3,000英尺处有三个明显的红灯。飞行员指出，这些灯光的移动速度比 JAZZ281 飞机慢。该事件随后被报告给温哥华（CYVR）空管值班经理，后者于0404时正式将其记录为一份 CIRVIS（关于报告重要情报目击事件的通信指令）报告。

**物体描述：** 该物体（或多个物体）被描述为三个红灯。它们保持在报告飞机上方3,000英尺的高度，且飞行速度比 JAZZ281 飞机慢。未报告其他物理特征，如形状、大小或声音。

**调查/后续：** 在收到 CIRVIS 报告后，温哥华（CYVR）空管立即进行了核查，确认目击地点附近没有其他已知飞机或雷达接触目标。AST/CADS 进行了正式的雷达回放，确认了 JAZZ281 在报告时的存在和位置；然而，回放证实该飞机方圆100海里内没有任何其他雷达接触目标。正式的 CIRVIS 报告随后被传真至加拿大交通部及情报、监视与侦察部（ISRD）进行后续处理。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p046.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pilot of flight QTR739, Edmonton ID personnel, Vancouver AMIS personnel, CADS (Canadian Air Defence Sector) personnel.

**Date / Time:** 2016-12-18; initial report at 1850z, subsequent log entry at 1911z.

**Location:** 5423N/11958W (at flight level 370).

**Sighting:** On December 18, 2016, at 1850z, the Edmonton ID office received a report of an unidentified flying object (UFO) sighting from the pilot of flight QTR739. At the time of the sighting, the aircraft was cruising at flight level 370 (FL370). The report was subsequently logged by the Canadian Air Defence Sector (CADS) at 1911z. The documentation confirms that the report originated from the Edmonton ID office regarding the observation made by the QTR739 pilot at the specified coordinates. Despite the official recording of the event, no further details regarding the sighting were provided by the pilot at the time of the report.

**Object:** The object is officially classified as a UFO. There is no available information regarding its shape, size, color, sound, movement, or duration. The records explicitly state that the pilot provided no physical description of the object during the initial report.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report, Vancouver AMIS (Aerospace Management Information System) was consulted to determine if any other flights, drones, or known aerial assets were operating in the vicinity or at that specific flight level. Vancouver AMIS confirmed they had no information on any flights or drones in the area. The event log includes various operational notes, such as the DSEL (Data System Element) transitioning to a paper log and subsequently returning to service, as well as the conclusion of the Zulu day. The documentation is marked for release under the Access to Information Act (ATIA) and contains classification and log-system text associated with the 2004 NORAD-USNORTHCOM protocols. No further identification or resolution of the object was recorded in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p046.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** QTR739航班飞行员、埃德蒙顿识别（ID）部门人员、温哥华航空航天管理信息系统（AMIS）人员、加拿大防空部门（CADS）人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 2016年12月18日；初步报告于协调世界时（z）1850时，后续日志记录于1911时。

**地点：** 北纬54度23分/西经119度58分（飞行高度层370）。

**目击经过：** 2016年12月18日1850时，埃德蒙顿识别办公室收到了一份来自QTR739航班飞行员关于不明飞行物（UFO）的目击报告。目击发生时，该飞机正处于飞行高度层370（FL370）巡航。该报告随后于1911时由加拿大防空部门（CADS）记录在案。文件证实，该报告源自埃德蒙顿识别办公室，内容涉及QTR739航班飞行员在指定坐标处的观测记录。尽管该事件有官方记录，但飞行员在报告时未提供关于此次目击的更多细节。

**物体描述：** 该物体被正式归类为不明飞行物（UFO）。目前没有关于其形状、大小、颜色、声音、运动方式或持续时间的可用信息。记录明确指出，飞行员在初步报告中未提供该物体的任何物理描述。

**调查/后续：** 报告发出后，相关部门咨询了温哥华航空航天管理信息系统（AMIS），以确定当时在该区域或特定飞行高度层是否有其他航班、无人机或已知的空中资产在运行。温哥华AMIS确认，他们没有关于该区域内任何航班或无人机的信息。事件日志中包含了一些操作说明，例如数据系统要素（DSEL）转换为纸质日志并随后恢复服务的过程，以及祖鲁日（Zulu day）的结束记录。该文件根据《信息获取法》（ATIA）被标记为可发布，并包含与2004年北美防空司令部-美国北方司令部（NORAD-USNORTHCOM）协议相关的分类和日志系统文本。所提供的文件中未记录该物体的进一步识别信息或最终结论。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p050.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pilots of Lufthansa 404, Pilots of Swiss Air 18

**Date / Time:** 2016-12-23 / 0031z (Initial report), 0049z (Follow-up broadcast)

**Location:** 49N 63W area (Specific coordinates: Lufthansa 404 at 49°57'N 63°34'W; Swiss Air 18 at 49°27'N 64°07'W)

**Sighting:** 
On December 23, 2016, at 0031z, two commercial aircraft operating in the vicinity of 49N 63W reported sightings of an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The pilots of Lufthansa 404, cruising at an altitude of 40,000 feet, reported observing an object positioned slightly below their aircraft and to the left. Simultaneously, the pilots of Swiss Air 18, operating at an altitude of 38,000 feet, reported observing a white light accompanied by a rotating beacon located approximately 1,000 to 2,000 feet below their flight level. 

Following these reports, at 0049z, the Denver-Boston air traffic control center issued a formal notification to all aircraft operating within the area, requesting that flight crews maintain a lookout for any further unusual activity.

**Object:** 
The object was described by the witnesses as a white light featuring a rotating beacon. While the specific size and physical structure of the craft remain unidentified, the movement was noted in relation to the aircraft altitudes (40,000 feet and 38,000 feet respectively), with the object maintaining a position slightly below the flight paths of both reporting vessels. No specific sound or duration of the sighting beyond the initial report at 0031z was documented in the provided files.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The primary follow-up action recorded in the file was the administrative broadcast issued by Denver-Boston at 0049z, which alerted all regional air traffic to the presence of the unusual activity. No further investigative reports, RCMP interrogations, weather data, or sketches were included in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p050.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 汉莎航空 404 号航班飞行员，瑞士航空 18 号航班飞行员

**日期 / 时间：** 2016年12月23日 / 00:31z（初步报告），00:49z（后续广播）

**地点：** 北纬49度、西经63度区域（具体坐标：汉莎航空 404 号航班位于北纬49度57分、西经63度34分；瑞士航空 18 号航班位于北纬49度27分、西经64度07分）

**目击经过：** 
2016年12月23日 00:31z，两架在北纬49度、西经63度附近空域飞行的商用飞机报告目击到了不明空中现象。汉莎航空 404 号航班的飞行员在 40,000 英尺巡航高度时，报告观察到一个位于其飞机左下方的不明物体。与此同时，在 38,000 英尺高度飞行的瑞士航空 18 号航班飞行员也报告称，观察到一个带有旋转信标的白光，位于其飞行高度下方约 1,000 至 2,000 英尺处。

在收到这些报告后，丹佛-波士顿空中交通管制中心于 00:49z 向该区域内的所有飞机发布了正式通知，要求机组人员密切留意任何进一步的异常活动。

**物体描述：** 
目击者将该物体描述为一束带有旋转信标的白光。虽然该飞行器的具体尺寸和物理结构仍无法确定，但根据两架报告飞机的飞行高度（分别为 40,000 英尺和 38,000 英尺）来看，该物体始终保持在两架飞机航线略下方的位置。所提供的文件中未记录该物体的具体声音信息，也未记录除 00:31z 初步报告之外的目击持续时间。

**调查/后续：** 
文件中记录的主要后续行动是丹佛-波士顿空管中心于 00:49z 发布的行政广播，旨在提醒该区域的所有空中交通注意此类异常活动。所提供的文档中未包含进一步的调查报告、加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的问询记录、气象数据或草图。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p054.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unidentified individual located on the east side of Digby Island (CYPR).

**Date / Time:** September 3, 2017, at 23:40z.

**Location:** East side of Digby Island (CYPR).

**Sighting:** On Sunday, September 3, 2017, at 23:40z, an unidentified individual positioned on the east side of Digby Island (CYPR) observed an anomalous object traversing the sky. The witness reported that the object was moving in a trajectory from west to east. According to the witness, the object was traveling at a velocity sufficient to produce an audible sound as it passed.

**Object:** The object was described as black in color and oblong in shape. It was estimated to be approximately the size of a volleyball. The object exhibited rapid movement, which generated a distinct sound during its transit.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, the Vancouver shift manager was notified and subsequently relayed a CIRVIS (Communication Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report to the Duty Officer (DO). Upon review of the details provided, it was officially determined that the object did not present a threat to national security or aviation safety. As part of the standard administrative procedure, the CIRVIS report was formally faxed to the AARQC (Aeronautical Authorities).
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p054.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名位于迪格比岛（CYPR）东侧的身份不明人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 2017年9月3日，23:40z。

**地点：** 迪格比岛（CYPR）东侧。

**目击经过：** 2017年9月3日星期日23:40z，一名位于迪格比岛（CYPR）东侧的身份不明人士观察到一个异常物体划过天空。目击者报告称，该物体正沿西向东的轨迹移动。据目击者描述，该物体的飞行速度足以在经过时产生可听见的声响。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为黑色，呈长方形。据估计其大小约为排球大小。该物体移动迅速，在飞行过程中产生了明显的声响。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，温哥华当值经理接到通知，并随后向值班官员（DO）转达了一份CIRVIS（重要情报目击报告通信指令）报告。经审查所提供的细节，官方认定该物体未对国家安全或航空安全构成威胁。作为标准行政程序的一部分，该CIRVIS报告已正式传真至AARQC（航空管理部门）。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p058.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The page records a CIRVIS report relayed by Edmonton ACC. It states that someone informed them of an incident from the previous night and that the object was observed at 7:15 pm local time near High Prairie, Alberta.

**Sighting:** Three red lights were seen hovering in the sky at about the height of a ceiling light in a tower. The lights were described as hovering for a few moments, then taking off and heading west before disappearing.

**Object:** One light was said to blink at the center, while the other two were solid. The report describes the object only as three lights, with no shape or other physical details given.

**Aftermath:** The item was logged at 2218Z, and the page later notes that the Zulu day ended and the log was closed at 2359Z. No further investigation, identification, or recovery is described on this page.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p058.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 该页面记录了一份由埃德蒙顿航空管制中心（Edmonton ACC）转达的 CIRVIS 报告。报告称，有人告知了前一天晚上发生的一起事件，该物体于当地时间晚上 7:15 在艾伯塔省海普雷里（High Prairie）附近被观测到。

**目击经过：** 天空中出现了三个红色的光点，悬停高度大约相当于塔台内天花板灯的高度。据描述，这些光点悬停了片刻，随后起飞并向西飞去，最终消失。

**物体描述：** 据称其中一个光点在中心位置闪烁，另外两个则保持常亮。报告仅将该物体描述为三个光点，未提供任何形状或其他物理细节。

**调查/后续：** 该条目于世界协调时（Z）2218时被记录，页面后续注明该祖鲁日（Zulu day）于 2359 时结束并关闭了日志。该页面未描述任何进一步的调查、识别或回收行动。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p062.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pilot of Dash 8 aircraft (Flight PVL1910)

**Date / Time:** January 17, 2019; initial observation at 2300z, reported to Montreal Centre at 0123z.

**Location:** Montreal airspace.

**Sighting:** On January 17, 2019, the pilot of a Dash 8 aircraft, operating as flight PVL1910, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in flight. The pilot initiated a CIRVIS (Communications Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report regarding the encounter. Although the sighting occurred at 2300z, it was formally reported to Montreal Centre at 0123z. The pilot explicitly noted that there were no other aircraft within a 50-nautical-mile radius ahead of their position, ruling out standard air traffic as the source of the lights.

**Object:** The object was described as a series of oscillating vertical lights. The lights displayed a distinct color pattern consisting of red, green, and white. The movement was characterized as oscillating in a vertical orientation. No further details regarding the size, shape, or sound of the object were recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was processed as a formal CIRVIS report, which was officially transmitted at 0401z. Following the pilot's confirmation that no other aircraft were in the vicinity, no further information was provided, and the case file indicates that no additional follow-up actions were taken.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p062.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Dash 8 飞机飞行员（航班号 PVL1910）

**日期 / 时间：** 2019年1月17日；初次观测时间为 2300z，于 0123z 向蒙特利尔中心报告。

**地点：** 蒙特利尔空域。

**目击经过：** 2019年1月17日，执行 PVL1910 航班任务的一架 Dash 8 飞机飞行员在飞行途中观测到一个不明空中现象。该飞行员针对此次遭遇发起了 CIRVIS（关于报告重要情报目击事件的通信指令）报告。尽管目击事件发生在 2300z，但正式向蒙特利尔中心报告的时间为 0123z。飞行员明确指出，在其前方 50 海里半径范围内没有其他飞机，从而排除了常规空中交通作为光源的可能性。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一系列垂直振荡的灯光。灯光呈现出红、绿、白三种颜色的独特组合。其运动特征为垂直方向上的振荡。关于该物体的大小、形状或声音，未记录到更多细节。

**调查/后续：** 该事件作为正式的 CIRVIS 报告进行处理，并于 0401z 正式发送。在飞行员确认附近没有其他飞机后，未提供更多信息，且案卷显示未采取任何后续行动。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p001.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The crew of aircraft call sign JZA 731, Montreal Area Control Centre (ACC), and Canadian Air Defence Sector (CADS) 21 Squadron.

**Date / Time:** 26 December 2019, at 2337Z.

**Location:** St. Lawrence River, Canada (Coordinates: 48:37:48N, 068:37:39W).

**Sighting:** At 2337Z on December 26, 2019, the flight crew of aircraft JZA 731 reported a significant aerial observation while operating over the St. Lawrence River. The crew observed a formation of approximately 40 lights in the sky. These lights were noted to be traveling in distinct groups of 15. The entire formation maintained a continuous eastbound heading throughout the duration of the sighting. No specific information regarding the altitude or speed of the objects was provided by the reporting crew.

**Object:** The objects were described exclusively as a collection of approximately 40 lights. They were observed moving in groups of 15. No physical features, such as shape, size, or structural details, were reported. The objects did not emit any audible sound, and no information regarding their physical composition was available. The duration of the sighting was not explicitly recorded, though the objects were observed maintaining a steady eastbound course.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the initial report by JZA 731, the Montreal Area Control Centre (ACC) was notified. Montreal ACC subsequently contacted the Canadian Air Defence Sector (CADS) 21 Squadron at 2320Z (noted as the time of initial contact regarding the report). 

Official follow-up documentation, released under the Access to Information Act (ATIA) as unclassified information, indicates that there was no preliminary analysis conducted to determine a possible cause for the sighting. Furthermore, investigators confirmed there was no information regarding other air traffic or balloon releases in the vicinity that could account for the lights. No physical evidence, such as materials or photographs, was recovered or submitted. Several fields in the official reporting form were left blank or marked as "No information," confirming that the investigation remained inconclusive.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p001.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 呼号为 JZA 731 的机组人员、蒙特利尔区域管制中心（ACC）以及加拿大防空部门（CADS）第 21 中队。

**日期 / 时间：** 2019 年 12 月 26 日，23:37Z（协调世界时）。

**地点：** 加拿大圣劳伦斯河（坐标：北纬 48:37:48，西经 068:37:39）。

**目击经过：** 2019 年 12 月 26 日 23:37Z，JZA 731 航班机组人员在圣劳伦斯河上空飞行时，报告了一次重大的空中观测事件。机组人员观察到天空中出现了一个由大约 40 个光点组成的编队。这些光点被发现以 15 个一组的形式行进。在整个目击过程中，整个编队始终保持向东航行。机组人员未提供有关这些物体高度或速度的具体信息。

**物体描述：** 这些物体仅被描述为约 40 个光点的集合。观察到它们以 15 个一组的形式移动。没有报告任何物理特征，如形状、大小或结构细节。这些物体未发出任何声音，也没有关于其物理构成的可用信息。目击持续时间未明确记录，但观察到这些物体保持着稳定的向东航向。

**调查/后续：** 在 JZA 731 提交初步报告后，蒙特利尔区域管制中心（ACC）接到了通知。随后，蒙特利尔 ACC 于 23:20Z（注：此为关于该报告的首次联络时间）联系了加拿大防空部门（CADS）第 21 中队。

根据《信息获取法》（ATIA）以非机密信息形式发布的官方后续文件显示，当局并未进行初步分析以确定目击事件的可能原因。此外，调查人员确认，附近没有其他空中交通或气球释放活动可以解释这些光点。未发现或提交任何实物证据（如材料或照片）。官方报告表中的多个字段被留空或标记为“无信息”，证实了该调查最终未得出结论。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p068.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** YVR Shift Manager

**Date / Time:** January 23, 2020, at 0308z (reported via CIRVIS at 0430z)

**Location:** 20 nautical miles (NM) southwest of Sandspit, BC

**Sighting:** 
On January 23, 2020, at 0308z, the YVR Shift Manager received reports of an anomalous aerial event occurring 20 nautical miles southwest of Sandspit, BC. The sighting consisted of a stream of 30 individual lights arranged in a row. According to the accounts, the lights were observed moving in a straight line from west to east. The duration of the sighting was recorded as lasting between 3 and 4 minutes. 

The observation was confirmed via air-visual observation. While the lights initially maintained a consistent linear trajectory, the account notes that the object or formation eventually "just stopped." A CIRVIS (Communication Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings) report was formally logged regarding the event at 0430z.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a stream of 30 lights arranged in a row, characterized collectively as a "flash of light." The formation moved in a straight line for a duration of 3 to 4 minutes before coming to a complete stop. No specific sound or physical structure beyond the lights was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Official follow-up procedures were initiated by the YVR Shift Manager. A playback of radar or monitoring data was conducted to verify the visual report; however, the playback yielded no results, and a subsequent check performed at 0521z confirmed that nothing was visible on the playback. 

The investigation considered the possibility that the lights were related to a SpaceX Starlink satellite launch; however, after checking schedules, it was determined that no such launch was scheduled for that time. Weather conditions at the time of the sighting were recorded as 600-4000, with clear skies above 10,000 feet.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p068.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 温哥华国际机场（YVR）值班经理

**日期 / 时间：** 2020年1月23日，03:08z（于04:30z通过CIRVIS报告）

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省桑兹皮特（Sandspit）西南方20海里处

**目击经过：**
2020年1月23日03:08z，温哥华国际机场（YVR）值班经理收到报告，称在不列颠哥伦比亚省桑兹皮特西南方20海里处发生了一起异常空中事件。目击内容为一串排列成行的30个独立光点。据描述，这些光点呈直线状由西向东移动。目击持续时间记录为3至4分钟。

该观测结果已通过空中目视确认。虽然这些光点最初保持着一致的直线轨迹，但报告指出，该物体或编队最终“突然停止”了移动。关于此次事件的CIRVIS（报告重要情报目击事件的通信指令）报告于04:30z正式登记。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为一串排列成行的30个光点，整体被形容为“一道闪光”。该编队在直线移动3至4分钟后完全停止。除光点外，未报告有任何特定的声音或物理结构。

**调查/后续：**
YVR值班经理启动了官方后续程序。相关人员对雷达或监控数据进行了回放以核实目击报告；然而，回放未发现任何异常，随后在05:21z进行的检查也证实回放记录中没有任何可见物体。

调查考虑了这些光点是否与SpaceX“星链”（Starlink）卫星发射有关；但在核对发射计划后，确定当时并未安排此类发射任务。目击时的天气状况记录为600-4000（云底高度），10,000英尺以上天空晴朗。

CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p160.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** YVR Shift Manager.

**Sighting:** At 0430z, a CIRVIS report was logged regarding a stream of lights observed at 0308z on 23 Jan 20. The sighting consisted of 30 lights in a row, moving from West to East.

**Object:** The object was described as a flash of light, lasting 3-4 minutes, moving in a straight line before it "just stopped". The sighting was confirmed via air-visual observation.

**Aftermath:** The report notes the weather as 600-4000 clear above 10,000. A playback was conducted, and it was noted that a possible Starlink launch was considered, however, nothing was scheduled. A subsequent check at 0521z indicated nothing was seen on playback.
CA-FOIA-CIRVIS--Canada-2010-2019-p160.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** YVR 轮班经理。

**目击：** 在 0430z，一份关于 1 月 23 日 0308z 观察到的一串灯光的 CIRVIS 报告被记录。目击事件包括 30 个排成一行的灯光，由西向东移动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A 36-year-old civilian (the same individual is the primary witness across both pages).

**Date / Time:** January 3, 1969, at approximately 9:30 PM.

**Location:** Port Arthur/Lakehead, Ontario (specifically Highway 11 between Port Arthur and Sunshine, the junction of Highway 11 and 17, and the area near the Fort William airport).

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 3, 1969, the witness was driving west on Highway 11 between Port Arthur and Sunshine when they observed a bright light hovering above the treetops. The object initially rose and moved behind a hill. Later, near the junction of Highway 11 and 17, the witness observed the object again, hovering over the treetops. The witness watched the object for nearly an hour from a laneway. Upon entering Fort William near the airport, the object appeared again, heading toward the airport, swooping down, and then the light went out. 

The witness reported that this light had been seen continuously over the Lakehead area, typically first sighted about an hour before dusk. During observations, the witness utilized eyeglasses and binoculars to track the object. The witness noted that the object would move forward with a burst of speed, stop and hang in the air, then revolve around and around. At times, it would shoot off in a slightly different direction, stop, and remain above the treetops. The witness also observed a jet plane in the vicinity at the same time, noting that the object appeared larger than the jet. The witness returned to the same location the following night with binoculars and observed the object again.

**Object:** The object was described as a very bright light of immense size. It featured red flashing lights around its center. While hovering over the treetops, small pinpoints of light were observed shooting to and from the larger lights. The object exhibited erratic movement, including bursts of speed, hovering, revolving, and sudden directional changes. It made no reported sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The witness expressed strong skepticism regarding official reports circulating at the time, which claimed the object was a weather balloon released from the United States. The witness explicitly disputed this explanation, maintaining that the object was something else entirely. The witness concluded their account by urging that the matter be investigated further and that official findings be published so that the public could be informed about the activity occurring in the skies above them.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名36岁的平民（该名人士为两页记录中的主要目击者）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月3日，晚上约9:30。

**地点：** 安大略省亚瑟港（Port Arthur）/ 湖首（Lakehead）地区（具体地点包括亚瑟港至阳光镇（Sunshine）之间的11号公路、11号与17号公路交汇处，以及威廉堡（Fort William）机场附近区域）。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月3日晚，目击者正驾车沿11号公路向西行驶，在亚瑟港至阳光镇之间，观察到一个明亮的光体悬浮在树梢上方。该物体起初上升并移动到一座小山后方。随后，在11号与17号公路的交汇处附近，目击者再次观察到该物体悬浮在树梢上。目击者从一条小路旁观察了该物体近一个小时。当进入威廉堡机场附近时，该物体再次出现，向机场方向飞去，俯冲而下，随后光芒熄灭。

目击者报告称，该光体在湖首地区被持续观察到，通常在黄昏前约一小时首次出现。在观察过程中，目击者使用了眼镜和双筒望远镜来追踪该物体。目击者指出，该物体会以极快的速度向前冲刺，随后停住并悬停在空中，接着不断旋转。有时，它会突然转向另一个方向，停下并保持在树梢上方。目击者同时观察到附近有一架喷气式飞机，并指出该物体的外观比飞机更大。次日晚上，目击者带着双筒望远镜回到同一地点，再次观察到了该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个体积极其巨大的明亮光体。其中心周围有红色的闪烁灯光。当悬浮在树梢上方时，可以看到微小的光点在较大的灯光之间来回穿梭。该物体表现出不规则的运动轨迹，包括加速冲刺、悬停、旋转以及突然改变方向。据报告，该物体未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击者对当时流传的官方报告表示强烈怀疑，该报告声称该物体是美国释放的气象气球。目击者明确反驳了这一解释，坚持认为该物体完全是其他东西。目击者在陈述结尾处敦促对此事进行进一步调查，并要求公布官方调查结果，以便公众了解在他们头顶的天空中究竟发生了什么。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** John Rae, Walter Lautrup, Van Jacobson, and Edward Rae (Superintendent of Kootenay National Park).

**Date / Time:** March 11, 1969, at 7:30 PM MST.

**Location:** Approximately 30 miles west of Radium Hot Springs, BC, specifically situated between Mt. Abbott and Mt. Stockdale.

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 11, 1969, four witnesses—John Rae, Walter Lautrup, Van Jacobson, and Edward Rae—observed an event they collectively interpreted as an aircraft crash. The weather conditions at the time were reported as clear. The witnesses observed a distinct vertical smoke trail that reached an altitude of approximately 10,000 feet. Following the descent of the object, a large amount of dark smoke was seen billowing from the ground at the impact site. This smoke remained visible for approximately 15 minutes. The witnesses, particularly John Rae, were noted by the RCMP as being highly reliable individuals, and their consensus was that they had witnessed a plane going down.

**Object:** The object was perceived by all witnesses as an aircraft. Its primary physical characteristics included a vertical descent path and the creation of a significant, dark smoke trail that extended to 10,000 feet. Upon reaching the ground, the object produced a large, billowing volume of smoke that persisted for 15 minutes. No sound or specific shape details beyond the smoke trail and the assumption of an aircraft were recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the reports, the RCMP conducted an inquiry with the Department of Transport (D.O.T.) to determine if any aircraft were overdue or missing; the D.O.T. confirmed that no aircraft were reported missing in the sub-division. On March 13, 1969, Mr. Duncan McIntosh (also referred to as MacIntosh) volunteered to conduct an aerial scan of the area in his private plane, accompanied by the NCO in charge of the Radium Detachment. Additionally, on March 12, 1969, an official Albatross aircraft was deployed to search the area. Both the private and official searches yielded negative results, with nothing sighted at the location. The information regarding the sighting and the subsequent search efforts was formally passed to the Rescue Co-ordination Centre to determine if further search operations were required. The RCMP maintained their assessment that the witnesses were very reliable, despite the lack of physical evidence found during the aerial sweeps.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·雷 (John Rae)、沃尔特·劳特鲁普 (Walter Lautrup)、范·雅各布森 (Van Jacobson) 以及爱德华·雷 (Edward Rae，库特尼国家公园负责人)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年3月11日，山区标准时间 (MST) 晚上7:30。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省镭温泉镇 (Radium Hot Springs) 以西约30英里处，具体位于阿博特山 (Mt. Abbott) 和斯托克代尔山 (Mt. Stockdale) 之间。

**目击经过：** 1969年3月11日晚，四名目击者——约翰·雷、沃尔特·劳特鲁普、范·雅各布森和爱德华·雷——共同目击了一起他们认为的飞机坠毁事件。据报告，当时天气晴朗。目击者观察到一条明显的垂直烟迹，高度达到约10,000英尺。物体坠落后，撞击地点冒出大量浓烟。这些烟雾持续可见约15分钟。加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 指出，目击者（尤其是约翰·雷）是非常可靠的人，他们一致认为自己目睹了一架飞机坠毁。

**物体描述：** 所有目击者都认为该物体是一架飞机。其主要物理特征包括垂直的下降轨迹，以及产生了一条延伸至10,000英尺高的显著浓烟轨迹。物体落地后，产生了大量持续15分钟的滚滚浓烟。除了烟迹和对飞机身份的推测外，没有记录到任何声音或具体的形状细节。

**调查/后续：** 报告发出后，加拿大皇家骑警向交通部 (D.O.T.) 进行了查询，以确定是否有飞机逾期未归或失踪；交通部确认该分区没有飞机失踪的报告。1969年3月13日，邓肯·麦金托什先生 (Mr. Duncan McIntosh) 自愿驾驶其私人飞机，在镭温泉镇分遣队负责警官的陪同下对该区域进行了空中扫描。此外，1969年3月12日，一架官方的信天翁 (Albatross) 飞机也被部署到该区域进行搜索。私人搜索和官方搜索均未发现任何结果，在现场一无所获。有关此次目击事件及后续搜索工作的信息已正式移交给救援协调中心，以确定是否需要进一步的搜索行动。尽管在空中搜寻中未发现任何实物证据，加拿大皇家骑警仍坚持认为目击者非常可靠。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Yves Parré (also referred to as Yves Lasse), an unnamed friend.

**Date / Time:** March 15, 1969, at approximately 20:45 hours.

**Location:** Fabreville / St-Laurent, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 15, 1969, at 20:45, two witnesses—Yves Parré and an unnamed friend—were driving in the Fabreville area when they observed a luminous, bright red object in the northeast sky. At the time of the sighting, the sky was completely overcast, rendering stars invisible. The witnesses observed the object remaining stationary for several seconds before it suddenly disappeared in a northeasterly direction. Based on the object's speed, its distinct red color, and the fact that it did not twinkle or flash, the witnesses concluded that the object was not a conventional airplane. Troubled by the encounter and driven by personal curiosity, the witnesses contacted the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) to inquire about the nature of the light.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, luminous red light. It appeared stationary for a few seconds before moving away. The witnesses noted that the light did not flash or twinkle, and its speed and movement patterns were inconsistent with those of an aircraft.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the National Research Council of Canada. On March 28, 1969, Peter M. Millman, the Head of Upper Atmosphere Research, provided a formal response to M. Yves Parré. Millman stated that, due to the limited amount of specific detail provided in the report, he was unable to definitively identify the origin of the light. Taking into account the overcast weather conditions reported at the time, Millman suggested that the object was likely either an unconventional type of aircraft light or a reflection of a terrestrial light source.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 伊夫·帕雷（Yves Parré，也被称为伊夫·拉塞 Yves Lasse），以及一位未具名的朋友。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年3月15日，约20:45。

**地点：** 魁北克省法布尔维尔（Fabreville）/ 圣洛朗（St-Laurent）。

**目击经过：** 1969年3月15日晚20:45，两名目击者——伊夫·帕雷和一位未具名的朋友——在法布尔维尔地区驾车时，观察到东北方向的天空中出现了一个明亮的红色发光物体。目击当时天空完全被云层覆盖，无法看到星星。目击者观察到该物体静止了数秒，随后突然向东北方向消失。基于该物体的速度、独特的红色，以及它既不闪烁也不发光的特点，目击者断定该物体并非传统飞机。由于这次遭遇令他们感到困惑，出于个人好奇，目击者联系了加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）以询问该光源的性质。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一团明亮的红色光团。它在移动前静止了几秒钟。目击者指出，该光团没有闪烁，其速度和运动模式与飞机不符。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件被报告给了加拿大国家研究委员会。1969年3月28日，高层大气研究负责人彼得·M·米尔曼（Peter M. Millman）向伊夫·帕雷先生作出了正式回复。米尔曼表示，由于报告中提供的具体细节有限，他无法明确确定该光源的来源。考虑到当时报告的阴天天气状况，米尔曼推测该物体很可能是一种非常规的飞机灯光，或者是地面光源的反射。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_16_-_Pages_45.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unnamed civilian (two separate reports/incidents)

**Date / Time:** November 4, 1980, at 2010 hours; November 5, 1980, at 0310 hours.

**Location:** Red Deer, Alberta.

**Sighting:** This file documents two distinct aerial observations reported in the Red Deer area. The first incident occurred on November 4, 1980, at 2010 hours, when an unnamed civilian observed a formation of strange lights over the south side of Red Deer. The witness noted that the lights were traveling in a north-easterly direction. The second incident occurred early the following morning on November 5, 1980, at 0310 hours. During this event, an unnamed witness observed a single object positioned approximately one-half mile above the ground under cloudy weather conditions.

**Object:** 
*   **November 4 Incident:** The object(s) appeared as blue and yellow lights. The formation was observed at an altitude of approximately 1,000 feet. The sighting lasted for 3 minutes, and the witness reported that no sound was heard during the event.
*   **November 5 Incident:** The object was described as round in shape and bright orange in color. It was positioned at an altitude of approximately one-half mile. The duration of this sighting was 5 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Both reports were processed through official military channels. The documentation was transmitted from the 43 Radar Squadron at CFB Penhold to the National Defence Operations Centre in Ottawa. Additionally, the reports were forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) and the Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_16_-_Pages_45.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 未具名平民（两起独立报告/事件）

**日期 / 时间：** 1980年11月4日，20:10；1980年11月5日，03:10。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省，红鹿市（Red Deer）。

**目击经过：** 本档案记录了在红鹿市地区报告的两起截然不同的空中观测事件。第一起事件发生在1980年11月4日20:10，当时一名未具名平民在红鹿市南侧上空观察到一组奇异的光团编队。目击者指出，这些光团正向东北方向移动。第二起事件发生在次日清晨，即1980年11月5日03:10。在此次事件中，一名未具名目击者在多云天气下，观察到一个位于地面上方约半英里处的单一物体。

**物体描述：**
*   **11月4日事件：** 该物体（或光团）表现为蓝色和黄色的光。观测到的编队高度约为1,000英尺。目击持续了3分钟，目击者报告称在事件过程中未听到任何声音。
*   **11月5日事件：** 该物体被描述为圆形，呈亮橙色。它位于约半英里高空。此次目击持续了5分钟。

**调查/后续：** 两份报告均通过官方军事渠道进行了处理。相关文件由位于彭霍尔德加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Penhold）的第43雷达中队传达至渥太华的国家国防作战中心。此外，这些报告还被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）及赫茨伯格天体物理研究所（Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics）进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A 26-year-old farmer, a 38-year-old farmer, two brothers (duck hunters, names redacted).

**Date / Time:** November 2, 1954, at 2145 GMT (Note: One report erroneously lists 1956).

**Location:** Auburn, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 2, 1954, multiple witnesses in the Auburn, N.S. area observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. Two farmers provided detailed accounts of the object’s trajectory: one observed it at 60 degrees above the horizon looking north-northeasterly, noting it traveled on a course of 240 degrees in a southwesterly direction at an estimated altitude of 50,000 feet. Estimates of its speed varied between 2,800 mph and 3,500 mph (roughly seven to ten times the speed of a bomber). 

Simultaneously, two brothers who were duck hunting three miles from Auburn observed the object flying above the clouds at 60 degrees above the horizon before it was lost from view. While one report suggests the hunters were not within hearing distance of the object, another account from the same investigation notes they were within hearing distance. Additional documentation describes the object being observed for six seconds, appearing at 90 degrees above the horizon, and last seen in a northwesterly direction. Observers noted the object did not resemble any known aircraft and left no exhaust trail.

**Object:** Descriptions of the object were varied but consistent in their strangeness. It was described as a round, "quite large" object with jagged edges. Its color shifted from yellow to a brilliant white as it passed overhead, maintaining a constant brilliance. It moved rapidly without producing any sound ("nil" noise). While some witnesses speculated it could be a meteor or shooting star, others emphasized its controlled, high-speed flight.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by F/O L.G. DeFreitas. Official follow-up included an assessment of the witnesses' mental stability at the Nova Scotia Dartmouth Mental Institution. While F/O DeFreitas noted that the duck-hunting brothers appeared "sincere and honest," he ultimately questioned their reliability, suggesting potential mental instability. The case was classified as "F3," noting that no aircraft in flight at the time reported any unusual activity. 

Weather data recorded for the event included scattered clouds at 8,000 feet and broken clouds at 20,000 feet, with no rain or snow. The temperature was 68 degrees with 86% humidity; the moon was not visible. One farmer noted he had seen a similar object in the same area in April 1954, while another farmer recalled seeing a similar reddish object in the same vicinity in approximately 1940.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名26岁农民，一名38岁农民，两名兄弟（猎鸭人，姓名已删减）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1954年11月2日，格林威治标准时间21:45（注：一份报告错误地将其列为1956年）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省奥本（Auburn, Nova Scotia）。

**目击经过：** 1954年11月2日晚，新斯科舍省奥本地区的数名目击者观察到一种不明空中现象。两名农民提供了该物体飞行轨迹的详细描述：其中一人在北偏东北方向观察到它位于地平线上方60度处，并指出它以240度的航向向西南方向飞行，估计高度为50,000英尺。对其速度的估算在每小时2,800英里至3,500英里之间（约为轰炸机速度的七到十倍）。

与此同时，在距离奥本三英里处猎鸭的两名兄弟观察到该物体在云层上方飞行，位于地平线上方60度处，随后消失在视野中。虽然一份报告称猎人们并未处于该物体的听觉范围内，但同一调查中的另一份记录则指出他们处于听觉范围内。其他文档描述该物体被观测了六秒钟，出现在地平线上方90度处，最后消失在西北方向。观察者指出，该物体不像任何已知的飞行器，且没有留下任何尾迹。

**物体描述：** 对该物体的描述各不相同，但在其奇异性上是一致的。它被描述为一个边缘参差不齐的圆形“相当大”的物体。当它从头顶掠过时，颜色从黄色变为明亮的白色，并保持恒定的亮度。它快速移动且没有发出任何声音（“零”噪音）。虽然一些目击者推测它可能是流星或陨星，但其他人则强调了其受控的高速飞行状态。

**调查/后续：** 该调查由L.G. 德弗雷塔斯（L.G. DeFreitas）空军中尉负责。官方后续行动包括在新斯科舍省达特茅斯精神病院对目击者的心理稳定性进行评估。尽管德弗雷塔斯中尉指出那两名猎鸭兄弟看起来“真诚且诚实”，但他最终还是质疑了他们的可靠性，暗示他们可能存在心理不稳定。该案件被归类为“F3”，并注明当时在空中的任何飞行器均未报告任何异常活动。

事件发生时的气象数据记录显示，8,000英尺处有零散云层，20,000英尺处有碎云，无雨雪。气温为68华氏度（约20摄氏度），湿度为86%；月亮不可见。一名农民指出，他曾在1954年4月在同一地区见过类似的物体，而另一名农民回忆称，大约在1940年也在附近见过类似的红色物体。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lawrence Allan Larocque, Ernest M. Fabien, Margaret Rose Mandeville, Mathew Tommy Unka, Gene Murie Norn (also referred to as Jean Murray Norn), Alice Hodges, Yvonne (Mrs. John) Boston, Francis (Mrs. George) Filiatrault, and Molly (Mrs. Merton) Mohr.

**Date / Time:** July 16, 1968, between midnight and 1:00 AM.

**Location:** Fort Resolution and Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, Canada.

**Sighting:** On the night of July 16, 1968, multiple witnesses in Fort Resolution and Fort Smith reported a high-speed aerial object. Gene Murie Norn, a forestry employee, first reported the object to nurse Alice Hodges after observing it while walking home in Fort Resolution between midnight and 12:30 AM. Norn described the object traveling northeast at high speed. Shortly thereafter, between 12:30 AM and 1:00 AM, other residents—Margaret Rose Mandeville, Ernest Michael Fabien, Lawrence Allan Larocque, and Mathew Tommy Unka—observed the same or a similar phenomenon. While some witnesses reported total silence, Mandeville and the group including Fabien, Larocque, and Unka reported hearing two distinct "shots" or backfire-like sounds as the object moved into the clouds. Simultaneously, in Fort Smith, Yvonne Boston, Francis Filiatrault, and Molly Mohr observed a luminous object moving south to north in a rising arc for 4–5 seconds.

**Object:** Descriptions varied but consistently highlighted a high-speed, luminous aerial phenomenon. The object was described as "jelly bean" shaped, long and pointed, oval, or round. It was intensely bright—brighter than stars—with a bluish-white, luminous appearance. Witnesses noted a "dark" front end and a rear that emitted multi-colored sparks (red, green, purple, white) and smoke/vapour trails extending 1/4 to 1/2 mile behind it. The object lacked wings, tail fins, or visible propulsion, and was described as "breathing" or flaring. It moved at speeds exceeding that of a jet, at altitudes estimated between 7,000 and 10,000 feet. Duration of the sightings ranged from 5 seconds to one minute.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP (Cst. J.W. Quinn, Resolution Detachment) conducted interviews and concluded that all witnesses were reliable, sober, and not prone to fabrication. Several witnesses provided hand-drawn sketches of the object. Official weather data for the time indicated a ceiling of 1,200 feet with scattered cumulus and alto-stratus clouds. The Department of Transport (D.O.T.) Aeradio confirmed that a Pacific Western Airlines Convair (Flight 182) had passed over at 9:10 PM, hours before the sighting, ruling it out as a cause. The RCMP noted the witnesses' expertise in aircraft spotting and their observation that the object’s lack of noise was inconsistent with conventional aircraft at that altitude. The case was filed under the National Research Council of Canada (RG 77, Vol. 306).
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 劳伦斯·艾伦·拉罗克 (Lawrence Allan Larocque)、欧内斯特·M·法比安 (Ernest M. Fabien)、玛格丽特·罗斯·曼德维尔 (Margaret Rose Mandeville)、马修·汤米·昂卡 (Mathew Tommy Unka)、吉恩·穆里·诺恩 (Gene Murie Norn，亦称 Jean Murray Norn)、爱丽丝·霍奇斯 (Alice Hodges)、伊冯·波士顿 (Yvonne Boston，约翰·波士顿夫人)、弗朗西斯·菲利亚特罗 (Francis Filiatrault，乔治·菲利亚特罗夫人) 以及莫莉·莫尔 (Molly Mohr，默顿·莫尔夫人)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月16日，午夜至凌晨1:00之间。

**地点：** 加拿大西北地区，雷索卢申堡 (Fort Resolution) 和史密斯堡 (Fort Smith)。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月16日晚，雷索卢申堡和史密斯堡的多名目击者报告称看到一个高速飞行的空中物体。林业局员工吉恩·穆里·诺恩在午夜至凌晨12:30之间步行回家时首次观察到该物体，并向护士爱丽丝·霍奇斯进行了报告。诺恩描述该物体正以极高速度向东北方向飞行。此后不久，即凌晨12:30至1:00之间，其他居民——玛格丽特·罗斯·曼德维尔、欧内斯特·迈克尔·法比安、劳伦斯·艾伦·拉罗克和马修·汤米·昂卡——也观察到了相同或类似的现象。虽然一些目击者称现场完全寂静，但曼德维尔以及包括法比安、拉罗克和昂卡在内的小组报告称，当物体进入云层时，听到了两声清晰的“枪响”或类似汽车回火的声音。与此同时，在史密斯堡，伊冯·波士顿、弗朗西斯·菲利亚特罗和莫莉·莫尔观察到一个发光物体以升起的弧线从南向北移动，持续了4至5秒。

**物体描述：** 描述虽有差异，但都一致强调这是一个高速发光的空中现象。该物体被描述为“软糖”状、长而尖、椭圆形或圆形。它极其明亮——比星星更亮——呈现出蓝白色的光芒。目击者注意到其前端呈“暗色”，尾部喷射出多种颜色的火花（红色、绿色、紫色、白色），并拖着长达1/4至1/2英里的烟雾/蒸汽尾迹。该物体没有机翼、尾翼或可见的推进装置，被描述为在“呼吸”或闪烁。它的飞行速度超过了喷气式飞机，估计高度在7,000至10,000英尺之间。目击持续时间从5秒到1分钟不等。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（雷索卢申分局的 J.W. Quinn 警官）进行了访谈，结论是所有目击者均可靠、清醒，且没有编造事实的倾向。几位目击者提供了该物体的手绘草图。当时的官方气象数据显示，云底高度为1,200英尺，有零散的积云和高层云。交通部 (D.O.T.) 航空无线电部门证实，太平洋西部航空公司的一架康维尔飞机（182号航班）曾在目击事件发生前数小时的晚上9:10飞过，排除了其作为成因的可能性。加拿大皇家骑警指出，目击者具备识别飞机的专业知识，他们观察到该物体缺乏噪音，这与该高度下的常规飞机不符。此案被归档在加拿大国家研究委员会（RG 77, Vol. 306）名下。

**Witnesses:** Miss Christien Riverin, Mrs. Coulomb, Mr. Bertram Dufor, and Mrs. Bertram Dufor.

**Date / Time:** August 17, 1968, at 1735Z (Note: Page 80 contains a typographical error citing 1958; the correct date is 1968).

**Location:** Arvida, Quebec (specifically the vicinity of St. Mathieu Parish).

**Sighting:** On August 17, 1968, at 1735Z, two simultaneous sightings were reported by four witnesses—Miss Christien Riverin, Mrs. Coulomb, and Mr. and Mrs. Bertram Dufor—all located in Arvida. The atmospheric conditions at the time were described as overcast, characterized by the presence of smoke and haze. The witnesses observed an object appearing over the St. Mathieu Parish area that resembled a large star. The primary object exhibited a distinct flight pattern, moving in an up-and-down motion accompanied by an oscillating side-to-side movement. During the observation, a smaller object was seen detaching or falling from the main body. This smaller object subsequently burst into a ball of fire before disappearing from view. Mrs. Coulomb provided the specific detail that the resulting fireball trailed black smoke as it descended and vanished.

**Object:** 
*   **Shape:** The primary object resembled a large star.
*   **Size:** Not explicitly quantified, but described as a "large star."
*   **Color:** The smaller detached object was described as a "ball of fire."
*   **Sound:** No sound was reported.
*   **Movement:** The main object moved in an up-and-down fashion with an oscillating side-to-side motion.
*   **Duration:** The duration was not explicitly stated, though the event involved a sequence of detachment, combustion, and disappearance.
*   **Additional Details:** A smaller object fell from the main object; the fireball trailed black smoke.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and processed through military and governmental channels. The report was transmitted by the 41st NORAD Division Headquarters located in North Bay. The information was subsequently forwarded to CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters) and the National Research Council for Radio and Electrical Engineering Division for further review and analysis.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 克里斯蒂安·里弗林小姐 (Miss Christien Riverin)、库隆夫人 (Mrs. Coulomb)、伯特伦·杜福尔先生 (Mr. Bertram Dufor) 及伯特伦·杜福尔夫人 (Mrs. Bertram Dufor)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月17日，17:35Z（注：第80页存在印刷错误，误写为1958年；正确日期应为1968年）。

**地点：** 魁北克省阿尔维达（具体为圣马修教区附近）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月17日17:35Z，四名目击者——克里斯蒂安·里弗林小姐、库隆夫人以及伯特伦·杜福尔夫妇——在阿尔维达同时报告了两次目击事件。当时的各种大气条件被描述为阴天，伴有烟雾和霾。目击者观察到圣马修教区上空出现了一个类似于大星星的物体。该主体呈现出独特的飞行模式，呈上下起伏运动，并伴有左右摇摆。在观察过程中，目击者看到一个较小的物体从主体上分离或坠落。这个小物体随后爆裂成一个火球，随即消失在视野中。库隆夫人提供了具体细节，称形成的火球在下降并消失时拖着黑烟。

**物体描述：**
*   **形状：** 主体类似于一颗大星星。
*   **大小：** 未明确量化，但被描述为“一颗大星星”。
*   **颜色：** 分离出来的小物体被描述为“火球”。
*   **声音：** 未报告有任何声音。
*   **运动：** 主体呈上下起伏运动，并伴有左右摇摆。
*   **持续时间：** 未明确说明，但事件包含了分离、燃烧和消失的过程。
*   **其他细节：** 一个较小的物体从主体上坠落；火球拖着黑烟。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已通过军事和政府渠道正式记录并处理。报告由位于北湾的北美防空司令部（NORAD）第41师总部发送。随后，相关信息被转发至加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）以及国家研究委员会无线电与电气工程部，以进行进一步的审查和分析。

**Witnesses:** R. Grandy Irwin, Mrs. Irwin, and one unnamed observer.

**Date / Time:** August 12, 1968 (9:45 P.M. / 12/00.45Z) and August 15, 1968 (nightfall).

**Location:** The veranda/steps of a residence at the corner of Water Street and St. Patricks Lane, Shelburne, N.S.

**Sighting:** 
The documentation details two distinct sighting events. The first occurred on August 12 at 9:45 P.M. (12/00.45Z). R. Grandy Irwin, observing from his home on Water Street, noted a light appearing between the "Evening Star" and a lesser star, positioned at an azimuth of 080 degrees and 35–40 degrees above the horizon. The object moved at an "enormous speed" in a south-westerly direction, executing six instantaneous, sharp 45-degree turns to the left and right without losing velocity. The sighting lasted approximately ten seconds before the object vanished to the southwest, either by traveling out of sight or being extinguished. Mr. Irwin attempted to alert his wife, but she was occupied watching television and did not witness this event.

The second event occurred on August 15, 1968, at nightfall. Mr. and Mrs. Irwin, along with an unnamed observer, watched the sky from their home. They observed the Evening Star in the West (approx. 40 degrees above the horizon) and a lesser star. A bright, slightly orange light appeared between them. The object moved steadily in a south-westerly direction at a speed comparable to a slow-moving plane. After approximately ten minutes, the object became motionless. It remained stationary in that position for two hours before observations were discontinued. Mr. Irwin noted that the object appeared to be at least twenty miles away, in the direction of Harper’s Lake.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a star-like, bright light with a slight orange hue. It possessed an intensity comparable to the Evening Star. During the August 12 sighting, it displayed high-speed, erratic, angular movement. During the August 15 sighting, it exhibited steady, slow-moving flight followed by a prolonged stationary period. There was no sound, no vapor trail, and no residue reported. Observations were conducted with the naked eye and 7x35 binoculars.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Mr. Irwin contacted the duty officer at the Air Force Station in Baccaro to report the sightings. He suggested that authorities conduct a daylight observation of the Harper’s Lake area, speculating that the object might be seeking sanctuary in that uninhabited vicinity during the day. An unnamed observer submitted a detailed written report to the unit via mail, requesting instructions for further forwarding. Official records note that the sky was clear during both nights of observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** R. 格兰迪·欧文 (R. Grandy Irwin)、欧文夫人 (Mrs. Irwin) 以及一名未具名的观察者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月12日（晚上9:45 / 12日00:45Z）及1968年8月15日（夜幕降临时）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省谢尔本 (Shelburne, N.S.)，沃特街 (Water Street) 与圣帕特里克巷 (St. Patricks Lane) 交汇处的一处住宅阳台/台阶。

**目击经过：**
相关记录详细描述了两次独立的目击事件。第一次发生在8月12日晚上9:45（12日00:45Z）。R. 格兰迪·欧文在沃特街的家中观察时，注意到在“长庚星”（Evening Star）与一颗较小的恒星之间出现了一道光，其方位角为080度，位于地平线上方35至40度处。该物体以“极高的速度”向西南方向移动，在不减速的情况下完成了六次瞬间的、锐利的45度左右转向。目击过程持续了约十秒，随后物体向西南方向消失，可能是飞出了视野，也可能是熄灭了。欧文先生曾试图提醒妻子，但她当时正在看电视，未能目击到这一事件。

第二次事件发生在1968年8月15日夜幕降临时。欧文夫妇与一名未具名的观察者在自家住宅观察天空。他们观察到西边（地平线上方约40度）的长庚星及一颗较小的恒星。一道明亮、略带橙色的光出现在它们之间。该物体以类似于慢速飞机的速度平稳地向西南方向移动。约十分钟后，物体停止了移动。它在那个位置保持静止长达两个小时，随后观察结束。欧文先生指出，该物体似乎位于至少二十英里外，即哈珀湖 (Harper’s Lake) 的方向。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为一颗类似恒星的明亮光点，带有轻微的橙色色调。其亮度与长庚星相当。在8月12日的目击中，它表现出高速、无规律的角运动。在8月15日的目击中，它表现出平稳、缓慢的飞行，随后进入了长时间的静止状态。据报告，该物体没有声音，没有尾迹，也没有留下任何残留物。观察是通过肉眼和7x35双筒望远镜进行的。

**调查/后续：**
欧文先生联系了巴卡罗 (Baccaro) 空军基地的值班军官报告了这些目击事件。他建议当局对哈珀湖地区进行日间观察，推测该物体可能在白天躲藏在该无人居住的区域。一名未具名的观察者通过邮件向该单位提交了一份详细的书面报告，并询问后续转交的指示。官方记录显示，两次观察期间天空均晴朗无云。

**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. [redacted] of Beausejour.

**Sighting:** At approximately 9:30 PM (CST) on April 15, 1972, the witnesses were traveling south by car on PTH 44, approximately 10-15 miles north of Westhawk Lake, Manitoba.

**Object:** The subjects observed an oval-shaped, greenish-white light, approximately 2 feet in diameter. The object traveled in front of their car at tree-top height, moving in a spinning motion and weaving from left to right continuously for approximately 10 minutes before disappearing. A few minutes later, the same object reappeared behind the car and followed it for approximately 5 minutes at the same height and in a similar manner before suddenly disappearing.

**Aftermath:** The sky was clear at the time. The sighting was not observed by any other persons in the area. The report was filed by the Falcon Beach Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 来自博塞茹尔（Beausejour）的[已涂黑]夫妇。

**目击：** 1972年4月15日晚上约9:30（中部标准时间），见证者正驾车沿44号省道（PTH 44）向南行驶，地点位于曼尼托巴省韦斯特霍克湖（Westhawk Lake）以北约10至15英里处。

**物体：** 目击者观察到一个椭圆形的绿白色光点，直径约2英尺。该物体在树梢高度出现在车前，以旋转方式持续左右摇摆飞行了约10分钟后消失。几分钟后，同一个物体再次出现在车后，并以同样的高度和方式跟随车辆飞行了约5分钟，随后突然消失。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Civilian resident of 11111 Braxton Road S.W., civilian resident of 11127 Braxton Road S.W. and family, civilian employee of Shell Oil Canada Ltd., the author (photographer), father-in-law, neighbor, Cst. R.M. Lequesne, Cst. Lequesne’s son-in-law, and various unnamed residents.

**Date / Time:** March 11, 1972; sightings reported between approximately 9:25 PM and 10:45 PM MST.

**Location:** Calgary, Alberta (specifically the Braxton Road S.W. area and other residential locations).

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 11, 1972, multiple residents across Calgary observed a brilliant, star-like object in the western sky. Accounts varied slightly in detail: some witnesses described the object as stationary, while others noted a slow, wandering, or weaving motion (left to right). One witness reported the object traveling from south to north. Observations were made both with the naked eye and through optical aids, including 8x30 and 8x50 binoculars. 

The author of one report, observing from their home, initially mistook the light for an aircraft with landing lights. Another witness, alerted by a neighbor to a "funny looking 'Sputnik,'" tracked the object for ten minutes. Cst. R.M. Lequesne and his son-in-law observed the object from a kitchen window, noting it appeared to hover. Several witnesses reported that the object disappeared rapidly or dropped below the horizon upon the approach of a light aircraft or after a period of 15 to 35 minutes of observation.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as circular and significantly brighter than a standard star (estimated at ten times brighter). Physical descriptions included a yellow center with blue fringes, shifting to brilliant white when viewed through field glasses. Other witnesses noted a multi-colored appearance (green, red, and blue) or a yellow core with a black periphery and an aurora of light blue surrounded by crimson. Estimated altitudes ranged from 500–1,000 feet to 5,000–6,000 feet. The object was silent and exhibited slow, wandering, or weaving movements, followed by a very rapid departure.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP, led by Cst. R.M. Lequesne, conducted an extensive investigation, interviewing multiple witnesses and deeming them reliable. Official inquiries were made to the McCall Field Control Tower and commercial air traffic, all of which reported no radar returns within a 30-mile radius and no aircraft in the vicinity. The Calgary Armed Forces Base confirmed no military exercises were occurring. 

The author of one report attempted to document the event using a MANKYA SEKOR 35MM camera with a telescopic lens. While some witnesses were initially puzzled, John Findlay, Assistant Chief Technician of the Calgary Planetarium, identified the object as the planet Venus, noting its magnitude of -3.8 and how atmospheric conditions can cause a star to appear to move or change color. Following this consultation, Cst. Lequesne concluded that the object was Venus, and many witnesses subsequently agreed with this assessment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 布拉克斯顿西南路（Braxton Road S.W.）11111号的平民居民、布拉克斯顿西南路11127号的平民居民及其家人、加拿大壳牌石油公司（Shell Oil Canada Ltd.）的平民雇员、报告作者（摄影师）、岳父、邻居、R.M. 勒凯恩警官（Cst. R.M. Lequesne）、勒凯恩警官的女婿，以及多位未具名的居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年3月11日；目击报告时间约为山区标准时间（MST）晚上9:25至10:45之间。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省卡尔加里（具体为布拉克斯顿西南路区域及其他住宅区）。

**目击经过：** 1972年3月11日晚，卡尔加里多地的居民观察到西侧天空中出现了一个明亮的星状物体。各方的描述细节略有差异：一些目击者称该物体处于静止状态，而另一些人则注意到它有缓慢的游移或左右摇摆的动作。有一名目击者报告称该物体由南向北移动。观察方式包括肉眼观测以及使用8x30和8x50双筒望远镜等光学辅助设备。

其中一份报告的作者在自家观察时，起初误以为该光点是开启了着陆灯的飞机。另一名目击者在邻居提醒下看到了一个“看起来很奇怪的‘人造卫星’”，并对该物体进行了十分钟的追踪。R.M. 勒凯恩警官和他的女婿从厨房窗户观察到了该物体，并指出它似乎处于悬停状态。多名目击者报告称，当轻型飞机靠近时，或者在观察了15至35分钟后，该物体迅速消失或降至地平线以下。

**物体描述：** 该物体被一致描述为圆形，且亮度远超普通恒星（估计亮度为其十倍）。物理特征描述包括：中心呈黄色，边缘带有蓝色光晕；通过双筒望远镜观察时，颜色会转变为耀眼的白色。其他目击者则注意到它呈现出多种颜色（绿色、红色和蓝色），或是中心为黄色、外围为黑色，并被深红色的浅蓝色光环所包围。估计高度从500–1,000英尺到5,000–6,000英尺不等。该物体全程保持静默，表现出缓慢的游移或摇摆运动，随后迅速离开。

**调查/后续：** 由R.M. 勒凯恩警官领导的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）进行了广泛的调查，采访了多名目击者，并认为他们证词可靠。官方对麦考尔机场（McCall Field）控制塔和民航交通进行了查询，对方均报告称在30英里半径内未发现雷达回波，且附近没有飞机。卡尔加里武装部队基地也证实当时没有进行任何军事演习。

其中一份报告的作者曾尝试使用配备长焦镜头的MANKYA SEKOR 35毫米相机记录这一事件。尽管一些目击者起初感到困惑，但卡尔加里天文馆的助理首席技术员约翰·芬德利（John Findlay）将该物体鉴定为金星，并指出其星等为-3.8，大气条件可能导致恒星看起来在移动或变色。在咨询过后，勒凯恩警官得出结论认为该物体即为金星，许多目击者随后也认同了这一评估。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Three employees of Gulf Oil Ltd. (Harbour Grace, Nfld.), two individuals located at the Gulf Branch Office (names redacted), one additional redacted civilian, and Cst. R.L. Taylor (RCMP).

**Date / Time:** November 6, 1971, at approximately 4:00 PM.

**Location:** Harbour Grace, Newfoundland (Conception Bay, near Harbour Grace Island).

**Sighting:** On November 6, 1971, at 4:00 PM, multiple witnesses at the Gulf Oil Ltd. branch office in Harbour Grace observed an unidentified object while looking east toward Harbour Grace Island. Accounts of the event vary significantly between the witnesses. One group of witnesses observed the object for approximately 15 minutes as it appeared over the north end of the island, moved behind it, reappeared over the center, and finally emerged over the south end. Another witness reported observing the object for approximately 20 minutes, noting it crossed the island in a northerly direction at an altitude of roughly 10 feet above the ground. This witness described the movement as non-linear, stating the object moved back and forth several times before heading toward the southern end of the island and disappearing off the tip of Feather Point. This witness emphasized that the object moved in every direction at a very high rate of speed as daylight faded. Conversely, three employees of Gulf Oil Ltd. reported that the object was a large flock of birds, likely ducks, flying in an up-and-down motion while moving south into Conception Bay. These witnesses claimed to be close enough to be certain of their identification.

**Object:** Descriptions of the object were inconsistent. Some witnesses described it as a round disc with a bubble on top, or alternatively as a round ball or diamond shape, dark grey or black in color. This group estimated the object was two and a half miles away, noting it appeared to fall at times and rise at others before disappearing behind drifting clouds. Another witness described the object as being approximately four feet in diameter, noting it was very distinct against the sky, particularly due to the contrast provided by light-colored clouds. The Gulf Oil employees, however, identified the object as a large flock of birds.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation led by Cst. R.L. Taylor. Official documentation includes a formal statement from a redacted civilian, which was witnessed and signed by Cst. Taylor. The investigation noted that weather conditions were clear with some clouds, though one witness described the atmosphere as slightly hazy over the island. Cst. Taylor’s final report concluded that the object was "definitely a flock of birds" and determined that no further action was necessary, despite the conflicting descriptions provided by other witnesses regarding the object's shape, size, and erratic, high-speed flight patterns.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 海湾石油有限公司（Gulf Oil Ltd.，位于纽芬兰省海港格雷斯）的三名员工、两名位于海湾石油分公司的个人（姓名已删减）、一名额外的平民（姓名已删减），以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员 R. L. 泰勒（R. L. Taylor）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年11月6日下午约4:00。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省海港格雷斯（海港格雷斯岛附近的康塞普申湾）。

**目击经过：** 1971年11月6日下午4:00，海湾石油有限公司海港格雷斯分公司的多名目击者在向东眺望海港格雷斯岛时，观察到了一个不明物体。目击者对事件的描述存在显著差异。其中一组目击者观察该物体约15分钟，看到它出现在岛屿北端，移动到岛后，又在岛屿中心重新出现，最后从南端显现。另一名目击者报告称观察该物体约20分钟，指出它以离地约10英尺的高度向北横穿岛屿。该目击者形容其运动轨迹并非直线，称物体在前往岛屿南端并从羽毛角（Feather Point）尖端消失前，曾多次来回移动。该目击者强调，随着天色渐暗，该物体以极高的速度向各个方向移动。相反，海湾石油有限公司的三名员工报告称，该物体是一大群鸟（很可能是鸭子），在向南飞入康塞普申湾时呈现出上下起伏的飞行姿态。这些目击者声称他们距离足够近，可以确定其身份。

**物体描述：** 对该物体的描述并不一致。一些目击者将其描述为顶部带有气泡的圆形盘状物，或圆形球体、菱形，颜色为深灰色或黑色。这组目击者估计物体距离约两英里半，并指出它有时看起来会下坠，有时又会上升，随后消失在漂浮的云层后。另一名目击者描述该物体直径约四英尺，并指出它在天空中非常清晰，特别是与浅色云层形成了鲜明对比。然而，海湾石油公司的员工则认定该物体是一大群鸟。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警由 R. L. 泰勒警员带队进行了调查。官方文件包括一份由一名平民（姓名已删减）提供的正式陈述，该陈述由泰勒警员见证并签字。调查记录显示，当时天气晴朗，伴有少量云层，尽管有一名目击者称岛屿上空的大气略显朦胧。泰勒警员的最终报告结论认为，该物体“绝对是一群鸟”，并判定无需采取进一步行动，尽管其他目击者对物体的形状、大小以及不规则的高速飞行模式提供了相互矛盾的描述。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Multiple individuals (names redacted)

**Date / Time:** January 20, 1979, and January 28, 1979; between 4:30 AM and 7:45 AM Atlantic Standard Time

**Location:** Sheffield, New Brunswick, and the Trans Canada Highway

**Sighting:** 
The event involves a prolonged sighting reported by multiple witnesses in the Sheffield, New Brunswick area. The documentation provides two distinct dates for the occurrence: January 20, 1979, and January 28, 1979. In both instances, the sighting took place during the early morning hours, specifically between 4:30 AM and 7:45 AM. 

Witnesses observed the phenomenon while positioned in a car and at a stationary location within Sheffield, as well as while traveling along the Trans Canada Highway. The sighting was characterized by its significant duration, lasting approximately 3 hours and 15 minutes. Throughout this period, the witnesses observed the object under clear weather conditions.

**Object:** 
The object was consistently described as round to oval in shape. Regarding its visual characteristics, the object initially appeared red in color before transitioning to white. Witnesses noted that the object exhibited fluctuations in the intensity of the light it projected throughout the duration of the sighting. No specific sound or mechanical movement was documented in the provided reports, nor were specific size dimensions recorded beyond the visual description of its shape and light intensity.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation was handled by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP), specifically by CST Peel of the Fredericton Detachment. Official records indicate that the sighting lasted for a total of 3 1/4 hours. The files conclude with the note that there is no other relevant information available regarding the event. No sketches or detailed meteorological data beyond the general observation of "clear conditions" were included in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:

**日期 / 时间：** 1979年1月20日及1979年1月28日；大西洋标准时间凌晨4:30至上午7:45之间

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省谢菲尔德（Sheffield, New Brunswick）及横贯加拿大公路（Trans Canada Highway）

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及新不伦瑞克省谢菲尔德地区多名目击者报告的长时间目击事件。相关记录提供了两个不同的发生日期：1979年1月20日和1979年1月28日。在这两次事件中，目击均发生在清晨时段，具体时间为凌晨4:30至上午7:45之间。

目击者在车内、谢菲尔德境内的固定地点以及沿横贯加拿大公路行驶时观察到了这一现象。此次目击事件的显著特点是持续时间极长，约为3小时15分钟。在此期间，目击者是在天气晴朗的条件下观察到该物体的。

**物体描述：**
该物体被一致描述为圆形至椭圆形。在视觉特征方面，该物体起初呈现红色，随后转变为白色。目击者指出，在整个目击过程中，该物体所投射的光线强度存在波动。现有报告中未记录到任何特定的声音或机械运动，也未记录除形状和光强视觉描述之外的具体尺寸数据。

此案由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）负责调查，具体由弗雷德里克顿分局的皮尔（Peel）警官处理。官方记录显示，目击事件总共持续了3小时15分钟。档案结尾注明，关于该事件没有其他相关信息。提供的文档中未包含任何草图，除“天气晴朗”这一一般性观察外，也未包含详细的气象数据。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two tractor-trailer operators, several other subjects in the Whitehorse area.

**Date / Time:** November 16, 1975, at approximately 4:20 AM Y.C.

**Location:** Mile 21 to Mile 31, Whitehorse-Carmacks Highway, near Fox Lake, Yukon.

**Sighting:** At approximately 4:20 AM on November 16, 1975, two tractor-trailer operators were traveling south on the Whitehorse-Carmacks Highway. While the vehicle was in the vicinity of Fox Lake (reported as Mile 21 in one account and Mile 31 in another), the operators observed an object descend toward them, maneuvering similarly to a helicopter, until it positioned itself over the rear of their trailer. At the time of the sighting, the sky was under a thin overcast. 

The object proceeded to travel in the same direction as the truck, maintaining a speed slightly greater than the truck’s 55 mph pace. After a brief period of travel, the object ascended at a "fantastic speed," moving in an arc toward the north and disappearing over some hills. The primary witnesses observed the object for a duration of between 25 and 35 seconds. Simultaneously, several other subjects located in the Whitehorse area reported witnessing a sudden, intense brightness in the sky lasting for a few seconds, though these individuals did not observe the object itself.

**Object:** The object was described as being significantly larger than the tractor-trailer. It emitted an intense, eye-straining light characterized by a very white center and bluish edges. This illumination was powerful enough to light up the surrounding area for approximately one mile in all directions, creating conditions comparable to daylight. The object demonstrated high maneuverability and extreme speed during its ascent. No specific sound was noted in the reports.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the Whitehorse RCMP detachment. Following the initial report, the details were transmitted via telecommunications to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre in Ottawa for further review. No additional sketches or specific meteorological data beyond the "thin overcast" condition were provided in the available documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两名半挂卡车司机，以及怀特霍斯（Whitehorse）地区的其他几名目击者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年11月16日，育空时间（Y.C.）凌晨4:20左右。

**地点：** 育空地区怀特霍斯至卡马克斯（Whitehorse-Carmacks）公路21英里至31英里处，靠近狐狸湖（Fox Lake）。

**目击经过：** 1975年11月16日凌晨4:20左右，两名半挂卡车司机正驾车沿怀特霍斯至卡马克斯公路向南行驶。当车辆行至狐狸湖附近时（有报告称在21英里处，另有报告称在31英里处），司机们观察到一个物体向他们俯冲而来，其机动方式类似于直升机，随后该物体悬停在他们拖车的后上方。目击时，天空有薄云覆盖。

该物体随后与卡车同向行驶，速度略高于卡车每小时55英里的时速。在短暂伴随行驶后，该物体以“惊人的速度”上升，向北划出一道弧线，随后消失在山丘后。主要目击者观察该物体的时间持续了25至35秒。与此同时，位于怀特霍斯地区的其他几名目击者报告称，天空中出现了持续几秒钟的突发性强光，但这些人并未直接观察到物体本身。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体明显比半挂卡车大得多。它发出的光芒极其强烈，令人目眩，中心呈亮白色，边缘呈蓝色。这种光照强度极大，足以将周围约一英里范围内的区域照亮，宛如白昼。该物体在上升过程中展现出了极高的机动性和极快的速度。报告中未提及任何特定的声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已报告给怀特霍斯皇家加拿大骑警（RCMP）分局。初步报告提交后，相关细节通过电信传输至渥太华的国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心进行进一步审查。现有文档中未提供除“薄云覆盖”之外的其他草图或具体气象数据。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_09_-_Pages_24.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Jim Bett, who was alone in his car, though other cars were parked at the pit observing the object.

**Sighting:** On October 28, 1975, at 0515Z, an object was observed hovering over the slag pit at Murray Mine on Highway 144 in Sudbury. The object hovered for a minute, departed at extremely high speed eastward towards Highway 17, then returned for another minute before leaving again in the same direction.

**Object:** The object was described as hat-shaped (cup and saucer), very bright, comparable to looking at a 150-watt bulb from a couple of feet away. It was positioned at an altitude of about 500 feet and featured a band of bright gold around it, approximately three-quarters of the way up. The object made no noise.

**Aftermath:** The total duration of the sighting was approximately two minutes. Mr. Bett phoned the information to the OPP while driving home from work, and the OPP relayed the report to CFS Falconbridge.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_09_-_Pages_24.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Jim Bett，当时他独自在车内，但矿坑处还有其他车辆停着观察该物体。

**目击：** 1975年10月28日0515Z，在萨德伯里144号公路的默里矿（Murray Mine）矿渣坑上方观察到一个物体。该物体悬停了一分钟，随后以极高速度向东朝17号公路方向飞离，之后又返回悬停了一分钟，最后再次向同一方向离开。

**Witnesses:** A resident located 9 miles west of Alexis Creek and two loggers located 23 miles away.

**Sighting:** On November 2, 1962, at approximately 2230Z, an unidentified object was observed traveling at a very low altitude in an east to west direction. The object made a gradual descent followed by a "terrific explosion."

**Object:** The object was described as cylindrical and resembling a propane tank.

**Aftermath:** The USAF radar site at Puntzi Lake (5207 North 12410 West) was unable to track the object on radar. Reports indicated that parts were breaking off and burning. The Senior Director of the 25 NORAD Region advised that there were no known overdue aircraft in the area.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_22_-_Pages_63.report_summary_zh:
