CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Bill (William) Muncaster, Francis (Fran) Muncaster, Rick Muncaster, Leonard Erickson, Bernice Erickson, Brian Blaine, Allen Blaine, Tom Moberg, and Eric Poulsen.

**Date / Time:** April 5, 1981, at approximately 20:15 hours (8:15 PM); follow-up sighting reported April 14, 1981.

**Location:** Rimbey, Alberta (specifically 10 miles east of the town).

**Sighting:** On the evening of April 5, 1981, a group of seven witnesses—Bill, Francis, and Rick Muncaster, Leonard and Bernice Erickson, and Brian and Allen Blaine—observed an unidentified object near Rimbey. The sighting occurred at dusk under cloudy, windy conditions and lasted for 20 minutes. Bill Muncaster reported the object hovering 200 feet above the tree line, approximately a quarter-mile from his residence. The object remained stationary for a period before moving twice, covering roughly a half-mile each time at a slow speed of 10–15 mph in a northerly direction before disappearing. While the Muncasters and Ericksons provided detailed descriptions of the object's shape, the other witnesses (Blaines) primarily observed the flashing lights due to the darkness.

A separate report was filed on April 14, 1981, by Tom Moberg and Eric Poulsen, who also observed two flashing red lights. This subsequent sighting was investigated by the Penhold tracking station, which identified the lights as two aircraft flying in formation.

**Object:** The primary object observed on April 5 was described as bell-shaped and bluish-grey in color. It featured two large flashing red lights spaced 100 to 200 feet apart. A distinct white beam of light, resembling a spotlight, emanated from the center of the object and struck the ground. In the April 14 incident, the objects were identified as two aircraft flying in formation; their appearance was attributed to strong headwinds that reduced their ground speed to near zero. The pilots had extinguished their side lights, leaving only the flashing red tail lights visible, and the observed "tipping" or movement was attributed to the pilots searching for a more favorable slipstream.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Rimbey RCMP Detachment conducted an investigation into the April 5 sighting, contacting the Number 43 Radar Squadron in Red Deer on April 7, 1981, to rule out weather balloons, though the squadron could provide no data. The report was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre in Ottawa. Regarding the April 14 sighting, the RCMP consulted Bill Wright for assistance. Transport Canada eventually confirmed to the Rimbey Detachment that two helicopters were operating in the area at the time of the Moberg/Poulsen sighting. The final documentation was copied to the Planetary Sciences Section of the National Research Council.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 比尔（威廉）·芒卡斯特 (Bill (William) Muncaster)、弗朗西斯（弗兰）·芒卡斯特 (Francis (Fran) Muncaster)、里克·芒卡斯特 (Rick Muncaster)、伦纳德·埃里克森 (Leonard Erickson)、伯尼斯·埃里克森 (Bernice Erickson)、布莱恩·布莱恩 (Brian Blaine)、艾伦·布莱恩 (Allen Blaine)、汤姆·莫伯格 (Tom Moberg) 和埃里克·波尔森 (Eric Poulsen)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1981年4月5日，约20:15（晚上8:15）；后续目击报告发生于1981年4月14日。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省林比 (Rimbey)（具体位置为该镇以东10英里处）。

**目击经过：** 1981年4月5日傍晚，七名目击者——比尔、弗朗西斯和里克·芒卡斯特，伦纳德和伯尼斯·埃里克森，以及布莱恩和艾伦·布莱恩——在林比附近观测到了一个不明物体。目击事件发生在黄昏时分，当时天气多云且有风，持续了20分钟。比尔·芒卡斯特报告称，该物体悬停在他住所外约四分之一英里处，树线以上200英尺的高度。该物体保持静止一段时间后移动了两次，每次以10-15英里/小时的低速向北移动约半英里，随后消失。芒卡斯特一家和埃里克森一家对物体的形状提供了详细描述，而其他目击者（布莱恩一家）由于天色昏暗，主要观察到了闪烁的灯光。

1981年4月14日，汤姆·莫伯格和埃里克·波尔森提交了一份单独的报告，他们也观察到了两盏闪烁的红灯。此次后续目击事件由彭霍尔德 (Penhold) 跟踪站进行了调查，该站将这些灯光识别为两架编队飞行的飞机。

**物体描述：** 4月5日观测到的主要物体被描述为钟形，呈蓝灰色。它带有两盏相距100至200英尺的大型闪烁红灯。一道类似探照灯的明显白光从物体中心射出并照射在地面上。在4月14日的事件中，这些物体被确认为两架编队飞行的飞机；其外观特征归因于强劲的逆风，使它们的对地速度几乎降为零。飞行员关闭了侧灯，只留下了闪烁的红色尾灯，而观察到的“倾斜”或移动则被归因于飞行员在寻找更理想的气流。

**调查/后续：** 林比皇家骑警 (RCMP) 分局对比尔·芒卡斯特报告的4月5日目击事件进行了调查，并于1981年4月7日联系了位于红鹿市 (Red Deer) 的第43雷达中队以排除气象气球的可能性，但该中队无法提供相关数据。报告随后被转交至渥太华的国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心。关于4月14日的目击事件，皇家骑警咨询了比尔·赖特 (Bill Wright) 以寻求协助。加拿大交通部最终向林比分局证实，在莫伯格和波尔森目击事件发生时，有两架直升机在该地区作业。最终文件被抄送至国家研究委员会行星科学部门。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_24_-_Pages_69.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed individual (interviewed by the RCMP).

**Date / Time:** June 30, 1965.

**Location:** Wollaston Lake District, Saskatchewan, Canada.

**Sighting:** On June 30, 1965, an unnamed witness observed an unidentified object in the sky over the Wollaston Lake District. The witness provided a specific visual estimation of the object’s size relative to their field of vision, noting that when viewed with the naked eye, the object appeared to be approximately 1/8 of an inch across, as if it were a mark placed on a piece of paper. The witness emphasized that this measurement was taken while the object was at an estimated altitude of 15,000 feet. The witness further clarified that the object would have been considerably larger in physical dimensions had it been closer to the earth’s surface.

**Object:** The object was described primarily by its visual scale at altitude. While it appeared to be 1/8 of an inch across at 15,000 feet, the report stresses that this is an angular measurement and the object’s actual physical size would be significantly greater if it were at ground level. No specific details regarding color, sound, or specific movement patterns were recorded in the available documentation, other than its presence in the sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Constable C.K.G. Conrad of the La Ronge Detachment filed the official report on August 6, 1965. This filing was a direct follow-up to a memorandum from the Officer Commanding (O.C.) of the Criminal Investigation Branch (C.I.B.) dated July 30, 1965. 

During the administrative processing of the file, a correction was made regarding the object's recorded size; a previous report had incorrectly documented the size as "about a quarter of an eightieth across," which was subsequently rectified to the 1/8-inch estimation. The final report was forwarded by Inspector E.S.W. Batty of the Prince Albert Sub-Division to the Commanding Officer in Regina for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_24_-_Pages_69.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名匿名人士（由加拿大皇家骑警进行访谈）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1965年6月30日。

**地点：** 加拿大萨斯喀彻温省，沃拉斯顿湖区（Wollaston Lake District）。

**目击经过：** 1965年6月30日，一名匿名目击者在沃拉斯顿湖区上空观测到一个不明物体。目击者对该物体相对于其视野的大小给出了具体的视觉估算，指出用肉眼观察时，该物体看起来大约有1/8英寸宽，就像在纸上留下的一个标记。目击者强调，这一测量是在该物体处于约15,000英尺高度时进行的。目击者进一步说明，如果该物体距离地面更近，其实际物理尺寸将会大得多。

**物体描述：** 该物体的描述主要基于其在高空中的视觉比例。虽然它在15,000英尺高度看起来有1/8英寸宽，但报告强调这是一个角测量值，如果该物体位于地面，其物理尺寸将显著更大。除其出现在天空中这一事实外，现有文档中未记录关于颜色、声音或具体运动模式的详细信息。

**调查 / 后续：** 此项调查由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）进行。拉龙日（La Ronge）分遣队的C.K.G.康拉德（C.K.G. Conrad）警官于1965年8月6日提交了正式报告。该备案是针对刑事调查处（C.I.B.）指挥官于1965年7月30日发出的备忘录所作的直接后续行动。

在档案的行政处理过程中，对物体记录的大小进行了更正；此前的一份报告曾错误地将其大小记录为“约八十分之一英寸的四分之一”，随后被更正为1/8英寸的估算值。最终报告由阿尔伯特王子城（Prince Albert）分区督察E.S.W.巴蒂（E.S.W. Batty）转发给里贾纳（Regina）的指挥官以供进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lynne Wanamaker, Lorraine Parkhouse, and Maureen Connor.

**Date / Time:** September 25, 1968, at 9:15 PM PDT.

**Location:** The intersection of Moscrop and Barker Streets, Burnaby, BC.

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 25, 1968, at approximately 9:15 PM PDT, three witnesses—Lynne Wanamaker, Lorraine Parkhouse, and Maureen Connor—were positioned at the intersection of Moscrop and Barker Streets in Burnaby, BC. The witnesses observed two bright orange lights situated in the northwest sky. The weather conditions at the time of the sighting were reported as clear. 

The observation lasted for a total duration of 10 minutes. During this time, the lights exhibited a distinct swaying motion. One of the two lights remained stationary, while the second light performed an anti-clockwise rotation, eventually coming to a stop directly below the top light. The witnesses noted that the lights eventually faded away, moving in a westerly direction. No sounds were reported in connection with the objects throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** The objects were described as two bright orange lights, visually comparable to street lights. In terms of size and positioning, they appeared to be 1 1/2 inches in diameter (as perceived by the witnesses) and were spaced approximately 1.5 diameters (or 4 inches) apart. The movement was characterized by a swaying motion, with one light remaining stationary while the other executed an anti-clockwise rotation before settling into a position beneath the stationary light. No auditory phenomena were associated with the objects.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the event, the witnesses contacted the Department of Transport (DOT) at the Vancouver International Airport. The DOT officials advised the witnesses to report the incident to the local police. Consequently, the Burnaby RCMP detachment was contacted and subsequently reached out to the airport control tower to verify if other reports had been filed. The airport tower confirmed that no other UFO reports had been received regarding the event.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 琳恩·瓦纳梅克 (Lynne Wanamaker)、洛林·帕克豪斯 (Lorraine Parkhouse) 和莫琳·康纳 (Maureen Connor)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月25日，太平洋夏令时间 (PDT) 晚上9:15。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比市，莫斯克罗普街 (Moscrop Street) 与巴克街 (Barker Street) 的交叉路口。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月25日晚，约太平洋夏令时间晚上9:15，三名目击者——琳恩·瓦纳梅克、洛林·帕克豪斯和莫琳·康纳——位于不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比市的莫斯克罗普街与巴克街交叉路口。目击者观察到西北方天空中出现了两道明亮的橙色光芒。据报告，当时天气状况晴朗。

观测过程持续了10分钟。在此期间，这些光点呈现出明显的摇摆运动。其中一个光点保持静止，而另一个光点则进行了逆时针旋转，最终停在上方光点的正下方。目击者注意到，这些光点最终向西移动并逐渐消失。在整个目击过程中，未听到与这些物体相关的任何声音。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两道明亮的橙色光芒，视觉上类似于路灯。就大小和位置而言，它们看起来直径约为1.5英寸（目击者的感知），彼此间隔约1.5个直径（或4英寸）的距离。其运动特征为摇摆式移动，其中一个光点保持静止，另一个则执行逆时针旋转，随后停留在静止光点的下方。这些物体未伴随任何听觉现象。

**调查/后续：** 事件发生后，目击者联系了温哥华国际机场的交通部 (DOT)。交通部官员建议目击者向当地警方报告此事。随后，目击者联系了本拿比皇家骑警 (RCMP) 分局，警方随即与机场控制塔取得联系，以核实是否还有其他相关报告。机场控制塔确认，未收到任何关于此次事件的其他不明飞行物报告。

**Witnesses:** George Lumb

**Date / Time:** November 14, 1968, at 8:00 PM

**Location:** A farm residence approximately 6 miles north of Rocky Mountain House, Alberta

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 14, 1968, at approximately 8:00 PM, George Lumb was on foot, crossing a road to visit a neighbor’s residence. During this time, he observed an unidentified object in the sky. The weather conditions were noted as clear and dark. Mr. Lumb observed the object traveling from the southwest toward the northeast. He noted that the object’s flight path followed the same course regularly taken by jet aircraft in that area. However, he emphasized that the object was moving at an extremely high rate of speed—significantly faster than any jet he had previously observed—and notably lacked the engine noise typically produced by jets flying over the region. The total duration of the sighting was approximately 2 to 3 minutes.

**Object:** The object was observed at a high altitude, which prevented the witness from distinguishing its specific physical shape. However, Mr. Lumb described its visual appearance as resembling "two light bulbs together." The lighting configuration consisted of a green light at the front and a red light at the back. The object moved at an extremely high rate of speed and was completely silent throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of multiple reports detailing the account of George Lumb regarding the sighting near Rocky Mountain House. The reports confirm the witness's location (a farm 6 miles north of the town), the specific time (8:00 PM), and the environmental conditions (clear and dark). The investigation notes highlight the witness's comparison of the object's trajectory to known jet flight paths, specifically emphasizing the discrepancy between the object's high velocity and lack of noise compared to conventional aircraft. No further official follow-up or meteorological data beyond the witness's observation of "clear and dark" conditions was recorded in these pages.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 乔治·兰姆 (George Lumb)

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年11月14日，晚上8:00

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省落基山庄 (Rocky Mountain House) 以北约6英里处的一处农场住宅

**目击经过：** 1968年11月14日晚上8点左右，乔治·兰姆正步行穿过一条马路去拜访邻居。在此期间，他观察到天空中出现了一个不明物体。当时天气晴朗且夜色深沉。兰姆先生观察到该物体从西南方向朝东北方向飞行。他注意到该物体的飞行路线与该地区喷气式飞机的常规航线一致。然而，他强调该物体的飞行速度极快——远超他以往见过的任何喷气式飞机——且明显缺乏喷气式飞机飞越该地区时通常会产生的引擎轰鸣声。整个目击过程持续了约2到3分钟。

**物体描述：** 由于该物体处于高空，目击者无法辨别其具体外形。不过，兰姆先生将其外观描述为“两个连在一起的灯泡”。其灯光配置为前方一盏绿灯，后方一盏红灯。该物体以极高的速度移动，且在整个目击过程中完全静音。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案包含多份详细记录乔治·兰姆关于落基山庄附近目击事件的报告。报告确认了目击者的位置（镇以北6英里的农场）、具体时间（晚上8:00）以及环境条件（晴朗且黑暗）。调查记录强调了目击者将该物体的轨迹与已知喷气式飞机航线进行的对比，特别指出了该物体的高速度与缺乏噪音这一特征，与常规飞机存在显著差异。除目击者关于“晴朗且黑暗”的天气描述外，这些文件中未记录进一步的官方后续调查或气象数据。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Donald Lynn, his wife, and their four children (aged 8–15 years).

**Date / Time:** November 12, 1968 (primary report); conflicting/erroneous dates noted in file include November 6, 1968, and November 13, 1958. Time recorded as 6:00 PM – 6:30 PM MST.

**Location:** Near Barons, Alberta (Lethbridge area).

**Sighting:** The Lynn family, consisting of Donald Lynn, his wife, and their four children, observed an unidentified object in the sky while near Barons, Alberta. The sighting occurred between 6:00 PM and 6:30 PM MST. The witnesses reported that the object appeared to be "quite low" in the sky. It was first sighted in the southwest, moved gradually toward the west, then shifted back to the southwest before finally disappearing over the horizon. While the primary case file identifies the date as November 12, 1968, other documents within the same file inconsistently record the event as occurring on November 6, 1968, or November 13, 1958.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped. It exhibited a distinct color-changing property, transitioning between bright red and yellow-orange. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented as report L2007, with internal references to correspondence CIB2986/5. The report was forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre in Ottawa for analysis. The Lethbridge Weather Office provided an official assessment of the sighting, concluding that the object was, in all probability, the planet Venus. The weather office noted that on the date in question, Venus rose at an angle of 15 degrees from the southwest at 4:52 PM MST and set at 6:52 PM MST, which aligns with the duration and trajectory reported by the witnesses.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 唐纳德·林恩（Donald Lynn）、他的妻子以及他们的四个孩子（年龄在8至15岁之间）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年11月12日（主要报告）；档案中记录的冲突/错误日期包括1968年11月6日和1958年11月13日。记录时间为山区标准时间（MST）下午6:00至6:30。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省巴伦斯（Barons）附近（莱斯布里奇地区）。

**目击经过：** 林恩一家（包括唐纳德·林恩、他的妻子及其四个孩子）在阿尔伯塔省巴伦斯附近观察到了天空中出现的一个不明物体。目击事件发生在山区标准时间下午6:00至6:30之间。目击者称，该物体在天空中的位置“相当低”。它最初出现在西南方，逐渐向西移动，随后又转回西南方，最后消失在地平线以下。虽然主要案卷将日期确定为1968年11月12日，但同一档案中的其他文件却不一致地记录该事件发生于1968年11月6日或1958年11月13日。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形。它表现出明显的变色特性，在亮红色和橙黄色之间转换。据报告没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件被正式记录为报告L2007，内部参考编号为CIB2986/5。报告被转交至渥太华的加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心进行分析。莱斯布里奇气象局对此次目击事件提供了官方评估，结论是该物体极有可能是金星。气象局指出，在相关日期，金星于山区标准时间下午4:52从西南方以15度角升起，并于下午6:52落下，这与目击者报告的持续时间和轨迹相吻合。

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was formally reported to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) detachment in Fredericton, New Brunswick. Following the initial report, the case was documented and subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) for further review and inclusion in their official UFO records.

**Witnesses:** Miss Heather Webb, her mother Joan Webb, and CST J Broomfield of the Kelowna detachment.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** William Lester (also identified as William Lester Calsall), School Principal, and eleven other individuals.

**Date / Time:** November 27, 1968, at 6:40 PM CST.

**Location:** Caronport, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 27, 1968, at approximately 6:40 PM CST, a group of twelve individuals—led by school principal William Lester (also referred to as William Lester Calsall)—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The weather conditions at the time were clear with a few broken clouds. The object remained stationary in the sky for a duration of 20 minutes. Following this stationary period, the object began moving in a south-east direction. The witnesses engaged in a pursuit of the object, following it in a car for a distance of 20 miles. Throughout this pursuit, which contributed to a total sighting duration of over one hour, the witnesses noted that the distance between their vehicle and the object consistently increased, preventing them from closing the gap.

**Object:** The object was described as having no defined shape. Visually, it appeared as a very strong, flickering white light, which was surrounded by red flickering lights along its outer edge. Estimates regarding the object’s dimensions and proximity varied slightly in the documentation, with some notes describing the object as being 300 to 400 feet in size, while other records from the same investigation refer to the object being 300 to 400 feet away. No sound or specific mechanical movement was reported other than its stationary hovering and subsequent steady travel to the south-east.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was officially documented and filed by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Moose Jaw Detachment in Saskatchewan. The investigation recorded the specific meteorological conditions (clear with broken clouds) and the logistical details of the witnesses' 20-mile pursuit. No further information regarding the origin of the object or a definitive explanation was provided in the available case files.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年11月27日，中部标准时间（CST）下午6:40。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省卡伦波特（Caronport, Saskatchewan）。

**目击经过：** 1968年11月27日傍晚，中部标准时间下午6:40左右，由学校校长威廉·莱斯特（亦称威廉·莱斯特·卡尔萨尔）带领的一组十二人目击了一个不明空中现象。当时天气晴朗，有少量碎云。该物体在天空中保持静止状态长达20分钟。随后，物体开始向东南方向移动。目击者们驱车对该物体进行了追逐，行程达20英里。在整个追逐过程中（总目击时长超过一小时），目击者注意到他们与物体之间的距离不断拉大，始终无法缩短差距。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体没有明确的形状。从视觉上看，它表现为一个非常强烈、闪烁的白光，外缘环绕着红色的闪烁灯光。关于物体尺寸和距离的估计在文档中略有出入，一些记录描述该物体大小为300至400英尺，而同一调查中的其他记录则称该物体距离目击者300至400英尺。除静止悬停及随后向东南方向平稳移动外，未报告任何声音或特定的机械运动。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）萨斯喀彻温省穆斯乔（Moose Jaw）分局正式记录并归档。调查记录了当时的气象条件（晴天伴有碎云）以及目击者20英里追逐过程的后勤细节。现有案卷中未提供关于该物体来源的进一步信息或明确的解释。

**Object:** The object was described as spherical in shape and emitted a bright, intense white glow. It was observed traveling at a very high rate of speed in a south-southwest direction. The object maintained an estimated altitude of approximately 1,000 feet throughout the sighting. Notably, the object did not leave any trail or exhaust plume behind it.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The event was documented as an official sighting report occurring in clear weather conditions. The primary investigation notes focus on the physical description of the object and the reported electromagnetic effects on the witnesses' vehicle (headlight malfunction and engine instability). No further follow-up actions or sketches were noted in the provided documentation.

The sighting was formally documented and reported by the RCMP Carlyle Detachment. The investigation and subsequent filing of the report were conducted in strict compliance with the RCMP Operational Manual CO-AIR protocols.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_23_-_Pages_66.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. JV Birt and family, RCMP Staff Sgt JS Barber, RCMP Technician Mr. WE Sedwick, and Const. WU Goodhand.

**Sighting:** On March 3, 1967, at 0205Z, witnesses observed an object while in Yorkton. Mr. Birt and his family were at their home at 13 Lincoln Ave, while RCMP personnel were either traveling on Broadway or at the RCMP radio room in the Federal Building on 3rd Ave.

**Object:** The object was described as very bright, changing colors from red to orange to white and back again. It was low on the horizon to the west and appeared round in shape.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted from CANRADSON Yorkton to CANFORCHED for the CFOC UFO report, with a note indicating it was for Dr. Millman at the NRC.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_23_-_Pages_66.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** JV Birt 先生及其家人、皇家骑警（RCMP）参谋中士 JS Barber、皇家骑警技术员 WE Sedwick 先生以及警员 WU Goodhand。

**目击：** 1967 年 3 月 3 日 0205Z，目击者在约克顿（Yorkton）观察到一个物体。Birt 先生及其家人当时位于林肯大道 13 号的家中，而皇家骑警人员则在百老汇街上或位于第三大道的联邦大楼内的皇家骑警无线电室中。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为非常明亮，颜色在红色、橙色和白色之间不断变换。它位于西方的低空，形状呈圆形。

**后续：** 该报告由约克顿 CANRADSON 发送至 CANFORCHED 以供 CFOC UFO 报告使用，并附有说明，指出该报告是提供给国家研究委员会（NRC）的 Millman 博士。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Multiple civilians (including a service station attendant, residents of Prince George, a member of the Civic Properties Commission, Mr. and Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], and employees of B.C. Bearing and Engineering and the City of Prince George).

**Date / Time:** January 1, 1969, between 5:00 P.M. and 7:00 P.M. PST.

**Location:** Prince George, BC (specifically Fifth Avenue near Alward, Burden, and Watrous Streets; Ospika Blvd).

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 1, 1969, a series of sightings occurred across Prince George. At 5:00 P.M., multiple witnesses, including a service station attendant, observed an object while driving near Fifth Avenue and Alward/Burden Streets; one witness pulled into a Shell Service Station to alert others. At 5:15 P.M., Mr. and Mrs. [redacted] observed an object while traveling by taxi on Fifth Avenue near Watrous Street. At 5:20 P.M., employees of B.C. Bearing and Engineering and the City of Prince George reported an object while traveling on 5th Avenue. A separate family reported a sighting at 5:30 P.M. while driving on Ospika Blvd. Additionally, a witness reported observing the object through binoculars between 6:30 P.M. and 7:00 P.M. The sightings were characterized by the object’s movement, with some witnesses noting it gained altitude and changed brightness.

**Object:** The object was described as having a yellowish-orange or dull orange glow. It was generally perceived as spherical or round, though some witnesses noted a square attachment at the bottom with diagonal straps across the top portion. Estimates of its size ranged from 3 to 4 feet in diameter to 1/8th to 1/20th the size of the moon. It was reported to hover at altitudes ranging from 200 feet to 10,000 feet. The object made no audible sound, and the duration of the sightings lasted between 1 and 1.5 hours.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP documented the reports as a formal complaint. An investigation conducted on January 4, 1969, discovered a device in a local backyard that matched the description of the sightings: a plastic laundry bag constructed with drinking straws, a straw cross-frame, and birthday candles intended to provide lift via hot air. The RCMP concluded that the sightings were likely caused by these homemade devices, possibly constructed by local children. Separately, the Department of Transport Radio Sound noted that a floating weather balloon was in the area on the same date, suggesting it was also a possible explanation for the sightings. A follow-up report was expected at the time of the initial documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 多名平民（包括一名加油站服务员、乔治王子城的居民、市政物业委员会的一名成员、[已删节]夫妇、[已删节]先生，以及不列颠哥伦比亚省轴承与工程公司和乔治王子城市政府的员工）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月1日，太平洋标准时间下午5:00至晚上7:00之间。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省乔治王子城（具体为靠近阿尔沃德街、伯登街和沃特鲁斯街的第五大道；奥斯皮卡大道）。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月1日傍晚，乔治王子城各地发生了一系列目击事件。下午5:00，包括一名加油站服务员在内的多名目击者在第五大道与阿尔沃德街/伯登街附近开车时观察到了一个物体；其中一名目击者驶入一家壳牌加油站以提醒他人。下午5:15，[已删节]夫妇在第五大道靠近沃特鲁斯街乘坐出租车时观察到了该物体。下午5:20，不列颠哥伦比亚省轴承与工程公司和乔治王子城市政府的员工在第五大道行驶时报告了该物体。另一个家庭报告称，他们在下午5:30驾车行驶在奥斯皮卡大道时也看到了该物体。此外，一名目击者报告称在下午6:30至7:00之间通过双筒望远镜观察到了该物体。这些目击事件的特征在于物体的运动，一些目击者注意到它在上升过程中改变了亮度。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为发出黄橙色或暗橙色的光。它通常被认为是球形或圆形的，尽管一些目击者注意到其底部有一个方形附件，顶部有对角线状的带子。对其尺寸的估计范围从直径3到4英尺，到月球大小的1/8到1/20不等。据报告，它悬停在200英尺到10,000英尺的高度。该物体没有发出任何声音，目击持续时间在1小时到1.5小时之间。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）将这些报告记录为正式投诉。1969年1月4日进行的一项调查在当地一个后院发现了一个与目击描述相符的装置：一个由塑料洗衣袋制成的装置，结构包括吸管、吸管十字架，以及旨在通过热空气提供升力的生日蜡烛。加拿大皇家骑警得出结论，这些目击事件很可能是由这些自制装置引起的，可能是当地儿童制作的。另外，交通部无线电探测部门指出，当天该地区有一个漂浮的气象气球，这表明它也可能是目击事件的解释之一。在最初记录时，预计会有后续报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of Edmonton, Alberta.

**Date / Time:** February 1, 1969, at approximately 8:00 A.M.

**Location:** One mile east of Sangudo, Alberta, on Highway 43.

**Sighting:** On the morning of February 1, 1969, a civilian witness traveling west on Highway 43 near Sangudo observed two distinct aerial phenomena. At approximately 8:00 A.M., the witness first spotted a small, oblong object at a very high altitude. This object was bright white and moved toward the north at a rapid speed; it remained visible for 10 seconds. Three minutes later, the witness observed a second, much larger object. This second craft was estimated to be at an altitude of 1,000 feet. It featured a flat base and an oval top, emitting a bright white glow. Like the first, this object moved rapidly to the north and was visible for 10 seconds before disappearing. The sky at the time of the sightings was reported as heavily clouded.

**Object:** 
*   **Object 1:** Small, oblong, bright white, high altitude, rapid northward movement, 10-second duration.
*   **Object 2:** Larger, flat base with an oval top, bright white glow/lights, 1,000-foot altitude, rapid northward movement, 10-second duration.
*   **Sound:** No sound reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was reported to the Mayerthorpe RCMP detachment, which subsequently drafted a message to the Edmonton Sub-Division. Following the report, the RCMP conducted patrols in the Sangudo area, though no additional witnesses were located. The witness’s reliability was noted as unknown, though the individual claimed to have observed a similar object four years prior in British Columbia. 

The RCMP Edmonton office transmitted the report via telecommunications to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre and other relevant agencies for further review. The official file was concluded on February 4, 1969, with no further investigative action taken.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名居住在艾伯塔省埃德蒙顿的平民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月1日，上午约8:00。

**地点：** 艾伯塔省桑古多（Sangudo）以东一英里处，43号高速公路上。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月1日上午，一名平民目击者在43号高速公路上向西行驶，途经桑古多附近时，观察到了两种截然不同的空中现象。上午8:00左右，目击者首先在高空发现了一个小型长方形物体。该物体呈亮白色，正以极快的速度向北移动；其可见时长为10秒。三分钟后，目击者观察到了第二个体积大得多的物体。据估计，第二个飞行器的高度约为1,000英尺。它具有平坦的底部和椭圆形的顶部，并散发出明亮的白光。与第一个物体一样，该物体也迅速向北移动，在消失前可见时长为10秒。据报告，目击发生时天空云层浓厚。

**物体描述：** 
*   **物体1：** 小型、长方形、亮白色、高空、快速向北移动、持续10秒。
*   **物体2：** 较大、底部平坦且顶部呈椭圆形、发出明亮的白光/灯光、高度1,000英尺、快速向北移动、持续10秒。
*   **声音：** 未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 
此次目击事件被报告给了梅耶索普（Mayerthorpe）的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）分遣队，该分遣队随后起草了一份报告发送给埃德蒙顿分区。报告提交后，加拿大皇家骑警在桑古多地区进行了巡逻，但未找到其他目击者。目击者的可靠性被标注为未知，尽管该目击者声称四年前在不列颠哥伦比亚省曾观察到过类似的物体。

加拿大皇家骑警埃德蒙顿办公室通过电信将该报告传送给了国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心及其他相关机构进行进一步审查。官方档案于1969年2月4日结案，未采取进一步调查行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted], her brother, several other people in the Spruce Lake area, and additional unnamed individuals.

**Date / Time:** December 30, 1968, at 8:30 PM Atlantic Standard Time (AST).

**Location:** Spruce Lake, near St. John, New Brunswick (moving along Route 1 towards St. George, N.B.).

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 30, 1968, multiple witnesses, including Mrs. [redacted], her brother, and several other individuals in the Spruce Lake area, observed an unidentified flying object. The sighting began at 8:30 PM AST and lasted for a duration of approximately 30 to 45 minutes. The object was observed traveling along Route 1 in the direction of St. George, New Brunswick. Throughout the duration of the event, the object exhibited significant variations in altitude, ranging from as high as one mile or more above the ground to as low as a few hundred yards away from the observers. The object maintained a speed estimated between 40 and 60 mph. Only one UFO was reported during this event.

**Object:** The object was described as having a distinct "half-moon" shape, characterized by a flat bottom and a rounded top. In terms of scale, it was estimated to be roughly the size of a helicopter. The lighting configuration was noted as a yellowish-white light that fluctuated in intensity, appearing bright at times and dim at others. Additionally, the object displayed red and green lights. No specific sound was reported, and the object’s movement was described as consistent with its travel along the highway route.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented and filed by the RCMP detachment in Fredericton, New Brunswick. Local RCMP officers conducted interviews with the primary witnesses, including Mrs. [redacted] and her brother. Following these interrogations, the RCMP concluded that the witnesses were sober, credible, and reliable. Despite the thoroughness of the initial questioning, the RCMP detachment determined that no further official action was required regarding the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]女士、她的兄弟、斯普鲁斯湖（Spruce Lake）地区的几位民众，以及其他未具名的个人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年12月30日，大西洋标准时间（AST）晚上8:30。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省圣约翰（St. John）附近的斯普鲁斯湖（沿1号公路向圣乔治方向移动）。

**目击经过：** 1968年12月30日晚，包括[已删除]女士、她的兄弟以及斯普鲁斯湖地区的几位民众在内的多名目击者，观察到了一个不明飞行物。目击事件始于大西洋标准时间晚上8:30，持续了约30至45分钟。该物体被观察到沿着1号公路向新不伦瑞克省圣乔治方向移动。在整个事件过程中，该物体的高度变化显著，从离地一英里或更高处，到距离观察者仅几百码的低空不等。据估计，该物体的飞行速度在每小时40至60英里之间。此次事件中仅报告了一个不明飞行物。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为具有独特的“半月形”，特征是底部平坦、顶部呈圆形。从规模上看，估计其大小与直升机相当。其灯光配置被描述为一种黄白色的光，亮度不稳定，时而明亮，时而暗淡。此外，该物体还显示出红色和绿色的灯光。未有关于该物体发出特定声音的报告，其移动方式被描述为与公路路线保持一致。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由新不伦瑞克省弗雷德里克顿（Fredericton）的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）分队记录并归档。当地皇家骑警对主要目击者（包括[已删除]女士和她的兄弟）进行了访谈。经过询问，皇家骑警得出结论：目击者神志清醒、可信且可靠。尽管进行了详尽的初步问询，但皇家骑警分队最终决定，无需针对此次目击事件采取进一步的官方行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Paul Lucier (DPW Fireman), Fred Koch (Businessman), an unnamed adult civilian, his son, and three unnamed juveniles.

**Date / Time:** November 24, 1968; between 4:30 p.m. and 5:00 p.m.

**Location:** Whitehorse, Yukon (specifically the vicinity of Rae Street and 3rd Avenue, and the corner of 6th and Ray).

**Sighting:** 
The event involved two distinct sets of observations. In the first account, Paul Lucier and Fred Koch observed an object from the corner of 6th and Ray while looking across the Yukon River valley toward Grey Mountain. They reported the object was approximately one mile away and remained in view for 5 to 6 minutes. They described the object as mostly stationary, though it exhibited slight sideways movement while traveling in a north-south direction. During the observation, 3 to 4 pieces appeared to fall from the object. The light intensity fluctuated, becoming brighter, then dimmer, repeating this cycle 5 to 6 times before finally fading. The witnesses noted the object moved west, stopped, moved south, then east, and faded out, only to light up again.

In a separate incident on the same day, an adult civilian, his son, and three juveniles observed a "burning object" descending in the vicinity of Rae Street and 3rd Avenue. This object was recovered and turned over to the RCMP.

**Object:** 
The descriptions of the objects varied significantly based on the witness group. Lucier and Koch described the object as a rectangular, elliptical, white light. They noted it was very bright, comparable to an aircraft landing light rather than a gaseous or burning light, with a reflection near the top suggesting it was composed of two sections. It eventually separated into two parts. No sound was reported by these witnesses.

Conversely, the object recovered by the civilian group was identified as a "Professional Dry Cleaning" plastic bag with soft drink straws scotch-taped to the bottom or open end. The bottom edges of the plastic and straws showed signs of being slightly burned.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP conducted an investigation into the physical object recovered by the civilians. They concluded that the plastic bag device was the result of an experiment by unknown persons. As the investigation into the origin of the device was non-resultant and the individuals responsible could not be identified, the RCMP requested and received authorization to destroy the exhibit.

Regarding the sighting by Lucier and Koch, the Department of Transport (DOT) and airport traffic tower records were consulted; both confirmed that no small aircraft were in the area between 4:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. The witnesses did not possess binoculars or a camera to document the event further.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 保罗·卢西尔（Paul Lucier，公共工程部消防员）、弗雷德·科赫（Fred Koch，商人）、一名未具名的成年平民、其子以及三名未具名的青少年。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年11月24日；下午4:30至5:00之间。

**地点：** 育空地区怀特霍斯（具体位于雷街与第三大道路口附近，以及第六大道与雷街路口）。

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及两组截然不同的观察记录。在第一起记录中，保罗·卢西尔和弗雷德·科赫在第六大道与雷街路口，隔着育空河谷望向灰山（Grey Mountain）方向时观察到了一个物体。据他们报告，该物体距离约一英里，在视野中停留了5至6分钟。他们描述该物体基本处于静止状态，但在沿南北方向移动时表现出轻微的侧向位移。观察期间，有3到4个碎片状物体从该物体上掉落。其光强不断波动，忽明忽暗，这一循环重复了5到6次，最终逐渐消失。目击者注意到该物体向西移动后停止，随后转向南，再转向东，在消失后又再次亮起。

在同一天的另一起事件中，一名成年平民、其子及三名青少年观察到一个“燃烧的物体”降落在雷街与第三大道路口附近。该物体随后被寻获并移交给了加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）。

**物体描述：**
根据目击者群体的不同，对物体的描述存在显著差异。卢西尔和科赫将该物体描述为一个长方形的椭圆形白光。他们指出其亮度极高，更像是飞机的着陆灯，而非气体或燃烧产生的光；物体顶部附近的反射表明它由两部分组成。最终，它分裂成了两部分。目击者未报告听到任何声音。

相反，平民小组寻获的物体被确认为一个“专业干洗”塑料袋，底部或开口处用透明胶带粘着软饮吸管。塑料袋的底边和吸管有轻微烧焦的痕迹。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警对平民寻获的实物进行了调查。他们得出结论，该塑料袋装置是未知人员进行实验的产物。由于对该装置来源的调查未果，且无法确定责任人，加拿大皇家骑警申请并获得了销毁该证物的授权。

关于卢西尔和科赫的目击事件，调查人员查阅了交通部（DOT）和机场交通塔台的记录；双方均证实，下午4:00至5:00之间该区域没有小型飞机活动。目击者当时未携带双筒望远镜或照相机，无法对事件进行进一步记录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Three civilians (residents of 5 Alpine Trailer Court, Cranbrook, BC), unidentified persons (responsible for the construction of the hoax devices).

**Date / Time:** October 31, 1968, at 9:30 PM (MST).

**Location:** Cranbrook, BC (specifically observed over Mount Baker, southwest of the city, and landing on the outskirts of Cranbrook).

**Sighting:** On the night of October 31, 1968, at 9:30 PM, three civilians located at 5 Alpine Trailer Court in Cranbrook observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The primary witness, while in their backyard, spotted an object hovering over the top of Mount Baker, southwest of the city. The object moved toward the outskirts of Cranbrook, appearing to clear the mountain top before gradually descending to a landing point on the city's outskirts. The sighting lasted between 5 and 15 minutes, with one witness utilizing field glasses to observe the craft. 

Subsequent investigation into the event, referenced as case CBK2327, revealed that the sighting was a hoax. It was determined that unidentified persons had constructed "X" shaped devices made of balsam wood. These structures were placed inside plastic bags and fitted with candles attached to each end of the "X." These devices were released to float in the sky, creating the appearance of a structured craft, with observers noting debris falling from the objects as they drifted.

**Object:** The witnesses initially described the object as cigar-shaped, measuring approximately 200 feet in length and 100 feet in width, featuring indentations at each end. The craft was reported to have bright orange flashes along its sides, lights resembling portholes, and bright lights at both ends. However, the follow-up investigation clarified that the "object" was actually a series of balsam wood "X" frames encased in plastic bags and propelled by candles.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the initial report, the Cranbrook RCMP detachment dispatched patrols to the area where the object was reported to have landed; however, the search yielded no results. The investigation eventually concluded that the event was a hoax involving the release of candle-powered devices. The final report regarding this incident was forwarded by the Cranbrook Detachment to the NRC Meteor Centre, RCMP Ottawa, and other relevant divisions for documentation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 三名平民（不列颠哥伦比亚省克兰布鲁克市阿尔派恩拖车营地 5 号的居民），身份不明者（恶作剧装置的制造者）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968 年 10 月 31 日，晚上 9:30（山区标准时间）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省克兰布鲁克市（具体观测位置为该市西南方的贝克山上方，并降落在克兰布鲁克郊区）。

**目击经过：** 1968 年 10 月 31 日晚 9:30，位于克兰布鲁克市阿尔派恩拖车营地 5 号的三名平民观测到一种不明空中现象。主要目击者在后院时，发现一个物体悬停在城市西南方的贝克山顶上方。该物体向克兰布鲁克郊区移动，在越过山顶后逐渐下降，最终降落在城市郊区。目击过程持续了 5 到 15 分钟，其中一名目击者使用了双筒望远镜观察该飞行器。

针对此事件（编号 CBK2327）的后续调查显示，这是一场恶作剧。调查确定，身份不明的人员制作了由香脂木制成的“X”形装置。这些结构被放置在塑料袋内，并在“X”的每一端安装了蜡烛。这些装置被释放后漂浮在空中，营造出一种结构化飞行器的外观；观察者还注意到，当物体漂浮时，有碎片从中掉落。

**物体描述：** 目击者最初将该物体描述为雪茄状，长约 200 英尺，宽约 100 英尺，两端有凹痕。据报告，该飞行器侧面有明亮的橙色闪光，带有类似舷窗的灯光，两端也有明亮的灯光。然而，后续调查澄清，该“物体”实际上是一系列包裹在塑料袋中并由蜡烛驱动的香脂木“X”形框架。

**调查/后续：** 在接到初步报告后，克兰布鲁克皇家骑警（RCMP）分遣队派遣巡逻队前往物体据称降落的区域进行搜查，但未发现任何结果。调查最终得出结论，该事件是一场涉及释放蜡烛动力装置的恶作剧。关于此事件的最终报告已由克兰布鲁克分遣队转交给加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心、渥太华皇家骑警总部及其他相关部门进行存档。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Goulet (Prothonotary of the Amos County Court)

**Date / Time:** July 27, 1968, between 10:00 P.M. and 10:30 P.M. D.S.T. (specifically noted as 10:15 P.M. to 10:30 P.M. in secondary documentation).

**Location:** 72 - 10th Ave. East, Amos, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On the night of July 27, 1968, Mr. Goulet, the Prothonotary of the Amos County Court, was standing outside his residence at 72 - 10th Ave. East in Amos, Quebec. He observed an unidentified object in the sky, which he described as being very clear with visible stars. The sighting lasted for a duration of three to five minutes. Mr. Goulet, who is noted by authorities to possess a good knowledge of astronomy, observed the object moving in a straight line from due south to due north at a very high altitude and a very fast speed.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape and approximately the size of a grapefruit (as perceived from the observer's vantage point). It emitted a brilliant white light, which the witness compared in brightness to the "morning star" (Venus). The object made no sound during the sighting and did not leave behind any persistent train, trail, or exhaust.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by the RCMP (NBAY SUBDIV). The official report highlights that the witness is considered a reliable individual with significant astronomical knowledge. Following the collection of these details, the file was submitted for information purposes and subsequently concluded.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 古莱先生（Goulet，阿莫斯县法院书记官）

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月27日，夏令时间晚上10:00至10:30之间（辅助文档中特别注明为晚上10:15至10:30）。

**地点：** 魁北克省阿莫斯市，东第10大道72号。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月27日晚，阿莫斯县法院书记官古莱先生正站在位于魁北克省阿莫斯市东第10大道72号的住所外。他观察到天空中出现了一个不明物体，当时天空非常晴朗，可见星光。目击过程持续了三到五分钟。据当局记录，古莱先生具备良好的天文学知识，他观察到该物体在高空以极快的速度沿正南向正北的直线飞行。

**物体描述：** 该物体呈圆形，从观察者的角度看，大小约为葡萄柚般。它发出明亮的白光，目击者将其亮度比作“晨星”（金星）。目击过程中，该物体未发出任何声音，也没有留下任何持续的轨迹、尾迹或废气。

**调查 / 后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（NBAY SUBDIV）记录在案。官方报告强调，目击者被认为是一位可靠的人士，且具备深厚的天文学知识。在收集完这些详细信息后，该档案被提交以供参考，随后结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Constable S.B. Barrie (No. 24647) and his wife, Mrs. Vivian Barrie.

**Date / Time:** October 3, 1969, at approximately 8:45 PM CST.

**Location:** Near Highway 44, approximately 5 miles northwest of Rennie, Manitoba (Whiteshell area).

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 3, 1969, under rainy and misty weather conditions, Constable S.B. Barrie and his wife, Mrs. Vivian Barrie, were traveling near Highway 44 in the Whiteshell area. At approximately 8:45 PM, they observed a light that initially appeared to be a reflection on their windshield. Upon stopping their 1968 Falcon vehicle, they identified the source as an object hovering over the bush. The sighting lasted for a duration of 15 to 20 minutes. As the witnesses approached within 500 feet of the object, their vehicle experienced a total electrical failure: the electric windshield wipers stopped working, the headlights went out, and the engine stalled. Cst. Barrie attempted to restart the engine, but the attempts failed. He then exited the vehicle to observe the object more closely. Following the object's departure, the witnesses noted a lingering "heaviness" in the air and a strange odor. Once the object had vanished, the vehicle’s electrical systems and engine functioned normally again.

**Object:** The object was described as an inverted saucer shape with a flat bottom, measuring approximately 20 feet in diameter. It possessed no definite outline other than an intense, luminous pink glow. The object hovered at an altitude of 50 to 100 feet above the trees, exhibiting a rocking motion and short, jerky movements. Before disappearing, it displayed an intense, white, snake-like tail that extended downwards toward the earth. The object eventually departed toward the southwest at an excessive, high rate of speed, moving noiselessly.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was officially reported to Corporal D.E. Shaw at the Pine Falls RCMP Detachment on October 29, 1969. The report documents the specific mechanical failures experienced by the witnesses' 1968 Falcon and the environmental conditions (rain and mist) present at the time of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 警员 S.B. 巴里（S.B. Barrie，警号 24647）及其妻子薇薇安·巴里（Vivian Barrie）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年10月3日，中部标准时间（CST）晚上8:45左右。

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省雷尼（Rennie）西北约5英里处的44号公路附近（怀特谢尔地区）。

**目击经过：** 1969年10月3日晚，在阴雨多雾的天气条件下，警员 S.B. 巴里和他的妻子薇薇安·巴里驾车行驶在怀特谢尔地区的44号公路附近。晚上8:45左右，他们观察到一道光，起初以为是挡风玻璃上的反光。在停下他们的1968年款猎鹰（Falcon）汽车后，他们确认光源是一个悬停在灌木丛上方的物体。目击过程持续了15到20分钟。当目击者靠近至距离该物体500英尺（约152米）处时，他们的车辆发生了彻底的电力故障：电动雨刷停止工作，前大灯熄灭，引擎熄火。巴里警员尝试重启引擎，但未能成功。随后他走出车外，以便更近距离地观察该物体。在该物体离开后，目击者注意到空气中残留着一种“沉重感”和一种奇怪的气味。当物体消失后，车辆的电气系统和引擎又恢复了正常运作。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个底部平坦的倒扣碟状物，直径约20英尺（约6米）。除了强烈的粉红色光芒外，它没有明确的轮廓。该物体悬停在树木上方50到100英尺（约15至30米）的高度，呈现出摇晃的姿态，并伴有短促、抽动式的移动。在消失前，它展现出一条强烈的、蛇状的白色尾迹，向下延伸至地面。最终，该物体以极高的速度向西南方向无声离去。

**调查/后续：** 该事件于1969年10月29日正式报告给派恩福尔斯（Pine Falls）皇家骑警分局的 D.E. 肖（D.E. Shaw）下士。报告记录了目击者所驾驶的1968年款猎鹰汽车发生的具体机械故障，以及目击时存在的环境条件（雨和雾）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** H. Curry, H. Curry’s son, Cst. F.W. Pushka, and several unnamed civilian residents of the Qu'Appelle District (including three persons deemed sincere/reliable by the RCMP and two individuals located at a home farmyard 1.5 miles south of Qu'Appelle).

**Date / Time:** August 4, 1968, at approximately 4:00 a.m.

**Location:** A farmyard near Qu'Appelle, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** At approximately 4:00 a.m., multiple witnesses observed an unidentified object hovering over a barn. One witness initially observed the object hovering 100 feet above their house, moving in an oval pattern for 10 minutes before waking their father. Upon returning outside, they observed the object hovering above the barn, moving away and returning. Other witnesses reported the object hovering for durations ranging from one to four minutes. Observations included the object spinning, stopping, and then darting at right angles from point to point. One witness noted the object moved to the southeast before departing. While some witnesses reported the object made no noise, another individual in the area reported hearing a distinct whirling or whining sound. Despite the proximity of the object, witnesses noted that no light was cast onto the ground or the barn. Due to the proximity of the object (estimated at 150 yards), some witnesses took cover.

**Object:** The object was described as circular or saucer-shaped, measuring 25–30 feet in diameter. Color descriptions varied, including "illuminated," "dull orange," and "greyish-white." It featured revolving lights on the bottom. The object maintained an altitude of approximately 80–100 feet (or twice the height of the barn). It exhibited erratic movement, including spinning, hovering, and rapid, angular transit.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by the RCMP Indian Head detachment and the Regina Identification Section. Statements were formally taken on August 9, 1968. Investigators discovered circular marks in the pasture near the barn, ranging from 4.5 to 5 feet in diameter; reports vary between finding four or six marks, with three described as well-pronounced. The Regina Identification Section examined these marks but could provide no explanation. Meteorological reports for the time of the sighting (2:30 a.m. to 4:55 a.m.) confirmed cloudy skies with lightning, thunder, and rain. While the RCMP deemed three of the witnesses "sincere and reliable," they ultimately concluded the investigation, noting that no photographs or diagrams were made of the ground marks as they were deemed of no significance. The reliability of the report from the two individuals 1.5 miles south of town remains officially categorized as unknown.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** H·柯里（H. Curry）、H·柯里的儿子、F·W·普什卡警官（Cst. F.W. Pushka），以及夸佩尔（Qu'Appelle）地区的几位匿名平民（包括三名被加拿大皇家骑警认定为真诚可靠的人，以及两名位于夸佩尔以南1.5英里处一处农家院落的个人）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月4日，凌晨4:00左右。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省夸佩尔附近的一处农家院落。

**目击经过：** 凌晨4:00左右，多名目击者观察到一个不明物体悬停在谷仓上方。一名目击者最初观察到该物体悬停在自家房屋上方100英尺处，以椭圆形轨迹移动了10分钟，随后叫醒了父亲。当他们再次回到室外时，观察到该物体悬停在谷仓上方，时而飞离，时而返回。其他目击者报告称，该物体悬停的时间从一分钟到四分钟不等。观察到的现象包括物体旋转、停止，然后以直角从一点疾驰至另一点。一名目击者指出，该物体在离开前向东南方向移动。虽然一些目击者报告称该物体没有发出任何声音，但该地区的另一名个人报告听到了一种明显的旋转声或呜呜声。尽管物体距离很近，但目击者注意到它没有将光线投射到地面或谷仓上。由于物体距离极近（估计为150码），一些目击者进行了躲避。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形或碟形，直径为25至30英尺。颜色描述各不相同，包括“发光”、“暗橙色”和“灰白色”。其底部有旋转的灯光。该物体保持在约80至100英尺（或谷仓高度的两倍）的高度。它表现出不规则的运动，包括旋转、悬停以及快速的直角移动。

**调查/后续：** 调查由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）印第安角（Indian Head）分遣队和里贾纳（Regina）鉴定部门进行。1968年8月9日正式记录了证词。调查人员在谷仓附近的牧场发现了直径为4.5至5英尺的圆形痕迹；关于痕迹数量的报告不一，有四处或六处之说，其中三处被描述为非常明显。里贾纳鉴定部门检查了这些痕迹，但无法提供任何解释。目击时间段（凌晨2:30至4:55）的气象报告证实当时天空多云，伴有闪电、雷声和降雨。虽然加拿大皇家骑警认为其中三名目击者“真诚可靠”，但最终结束了调查，并指出由于认为地面痕迹没有意义，因此未对其进行拍照或绘制图表。来自镇南1.5英里处两名个人的报告可靠性在官方记录中仍被归类为未知。

**Witnesses:** Elizabeth McKibbon (nurse), Melita Dyson (nurse's aid), Robert Clark, Sam Holwell, Jesse Turnbull and family, Stephan Macdonald, and Bernard Dyson.

**Sighting:** On 13 November 1978 at approximately 1600 hours, witnesses observed a bright red circular object high in the sky, surrounded by a red glow and emitting a short jet-plane-like trail. The object was stationary for about 30 minutes and viewed with binoculars. A second, larger object appeared, and both moved toward each other on a collision course before changing direction and entering a dark grey cloud formation, which dissipated as they passed through. Earlier that afternoon, between 1300 and 1400 hours, other witnesses observed fireballs hitting the ground near Martins Pond.

**Object:** Bright red circular objects with a red glow and trail; fireballs.

**Aftermath:** Miss McKibbon and school teacher Stephan Macdonald checked the area at Martins Pond, where fireballs had reportedly burned approximately one acre of bog land. No debris was found. Numerous residents observed the events, and some are showing concern regarding the local water supply.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 护士 Elizabeth McKibbon、护士助理 Melita Dyson、Robert Clark、Sam Holwell、Jesse Turnbull 及其家人、Stephan Macdonald 和 Bernard Dyson。

**目击：** 1978年11月13日约1600时，目击者观察到一个高空中的明亮红色圆形物体，周围有红光，并留下一条类似喷气式飞机的短尾迹。该物体静止约半小时，并被用双筒望远镜观察。随后出现了第二个类似的较大物体，两者在移动中似乎处于碰撞航线上，但在接近时改变方向并进入一团深灰色云层，云层在物体穿过后消散。当天下午1300至1400时之间，其他目击者观察到火球击中 Martins Pond 附近的地面。

**物体：** 带有红光和尾迹的明亮红色圆形物体；火球。

**后续：** McKibbon 小姐与教师 Stephan Macdonald 检查了 Martins Pond 地区，据报道火球烧毁了约一英亩的沼泽地。未发现任何碎片。许多居民目击了这些事件，一些居民对当地供水表示担忧。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A party of local citizens, Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted] (four individuals from Skidegate Mission, BC), and five additional citizens (totaling two groups).

**Date / Time:** January 27, 1968, at 2:15 P.M.

**Location:** Queen Charlotte City, BC (specifically observed from in front of the Apollo Bowling Alley, with the object appearing over Robertson Island in Skidegate Inlet).

**Sighting:** On the afternoon of January 27, 1968, multiple groups of witnesses observed an unidentified flying object while in the downtown area of Queen Charlotte City. The weather conditions were noted as cloudy and overcast, with a low ceiling estimated between 700 and 750 feet. 

Four witnesses from Skidegate Mission, standing near the Apollo Bowling Alley, observed the object at an altitude of approximately 400 to 500 feet. They reported that the object hovered for a duration of three to five minutes. While one group of witnesses described the object arriving from and returning to the west, the Skidegate Mission group observed it moving away in a southwesterly direction using a distinct, quick zig-zag motion.

**Object:** The object was described as dark or black in color and roughly whale-shaped, resembling a helicopter but notably smaller and lacking rotors or any external moving parts. Witnesses reported that the object was completely noiseless, though it was observed emitting smoke or vapor while hovering. 

A conflicting or potentially separate explanation provided in the official file identified the object as a man-made device constructed to resemble a 45-gallon drum. This version described the object as having a body made of paper tissue with a lighted candle inside to provide the heat necessary for lift.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation into the sightings. They interviewed the witnesses and concluded that the individuals from Skidegate Mission were reliable and that their accounts should be considered credible. 

A separate investigation by the RCMP determined that the object was a man-made device constructed and launched by a local resident of Queen Charlotte City. The individual responsible for the device admitted to building it and lighting the candle to cause it to rise. The resident stated that the object was not launched with the intent of causing an unnecessary investigation. Following this explanation, the RCMP concluded the file with no further action required.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一群当地市民，包括 [已删除] 女士、[已删除] 先生、[已删除] 女士、[已删除] 先生（四人均来自不列颠哥伦比亚省斯基德盖特传教区），以及另外五名市民（共计两组）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968 年 1 月 27 日，下午 2:15。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省夏洛特皇后市（具体观测点位于阿波罗保龄球馆前方，物体出现在斯基德盖特湾罗伯逊岛上空）。

**目击经过：** 1968 年 1 月 27 日下午，多组目击者在夏洛特皇后市中心区域观测到一个不明飞行物。当时天气多云阴沉，云层较低，估计高度在 700 至 750 英尺之间。

来自斯基德盖特传教区的四名目击者站在阿波罗保龄球馆附近，观测到该物体位于约 400 至 500 英尺的高度。他们报告称，该物体悬停了三到五分钟。虽然有一组目击者称该物体是从西方飞来并返回西方，但斯基德盖特传教区的那组目击者则观察到它以一种独特的、快速的“之”字形移动方式向西南方向飞离。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为深色或黑色，大致呈鲸鱼形状，类似于直升机，但明显较小，且没有旋翼或任何外部运动部件。目击者报告称，该物体完全静音，但在悬停时会喷出烟雾或蒸汽。

官方档案中提供了一种相互矛盾或可能是独立的解释，认为该物体是一个被制成 45 加仑油桶形状的人造装置。该版本描述称，该物体主体由薄纸制成，内部点燃蜡烛以提供升力所需的热量。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对此次目击事件进行了调查。他们采访了目击者，并得出结论：来自斯基德盖特传教区的目击者表现可靠，他们的陈述应被视为可信。

加拿大皇家骑警的另一项调查确定，该物体是由夏洛特皇后市的一名当地居民制造并放飞的人造装置。该负责人承认制造了该装置，并点燃蜡烛使其升空。该居民表示，放飞该物体并非为了引起不必要的调查。在这一解释之后，加拿大皇家骑警结案，无需采取进一步行动。

**Witnesses:** Several civilians in the community of Westport, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On August 22, 1969, at approximately 10:30 P.M., witnesses observed a bright, round, red object stationary in the sky east of the community. The sky was clear. The object had blue smoke trailing above it in the shape of the letter "S". It appeared to be sparkling around its circumference before exploding with pieces flying in all directions. Following the explosion, the object decreased in size, resembling a distant star, and slowly descended behind a hill. The total observation time was about five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, round, red light. Estimates of its size varied from one to two feet in diameter to 25 feet in diameter. One witness estimated it was 8 miles above the earth and initially thought it was a jet plane on fire.

**Aftermath:** Witnesses reported a loud jukebox playing nearby, but heard no noise from the explosion. The RCMP Baie Verte detachment investigated the report, interviewed witnesses, and forwarded a message (BV 54) to the O.C. St. John's Sub/Division. The witnesses were considered steady and reliable.

**见证者：** 纽芬兰韦斯特波特社区的几位平民。

**目击：** 1969年8月22日晚上10点30分左右，目击者观察到一个明亮的圆形红色物体停留在社区东部的天空中。当时天空晴朗。该物体上方拖着蓝色的烟雾，形状呈“S”型。它在爆炸前圆周闪烁，随后碎片向四面八方飞散。爆炸后，物体体积缩小，看起来像一颗遥远的星星，并缓慢下降到山后。总观测时间约为五分钟。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个明亮的圆形红光。对其尺寸的估计各不相同，从直径一到两英尺到直径25英尺不等。一位目击者估计它距离地面约8英里，最初以为是一架着火的喷气式飞机。

**后续：** 目击者报告说附近有自动点唱机在播放音乐，但没有听到爆炸声。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）贝维尔特分遣队对此进行了调查，采访了目击者，并将一份报告（BV 54）转发给了圣约翰斯分区指挥官。目击者被认为是稳重可靠的人。
