CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Local camera enthusiasts.

**Sighting:** On Wednesday, June 19th, 1968, at approximately 10:30 p.m., an unidentified flying object was observed in the sky above Frobisher Bay moving in a northerly direction.

**Object:** The object appeared to be a star moving very slowly across the sky in a west to east direction. It disappeared sometime after midnight.

**Aftermath:** The Department of Transport meteorological officer in Frobisher Bay expressed the opinion that the object was an experimental or weather balloon at a height of well over 100,000 feet. The report notes there were no reports of landings by "little green men or other weird sun-could creatures" or reports that "all our women are pregnant." The document was forwarded by D. Davies, Regional Administrator, and received by Ian Halliday of the Dominion Observatory, who noted it was forwarded as a non-meteoric sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 当地的摄影爱好者。

**目击：** 1968年6月19日星期三晚上约10:30，在弗罗比舍湾上空观察到一个不明飞行物，向北移动。

**物体：** 该物体看起来像一颗星星，正非常缓慢地从西向东横穿天空。它在午夜后消失。

**后续：** 弗罗比舍湾的交通部气象官员认为该物体是一个高度超过10万英尺的实验性气球或气象气球。报告指出，没有关于“小绿人或其他怪异生物”着陆的报告，也没有关于“我们所有的妇女都怀孕了”的报告。该文件由区域行政官D. Davies转发，并由自治领天文台的Ian Halliday收到，他注明该报告是作为非流星目击事件转发的。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Jean Widish, John Widish, Janet Widish, Debbie Widish

**Date / Time:** January 31, 1977, at approximately 9:30 PM

**Location:** Rosenburg/Arborg, Manitoba (Land NBR NW19-24-3E)

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 31, 1977, at approximately 9:30 PM, the Widish family—Jean, John, and their daughters Janet and Debbie—were watching television when they noticed interference on their set. Looking out the window, they observed a strange light located approximately one mile west of their residence. The object hovered at an altitude of 40 to 50 feet above the ground. The family watched the object for approximately half an hour as it revolved very slowly. Eventually, the object appeared to descend or move behind a bush, where it disappeared from their line of sight. The weather conditions at the time were described as very clear, quiet, and windless. Additionally, Jean Widish reported that her husband, John, had witnessed a similar object in June 1976; that previous sighting occurred 300 yards away and featured yellow lights.

**Object:** The object was described as being approximately the size of a television screen. It featured red and blue revolving lights (or flashers). The object moved with a slow, revolving motion and remained visible for a duration of about 30 minutes before disappearing behind vegetation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was filed by Constable J.L.P. McMahon of the RCMP Arborg Detachment. Following the sighting, the RCMP conducted a patrol of the area to search for physical evidence; however, this search revealed no tracks or unusual markings on the ground. The RCMP also conducted inquiries with the nearest neighbors, all of which yielded negative results regarding similar sightings or unusual activity.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 简·威迪什 (Jean Widish)、约翰·威迪什 (John Widish)、珍妮特·威迪什 (Janet Widish)、黛比·威迪什 (Debbie Widish)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年1月31日，晚上约9:30

**地点：** 马尼托巴省罗森堡/阿伯格 (Rosenburg/Arborg)（土地编号 NW19-24-3E）

**目击经过：** 1977年1月31日晚上约9:30，威迪什一家——简、约翰以及他们的女儿珍妮特和黛比——正在看电视时，注意到电视信号出现了干扰。他们向窗外望去，发现距离住所西侧约一英里处有一个奇怪的光源。该物体悬停在离地约40到50英尺的高度。全家人观察了该物体约半小时，它在空中缓慢旋转。最终，该物体似乎下降或移动到了灌木丛后，从他们的视线中消失了。当时的天气状况被描述为非常晴朗、安静且无风。此外，简·威迪什还提到，她的丈夫约翰曾在1976年6月目击过类似的物体；那次目击事件发生在300码外，当时看到的物体带有黄色的灯光。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为大约电视屏幕大小。它带有红色和蓝色的旋转灯（或闪光灯）。该物体以缓慢的旋转方式移动，并持续可见约30分钟，随后消失在植被后方。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 阿伯格分局的警官 J.L.P. 麦克马洪 (J.L.P. McMahon) 提交。目击事件发生后，加拿大皇家骑警对该地区进行了巡逻以搜寻物理证据；然而，搜寻结果显示地面上没有任何痕迹或异常标记。警方还向附近的邻居进行了询问，但均未获得有关类似目击事件或异常活动的反馈。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Earl Jeffrey (former pilot), Ruth Totten, Joseph Shaw (reporting witness)

**Date / Time:** January 2, 1977, at 8:20 P.M. Atlantic Standard Time (initial specific sighting); recurring sightings reported by Ruth Totten from late October 1976 through January 1977.

**Location:** Bible Hill and Upper Economy, Colchester County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** 
On January 2, 1977, at 8:20 P.M. AST, Earl Jeffrey, a former pilot, observed an unidentified object from the Weather Station in Bible Hill. He tracked the object for approximately 10 minutes as it moved at a very slow speed in a westerly direction, positioned at an angle of roughly 20 degrees above the horizon. Mr. Jeffrey explicitly stated that the object was neither a star nor an aircraft.

Separately, Ruth Totten reported a series of recurring sightings beginning in late October 1976. She observed a round, oval-shaped object in the direction of Cape Blomidon on every clear night. According to Ms. Totten, the object typically appeared at dusk and remained visible until before midnight. She noted that the object would initially appear high in the sky and gradually move closer to the ground as the night progressed. She described the object as remaining stationary for periods of time before moving slowly away.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a round or oval-shaped sphere, smaller than the moon but brighter than the surrounding stars. Earl Jeffrey observed it as a pulsating sphere that cycled through red, white, and blue colors. Ruth Totten described the object as having red and green lights that flashed from the top, bottom, or ends of the craft. The object was reported to be silent, leaving no trail or exhaust behind it.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation was initiated after Joseph Shaw, an employee at the Bible Hill Weather Station, received public inquiries and a letter from Ruth Totten regarding her persistent sightings. Mr. Shaw formally reported the matter to the RCMP on January 13, 1977. Cpl. E.E. Best of the Parrsboro Detachment conducted follow-up investigations, which included obtaining a formal statement from Ruth Totten on January 20, 1977. A telex summarizing the reports and the investigation was forwarded by the RCMP on January 19, 1977.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 厄尔·杰弗里（Earl Jeffrey，前飞行员）、露丝·托滕（Ruth Totten）、约瑟夫·肖（Joseph Shaw，报告目击者）

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年1月2日，大西洋标准时间晚上8:20（首次具体目击）；露丝·托滕报告称从1976年10月下旬至1977年1月期间有多次反复目击。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省科尔切斯特县，圣经山（Bible Hill）及上埃科诺米（Upper Economy）。

**目击经过：** 
1977年1月2日大西洋标准时间晚上8:20，前飞行员厄尔·杰弗里在圣经山气象站观测到一个不明物体。他追踪该物体约10分钟，当时物体正以极慢的速度向西移动，位于地平线上方约20度的角度。杰弗里先生明确表示，该物体既不是恒星，也不是飞机。

此外，露丝·托滕报告称，从1976年10月下旬开始，她经历了一系列反复的目击事件。在每个晴朗的夜晚，她都能在布洛米顿角（Cape Blomidon）方向观察到一个圆形或椭圆形的物体。据托滕女士描述，该物体通常在黄昏时分出现，并一直可见到午夜前。她注意到，物体起初出现在高空，随着夜色渐深，会逐渐向地面靠近。她描述该物体有时会保持静止，随后缓慢移开。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为一个圆形或椭圆形的球体，比月亮小，但比周围的星星更亮。厄尔·杰弗里观察到它是一个会发出脉冲光的球体，颜色在红、白、蓝之间循环变换。露丝·托滕则描述该物体顶部、底部或末端闪烁着红光和绿光。据报告，该物体飞行时保持静止，没有留下任何尾迹或废气。

**调查/后续：** 
此次调查始于圣经山气象站员工约瑟夫·肖收到公众咨询以及露丝·托滕关于其持续目击事件的来信之后。肖先生于1977年1月13日正式向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了此事。帕斯伯勒（Parrsboro）分队的E.E.贝斯特（E.E. Best）下士进行了后续调查，其中包括于1977年1月20日获取了露丝·托滕的正式陈述。加拿大皇家骑警于1977年1月19日转发了一份总结了相关报告及调查情况的电传。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Arisma Gauvin, Mrs. Martial Gauvin, Isabelle Gauvin

**Date / Time:** February 2, 1977, at 9:27 PM AST

**Location:** Morais Office Road, Gloucester County, New Brunswick (facing north)

**Sighting:** On the evening of February 2, 1977, at 9:27 PM AST, three witnesses—Arisma Gauvin, Mrs. Martial Gauvin, and Isabelle Gauvin—were located on Morais Office Road in Gloucester County, New Brunswick. While facing north under a clear sky illuminated by a full moon, the witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately two minutes. According to the witnesses, the object traveled in a northerly direction before the lights extinguished and the object disappeared from view.

**Object:** The object was described as a formation of lights rather than a solid, discernible mass. It consisted of three flashing red lights arranged in a triangular pattern, accompanied by one very brilliant, central red light. When viewed from the ground, the witnesses estimated the object’s size to appear roughly one foot in length. The estimated altitude of the object was comparable to that of a standard single-engine aircraft. The movement was described as a steady progression toward the north. The observation concluded when the central bright light went out, followed by the remaining lights turning off, resulting in the object's disappearance.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by Constable T. Aucoin of the RCMP Caraquet Detachment. The official report notes that the sky conditions were clear with a full moon at the time of the sighting. At the time the report was filed, no further information or additional leads were available regarding the nature of the object.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 阿里斯马·戈万 (Arisma Gauvin)、马歇尔·戈万夫人 (Mrs. Martial Gauvin)、伊莎贝尔·戈万 (Isabelle Gauvin)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年2月2日，大西洋标准时间晚上9:27

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省格洛斯特县，莫赖斯办公路 (Morais Office Road)（朝北方向）

**目击经过：** 1977年2月2日晚9:27，三名目击者——阿里斯马·戈万、马歇尔·戈万夫人和伊莎贝尔·戈万——位于新不伦瑞克省格洛斯特县的莫赖斯办公路上。在满月照亮的晴朗夜空下，他们面向北方时观察到了一种不明空中现象。目击过程持续了约两分钟。据目击者称，该物体向北飞行，随后灯光熄灭，物体从视野中消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一组灯光，而非一个坚实、可辨认的实体。它由三个呈三角形排列的闪烁红灯组成，中心还伴有一盏非常明亮的红灯。从地面观察，目击者估计该物体看起来约一英尺长。其估计高度与标准的单引擎飞机相当。其运动轨迹被描述为向北的平稳行进。当中心亮光熄灭，随后其余灯光也随之关闭时，观察结束，物体随即消失。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 卡拉凯特分局的 T. 奥昆 (T. Aucoin) 警官记录在案。官方报告指出，目击时天空晴朗，且为满月。在报告提交时，关于该物体性质的更多信息或线索尚不明确。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Bobiwash and four other persons.

**Date / Time:** February 3, 1977, at 10:15 local time.

**Location:** A wooded area near Orell Street, Garson, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On February 3, 1977, at approximately 10:15 local time, Mr. Bobiwash and four other individuals were present in a wooded area near Orell Street in Garson, Ontario. During this time, the group observed two distinct aerial objects. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately ten minutes. Following the observation, Mr. Bobiwash left the area and returned to his home specifically to contact the local air base to report the incident. No further information regarding the event was documented beyond this initial report.

**Object:** The witnesses reported observing two separate objects simultaneously:
*   **Object 1:** Described as square-shaped and featuring a green light.
*   **Object 2:** Described as round-shaped and featuring a flashing green light.
*   **Movement/Sound:** No specific movement patterns or auditory details were recorded in the provided documentation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The official records note that the weather conditions at the time of the sighting were described as "scattered" with a visibility range of 8 to 10 miles. The documentation consists of reports detailing the witnesses' account and the subsequent action taken by Mr. Bobiwash to notify the air base. No further official investigation notes, sketches, or RCMP interrogation transcripts were provided in the source material.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 博比瓦什（Bobiwash）先生及其他四人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年2月3日，当地时间10:15。

**地点：** 安大略省加森（Garson）奥雷尔街（Orell Street）附近的林区。

**目击经过：** 1977年2月3日当地时间约10:15，博比瓦什先生和其他四人在安大略省加森市奥雷尔街附近的一片林区。期间，该群体观察到了两个独特的空中物体。目击过程持续了约十分钟。观察结束后，博比瓦什先生离开现场并返回家中，专门联系了当地空军基地报告了这一事件。除这份初步报告外，没有记录关于该事件的更多信息。

**物体描述：** 目击者称同时观察到了两个独立的物体：
*   **物体1：** 描述为方形，带有一盏绿灯。
*   **物体2：** 描述为圆形，带有一盏闪烁的绿灯。
*   **运动/声音：** 提供的文档中未记录具体的运动模式或声音细节。

**调查/后续：** 官方记录指出，目击时的天气状况被描述为“零散云层”，能见度范围为8至10英里。相关文档包括了目击者的陈述报告，以及博比瓦什先生随后通知空军基地的行动记录。原始资料中未提供进一步的官方调查记录、草图或加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的审讯笔录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Gary Wayne Robertson, Valerie Robertson, Simon Wright, and Mark Wright, all residing at the same residence in Clinton Creek, YT.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on February 4, 1977, at 8:50 PM Yukon Standard Time. The weather was slightly cloudy with light cover, and visibility was excellent with a visible full moon. The observation was made from the witnesses' residence.

**Object:** The object was described as a singular, extremely bright light that pulsed and changed colors between light blue, red, and green. It was positioned approximately 30 degrees above the horizon in the southern sky. The movement was slow, consistent, and uniform, with no erratic behavior. The object was estimated to be approximately 13 miles away, though there was no indication of its actual size or distance.

**Aftermath:** The sighting lasted for approximately 1.5 hours. The Whitehorse RCMP detachment reported that there were no reports of any aircraft in the immediate area of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Gary Wayne Robertson、Valerie Robertson、Simon Wright 和 Mark Wright，均居住在育空地区克林顿溪的同一住所。

**目击：** 事件发生于1977年2月4日育空标准时间晚上8:50。当时天气微云，有轻微遮盖，能见度极佳，满月清晰可见。观察地点为见证者的住所。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个单一且极其明亮的光点，呈现脉冲状，颜色在浅蓝色、红色和绿色之间变换。它位于南部天空，地平线上方约30度处。物体的移动缓慢、持续且均匀，没有任何不规则的动作。据估计该物体距离约13英里，但没有关于其确切大小或距离的迹象。

**后续：** 目击持续了约1.5小时。白马市皇家骑警分局报告称，在目击区域附近没有收到任何飞机活动的报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miles Ward, who was observed by his mother, Mrs. Joyce Ward, who called in the report.

**Sighting:** On February 15, 1977, at 4:00Z, a single light was observed following the witness while he was on his ski-doo. The object traveled northwest toward Lake Manitoba and descended behind trees as if to land.

**Object:** A single light.

**Aftermath:** The report notes that there was no sound made by the UFO. The incident was reported to CFB Portage La Prairie and forwarded to DREO and NDHQ.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Miles Ward，由其母亲 Mrs. Joyce Ward 观察到并报告。

**目击：** 1977年2月15日 4:00Z，目击者在驾驶雪地摩托时，发现一个单体光点跟随他。该物体向西北方向朝曼尼托巴湖移动，并降落在树后，看起来像是要着陆。

**物体：** 一个单体光点。

**后续：** 报告指出该不明飞行物未发出任何声音。此事件已报告给 CFB Portage La Prairie，并转交至 DREO 和 NDHQ。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Eric Brown, Rob Brown (brother), and Glen Morse (step-brother).

**Sighting:** On February 16, 1977, at 23:00Z, the witnesses observed an object from their home in Lavigne, Ontario. The weather was described as very clear with low clouds on the horizon.

**Object:** The object was described as a whitish blue light, flat and long, oriented horizontally. It was moving very fast from south to north, positioned just above the clouds on the horizon. The duration of the sighting was a minute and a half. The object traveled in a straight flight path with no turns and left no contrails.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted from 22nd NORAD Headquarters North Bay to the National Defence Operation Centre in Ottawa and the National Research Council.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Eric Brown、Rob Brown（兄弟）和 Glen Morse（继兄弟）。

**目击：** 1977年2月16日23:00Z，目击者在安大略省拉维涅（Lavigne）的家中观察到一个物体。当时天气非常晴朗，地平线上有低云。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一道白蓝色的光，扁平且长，呈水平方向。它在地平线云层上方快速从南向北移动。目击持续时间为一分半钟。物体呈直线飞行，没有转弯，也没有留下凝结尾迹。

**后续：** 该报告由第22北美防空司令部（NORAD）总部从北湾发送至渥太华的国防行动中心及加拿大国家研究委员会。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed civilian who requested anonymity.

**Sighting:** On April 18, 1977, at 7:20 p.m. local time, a witness observed an object over Mississippi Lake while looking through the window of a house in front of the lake. The sky was clear with the sun going down and no stars visible. The sighting lasted 3-5 minutes with no movement observed.

**Object:** The object was described as a red, round object with a tail. It was estimated to be 25 times the size of a star at 15 degrees elevation. It had an exhaust in the back that was wider than a jet's exhaust. There was also a small red flashing light to the left of the object. The object made no sound and suddenly disappeared.

**Aftermath:** The report was received by Annie on April 19, 1977, at 10:30.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名要求匿名的平民。

**目击：** 1977年4月18日当地时间晚上7点20分，一名目击者在湖前的一所房子里透过窗户观察到了一个物体。当时天空晴朗，太阳正在下山，没有星星可见。目击持续了3到5分钟，物体没有移动。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个带有尾巴的红色圆形物体。据估计，它在15度仰角处的大小是星星的25倍。它后部有排气，比喷气式飞机的排气更宽。物体左侧还有一个小的红色闪烁灯。该物体没有发出声音，并突然消失了。

**后续：** 该报告由Annie于1977年4月19日10点30分接收。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Susan Jolin, her mother, her father, and her brother.

**Date / Time:** April 18, 1977, between 0800Z and 0830Z.

**Location:** Edmonton, Alberta (Northwest quadrant of the sky).

**Sighting:** On April 18, 1977, between 0800Z and 0830Z, Susan Jolin and her family (mother, father, and brother) observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the northwest quadrant of the sky. The witnesses reported that the object was positioned well above the horizon. Throughout the duration of the sighting, the object exhibited erratic flight patterns, including hovering, dropping rapidly, pausing for a period of time, and subsequently climbing back up to near its original position. The observation was sustained for at least 30 minutes, as the object was still under observation by the family at 0830Z.

**Object:** The object was described as round in shape. In terms of scale, it appeared larger than a star but significantly smaller than the moon. A defining characteristic of the object was its continually changing color, which cycled between green, yellow, and blue. No sound was reported, and only one object was observed in that specific quadrant of the sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting occurred under clear sky conditions with some thin cirrus patches present. During the event, a weather forecaster at the unit was alerted and conducted a visual check of the sky; however, the forecaster was unable to spot the object reported by the Jolin family. No further identification of the object was established at the time of the report.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 苏珊·乔林（Susan Jolin）、她的母亲、父亲和兄弟。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年4月18日，0800Z至0830Z之间。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省埃德蒙顿（天空西北象限）。

**目击经过：** 1977年4月18日0800Z至0830Z期间，苏珊·乔林及其家人（母亲、父亲和兄弟）在天空的西北象限观测到一个不明空中现象。目击者报告称，该物体位于地平线以上相当高的高度。在整个目击过程中，该物体表现出不规则的飞行模式，包括悬停、快速下坠、短暂停留，随后又爬升回接近其原始位置的高度。观测持续了至少30分钟，因为直到0830Z时，该家人仍在观测该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形。从比例上看，它看起来比星星大，但明显比月亮小。该物体的一个显著特征是其颜色不断变化，在绿色、黄色和蓝色之间循环。未报告有任何声音，且在该天空象限内仅观测到一个物体。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生时天空晴朗，仅有少量薄卷云。事件期间，该单位的一名天气预报员接到通知并对天空进行了目视检查；然而，预报员未能发现乔林一家所报告的物体。在报告发布时，该物体未得到进一步的确认。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** LT H. Kennedy (also referred to as Capt. H. Kennedy), Capt. G. Whelan, Pte. M. Marchand, Pte. M. Ascot, the crew of a Sea King helicopter, the crew of a Tracker aircraft, and the crew of a light aircraft.

**Date / Time:** April 19, 1977 (initial sighting at dusk); April 21, 1977 (subsequent aircraft observations).

**Location:** CFB Greenwood, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of April 19, 1977, at dusk, personnel stationed at the CFB Greenwood control tower—LT H. Kennedy, Capt. G. Whelan, Pte. M. Marchand, and Pte. M. Ascot—observed two strobe-type lights positioned 1,000 to 1,500 feet above the ground. These lights were located between five and ten miles southeast of the control tower. The lights moved in tandem as a pair, executing rapid maneuvers that covered 500 to 800 feet vertically and one mile horizontally. The sighting lasted for a duration of 15 to 20 minutes. The observers noted that the lights did not fade out, nor did they travel any significant distance from the general area before they disappeared. 

A follow-up report (supplementing operational report OPS 498) indicates that on April 21, 1977, three additional aircraft—a Sea King helicopter, a Tracker aircraft, and a light aircraft—observed a UFO while closing in on Greenwood from the southeast. These aircraft were positioned at distances of 20 miles, 10 miles, and 5 miles from the base, respectively. The UFO was observed moving relative to these aircraft, performing extremely fast, split-second maneuvers.

**Object:** The objects were described as two strobe-type lights. Despite the use of binoculars by the control tower personnel, no distinct physical shape could be determined. The movement was characterized as very rapid, involving sudden vertical and horizontal shifts, as well as "split-second" maneuvers observed by the flight crews on April 21.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The control tower observers reported the sighting to local authorities and radar. Greenwood radar confirmed the presence of one aircraft target located 32 miles east of the base; however, Halifax Terminal reported no IFR (Instrument Flight Rules) traffic in the area at the time of the sighting. The reports from the flight crews and tower personnel were compiled and formally transmitted to the National Research Council in Ottawa for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** H. 肯尼迪中尉（亦被称为 H. 肯尼迪上尉）、G. 惠兰上尉、M. 马尚列兵、M. 阿斯科特列兵，以及一架海王直升机机组人员、一架追踪者飞机机组人员和一架轻型飞机机组人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年4月19日（黄昏时分首次目击）；1977年4月21日（后续飞行器观测）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省格林伍德加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Greenwood）。

**目击经过：** 1977年4月19日黄昏，驻扎在格林伍德基地控制塔的人员——H. 肯尼迪中尉、G. 惠兰上尉、M. 马尚列兵和M. 阿斯科特列兵——观察到两个频闪灯状的光点，位于地面上方1000至1500英尺处。这些光点位于控制塔东南方5至10英里处。两个光点成对移动，并进行了快速机动，垂直移动距离达500至800英尺，水平移动距离达1英里。目击持续了15至20分钟。观察者指出，这些光点在消失前并未减弱亮度，也没有离开该区域太远。

一份后续报告（补充了OPS 498行动报告）显示，1977年4月21日，另外三架飞行器——一架海王直升机、一架追踪者飞机和一架轻型飞机——在从东南方向接近格林伍德基地时观测到了一个不明飞行物（UFO）。这些飞行器当时分别距离基地20英里、10英里和5英里。据观测，该不明飞行物相对于这些飞行器进行移动，并执行了极快的、瞬间完成的机动动作。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两个频闪灯状的光点。尽管控制塔人员使用了双筒望远镜，但仍无法确定其具体的物理形状。其运动特征非常迅速，包括突然的垂直和水平位移，以及4月21日飞行机组人员所观察到的“瞬间”机动。

**调查/后续：** 控制塔观察员向当地有关部门和雷达站报告了此次目击事件。格林伍德雷达确认在基地以东32英里处存在一个飞行目标；然而，哈利法克斯终端区报告称，在目击发生时，该区域没有仪表飞行规则（IFR）下的空中交通。飞行机组人员和塔台人员的报告被汇总并正式提交至渥太华的国家研究委员会进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** One individual.

**Sighting:** On October 27, 1971, at 3:30 AM Central Standard Time, a witness driving west on PTH 1, approximately 6 miles east of Brandon, Manitoba, observed an object in the side view mirror.

**Object:** The object was bright white in color and shaped like two plates, one inverted on top of the other, with a triangular-shaped object on the top center. It appeared quite large in size and was heading east away from over PTH 1.

**Aftermath:** The object was visible for approximately 2 minutes before lifting its north side, leveling off, fading slowly, and disappearing suddenly. No further sightings have been reported to the Brandon Detachment to date.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名个人。

**目击：** 1971年10月27日中部标准时间凌晨3:30，一名目击者在曼尼托巴省布兰登以东约6英里的PTH 1公路上向西行驶时，通过侧视镜观察到一个物体。

**物体：** 该物体呈亮白色，形状像两个盘子，一个倒扣在另一个上面，顶部中心有一个三角形物体。它看起来体积很大，正向东远离PTH 1公路方向移动。

**后续：** 该物体可见约2分钟，随后其北侧抬起，恢复水平，缓慢褪色并突然消失。截至目前，布兰登分局未收到进一步的目击报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian driver and four other observers of various ages.

**Sighting:** On October 11, 1971, at 7:30 PM, the sky was heavily overcast with frequent rain squalls. The primary witness was driving on Highway 32 at Hodges Cove, Trinity Bay, Newfoundland, heading west toward the Trans-Canada Highway.

**Object:** The object was described as a brilliant white light that appeared from a westerly direction. It was joined by a series of lights, approximately nine in total, of the same brightness. The lights appeared in a diagonal line crossing the sky from west to east, then broke formation and chased each other. They moved at a fast rate of speed, remained in the area for about one minute, and then disappeared out over the bay. No noise was heard during the observation. The objects appeared to be lower than a low-flying aircraft.

**Aftermath:** The report was filed by the RCMP Clarenville Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名平民驾驶员及其他四名不同年龄的观察者。

**目击：** 1971年10月11日晚7:30，当时天空阴云密布并伴有频繁的阵雨。主要目击者当时正驾车行驶在纽芬兰省三一湾霍奇斯湾的32号公路上，向西前往横贯加拿大公路。

**物体：** 物体被描述为一道从西面出现的明亮白光。随后有约九个同样亮度的光点加入。这些光点以对角线排列从西向东横穿天空，随后打破队形并相互追逐。它们以极快的速度移动，在区域内停留约一分钟后消失在海湾上空。观测过程中未听到任何声音。物体看起来比低空飞行的飞机还要低。

**后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）克拉伦维尔分局提交。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two individuals (names redacted) and other part-time assistants employed by Alberta Hail Studies.

**Sighting:** The report details inquiries made regarding Unidentified Flying Objects reported in the Red Deer area on August 15th and 18th, 1971.

**Object:** The investigation determined that the objects were weather balloons. On August 15th, three balloons tied together with a dangling yellow railway flare were released at 11:00 P.M. near #2 Highway on the Delburne Road. On August 18th, three Radio-Sonde weather balloons with red flares were released between 11:30 P.M. and 1:00 A.M. at various locations around Red Deer.

**Aftermath:** The individuals involved admitted to the releases but refused to provide written statements. The RCMP concluded the report by stating the sightings were established as a hoax and requested that a Telex be sent to advise of this conclusion.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 两名个人（姓名已涂黑）以及阿尔伯塔冰雹研究项目（Alberta Hail Studies）的其他兼职助理。

**目击：** 该报告详细记录了对1971年8月15日和18日在红鹿市（Red Deer）地区报告的不明飞行物进行的调查。

**物体：** 调查确定这些物体是气象气球。8月15日晚上11点，在德尔伯恩路（Delburne Road）的2号高速公路附近，有人释放了三个系在一起并悬挂黄色铁路信号弹的气球。8月18日，在晚上11点30分至凌晨1点之间，在红鹿市周边不同地点释放了三个带有红色信号弹的无线电探空仪气象气球。

**后续：** 相关人员承认了这些释放行为，但拒绝提供书面陈述。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）在报告中得出结论，称这些目击事件已被证实为恶作剧，并要求发送电传以通报此结论。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. G. J. McMullen.

**Sighting:** The witness observed a bright object in the sky near midnight on February 20.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright light. Peter M. Millman, Head of Upper Atmosphere Research, concluded that the description, position, and duration of the object agreed well with the star Sirius.

**Aftermath:** The agency suggested that unusual atmospheric conditions during the Canadian winter can cause the star to change color and perform other peculiar movements when low in the sky. Calculations indicated the object would have disappeared near 1:30 a.m., which aligned with the witness's observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** G. J. McMullen 夫人。

**目击：** 目击者于 2 月 20 日午夜左右观察到天空中出现一个明亮的物体。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一道亮光。高层大气研究负责人 Peter M. Millman 得出结论，该物体的描述、位置和持续时间与天狼星（Sirius）非常吻合。

**后续：** 该机构指出，加拿大冬季异常的大气条件可能导致该恒星在低空时出现颜色变化和其他奇特的运动。计算结果显示该物体应在凌晨 1:30 左右消失，这与目击者的观察结果一致。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Bradley (employee of the Vancouver City Planning Department)

**Date / Time:** February 27, 1969, at 9:10 AM P.S.T.

**Location:** Vancouver, British Columbia (observed from the 11th floor of Vancouver City Hall)

**Sighting:** On the morning of February 27, 1969, at 9:10 AM, Mr. Bradley, an employee of the Vancouver City Planning Department, was positioned at a window on the 11th floor of City Hall. While looking toward the north, he observed an unidentified object rising from behind Grouse Mountain. The witness reported that the object ascended in a straight vertical trajectory. At the time of the sighting, the weather conditions were described as a bright, sunny day with a clear blue sky; while there was slight low-hanging ground haze, the visibility over the mountains remained clear.

**Object:** The object was described as a rocket or a similar craft. It was observed leaving a distinct white smoke trail in its wake as it rose into the air. While the witness provided this description, official follow-up notes suggest the possibility that the object may have been a jet aircraft, with the observed "smoke trail" being a condensation trail (contrail) typical of high-altitude jet traffic frequenting the area.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was formally transmitted by the RCMP Vancouver S/DIV to the NRC Meteor Centre and CANFORCEHEAD. The RCMP assessed the witness, Mr. Bradley, as a reliable individual. Regarding physical investigation, the RCMP determined they could not conduct an on-site search of the area behind Grouse Mountain, as the terrain was inaccessible without air support. No other sightings were reported in that specific area, and no further information was ascertained. The file was officially marked as concluded by S/Sgt J.W. Duggan.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 布拉德利先生（温哥华城市规划局员工）

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月27日上午9:10（太平洋标准时间）

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华（从温哥华市政厅11楼观测）

**目击经过：** 1969年2月27日上午9:10，温哥华城市规划局员工布拉德利先生站在市政厅11楼的窗边。当他向北望去时，观察到一个不明物体从松鸡山（Grouse Mountain）后方升起。目击者称，该物体呈垂直直线轨迹上升。目击发生时，天气晴朗，天空湛蓝；尽管地面有轻微的低空薄雾，但山区的能见度依然清晰。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为火箭或类似的飞行器。它在升空过程中留下了明显的白色烟迹。尽管目击者提供了上述描述，但官方后续记录指出，该物体也可能是喷气式飞机，所观察到的“烟迹”可能是高空喷气式飞机在该地区飞行时常见的凝结尾迹。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）温哥华分部正式转交给加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心及加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHEAD）。加拿大皇家骑警认为目击者布拉德利先生是一位可靠的人。关于实地调查，加拿大皇家骑警认定无法对松鸡山后方的区域进行现场搜寻，因为该地形若无空中支援将无法进入。该特定区域未收到其他目击报告，也未获得进一步信息。该档案由J.W. 杜根（J.W. Duggan）高级警长正式标记为结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Vincent Samuel Pope, Emma Anna Pope, Mariem Janet Pope, Raymond Lawrence Poland, Janet (surname unknown), and Ben Fisher.

**Date / Time:** January 22, 1969, at approximately 7:30 PM (Poland/Janet) and 9:30 PM (Fisher). Previous sightings reported by the Pope family occurred throughout 1968.

**Location:** Blaeberry area, 13 miles Northwest of Golden, B.C.; Willow Bank Mountain; Highway 1 near the Columbia River.

**Sighting:** 
On the evening of January 22, 1969, at approximately 7:30 PM, Raymond Lawrence Poland and Janet observed two bright white lights while tending to horses in a barnyard. The lights were moving in a northerly direction, spaced approximately 100 feet apart, and descended at a 45-degree angle. Poland estimated the lights were four miles away at an altitude of 300 feet. He noted that the horses had been acting strangely throughout the day. Poland stated he had witnessed similar lights five or six times over the previous year and explicitly ruled out planes, flares, or shooting stars.

Separately, at approximately 9:30 PM that same evening, local service station owner and private pilot Ben Fisher observed a fairly large white light traveling horizontally near the mountain range across the Columbia River while driving on Highway 1.

Additionally, the Pope family provided statements regarding sightings occurring in 1968. Vincent Samuel Pope reported seeing a large round light traveling south, followed by a greyish cigar-shaped object moving in the opposite direction near Willow Bank Mountain. Emma Anna Pope reported a large yellowish ball, approximately the size of the moon, moving in a south-westerly direction before it accelerated and disappeared. Mariem Janet Pope described seeing a "great big round thing" in the sky, roughly the size of a star, moving from east to west. Raymond Poland noted that he and his sister’s family had observed similar phenomena on previous occasions but had refrained from reporting them until this time.

**Object:** 
The objects were described variously as two bright white lights (approx. 10 feet in diameter), a large round light, a greyish cigar-shaped object, a large yellowish ball (moon-sized), and a star-sized round object. The lights observed by Poland moved at a "terrific speed" and extinguished simultaneously after one minute. Fisher’s observation was of a large white light moving horizontally.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP conducted an investigation, taking formal statements from all witnesses on January 24, 1969. The statements were witnessed by D.R. Strobel. On January 23, 1969, the RCMP contacted Search & Rescue Headquarters, which confirmed there were no missing aircraft in the area. A telex regarding the sightings was subsequently sent to the NRC Meteor Centre. The witnesses expressed apprehension regarding the potential for negative local public opinion concerning their reports.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 文森特·塞缪尔·波普 (Vincent Samuel Pope)、艾玛·安娜·波普 (Emma Anna Pope)、玛丽姆·珍妮特·波普 (Mariem Janet Pope)、雷蒙德·劳伦斯·波兰 (Raymond Lawrence Poland)、珍妮特 (Janet，姓氏不详) 以及本·费舍尔 (Ben Fisher)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月22日，约晚上7:30（波兰/珍妮特）及晚上9:30（费舍尔）。波普一家此前在1968年全年也曾报告过类似目击事件。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省戈尔登市西北13英里处的布莱伯利 (Blaeberry) 地区；柳岸山 (Willow Bank Mountain)；哥伦比亚河附近的1号高速公路。

**目击经过：**
1969年1月22日晚约7:30，雷蒙德·劳伦斯·波兰和珍妮特在马厩照看马匹时，观察到两道明亮的白光。这些光点向北移动，彼此间隔约100英尺，并以45度角下降。波兰估计这些光点距离他们四英里，高度为300英尺。他提到马匹整天表现得都很反常。波兰表示，他在过去一年中曾五六次目击过类似的光点，并明确排除了飞机、照明弹或流星的可能性。

同日晚约9:30，当地加油站老板兼私人飞行员本·费舍尔在1号高速公路上开车时，观察到一道相当大的白光在哥伦比亚河对岸的山脉附近水平移动。

此外，波普一家也提供了关于1968年目击事件的陈述。文森特·塞缪尔·波普报告称，他看到一个巨大的圆形光点向南移动，随后一个灰色的雪茄状物体在柳岸山附近向相反方向移动。艾玛·安娜·波普报告称，她看到一个巨大的黄色球体，大约有月亮那么大，向西南方向移动，随后加速消失。玛丽姆·珍妮特·波普描述称，她看到天空中有一个“巨大的圆形物体”，大约有星星那么大，从东向西移动。雷蒙德·波兰指出，他和姐姐一家此前也曾观察到类似现象，但直到这次才决定上报。

**物体描述：**
这些物体被描述为多种形态：两道明亮的白光（直径约10英尺）、一个巨大的圆形光点、一个灰色的雪茄状物体、一个巨大的黄色球体（月球大小）以及一个星星大小的圆形物体。波兰观察到的光点以“极快的速度”移动，并在持续一分钟后同时熄灭。费舍尔观察到的则是一个水平移动的大型白光。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 进行了调查，并于1969年1月24日对所有目击者进行了正式笔录。这些陈述由D.R. 斯特罗贝尔 (D.R. Strobel) 见证。1969年1月23日，加拿大皇家骑警联系了搜救总部，确认该地区没有失踪飞机。随后，一份关于此次目击事件的电传被发送至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心。目击者们表示，他们担心这些报告可能会引发当地公众的负面评价。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ronald Arden Nowlan (also referred to as Ronald Nolan), Betty Ann Nowlan (Mrs. Nolan), Owen Wood, Jean Wood, Peggy Wood, and George Fields.

**Date / Time:** February 21, 1969, at 9:15 PM Atlantic Time. The sighting lasted until approximately 10:30 PM (a total duration of 1 hour and 15 minutes).

**Location:** A home located behind North River Road, 1/2 mile north of Highway 104 in Onslow, Colchester County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the night of February 21, 1969, a group of five witnesses—Ronald and Betty Ann Nowlan, along with Owen, Jean, and Peggy Wood—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The witnesses were located at a residence near North River Road. The sighting began at 9:15 PM and continued for one hour and fifteen minutes. The witnesses reported that the object remained stationary throughout the duration of the event. A notable characteristic of the sighting was that the object’s light would extinguish sharply for a period of 4 to 5 minutes before reappearing just as abruptly. At approximately 10:30 PM, George Fields contacted the RCMP to report the sighting on behalf of Ronald Nowlan. Owen and Jean Wood corroborated the account provided by the Nowlans.

**Object:** The object was described as being shaped like a triangle with a "long nose." One report specifically characterized the shape as an isosceles triangle with two sides longer than the third. The object appeared to be hollow and was described as very bright, with lighting around the exterior. The light emitted was compared to a fluorescent light with a distinct blue tint. Due to the cloudy, low-ceiling weather conditions, the witnesses were unable to accurately estimate the object's distance or altitude, though it appeared to be very low in the sky. No sound or movement was reported other than the object remaining stationary.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP received the report via George Fields at 10:30 PM. Constable R.O. Pedersen was dispatched to investigate the scene. Upon his arrival and assessment, Cst. Pedersen concluded that the witnesses had observed the Northern Lights. Due to the difficulty in contacting witnesses and the investigating officer's conclusion regarding the nature of the lights, the official reporting process was delayed. A formal telex regarding the incident was eventually forwarded to the National Research Council (N.R.C.) Meteor Centre on March 3, 1969, with copies sent to RCMP Headquarters in Ottawa.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗纳德·阿登·诺兰（Ronald Arden Nowlan，亦称罗纳德·诺兰）、贝蒂·安·诺兰（Betty Ann Nowlan，诺兰夫人）、欧文·伍德（Owen Wood）、简·伍德（Jean Wood）、佩吉·伍德（Peggy Wood）以及乔治·菲尔兹（George Fields）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月21日，大西洋标准时间晚上9:15。目击过程持续至晚上10:30左右（总时长为1小时15分钟）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省科尔切斯特县昂斯洛（Onslow），北河路（North River Road）后方的一处住宅，位于104号公路以北0.5英里处。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月21日晚，五名目击者——罗纳德·诺兰和贝蒂·安·诺兰夫妇，以及欧文、简和佩吉·伍德——观察到了一种不明空中现象。目击者当时位于北河路附近的一处住宅内。目击事件始于晚上9:15，持续了1小时15分钟。据目击者称，该物体在整个过程中保持静止。此次目击的一个显著特征是，物体的光线会突然熄灭4到5分钟，然后又同样突然地重新出现。晚上10:30左右，乔治·菲尔兹代表罗纳德·诺兰联系了加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了此次目击事件。欧文·伍德和简·伍德证实了诺兰夫妇提供的陈述。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为三角形，带有“长鼻”。一份报告特别将其形状描述为等腰三角形，其中两条边长于第三条边。该物体看起来是空心的，且非常明亮，外部有灯光环绕。其发出的光被比作带有明显蓝色调的荧光灯。由于当时天气多云且云层较低，目击者无法准确估计物体的距离或高度，但它看起来在天空中位置很低。除物体保持静止外，未报告有任何声音或移动。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警于晚上10:30通过乔治·菲尔兹接到了报告。R.O. 佩德森（R.O. Pedersen）警官被派往现场进行调查。在抵达并评估现场后，佩德森警官得出结论，认为目击者看到的是北极光。由于难以联系到目击者，且调查警官对光线性质的结论已定，正式报告流程被推迟。关于此事件的正式电传最终于1969年3月3日转发至国家研究委员会（N.R.C.）流星中心，并抄送至位于渥太华的加拿大皇家骑警总部。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Commissioner M.F.A. Lindsay, D/Comm. W.H. Kelly, 3/Cst. D.B. Best, 3/Cst. R.D. Lloyd, 3/Cst. R.V. McCrossin, Cst. W.S. Majaury (also referred to as VS Majaury), and 3/Cst. R.J. Shannahan.

**Date / Time:** March 4, 1969. Two distinct timeframes were reported: 7:45 PM to 9:34 PM EST, and approximately 10:00 PM EST.

**Location:** Parliament Hill, Ottawa; the Prime Minister’s residence on Sussex Drive, Ottawa; and the Ottawa River (behind the Parliament Buildings).

**Sighting:** On March 4, 1969, multiple RCMP officers reported sightings of anomalous objects. At 7:45 PM, Commissioner Lindsay, D/Comm. Kelly, and Csts. Best, Lloyd, McCrossin, and Majaury observed an object from Parliament Hill. It moved at a high rate of speed from south to north, stopped over Hull, Quebec, and remained visible until 9:34 PM, when it moved northwest and disappeared. 

Separately, at approximately 10:00 PM, 3/Cst. R.J. Shannahan, while on foot patrol between the Government House Police Lodge and the Prime Minister’s residence, observed two bright, flashing red lights. One light traveled east and vanished within a minute; the other traveled west toward Parliament Hill and was visible for five to six minutes. Simultaneously, at 10:00 PM, 3/Cst. R.D. Lloyd observed a different object at low altitude over the Ottawa River behind the Parliament Buildings. He described it as falling straight down before burning out.

**Object:** 
*   **7:45 PM Object:** Described as round, much brighter and larger than a star or planet, but smaller than the moon. It appeared at a high altitude, higher than standard aircraft.
*   **10:00 PM Lights (Shannahan):** Two bright, flashing red lights with no definite shape, no visible trail, and no engine noise.
*   **10:00 PM Object (Lloyd):** Small, star-like, with no discernable shape. It appeared to fall vertically and burn out, briefly displaying an orange-brown tail before disappearing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sightings occurred under clear weather conditions with excellent visibility. Following the 10:00 PM sightings, the information was radioed to the Police Lodge and reported to Sgt. Smith (N.C.O. i/c "A" Div. Desk). A watch was maintained at the Prime Minister’s residence for one hour, but no further sightings occurred. Captain H.R. Wolff of R.C.A.F. Uplands was notified regarding the 7:45 PM sighting but declined to take action. The file was concluded by 3/Cst. R.D. Lloyd and JAHB (N.C.O. i/c Sec. #2). Multiple telex messages were generated to document these events.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 专员 M.F.A. 林赛 (M.F.A. Lindsay)、副专员 W.H. 凯利 (W.H. Kelly)、三等警员 D.B. 贝斯特 (D.B. Best)、三等警员 R.D. 劳埃德 (R.D. Lloyd)、三等警员 R.V. 麦克罗辛 (R.V. McCrossin)、警员 W.S. 马乔里 (W.S. Majaury，亦称 VS Majaury) 以及三等警员 R.J. 香纳汉 (R.J. Shannahan)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年3月4日。报告了两个不同的时间段：东部标准时间晚上7:45至9:34，以及晚上10:00左右。

**地点：** 渥太华国会山；渥太华苏塞克斯大道（Sussex Drive）的总理官邸；以及渥太华河（国会大厦后方）。

**目击经过：** 1969年3月4日，多名加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员报告了异常物体的目击事件。晚上7:45，林赛专员、凯利副专员以及贝斯特、劳埃德、麦克罗辛和马乔里警员在国会山观察到一个物体。它以极高的速度从南向北移动，随后停在魁北克省赫尔（Hull）上空，并一直保持可见状态直到晚上9:34，之后向西北方向移动并消失。

另外，在晚上10:00左右，三等警员 R.J. 香纳汉在政府大楼警卫室与总理官邸之间巡逻时，观察到两道明亮的闪烁红光。其中一道光向东移动并在不到一分钟内消失；另一道光向西朝国会山方向移动，可见持续时间为五到六分钟。与此同时，晚上10:00，三等警员 R.D. 劳埃德在国会大厦后方的渥太华河上空观察到了另一个低空飞行的物体。他描述该物体垂直坠落，随后熄灭。

**物体描述：**
*   **7:45 PM 的物体：** 被描述为圆形，比恒星或行星亮得多、大得多，但比月亮小。它出现在高空，高于标准飞行器的高度。
*   **10:00 PM 的光点（香纳汉目击）：** 两道明亮的闪烁红光，没有明确的形状，没有可见的尾迹，也没有引擎噪音。
*   **10:00 PM 的物体（劳埃德目击）：** 小而像星星，没有明显的形状。它看起来是垂直坠落并熄灭的，在消失前短暂地显现出一条橙棕色的尾迹。

**调查/后续：**
目击事件发生时天气晴朗，能见度极佳。10:00 PM 的目击事件发生后，相关信息通过无线电传达至警卫室，并报告给了史密斯警长（“A”分部值班室负责人）。总理官邸随后进行了为期一小时的监视，但未再有新的目击报告。加拿大皇家空军（R.C.A.F.）厄普兰兹（Uplands）基地的 H.R. 沃尔夫（H.R. Wolff）上尉获悉了7:45 PM的目击事件，但拒绝采取行动。该档案由三等警员 R.D. 劳埃德和 JAHB（第2分部负责人）结案。为记录这些事件，相关部门发送了多份电传信息。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Robert Douglas (Mechanic, Geophysical Service Inc. Party 422), Michael (Mike) Byciuk (Party Chief, Geophysical Service Inc. Party 422), Herbert (Bud) Douglas (Mechanic), and William DeWetter (Grader Operator, Pan American Oil Co.).

**Date / Time:** February 6, 1969 (2:00 AM and 8:00 AM); February 15/18, 1969 (11:00 PM); March 1, 1969 (12:30 AM); March 7, 1969 (12:00 NN); March 8, 1969 (11:00 PM – 1:00 AM). All times Mountain Standard Time (MST).

**Location:** Vicinity of Fort Liard, NWT, and Fort Nelson, BC (specifically coordinates 60° 10' N, 123° 30' W; 60° 8' N, 123° 31' W; and 60° 0' N, 123° 20' W).

**Sighting:** A series of UFO sightings occurred between February and March 1969. Geophysical Service Inc. (GSI) employees Robert Douglas and Michael Byciuk reported three primary events on February 6, March 1, and March 7. These sightings lasted between 10 minutes and one hour under clear, starry skies. The witnesses, initially hesitant to report due to fear of ridicule, came forward after learning of similar sightings in Fort Simpson and Fort Nelson. Separately, William DeWetter observed an object on March 8 near the Pointed Mountain airstrip. DeWetter noted the object appeared, receded, vanished, and reappeared from the same direction multiple times over a two-hour window, with each individual observation lasting approximately two minutes.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as round, resembling the bottom half of a globe or a disc. GSI witnesses described it as very bright red, occasionally changing to a greyish-blue; when red, the shape was indiscernible, but it became clear when blue. Byciuk and Douglas also described it as having a "flared" top, as if surrounded by a ring. DeWetter described the object as 50–70 feet in diameter, initially round and red, later shifting to a misty blue or green before fading at the edges. The object maintained an altitude of 500–1000 feet and was estimated to be 15–20 miles away. Movement was erratic: the object was observed moving rapidly, slowly, or remaining stationary, consistently traveling in a southerly or southeasterly direction (225-degree azimuth).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Observations by GSI personnel were conducted using transit instruments with 27x and 40x magnification. Reports were filed with the RCMP in Fort Smith, Fort Nelson, and Prince George. RCMP officers interviewed the witnesses and deemed them highly reliable. The reports were transmitted to the ARC Meteor Centre and CANFORCEHQ. An RCMP officer conducted a follow-up patrol to the Pointed Mountain airstrip on March 20, 1969, to document DeWetter’s account. No further investigation was pursued as the seismic crews had vacated the region by the end of March 1969, leaving the area unpopulated.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗伯特·道格拉斯（Robert Douglas，地球物理服务公司第422勘探队机械师）、迈克尔（迈克）·拜丘克（Michael (Mike) Byciuk，地球物理服务公司第422勘探队队长）、赫伯特（巴德）·道格拉斯（Herbert (Bud) Douglas，机械师）以及威廉·德韦特（William DeWetter，泛美石油公司平地机操作员）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月6日（凌晨2:00及上午8:00）；1969年2月15日/18日（晚上11:00）；1969年3月1日（凌晨12:30）；1969年3月7日（中午12:00）；1969年3月8日（晚上11:00至次日凌晨1:00）。所有时间均为山区标准时间（MST）。

**地点：** 西北地区利亚德堡（Fort Liard）及不列颠哥伦比亚省纳尔逊堡（Fort Nelson）附近（具体坐标为北纬60°10'，西经123°30'；北纬60°8'，西经123°31'；以及北纬60°0'，西经123°20'）。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月至3月间发生了一系列UFO目击事件。地球物理服务公司（GSI）的员工罗伯特·道格拉斯和迈克尔·拜丘克报告了2月6日、3月1日和3月7日的三起主要事件。在晴朗的星空下，这些目击事件持续了10分钟到1小时不等。目击者起初因担心遭到嘲笑而犹豫是否上报，但在得知纳尔逊堡和辛普森堡也有类似目击事件后，他们决定站出来。另外，威廉·德韦特于3月8日在尖山（Pointed Mountain）简易机场附近观察到了一个物体。德韦特指出，该物体在两小时内多次从同一方向出现、后退、消失并再次现身，每次观察持续约两分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被一致描述为圆形，类似于半个球体或圆盘。GSI的目击者称其为非常明亮的红色，偶尔会变为灰蓝色；当呈现红色时，其形状难以辨认，但变为蓝色时则清晰可见。拜丘克和道格拉斯还描述其顶部有“耀斑”，仿佛被一个环包围。德韦特描述该物体直径为50至70英尺，起初呈红色圆形，随后转变为朦胧的蓝色或绿色，边缘逐渐消散。该物体保持在500至1000英尺的高度，估计距离为15至20英里。其运动轨迹不稳定：物体被观察到时而快速移动，时而缓慢移动，或保持静止，始终向南或东南方向（方位角225度）飞行。

**调查/后续：** GSI人员使用27倍和40倍放大倍率的经纬仪进行了观测。相关报告已提交给位于史密斯堡（Fort Smith）、纳尔逊堡和乔治王子城（Prince George）的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）。皇家骑警警官对目击者进行了访谈，认为他们非常可靠。报告随后被转交给ARC流星中心和加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHQ）。一名皇家骑警警官于1969年3月20日对尖山简易机场进行了后续巡逻，以记录德韦特的陈述。由于地震勘探队已于1969年3月底撤离该地区，导致该区域无人居住，因此后续未再进行深入调查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Raymond Hinchey, Margaret (Mrs. Raymond) Hinchey

**Date / Time:** April 14, 1969, at approximately 12:00 midnight to 12:15 a.m. (April 15)

**Location:** Carlisle Road, Douglas, York County, New Brunswick; object observed over the St. John River.

**Sighting:** On the night of April 14, 1969, Raymond and Margaret Hinchey observed an unidentified flying object over the St. John River. The sighting lasted approximately 15 minutes, beginning around midnight. Raymond Hinchey utilized 7x50 binoculars to track the object, while Margaret Hinchey observed it with the naked eye. The witnesses reported the object moving in a southeasterly direction from the Douglas area toward New Maryland. The object exhibited complex flight characteristics, including gliding, hovering, and gyrating in a wobbling motion. It was observed to "bellow" up and down, changing shape before returning to its original form, and spinning at a fast rate. The witnesses explicitly stated that the object was not an aircraft. It eventually disappeared in a south-westerly direction.

**Object:** The object was described as large, measuring approximately 100–150 feet across and 10 feet thick, with an overall shape described as flat, round, or oval (resembling a "hamburger"). Margaret Hinchey noted a distinct dome on the top that emitted a bright yellowish-white glow. The object featured pulsating lights in red, blue, and white; these were set in a concave area between the upper and lower points of the craft. Specifically, the lights were primarily red and blue at the front and white at the rear. The object was silent, with no audible noise reported. It maintained an estimated altitude of 3,000 to 5,000 feet and traveled at a slow speed, estimated between 100 and 150 m.p.h.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation, contacting the Department of Transport (DOT) control tower at the Fredericton Airport. The tower confirmed that the sky was clear with unlimited visibility at midnight and reported no other sightings. Officials advised that no aircraft had been in the area since 10:40 p.m. on April 14, 1969. While the tower initially suggested the possibility of aircraft from the RCAF Summerside base, this was not confirmed. A radiogram was submitted to the Fredericton Sub/Division. Investigators concluded the object was not a meteorite or an aircraft. The official report noted that the reliability of the witnesses was unknown, suggesting that their accounts might have been influenced by reading articles on UFOs, though the investigator conceded there was no specific evidence to discredit the witnesses. No definitive explanation for the object's origin was determined.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 雷蒙德·欣奇 (Raymond Hinchey)、玛格丽特·欣奇 (Margaret Hinchey，雷蒙德之妻)

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年4月14日，午夜12:00至凌晨12:15（4月15日）

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省约克县道格拉斯卡莱尔路；物体出现在圣约翰河上空。

**目击经过：** 1969年4月14日晚，雷蒙德·欣奇和玛格丽特·欣奇在圣约翰河上空观测到一个不明飞行物。目击过程持续了约15分钟，始于午夜左右。雷蒙德·欣奇使用7x50双筒望远镜追踪该物体，而玛格丽特·欣奇则用肉眼观察。目击者报告称，该物体从道格拉斯地区向东南方向移动，朝新马里兰方向飞去。该物体表现出复杂的飞行特征，包括滑翔、悬停以及摇晃式的旋转。据观察，它还会上下“膨胀”，在恢复原状前会发生形状改变，并以极快的速度旋转。目击者明确表示该物体并非飞机。最终，它向西南方向消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的飞行器，直径约100至150英尺，厚度约10英尺，整体形状扁平、呈圆形或椭圆形（类似于“汉堡包”）。玛格丽特·欣奇注意到顶部有一个明显的圆顶，散发出明亮的黄白色光芒。该物体带有红色、蓝色和白色的脉冲灯；这些灯光位于飞行器上下部分之间的凹陷区域。具体而言，前部主要为红蓝灯，后部为白灯。该物体全程静音，未听到任何噪音。它保持在约3,000至5,000英尺的高度，以每小时100至150英里的估计速度缓慢飞行。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 进行了调查，并联系了弗雷德里克顿机场的交通部 (DOT) 控制塔。控制塔确认午夜时分天空晴朗，能见度无限，且未报告其他目击事件。官方告知，自1969年4月14日晚10:40起，该地区没有飞机经过。虽然控制塔最初暗示可能是来自萨默赛德加拿大皇家空军 (RCAF) 基地的飞机，但并未得到证实。一份无线电报被提交至弗雷德里克顿分局。调查人员得出结论，该物体既不是陨石也不是飞机。官方报告指出，目击者的可靠性未知，暗示他们的陈述可能受到阅读过UFO相关文章的影响，尽管调查人员也承认没有具体证据可以反驳目击者的证词。该物体的来源最终未得出明确解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Thorhauge, Mrs. Leigh Anderson, Mr. Anderson, Mrs. [redacted] (of 25 Saginaw Crescent), Mr. [redacted] (of 23 Saginaw Crescent), and Mrs. [redacted] (of 23 Saginaw Crescent).

**Date / Time:** September 27, 1972, between 6:45 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. EDT.

**Location:** Ottawa, Ontario (specifically residences on Saginaw Crescent).

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 27, 1972, multiple residents in Ottawa observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sky was reported as clear during the duration of the event. Mrs. Thorhauge, Mrs. Leigh Anderson, and Mr. Anderson observed the object from their respective residences. Simultaneously, Mrs. [redacted] of 25 Saginaw Crescent and Mr. and Mrs. [redacted] of 23 Saginaw Crescent witnessed the same event. All witnesses reported that the object appeared in the western sky and maintained visibility for approximately 15 minutes. The observers noted that the object moved from the west toward the south, exhibiting a slight descent during its transit. The witnesses confirmed that only one object was spotted during the sighting.

**Object:** The object was described as an oval-shaped entity emitting a very bright light. While no specific estimate of the object's altitude was provided by the witnesses, it was observed to be a singular, distinct light source. No sound was reported, and the object remained visible until it disappeared from sight at approximately 7:00 p.m.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP "A" Division in Ottawa conducted interviews with the witnesses and formally concluded that the individuals involved were reliable sources. Following the initial report, the information was relayed immediately via telephone (line 6-7811) to the duty officer at the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) Uplands base. Additionally, a formal copy of the investigation report was forwarded to the Meteor Centre on October 23, 1972, for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 托尔豪格夫人 (Mrs. Thorhauge)、利·安德森夫人 (Mrs. Leigh Anderson)、安德森先生 (Mr. Anderson)、[已涂黑]夫人（萨基诺新月街25号）、[已涂黑]先生（萨基诺新月街23号）以及[已涂黑]夫人（萨基诺新月街23号）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年9月27日，东部夏令时间下午6:45至7:00之间。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华（具体为萨基诺新月街的住宅区）。

**目击经过：** 1972年9月27日傍晚，渥太华的多名居民观察到一种不明空中现象。据报告，事件发生期间天空晴朗。托尔豪格夫人、利·安德森夫人和安德森先生分别从各自的住所观察到了该物体。与此同时，萨基诺新月街25号的[已涂黑]夫人以及23号的[已涂黑]夫妇也目击了同一事件。所有目击者均报告称，该物体出现在西侧天空中，可见时长约为15分钟。观察者们指出，该物体从西向南移动，在移动过程中有轻微的下降。目击者证实，在整个目击过程中只看到了一个物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个发出极亮光芒的椭圆形实体。虽然目击者没有提供该物体高度的具体估计值，但观察到它是一个单一且清晰的光源。未报告有任何声音，该物体一直保持可见，直到下午7:00左右消失在视野中。

**调查/后续：** 渥太华加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) “A”分部对目击者进行了访谈，并正式得出结论：相关人员均为可靠的信息来源。在初步报告之后，相关信息通过电话（线路6-7811）立即传达给了加拿大武装部队 (CAF) 阿普兰基地的当值军官。此外，调查报告的正式副本已于1972年10月23日转交至流星中心，以供进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Inspector William McFarland (RCMP), Thea McFarland, Bob McFarland (13), Tim McFarland (12), Catherine McFarland (7), Mrs. A. Reimann, Mrs. Wayne Inkpen, John Kryschuk, Ken Bilkoski, Keith Lafreniere, Les Englot.

**Date / Time:** September 7, 1972, at 9:45 p.m. (Note: Page 243 contains a typographical error citing 1967; the case file context and subsequent pages confirm the 1972 date).

**Location:** Highway 203, near Lydiatt and Beausejour, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 7, 1972, Inspector William McFarland of the RCMP was traveling south on Highway 203 near Lydiatt/Beausejour with his wife, Thea, and their three children, Bob, Tim, and Catherine. While en route during a transfer from "DEPOT" Division to Ottawa, the family observed a bright, luminous object approaching from the east at an altitude of approximately 30 feet. The object pursued the McFarland vehicle for a duration of 20 to 25 minutes. Upon the family's arrival at the residence of Mrs. A. Reimann, the object hovered at an altitude of 30 feet above the house for an additional five minutes before moving behind a cluster of trees. Inspector McFarland, a veteran police officer, maintained a skeptical stance regarding the nature of the phenomenon but acknowledged that he could not explain or deny the observations made by himself and his family.

**Object:** The object was described as an oblong, glowing craft, comparable in size and shape to an oval dining room table, measuring approximately four to five feet in length and one foot in depth. It emitted a soft, bright white light and appeared to have no sharp edges. Witnesses noted the object possessed a halo-like appearance and exhibited a rotating, swinging motion during its flight and hover.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was documented in a September 19, 1972, article in the *Beausejour Beaver*. Although the event was not formally reported to the Beausejour RCMP detachment at the time, the matter was referred to "D" Division for information, with the possibility that further statements might be requested from Inspector McFarland. Official inquiries confirmed that the CFS Beausejour radar site reported no unusual activity or targets on the evening of the sighting. The case file also contextualizes this event by referencing a history of regional UFO reports, including sightings by Mrs. Wayne Inkpen (May 31, 1967), John Kryschuk (April 3, 1968), and a report from August 30, 1968, involving Ken Bilkoski, Keith Lafreniere, and Les Englot, who described a disc-shaped object featuring red and white lights.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_28_-_Pages_81.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威廉·麦克法兰警督（加拿大皇家骑警）、西娅·麦克法兰、鲍勃·麦克法兰（13岁）、蒂姆·麦克法兰（12岁）、凯瑟琳·麦克法兰（7岁）、A. 雷曼夫人、韦恩·英克彭夫人、约翰·克里舒克、肯·比尔科斯基、基思·拉弗雷尼尔、莱斯·恩格洛特。

**日期/时间：** 1972年9月7日，晚上9:45（注：第243页存在印刷错误，误写为1967年；根据案卷背景及后续页面确认，应为1972年）。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省利迪亚特（Lydiatt）与博塞茹尔（Beausejour）附近的203号公路。

**目击经过：** 1972年9月7日晚，加拿大皇家骑警威廉·麦克法兰警督正驾车沿203号公路向南行驶，前往博塞茹尔/利迪亚特附近，车上载有其妻子西娅及三个孩子鲍勃、蒂姆和凯瑟琳。当时他们正从“DEPOT”分部调往渥太华的途中，一家人观察到一个明亮的发光物体从东面靠近，飞行高度约为30英尺。该物体尾随麦克法兰一家的车辆长达20至25分钟。当他们抵达A. 雷曼夫人的住所时，该物体在屋顶上方30英尺处悬停了五分钟，随后移动到一片树丛后方。身为资深警官的麦克法兰警督对该现象的本质持怀疑态度，但他承认自己无法解释或否认他和家人所目击到的情况。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个长方形的发光飞行器，大小和形状类似于一张椭圆形的餐桌，长约四至五英尺，厚约一英尺。它发出柔和而明亮的白光，看起来没有明显的棱角。目击者指出，该物体呈现出光环状，在飞行和悬停过程中表现出旋转和摆动的动作。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件被记录在1972年9月19日的《博塞茹尔海狸报》（*Beausejour Beaver*）上。尽管当时并未正式向博塞茹尔的加拿大皇家骑警分局报案，但该事件已被转交至“D”分部备案，并可能要求麦克法兰警督提供进一步陈述。官方调查证实，博塞茹尔加拿大武装部队（CFS）雷达站报告称，在目击当晚并未发现任何异常活动或目标。案卷还通过参考该地区的历史UFO报告对此次事件进行了背景说明，其中包括韦恩·英克彭夫人（1967年5月31日）、约翰·克里舒克（1968年4月3日）的目击报告，以及1968年8月30日由肯·比尔科斯基、基思·拉弗雷尼尔和莱斯·恩格洛特提交的报告，他们当时描述了一个带有红白灯光的圆盘状物体。

**见证者：** 一名平民、其妻子以及另一位女士（Mrs [redacted]）。

**目击：** 1972年9月26日晚上约9:45，目击者在阿尔伯塔省Steen River西北方5英里处观察到一个物体。该物体从东南方向出现并向西北方向移动。

**Witnesses:** A resident of Calgary, a resident of Brooks, numerous residents in the Brooks area, an RCMP officer, two hitchhikers from Forestburg, Master [redacted] (743 Commsqn CAF, Camp Wainwright), his wife, his sons, his mother, two individuals from Trochu, two civilian observers (including a resident of Airdrie), Ex S/Sgt A J Carter, Mrs [redacted], 5 members of the RCMP detachment, Cst JR Mortlock (RCMP Cochrane), Cst P V Jacques (RCMP Drumheller), Cst LL Lanza, Ex S/Sgt E Dunk, CST T B Bragg (RCMP Fort Macleod), three unnamed observers in Blairmore/Bellevue, a tourist from Yellowknife, an unnamed individual from Wymark, CST R.W. Lowe (RCMP), S/SGT J.R. Nickel (RCMP), Cst DW Nicklin (RCMP Airdrie), and one observer in Patricia.

**Date / Time:** August 10, 1972 (with one prior sighting on August 6, 1972, at 3:00 AM). Sightings on August 10 occurred between 1:30 PM and 3:05 PM MDT/PDST.

**Location:** Widespread across Alberta and British Columbia, including Calgary, Brooks, Patricia, Morrin, Huxley, Trochu, Airdrie, Cochrane, Fort Macleod, Blairmore, Bellevue, Lethbridge, C.F.B. Wainwright, Salmon Arm, Pincher Creek, Cranbrook, Kimberley, Fernie, Invermere, Creston, Ymir, Fruitvale, Trail, Golden, and Wymark, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On August 10, 1972, a massive wave of sightings occurred across Western Canada. Witnesses consistently described an object traveling at extremely high speeds, generally moving from the south/southwest toward the north/northeast. Accounts varied: some saw a "fireball" or "jet on fire," while others described a solid, metallic object. Near Morrin, an RCMP officer and hitchhikers observed the object climb, level off, and disintegrate. Near Huxley, witnesses watched a ball reflect the sun for 90 seconds before accelerating. Near Airdrie, observers saw an object rise from Calgary, burn with changing colors (white, blue, yellow), and eventually drop a silver object. In Blairmore, an explosion was heard after the object passed. In BC, sightings ranged from a "fluorescent white" object in Salmon Arm to a "cylindrical" object in Creston. A separate, earlier sighting on August 6 in Salmon Arm involved a hovering, light-emitting object.

**Object:** Descriptions varied significantly: round, oval, conical, or raindrop-shaped; silver, blue, or yellowish-green. Sizes were often compared to jets or balls. Features included red, green, blue, or yellow flames/fire tails, and white vapor trails that persisted for up to 15 minutes. Movement was described as "too fast for aircraft," with some reports of the object spinning, climbing, leveling off, or disintegrating in flight. Most observers reported no sound, though one witness reported a loud explosion.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted extensive interviews and filed reports with the NRC Meteor Centre and CANFORCEHED. While some officials and US scientists suggested the object was a meteor or comet remains, many witnesses explicitly rejected this explanation. RCMP detachments (Drumheller, Airdrie, Three Hills, Swift Current, etc.) documented the events via telex and reports. Attempts were made to photograph vapor trails. The files were generally concluded with no further action, though the reliability of witnesses was frequently noted as "very good."

**目击者：** 一名卡尔加里居民、一名布鲁克斯居民、布鲁克斯地区的众多居民、一名加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警官、两名来自福雷斯特堡的搭车客、[已删除]军士长（加拿大武装部队第743通信中队，温赖特营地）、他的妻子、他的儿子们、他的母亲、两名来自特罗丘的个人、两名平民观察员（包括一名艾尔德里居民）、前参谋警长 A·J·卡特（A J Carter）、[已删除]夫人、5名加拿大皇家骑警分遣队成员、J·R·莫特洛克警员（RCMP科克伦分局）、P·V·雅克警员（RCMP德拉姆黑勒分局）、L·L·兰扎警员、前参谋警长 E·邓克（E Dunk）、T·B·布拉格警员（RCMP麦克劳德堡分局）、三名布莱尔莫尔/贝尔维尤的匿名观察员、一名来自耶洛奈夫的游客、一名来自怀马克的匿名人士、R·W·洛警员（RCMP）、J·R·尼克尔参谋警长（RCMP）、D·W·尼克林警员（RCMP艾尔德里分局）以及一名帕特里夏的观察员。

**日期/时间：** 1972年8月10日（此前在1972年8月6日凌晨3:00曾有一次目击）。8月10日的目击事件发生在山区夏令时间/太平洋夏令时间下午1:30至3:05之间。

**地点：** 广泛分布于艾伯塔省和不列颠哥伦比亚省，包括卡尔加里、布鲁克斯、帕特里夏、莫林、赫克斯利、特罗丘、艾尔德里、科克伦、麦克劳德堡、布莱尔莫尔、贝尔维尤、莱斯布里奇、温赖特加拿大武装部队基地、萨蒙阿姆、平彻克里克、克兰布鲁克、金伯利、弗尼、因弗米尔、克雷斯顿、伊米尔、弗鲁特韦尔、特雷尔、戈尔登，以及萨斯喀彻温省的怀马克。

**目击经过：** 1972年8月10日，加拿大西部发生了一场大规模的目击事件。目击者一致描述了一个以极高速度飞行的物体，总体移动方向是从南/西南向北/东北。描述各不相同：有人看到的是“火球”或“着火的喷气式飞机”，而另一些人则描述为一个坚固的金属物体。在莫林附近，一名加拿大皇家骑警警官和搭车客观察到该物体爬升、平飞，随后解体。在赫克斯利附近，目击者观察到一个球体反射阳光长达90秒，随后加速离去。在艾尔德里附近，观察者看到一个物体从卡尔加里升起，燃烧时颜色不断变化（白色、蓝色、黄色），最终掉落了一个银色物体。在布莱尔莫尔，物体经过后传出了爆炸声。在不列颠哥伦比亚省，目击描述从萨蒙阿姆的“荧光白色”物体到克雷斯顿的“圆柱形”物体不等。8月6日在萨蒙阿姆发生的另一起较早的目击事件涉及一个悬停并发出光芒的物体。

**物体描述：** 描述差异显著：形状为圆形、椭圆形、圆锥形或雨滴形；颜色为银色、蓝色或黄绿色。尺寸常被比作喷气式飞机或球体。特征包括红色、绿色、蓝色或黄色的火焰/火尾，以及持续长达15分钟的白色尾迹。其运动被描述为“快到无法用飞机解释”，一些报告称该物体在飞行中旋转、爬升、平飞或解体。大多数观察者报告称没有声音，但有一名目击者报告听到了巨大的爆炸声。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警进行了广泛的访谈，并向国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心和加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）提交了报告。尽管一些官员和美国科学家认为该物体是流星或彗星残骸，但许多目击者明确拒绝了这一解释。加拿大皇家骑警各分遣队（德拉姆黑勒、艾尔德里、三山、斯威夫特卡伦特等地）通过电传和报告记录了这些事件。调查人员曾尝试拍摄尾迹。这些档案最终通常以“无进一步行动”结案，但目击者的可靠性经常被标注为“非常好”。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Vicki BURNS, Ray MILLER, Alice MILLER, Wayne MILLER, Lenore MILLER, Jean ANDERSON, Ken STEPHENS, George SEVIGNY, Gus STRIEFEL, Cindy (Cyndie) STEPHEN, Karen SEVIGNY, Rick (Ricky) STEPHENS, Mrs. Lenore LOFTUS, Mr. LOFTUS, Wayne LOFTUS, R.T. MOLLER, Cpl. DOIRON, Cpl. PERRIN, Cst. HOLYK.

**Date / Time:** April 6, 1978; sightings occurred primarily between 7:30 p.m. and 11:00 p.m.

**Location:** Prince George, BC (specifically the Burns farm, 10 miles west of Prince George; 4278 Hart Highway; and the Miworth area).

**Sighting:** At approximately 7:30–7:45 p.m., Vicki Burns observed a 2-inch diameter beam of light extending from a group of trees into her barn. Inside, she found her horses in a state of extreme panic: one had its front feet through a plywood wall, another was motionless on its side before darting into a screen, and a young gelding attempted to climb a 6-foot door. Neighbors and family members (Anderson, Miller, Loftus) arrived to assist with the agitated animals. Following the barn incident, multiple witnesses observed an object in the sky. Accounts describe the object as moving erratically, darting between spots, and pulsating. While some witnesses (Miller, Moller) initially compared it to a satellite or star, others (Stephens, Sevigny) observed it through telescopes and rifle scopes, describing it as stationary for long periods before moving west or south. The object was reported to be visible for up to three hours by some observers.

**Object:** Descriptions varied based on viewing equipment. Naked-eye observers described a round, misty white light, similar in brightness to a star or one-third the size of the moon. Through telescopes and rifle scopes, the object appeared disc-shaped or like "two plates put together." It featured flashing red, blue, amber, and orange lights. The body of the object reportedly glowed orange continuously. It was silent, with no fireballs or bursts observed. Estimates of size ranged from a small plane to a 737 jet at 30,000 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
*   **Veterinary:** Dr. McKee examined the horses, attributing their condition to severe shock/fright and noting ringworm spots on a filly’s neck. Dr. Bixby was also consulted for medication.
*   **RCMP/Military:** Vicki Burns contacted the RCMP on April 10, 1978. Cpl. Doiron and Cpl. Perrin investigated; C.F.B. Baldy Hughes radar base was contacted, and while Ken Stephens claimed the base confirmed seeing the object, official reports stated nothing was detected on radar. 
*   **Radiation:** Chief Trask (C.F.B. Baldy Hughes) tested the barn for radiation with negative results. Ken Stephens later visited the site with a Geiger counter, obtaining a "small reading."
*   **Documentation:** Statements were taken from all witnesses by RCMP officers (including Cst. Holyk). Dr. McNamara of the National Research Council was provided with witness names for further review.

**目击者：** 维基·伯恩斯 (Vicki BURNS) 夫人、雷·米勒 (Ray MILLER)、爱丽丝·米勒 (Alice MILLER)、韦恩·米勒 (Wayne MILLER)、勒诺·米勒 (Lenore MILLER)、简·安德森 (Jean ANDERSON)、肯·斯蒂芬斯 (Ken STEPHENS)、乔治·塞维尼 (George SEVIGNY)、格斯·斯特里费尔 (Gus STRIEFEL)、辛迪 (辛迪)·斯蒂芬 (Cindy (Cyndie) STEPHEN)、凯伦·塞维尼 (Karen SEVIGNY)、里克 (里基)·斯蒂芬斯 (Rick (Ricky) STEPHENS)、勒诺·洛夫图斯 (Lenore LOFTUS) 夫人、洛夫图斯 (LOFTUS) 先生、韦恩·洛夫图斯 (Wayne LOFTUS)、R.T. 莫勒 (R.T. MOLLER)、多伊隆 (DOIRON) 下士、佩兰 (PERRIN) 下士、霍利克 (HOLYK) 警员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年4月6日；目击事件主要发生在晚上7:30至11:00之间。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省乔治王子城（具体地点包括乔治王子城以西10英里的伯恩斯农场、哈特公路4278号以及米沃斯地区）。

**目击经过：** 晚上7:30至7:45左右，维基·伯恩斯观察到一束直径约2英寸的光束从树丛中射入她的谷仓。进入谷仓后，她发现马匹处于极度恐慌状态：其中一匹马的前蹄穿过了胶合板墙，另一匹马侧卧在地一动不动，随后猛地冲向纱窗，还有一匹年轻的阉马试图爬上一扇6英尺高的门。邻居和家庭成员（安德森、米勒、洛夫图斯）赶来协助安抚这些受惊的动物。谷仓事件发生后，多名目击者在天空中观察到了一个物体。据描述，该物体移动轨迹不规则，在不同点之间快速穿梭并不断闪烁。虽然一些目击者（米勒、莫勒）起初将其比作卫星或星星，但其他人（斯蒂芬斯、塞维尼）通过望远镜和步枪瞄准镜观察后，称其在移动到西面或南面之前，曾长时间保持静止。据部分观察者称，该物体可见时间长达三个小时。

**物体描述：** 描述因观察设备的不同而有所差异。肉眼观察者将其描述为一团圆形的、朦胧的白光，亮度与星星相当，或约为月球大小的三分之一。通过望远镜和步枪瞄准镜观察时，该物体呈圆盘状，看起来像“两只扣在一起的盘子”。它闪烁着红色、蓝色、琥珀色和橙色的光。据称，该物体的本体持续发出橙色的光芒。它在飞行过程中保持静止，没有观察到火球或爆炸。对其大小的估计范围从小型飞机到3万英尺高空的波音737客机不等。

**调查/后续：**
*   **兽医：** 麦基 (McKee) 医生检查了马匹，将其状况归因于严重的惊吓/恐惧，并注意到一匹小雌马的脖子上有癣斑。比克斯比 (Bixby) 医生也受邀提供了药物建议。
*   **加拿大皇家骑警/军方：** 维基·伯恩斯于1978年4月10日联系了加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP)。多伊隆下士和佩兰下士进行了调查；相关人员联系了巴尔迪休斯 (C.F.B. Baldy Hughes) 空军基地雷达站。尽管肯·斯蒂芬斯声称该基地确认看到了该物体，但官方报告称雷达并未探测到任何异常。
*   **辐射：** 特拉斯克 (Trask) 局长（巴尔迪休斯空军基地）对谷仓进行了辐射检测，结果为阴性。肯·斯蒂芬斯后来带着盖革计数器再次访问了现场，并获得了一个“微小的读数”。
*   **记录：** 加拿大皇家骑警（包括霍利克警员）对所有目击者进行了笔录。国家研究委员会的麦克纳马拉 (McNamara) 博士收到了目击者名单，以便进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miss Teetsia Blokzyk and Miss Lorriane Vilkers.

**Object:** The object was described as cigar-shaped, blackish-gray in color, and large in size. It featured two square lights on its bottom.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 蒂西亚·布洛齐克（Teetsia Blokzyk）小姐和洛林·维尔克斯（Lorriane Vilkers）小姐。

**日期：** 事件发生于1978年4月2日，时间约为东部标准时间（E.S.T.）晚上8:30至9:00。

**地点：** 该物体被观察到在离地约200英尺的高空盘旋于一片田野之上。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为雪茄状，呈灰黑色，体积巨大。其底部装有两盏方形灯。

**调查/后续：** 目击者向尼亚加拉地区警方报告了此次目击事件。随后，电子生物研究中心（Electronic Bio Research）的唐纳德·W·戈尔丁（Donald W. Golding）先生将该事件上报给了渥太华国防参谋长中队指挥官。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Mike Bourguis (also recorded as Bourgois and Bourgeois)

**Date / Time:** April 25, 1978, at 2205Z; an additional report notes April 22, 1978, at 0830Z.

**Location:** 805 Holt St, Kamloops, BC; and nineteen miles west of Kamloops on the CNR track.

**Sighting:** The documentation contains conflicting accounts regarding the duration and specific circumstances of the sighting. One set of reports, originating from the witness's residence at 805 Holt St, describes a stationary object observed for a duration of one and a half hours. According to this account, the object remained in a fixed position before eventually backing away. 

A second set of reports, linked to a location nineteen miles west of Kamloops on the CNR track, describes a transient event lasting approximately five minutes. In this version, the object was observed passing over the area, during which it cast an orange reflection upon a nearby lake. The witness reported that the object made no noise during this transit.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as round in shape. Its coloration was noted as a combination of red, white, and orange. Regarding movement and sound, the accounts vary between a stationary object that eventually "backed up" and a silent object that passed over the landscape, leaving an orange reflection on the water below.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally processed by Canadian Forces Station (CFS) Kamloops. Official reports were transmitted to the National Defence Operations Centre (NDOC) in Ottawa, National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ), and the National Research Council of Canada (NRC). The discrepancy in dates (April 22 vs. April 25) and durations (five minutes vs. one and a half hours) suggests either multiple distinct sightings or significant inconsistencies in the initial reporting process.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 迈克·布尔吉斯先生（Mike Bourguis，记录中亦作 Bourgois 或 Bourgeois）

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年4月25日，22:05Z；另有一份报告记录为1978年4月22日，08:30Z。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省坎卢普斯市霍尔特街805号；以及坎卢普斯以西19英里的加拿大国家铁路（CNR）轨道处。

**目击经过：** 相关文档中关于目击事件的持续时间和具体情况存在相互矛盾的描述。其中一组报告源自目击者位于霍尔特街805号的住所，描述了一个静止不动的物体，观测时长为一个半小时。根据该说法，物体保持固定位置，随后向后退去。

第二组报告与坎卢普斯以西19英里的加拿大国家铁路轨道地点有关，描述了一个持续约五分钟的短暂事件。在此版本中，物体被观测到从该区域上空经过，期间在附近的湖面上投射出橙色的反光。目击者称，该物体在经过时未发出任何声响。

**物体描述：** 该物体被一致描述为圆形。其颜色被记录为红、白、橙三色的组合。关于运动方式和声音，各方说法不一：有的描述为静止后“后退”的物体，有的则描述为从地表上方掠过、在下方水面留下橙色反光的静音物体。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件由加拿大武装部队坎卢普斯站（CFS Kamloops）正式处理。官方报告被传达至渥太华的国家国防作战中心（NDOC）、国防总部（NDHQ）以及加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）。日期（4月22日与4月25日）和持续时间（五分钟与一个半小时）上的差异表明，这要么是多次不同的目击事件，要么是初始报告过程中存在重大不一致。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Harold Charter (Radar Operator with 21 years of experience), Ottawa Air Traffic Control (RAPCON) personnel.

**Date / Time:** April 25, 1978; 1030Z to 1047Z (Total duration: 17 minutes).

**Location:** Ottawa, Ontario (observed via Ottawa RAPCON radar).

**Sighting:**
On April 25, 1978, between 1030Z and 1047Z, Ottawa Air Traffic Control (RAPCON) detected an unidentified radar return. The primary witness, Mr. Harold Charter, a radar operator with 21 years of professional experience, monitored the target throughout the 17-minute duration of the event. The object was initially detected at a distance of 110 miles from the RAPCON station at a bearing of 292 degrees. 

According to the radar data, the object engaged in a repetitive "race track" flight pattern, which it performed seven times. During these maneuvers, the object traveled outbound to a distance of 90 nautical miles on a heading of 292 degrees before turning back. The observation concluded when the object eventually faded from the radar screen while continuing on a heading of 292 degrees at its established speed.

**Object:**
*   **Shape/Size:** Not visually observed; identified solely as a radar return.
*   **Color:** N/A.
*   **Sound:** N/A.
*   **Movement:** The object exhibited highly unusual flight characteristics, specifically a repetitive race track pattern performed seven times. It maintained a consistent estimated speed of 1100 knots. The turns were described as "very tight" and were executed with extreme precision, with each turn accomplished within 1/6 of a minute.
*   **Duration:** 17 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The incident was documented through official Ottawa RAPCON radar logs. The equipment utilized for the observation was a RAPCON radar system operating at a rotation rate of 6-RPM. No further physical evidence, sketches, or weather-related interference reports were noted in the provided documentation beyond the technical radar parameters recorded by Mr. Harold Charter.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 哈罗德·查特先生（Harold Charter，拥有21年经验的雷达操作员）、渥太华空中交通管制（RAPCON）人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年4月25日；1030Z至1047Z（总持续时间：17分钟）。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华（通过渥太华RAPCON雷达观测）。

**目击经过：**
1978年4月25日，在1030Z至1047Z之间，渥太华空中交通管制（RAPCON）探测到一个不明雷达回波。主要目击者哈罗德·查特先生是一位拥有21年专业经验的雷达操作员，他在整个17分钟的事件过程中对该目标进行了监控。该物体最初在距离RAPCON站110英里、方位角292度处被探测到。

根据雷达数据显示，该物体进行了一种重复的“跑道型”（race track）飞行模式，并重复了七次。在这些机动过程中，物体沿292度航向向外飞行至90海里处，随后折返。当该物体以既定速度沿292度航向继续飞行并最终从雷达屏幕上消失时，观测结束。

**物体描述：**
*   **形状/大小：** 未进行目视观测；仅被识别为雷达回波。
*   **颜色：** 不适用。
*   **声音：** 不适用。
*   **运动：** 该物体表现出极不寻常的飞行特性，特别是重复进行了七次的跑道型飞行模式。它保持了约1100节的恒定预估速度。其转弯被描述为“非常急促”，且执行得极其精确，每次转弯均在1/6分钟内完成。
*   **持续时间：** 17分钟。

**调查/后续：**
该事件通过渥太华RAPCON的官方雷达日志进行了记录。观测所使用的设备为转速为6转/分的RAPCON雷达系统。除哈罗德·查特先生记录的技术雷达参数外，提供的文档中未提及任何进一步的物证、草图或与天气相关的干扰报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Walter Brent Murray (student), Stan Valenta, Nelson Smith, Mrs. Nelson Smith, Cst. P. Whattam (RCMP).

**Date / Time:** April 25, 1978. Primary sighting occurred at approximately 12:10–12:15 a.m. (0010–0015 hours). Follow-up documentation notes a time of 2050 hours (8:50 p.m.) for the interview/report.

**Location:** Ninette, Manitoba. The sighting occurred while the witness was driving north on Provincial Trunk Highway (PTH) 18, specifically two miles south of the junction of PTH 18 and PTH 23, and later near the north edge of Ninette.

**Sighting:** While driving north on PTH 18, Walter Brent Murray observed a single, bright, fluorescent orange, egg-shaped object. Shortly thereafter, five additional identical objects appeared, joining the first to form an east-west line. The objects maintained equal spacing and size, hovering in position. They eventually moved slowly eastward, crossing PTH 18 one mile north of Ninette. The objects descended rapidly—described as moving "like a helicopter landing"—behind the trees and brush of a valley rim, leaving a visible glow behind the foliage. Seconds later, the objects ascended vertically from the same location and vanished one by one, moving quickly to the northeast. During the event, Murray attempted to flag down a passing vehicle (a pink Thunderbird) in Ninette, but the driver did not stop. Murray noted that his car radio (CKY 58, Winnipeg) was playing during the event, but he could not recall hearing it until the lights disappeared, at which point the audio seemed unusually loud. Murray reported feeling scared during the encounter.

**Object:** Six identical, egg-shaped objects. They were described as extremely bright, fluorescent orange, and glowing, with no visible protuberances or secondary colors. They moved harmoniously, maintaining equal distance from one another. The objects produced a high-pitched, short whistle upon appearing and disappearing. The duration of the observation was estimated between 3 and 10 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Cst. P. Whattam of the Killarney RCMP detachment conducted the investigation. He patrolled the sighting area with Murray and interviewed neighbors Stan Valenta (living 4 km north/east of Ninette) and Mr. and Mrs. Nelson Smith (living 2 km east of Valenta). None of these neighbors reported seeing or hearing anything unusual. Cst. Whattam noted that C.F.B. Shilo is located 25–30 km north of Ninette and suggested the lights might have originated there, though he concluded he could offer no definitive explanation. Murray confirmed he was not under the influence of alcohol or medication, had received 12 hours of sleep prior to the event, and admitted to a personal belief in flying saucers. The incident was reported to the NRC Meteor Centre.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 沃尔特·布伦特·默里（Walter Brent Murray，学生）、斯坦·瓦伦塔（Stan Valenta）、尼尔森·史密斯（Nelson Smith）、尼尔森·史密斯夫人（Mrs. Nelson Smith）、P. 沃特姆警官（Cst. P. Whattam，加拿大皇家骑警）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年4月25日。主要目击时间约为凌晨12:10至12:15（00:10–00:15）。后续记录显示，访谈/报告时间为20:50。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省尼内特（Ninette）。目击事件发生时，目击者正驾车沿18号省道（PTH 18）向北行驶，具体位置在18号省道与23号省道交汇处以南两英里处，随后出现在尼内特北缘附近。

**目击经过：** 当沃尔特·布伦特·默里沿18号省道向北行驶时，观察到一个明亮的荧光橙色蛋形物体。不久之后，又出现了五个完全相同的物体，它们与第一个物体汇合，排成一条东西向的直线。这些物体保持着相等的间距和大小，悬停在空中。随后，它们缓慢向东移动，在尼内特以北一英里处穿过了18号省道。这些物体迅速下降——被描述为“像直升机着陆一样”——落入山谷边缘的树丛后方，在叶丛后留下了可见的余光。几秒钟后，这些物体从同一地点垂直升起，并逐一消失，迅速向东北方向飞去。事件期间，默里曾试图在尼内特拦下一辆经过的车辆（一辆粉红色的雷鸟轿车），但司机没有停车。默里注意到，他的车载收音机（温尼伯CKY 58电台）在事件发生时一直开着，但他直到光点消失前都记不起曾听到过声音，而光点消失时，收音机的声音似乎异常响亮。默里表示在遭遇过程中感到非常害怕。

**物体描述：** 六个完全相同的蛋形物体。它们被描述为极其明亮、呈荧光橙色且发光，没有可见的突起物或次要颜色。它们移动协调，彼此保持等距。这些物体在出现和消失时发出了短促的高频哨音。观察持续时间估计在3到10分钟之间。

**调查/后续：** 基拉尼（Killarney）加拿大皇家骑警支队的P. 沃特姆警官负责了此项调查。他与默里一同巡视了目击区域，并采访了邻居斯坦·瓦伦塔（住在尼内特东北方4公里处）以及尼尔森·史密斯夫妇（住在瓦伦塔以东2公里处）。这些邻居均表示没有看到或听到任何异常情况。沃特姆警官指出，希洛加拿大武装部队基地（C.F.B. Shilo）位于尼内特以北25至30公里处，并暗示这些光点可能源自该基地，但他最终表示无法给出明确的解释。默里确认自己当时未受酒精或药物影响，事发前已休息了12个小时，并承认自己个人相信飞碟的存在。该事件已报告给加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_13_-_Pages_36.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Hugh Rosebush, his wife, and his son.

**Sighting:** The sightings occurred on the nights of April 24, 25, and 26, 1978, from approximately 1930L to 2100L. The sky was clear for all sightings. Mr. Rosebush observed the phenomenon from his home at 12 Carl St, Belleville, Ontario.

**Object:** A single green light located to the northwest, which was observed rising and falling rapidly. The witness was unable to estimate the distance of the object.

**Aftermath:** Local police were sent to investigate. Mr. Rosebush contacted CFB Ops Trenton at 2100L to report that the light had disappeared over the horizon to the north-west. He indicated he would attempt to observe the light again on April 27.
