CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Boyd D. Geisler, Tracy L. Dobrescu, Kevin Sorenson, Cpl. R.C. Ferguson, Cst. J.K. Monaghan, Cst. D.J. Mann, Cst. Brian C. Woodward.

**Date / Time:** April 18, 1975; sightings occurred between approximately 7:30 PM and 11:45 PM CST.

**Location:** Moose Jaw, Tuxford, Marquis, and Keeler districts, Saskatchewan (including Highway #1 and Highway #42).

**Sighting:** The event began around 7:30 PM when Boyd Geisler observed a bright light while traveling west on a grid road near Tuxford. By 9:15 PM, he stopped his vehicle and observed the object for 45 minutes. He was accompanied by Tracy L. Dobrescu, who later corroborated his account. They reported the object hovering, descending, and emitting flashes of light similar to a mirror reflection. 

Simultaneously, RCMP officers were tracking a similar phenomenon. At 9:30 PM, Cpl. Ferguson and Cst. Monaghan observed a bright light to the northwest from Moose Jaw. At 10:00 PM, Cst. Woodward, parked five miles west of Moose Jaw on the Trans-Canada Highway, experienced heavy radio static and observed a light so intense it illuminated the area around his vehicle. At 10:15 PM, Cst. Woodward received a dispatch regarding a complaint from Kevin Sorenson concerning a UFO in the Keeler/Marquis district. The officers eventually converged and monitored the object for approximately one hour as it traveled northwest, maintaining a constant altitude. The sighting concluded at 11:45 PM when the object disappeared near the location of an Air Canada flight traveling from Regina to Edmonton.

**Object:** Descriptions varied based on observation methods. Initially appearing as a high-intensity white light with no discernible shape, closer inspection through field glasses revealed a triangular structure. Geisler reported that the object transformed into a semi-symmetric circle with a triangular section that emitted a beam of light from its center. It was observed tilting side-to-side, hovering, and varying in altitude from below to above cloud level. It remained at an estimated altitude of 1,500 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** RCMP officers (Ferguson, Monaghan, Mann, and Woodward) filed multiple statements and reports. Cst. Woodward noted significant radio interference during the event, and Geisler reported similar static on his car radio while on Highway #42. Official inquiries were made with the Regina Air Traffic Control and the Ministry of Transport, both of which reported no radar contact with any unidentified objects. CFB Moose Jaw confirmed their radar was not in operation at the time. Air Canada flights 233 and 286 were in the area between 11:20 PM and 11:30 PM, but crews reported nothing unusual, and the object's disappearance was noted in proximity to a commercial flight. Atmospheric conditions were reported as clear with scattered clouds and visibility exceeding 15 miles.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 博伊德·D·盖斯勒 (Boyd D. Geisler)、特蕾西·L·多布雷斯库 (Tracy L. Dobrescu)、凯文·索伦森 (Kevin Sorenson)、R.C. 弗格森下士 (Cpl. R.C. Ferguson)、J.K. 莫纳汉警官 (Cst. J.K. Monaghan)、D.J. 曼警官 (Cst. D.J. Mann)、布莱恩·C·伍德沃德警官 (Cst. Brian C. Woodward)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年4月18日；目击事件发生在北美中部标准时间 (CST) 晚上7:30至11:45之间。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省穆斯乔 (Moose Jaw)、塔克斯福德 (Tuxford)、马奎斯 (Marquis) 和基勒 (Keeler) 地区（包括1号公路和42号公路）。

**目击经过：** 事件始于晚上7:30左右，当时博伊德·盖斯勒在塔克斯福德附近的一条网格公路上向西行驶时，观察到一个明亮的光点。晚上9:15，他停车观察该物体长达45分钟。与他同行的特蕾西·L·多布雷斯库随后证实了他的说法。他们报告称，该物体在空中盘旋、下降，并发出类似镜面反射的闪光。

与此同时，加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 的警官们也在追踪类似的现象。晚上9:30，弗格森下士和莫纳汉警官在穆斯乔西北方向观察到了一个明亮的光点。晚上10:00，停在横贯加拿大公路穆斯乔以西五英里处的伍德沃德警官经历了严重的无线电静电干扰，并观察到一道极其强烈的光，照亮了他车辆周围的区域。晚上10:15，伍德沃德警官接到调度，称凯文·索伦森投诉在基勒/马奎斯地区发现不明飞行物。警官们最终汇合，并对该物体进行了约一小时的监视，观察到它向西北方向移动，并保持恒定高度。目击事件于晚上11:45结束，当时该物体在从里贾纳飞往埃德蒙顿的一架加拿大航空航班附近消失。

**物体描述：** 根据观察方式的不同，描述也有所差异。起初，它表现为一个没有明显形状的高强度白光，通过野外望远镜近距离观察时，发现其具有三角形结构。盖斯勒报告称，该物体转变为一个半对称的圆形，带有一个三角形部分，从中心射出一束光。观察到它左右倾斜、盘旋，并在云层下方到上方的不同高度间变动。据估计，它保持在1500英尺的高度。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警警官（弗格森、莫纳汉、曼和伍德沃德）提交了多份陈述和报告。伍德沃德警官指出事件期间存在严重的无线电干扰，盖斯勒也报告称他在42号公路上行驶时，车载收音机出现了类似的静电干扰。官方对里贾纳空中交通管制中心和交通部进行了询问，双方均报告称雷达未监测到任何不明物体。穆斯乔加拿大空军基地确认其雷达当时未处于运行状态。加拿大航空233号和286号航班在晚上11:20至11:30之间经过该区域，但机组人员未报告任何异常情况，且该物体的消失被记录在靠近一架商业航班的位置。据报告，当时大气条件晴朗，有零星云层，能见度超过15英里。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Ann Gervais 女士及其儿子。

**目击：** 该页面报告了 1975 年 4 月 24 日在乔治王子城 Parkridge Heights 发生的五次独立目击事件，时间跨度为 2015 至 2125 小时。观测期间天气从多云转为晴朗。事件总持续时间为 1 小时 10 分钟。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ken McNair, Terry McCormick, Con Pelletier, the author (of the Page 163 report), and one additional respondent (name partially illegible on the handwritten form).

**Date / Time:** January 19, 1975, at approximately 7:00 A.M. EST.

**Location:** Scorch Lake, near Foleyet, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the morning of January 19, 1975, the witnesses were at Scorch Lake preparing to unload gear from their vehicle. Ken McNair first spotted the object and alerted the others. The sighting lasted between one and one and a half minutes. According to the primary group, the object was observed against a black dawn sky. One respondent noted that the object moved from west to east across the sky, initially appearing at an elevation of 30 degrees above the horizon. As the object veered upward and in a southerly direction, its brightness diminished before it vanished at an elevation of approximately 35 degrees. Witnesses removed their hats in an attempt to hear the object, but reported no noise from the craft itself, noting only a slight wind.

**Object:** The object was described as "self-luminous" and brighter than a star. While the primary group described it as having a fuzzy and indistinct shape, the handwritten report noted a slight black ring and a white appearance. The object featured a single bright light located toward the front and bottom of the craft. Regarding scale, the witness compared the object’s length to a "Twin Otter" aircraft but noted it possessed significantly greater bulk. No markings were visible at the distance observed. The object initially traveled at a slow pace (estimated at 100 m.p.h.) before accelerating to a "terrific speed," estimated by one witness to be between 800 and 900 m.p.h. before it disappeared, changing its trajectory from an easterly to a southeasterly direction.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation includes a formal sighting narrative and a handwritten questionnaire. Environmental conditions were noted as very cold with a wind from the north; the sky to the south was clear enough to observe stars. The handwritten report specifies that the wind was slight at the time of the sighting but increased in intensity after daylight. The witnesses were located in a wilderness area where no animals were present. No official RCMP or investigative follow-up notes were provided in the provided pages, though the data was compiled into a formal report format.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 肯·麦克奈尔（Ken McNair）、特里·麦考密克（Terry McCormick）、康·佩尔蒂埃（Con Pelletier）、报告作者（第163页报告作者）以及另外一名受访者（手写表格上的名字部分难以辨认）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年1月19日，美国东部时间上午7:00左右。

**地点：** 安大略省福莱耶特（Foleyet）附近的斯科奇湖（Scorch Lake）。

**目击经过：** 1975年1月19日清晨，目击者们在斯科奇湖准备从车上卸下装备。肯·麦克奈尔首先发现了该物体并提醒了其他人。目击过程持续了一分半钟左右。据主要目击群体描述，该物体出现在黎明前的漆黑天空中。一位受访者指出，物体从西向东横穿天空，最初出现在地平线上方30度的高度。当物体向上并向南转向时，其亮度减弱，随后在约35度的高度消失。目击者们摘下帽子试图听清物体的声音，但报告称该飞行器本身没有任何声响，只听到了微风声。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为“自发光”，比星星更亮。虽然主要群体将其描述为形状模糊不清，但手写报告中提到它有一个细微的黑色圆环，外观呈白色。该物体在飞行器的前部下方有一个明亮的灯光。在尺寸方面，目击者将其长度与“双水獭”（Twin Otter）飞机进行了比较，但指出其体积要大得多。在观测距离内未见任何标记。该物体最初以缓慢的速度飞行（估计为每小时100英里），随后加速至“极高速度”，据一位目击者估计在每小时800至900英里之间，之后消失，其飞行轨迹也从向东转变为向东南方向。

**调查/后续：** 相关文档包括一份正式的目击叙述和一份手写调查问卷。记录显示当时环境非常寒冷，有北风；南方的天空足够晴朗，可以观测到星星。手写报告特别指出，目击时风力较小，但在天亮后风力增强。目击者当时位于荒野地区，周围没有动物。所提供的页面中未包含加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）或后续调查的官方记录，但相关数据已被整理成正式报告格式。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Ouida Emily McAdam (52, University of Lethbridge employee), an unnamed driver (likely McAdam), an unnamed working companion, an unnamed fireman, an unnamed man in a half-ton truck, and an unnamed individual who reported a sighting on CJOC radio.

**Date / Time:** January 23, 1975 (6:10 A.M. – 6:50 A.M. M.S.T.) and February 25, 1975 (approx. 6:30 A.M.).

**Location:** Lethbridge, Alberta (specifically the Oldman River coulee, Scenic Drive, and the University of Lethbridge area).

**Sighting:** On January 23, 1975, between 6:25 A.M. and 6:50 A.M., a witness driving west toward the University near the Oldman River observed an object approximately two car lengths ahead. Frightened, the driver performed a U-turn; the object followed the vehicle for two car lengths at car-roof height. Upon reaching the top of the hill, the object turned south and ascended rapidly. After the witness stopped to recover, they proceeded toward the university, at which point the object returned, headed west at high altitude, and suddenly vanished southward. Another witness reported a similar sighting at 6:10 A.M. via CJOC radio. The witness initially mistook the object for a street light but realized no such lights existed in that direction. A separate sighting occurred on February 25, 1975, at 6:30 A.M., where a reporter, a fireman, and a man in a half-ton truck observed an object on the west side of the river moving from south to north, ascending and descending near the horizon.

**Object:** The January 23 object was described as a solid, circular, orange-colored craft with a diameter of approximately 20 feet. It featured a dome on top that was a lighter shade than the rim. It was brighter than the background, made no noise, and left no exhaust, smoke, or debris. It performed sharp turns and high-altitude maneuvers. The February 25 object was described as appearing like the sun, but larger in size.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The case was documented via National Research Council of Canada (NRC) UFO sighting questionnaires (RG 77, Vol. 308). Investigations included mapping the sightings on Lethbridge city maps, noting specific flight paths near the High Level Bridge and Highway 3A. The witness reported significant psychological distress ("shock") and was contacted by various media outlets, including the *Lethbridge Herald*, the *Meliorist* (University paper), CBC Toronto, and Calgary media. The witness ruled out conventional explanations such as meteors, satellites, flares, or weather phenomena. Official records note the witness had 90% hearing loss and wore glasses, and that the inquiry was prompted by local radio and newspaper coverage.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威达·艾米丽·麦克亚当（Ouida Emily McAdam，52岁，莱斯布里奇大学员工）、一名未具名驾驶员（可能为麦克亚当本人）、一名未具名同事、一名未具名消防员、一名驾驶半吨卡车的未具名男子，以及一名在CJOC电台报告目击事件的未具名人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年1月23日（山区标准时间上午6:10 – 6:50）及1975年2月25日（约上午6:30）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省莱斯布里奇（具体地点为奥尔德曼河谷、景观大道及莱斯布里奇大学区域）。

**目击经过：** 1975年1月23日上午6:25至6:50之间，一名目击者驾车向西前往大学，在靠近奥尔德曼河时，发现前方约两辆车身距离处有一个物体。驾驶员感到惊慌并掉头行驶；该物体以车顶高度跟随车辆行驶了约两辆车的距离。当车辆到达山顶时，该物体转向南方并迅速升空。目击者停车平复情绪后继续前往大学，此时该物体再次出现，向西高空飞行，随后突然向南消失。另一名目击者于上午6:10通过CJOC电台报告了类似的目击事件。该目击者起初将物体误认为是路灯，但随后意识到该方向并无路灯。1975年2月25日上午6:30发生了另一起目击事件，一名记者、一名消防员和一名驾驶半吨卡车的男子观察到河西侧有一个物体由南向北移动，并在地平线附近升降。

**物体描述：** 1月23日的物体被描述为一个坚固的圆形橙色飞行器，直径约20英尺。其顶部有一个圆顶，颜色比边缘更浅。该物体比背景更亮，飞行时没有噪音，也没有留下废气、烟雾或碎片。它能进行急转弯和高空机动。2月25日的物体被描述为看起来像太阳，但体积更大。

**调查/后续：** 该案件通过加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的UFO目击调查问卷（RG 77, Vol. 308）进行了记录。调查内容包括将目击地点标注在莱斯布里奇城市地图上，并记录了其在高级别桥（High Level Bridge）和3A号公路附近的具体飞行路径。目击者报告称遭受了严重的心理创伤（“休克”），并受到了包括《莱斯布里奇先驱报》、《Meliorist》（大学校报）、CBC多伦多频道及卡尔加里媒体在内的多家媒体的采访。目击者排除了流星、卫星、照明弹或天气现象等常规解释。官方记录指出，该目击者有90%的听力损失并佩戴眼镜，此次调查是由当地广播和报纸的报道所引发的。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Rod McArter of Datagraphics and a friend.

**Sighting:** The witness reported seeing an object near Wakefield around 9:00 PM, looking east. The object was described as blinking red and green and was observed for a long time, moving around to the south. It was reported to have been seen on more than one evening.

**Object:** Initially reported as a blinking red and green object, later identified by the witnesses as the star Vega.

**Aftermath:** The author suggested that certain bright stars appear to flash red and green due to atmospheric conditions and position, noting that Vega was in the east around 8:20 PM. The author provided a star map to the witness. Later, the witness reported that he went to his friend's house on the next clear night, observed the object again, and they agreed with some chagrin that they were observing the star Vega.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 来自 Datagraphics 的 Rod McArter 及其一位朋友。

**目击：** 目击者报告称在 Wakefield 附近看到一个物体，时间约为晚上 9 点，朝东看。该物体被描述为闪烁着红色和绿色，被观察了很长时间，并向南移动。据称该物体在不止一个晚上被看到。

**物体：** 最初报告为一个闪烁红绿光的物体，后被目击者确认为织女星 (Vega)。

**后续：** 作者指出，由于大气条件和位置原因，某些明亮的恒星看起来会闪烁红绿光，并提到晚上 8:20 左右织女星位于东方。作者向目击者提供了星图。后来，目击者报告说他在下一个晴朗的夜晚去了朋友家，再次观察到了该物体，他们带着些许懊恼一致认为他们观察到的是织女星。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pte Bottaro LP and Pte Munro RJ, who were part of a new course of recruits at the base. Military Police also confirmed they saw the object.

**Sighting:** The object was observed at 0055 GMT on April 30, 1975, at the west entrance to building 34-7 at CFB Cornwallis. The object proceeded east across the horizon, changed direction to the north, and then proceeded south until it dropped below the horizon.

**Object:** The object's colors ranged from white when first sighted to green, then to red, and finally emitted some blue light before disappearance.

**Aftermath:** The sighting lasted for 30 minutes. The report was sent to the National Research Council (NRC) for the Radio and Electrical Engineering Division.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Pte Bottaro LP 和 Pte Munro RJ，他们是该基地新招募课程的学员。军事警察也证实他们看到了该物体。

**目击：** 目击事件发生在1975年4月30日格林威治标准时间0055，地点位于康沃利斯加拿大军队基地（CFB Cornwallis）34-7号楼的西入口。该物体向东横穿地平线，改变方向转向北，然后继续向南移动，直到降至地平线以下。

**物体：** 物体的颜色在最初目击时为白色，随后变为绿色，接着变为红色，最后在消失前发出了一些蓝光。

**后续：** 目击持续了30分钟。该报告被发送至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）无线电与电气工程部门。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. James Wizniak, Mrs. Lena Eileen Wizniak, Barry William Kocay, Mike Arthur Lasko, Lillian May Lawford, Cst. B.M. Beck (RCMP), and two unnamed acquaintances (one associated with Mr. Wizniak, one with Mr. Kocay).

**Date / Time:** April 28, 1975, beginning at approximately 10:00 P.M. and continuing past midnight.

**Location:** Hudson Bay, Saskatchewan (Northwest and Northeast sectors).

**Sighting:** At 10:00 P.M. on April 28, 1975, the Hudson Bay RCMP detachment received reports of a UFO. Cst. B.M. Beck observed the object using detachment binoculars, noting it remained stationary for five minutes before dropping a few feet and stabilizing. Multiple witnesses, including Barry Kocay, Lillian Lawford, and the Wizniaks, observed the object throughout the night. Witnesses described the object moving in erratic patterns—traveling miles in seconds, reversing direction, and gaining altitude—without making any noise. Several witnesses utilized rifle scopes (4-power) to observe the object in greater detail. Lena Wizniak reported the light was bright enough to illuminate the cross-hairs of her scope and cause eye strain. The object remained visible to various observers until after midnight, eventually fading or moving toward the Northwest.

**Object:** The object was described as round or elliptical, surrounded by a misty, hazy fog. It featured a brilliant central light (compared to an arc welder) and, at its base, distinct "windows" or squares of light. Some observers noted three smaller, half-moon-shaped lights on each side, while others reported red and blue flashing lights on the bottom. When stable, the object exhibited a downward-directed spotlight effect. It appeared to revolve while hovering and, when moving upward, seemed to diminish in size.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted a formal investigation, obtaining signed statements from all primary witnesses. Cst. B.M. Beck confirmed the reliability of the witnesses and noted that his own observations through binoculars corroborated their accounts. The RCMP verified that witnesses had not consumed alcohol. A diagram was included in the original file. The report was forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the National Research Council in Ottawa. Internal RCMP notes suggested the possibility of the object being Venus or Saturn, though the erratic movement and physical descriptions provided by the witnesses were documented as part of the official record. The RCMP attempted to keep the investigation low-key despite significant media interest.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 詹姆斯·维兹尼亚克先生 (Mr. James Wizniak)、莉娜·艾琳·维兹尼亚克夫人 (Mrs. Lena Eileen Wizniak)、巴里·威廉·科凯 (Barry William Kocay)、迈克·亚瑟·拉斯科 (Mike Arthur Lasko)、莉莲·梅·劳福德 (Lillian May Lawford)、B.M. 贝克警官 (Cst. B.M. Beck，加拿大皇家骑警) 以及两位未具名的熟人（分别与维兹尼亚克先生和科凯先生同行）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年4月28日，约晚上10:00开始，持续至午夜之后。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省哈德逊湾（西北和东北区域）。

**目击经过：** 1975年4月28日晚上10:00，哈德逊湾加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 分局接到关于不明飞行物的报告。B.M. 贝克警官使用分局的望远镜观察了该物体，注意到它保持静止五分钟后，下降了几英尺并趋于稳定。包括巴里·科凯、莉莲·劳福德和维兹尼亚克夫妇在内的多名目击者整晚都在观察该物体。目击者描述称，该物体以不规则的模式移动——在几秒钟内移动数英里、改变方向并提升高度——且全程没有任何声音。几位目击者使用了步枪瞄准镜（4倍率）来更详细地观察该物体。莉娜·维兹尼亚克报告称，光线非常明亮，足以照亮她瞄准镜的十字准线，并导致眼睛疲劳。该物体在午夜后仍可见，最终逐渐消失或向西北方向移动。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形或椭圆形，周围环绕着朦胧的雾气。它具有一个明亮的核心光源（被比作电弧焊），底部有明显的“窗户”或方形光点。一些观察者注意到其两侧各有三个较小的半月形灯，而另一些人则报告底部有红色和蓝色的闪烁灯光。当物体稳定时，会产生一种向下投射的聚光灯效果。它在悬停时似乎在旋转，向上移动时体积似乎会缩小。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警进行了正式调查，并获得了所有主要目击者的签名陈述。B.M. 贝克警官证实了目击者的可靠性，并指出他自己通过望远镜的观察结果与他们的描述相吻合。加拿大皇家骑警核实了目击者并未饮酒。原始档案中包含了一份示意图。该报告被转交至渥太华的国家研究委员会高层大气研究部门。加拿大皇家骑警的内部记录暗示该物体可能是金星或土星，但目击者提供的关于其不规则运动和物理特征的描述已被记录在案。尽管媒体对此事兴趣浓厚，但加拿大皇家骑警仍试图低调处理此次调查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Three individuals in a half-ton truck (including the primary witness, their father, their uncle, and Rod Parker’s sister).

**Date / Time:** May 4, 1975, between 11:15 PM and 11:59 PM C.S.T.

**Location:** 4.5 miles west and 1 mile south of Haywood, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On the night of May 4, 1975, a group of witnesses traveling in a half-ton truck observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. While driving at approximately 30 mph, the witnesses were positioned 4.5 miles west and 1 mile south of Haywood. During the observation, the group noted an emergency vehicle passing them on Highway #2 as they crossed the intersection of Highway #338. 

The accounts of the sighting vary slightly among the witnesses. One witness reported observing a light that moved sideways, as well as up and down, before it appeared to fall. Another perspective, provided by those in the truck, described the object as remaining stationary in the clear night sky. One witness noted a smaller ball of light moving around the larger primary object. While one witness explicitly stated the object was not a star and observed its erratic movement, another witness—who expressed general disbelief in UFOs—did not pay close attention to the observations made by his father. One witness noted that they did not see the object move further as they eventually went to bed.

**Object:** The object was described as a light that was not a star. Witnesses in the truck estimated the primary object to be approximately 4 inches in diameter (relative to their perspective) and dull red in color. While one witness could not determine the size due to the distance, others noted the presence of a smaller ball of light orbiting or moving around the larger, stationary red object. The duration of the sighting spanned from approximately 11:15 PM until at least 11:59 PM.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Carman Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation into the event. On May 5, 1975, at 9:37 PM, Cst. C.J. Cock took a formal statement from the primary witness. Additionally, the Carman Detachment dispatched a telex regarding the sighting to the National Research Council Meteor Centre in Ottawa on May 5, 1975, to report the incident for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 半吨卡车上的三名人员（包括主要目击者、其父亲、叔叔以及罗德·帕克（Rod Parker）的妹妹）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月4日，中部标准时间（C.S.T.）晚上11:15至11:59之间。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省海伍德（Haywood）以西4.5英里、以南1英里处。

**目击经过：** 1975年5月4日晚，一群目击者乘坐一辆半吨卡车时观察到一种不明空中现象。当时车辆正以约30英里的时速行驶，位置位于海伍德以西4.5英里、以南1英里处。在观察过程中，该群体注意到当他们穿过338号公路交叉口时，有一辆紧急救援车辆在2号公路上经过他们。

不同目击者对此次目击事件的描述略有差异。一名目击者报告称看到一道光在横向移动，并伴有上下起伏，随后似乎坠落了。卡车上其他人的视角则描述该物体在晴朗的夜空中保持静止。一名目击者注意到有一个较小的光球围绕着较大的主体移动。虽然有一名目击者明确表示该物体并非恒星，并观察到了其不规则的运动，但另一名对不明飞行物持普遍怀疑态度的目击者则并未太在意其父亲所观察到的情况。一名目击者提到，在他们最终上床睡觉时，并没有看到该物体有进一步的移动。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一道并非恒星的光。卡车上的目击者估计主体直径约为4英寸（相对于他们的视角），颜色为暗红色。虽然有一名目击者因距离原因无法确定其大小，但其他人注意到有一个较小的光球在围绕着那个较大的静止红色物体旋转或移动。目击持续时间从晚上约11:15一直持续到至少晚上11:59。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）卡曼（Carman）分队对该事件进行了调查。1975年5月5日晚上9:37，C.J. 考克（C.J. Cock）警官记录了主要目击者的正式陈述。此外，卡曼分队于1975年5月5日向渥太华的国家研究委员会流星中心（National Research Council Meteor Centre）发送了一份关于此次目击事件的电传，以报告该事件并请求进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A man from Haywood, his brother, and his son.

**Sighting:** On May 4, 1975, at approximately 11:59 PM CST, a man driving south of St. Claude, Manitoba, observed an object in the sky for approximately 15 minutes. The sky was clear at the time.

**Object:** The witness described the object as a ball of fire, red and white in color, and approximately 20 feet in diameter, or about the size of a house. It was noted to be bigger than the North Star and dull red in color. The witness stated it appeared to be burning molten metal.

**Aftermath:** The object moved south and then north. A red light appeared to strike the ship, causing it to take off faster. The witness stated the object appeared to be very close, located northwest of his position, and that it crashed in the vicinity of Lake Manitoba, where it appeared to burn out.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名来自海伍德的男子、他的兄弟以及他的儿子。

**目击：** 1975年5月4日，中部标准时间晚上11:59左右，一名在曼尼托巴省圣克劳德地区以南驾车的男子观察到一个物体，持续了约15分钟。当时天空晴朗。

**物体：** 目击者描述该物体为一个火球，呈红白两色，直径约20英尺，大小如同一座房子。它比北极星大，颜色暗红。目击者称其看起来像是在燃烧的熔融金属。

**后续：** 该物体向南移动，随后转向北。一道红光似乎击中了该飞船，使其加速离开。目击者称该物体看起来非常近，位于他所在位置的西北方，并坠毁在曼尼托巴湖附近，在那里它似乎燃烧殆尽。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. G.B. Guest, Cst. C.D. Manthorne, c/m J. Kereluik, and numerous local residents.

**Date / Time:** May 4, 1975, at approximately 12:40 a.m.

**Location:** Dauphin, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** At approximately 12:40 a.m. on May 4, 1975, two RCMP officers (Cst. G.B. Guest and Cst. C.D. Manthorne) and civilian J. Kereluik, while on patrol in Dauphin, observed two bright objects approaching the town from the northwest. Numerous local residents also reported witnessing the event. The objects traveled over the town and continued toward the southeast, remaining visible for a duration of approximately 10 minutes before fading from view. At the time of the sighting, the sky was overcast with a cloud ceiling of 2,500 feet; the objects were observed to be flying below this ceiling.

**Object:** The objects were described as two bright yellow lights. They maintained a constant light intensity throughout the duration of the sighting. The objects appeared to be positioned a few hundred yards apart from one another. No specific shape was discernible for either object. They moved very slowly and traveled in complete silence, producing no audible sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, the RCMP conducted inquiries with the local Department of Transport (DOT) station. The DOT confirmed there was no local air traffic at the time and reported that the Winnipeg head office had no corresponding radar detections. A telex regarding the incident was sent to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre in Ottawa. Additionally, a formal report was forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch at the National Research Council for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 警员 G.B. Guest、警员 C.D. Manthorne、平民 J. Kereluik 以及众多当地居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月4日，凌晨约12:40。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省多芬市 (Dauphin, Manitoba)。

**目击经过：** 1975年5月4日凌晨约12:40，两名加拿大皇家骑警（警员 G.B. Guest 和警员 C.D. Manthorne）与平民 J. Kereluik 在多芬市巡逻时，观察到两个明亮的物体从西北方向向该镇靠近。许多当地居民也报告目击了这一事件。这些物体飞越城镇并继续向东南方向移动，可见时间持续了约10分钟，随后消失在视野中。目击时，天空阴云密布，云层高度为2500英尺；观察到这些物体是在云层下方飞行。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两道明亮的黄光。在整个目击过程中，它们的光强保持恒定。这两个物体看起来彼此相距几百码。无法辨认出任何具体的形状。它们移动非常缓慢，且全程完全静音，没有发出任何可听见的声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，加拿大皇家骑警向当地交通部 (DOT) 站点进行了询问。交通部确认当时没有当地空中交通，并报告温尼伯总部也没有相应的雷达探测记录。一份关于该事件的电传被发送至渥太华的国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心。此外，一份正式报告被转交至国家研究委员会天体物理分部的高层大气研究科，以供进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Robert Diemert, Elaine Diemert, Robert Sheldon (also spelled Shelton), James Alldread (also spelled Audread), Harold Taylor, Cst. Ian Lloyd Nicholson, Paul Brian Sanders, Cst. W.B. Wotherspoon, Cst. C.J. Cock.

**Date / Time:** May 7, 1975 (approx. 11:00 P.M. – 11:45 P.M. C.S.T.); May 8, 1975; May 9, 1975 (7:28 P.M. – 7:40 P.M. and 12:15 A.M.); May 10, 1975 (11:45 P.M.).

**Location:** Carman, Manitoba, specifically at or near the Friendship Airfield, Highway 13, Graysville, and the junction of Highways 3 and 13.

**Sighting:** Between May 7 and May 10, 1975, multiple witnesses reported a series of aerial phenomena in the Carman district. On May 7, Robert and Elaine Diemert, Robert Sheldon, James Alldread, and Harold Taylor observed a red light approaching from the west, veering north, and proceeding east. Witnesses pursued the object in an automobile from the airfield toward town and along Highway 13, eventually losing sight of it as it headed toward Winnipeg. On May 9, Cst. Nicholson tracked a similar object for 12 minutes while on patrol, and Harold Taylor observed an object for 10 minutes near the airfield. On May 10, Paul Sanders observed a glowing object for five minutes using binoculars near the junction of Highways 3 and 13. All witnesses consistently reported that the objects made no noise, did not resemble conventional aircraft, and exhibited speeds ranging from 60 to 95 mph at altitudes between 500 and 1,500 feet.

**Object:** Descriptions varied but consistently featured red illumination. The object was described as oval-shaped, saucer-shaped, or an elongated "flying neon tube" with two straight lines and a brighter round center. Sizes ranged from "golf ball" size (at distance) to the size of a DC-3 or two-to-three light-plane wingspans. Specific details included a constant bright red center, an "X-shaped" white light background (reported by Cst. Nicholson), and 4–6 pulsating red lights visible when the object tipped or descended (reported by Sanders). No flashing, green, or white strobe lights were observed.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP (Csts. Wotherspoon, Cock, and Nicholson) conducted formal interviews and collected signed written statements from all primary witnesses. Robert Diemert, noted as an expert in vintage aircraft restoration, and pilot Robert Sheldon were considered highly reliable. The RCMP forwarded the collected reports to the National Research Council’s Astrophysics Branch. Weather conditions were reported as clear with slight wind. Despite attempts to track the objects via automobile and binoculars, witnesses were unable to intercept or identify the craft, and the Portage La Prairie RCMP detachment reported no corresponding radar or aircraft activity.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗伯特·迪默特 (Robert Diemert)、伊莱恩·迪默特 (Elaine Diemert)、罗伯特·谢尔顿 (Robert Sheldon，亦拼作 Shelton)、詹姆斯·奥尔德雷德 (James Alldread，亦拼作 Audread)、哈罗德·泰勒 (Harold Taylor)、伊恩·劳埃德·尼科尔森警官 (Cst. Ian Lloyd Nicholson)、保罗·布莱恩·桑德斯 (Paul Brian Sanders)、W.B. 沃瑟斯庞警官 (Cst. W.B. Wotherspoon)、C.J. 科克警官 (Cst. C.J. Cock)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月7日（约晚上11:00至11:45，中部标准时间）；1975年5月8日；1975年5月9日（晚上7:28至7:40及凌晨12:15）；1975年5月10日（晚上11:45）。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省卡曼 (Carman)，具体位于或靠近友谊机场 (Friendship Airfield)、13号公路、格雷斯维尔 (Graysville) 以及3号和13号公路交汇处。

**目击经过：** 1975年5月7日至5月10日期间，多名目击者在卡曼地区报告了一系列空中现象。5月7日，罗伯特·迪默特夫妇、罗伯特·谢尔顿、詹姆斯·奥尔德雷德和哈罗德·泰勒观察到一个红光物体从西面靠近，转向北面，随后向东飞行。目击者驾车从机场向城镇方向及沿13号公路追逐该物体，最终在物体飞往温尼伯方向时失去了踪迹。5月9日，尼科尔森警官在巡逻时追踪了类似物体12分钟，哈罗德·泰勒也在机场附近观察了该物体10分钟。5月10日，保罗·桑德斯在3号和13号公路交汇处附近使用双筒望远镜观察了一个发光物体5分钟。所有目击者一致报告称，这些物体没有发出任何声音，不像传统飞行器，且飞行速度在每小时60至95英里之间，高度在500至1500英尺之间。

**物体描述：** 描述虽有差异，但都一致提到红色的光照。该物体被描述为椭圆形、碟形，或是一个细长的“飞行霓虹灯管”，带有两条直线和一个较亮的圆形中心。尺寸从（远距离观察时的）“高尔夫球”大小到DC-3飞机大小，或相当于两到三架轻型飞机的翼展。具体细节包括一个持续明亮的红色中心、一个“X形”白色背景光（尼科尔森警官报告），以及当物体倾斜或下降时可见的4至6个脉冲红灯（桑德斯报告）。未观察到闪烁的绿光或白光频闪灯。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（沃瑟斯庞、科克和尼科尔森警官）进行了正式访谈，并收集了所有主要目击者的亲笔签名陈述。作为古董飞机修复专家的罗伯特·迪默特和飞行员罗伯特·谢尔顿被认为是非常可靠的证人。加拿大皇家骑警将收集到的报告转交给了国家研究委员会的天体物理学分部。据报告，当时天气晴朗，微风。尽管目击者试图通过汽车和双筒望远镜追踪这些物体，但未能拦截或识别该飞行器，且波蒂奇拉普雷里 (Portage La Prairie) 的加拿大皇家骑警分局报告称，当时没有相应的雷达记录或飞行活动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Jack Dickson, Mrs. Jack Dickson, Mr. Mel Eberwein, Mrs. Mel Eberwein

**Date / Time:** May 12, 1975, at approximately 10:30 P.M. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) to 11:30 P.M. MDT.

**Location:** Lethbridge, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the night of May 12, 1975, under clear sky conditions, Mr. Jack Dickson first observed an unidentified object located directly west of Lethbridge at approximately 10:30 P.M. Upon spotting the object, Mr. Dickson alerted his wife and their neighbors, Mr. and Mrs. Mel Eberwein. All four individuals observed the object as it moved in a northerly direction until it eventually appeared to be positioned north of Lethbridge. The group maintained visual contact with the object for approximately one hour, until roughly 11:30 P.M.

**Object:** The object was described as round in shape and was estimated to be at an altitude of approximately 15,000 feet. It emitted a very intense, bright white light; Mr. Mel Eberwein specifically compared the quality of this light to that of an electric welding arc. The witnesses also noted that the object displayed distinct traces of red and blue light within its illumination. No sound was reported, and the object maintained a consistent movement pattern toward the north throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report, the RCMP conducted an investigation involving multiple detachments, including Lethbridge, Picture Butte, and Ft. Macleod. None of the officers contacted at these detachments were able to locate or observe the object. During the follow-up, a Corporal noted that the only exceptionally bright object visible in the sky at the time was a star within the Great Bear constellation, suggesting this may have been the source of the sighting. Additionally, the RCMP contacted the Lethbridge Airport control tower, which confirmed that no pilots had reported any unusual activity or sightings in the area. The reporting officer concluded that while the witnesses were sincere in their accounts, the nature of the object remains questionable, particularly given the lack of corroborating reports from other members of the public or aviation personnel.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 杰克·迪克森先生（Mr. Jack Dickson）、杰克·迪克森夫人（Mrs. Jack Dickson）、梅尔·埃伯温先生（Mr. Mel Eberwein）、梅尔·埃伯温夫人（Mrs. Mel Eberwein）

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月12日，大约晚上10:30（山区夏令时间，MDT）至晚上11:30（MDT）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省莱斯布里奇（Lethbridge, Alberta）。

**目击经过：** 1975年5月12日晚，在天空晴朗的条件下，杰克·迪克森先生于晚上10:30左右首次观察到一个位于莱斯布里奇正西方向的不明物体。发现该物体后，迪克森先生立即通知了他的妻子以及邻居梅尔·埃伯温夫妇。四人共同观察到该物体向北移动，最终停留在莱斯布里奇的北部。该群体对该物体保持了约一小时的目视接触，直到晚上11:30左右。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，估计高度约为15,000英尺。它发出非常强烈、明亮的白光；梅尔·埃伯温先生特别将这种光的质感比作电焊弧光。目击者还注意到，该物体在光照中呈现出明显的红色和蓝色光迹。目击过程中未听到任何声音，且该物体始终保持向北的稳定移动模式。

**调查/后续：** 报告提交后，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）进行了调查，涉及莱斯布里奇、皮克彻比特（Picture Butte）和麦克劳德堡（Ft. Macleod）等多个分局。受访的警官均未能定位或观察到该物体。在后续调查中，一名下士指出，当时天空中唯一可见的异常明亮物体是大熊星座中的一颗恒星，并暗示这可能是目击事件的来源。此外，加拿大皇家骑警联系了莱斯布里奇机场控制塔，塔台确认没有任何飞行员报告该地区有任何异常活动或目击事件。负责警官总结称，尽管目击者陈述诚恳，但该物体的性质仍存疑，特别是考虑到缺乏其他公众成员或航空人员的佐证报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** WO Willits, Sgt Cossaboom

**Date / Time:** 15 May 1975, 0300Z

**Location:** CFS Lac St Denis

**Sighting:** 
On May 15, 1975, at 0300Z, a UFO sighting was reported at CFS Lac St Denis by WO Willits and Sgt Cossaboom. The witnesses observed the phenomenon under clear weather conditions, noting only occasional clouds present on the horizon. 

According to the accounts provided by both witnesses, the object was visible for a total duration of 20 minutes. The object was observed at an estimated distance of 2 to 3 miles to the west of the station. The witnesses described the object’s movement as a slow, horizontal motion, specifically noting that it moved back and forth. Throughout the duration of the sighting, the witnesses compared the object to the surrounding stars, noting that the object was significantly more intense in brightness than the stars visible in the sky.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a bright white light, circular in shape. It exhibited a varying intensity throughout the observation period. Its movement was characterized as slow and horizontal, with a distinct back-and-forth motion. The object was estimated to be located 2 to 3 miles away from the station and remained in view for 20 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was formally reported by CFS Lac St Denis. The documentation indicates that the report was transmitted from the station to NRHQ North Bay, and subsequently forwarded to RCCWC/NDHQ Ottawa. The information was then directed to the National Research Council (specifically the Division of Radio and Electrical Engineering) for further review and analysis. No additional sketches or RCMP interrogation records were noted in these specific pages.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威利茨准尉 (WO Willits)、科萨布姆中士 (Sgt Cossaboom)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月15日，0300Z

**地点：** 拉克圣丹尼斯加拿大武装部队基地 (CFS Lac St Denis)

**目击经过：** 
1975年5月15日0300Z，拉克圣丹尼斯加拿大武装部队基地的威利茨准尉和科萨布姆中士报告了一起不明飞行物目击事件。目击者在天气晴朗的条件下观察到了这一现象，仅注意到地平线上有零星云层。

根据两位目击者的陈述，该物体总共可见时长为20分钟。据估计，该物体位于基地以西2至3英里处。目击者描述该物体的移动方式为缓慢的水平运动，并特别指出它在进行来回摆动。在整个目击过程中，目击者将其与周围的恒星进行了对比，指出该物体的亮度明显强于天空中可见的恒星。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为一个明亮的白色圆形光点。在观察期间，其亮度呈现出强弱变化。其运动特征为缓慢的水平移动，并伴有明显的来回摆动。据估计，该物体距离基地2至3英里，并在视野中停留了20分钟。

**调查/后续：** 
该目击事件由拉克圣丹尼斯加拿大武装部队基地正式上报。文件记录显示，该报告先是从基地传送到北湾 (North Bay) 北部地区总部 (NRHQ)，随后被转交至渥太华的加拿大武装部队救援协调中心/国防部总部 (RCCWC/NDHQ)。随后，相关信息被送往加拿大国家研究委员会（具体为无线电与电气工程部）进行进一步的审查和分析。在这些特定页面中，未记录有额外的草图或加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 的审讯记录。

**Witnesses:** Lyle Carson and Mrs. Lyle Carson.

**Sighting:** On 12 May 1975 at 11:30 PM CST, under cloudy skies, Lyle Carson observed a green light that eventually moved east. The observation lasted 10 to 15 minutes.

**Object:** A green light.

**Aftermath:** On 14 May 1975, while checking fences 400 yards east of his farm, Lyle Carson discovered a perfectly round circle burnt in the grass. The circle measured 5 feet in diameter and was 6 inches thick on the outside edge. RCMP detachment in Tisdale, Saskatchewan, took photos and samples of the burned area to be forwarded.

**物体：** 一个绿色的光。

**后续：** 1975年5月14日，Lyle Carson 在其农场以东400码处检查围栏时，发现了一个在草地上烧出的完美圆形痕迹。该圆圈直径为5英尺，外缘厚度为6英寸。萨斯喀彻温省蒂斯代尔（Tisdale）的皇家骑警（RCMP）分队拍摄了照片并采集了烧焦区域的样本，以便后续转发。

**Witnesses:** Donald Cessford (45 years old, ex-armed forces personnel with aircraft experience) and his wife, Molly Cessford (45 years old), both of Minto Rd, Courtenay, BC.

**Sighting:** The event occurred at approximately 12:10 AM Pacific Standard Time on May 10, 1975. The sky was very clear with a temperature of approximately 50 degrees Fahrenheit. The witnesses were seated in their private vehicle at the time of the sighting.

**Object:** The object was described as a stationary, bright orange, oblong shape, approximately 25-30 feet in length horizontally. It was positioned approximately 20-30 feet above the horizon. A bright white light was noted on each end of the object.

**Aftermath:** The object was observed for approximately 60 seconds before it disappeared into thin air. The reporting officer noted that both witnesses were of sound mind and body, and the primary witness was sober at the time of the report.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Donald Cessford（45岁，前武装部队人员，有飞行经验）及其妻子 Molly Cessford（45岁），居住于不列颠哥伦比亚省考特尼市 Minto 路。

**目击：** 事件发生于1975年5月10日太平洋标准时间凌晨12:10左右。当时天空非常晴朗，气温约为华氏50度。目击者在目击时正坐在私家车内。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个静止的、明亮的橙色长方形物体，水平长度约为25-30英尺。它位于地平线上方约20-30英尺处。物体两端各有一个明亮的白光。

**后续：** 该物体被观察了约60秒，随后消失在空气中。报告警官指出，两位目击者均神志清醒，且主要目击者在报告时处于清醒状态。

**Witnesses:** Robert Edward Diemert, Elaine Diemert, Mary Kendrick, Bill Kendrick, Howard Bennett, Kerry McIntyre, and Allan Kerr.

**Sighting:** On May 13, 1975, at approximately 11:30 pm, Robert Diemert and his group sighted an oblong U.F.O. flying in an easterly direction for two minutes. Between 11:30 pm and 11:45 pm, Howard Bennett and Kerry McIntyre sighted a U.F.O. near Graysville, Manitoba, which is 7 miles west of Carman. Allan Kerr, a cameraman for CKY-TV, also sighted the object from a position 2 miles north and 1/2 mile east of Carman.

**Object:** The object seen by Diemert's group was described as oblong. The object seen by Bennett and McIntyre was at or near ground level, tilted at a 45-degree angle, and glowing red.

**Aftermath:** Allan Kerr advised that he may have 15-20 seconds of film of the object, though he noted it was shot from a considerable distance and might not be suitable once developed. The RCMP offered to contact these witnesses if the National Research Council required further information.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Robert Edward Diemert, Elaine Diemert, Mary Kendrick, Bill Kendrick, Howard Bennett, Kerry McIntyre 以及 Allan Kerr。

**物体：** Diemert一行人描述物体为长方形。Bennett和McIntyre描述物体位于或接近地面，以约45度角倾斜，并发出红光。

**Witnesses:** Henriette Bertouille (also referred to as Mrs. Henriette Bertouille)

**Date / Time:** May 29, 1975, at approximately 12:05 A.M.

**Location:** Provincial Road (PR) 245, approximately 2 miles west of Notre Dame de Lourdes, Manitoba (specifically identified as 6-7-9N and 5-7-9 W of the Rural Municipality of South Norfolk).

**Sighting:** 
On May 29, 1975, at 12:05 A.M., Henriette Bertouille, a nurse, was driving west on PR 245, roughly two miles west of Notre Dame de Lourdes, when she observed three unidentified objects. The sighting lasted for a duration of two to three minutes. According to the witness, the objects were traveling at a very high speed in a south-easterly direction at an altitude of approximately 100 feet above the tree tops. The closest distance between the witness and the objects was estimated to be approximately one mile. The objects eventually disappeared behind a cloud or a tree and were not seen again that evening.

**Object:** 
The witness described the objects as three bright red, round discs. Initially, they appeared to be the size of a baseball, but they grew larger as they approached the witness. Each disc was estimated to be approximately 3 feet in diameter. No specific sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP conducted an investigation and determined the witness, a nurse, to be mentally stable and reliable. Regarding environmental conditions, the sky was reported to be clear in the south and west at the time of the sighting, though it was beginning to cloud over in the north. The official report was formally forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch at the National Research Council in Ottawa, Ontario, for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 亨丽埃特·贝尔图耶（Henriette Bertouille，亦被称为亨丽埃特·贝尔图耶夫人）

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Jack Hunter, Tory Hunter, Christopher Bauer

**Date / Time:** May 31, 1975, at approximately 10:30 PM

**Location:** Marsh Lake District, near Mile 880.5 of the Alaska Highway, Yukon Territory

**Sighting:** On the night of May 31, 1975, Mrs. Jack Hunter, her son Tory Hunter, and their friend Christopher Bauer were present in the Marsh Lake area. At 10:30 PM, under clear skies with no cloud cover, the three witnesses observed an unidentified object passing directly over their location. The object traveled in a straight line at a high rate of speed, maintaining an altitude just above the tree line (estimated to be under 100 feet). The entire sighting lasted for approximately two seconds before the object disappeared from the witnesses' line of sight.

**Object:** The object was described as being shaped like an oversized or enlarged throwing dart, featuring a narrow front section and distinct fins on the rear. It was solid black in color and did not emit any flames or light. The only auditory phenomenon reported was a "swishing" sound, described as being similar to wind noise. The object moved at a high rate of speed and maintained a consistent, straight trajectory at a very low altitude.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was investigated by the Whitehorse detachment of the RCMP. Inspector J. Hunter and CST Sutton were involved in the documentation and reporting of the event. The RCMP conducted interviews with all three witnesses—Mrs. Jack Hunter, Tory Hunter, and Christopher Bauer—and noted in their official report that all individuals involved were of reputable character. The RCMP confirmed that no other sightings were reported in the area at that time. Following the investigation, the official report was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa, specifically directed to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch and the Meteor Centre.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 杰克·亨特夫人（Mrs. Jack Hunter）、托里·亨特（Tory Hunter）、克里斯托弗·鲍尔（Christopher Bauer）

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月31日，晚上约10:30

**地点：** 育空地区，阿拉斯加公路880.5英里路标附近的马什湖区（Marsh Lake District）

**目击经过：** 1975年5月31日晚，杰克·亨特夫人、她的儿子托里·亨特以及他们的朋友克里斯托弗·鲍尔身处马什湖地区。晚上10:30，在天空晴朗、无云遮挡的情况下，三名目击者观察到一个不明物体直接从他们头顶上方经过。该物体以极高的速度沿直线飞行，飞行高度仅略高于树梢（估计不到100英尺）。整个目击过程持续了约两秒钟，随后该物体便从目击者的视野中消失了。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为形状像一个超大号的飞镖，前端较窄，尾部有明显的鳍状结构。它通体呈纯黑色，没有发出任何火焰或光芒。据报告，唯一的听觉现象是一种类似于风声的“嗖嗖”声。该物体以极高的速度移动，并以极低的飞行高度保持着连贯的直线轨迹。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Marie Klatt

**Date / Time:** June 4, 1975, at approximately 12:00 AM to 12:10 AM

**Location:** Beaconia, Manitoba (over Lake Winnipeg)

**Sighting:** 
On the night of June 4, 1975, Mrs. Marie Klatt observed an unidentified flying object while standing on the front lawn of her residence in Beaconia. The sky was noted as clear with many stars visible. 

There is a discrepancy in the reported direction of the object’s travel between the initial observation and the follow-up report. In her initial account, Mrs. Klatt stated she watched the object for approximately 20 minutes as it traveled in a direct line from north to south over Lake Winnipeg. However, in her report to the Grand Marais RCMP detachment at 12:10 AM, she stated she had been watching the light for ten minutes as it moved from south to north over the lake. During the latter part of the sighting, she observed the object hover for a period of time before it eventually disappeared into the horizon to the north.

**Object:** 
The witness described the object as appearing larger than an airplane. Its shape was compared to an "inverted light bulb," and it was noted to be spinning. The object emitted a constant yellowish or yellowish-white light and appeared to be surrounded by a haze. It made no noise and flew at an altitude lower than that of a typical jet. No precise estimate regarding the object's physical size or its exact distance above the earth was provided.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was investigated by Cpl. R.L. Mawson and Cst. K.P. Amirault of the Grand Marais RCMP detachment. The officers conducted a patrol of the area and scanned the sky but observed nothing unusual. No other reports of strange lights were received by the detachment that night. 

In their official notes, the investigating officers described Mrs. Klatt as completely sober and genuine in her account, characterizing her as a reliable person. The investigation concluded with no further sightings or corroborating evidence found, and the case was documented for further reporting.

**目击者：** 玛丽·克拉特夫人 (Mrs. Marie Klatt)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月4日，大约凌晨12:00至12:10

**地点：** 马尼托巴省比科尼亚 (Beaconia, Manitoba)（温尼伯湖上空）

**目击经过：**
1975年6月4日晚，玛丽·克拉特夫人在比科尼亚的住所前草坪上观察到一个不明飞行物。当时天空晴朗，繁星可见。

关于该物体飞行方向的报告在最初观察与后续报告之间存在出入。在最初的陈述中，克拉特夫人称她观察了该物体约20分钟，它在温尼伯湖上空由北向南直线飞行。然而，在凌晨12:10向大马雷 (Grand Marais) 皇家骑警分局报告时，她却称自己观察了该光点10分钟，它在湖上空由南向北移动。在目击的后半段，她观察到该物体悬停了一段时间，随后最终消失在北方的地平线上。

**物体描述：**
目击者描述该物体看起来比飞机大。其形状被比作“倒置的灯泡”，并伴有旋转。该物体发出持续的黄色或黄白色光芒，周围似乎笼罩着一层薄雾。它飞行时没有任何声音，飞行高度低于普通喷气式飞机。关于该物体的具体物理尺寸或其离地面的确切距离，并未提供精确的估计。

**调查/后续：**
大马雷皇家骑警分局的R.L. 莫森 (R.L. Mawson) 下士和K.P. 阿米罗 (K.P. Amirault) 警员对此目击事件进行了调查。警员们对该地区进行了巡逻并扫描了天空，但未发现任何异常。当晚，该分局未收到其他关于奇异光点的报告。

在官方记录中，调查警员描述克拉特夫人神志完全清醒，陈述真实，并称她是一位可靠的人。调查最终未发现进一步的目击事件或佐证，该案件被记录在案以备后续报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Worobetz, Russel Worobetz, Cst. D.R. Stephenson

**Date / Time:** May 30–31, 1975 (Initial discovery); June 1, 1975, at 11:00 AM (RCMP investigation)

**Location:** A 30-acre stubble field, approximately one-quarter mile south of the Worobetz farm buildings, near Hazel Dell, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** The incident began when Russel Worobetz discovered suspicious burn marks in his stubble field while cultivating on Friday, May 30, 1975. His wife, Mrs. Worobetz, subsequently contacted the Sturgis RCMP detachment to report the findings, expressing her belief that the marks were caused by a UFO. 

Upon investigation by Cst. D.R. Stephenson, it was confirmed that there were two distinct burned areas located on a small knoll that overlooked a fairly large area of the surrounding terrain. Russel Worobetz stated definitively that he had not conducted any stubble burning on his property during the previous fall or the current spring, and he noted that no neighbors had performed any burning in the vicinity either. Worobetz further reasoned that the burns must have occurred during that spring, as he believed that any older burn marks would have been washed away by runoff water. He also confirmed that no unauthorized persons had been observed in the field.

**Object:** The physical evidence consisted of two circular burned spots, each measuring approximately 5 feet in diameter. The two spots were situated about 4 feet apart from one another. The soil within these circles appeared to be "fairly well burned" and the condition of the marks suggested they were fresh.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Due to the late hour of the initial report, the RCMP determined that an investigation during the night would be ineffective. On June 1, 1975, at 11:00 AM, Cst. D.R. Stephenson conducted a formal patrol and site inspection. During this visit, he interviewed Russel Worobetz and examined the site. 

The RCMP contacted the Yorkton detachment for guidance; the Officer Commanding (O.C.) advised that color photographs of the spots be taken. Cst. Stephenson utilized his private camera to document the scene. Following the documentation, the RCMP concluded that no further investigation was warranted at that time. A copy of the official report was forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section for their information.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 沃罗贝茨夫人（Mrs. Worobetz）、拉塞尔·沃罗贝茨（Russel Worobetz）、D.R. 斯蒂芬森警官（Cst. D.R. Stephenson）

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月30日至31日（最初发现）；1975年6月1日上午11:00（加拿大皇家骑警调查）

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省黑泽尔戴尔（Hazel Dell）附近，沃罗贝茨农场建筑以南约四分之一英里处的一块30英亩的茬地。

**目击经过：** 事件始于1975年5月30日星期五，当时拉塞尔·沃罗贝茨在耕作时发现其茬地里有可疑的烧焦痕迹。随后，他的妻子沃罗贝茨夫人联系了斯特吉斯（Sturgis）的加拿大皇家骑警分局报告了这一发现，并表示她认为这些痕迹是由不明飞行物（UFO）造成的。

经D.R. 斯蒂芬森警官调查确认，在一处俯瞰周围大片地形的小山丘上，确实存在两块明显的烧焦区域。拉塞尔·沃罗贝茨明确表示，他在去年秋天或今年春天都没有在自己的土地上进行过任何焚烧茬地的作业，并指出附近也没有邻居进行过任何焚烧活动。沃罗贝茨进一步推断，这些烧焦痕迹一定是在那个春天形成的，因为他认为任何更早的烧焦痕迹都会被径流冲刷掉。他还确认，未曾观察到有未经授权的人员进入该田地。

**物体描述：** 实物证据包括两个圆形的烧焦斑点，每个直径约为5英尺（约1.5米）。这两个斑点彼此相距约4英尺（约1.2米）。圆圈内的土壤看起来“烧得相当彻底”，且痕迹的状态表明它们是近期形成的。

**调查/后续：** 由于最初报告的时间较晚，加拿大皇家骑警认为夜间调查效果不佳。1975年6月1日上午11:00，D.R. 斯蒂芬森警官进行了正式的巡逻和现场勘查。在访问期间，他采访了拉塞尔·沃罗贝茨并检查了现场。

加拿大皇家骑警联系了约克顿（Yorkton）分局寻求指导；指挥官（O.C.）建议对这些斑点拍摄彩色照片。斯蒂芬森警官使用他的私人相机记录了现场。记录完成后，加拿大皇家骑警认为当时无需进行进一步调查。官方报告的副本被转发至高层大气研究部门（Upper Atmosphere Research Section）以供参考。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Malcom Herman

**Date / Time:** June 1, 1975 (Report date)

**Location:** Woodley District, Saskatchewan

**Sighting:** 
The event involves the discovery of a physical ground marking on agricultural land in the Woodley District. Malcom Herman, a local civilian described by the investigating RCMP officer as an honest and reliable individual, contacted the authorities to report a suspicious bare patch of earth he had discovered in his field. Mr. Herman suspected that the marking was the result of a UFO landing, having heard reports of such phenomena in the area. It is important to note that neither Mr. Herman nor any of his neighbors reported an actual visual sighting of an aerial object or craft at the time of the discovery.

**Object:** 
The physical evidence consisted of a bare patch of earth located on stubble land. The marking was described as a near-perfect circle measuring approximately 8 feet in diameter. The surface of the circle was characterized by the majority of the area being packed hard; however, there was a distinct exception in the center, where an area approximately 1 foot in diameter remained different from the surrounding packed earth. No sound, movement, or duration of an object was recorded, as no craft was observed.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
An RCMP patrol was dispatched to the scene to conduct an investigation and obtain a formal description of the site. The investigating officers noted that it was impossible to determine how long the patch had existed, as the field in question had not been worked or cultivated since the fall of 1974. 

In their official report, the RCMP acknowledged that they had investigated similar ground markings in the past, noting that there was no explainable reason for their existence. The file references a previous report regarding similar ground findings that had been submitted to the department in October 1974, suggesting a pattern of unexplained ground anomalies in the region. No further physical evidence or photographic sketches were explicitly detailed in the provided documentation beyond the descriptive measurements provided by the RCMP patrol.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 马尔科姆·赫尔曼 (Malcom Herman)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月1日（报告日期）

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省，伍德利区 (Woodley District)

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及在伍德利区的一块农田上发现的地面物理痕迹。当地平民马尔科姆·赫尔曼向当局报告称，他在自己的田地里发现了一块可疑的裸露土地。负责调查的加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警官形容赫尔曼先生是一位诚实可靠的人。赫尔曼先生怀疑该痕迹是由于不明飞行物着陆造成的，因为他曾听说过该地区出现过此类现象。需要指出的是，在发现该痕迹时，赫尔曼先生及其邻居均未目击到任何空中物体或飞行器。

**物体描述：**
物理证据是一块位于茬地上的裸露土地。该痕迹被描述为一个直径约8英尺的近乎完美的圆形。圆圈表面大部分区域被压得非常坚硬；但在中心位置有一个明显的例外，那里有一块直径约1英尺的区域与周围压实的土地不同。由于未观察到任何飞行器，因此没有关于物体声音、移动或持续时间的记录。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警派遣了一支巡逻队前往现场进行调查，并对该地点进行了正式描述。调查警官指出，由于该田地自1974年秋季以来一直未进行耕作或翻土，因此无法确定这块痕迹存在了多久。

在官方报告中，加拿大皇家骑警承认他们过去曾调查过类似的地面痕迹，并指出这些痕迹的出现没有任何可解释的原因。档案中提到了1974年10月提交给该部门的一份关于类似地面发现的报告，这表明该地区存在一种无法解释的地面异常模式。除了加拿大皇家骑警巡逻队提供的描述性测量数据外，所提供的文件中没有详细说明任何进一步的物理证据或摄影草图。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Vic Pepler (also referred to as V. R. Pepler)

**Date / Time:** June 10, 1975; approximately 8:30 p.m. to 9:45 p.m.

**Location:** Montague, Prince Edward Island, Canada

**Sighting:** 
On the evening of June 10, 1975, Vic Pepler, a local watchmaker and jeweller, observed an unidentified aerial object for a duration of one hour and fifteen minutes. Pepler utilized a tripod-mounted spotting scope equipped with 20-power and 48-power eyepieces to track the object. Throughout the observation, the object remained visible until it began to lose reflected sunlight around 9:45 p.m. 

Pepler noted that the object appeared to be at a very high altitude, a conclusion supported by the fact that reports of the same sighting were received from as far away as the Magdalen Islands. Pepler remarked that the object’s distinctness, behavior, and physical form were unlike anything he had previously observed. Analytical notes and sketches associated with the report include circular diagrams mapping the object's position, orientation, and drift. These diagrams utilize compass markings and dotted lines to illustrate the object's movement from the top right to the lower left (northeast to southwest) over the course of the 1.5-hour observation period.

**Object:** 
The object was described as perfectly upright and bullet-shaped, though one observer noted it resembled the end gable of a barn. It was characterized by a bright yellow color caused by reflected sunlight, featuring a distinct, brighter line running through it that resembled the lighted filament of an electric bulb. A unique "hanging drapery" effect was observed at the base of the object. 

While the object appeared stationary, it exhibited a slow drift from the northeast to the southwest. As the object sank toward the horizon, its light shifted from a reddish-gold hue to a colder, yellowish-white. Sketches provided by the witness depict a tall, clearly defined form with a pointed top and a curved, bright internal line. Annotations suggest the object was extremely bright, with its edges and form clearly visible against the sky due to the specific lighting conditions.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The documentation includes formal sketches and a written account provided by Vic Pepler. The file contains analytical notes regarding the object's size relative to the field of view and its trajectory. The records are held under the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) archives, specifically identified as RG 77, Vol. 308. No formal conclusion or official government determination is recorded in the provided pages.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 维克·佩普勒（Vic Pepler，亦被称为 V. R. Pepler）

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月10日；约晚上8:30至9:45

**地点：** 加拿大爱德华王子岛省蒙塔古（Montague）

**目击经过：** 
1975年6月10日晚，当地钟表匠兼珠宝商维克·佩普勒观测到一个不明飞行物，持续时间长达一小时十五分钟。佩普勒使用了一台安装在三脚架上的观测镜，并配备了20倍和48倍目镜来追踪该物体。在整个观测过程中，该物体一直清晰可见，直到晚上9:45左右，随着反射的阳光逐渐消失，它才隐去。

佩普勒指出，该物体似乎处于极高的高度，远至马格达伦群岛（Magdalen Islands）也有关于此次目击的报告，这一事实支持了他的判断。佩普勒表示，该物体的清晰度、行为和物理形态与他以往观测到的任何事物都截然不同。与该报告相关的分析笔记和草图包括了绘制物体位置、方位和漂移路径的圆形图表。这些图表利用罗盘标记和虚线，展示了该物体在1.5小时的观测期间从右上角向左下角（东北向西南）的移动轨迹。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为完全垂直且呈子弹状，不过有一位观察者指出它看起来像谷仓的端山墙。其特征是因反射阳光而呈现出明亮的黄色，物体中间有一条明显的、更亮的光线，类似于电灯泡中发光的灯丝。在物体底部观察到一种独特的“悬垂帷幕”效果。

虽然该物体看起来是静止的，但它表现出从东北向西南的缓慢漂移。随着物体向地平线沉降，其光线从红金色转变为较冷的黄白色。目击者提供的草图描绘了一个高大、轮廓清晰的形态，顶部尖锐，内部有一条弯曲的亮线。注释表明该物体极其明亮，由于特定的光照条件，其边缘和形态在天空中清晰可见。

**调查/后续：** 
相关档案包括正式草图和维克·佩普勒提供的书面陈述。文件中包含关于物体相对于视场大小及其轨迹的分析笔记。这些记录保存在加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的档案中，具体编号为 RG 77, Vol. 308。在提供的页面中，未记录任何正式结论或政府官方定论。

**Witnesses:** Cst J.R. Brault, Cst W.F. Joyce, and Cst R.J. Howe of the RCMP Brandon Detachment.

**Sighting:** On June 20, 1975, at approximately 11:10 PM, Cst Brault observed an illuminated object while on patrol 5 miles west of Kirkhams Bridge in the RM of Daly. At 11:30 PM, Csts Joyce and Howe, also on patrol in the area, sighted the same light.

**Object:** The object appeared as a bright white light suspended 200 to 300 feet above the ground. It was stationary and observed to become brighter on several occasions. A red flash was observed in the white light just before it disappeared at approximately 12:30 AM on June 21, 1975.

**Aftermath:** Cst Brault attempted to close with the object but had negative results. The officers pursued the object to approximately 3 miles southeast of Hamiota where it disappeared. A search of the area revealed nothing. Brandon Airport Tower was contacted and confirmed no aircraft were in the area. The reporting officer and other members involved concluded the object could be classified as a UFO.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Patrick McEnturff, Mrs. McEnturff

**Date / Time:** June 21, 1975, at 0400Z (also recorded as 210400Z)

**Location:** Crestview area, Winnipeg, Manitoba

**Sighting:** On June 21, 1975, at 0400Z, Mr. and Mrs. McEnturff observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the Crestview area of Winnipeg. The weather conditions at the time of the sighting were reported as partly cloudy. According to the witnesses, the object appeared from the northeast and moved in an erratic pattern. The object was initially observed moving slowly before it transitioned to a stationary position at a low altitude, where it remained for approximately 10 minutes. Following this stationary period, the object moved off in the same direction from which it had originally appeared. During its departure, the object increased its speed. The total duration of the sighting was 25 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as being extremely bright. Its luminosity was significant enough that it cast a reflection off the tops of the clouds as it passed through them. Regarding its movement, the object exhibited an erratic flight path, transitioning from a slow-moving state to a stationary hover at a low altitude for 10 minutes, before accelerating and departing the area.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally reported and documented by CFB Ops Winnipeg. The official report was subsequently transmitted to National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa and the National Research Council (NRC) for further review and record-keeping.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 帕特里克·麦肯特夫先生 (Mr. Patrick McEnturff)、麦肯特夫夫人 (Mrs. McEnturff)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年6月21日，0400Z（亦记录为210400Z）

**地点：** 马尼托巴省温尼伯市克雷斯特维尤 (Crestview) 地区

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为极其明亮。其亮度极高，以至于在穿过云层时，云顶都映出了它的反光。在运动轨迹方面，该物体表现出不规则的飞行路径，从缓慢移动状态转为在低空悬停10分钟，随后加速离开该区域。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Witness 1, Witness 2, and unnamed civilians returning home from downtown.

**Date / Time:** May 5–6, 1975; initial sighting at 21:13.

**Location:** Cornwall, Ontario; path moving north-northeast along the St. Lawrence River, through Summerstown and Lancaster, crossing the Quebec-Ontario border, and looping near Montreal, Quebec.

**Sighting:** At 21:13, witnesses observed a series of six UFOs traveling from the southwest to the northeast. The first object crossed the horizon in approximately 45 seconds. Thirty seconds later, a second object appeared, crossing the horizon in 20 seconds. Four additional objects followed at 20-second intervals, all traveling along the same flight path. The total duration of the event was estimated at 2 minutes and 30 seconds. Witnesses noted the sky was perfectly clear with high visibility of stars, though the moon was not visible. The objects maintained a high altitude, estimated between 20,000 and 30,000 feet, and remained in sight until passing over the horizon. While the first object was initially mistaken for an airliner, Air Canada confirmed no aircraft were in the vicinity.

**Object:** The objects were described as larger than a DC-9 aircraft. Physical descriptions included non-flashing red and green lights, while the sixth object exhibited a yellowish glow with randomly positioned red lights. Sketch B depicts large white lights, small red lights, and a hazy outline. A secondary sketch (Fig. 3) illustrates a rectangular or box-like shape. The objects moved at extremely high speeds, with the second object notably outspeeding the first. When viewed through 8x50 binoculars, the objects appeared to move in a distinct, formation-like line.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation was conducted by "Whitaud Investigator Inc." (located at 181/1810/1819 Edythe Avenue, Cornwall, Ontario). Official documentation includes three diagrams (Fig. 1, 2, and 3) mapping the flight path and the objects' orientation relative to the witnesses' residences. Investigators formally ruled out conventional explanations, including aircraft (confirmed by Air Canada), balloons, satellites, flares, ball lightning, heat inversions, noctilucent clouds, and the planet Venus. The case was officially classified as "Unidentified."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 目击者1、目击者2，以及从市中心返家的多名匿名平民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年5月5日至6日；首次目击时间为21:13。

**地点：** 安大略省康沃尔（Cornwall）；飞行路径沿圣劳伦斯河向北-东北方向移动，途经萨默斯敦（Summerstown）和兰开斯特（Lancaster），跨越魁北克省与安大略省边界，并在魁北克省蒙特利尔附近盘旋。

**目击经过：** 21:13，目击者观察到六个不明飞行物（UFO）从西南向东北方向飞行。第一个物体在大约45秒内穿过地平线。30秒后，第二个物体出现，并在20秒内穿过地平线。随后又有四个物体以20秒的间隔依次出现，均沿同一航线飞行。事件总持续时间估计为2分30秒。目击者指出当时天空非常晴朗，星光清晰可见，但月亮不可见。这些物体保持在高空，估计高度在20,000至30,000英尺之间，直至消失在地平线外。虽然第一个物体最初被误认为是客机，但加拿大航空公司（Air Canada）证实当时附近并无任何飞机。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为比DC-9型客机还要大。外观特征包括不闪烁的红灯和绿灯，其中第六个物体呈现出黄色的光晕，并带有随机分布的红灯。草图B描绘了巨大的白光、小红灯以及模糊的轮廓。另一份草图（图3）则展示了一个矩形或盒状的形状。这些物体以极高的速度移动，第二个物体的速度明显快于第一个。通过8x50双筒望远镜观察时，这些物体呈现出明显的编队飞行状态。

**调查/后续：** 该调查由“Whitaud Investigator Inc.”（地址：安大略省康沃尔市Edythe大道181/1810/1819号）负责。官方档案包含三张图表（图1、2和3），详细绘制了飞行路径以及物体相对于目击者住所的方位。调查人员正式排除了常规解释，包括飞机（已获加拿大航空公司证实）、气球、卫星、照明弹、球状闪电、逆温层、夜光云以及金星。该案件被正式归类为“不明飞行物”。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Frederika Giesbrecht, Robert Diemert, Elaine Diemert, and James Audread, all of Carman, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** The witnesses reported a U.F.O. passing over the Carman district at approximately 12:05 a.m. on June 27, 1975. The object was observed flying from the south-west at an estimated altitude of 2,000 feet and a speed of 800 mph. The sighting was made from a distance of 5 to 10 miles.

**Object:** The object was described as being approximately the size of a DC-3. It featured a brilliant white strobe-type light that appeared to revolve around the perimeter of another constant red or blue light. The object passed to the north of Carman, Manitoba, and continued on to the east or possibly slightly north-east.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP detachment considers the witnesses to be reliable. The report was forwarded to the National Research Council's Astrophysics Branch.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Frederika Giesbrecht、Robert Diemert、Elaine Diemert 和 James Audread，均为曼尼托巴省卡曼居民。

**目击：** 目击者报告称，1975年6月27日凌晨12:05左右，一个不明飞行物飞越曼尼托巴省卡曼地区。据估计，该物体从西南方向飞来，高度约为2,000英尺，速度为800英里/小时。观测距离为5至10英里。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为大约有DC-3飞机大小。它具有一个明亮的白色频闪灯，似乎在另一个恒定的红色或蓝色灯光周围旋转。该物体经过卡曼以北，随后向东或略偏东北方向飞去。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）认为这些目击者是可靠的。该报告已转交给加拿大国家研究委员会天体物理分部。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Raymond Malcolm Timmons, Beverly Ann Timmons (Mrs. Raymond Malcolm Timmons), and their three children.

**Date / Time:** July 2, 1975; sighting began at approximately 11:50 P.M. and continued until 12:00 midnight (and beyond).

**Location:** A field near the residence of the Timmons family in Cumberland, Prince Edward Island.

**Sighting:** On the night of July 2, 1975, the Timmons family observed an unidentified object maneuvering over a field near their home. According to the accounts, the sighting began at 11:50 P.M. and lasted for a total duration of approximately 15 minutes. The witnesses reported that the object hovered over the field and performed erratic, split-second movements, shifting both left-to-right and up-and-down. At one point during the event, the object approached to within 500 feet of the family’s house. The witnesses noted that the object eventually emitted a white light before disappearing toward the north. Throughout the duration of the sighting, the witnesses reported that the object made no sound.

**Object:** The object was described as having no identifiable shape. It featured two distinct lights—one red and one green. The red light was observed to fluctuate in intensity, shifting from bright to dim. The object’s altitude was estimated to range between 0 and 150 feet at various points during the encounter. The movement was characterized by rapid, split-second transitions, and the object remained in a hovering state for approximately 5 minutes of the 15-minute total duration.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report, Constable T. W. Ralph and another RCMP officer patrolled to the scene to conduct an on-site interview with Mr. Timmons. Official inquiries were made with both the Charlottetown Airport and C.F.B. Summerside; both facilities confirmed they had no radar contact or visual sightings of any object in the area at that time. The weather conditions were reported as clear. The incident was formally documented, and a telex regarding the sighting was transmitted to the National Research Council in Ottawa. The report was filed for information purposes.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 雷蒙德·马尔科姆·蒂蒙斯 (Raymond Malcolm Timmons)、贝弗利·安·蒂蒙斯 (Beverly Ann Timmons，雷蒙德·马尔科姆·蒂蒙斯夫人) 及其三个孩子。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年7月2日；目击事件始于晚上11:50左右，持续至午夜12:00（及之后）。

**地点：** 爱德华王子岛坎伯兰 (Cumberland) 蒂蒙斯一家住所附近的田野。

**目击经过：** 1975年7月2日晚，蒂蒙斯一家观察到一个不明物体在他们家附近的田野上空盘旋。据描述，目击事件始于晚上11:50，总持续时间约为15分钟。目击者称，该物体在田野上空盘旋，并进行了不规则的瞬间移动，在左右和上下方向上不断变换位置。事件期间，该物体一度靠近至距离蒂蒙斯家仅500英尺（约152米）处。目击者注意到，该物体最终发出了一道白光，随后向北方消失。在整个目击过程中，目击者称该物体没有发出任何声音。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体没有明确的形状。它带有两盏明显的灯——一红一绿。观察发现红光的亮度会发生波动，在明亮与暗淡之间交替。在遭遇过程中的不同时刻，该物体的飞行高度估计在0到150英尺（约0至46米）之间。其运动特征为快速的瞬间位移，在15分钟的总时长内，该物体保持盘旋状态的时间约为5分钟。

**调查/后续：** 报告发出后，T. W. 拉尔夫 (T. W. Ralph) 警官与另一名加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警员前往现场，对蒂蒙斯先生进行了现场访谈。官方分别向夏洛特敦机场 (Charlottetown Airport) 和萨默赛德加拿大武装部队基地 (C.F.B. Summerside) 进行了问询；两处设施均确认当时在该区域没有任何雷达接触或目视记录。据报告，当时天气晴朗。该事件被正式记录在案，一份关于此次目击事件的电传被发送至渥太华的国家研究委员会 (National Research Council)。该报告已归档以供参考。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. J. Macintyre (Joseph Alexander Wallace McIntyre), Katherine McIntyre, Richard McIntyre (13-year-old son), Oliver David Mulhall, Sylvia Mulhall.

**Date / Time:** July 4, 1975; July 5, 1975; July 9, 1975, at approximately 11:00 PM.

**Location:** Winnipeg, Manitoba (Specific addresses: 1359 Cavalier, West End; 284 Magnus Ave).

**Sighting:** 
The reports detail a series of sightings in Winnipeg during early July 1975. On July 4, Oliver David Mulhall and his wife, Sylvia, observed three large objects flying in a straight line from the southeast to the southwest, beginning at 10:30 PM and lasting for 90 minutes. They reappeared on July 5, moving at a higher speed and remaining visible for 35 minutes. Mr. Mulhall, a veteran with six years of British Army experience, initially withheld his report due to fear of ridicule but came forward after seeing a newspaper request for information.

On July 9, 1975, at approximately 11:00 PM, Joseph Alexander Wallace McIntyre, his wife Katherine, and their son Richard observed two objects in the sky for 35 minutes. These objects were seen hovering, separating, and then moving back together. A separate account from the McIntyre residence at 1359 Cavalier describes the observation of two fiery red lights joined by a white light, which hovered together for five minutes before departing to the west, with a total sighting duration of 10 to 15 minutes.

**Object:** 
The objects were described with varying characteristics. The Mulhall sighting involved a central object surrounded by 24–30 smaller white lights in a circle; the center object shifted colors between light blue, orange, and red, with the light intensity fluctuating as the smaller objects moved toward and away from the center. The flanking objects blinked white, appearing to send messages. 

The McIntyre family described the objects as top-shaped and approximately twice the size of an army tank. These objects displayed lights that cycled through brilliant green, blue, and white. Another account from the same family described the objects as flat and oval-shaped, featuring two fiery red lights and one white light.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sightings were reported to the authorities following newspaper solicitations for UFO reports. Joseph McIntyre explicitly noted that he was a moderate social drinker and had consumed no intoxicants on the night of July 9. Regarding the Mulhall report, an NRC (National Research Council) note suggested that the observed phenomena might be attributed to atmospheric diffraction or the effects of viewing the lights through an intervening window screen. No further official explanation was provided for the top-shaped objects or the specific maneuvers described by the McIntyre family.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** J. 麦金泰尔先生（约瑟夫·亚历山大·华莱士·麦金泰尔）、凯瑟琳·麦金泰尔、理查德·麦金泰尔（13岁儿子）、奥利弗·大卫·马尔霍尔、西尔维娅·马尔霍尔。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年7月4日、1975年7月5日、1975年7月9日，约晚上11:00。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省温尼伯（具体地址：西区卡瓦利耶街1359号；马格努斯大道284号）。

**目击经过：**
报告详细记录了1975年7月初在温尼伯发生的一系列目击事件。7月4日晚上10:30起，奥利弗·大卫·马尔霍尔及其妻子西尔维娅观察到三个大型物体呈直线从东南向西南飞行，过程持续了90分钟。这些物体于7月5日再次出现，移动速度更快，可见时长为35分钟。马尔霍尔先生曾有六年英国陆军服役经验，起初因担心被嘲笑而未报告，但在看到报纸征集相关信息后才站出来说明情况。

1975年7月9日晚上约11:00，约瑟夫·亚历山大·华莱士·麦金泰尔、其妻凯瑟琳及其子理查德观察到天空中出现了两个物体，持续了35分钟。这些物体被观察到处于悬停状态，随后分离，接着又重新汇合。来自卡瓦利耶街1359号麦金泰尔住所的另一份记录描述称，观察到了两个火红色的光点伴随一个白光点，它们共同悬停了五分钟后向西离去，目击总时长为10至15分钟。

**物体描述：**
这些物体被描述具有不同的特征。马尔霍尔目击到的物体中心由24至30个环绕的白色小光点组成；中心物体在浅蓝、橙色和红色之间变换颜色，随着周围小物体向中心靠近或远离，光强也会发生波动。侧翼的物体闪烁着白光，看起来像是在发送某种信息。

麦金泰尔一家将物体描述为陀螺状，大小约为陆军坦克两倍。这些物体发出的光在明亮的绿色、蓝色和白色之间循环。该家庭的另一份记录则将物体描述为扁平的椭圆形，带有两个火红色的光点和一个白色的光点。

**调查/后续：**
在报纸征集UFO报告后，这些目击事件被上报给了有关部门。约瑟夫·麦金泰尔明确表示，他平时适度饮酒，但在7月9日当晚并未饮用任何酒精饮料。关于马尔霍尔的报告，加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的一份说明指出，所观察到的现象可能归因于大气衍射，或是透过窗纱观察灯光所产生的视觉效果。对于麦金泰尔一家所描述的陀螺状物体及其特定机动动作，官方未提供进一步解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Frederika Giesbrecht

**Date / Time:** July 7, 1975, between 2:00 AM and 3:00 AM (Specific photographic timestamps: 2:25 AM, 2:44 AM, and 2:45 AM; one photographic record notes 2:27 AM)

**Location:** Carman, Manitoba

**Sighting:** On the early morning of July 7, 1975, Frederika Giesbrecht observed an unidentified light from her kitchen window in Carman, Manitoba. She was awake at the time because she was tending to a sick dog. The witness observed the light facing east, estimating its distance to be approximately 15 to 16 miles away. According to her account, the object initially appeared as a steady, non-pulsating light. It moved toward the witness, disappeared from view, and subsequently reappeared appearing significantly larger, brighter, and closer than before.

**Object:** The object was described as a yellow, almost white light that resembled the planet Venus. It emitted a steady glow and did not pulsate. Physically, it appeared as a single, small, bright point of light against the dark night sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was documented by the RCMP, with a formal statement signed by the witness and Cst. W.B. Wotherspoon of the Carman Detachment. Frederika Giesbrecht captured three photographs of the object using a camera equipped with a telephoto lens and a 3.8 mm lens. The photographic record is as follows:
*   **Photo 1:** Taken at 2:25 AM (noted as 2:27 AM on the image) with a 1/2 second exposure.
*   **Photo 2:** Taken at 2:44 AM.
*   **Photo 3:** Taken at 2:45 AM with a 3-second exposure.

The images show a single, small, bright light source against a dark background. A handwritten note included in the official file suggests that the planet Jupiter was rising low in the east at the time of the sighting, providing a potential astronomical explanation for the observation. The case is filed under the National Research Council of Canada, RG 77, Vol. 308.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 弗雷德里卡·吉斯布雷希特 (Frederika Giesbrecht)

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年7月7日，凌晨2:00至3:00之间（照片具体时间戳为：凌晨2:25、2:44和2:45；其中一份照片记录标注为凌晨2:27）

**地点：** 马尼托巴省卡曼 (Carman, Manitoba)

**目击经过：** 1975年7月7日凌晨，弗雷德里卡·吉斯布雷希特在马尼托巴省卡曼的家中，透过厨房窗户观察到了一个不明光源。当时她因照顾生病的狗而未入睡。目击者观察到的光位于东方，估计距离约15至16英里。据她描述，该物体最初表现为一个稳定、不闪烁的光点。它向目击者方向移动，随后消失在视野中，之后又再次出现，且比之前看起来更大、更亮、距离更近。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一种类似于金星的黄色、近乎白色的光。它发出稳定的光芒，没有闪烁。从物理形态上看，它在漆黑的夜空中表现为一个单一、微小且明亮的光点。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 记录在案，并由目击者与卡曼分局的 W.B. 沃瑟斯庞 (W.B. Wotherspoon) 警员共同签署了正式陈述。弗雷德里卡·吉斯布雷希特使用配备长焦镜头和3.8毫米镜头的相机拍摄了三张该物体的照片。照片记录如下：
*   **照片1：** 拍摄于凌晨2:25（图像上标注为2:27），曝光时间为1/2秒。
*   **照片2：** 拍摄于凌晨2:44。
*   **照片3：** 拍摄于凌晨2:45，曝光时间为3秒。

照片显示在黑暗背景下有一个单一、微小且明亮的光源。官方档案中包含的一份手写笔记指出，在目击当时，木星正从东方低空升起，这为此次观测提供了一种潜在的天文学解释。该案件归档于加拿大国家研究委员会 (National Research Council of Canada)，编号为 RG 77, Vol. 308。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Thomas (Tom) Whittaker and his family, Cst. R. E. Vokey, Cst. J.A. MacDonald, and the reporting RCMP officer.

**Date / Time:** July 13, 1975, at approximately 11:10 P.M. (initial sighting); RCMP arrival at approximately 12:00 A.M. (midnight); duration of final object approximately 1.5 hours.

**Location:** Glenfinnan, Prince Edward Island (North-East of Charlottetown).

**Sighting:** On the night of July 13, 1975, Mr. Thomas Whittaker and his family observed unidentified flying objects in the sky over Glenfinnan. Mr. Whittaker initially reported the sighting at approximately 11:10 P.M. By the time RCMP Constables R. E. Vokey and J.A. MacDonald arrived at the Whittaker residence at midnight, the sky was noted as clear and star-filled. 

The witnesses reported that they had initially observed three distinct objects. According to the family and the responding officers, two of these objects disappeared after approximately 15 minutes of observation. The third object remained visible in the sky for a total duration of approximately 1.5 hours. The RCMP officers confirmed their own observation of the remaining object to the north-east of Charlottetown from the Whittaker driveway.

**Object:** The objects were described as round, though their precise size and shape could not be definitively determined due to the great distance from the observers. The objects emitted green, red, and white lights that alternated in color. They were characterized by their erratic flight patterns, capable of performing both vertical and horizontal movements in "split-second" intervals. No sound was reported in association with the objects.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Upon arrival at the scene, the RCMP officers conducted a visual investigation and confirmed the presence of the light source. To rule out conventional aircraft, the RCMP contacted the Charlottetown Airport, CFB Summerside, and the Moncton Airport. All three facilities reported that their radar screens were clear and that there was no known aircraft traffic in the area at the time of the sighting. Following these inquiries, the official file was forwarded to the National Research Council Meteor Centre in Ottawa for further review, after which the case was closed.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 托马斯（汤姆）·惠特克（Thomas Whittaker）先生及其家人、警员 R. E. 沃基（R. E. Vokey）、警员 J. A. 麦克唐纳（J. A. MacDonald）以及负责报告的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警官。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年7月13日，约晚上11:10（首次目击）；加拿大皇家骑警于午夜12:00左右抵达；最后一个物体持续出现约1.5小时。

**地点：** 爱德华王子岛省格伦芬南（夏洛特敦东北方向）。

**目击经过：** 1975年7月13日晚，托马斯·惠特克先生及其家人在格伦芬南上空观测到不明飞行物。惠特克先生于晚上11:10左右首次报告了此次目击事件。当加拿大皇家骑警警员 R. E. 沃基和 J. A. 麦克唐纳于午夜抵达惠特克家中时，天空晴朗，繁星点点。

目击者称，他们最初观察到了三个不同的物体。据该家庭和出警警官所述，其中两个物体在观察约15分钟后消失。第三个物体在天空中持续可见，总时长约1.5小时。加拿大皇家骑警警官在惠特克家的车道上，亲自确认了该物体位于夏洛特敦东北方向。

**物体描述：** 物体被描述为圆形，但由于距离观测者极远，无法确定其确切大小和形状。这些物体发出交替变换的绿色、红色和白色光芒。其飞行模式极不稳定，能够在“瞬间”完成垂直和水平移动。据报告，这些物体未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 抵达现场后，加拿大皇家骑警警官进行了目视调查，并确认了光源的存在。为排除常规飞行器，加拿大皇家骑警联系了夏洛特敦机场、萨默赛德加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Summerside）和蒙克顿机场。这三处设施均报告称，其雷达屏幕显示正常，且在目击事件发生时该区域没有已知的飞行器活动。在进行这些问询后，官方档案被转交至渥太华的国家研究委员会流星中心进行进一步审查，随后该案件结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_08_-_Pages_21.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Stella Good

**Date / Time:** July 16, 1975 (reported in some documents as July 17, 1975), at approximately 1:10 A.M. Daylight Saving Time (DST).

**Location:** PTH-2, approximately 3 miles east of Rathwell, Manitoba (specifically NE 10-8-8 West in the Rural Municipality of South Norfolk).

**Sighting:** On the night of the sighting, Mrs. Stella Good was driving west on PTH-2. Under clear skies with the moon and stars visible, she observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for approximately 10 seconds. Mrs. Good was positioned approximately 1/4 of a mile away from the object as it traversed the area. Following the event, Mrs. Good contacted the RCMP Treherne Detachment to report the incident. A formal statement was taken from her at her farm later that morning.

**Object:** The object was described as being V-shaped and approximately 6 feet in length. It displayed a very bright, multi-colored appearance, specifically featuring blue, green, and red colors. The object was observed traveling at a very high rate of speed in a northerly direction, maintaining an altitude of approximately 150 feet above the ground.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Treherne Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation into the report. During their assessment, the RCMP noted that Mrs. Stella Good was considered to be a mentally stable and reliable witness. Following the collection of her statement, the official report was forwarded to the Upper Atmosphere Research Section of the Astrophysics Branch at the National Research Council in Ottawa, Ontario, for further review.
