A secondary reference in the file notes a related report dated August 7, 1968, which pertains to the same incident.
CA-FOIA-Part_01-p298-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 维克多·派（Victor Pye）、哈罗德·拉斯穆森（Harold Rasmussen）及其他当地居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月12日，晚上8:00左右。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省悉尼矿区（Sydney Mines）/北悉尼（North Sydney），托宾路（Tobin Road）。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月12日晚，包括维克多·派和哈罗德·拉斯穆森在内的多名当地居民目击了一起空中事件。哈罗德·拉斯穆森观察到一个类似于汽车前灯、后方拖着火焰的物体，正从东向西飞行。该物体发出了明显的轰鸣声。在经过时，它撞上了维克多·派住所正前方的电线。撞击引发了巨大的响声、明亮的蓝色闪光以及烟雾。撞击后，地面燃起了一小片草火，形成了一个面积约三平方英尺的完美圆形。在烧焦区域的中心发现了一块小石头。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为外观类似于汽车前灯，后方拖着火焰。它在飞行和移动过程中发出轰鸣声。虽然最初的报告将其归类为不明飞行物，但随后的官方评估认为该物体可能是一颗流星。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）北悉尼分局进行了调查，收集了烧焦的草地、泥土以及在撞击现场发现的石头样本。这些材料被送往道格拉斯（Douglas）先生处进行分析，并请求加拿大地质调查局对样本进行检验。东部电力公司（Eastern Light and Power Company）对现场的电线进行了调查，确认该地区发生了电力短缺；他们报告称，电线在撞击点两侧各10英尺的范围内出现了凹痕，且看起来有光泽。

此次调查面临行政审查，加拿大皇家骑警悉尼分区指挥部因北悉尼分局提交报告延迟40天而对其进行了训斥。该档案最终被转交至渥太华的专员处，并于1968年8月29日由哈利法克斯的刑事调查处（C.I.B.）正式结案。北悉尼分局的D.J.L. 温（D.J.L. Wein）最终认定该物体为陨石而非不明飞行物，随后档案被关闭。档案中的一份次要参考资料提到了一份日期为1968年8月7日的相关报告，该报告与此事件有关。

CA-FOIA-Part_14-p012-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cecil Hogan, Cecilia Hogan, RCMP Const. Caines (S.A. Caines), RCMP Const. Andrews, Mr. Jack Barry, Cpl. J.C. Gallant, Lionel Teed (Air Traffic Controller), Robert Gilbert (Air Traffic Controller), and Gander Tower personnel.

**Date / Time:** November 1, 1978, at approximately 2330 hours (with follow-up reports extending into November 2, 1978).

**Location:** Gander, Newfoundland (specifically observed from the Gander Airport control tower, the Trans-Canada Highway approximately 3 miles east of Gander, and the residence of Cecilia Hogan).

**Sighting:** On the night of November 1, 1978, at 2330 hours, a UFO was observed by multiple parties under clear sky conditions with good visibility. Air traffic controllers Lionel Teed and Robert Gilbert observed the object while on duty in the Gander Airport tower. Simultaneously, RCMP members Cpl. J.C. Gallant and Cst. S.A. Caines were positioned on the Trans-Canada Highway, approximately 3 miles east of Gander, where they monitored the object for approximately ten minutes in a stationary position before it gained altitude, faded, reappeared briefly, and finally disappeared to the east. Cecilia Hogan observed the object from her home, noting it appeared to be at a very low altitude, which contrasted with the RCMP members' assessment that the object was quite high and located east of Gander. Cecil Hogan also reported observing the object, which remained visible for a total duration of 35 minutes. Later in the event, the object appeared very dim and was visible by looking south toward the Trans-Canada Highway.

**Object:** The object was described as round. Cecilia Hogan provided a detailed description, noting it featured small blue windows, a very bright blue light, and orange and red flashing lights. While some reports indicated the object made no sound, Cecilia Hogan reported that it produced a "strange noise." The object’s movement involved remaining stationary for ten minutes before gaining altitude and eventually disappearing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The object was not detected on Gander Tower radar. Following the event, Mr. Jack Barry of Clarenville contacted the 226 Radar Squadron to express public concern regarding the frequency of UFO sightings in the Clarenville area and to inquire if the military would conduct an investigation. The 226 Radar Squadron informed Mr. Barry that no military investigation would be initiated unless directed by higher headquarters, though they agreed to document his concerns in their official report. The RCMP Gander Detachment (Cpl. Gallant and Cst. Caines) and Gander Tower personnel (Teed and Gilbert) served as the primary official observers for the incident.
CA-FOIA-Part_14-p012-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 塞西尔·霍根 (Cecil Hogan)、塞西莉亚·霍根 (Cecilia Hogan)、加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警员凯恩斯 (S.A. Caines)、加拿大皇家骑警警员安德鲁斯 (Andrews)、杰克·巴里先生 (Mr. Jack Barry)、下士 J.C. 加兰特 (J.C. Gallant)、莱昂内尔·蒂德 (Lionel Teed，空中交通管制员)、罗伯特·吉尔伯特 (Robert Gilbert，空中交通管制员) 以及甘德机场塔台工作人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年11月1日，约23:30（后续报告持续至1978年11月2日）。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省甘德市（具体观测点包括甘德机场控制塔、甘德以东约3英里处的横贯加拿大公路，以及塞西莉亚·霍根的住所）。

**目击经过：** 1978年11月1日晚23:30，在天空晴朗、能见度良好的条件下，多方观测到了一个不明飞行物 (UFO)。空中交通管制员莱昂内尔·蒂德和罗伯特·吉尔伯特在甘德机场塔台值班时观测到了该物体。与此同时，加拿大皇家骑警下士 J.C. 加兰特和警员 S.A. 凯恩斯位于甘德以东约3英里的横贯加拿大公路上，他们对该物体进行了约十分钟的监测，当时物体处于静止状态，随后它开始爬升、变暗、短暂重现，最后向东消失。塞西莉亚·霍根从家中观测到了该物体，她指出物体高度看起来非常低，这与加拿大皇家骑警认为物体高度较高且位于甘德以东的评估形成了对比。塞西尔·霍根也报告称观测到了该物体，其可见时长总计达35分钟。事件后期，该物体看起来非常暗淡，向南望向横贯加拿大公路方向时仍可见。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形。塞西莉亚·霍根提供了详细描述，指出其带有小型蓝色窗户、一盏非常明亮的蓝灯，以及闪烁的橙色和红色灯光。虽然一些报告称该物体没有发出声音，但塞西莉亚·霍根报告称它产生了一种“奇怪的噪音”。该物体的运动轨迹包括静止停留十分钟，随后爬升并最终消失。

**调查/后续：** 甘德机场塔台雷达未探测到该物体。事件发生后，克拉伦维尔的杰克·巴里先生联系了第226雷达中队，表达了公众对克拉伦维尔地区UFO目击事件频繁发生的担忧，并询问军方是否会进行调查。第226雷达中队告知巴里先生，除非接到上级指挥部的指示，否则军方不会启动调查，但他们同意将他的担忧记录在官方报告中。加拿大皇家骑警甘德分局（加兰特下士和凯恩斯警员）以及甘德塔台人员（蒂德和吉尔伯特）是此次事件的主要官方观测者。

CA-FOIA-Part_14-p021-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Michele GINGERA, Lori KIRCHHOFER, Linda Gail KIRCHHOFER, Colleen KIRCHHOFER, and Ken SWITALA.

**Date / Time:** November 7, 1978, at approximately 8:25 p.m. – 8:30 p.m. (Note: RCMP records also reference a related sighting by Ken SWITALA on November 5, 1978).

**Location:** 317 Geikie Street, Jasper, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 7, 1978, at approximately 8:25 p.m., witnesses Michele GINGERA, Lori KIRCHHOFER, and Linda KIRCHHOFER were at a residence on Geikie Street in Jasper. The weather was reported as very cloudy with heavy rain. The witnesses observed the lights at the KIRCHHOFER residence fluctuate (flicker) on and off three times; simultaneously, all streetlights on Geikie Street reportedly went out. Colleen KIRCHHOFER also observed this light flickering. 

While the group was walking toward a hockey game near a local church, Lori KIRCHHOFER alerted the others to an object in the sky. The witnesses observed the object moving in a south-westerly direction over the town. The altitude of the object was estimated to be higher than the town itself but lower than the peak of Signal Mountain. The sighting lasted for approximately two minutes before the object disappeared.

**Object:** The object was described with varying but consistent characteristics: it was round or oval in shape. Its color was reported as a mix of green, red, and a "bluey, greenish-yellow." The object was observed flickering on and off very rapidly. Witnesses described its movement as erratic, noting it moved both vertically and horizontally, and at one point appeared to be "jotting" back and forth. The light emitted by the object was bright enough to illuminate a large area in the vicinity of Signal Mountain.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Jasper Detachment documented the event based on information provided by Ernie GINGERA and the witnesses at the KIRCHHOFER residence. The official report includes the witness accounts as "Appendix A." The RCMP noted that a similar incident had been reported to their office by a Mr. Ken SWITALA on November 5, 1978. Despite the reports, the RCMP stated that no further sightings were reported to their office following this event, and no further official action was taken.
CA-FOIA-Part_14-p021-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 米歇尔·金格拉 (Michele GINGERA)、洛里·基尔霍夫 (Lori KIRCHHOFER)、琳达·盖尔·基尔霍夫 (Linda Gail KIRCHHOFER)、科琳·基尔霍夫 (Colleen KIRCHHOFER) 以及肯·斯威塔拉 (Ken SWITALA)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年11月7日，约晚上8:25 – 8:30。（注：加拿大皇家骑警的记录中也提到了肯·斯威塔拉于1978年11月5日目击的相关事件）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省贾斯珀市，盖基街 (Geikie Street) 317号。

**目击经过：** 1978年11月7日晚约8:25，目击者米歇尔·金格拉、洛里·基尔霍夫和琳达·基尔霍夫身处贾斯珀市盖基街的一处住宅内。据报告，当时天气多云且有大雨。目击者观察到基尔霍夫住所的灯光闪烁了三次；与此同时，盖基街上的所有路灯据称全部熄灭。科琳·基尔霍夫也观察到了这一灯光闪烁现象。

当一行人步行前往当地教堂附近观看曲棍球比赛时，洛里·基尔霍夫提醒其他人注意天空中的一个物体。目击者观察到该物体正向西南方向移动，飞越城镇上空。据估计，该物体的高度高于城镇，但低于信号山 (Signal Mountain) 的山顶。目击过程持续了约两分钟，随后物体消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体的描述虽有差异但特征一致：呈圆形或椭圆形。颜色被描述为绿色、红色以及一种“带蓝的绿黄色”的混合色。观察到该物体在快速地闪烁。目击者形容其运动轨迹不稳定，指出它既有垂直运动也有水平运动，一度看起来在“急促地”来回移动。该物体发出的光非常明亮，足以照亮信号山附近的一大片区域。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 贾斯珀分局根据厄尼·金格拉 (Ernie GINGERA) 及基尔霍夫住所目击者提供的信息记录了此次事件。官方报告将目击者的陈述作为“附录A”收录。加拿大皇家骑警指出，肯·斯威塔拉先生曾于1978年11月5日向其办公室报告过一起类似事件。尽管有这些报告，加拿大皇家骑警表示在此次事件后未再收到其他目击报告，也未采取进一步的官方行动。

CA-FOIA-Part_14-p031-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Edmond Robichaud, Larry Robichaud, Sandra Robichaud (daughter of Mrs. Edmond Robichaud).

**Date / Time:** November 12, 1978, between 23:00 and 23:45 hours (initial sighting); object remained visible until at least 01:00 hours on November 13, 1978. Follow-up statements were taken on November 13, 1978, at 17:07–17:15 hours.

**Location:** A residence in Acadie Siding, New Brunswick (three kilometers south of Rogersville).

**Sighting:** On the night of November 12, 1978, under clear skies, the Robichaud family observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. Mrs. Edmond Robichaud and her daughter, Sandra, first identified the object as a U.F.O. while observing it from their home. Larry Robichaud and his sister also observed the object, initially mistaking it for an aircraft before noting its unusual behavior. The witnesses reported that the object moved in an East-West direction and gradually climbed in altitude. After its maneuvers, the object appeared to transform into a bright, star-like point of light that remained stationary in the sky. Mrs. Edmond Robichaud noted that the object was still visible as a star at 01:00 hours when she retired for the evening. The duration of the primary observation period was reported as approximately 15 to 30 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as circular or round, though its precise form was difficult to discern due to the distance, which was estimated to be more than one mile (beyond the local hydro lines). It featured distinct, flashing red lights and blinking bluish-green lights, with the witnesses noting that the object appeared to change colors. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was investigated by the RCMP, with Constable J.E.D. Hache taking voluntary statements from the witnesses. On November 13, 1978, Lieutenant Dean of C.F.B. Chatham was consulted regarding potential military activity. Lt. Dean confirmed that a Vaudou plane had traveled through the area at 23:00 hours on the night of the sighting; however, he clarified that the aircraft did not possess blue or green lights and that its red lights were of a different nature than those described by the witnesses. A radiogram detailing the event was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council in Ottawa. Statements from Mrs. Edmond Robichaud and Larry Robichaud were formally attached to the official report, while Sandra Robichaud’s statement was delayed due to her travel to Saint John, N.B.
CA-FOIA-Part_14-p031-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 埃德蒙·罗比肖夫人 (Mrs. Edmond Robichaud)、拉里·罗比肖 (Larry Robichaud)、桑德拉·罗比肖 (Sandra Robichaud，埃德蒙·罗比肖夫人的女儿)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1978年11月12日，23:00至23:45之间（首次目击）；该物体至少持续可见至1978年11月13日01:00。后续证词于1978年11月13日17:07至17:15期间采集。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省阿卡迪赛丁 (Acadie Siding) 的一处住宅（罗杰斯维尔以南三公里处）。

**目击经过：** 1978年11月12日晚，在晴朗的天空下，罗比肖一家观察到一种不明空中现象。埃德蒙·罗比肖夫人和她的女儿桑德拉在家中观察时，首先将其认定为UFO。拉里·罗比肖和他的妹妹也观察到了该物体，起初误以为是飞机，随后注意到其异常的飞行行为。目击者报告称，该物体呈东西方向移动，并逐渐爬升高度。在完成机动后，该物体似乎变成了一个明亮的、星状的光点，并在天空中保持静止。埃德蒙·罗比肖夫人指出，当她在凌晨01:00休息时，该物体仍作为一颗“星星”可见。据报告，主要观察时段持续了约15至30分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，但由于距离较远（估计超过一英里，位于当地输电线之外），难以辨别其精确形状。它具有明显的闪烁红灯和闪烁的蓝绿色灯光，目击者注意到该物体似乎会变换颜色。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 进行调查，J.E.D. 哈切 (J.E.D. Hache) 警官采集了目击者的自愿证词。1978年11月13日，查塔姆加拿大空军基地 (C.F.B. Chatham) 的迪恩 (Dean) 中尉就潜在的军事活动接受了咨询。迪恩中尉证实，在目击当晚23:00，一架“伏都”(Vaudou) 战斗机曾飞越该地区；但他澄清说，该飞机没有蓝色或绿色灯光，且其红灯的性质与目击者描述的不同。随后，一份详细说明该事件的无线电报被转发至渥太华的国家研究委员会。埃德蒙·罗比肖夫人和拉里·罗比肖的证词被正式附在官方报告中，而桑德拉·罗比肖的证词因其前往新不伦瑞克省圣约翰市而有所延迟。

CA-FOIA-Part_14-p090-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Gerry Lafleur and his wife

**Date / Time:** January 5, 1979, at 23:00 hours; the object remained visible until 08:20 on January 6, 1979.

**Location:** Near Kathleen, Alberta (witnesses observed from their residence at Box 58, McLennan, Alberta).

**Sighting:** On the night of January 5, 1979, at approximately 23:00, Gerry Lafleur and his wife observed an unidentified object in the sky while at their residence near Kathleen, Alberta. The witnesses reported that the object remained stationary in the sky at an elevation of 45 degrees above the horizon for the duration of the night. The object maintained this fixed position for over nine hours until 08:20 the following morning, at which time it moved toward the southwest and disappeared from view.

**Object:** The object was described as bright white in color and oblong in shape. In terms of size, the witnesses estimated it to be slightly smaller than the moon. No specific sounds or mechanical details were reported, and the object remained static until its final movement at dawn.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was documented by the RCMP McLennan Detachment. The reporting officer, Cst. B.P.G. Bedard, conducted a follow-up investigation by checking with several neighbors in the area to see if anyone else had observed the phenomenon; however, no other reports were received. Cst. Bedard concluded his report by noting that he considers Mr. Lafleur to be a reliable witness.
CA-FOIA-Part_14-p090-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 格里·拉弗勒（Gerry Lafleur）及其妻子

**日期 / 时间：** 1979年1月5日23:00；该物体一直可见至1979年1月6日08:20。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省凯瑟琳（Kathleen）附近（目击者从其位于阿尔伯塔省麦克伦南（McLennan）58号信箱的住所进行观察）。

**目击经过：** 1979年1月5日晚约23:00，格里·拉弗勒及其妻子在阿尔伯塔省凯瑟琳附近的住所观察到了天空中出现的一个不明物体。据目击者报告，该物体在整晚都静止悬浮在高于地平线45度的天空中。该物体保持这一固定位置超过九个小时，直到次日清晨08:20，随后向西南方向移动并消失在视野中。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为亮白色，呈长方形。在大小方面，目击者估计它比月亮略小。报告中未提及任何特定的声音或机械细节，且该物体在黎明时分最后一次移动前一直保持静止状态。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）麦克伦南分局记录在案。负责报告的警官B.P.G. 贝达德（Cst. B.P.G. Bedard）进行了后续调查，询问了该地区的几位邻居，以确认是否还有其他人观察到这一现象；然而，未收到其他报告。贝达德警官在报告结尾指出，他认为拉弗勒先生是一位可靠的目击者。

CA-FOIA-Part_14-p250-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Scott Foster, located at 100 Wellington St, Kingston, Ontario.

**Sighting:** The observation occurred on September 22, 1979, at 220858Z. The weather conditions were clear and steady. The witness was located between Ontario Street and the lakefront at the foot of Wellington Street in the City of Kingston.

**Object:** The object was described as a starlike body, smaller than the moon, with a magnitude of 1 and a white color. The duration of the event was 1 second.

**Aftermath:** The observation was reported to the NRC Ottawa Meteor Centre. The trajectory was noted as 9 hours from plus 50 degrees to plus 45 degrees between the Big Dipper and [unclear].
CA-FOIA-Part_14-p250-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 斯科特·福斯特（Scott Foster）先生，位于安大略省金斯顿市惠灵顿街100号。

**日期：** 1979年9月22日，220858Z（格林威治标准时间）。

**地点：** 目击地点位于安大略省金斯顿市惠灵顿街尽头，安大略街与湖滨之间。当时天气晴朗且稳定。

**目击经过：** 该物体被描述为一个星状天体，比月亮小，亮度为1等星，颜色呈白色。事件持续时间为1秒。

**调查/后续：** 该观测记录已上报至渥太华国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心。记录显示其轨迹为从9点钟方向的北斗七星之间，由北纬50度移动至北纬45度（注：此处原文“[unclear]”部分不清晰）。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p008-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The unnamed narrator (writer), her husband, her daughter, Jean, Creighton, and Miss Amy M.

**Date / Time:** August 1957; specific sightings occurred on August 2nd (3:00 A.M.), August 22nd (11:00 P.M. – midnight), and a separate event at 1:15 A.M. (date unspecified). Miss Amy M.’s sighting occurred in late July.

**Location:** Canada (specific locale not provided in text).

**Sighting:** Throughout August 1957, the witnesses engaged in a consistent watch of the night sky, reporting sightings on every clear night. On August 2nd at 3:00 A.M., Jean observed a red, glowing object flying northeast, followed by a light resembling a bright star moving northwest. Approximately one and a half weeks prior to August 22nd, Creighton and the narrator observed an object crossing their path at a 40-degree angle. On August 22nd, between 11:00 P.M. and midnight, the narrator and Jean observed another object. 

In a separate account, the narrator (writer) reported that at 1:15 A.M., while in her kitchen, she heard a soft, purring motor sound. Upon going to the front door, she observed an aircraft-like object about half a block away, traveling on a course similar to previous sightings but slightly further east. Her husband and Jean were also present to witness this object. The narrator’s daughter reported hearing a strange, high-pitched sound during the event. The narrator noted that while many friends have seen these objects, they have not reported them to officials. Additionally, Miss Amy M. reported a separate experience in late July involving a fog-like or sun-colored object moving past her window, though she later speculated it may have been the sun obscured by fog.

**Object:** The objects were described as luminous, appearing either as red, glowing entities or as bright stars. Some displayed tiny white and green lights that blinked in a pattern similar to a marquee. The object seen at 1:15 A.M. displayed one very large, very white light. The objects were observed to move at more than a leisurely pace, occasionally dimming or extinguishing entirely before reappearing. They were never seen flying in formation, though two could be visible in the same direction simultaneously. The objects observed on August 22nd were noted to rotate and emitted a velvety, purring sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The witnesses attempted to observe the objects using a 16.5x50x50 telescope, but found the objects difficult to focus on due to their size and distance. The witnesses have maintained a nightly vigil since August 2nd, reporting that they see at least two objects on every clear night. No official RCMP or meteorological investigation notes were included in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p008-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 未具名的叙述者（作者）、她的丈夫、她的女儿、琼（Jean）、克雷顿（Creighton）以及艾米·M小姐（Miss Amy M.）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1957年8月；具体目击事件分别发生在8月2日（凌晨3:00）、8月22日（晚上11:00至午夜），以及另一起发生在凌晨1:15的事件（具体日期未详述）。艾米·M小姐的目击事件发生在7月下旬。

**地点：** 加拿大（文中未提供具体地点）。

**目击经过：** 在1957年8月期间，目击者们持续观测夜空，并在每个晴朗的夜晚都有所发现。8月2日凌晨3:00，琼观察到一个红色的发光物体向东北方向飞行，随后又出现了一个类似明亮恒星的光点向西北方向移动。在8月22日之前约一周半，克雷顿和叙述者观察到一个物体以40度角穿过他们的视线。8月22日晚上11:00至午夜之间，叙述者和琼观察到了另一个物体。

在另一起事件中，叙述者（作者）报告称，凌晨1:15，当她在厨房时，听到了一种柔和的、类似马达的嗡嗡声。她走到前门，观察到一个距离约半个街区远的飞行器状物体，其航向与之前的目击事件相似，但位置略偏东。她的丈夫和琼也在场目睹了该物体。叙述者的女儿报告称，在事件发生期间听到了一种奇怪的高频声音。叙述者指出，尽管许多朋友都见过这些物体，但他们并未向官方报告。此外，艾米·M小姐报告了7月下旬的一次独立经历，涉及一个雾状或太阳色的物体从她窗前经过，尽管她后来推测那可能是被雾遮挡的太阳。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为发光体，表现为红色的发光实体或明亮的恒星。有些物体显示出微小的白色和绿色灯光，并以类似跑马灯的模式闪烁。凌晨1:15观察到的物体显示出一道非常大且非常明亮的白光。据观察，这些物体的移动速度超过了悠闲的节奏，有时会变暗或完全熄灭，随后又重新出现。它们从未被观察到以编队形式飞行，尽管有时可以在同一方向同时看到两个物体。8月22日观察到的物体被注意到会旋转，并发出一种如天鹅绒般的嗡嗡声。

**调查/后续：** 目击者曾尝试使用16.5x50x50的望远镜观测这些物体，但由于物体的大小和距离原因，难以聚焦。自8月2日起，目击者们一直保持着每晚的守望，并报告称在每个晴朗的夜晚至少能看到两个物体。所提供的文档中未包含加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）或气象部门的任何官方调查记录。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p011-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The writer and others referred to as "we" report observations of far-distant moving lights in the Chignecto area. The letter also mentions an electronics engineer consulted by the writer about visibility at distance.

**Sighting:** The page says some distant moving lights were traveling at a speed that made high-flying jet planes seem to be moving when the aircraft itself could not be seen, only a vapour trail slowly growing longer. The writer says many of these were seen between midnight and two in the morning. It is suggested that some lights may have been reflections of the sun's rays off aircraft at sunrise or sunset. The writer also says some craft seemed to follow the same route for several days and then a different one for a while.

**Object:** The observed objects are described as moving lights, possibly conventional planes or perhaps a new and secret form of craft. Their manoeuvres are said not to be unlike known aircraft, but their frequency, lighting, sound, hovering, and sudden disappearance are noted as unusual.

**Aftermath:** The writer concludes that the Chignecto area seems to have been under continuing scrutiny by an unknown entity and suggests that a professional observer with adequate instruments might be rewarded with information. The writer notes that school will resume after Sept. 4, which will curtail nocturnal watches, but offers continued help if needed.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p011-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 撰写人及其他被称为“我们”的人报告了在奇格内克托（Chignecto）地区观察到的远距离移动光点。信中还提到了一位电子工程师，撰写人曾就远距离可见度问题咨询过他。

**目击经过：** 文中提到，一些远处的移动光点飞行速度极快，相比之下，高空喷气式飞机看起来就像静止不动一样（有时甚至看不见飞机本身，只能看到正在缓慢延长的尾迹）。撰写人表示，这些光点大多出现在午夜至凌晨两点之间。有人认为，其中一些光点可能是日出或日落时阳光照射在飞机上产生的反射。撰写人还指出，有些飞行器似乎连续几天沿同一航线飞行，随后又会更换航线。

**物体描述：** 所观察到的物体被描述为移动的光点，可能是常规飞机，也可能是某种新型且机密的飞行器。据称，它们的机动方式与已知飞行器并无二致，但其出现的频率、灯光、声音、悬停状态以及突然消失的特性被认为不同寻常。

**调查/后续：** 撰写人总结认为，奇格内克托地区似乎一直处于某种未知实体的持续监视之下，并建议由配备专业仪器的观察员进行观测，或许能获得更多信息。撰写人提到，9月4日学校开学后，夜间观测活动将会减少，但表示如有需要，仍愿提供协助。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p018-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The writer says a neighbor, a man with a responsible position with the C.N.R., had little patience with UFO interest but later came home from work and described what he had seen. The writer also refers to a Mounted Policeman who reportedly had heard of other reports, though he would not give details.

**Sighting:** The neighbor was driving from Cape Tormentine when the object was first noticed, around halfway between Cape Tormentine and Port Elgin, near Melrose. The writer says the sighting occurred about the same time as their own observation. The page describes a bright object in the sky that at first could have been mistaken for the moon, but then became extremely bright and illuminated the countryside before going out. The writer believes it may have been seen from a broad area and says there was no mention of it in the New Brunswick papers or on radio.

**Object:** The object is described as a bright “ball” in the sky. The writer says it did not have the reddish quality associated with meteors in the lower atmosphere, stayed apparently stationary, and seemed very bright and unusual. The neighbor thought it might have been a meteor, but said it had been too low, only a few hundred feet up, and too stationary for that.

**Aftermath:** The writer argues that the object’s position and direction would place it somewhere between Dorchester Chemical Park and C.F.B. Gagetown if it was seen from the reported road. The neighbor’s interview is called unsatisfactory because he took several minutes to arrive, the object disappeared before he got out of the car, and he then asked why the witnesses were the only ones seeing these things.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p018-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 撰稿人称，一位邻居——一名在加拿大国家铁路公司（C.N.R.）担任要职的男子——原本对不明飞行物（UFO）兴趣寥寥，但后来在下班回家后描述了他所见到的景象。撰稿人还提到了一名骑警，据称该警员曾听说过其他相关报告，但他拒绝透露具体细节。

**日期：** （原文未提供具体日期）

**地点：** 托曼廷角（Cape Tormentine）至埃尔金港（Port Elgin）之间的路段，靠近梅尔罗斯（Melrose）。

**目击经过：** 这位邻居在从托曼廷角驾车行驶时首次注意到了该物体，地点大约位于托曼廷角和埃尔金港的中途，靠近梅尔罗斯。撰稿人表示，此次目击事件发生的时间与他们自己的观测时间大致相同。文中描述天空中出现了一个明亮的物体，起初可能被误认为是月亮，但随后变得极其明亮，照亮了周围的乡村，然后熄灭。撰稿人认为该物体可能在很广的范围内都被看到了，并表示新不伦瑞克省的报纸和广播中均未提及此事。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为天空中一个明亮的“球体”。撰稿人称，它没有低层大气中流星通常带有的那种微红色，看起来处于静止状态，且显得异常明亮。邻居曾认为它可能是一颗流星，但表示它高度太低（仅几百英尺），且过于静止，不符合流星特征。

**调查/后续：** 撰稿人认为，如果从报告中所述的道路观测，该物体的位置和方向应位于多切斯特化学园区（Dorchester Chemical Park）和加格敦加拿大武装部队基地（C.F.B. Gagetown）之间。对邻居的采访被认为是不尽如人意的，因为他花了数分钟才抵达现场，且在下车前物体就已经消失了；随后他还质疑为何目击者们是唯一看到这些现象的人。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p025-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Dorr, Mrs. Dawson, William H. Dawson, the unnamed writer/narrator.

**Date / Time:** September 11, 1967; shortly before 7:00 p.m.

**Location:** Southwestern Halifax, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 11, 1967, shortly after sunset, a group of observers—including Mrs. Dorr, Mrs. Dawson, William H. Dawson, and the narrator—witnessed two unidentified objects over southwestern Halifax. Mrs. Dorr first spotted the objects with the naked eye, followed by Mrs. Dawson, who observed them using binoculars. The narrator also viewed the objects and coordinated with the others to confirm they were tracking the same phenomena. 

The objects moved lazily in a northerly direction across the city. The witnesses were able to trade places to view the objects through various instruments, including binoculars and a telescope. The objects eventually came to a stop at an elevation of 10 to 15 degrees above the western horizon. They hovered in this position for approximately 3 to 4 minutes before vanishing in a westerly direction just before 7:00 p.m. William H. Dawson, who has investigated aerial phenomena for over 20 years, noted that from a distance, the objects appeared solid and rigid, possessing a clarity of outline comparable to a vehicle crossing the Angus L. MacDonald Bridge.

**Object:** The two objects appeared as extremely bright, white "cells of light." When viewed at maximum magnification, they resolved into two distinct bodies, each appearing roughly the size of a quarter held at arm's length. They were described as resembling two bright, oval eyes or "flintened bells" floating side by side. While they appeared solid and rigid from a distance, William H. Dawson noted they lacked any visible signs of being constructed from thin, woven metallic strands. He further described their movement as possessing a buoyancy and weightlessness similar to a tea strainer. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, the narrator contacted the newsroom of Radio Station CJCH to inquire if other reports had been filed in the metro area. Official inquiries yielded conflicting information: Search-and-Rescue reported only one aircraft in the vicinity at the time, whereas a Navy spokesman claimed several planes were aloft at 6:00 p.m. The narrator concluded that the sighting was "100% definite" and not of man-made origin. William H. Dawson stated that the experience entirely obliterated any previous doubts he held regarding the existence of UFOs, characterizing the event as a significant reward for his decades of research into the mysteries of the universe.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p025-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 多尔夫人 (Mrs. Dorr)、道森夫人 (Mrs. Dawson)、威廉·H·道森 (William H. Dawson) 以及未具名的撰稿人/叙述者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年9月11日；下午7:00前不久。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省哈利法克斯西南部。

**目击经过：** 1967年9月11日傍晚，日落后不久，一群观察者——包括多尔夫人、道森夫人、威廉·H·道森和叙述者——在哈利法克斯西南部上空目击了两个不明物体。多尔夫人首先用肉眼发现了这些物体，随后道森夫人用双筒望远镜进行了观察。叙述者也观察了这些物体，并与其他人核对，确认他们追踪的是同一现象。

这些物体缓慢地向北穿过城市。目击者们轮流使用包括双筒望远镜和天文望远镜在内的各种仪器进行观测。最终，这些物体在西方地平线上方10到15度的高度停了下来。它们在该位置悬停了约3到4分钟，随后在下午7:00前向西消失。拥有超过20年空中现象调查经验的威廉·H·道森指出，从远处看，这些物体显得坚固且轮廓清晰，其清晰度堪比一辆驶过安格斯·L·麦克唐纳大桥 (Angus L. MacDonald Bridge) 的车辆。

**物体描述：** 这两个物体表现为极其明亮的白色“光团”。在最大放大倍率下观察时，它们呈现为两个独立的实体，每个看起来大约相当于手臂伸直时一枚25美分硬币的大小。它们被描述为像两只明亮的椭圆形眼睛或并排漂浮的“燧石钟”。虽然从远处看它们显得坚固，但威廉·H·道森指出，它们没有任何由薄金属丝编织而成的构造迹象。他进一步描述其运动方式具有一种类似于滤茶器的浮力和失重感。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，叙述者联系了CJCH广播电台的新闻编辑室，询问市区是否还有其他相关报告。官方调查结果相互矛盾：搜救部门报告称当时附近只有一架飞机，而海军发言人则声称下午6:00时有几架飞机在空中。叙述者断定此次目击事件是“百分之百确定”的，且并非人造。威廉·H·道森表示，这次经历彻底消除了他之前对不明飞行物（UFO）存在的所有怀疑，并将此次事件描述为对他数十年来研究宇宙奥秘的重要回报。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p028-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed farmer (resident of New Germany, NS), Michael Molloy.

**Date / Time:** August 1966 (radio anomalies); "One night last fall" (sighting); June 21, 1967, to June 30, 1967 (radio anomalies).

**Location:** New Germany, Nova Scotia (specifically a farm located in the woods approximately five miles from the town).

**Sighting:** The event involves two distinct but potentially related phenomena: a visual UFO sighting and anomalous radio interference. The unnamed farmer, living in an isolated area five miles from New Germany, reported that a saucer-shaped UFO descended from the sky one night during the previous autumn. The object circled his farmhouse at an altitude of approximately fifty feet. The farmer noted that the object was completely silent and produced no wind or breeze during its proximity. After circling, the object ascended rapidly and disappeared from view. 

Separately, Michael Molloy reported significant radio reception anomalies in the New Germany area. In August 1966, Molloy observed that the Boston radio station WBZ (1030 kHz) was received with unusual, constant clarity and strength, persisting day and night even when other stations faded. Molloy later reported that on June 21, 1967, the 1030 kHz signal vanished, only to return five minutes later. This signal persisted until June 30, 1967, at 1:30 p.m., when the station suddenly cut out during a musical track without the typical signs of fading or static.

**Object:** The UFO was described as saucer-shaped. While hovering over the house, it appeared as a sparkling, flickering, brilliant white light. Upon its rapid ascent and departure, the object shifted color to red. It was noted for its lack of sound and lack of atmospheric disturbance (no breeze).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Michael Molloy conducted his own follow-up by contacting the WBZ radio station in Boston. The station officially denied any changes to their power output or operational procedures during the period in question. Molloy hypothesized that the anomalous radio behavior was not caused by the station itself, but rather by UFOs intercepting radio signals and re-broadcasting them to larger extraterrestrial landing bases. Following these events, Molloy requested official forms to document any future UFO sightings. No other witnesses were identified for the farmer's sighting due to the isolated nature of his property.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p028-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一位未具名的农场主（新德国镇居民），迈克尔·莫洛伊（Michael Molloy）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1966年8月（无线电异常）；“去年秋天的一个晚上”（目击事件）；1967年6月21日至1967年6月30日（无线电异常）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省新德国镇（具体位于距离该镇约五英里林区内的一处农场）。

**目击经过：** 该事件涉及两种截然不同但可能相关的现象：视觉上的UFO目击和异常的无线电干扰。那位居住在新德国镇外五英里偏远地区的未具名农场主报告称，去年秋天的一个晚上，一个碟状UFO从天而降。该物体在距离他农舍约五十英尺的空中盘旋。农场主注意到，该物体完全静音，且在靠近时没有产生任何风或气流。盘旋过后，物体迅速升空并消失在视野中。

另外，迈克尔·莫洛伊报告称，新德国镇地区出现了严重的无线电接收异常。1966年8月，莫洛伊观察到波士顿的WBZ广播电台（1030 kHz）信号接收异常清晰且强劲，这种状态持续了昼夜，即便在其他电台信号减弱时依然如故。莫洛伊后来报告称，1967年6月21日，1030 kHz的信号突然消失，五分钟后又恢复正常。该信号一直持续到1967年6月30日下午1:30，当时电台在播放音乐时突然中断，且没有出现通常的信号衰减或静电干扰迹象。

**物体描述：** 该UFO被描述为碟状。当它悬停在屋顶上方时，看起来像是一道闪烁、跳动且明亮的白光。在迅速升空离开时，物体颜色转变为红色。其特点是完全无声，且未造成任何大气扰动（无风）。

**调查/后续：** 迈克尔·莫洛伊自行进行了后续调查，联系了位于波士顿的WBZ广播电台。该电台官方否认在相关时期内对其功率输出或操作程序进行过任何更改。莫洛伊推测，这种异常的无线电行为并非由电台本身引起，而是由UFO拦截了无线电信号，并将其转播至更大的外星着陆基地。事件发生后，莫洛伊索取了官方表格，以便记录未来可能出现的任何UFO目击事件。由于农场主住所位置偏僻，未发现其他目击者。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p035-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The page is a first-person handwritten account by one witness. No other names or identifying details are visible.

**Sighting:** The witness says the object flew up and down over the island, vertically and horizontally, for perhaps five to ten minutes before heading east immediately in front of the witness. The writer says they only question whether the occupants were trying to see the moon, or whether the plane was well lighted on the outside as well as within. They add that they do not think fault or starlike lights were involved.

**Object:** The object was seen as a lighted object and, in the witness's view, was quite obviously a falling star seen too often in August. The witness also says it was a flame, although more brightly lighted than they had seen before, and that it flew off in one direction.

**Aftermath:** No official response, report number, or later follow-up is visible on this page. The only clearly printed institutional marking on the page is "National Research Council of Canada / Conseil national de recherches du Canada" in the footer.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p035-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 该页面为一名目击者的第一人称手写记录。未见其他姓名或身份信息。

**日期：** 未提供。

**地点：** 未提供。

**目击经过：** 目击者称，该物体在岛屿上空上下、垂直及水平飞行了约五到十分钟，随后径直向东飞去，且正好从目击者正前方经过。作者表示，他们只是在质疑飞行器内的乘员是否在试图观察月球，或者该飞行器外部和内部是否都照明充足。他们补充说，认为这并非故障灯或星状光点。

**物体描述：** 该物体被视为一个发光体，在目击者看来，它显然是八月份经常能见到的流星。目击者还称它像是一团火焰，尽管比他们以往见过的都要明亮，且最终向一个方向飞离。

**调查/后续：** 该页面上未见任何官方回复、报告编号或后续跟进记录。页面页脚处唯一清晰印有的机构标识是“加拿大国家研究委员会”（National Research Council of Canada / Conseil national de recherches du Canada）。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p038-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unnamed narrator (Page 38), Unnamed narrator and his wife (Page 40), Rod Mattatall, Mrs. Evelyn Hicks

**Date / Time:** October 27, 1968

**Location:** Amherst, Nova Scotia / Sackville, New Brunswick / Atlanta (NB)

**Sighting:** On the night of October 27, 1968, multiple witnesses observed an unusual, bright light in the sky. One observer initially mistook the object for a star, noting it appeared through dark clouds, but quickly concluded it was not a star because it was approximately 15 times larger than any celestial body. This witness tracked the object moving directly north at an estimated altitude of 1.5 miles and a distance of 80 miles. 

Another account describes the object moving northwest over the Bay of Fundy while maintaining a constant altitude. The object exhibited complex flight patterns: it would hover, then move rapidly, and at one point, approximately 5 miles west of Amherst, it veered south, performing a noticeable "dip" before leveling off and continuing its journey. As it moved away, the intensity of the light appeared to fade. 

Rod Mattatall and Mrs. Evelyn Hicks, observing from an office in Atlanta, also witnessed the light. While some observers suggested the object might have been a helicopter, Mattatall explicitly rejected this, insisting it was "just a very bright light" and maintaining that he was a serious observer, not a "crackpot." The unnamed witness from Sackville noted that his wife also observed the movement, though she was initially skeptical about reporting the incident.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, very bright white light. It was significantly larger than a star (estimated 15 times larger). Its behavior included hovering, rapid linear movement, and distinct maneuvers, such as dipping and changing course (veering south). It maintained a consistent altitude while traveling over the Bay of Fundy and was tracked over a distance of at least 80 miles. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of handwritten witness statements and personal reports. Following the sighting, one witness attempted to verify the event by calling the CKDH radio station in Amherst to inquire if other UFO reports had been filed that night; he was informed there were none and subsequently took no further action. Rod Mattatall provided his contact information (P.O. Box 1045, Pringle St., Sackville, N.B.) as part of his formal statement. The files contain institutional markings from the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), indicating the reports were collected for official review, though no formal conclusion or weather data analysis is included in the provided pages.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p038-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 未具名叙述者（第38页）、未具名叙述者及其妻子（第40页）、罗德·马塔托（Rod Mattatall）、伊芙琳·希克斯夫人（Mrs. Evelyn Hicks）

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年10月27日

**地点：** 新斯科舍省阿默斯特（Amherst, Nova Scotia）/ 新不伦瑞克省萨克维尔（Sackville, New Brunswick）/ 亚特兰大（新不伦瑞克省）

**目击经过：** 1968年10月27日晚，多名目击者观察到天空中出现了一道异常明亮的光。其中一名观察者起初将该物体误认为是星星，注意到它穿过乌云显现，但很快断定它并非恒星，因为它的体积大约是任何天体的15倍。该目击者追踪到该物体正向正北方移动，估计高度为1.5英里，距离为80英里。

另一份记录描述该物体在保持恒定高度的同时，向西北方向飞越芬迪湾（Bay of Fundy）。该物体表现出复杂的飞行模式：它会悬停，然后快速移动；在阿默斯特以西约5英里处，它曾转向南方，做出了明显的“俯冲”动作，随后恢复平飞并继续航行。随着它逐渐远去，光线的强度似乎有所减弱。

在亚特兰大一间办公室观察的罗德·马塔托和伊芙琳·希克斯夫人也目睹了这道光。尽管一些观察者认为该物体可能是一架直升机，但马塔托明确否认了这一点，坚持认为它“只是一道非常明亮的光”，并强调自己是一位严肃的观察者，而非“疯子”。来自萨克维尔的未具名目击者提到，他的妻子也观察到了这一移动过程，尽管她起初对报告此事持怀疑态度。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为单一、非常明亮的白光。它明显比星星大得多（估计大15倍）。其行为包括悬停、快速直线移动以及明显的机动动作，例如俯冲和改变航向（转向南方）。它在飞越芬迪湾时保持了恒定的高度，并被追踪了至少80英里的距离。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案由手写的目击者陈述和个人报告组成。目击事件发生后，一名目击者曾试图通过致电阿默斯特的CKDH广播电台来核实当晚是否还有其他UFO报告；他被告知并没有，随后便未再采取进一步行动。罗德·马塔托在正式陈述中提供了他的联系方式（新不伦瑞克省萨克维尔，普林格街1045号信箱）。档案中包含加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的机构标记，表明这些报告已被收集以供官方审查，但所提供的页面中未包含正式结论或天气数据分析。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p049-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The page does not name any witnesses. It is a report form that is to be returned to Professor R. H. MacNeill at Acadia University in Wolfville, Nova Scotia, but no reporter name is filled in.

**Sighting:** The handwritten narrative says an object was seen “above a line” coming from the North East. It then “turned around gradually” and went to the South East. No exact time, date, or observing conditions are given on this page.

**Object:** The object is not described in detail beyond its movement and direction. The handwritten note emphasizes the change of course, from North East to South East, but does not mention shape, size, color, lights, sound, or duration.

**Aftermath:** The form includes blank lines for “Reported by” and “Address,” suggesting the report was not fully completed on this page. The printed footer identifies the National Research Council of Canada and the file marking “RG 77, Vol. 306.”
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p049-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 该页面未提及任何目击者姓名。这是一份旨在寄回给新斯科舍省沃尔夫维尔市阿卡迪亚大学 R. H. 麦克尼尔（R. H. MacNeill）教授的报告表格，但表格中并未填写报告人的姓名。

**目击经过：** 手写叙述称，有一个物体出现在“一条线”上方，来自东北方向。随后它“逐渐转向”，向东南方向飞去。该页面未提供确切的时间、日期或观测条件。

**物体描述：** 除运动轨迹和方向外，该物体没有其他详细描述。手写笔记强调了其航向从东北向东南的改变，但未提及形状、大小、颜色、灯光、声音或持续时间。

**调查/后续：** 表格中包含“报告人”和“地址”的空白行，表明该页面的报告并未填写完整。印刷的页脚标明了加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council of Canada）以及文件编号“RG 77, Vol. 306”。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p104-claude.report_summary:
The page says that the Canadian Aerial Phenomena Research Organization (CAPRO) wrote to Dr. Peter Millman at the National Research Council regarding a UFO sighting in Victoria, B.C. on September 29, 1968.

**Witnesses:** Mr. H. Voorsluys and Mr. R. F. Neal.

**Sighting:** The men reported observing and photographing a glowing object at approximately 8:30 p.m. MDST. One photograph showed a blurred light source followed by four circular lights, with the witness claiming five objects were ejected from the front-running light.

**Object:** A glowing object that appeared as a light source in night-time exposures.

**Aftermath:** CAPRO requested Dr. Millman's evaluation of the photographs, noting that one exposure showed star tracks and a light track moving opposite to the stars. The letter also mentions a separate sighting in Ste. Rose, Manitoba, on February 2, 1969, and a report from a Dawson Creek newspaper regarding a circular object observed at 5:45 p.m. MST on February 2nd.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p104-claude.report_summary_zh:
该页面记载，加拿大空中现象研究组织（CAPRO）曾就1968年9月29日发生在不列颠哥伦比亚省维多利亚市的一起UFO目击事件，致信国家研究委员会的彼得·米尔曼（Peter Millman）博士。

**目击者：** H. 沃斯勒伊斯（H. Voorsluys）先生和 R. F. 尼尔（R. F. Neal）先生。

**目击经过：** 两人报告称在山区夏令时间（MDST）晚上8:30左右观察并拍摄到了一个发光物体。其中一张照片显示了一个模糊的光源，后面跟着四个圆形光点；目击者声称有五个物体从领头的光源中喷射出来。

**物体描述：** 一个在夜间曝光照片中呈现为光源的发光物体。

**调查/后续：** CAPRO请求米尔曼博士对这些照片进行评估，并指出其中一张曝光照片显示了星迹，以及一条与星迹运动方向相反的光迹。信中还提到了1969年2月2日在曼尼托巴省圣罗斯（Ste. Rose）发生的另一起目击事件，以及道森克里克（Dawson Creek）一家报纸关于2月2日下午5:45（山区标准时间）观察到一个圆形物体的报道。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p111-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Harold Scott (residing at 10125 - 153 Street, Edmonton, Alberta)

**Date / Time:** February 1, 1969, at approximately 8:00 A.M.

**Location:** Highway 43, one mile east of Sangudo, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the morning of February 1, 1969, while traveling west on Highway 43, Harold Scott observed two distinct aerial phenomena. At approximately 8:00 A.M., under a sky covered with heavy clouds, Scott witnessed the first object. He described it as a small, oblong, bright white object moving north at a rapid speed at a very high altitude. This initial sighting lasted for 10 seconds. Approximately three minutes later, Scott observed a second object, which he speculated might have been the same craft as the first. This second object appeared much closer and larger, estimated to be at an altitude of 1,000 feet. It featured a flat base and an oval top, emitting a bright white glow. Like the first, this sighting lasted for 10 seconds before the object disappeared. Scott noted that he had previously observed similar objects four years prior while in British Columbia.

**Object:** 
*   **First Object:** Small, oblong, bright white, moving north at rapid speed at a very high altitude.
*   **Second Object:** Larger, flat base with an oval top, bright white glow/lights, moving north at rapid speed at an altitude of approximately 1,000 feet.
*   **Duration:** Each sighting lasted 10 seconds, with a three-minute interval between the two events.
*   **Sound:** No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was initially received by the Mayerthorpe RCMP Detachment, who subsequently notified the Officer Commanding (O.C.) of the Edmonton Sub-Division. Following the report, RCMP conducted patrols in the Sangudo area, but were unable to locate any other witnesses to corroborate the sighting. The file was forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre and the RCMP "K" Division in Edmonton. While the witness’s reliability was officially noted as unknown, the reporting officer observed that Scott appeared calm and collected during the interview. No further action was taken, and the file was concluded.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p111-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 哈罗德·斯科特（Harold Scott，居住地址：10125 - 153 Street, Edmonton, Alberta）

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月1日，大约上午8:00。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省桑古多（Sangudo）以东一英里处的43号高速公路。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月1日上午，哈罗德·斯科特在沿43号高速公路向西行驶时，观察到了两种截然不同的空中现象。大约上午8:00，在阴云密布的天空下，斯科特目击了第一个物体。他将其描述为一个小型、长方形、明亮的白色物体，正以极快的速度向北飞行，高度非常高。这次初步目击持续了10秒。大约三分钟后，斯科特观察到了第二个物体，他推测这可能与第一个是同一个飞行器。第二个物体看起来近得多也大得多，估计高度在1000英尺左右。它具有平坦的底部和椭圆形的顶部，并发出明亮的白光。与第一次一样，这次目击也持续了10秒，随后物体消失了。斯科特提到，他四年前在不列颠哥伦比亚省时也曾观察到过类似的物体。

**物体描述：**
*   **第一个物体：** 小型、长方形、明亮白色，以极快速度在高空向北移动。
*   **第二个物体：** 较大，底部平坦，顶部呈椭圆形，发出明亮的白光/灯光，以极快速度在约1000英尺的高度向北移动。
*   **持续时间：** 每次目击持续10秒，两次事件间隔三分钟。
*   **声音：** 未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该报告最初由梅耶索普（Mayerthorpe）皇家骑警分局接收，随后通知了埃德蒙顿分区指挥官。报告提交后，皇家骑警在桑古多地区进行了巡逻，但未能找到其他目击者来证实这一目击事件。档案被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心及位于埃德蒙顿的皇家骑警“K”分部。虽然目击者的可靠性被官方记录为“未知”，但负责报告的警官观察到，斯科特在接受采访时表现得冷静且镇定。此后未采取进一步行动，档案随之结案。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p155-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Margaret (Mrs. James Hartness) Beardsley.

**Sighting:** The page describes an investigation into sightings reported to the RCMP Detachment. Mrs. Beardsley, a resident of Deer Lake, Nfld., identified the object she observed as the planet Venus. She explains that the object appears to jump or vibrate due to atmospheric pressure and optical illusions caused by haze, smoke, and clouds.

**Object:** The report concludes that the sightings are not Unidentified Flying Objects, but rather the planet Venus, meteors, or fireballs. Specifically, an incident on 30 DEC 68 involving sunset rays on jet aircraft vapor is noted.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP officer, Sgt. R.W. Morrison of the Corner Brook City Detachment, concludes that the reports are classified as astronomical or atmospheric phenomena and are submitted for information purposes only.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p155-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 玛格丽特·比尔兹利（Margaret Beardsley，詹姆斯·哈特内斯夫人）。

**日期：** 未提供具体日期（报告提及1968年12月30日的相关事件）。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省鹿湖（Deer Lake, Nfld.）。

**目击经过：** 该页面描述了针对向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）分局报告的目击事件所进行的调查。居住在纽芬兰省鹿湖的玛格丽特·比尔兹利女士确认，她所观察到的物体是金星。她解释说，该物体之所以看起来在跳动或振动，是由于大气压力以及雾霾、烟雾和云层所引发的视错觉造成的。

**物体描述：** 报告结论指出，这些目击事件并非不明飞行物，而是金星、流星或火球。报告特别提到了1968年12月30日发生的一起事件，该事件涉及喷气式飞机尾迹在日落余晖下的现象。

**调查/后续：** 来自科纳布鲁克市（Corner Brook City）分局的加拿大皇家骑警警官R.W.莫里森（Sgt. R.W. Morrison）得出结论，这些报告被归类为天文或大气现象，仅供参考存档。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p175-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The author (unnamed), Mrs. T. Homelaar, Mrs. Agnes J. B. Miller, Mrs. Hemelhan, and a group of people at a school.

**Date / Time:** February 20, 1969; approximately 12:00 AM (midnight) to 1:30 AM.

**Location:** Newmarket, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the night of February 20, 1969, a UFO sighting occurred in Newmarket, Ontario, involving multiple observers. The author and Mrs. T. Homelaar observed a bright object from a living room window facing west-southwest. Simultaneously, Mrs. Agnes J. B. Miller reported that Mrs. Hemelhan observed the object for an extended period while at a school where a group of people were gathered to watch it. The witnesses reported the object remained visible for approximately one and a half hours. Mrs. Miller noted that the object eventually departed in a circular movement at a "fantastic speed."

**Object:** The object was described as resembling a very large star. Its appearance was highly dynamic, characterized by a flickering light that shifted between red and white, with additional flashes of green and orange. At various intervals, the object’s luminosity would dim significantly, making it difficult to see, before returning to a very bright, luminous white state. The object remained relatively stationary or hovered for the duration of the sighting before executing a high-speed, circular departure at 1:30 AM. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The author of the first report contacted the Malton Control Tower Supervisor immediately after the object disappeared from view at 1:30 AM. The author offered to provide further technical details, including calculations and specific compass directions, to assist in any investigation. Mrs. Agnes J. B. Miller’s correspondence inquired whether the object could have been a meteor and requested official information regarding the event. She expressed a strong interest in the research work being conducted on the matter and invited further contact to provide additional information. No official weather data or formal RCMP interrogation reports were included in the provided documentation.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p175-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 作者本人（未具名）、T. 霍姆拉尔夫人（Mrs. T. Homelaar）、艾格尼丝·J. B. 米勒夫人（Mrs. Agnes J. B. Miller）、赫梅尔汉夫人（Mrs. Hemelhan），以及学校的一群人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月20日；大约凌晨12:00至凌晨1:30。

**地点：** 安大略省纽马克特（Newmarket, Ontario）。

**目击经过：** 1969年2月20日晚，安大略省纽马克特发生了一起涉及多名目击者的UFO事件。作者与T. 霍姆拉尔夫人从朝向西南偏西的客厅窗户观察到了一个明亮的物体。与此同时，艾格尼丝·J. B. 米勒夫人报告称，赫梅尔汉夫人在一所学校观察该物体长达一段时间，当时学校里聚集了一群人共同观看。目击者称该物体可见时间持续了约一个半小时。米勒夫人指出，该物体最终以“惊人的速度”做圆周运动后离开。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为看起来像一颗非常大的恒星。其外观极具动态，特征是闪烁的光芒在红色和白色之间变换，并伴有绿色和橙色的闪光。在不同时段，物体的亮度会显著减弱，使其难以辨认，随后又恢复到非常明亮、发光的白色状态。在目击期间，该物体保持相对静止或悬停，直到凌晨1:30以高速圆周运动离开。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 第一份报告的作者在物体于凌晨1:30消失后，立即联系了马尔顿（Malton）控制塔主管。作者主动提出提供进一步的技术细节，包括计算数据和具体的罗盘方位，以协助任何调查工作。艾格尼丝·J. B. 米勒夫人在信件中询问该物体是否可能是流星，并要求提供有关该事件的官方信息。她对该课题的研究工作表现出浓厚兴趣，并邀请进一步联系以提供更多信息。所提供的文档中未包含官方气象数据或加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的正式询问报告。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p260-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Anonymous observer (first-person account), Anonymous witness (requested confidentiality), Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) officer stationed in Pembroke.

**Date / Time:** June 9, 1965 (Event date); July 2, 1969, at 3:40 AM (OPP observation).

**Location:** Petawawa Point, Ottawa River, Ontario.

**Sighting:** 
The event involves multiple accounts of an unidentified aerial phenomenon observed near the Ottawa River. One observer, writing in the first person, reported seeing a white light while positioned in a vehicle at Petawawa Point. The light appeared to be at tree level and was brighter than a star. The observer noted the light moved to the right and compared its appearance to moonlight reflecting on water, though it remained clearly in the sky. Seeking a better vantage point, this witness moved to the top of a ski hill on County Road 25 in Petawawa, and subsequently to the Pembroke Golf Course. From the final location, the witness observed a light appearing to hover over the Quyon, Ontario bridge on Highway 92, before it vanished.

A second anonymous witness reported an object in motion, estimated to be approximately 2 miles away. This witness noted that the object moved slower than a piston or jet aircraft at the same apparent altitude. The witness confirmed there were no conventional aircraft in the vicinity during or immediately after the sighting.

A third account comes from an Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) officer stationed in Pembroke. On July 2, 1969, at 3:40 AM, the officer observed an object for approximately 15 minutes at Petawawa Point. The night was clear with visible stars. The officer observed the object first through a vehicle windshield and then stepped outside to view it directly.

**Object:** 
The object was consistently described as a bright white light, notably brighter than the surrounding stars or the background of the sky. The anonymous witness estimated the object’s apparent size to be approximately 18 inches when held at arm’s length. The object was silent, making no sound during the observation. Its movement was described as slow—slower than conventional aircraft—and it exhibited a capacity for directional change. The duration of the sighting by the OPP officer was approximately 15 minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The documentation includes a handwritten note titled "Diagram on Back" detailing the movements of the first observer. The anonymous witness noted that they were never interrogated by Air Force investigators or government officials, nor were they instructed to keep the incident confidential, though they requested their name be withheld. The OPP officer’s report was formally filed with the Canadian Aerial Phenomena Research Organization (CAPRO) and is currently held within the National Research Council of Canada files. The reports acknowledge the proximity of a local airport, which was considered during the assessment of the object's movement.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p260-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 匿名观察者（第一人称叙述）、匿名目击者（要求保密）、驻扎在彭布罗克（Pembroke）的安大略省警察局（OPP）警官。

**日期 / 时间：** 1965年6月9日（事件发生日期）；1969年7月2日凌晨3:40（安大略省警察局警官观察记录）。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华河，佩塔瓦瓦角（Petawawa Point）。

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及多起在渥太华河附近观察到的不明空中现象。一名观察者在第一人称叙述中报告称，当时他坐在佩塔瓦瓦角的一辆车内，看到了一道白光。这道光看起来与树木高度齐平，比星星更亮。观察者注意到光线向右移动，并将其外观比作水面反射的月光，但它显然悬浮在空中。为了寻找更好的观测点，该目击者前往了佩塔瓦瓦25号县道上的滑雪山顶，随后又前往了彭布罗克高尔夫球场。从最后一个地点观察时，目击者看到一道光似乎悬停在92号高速公路的奎永（Quyon）大桥上方，随后消失。

第二位匿名目击者报告称看到了一个正在移动的物体，估计距离约2英里。该目击者指出，该物体的移动速度比在相同视高度下的活塞式飞机或喷气式飞机要慢。目击者证实，在目击期间或之后，附近没有常规飞行器。

第三份报告来自驻扎在彭布罗克的安大略省警察局（OPP）警官。1969年7月2日凌晨3:40，该警官在佩塔瓦瓦角观察了一个物体约15分钟。当晚天空晴朗，星光可见。警官先是通过车窗观察该物体，随后走出车外进行直接观测。

**物体描述：**
该物体被一致描述为一道明亮的白光，明显比周围的星星或天空背景更亮。匿名目击者估计，若以手臂伸直的距离测量，该物体的视大小约为18英寸。该物体保持静默，在观察过程中未发出任何声音。其移动方式被描述为缓慢——比常规飞行器慢——并表现出改变方向的能力。安大略省警察局警官的目击持续时间约为15分钟。

**调查/后续：**
相关档案包含一份题为“背面图示”的手写笔记，详细记录了第一位观察者的移动轨迹。匿名目击者指出，他们从未受到空军调查人员或政府官员的质询，也没有被要求对该事件保密，尽管他们本人要求隐去姓名。安大略省警察局警官的报告已正式提交给加拿大空中现象研究组织（CAPRO），目前保存在加拿大国家研究委员会的档案中。报告中承认了当地机场的存在，并在评估物体移动情况时将其纳入了考量。

CA-FOIA-Part_03-p264-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** William Robert Mc... (identified as an Ontario Provincial Police officer)

**Date / Time:** 1969-06-04

**Location:** Killarney, Ontario (specifically near Tomlinson St. Lighthouse, Highway #11, and the Pembroke/Fraserdale area)

**Sighting:** The witness, an Ontario Provincial Police officer, observed an unidentified object while driving back from Fraserdale near a hydro-electric construction site. The sighting lasted approximately 6–8 minutes. The witness first noticed the object "by accident" through his windshield while driving at night under clear weather conditions. Initially, the object appeared as a bright, star-like point of light, slightly brighter than a high-beam headlight seen from a great distance. 

The object remained stationary for 3–4 minutes before suddenly moving with what the witness described as an "old smooth motion." It proceeded to lower very slowly to an altitude of approximately 65 degrees (northeast) before moving away. The witness noted that the object’s motion was highly regular and that it appeared to be faster than a jet aircraft. Throughout the event, the object did not produce smoke, leave a trail, drop any debris, or emit any sound. The witness observed the object to the northwest, with the moon positioned behind him to the southwest.

**Object:** The object was described as a ball of light that changed in intensity and color, though the witness attributed the color shift to the object's changing motion. It was sharply outlined at its closest point. Estimates of its size varied, with the witness noting it was "larger" than standard comparison sizes, with diameter estimates ranging from 100 to 200 feet, and a separate distance estimate of approximately 500 feet. The witness explicitly ruled out helicopters or airplanes due to the total lack of sound and the object's unique, regular flight characteristics.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The file consists of a formal questionnaire and a personal letter from the witness. The witness confirmed he was not interrogated by authorities, was not asked to conceal the incident, and had no prior history of reporting unidentified objects. The documentation includes a sketch of the elevation (marked N/E) and a map section detailing the route near Highway #41, the turn toward Pembroke, and local county roads. The witness expressed a desire for further information, requesting correspondence, magazines, or pamphlets to help him understand the nature of the sighting. No military, airport, or research installations were identified in the immediate vicinity of the observation.
CA-FOIA-Part_03-p264-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威廉·罗伯特·麦克……（William Robert Mc...，身份为安大略省省警警官）

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年6月4日

**地点：** 安大略省基拉尼（Killarney）（具体位于汤姆林森街灯塔、11号公路以及彭布罗克/弗雷泽代尔地区附近）

**目击经过：** 目击者是一名安大略省省警警官，他在从弗雷泽代尔（Fraserdale）附近的一个水电施工现场驾车返回途中，观察到了一个不明物体。目击过程持续了约6至8分钟。目击者是在夜间天气晴朗的情况下驾车时，通过挡风玻璃“偶然”发现了该物体。起初，该物体看起来像一个明亮的星状光点，比从远处看到的远光灯还要亮一些。

该物体保持静止状态约3至4分钟，随后突然移动，目击者将其描述为一种“平稳的旧式运动”。它随后非常缓慢地下降到约65度（东北方向）的高度，然后飞离。目击者指出，该物体的运动非常有规律，且速度似乎比喷气式飞机还要快。在整个过程中，该物体没有产生烟雾、没有留下尾迹、没有掉落任何碎片，也没有发出任何声音。目击者是在西北方向观察到该物体的，当时月亮位于他身后的西南方向。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个光球，其亮度和颜色会发生变化，尽管目击者认为颜色的变化是由于物体运动方式的改变所致。在最近距离时，它的轮廓非常清晰。关于其尺寸的估计各不相同，目击者指出它比标准的参照物要“大”，直径估计在100到200英尺之间，另有距离估计约为500英尺。目击者明确排除了直升机或飞机的可能性，因为该物体完全没有声音，且具有独特、规律的飞行特征。

**调查/后续：** 该档案包含一份正式调查问卷和一封来自目击者的亲笔信。目击者证实，他没有受到当局的审讯，也没有被要求隐瞒此次事件，且此前没有任何报告不明飞行物的记录。档案资料包括一张高度草图（标记为东北方向）和一张地图截面，详细标明了靠近41号公路的路线、通往彭布罗克的转弯处以及当地的县道。目击者表示希望获得更多信息，并请求提供相关信件、杂志或小册子，以帮助他了解此次目击事件的本质。在观测地点附近未发现任何军事、机场或研究设施。

CA-FOIA-Part_04-p012-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Diateurbaril (Fire Inspector and Mayor), and at least three other townspeople.

**Date / Time:** July 3, 1969, at 2215Z.

**Location:** Belleterre, Quebec (Coordinates: 47° 25' N, 78° 40' W).

**Sighting:** On the evening of July 3, 1969, at 2215Z, Mr. Diateurbaril—the Fire Inspector and Mayor of Belleterre—along with at least three other townspeople, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting took place under conditions of clear, excellent visibility. The witnesses tracked the object for a duration of one and a half hours as it moved across the sky from north to south. The observation was conducted initially with the naked eye and subsequently aided by the use of 10x50 binoculars.

**Object:** The object was described as conical in shape and brilliant in appearance. It was estimated to be at an altitude of at least 50,000 feet. Based on the visual estimation of the witnesses, the object was calculated to be 278 feet long at a distance of 1,000 yards. Mr. Diateurbaril noted that the object’s appearance was reminiscent of an Apollo spacecraft, though he specified that it possessed larger tail fins than the Apollo design. No specific sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and transmitted by the 41 NORAD Division Headquarters in North Bay. The report was forwarded to the RCCWC/CANFORCEHQ and the National Research Council (Radio and Electrical Engineering Division) for further review and analysis.
CA-FOIA-Part_04-p012-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 迪亚图巴里尔先生（Diateurbaril，消防检查员兼市长）以及至少三名其他镇民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年7月3日，22:15Z（祖鲁时间）。

**地点：** 魁北克省贝尔泰尔（Belleterre）（坐标：北纬47° 25'，西经78° 40'）。

**目击经过：** 1969年7月3日晚22:15Z，贝尔泰尔市的消防检查员兼市长迪亚图巴里尔先生与至少三名其他镇民共同目击了一个不明空中现象。目击发生时，天气晴朗，能见度极佳。目击者对该物体进行了长达一个半小时的追踪，观察到它从北向南横跨天空。观察过程最初通过肉眼进行，随后借助了10x50双筒望远镜。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆锥形，外观明亮。据估计，其飞行高度至少在50,000英尺以上。根据目击者的目测估算，该物体在1,000码距离处的长度约为278英尺。迪亚图巴里尔先生指出，该物体的外观让人联想到阿波罗号宇宙飞船，但他特别提到，其尾翼比阿波罗号的设计更大。未报告有任何特定声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已由位于北湾（North Bay）的北美防空司令部（NORAD）第41师总部正式记录并上报。报告随后被转交至加拿大救援协调中心（RCCWC）/加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHQ）以及加拿大国家研究委员会（无线电与电气工程部）进行进一步的审查与分析。

CA-FOIA-Part_04-p294-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Howard Lockwood (RR7 Belleville, Ont), Paul Wood (43 Fraser Drive, Batawa, Ont)

**Date / Time:** July 24, 1970, at 0945Z

**Location:** Plevna Lake, Ontario (4456N 7702W)

**Sighting:** On July 24, 1970, at 0945Z, witnesses Howard Lockwood and Paul Wood observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the vicinity of Plevna Lake, Ontario. Both witnesses provided consistent accounts of the event, which took place under hazy weather conditions. The object was observed traveling across the sky in a west-bound trajectory from an easterly direction. The sighting lasted for a total duration of one minute and fifteen seconds. During this time, the witnesses reported hearing a distinct "sizzling" noise associated with the object’s presence.

**Object:** The object was described as a dark, cigar-shaped craft. It featured five visible portholes along its structure. The witnesses estimated the object’s altitude to be between 2,000 and 3,000 feet. The movement was described as a steady transit from east to west, accompanied by a sizzling sound throughout the duration of the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The event was documented in official records (pages 294 and 295 of the case file). The documentation confirms the location coordinates as 4456N 7702W and notes the specific atmospheric conditions as hazy. No further investigative actions, such as physical evidence collection or additional witness interrogations, were noted in the provided file pages beyond the initial reporting of the sighting details and witness contact information.
CA-FOIA-Part_04-p294-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 霍华德·洛克伍德（Howard Lockwood，安大略省贝尔维尔 RR7），保罗·伍德（Paul Wood，安大略省巴塔瓦弗雷泽大道 43 号）

**日期 / 时间：** 1970 年 7 月 24 日，0945Z（格林威治标准时间）

**地点：** 安大略省普莱夫纳湖（北纬 44 度 56 分，西经 77 度 02 分）

**目击经过：** 1970 年 7 月 24 日 0945Z，目击者霍华德·洛克伍德和保罗·伍德在安大略省普莱夫纳湖附近观察到一种不明空中现象。两位目击者对事件的描述一致，当时天气状况较为朦胧。该物体从东向西飞行，横穿天空。目击过程持续了 1 分 15 秒。在此期间，目击者报告称听到了与该物体伴随出现的明显“嘶嘶”声。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一艘深色的雪茄形飞行器。其结构上可见五个舷窗。目击者估计该物体的高度在 2,000 到 3,000 英尺之间。其飞行轨迹被描述为从东向西平稳移动，且在整个观测过程中伴有嘶嘶声。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被记录在案（档案第 294 页和 295 页）。记录确认了地理坐标为北纬 44 度 56 分，西经 77 度 02 分，并注明当时的大气条件为朦胧。除初步报告的目击细节和目击者联系方式外，所提供的档案页面中未记录进一步的调查行动，如物证收集或额外的目击者问询。

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p018-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Michael Hickey, Denise (Hickey’s girlfriend), Paul Giroux, Frank, and Pete.

**Date / Time:** September 14, 1970; initial sighting at 10:00 p.m. EDT, secondary sighting at 10:45 p.m. EDT.

**Location:** Montreal Road, Eastview/Ottawa, Ontario (extending toward Orleans and the Overbrook/Vanier areas).

**Sighting:** 
At 10:00 p.m., the group of witnesses (Hickey, Denise, Giroux, Frank, and Pete) were traveling east on Montreal Road, just outside of Eastview, when they observed an object flying below cloud level. The object was moving east at a normal speed. The witnesses attempted to pursue the object in their vehicle, traveling as far as Orleans, but they lost sight of it and observed nothing further during that leg of the trip.

At 10:45 p.m., while the witnesses were returning toward Ottawa, they encountered a second event. Just before entering the Vanier area (approximately one mile east of Ottawa), they observed an object traveling west below the cloud level. Simultaneously, a second object was observed passing below the first, heading east. According to the witnesses, the two objects passed one another without stopping or exhibiting any unusual maneuvers. The westbound object appeared to tilt and descend toward the Overbrook area. The second object (the one heading east) continued to lose altitude, passing over Ottawa until it was obscured from view by houses, trees, and city lights.

**Object:** 
The objects were described as flying at a low altitude, below the cloud layer. They were characterized by flashing red lights; specifically, one object was noted to have a "red flashing rotary light." The second object observed at 10:45 p.m. was noted to have "much stronger lights" than the first. The objects moved at what the witnesses described as a "normal speed."

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The sighting was reported to the National Research Council (NRC) via telephone on September 15, 1970. 

Additionally, the case file notes a separate, unrelated report received at 12:00 a.m. regarding a UFO sighting in the west end of Gatineau. In that incident, witnesses reported a light in an upstairs room that flashed orange every 5 to 7 minutes between 7:15 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. The observer of the Gatineau event indicated an intention to report the sighting to the NRC.
CA-FOIA-Part_05-p018-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 迈克尔·希基（Michael Hickey）、丹妮丝（Denise，希基的女友）、保罗·吉鲁（Paul Giroux）、弗兰克（Frank）和皮特（Pete）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1970年9月14日；首次目击时间为美国东部时间晚上10:00，第二次目击时间为美国东部时间晚上10:45。

**地点：** 安大略省渥太华东景（Eastview）的蒙特利尔路（Montreal Road）（延伸至奥尔良（Orleans）及奥弗布鲁克/瓦尼埃（Overbrook/Vanier）地区）。

**目击经过：**
晚上10:00，目击者一行人（希基、丹妮丝、吉鲁、弗兰克和皮特）正驱车沿蒙特利尔路向东行驶，刚出东景地区时，他们观察到一个物体在云层下方飞行。该物体正以正常速度向东移动。目击者试图驾车追赶该物体，一直追到奥尔良，但随后失去了目标，在行程的那一段路程中未再有发现。

晚上10:45，当目击者返回渥太华途中，遇到了第二次事件。就在进入瓦尼埃地区之前（距离渥太华以东约一英里处），他们观察到一个物体在云层下方由西向东飞行。与此同时，观察到第二个物体从第一个物体下方穿过，向东飞行。据目击者称，这两个物体相互交错而过，没有停顿，也没有表现出任何异常的机动动作。向西飞行的物体似乎发生了倾斜，并向奥弗布鲁克地区下降。第二个物体（向东飞行的那个）高度持续下降，飞越渥太华上空，直至被房屋、树木和城市灯光遮挡，消失在视野中。

**物体描述：**
据描述，这些物体在低空飞行，位于云层之下。它们的特征是闪烁着红灯；具体而言，其中一个物体被注意到带有“红色旋转闪烁灯”。在晚上10:45观察到的第二个物体被指出拥有比第一个物体“强得多”的灯光。目击者称这些物体以“正常速度”移动。

**调查/后续：**
该目击事件于1970年9月15日通过电话报告给了加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）。

此外，案卷中还记录了一份于凌晨12:00收到的、与此无关的独立报告，内容涉及加蒂诺（Gatineau）西区的一起UFO目击事件。在那起事件中，目击者报告称，在晚上7:15至11:30之间，楼上一间房内有一盏灯每隔5到7分钟闪烁一次橙色光。加蒂诺事件的观察者表示打算将此次目击事件报告给NRC。

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p142-claude.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p239-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mario Loscerbo, John Funk

**Date / Time:** September 18, 1971, between 10:00 PM and 12:00 AM (Reported to RCMP on September 19, 1971)

**Location:** On top of a mountain north of Loon Lake, near Ashcroft, B.C.

**Sighting:** On the night of September 18, 1971, witnesses Mario Loscerbo and John Funk were positioned on a mountain north of Loon Lake, B.C., when they observed three unidentified flying objects in a clear sky. The witnesses utilized a rifle scope to monitor the objects for approximately two hours. During the observation, the witnesses noted that they had only received one hour of sleep the previous night, though they explicitly stated they had not been drinking. Due to extreme fatigue, they eventually ceased their observation. Upon waking the following morning, they inspected the area where objects #2 and #3 had been sighted; they observed nothing but a high, snow-covered mountain in that direction. The sighting was formally reported to the RCMP Ashcroft Detachment on September 19, 1971.

**Object:** The witnesses described three distinct objects:
*   **Object #1:** Located in a southerly direction, approximately 25 degrees above the horizon. It was described as bright white and shaped like a "peace symbol." It exhibited a bobbing motion (up and down) before eventually becoming stationary.
*   **Object #2:** Located in a westerly direction, approximately 2 degrees above the horizon. It was described as hexagon-shaped and red in color.
*   **Object #3:** Also located in a westerly direction, 2 degrees above the horizon. It featured a white center surrounded by a red ring and exhibited a bobbing motion similar to Object #1.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was investigated by the RCMP Ashcroft Detachment. Cpl. J.A. Fisher conducted the follow-up and noted that no other reports or additional information regarding the sighting were available. Based on the impression of the RCMP members who interviewed Loscerbo and Funk, the reliability of the witnesses and the information provided was considered to be "good."
CA-FOIA-Part_05-p239-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 马里奥·洛塞博 (Mario Loscerbo)、约翰·芬克 (John Funk)

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年9月18日，晚上10:00至午夜12:00之间（于1971年9月19日向加拿大皇家骑警报告）

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省阿什克罗夫特 (Ashcroft) 附近，卢恩湖 (Loon Lake) 北侧的山顶

**目击经过：** 1971年9月18日晚，目击者马里奥·洛塞博和约翰·芬克位于不列颠哥伦比亚省卢恩湖北侧的一座山上，当时他们在晴朗的夜空中观察到了三个不明飞行物。目击者使用步枪瞄准镜对这些物体进行了约两个小时的监视。在观察过程中，目击者提到他们前一天晚上只睡了一个小时，但明确表示并未饮酒。由于极度疲劳，他们最终停止了观察。次日清晨醒来后，他们检查了曾目击到2号和3号物体的位置；他们发现该方向除了高耸的雪山外，别无他物。此次目击事件于1971年9月19日正式报告给加拿大皇家骑警阿什克罗夫特分局。

**物体描述：** 目击者描述了三个不同的物体：
*   **1号物体：** 位于南方，地平线上方约25度处。被描述为亮白色，形状像一个“和平标志”。它在最终静止前表现出上下晃动的动作。
*   **2号物体：** 位于西方，地平线上方约2度处。被描述为六边形，颜色为红色。
*   **3号物体：** 同样位于西方，地平线上方约2度处。其特征是中心为白色，周围环绕着红色圆环，并表现出与1号物体类似的晃动动作。

**调查/后续：** 此次目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警阿什克罗夫特分局进行了调查。J.A. 费舍尔 (J.A. Fisher) 下士负责跟进，并指出没有关于此次目击事件的其他报告或额外信息。根据采访洛塞博和芬克的皇家骑警成员的印象，目击者的可靠性以及所提供的信息被认为是“良好”的。

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p244-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Elizabeth (Mrs. John) Swan, Stephen Foster (age 9), Ian Swan (age 9), Fiona Swan (age 14), and Debra Stanley (age 14).

**Date / Time:** October 10, 1971 (with one document noting October 11), at approximately 7:30 P.M.

**Location:** Highway 38 / Hodges Cove road, Trinity Bay, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** While traveling in a vehicle on the Hodges Cove road, the group of five witnesses observed a series of lights in the sky. The weather conditions were described as heavily overcast with frequent rain squalls and gale-force winds. The witnesses observed between 6 and 8 bright white lights arranged in a diagonal line. The lights were seen moving at a very fast rate of speed from west to east. During the observation, the lights appeared to break formation and chase one another. Some witnesses noted that the lights would go on and off, similar to the appearance of runway landing lights. The duration of the sighting was approximately one minute before the lights disappeared into the clouds and over the bay. There was no noise associated with the objects. The witnesses held conflicting opinions regarding the altitude of the lights, with some comparing them to low-flying aircraft and others suggesting they were as high as the stars.

**Object:** The objects were described as a series of 6 to 8 brilliant white lights. They were observed in a diagonal formation that broke apart during the event. The movement was characterized as very fast, with the lights appearing to chase each other. Some lights flickered on and off. The objects made no sound. The witnesses explicitly stated the lights were not identified as flares or fireworks.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) conducted an investigation into the report. The reporting officer documented the severe weather conditions, specifically noting the heavy rain and gale-force winds present at the time of the sighting. The RCMP concluded that the lights were likely the result of reflections from the headlights of 5 to 6 oncoming vehicles, which were amplified or distorted by the adverse weather conditions. No other official explanation was provided.
CA-FOIA-Part_05-p244-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 伊丽莎白·斯旺（Elizabeth Swan，约翰·斯旺夫人）、斯蒂芬·福斯特（Stephen Foster，9岁）、伊恩·斯旺（Ian Swan，9岁）、菲奥娜·斯旺（Fiona Swan，14岁）以及黛布拉·斯坦利（Debra Stanley，14岁）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年10月10日（一份文件记录为10月11日），大约晚上7:30。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省三一湾（Trinity Bay），38号公路 / 霍奇斯湾路（Hodges Cove road）。

**目击经过：** 当这五名目击者乘车行驶在霍奇斯湾路上时，观察到了天空中出现的一系列光点。当时的天气状况被描述为阴云密布，伴有频繁的阵雨和强风。目击者观察到6到8个排列成对角线的明亮白光。这些光点以极快的速度从西向东移动。在观察过程中，这些光点似乎打破了队形并相互追逐。一些目击者指出，这些光点会像机场跑道着陆灯一样忽明忽暗。目击持续了大约一分钟，随后光点消失在云层中并越过了海湾。这些物体没有发出任何声音。目击者对于光点的高度看法不一，有人将其比作低空飞行的飞机，也有人认为它们像星星一样高。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为一连串6到8个明亮的白光。它们最初以对角线队形出现，但在事件过程中队形散开。其运动特征非常迅速，光点看起来在相互追逐。部分光点忽明忽暗。这些物体没有发出任何声音。目击者明确表示，这些光点并非照明弹或烟花。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对该报告进行了调查。负责警官记录了当时恶劣的天气状况，特别指出了目击时正值大雨和强风天气。加拿大皇家骑警得出的结论是，这些光点很可能是5到6辆迎面驶来的车辆的车灯反射，并因恶劣天气而产生放大或扭曲。官方未提供其他解释。

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p285-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A student, their father, an aunt, an uncle, local boys, Glenda Johnson, Mrs. Charles Johnson, and an unnamed civilian witness.

**Date / Time:** February 19, 1971 (Note: While the prompt header specifies 1972, the source text for Page 285 explicitly records 1971); sightings also occurred in late September and early October at approximately 8:30 PM and 10:30 PM.

**Location:** Lunenburg County, Nova Scotia (specifically referencing R.R. 1 and a local bridge).

**Sighting:** On February 19, 1971, a student was awakened by a loud noise described as a crackling sound resembling a high-powered motor. Upon looking out their window, the student observed a UFO flying over a neighbor’s house. The object moved in a zigzag path, hovered for ten minutes, and emitted a humming sound. Simultaneously, an unnamed civilian witness observed an object from a window for approximately ten minutes before it moved a certain distance. The student’s aunt also reported seeing a bright light over the woods. 

In a separate account, Glenda Johnson reported observing strange lights or "things" while on the telephone. She noted that these objects moved around, stopped, and then continued on, appearing to have no visible source. She observed one object turn red and noted another that shifted position before extinguishing. These sightings were part of a pattern of local activity; in late September and early October, local boys reported sightings from a bridge, including lights forming a triangle, a blinking red light, and multiple objects following similar flight paths at 8:30 PM and 10:30 PM.

**Object:** The primary object observed on February 19 was described as having a dark grey top and a dome-like shape with a protrusion on top. The underside featured a light divided into sections resembling a bicycle wheel. The craft displayed a steady white light on its side, with green and yellow colors visible on the body. No windows were observed. The object appeared to wobble during flight. Other reported objects were described impressionistically as strange lights, sometimes red, which moved erratically or formed geometric patterns like triangles.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The civilian witness provided a hand-drawn sketch of the object as seen from their window, which included a diagram illustrating the object's movement over the ten-minute duration. The student witness corresponded with a Professor Mc'Nail to share their observations. Glenda Johnson’s account was documented in a letter addressed to Mrs. Charles Johnson, which was subsequently filed under the National Research Council of Canada header. The reports suggest a recurring phenomenon in the Lunenburg area, with witnesses noting that the objects were not always present when actively sought, but were frequently observed by chance.
CA-FOIA-Part_05-p285-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名学生、其父亲、一位姑姑/阿姨、一位叔叔/舅舅、当地男孩们、格伦达·约翰逊（Glenda Johnson）、查尔斯·约翰逊夫人（Mrs. Charles Johnson）以及一名未具名的平民目击者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年2月19日（注：尽管提示标题中注明为1972年，但第285页的原始文本明确记录为1971年）；9月下旬和10月上旬的晚上8:30和10:30左右也发生了目击事件。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省卢嫩堡县（具体指R.R. 1地区及当地一座桥梁）。

**目击经过：** 1971年2月19日，一名学生被一阵巨大的噪音惊醒，该声音被描述为类似于大功率马达发出的噼啪声。学生向窗外望去，观察到一个不明飞行物（UFO）飞过邻居的房子。该物体以之字形路径移动，悬停了十分钟，并发出嗡嗡声。与此同时，一名未具名的平民目击者从窗户观察到一个物体约十分钟，随后该物体移动了一段距离。学生的姑姑/阿姨也报告称看到树林上方有明亮的光。

在另一份叙述中，格伦达·约翰逊报告称在打电话时观察到了奇怪的光或“东西”。她指出，这些物体四处移动、停下，然后继续前进，且似乎没有可见的动力源。她观察到一个物体变成了红色，并注意到另一个物体在熄灭前改变了位置。这些目击事件是当地一系列活动的一部分；9月下旬和10月上旬，当地男孩们报告在桥上看到了目击事件，包括形成三角形的光、闪烁的红光，以及多个在晚上8:30和10:30沿相似飞行路径移动的物体。

**物体描述：** 2月19日观察到的主要物体被描述为顶部呈深灰色，呈圆顶状，顶部有一个突起。底部有一个被分割成若干部分的灯，类似于自行车轮。该飞行器侧面显示出稳定的白光，机身上可见绿色和黄色。未观察到窗户。该物体在飞行过程中似乎摇晃不定。其他被报告的物体被印象派地描述为奇怪的光（有时为红色），它们移动轨迹不规则，或形成三角形等几何图案。

**调查/后续：** 该平民目击者提供了一张从窗户观察到的物体手绘草图，其中包括一张说明该物体在十分钟内移动轨迹的图表。学生目击者与麦克尼尔教授（Professor Mc'Nail）进行了通信，分享了他们的观察结果。格伦达·约翰逊的叙述被记录在一封寄给查尔斯·约翰逊夫人的信中，随后被归档在加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council of Canada）的标题下。这些报告表明卢嫩堡地区存在一种反复出现的现象，目击者指出，这些物体并非在主动搜寻时总会出现，但经常会被偶然发现。

CA-FOIA-Part_05-p294-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A 16-year-old individual, their family, and neighbours.

**Sighting:** Two separate sightings occurred. The first was on November 18, 1971, from approximately 6:03 p.m. to 6:20 p.m. The second was on November 21, 1971, from approximately 8:01 p.m. to 8:29 p.m.

**Object:** The witnesses observed an object that they concluded could not be an aircraft because it was flying too low and was spinning rapidly with a red glow.

**Aftermath:** The author of the letter, who claims to be 16 years old, references reading about Capt. Mantell in a book titled "Intercept - But Don't Shoot" and requests information from the agency regarding the object they observed.
CA-FOIA-Part_05-p294-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名16岁的青少年、其家人及邻居。

**日期：** 发生了两次独立的目击事件。第一次是在1971年11月18日，大约下午6:03至6:20；第二次是在1971年11月21日，大约晚上8:01至8:29。

**地点：** （原文未提供具体地点信息）

**目击经过：** 目击者观察到一个物体，他们断定那不可能是飞机，因为它飞行高度过低，且在快速旋转的同时散发出红色的光芒。

**调查/后续：** 这封信的作者自称16岁，他在书中（书名为《拦截——但不要开火》/ *Intercept - But Don't Shoot*）读到了关于曼特尔上尉（Capt. Mantell）的内容，并向该机构请求提供有关他们所观察到的物体的信息。

CA-FOIA-Part_06-p002-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Elmer Kutcher

**Date / Time:** January 29, 1972, at 0115Z

**Location:** 4077 Larouque Ave, Hanmer, Ontario

**Sighting:** On January 29, 1972, at 0115Z, Elmer Kutcher, a resident of 4077 Larouque Ave in Hanmer, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for a total duration of one hour and ten minutes. Mr. Kutcher observed the object positioned over the peak of a roof. The sighting was significant enough that the report was formally transmitted to authorities at 0115Z, with follow-up updates provided at 0130Z and 0200Z.

**Object:** The object was described as square in shape. There is a slight discrepancy in the recorded spatial data between the provided documentation: one record places the object at an altitude of 900 feet with a distance of 700 feet from the witness, while the other record notes an altitude of 700 feet with a distance of 900 feet from the witness. No specific details regarding color, sound, or movement were provided in the available records, other than its stationary or hovering position relative to the roof peak.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the initial report at 0115Z, the information was relayed to the Canadian Forces Headquarters in Ottawa and the National Research Council. The documentation confirms that the same report was passed along for official review at two subsequent intervals: 0130Z and 0200Z.
CA-FOIA-Part_06-p002-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 埃尔默·库彻 (Elmer Kutcher)

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年1月29日，0115Z（祖鲁时间）

**地点：** 安大略省汉默，拉鲁克大道4077号 (4077 Larouque Ave, Hanmer, Ontario)

**目击经过：** 1972年1月29日0115Z，居住在汉默拉鲁克大道4077号的埃尔默·库彻观察到一种不明空中现象。此次目击事件总持续时间为一小时十分钟。库彻先生观察到该物体位于屋顶上方。此次目击事件引起了足够重视，报告于0115Z正式提交给有关当局，并分别在0130Z和0200Z提供了后续更新。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为方形。现有记录中的空间数据存在细微出入：一份记录显示该物体高度为900英尺，距离目击者700英尺；而另一份记录则指出其高度为700英尺，距离目击者900英尺。除其相对于屋顶保持静止或悬停的状态外，现有记录中未提供关于颜色、声音或移动方式的具体细节。

**调查 / 后续：** 在0115Z收到初步报告后，相关信息被转达至位于渥太华的加拿大武装部队总部及加拿大国家研究委员会。文件证实，同一报告分别在随后的0130Z和0200Z两个时间点被转交进行官方审查。

CA-FOIA-Part_06-p006-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** John Delect (also referred to as Mr. Jean Delec)

**Date / Time:** February 20, 1972, at 202335Z

**Location:** Ste Sauveur, Quebec (P.Q.)

**Sighting:**
On the evening of February 20, 1972, at 202335Z, a UFO sighting was reported in Ste Sauveur, Quebec. The witness, identified in the documentation as both John Delect and Mr. Jean Delec, observed the phenomenon while at his home. According to the witness account, the sighting lasted for a total duration of three minutes. During this time, the witness observed a large, luminous white object traveling across the sky in a trajectory moving from the north toward the south. The atmospheric conditions at the time of the sighting were reported as clear, providing good visibility for the observation.

**Object:**
The object was described as a large, luminous white light. It maintained a consistent appearance throughout the three-minute duration of the sighting. Its primary movement was a steady transit from the north to the south. No specific sound or mechanical details were noted in the provided reports.

**Investigation / Follow-up:**
The sighting was formally documented and classified as "unclassified." Following the initial report, the case file was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) for further review and record-keeping. The documentation confirms that the weather conditions were verified as clear at the time of the event.
CA-FOIA-Part_06-p006-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·德莱克（John Delect，也被称为让·德莱克先生 / Mr. Jean Delec）

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年2月20日，20:33:35Z

**地点：** 魁北克省圣索沃尔（Ste Sauveur, Quebec）

**目击经过：**
1972年2月20日晚20:33:35Z，魁北克省圣索沃尔发生了一起不明飞行物目击事件。目击者在档案中分别被称为约翰·德莱克和让·德莱克先生，他在家中观察到了这一现象。据目击者描述，整个目击过程持续了三分钟。在此期间，目击者看到一个巨大的、发着白光的物体正从北向南横穿天空。据报告，当时大气条件晴朗，能见度良好，便于观察。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为一个巨大的、发着白光的亮光。在三分钟的目击过程中，其外观保持一致。其主要运动轨迹是从北向南平稳穿行。提供的报告中未提及任何特定的声音或机械细节。

**调查/后续：**
该目击事件已被正式记录并归类为“未分类”。在初步报告提交后，该案卷被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）进行进一步审查和存档。相关文件证实，事件发生时的天气状况确为晴朗。

CA-FOIA-Part_06-p009-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** C.A.R. Beaulieu (a commercial artist from Levis, P.Q.)

**Date / Time:** January 11, 1972 (estimated; identified as the second week of January 1972)

**Location:** Île d'Orléans, Quebec (specifically the southwest point/foreland of the island)

**Sighting:** 
The witness, C.A.R. Beaulieu, reported observing an unidentified aerial phenomenon under a very dark sky. According to his account, the object moved at a speed comparable to that of an airplane. Throughout the duration of the sighting, the object remained completely silent, producing no audible noise. As the object traversed the sky, it was observed to change its form or shape. The object eventually lost altitude and descended until it disappeared from view in the vicinity of the southwest point (southwest foreland) of Île d'Orléans.

**Object:** 
The object was described primarily as a light. Its most notable characteristic was its ability to change shape while in motion. It traveled at the speed of a conventional airplane and was noted for being entirely silent. The duration of the sighting was sufficient for the witness to observe the object’s descent and eventual disappearance near the island's southwest point.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Following the event, the witness—who is a commercial artist by profession—created a drawing to illustrate the sighting. On January 14, 1972, Mr. Beaulieu submitted a formal letter along with his illustration to the Ministry of Transport in Ottawa. In his correspondence, he expressed his hope that his documentation and the visual representation of the event would prove useful for official records or investigation.
CA-FOIA-Part_06-p009-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** C.A.R. 博利厄（C.A.R. Beaulieu，来自魁北克省莱维斯的商业艺术家）

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年1月11日（估算值；确认为1972年1月的第二周）

**地点：** 魁北克省奥尔良岛（Île d'Orléans，具体位于该岛西南角/西南岬）

**目击经过：**
目击者 C.A.R. 博利厄报告称，他在一片漆黑的夜空中观察到一种不明空中现象。据他描述，该物体的移动速度与飞机相当。在整个目击过程中，该物体保持完全静默，未发出任何声响。当物体划过天空时，被观察到发生了形态或形状上的改变。最终，该物体高度下降，直至在奥尔良岛西南角（西南岬）附近消失在视野中。

**物体描述：**
该物体主要被描述为一个光点。其最显著的特征是在运动过程中能够改变形状。它以常规飞机的速度飞行，且全程保持完全静默。目击持续的时间足够长，使目击者能够观察到该物体的下降过程，以及它最终在岛屿西南角附近消失的情景。

**调查/后续：**
事件发生后，身为商业艺术家的目击者绘制了一幅草图来还原此次目击事件。1972年1月14日，博利厄先生致信渥太华交通部，并附上了他的插图。他在信中表示，希望这些记录和视觉呈现能对官方存档或调查有所帮助。

CA-FOIA-Part_06-p013-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Earl Charles (Chuck) Graham, Larry Thielen, Fred Brasnett, N.R. (Norman Ray) Kempthorne, Mr. & Mrs. R.H. Atkins, and Cst. R.M. Lequesne.

**Date / Time:** March 11, 1972; sightings reported between approximately 9:25 PM and 10:45 PM MST.

**Location:** Calgary, Alberta (specifically observed from residences including 11111 Braxton Rd. S.W.).

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 11, 1972, multiple residents observed a brilliant, stationary-to-wandering light in the western sky. Chuck Graham initiated the reports after spotting the object from his kitchen window, initially mistaking it for an aircraft with landing lights. He alerted his father-in-law, N.R. Kempthorne, and his neighbor, Larry Thielen. Thielen observed the object moving from south to north, appearing stationary relative to window frame reference points, though he noted a slight vertical shift. Fred Brasnett, observing from his own residence, described the object as moving in an upward angular projection. Witnesses reported the object hovered or moved in a slow, weaving, "wandering" motion.
