**物体描述：** 可见的叙述称，该物体呈银色，被观测了数小时。文中进一步提到，天气状况阻碍了进一步的观测。此页面未填写关于尾迹、噪音或其他技术细节的信息。

**调查/后续：** 该表格似乎是加拿大公共档案馆（Public Archives Canada）所保存的一份正式国防部报告的一部分。页面下边缘包含档案和文件编号，其余部分大多为留有许多空白字段和已涂黑目击者信息的表格。

CA-FOIA-Part_20-p197-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cleveland ATC, Toronto ATC, Niagara AC&WU, 3 RCAF aircrew members, Buffalo Tower, Centralia Tower operator, London Tower operators, RCAF F51 pilots, RCAF T3 pilots, a woman south of Wingham, a bus driver, and the crew (pilots and 1st Officer) of T.C.A. Flight 233.

**Date / Time:** April 20, 1952; sightings occurred between 1113 and 1152 hours.

**Location:** Toronto, London, Centralia, Wingham, and areas 18 miles south of Longhon, Ontario.

**Sighting:** Between 1113 and 1152 hours on April 20, 1952, a series of coordinated sightings were reported across Ontario. Cleveland ATC initiated the reports, observing objects west of Toronto traveling west and leaving vapour trails. These observations were corroborated by Toronto ATC and Niagara AC&WU. Three RCAF aircrew members near Lindsay reported four distinct objects traveling from east to west. 

Simultaneously, Centralia and London tower operators observed objects and vapour trails to their northeast, heading west. One London operator estimated the objects crossed the horizon in just 3 seconds at an altitude of 30,000 to 35,000 feet. A bus driver reported sightings 18 miles south of Longhon. Additionally, a woman south of Wingham provided a unique account of a 5-foot-long object emitting flames that hovered over her house before heading west, leaving a trail of fire. The crew of T.C.A. Flight 233 also reported observing five objects at an altitude of approximately 1,500 feet. Buffalo Tower confirmed the presence of vapour trails northwest of their location.

**Object:** The objects were generally described as high-speed craft capable of movement faster than conventional jet aircraft. Most sightings involved objects leaving persistent vapour trails, which were observed to last between 1 hour 30 minutes and 1 hour 45 minutes. While most objects were in motion, some were observed standing still before accelerating westward. The specific object reported near Wingham was described as 5 feet long, emitting flames, and leaving a trail of fire. T.C.A. Flight 233 observed five objects at a lower altitude of 1,500 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** At the time of the sightings, approximately 15 RCAF F51 and T3 aircraft were airborne in the region. Most of the pilots operating these aircraft reported seeing the objects during their flights. The duration of the vapour trails—lasting up to 1 hour 45 minutes—was noted as a significant physical characteristic of the event. The reports were compiled from multiple air traffic control centers, tower operators, and civilian witnesses, indicating a widespread aerial phenomenon across the Ontario region.
CA-FOIA-Part_20-p197-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 克利夫兰空中交通管制中心（Cleveland ATC）、多伦多空中交通管制中心（Toronto ATC）、尼亚加拉防空预警中心（Niagara AC&WU）、3名加拿大皇家空军（RCAF）机组人员、布法罗塔台（Buffalo Tower）、森特勒利亚塔台（Centralia Tower）操作员、伦敦塔台（London Tower）操作员、加拿大皇家空军F51飞行员、加拿大皇家空军T3飞行员、一名温汉姆（Wingham）南部的女性、一名巴士司机，以及加拿大横贯航空（T.C.A.）233号航班的机组人员（飞行员及副驾驶）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1952年4月20日；目击事件发生在11:13至11:52之间。

**地点：** 安大略省的多伦多、伦敦、森特勒利亚、温汉姆，以及朗洪（Longhon）以南18英里处。

**目击经过：** 1952年4月20日11:13至11:52期间，安大略省各地报告了一系列协调一致的目击事件。克利夫兰空中交通管制中心率先发起报告，观测到多伦多以西有物体向西飞行并留下了尾迹。这些观测结果得到了多伦多空中交通管制中心和尼亚加拉防空预警中心的证实。林赛（Lindsay）附近的3名加拿大皇家空军机组人员报告称，有4个明显的物体正从东向西飞行。

与此同时，森特勒利亚和伦敦的塔台操作员观测到其东北方向有物体及尾迹向西移动。一名伦敦操作员估计，这些物体在3万至3.5万英尺的高度，仅用3秒钟就穿过了地平线。一名巴士司机在朗洪以南18英里处报告了目击情况。此外，温汉姆南部的一名女性提供了一份独特的描述：一个5英尺长的物体喷射着火焰，在她的房子上方盘旋，随后向西飞去，留下一道火迹。加拿大横贯航空233号航班的机组人员也报告称，在约1500英尺的高度观测到了5个物体。布法罗塔台证实了其西北方向存在尾迹。

**物体描述：** 这些物体通常被描述为能够以超过常规喷气式飞机速度飞行的高速飞行器。大多数目击事件涉及留下持久尾迹的物体，这些尾迹被观测到持续了1小时30分钟至1小时45分钟。虽然大多数物体处于运动状态，但也有部分物体被观测到在加速向西飞行前处于静止状态。温汉姆附近报告的特定物体被描述为长5英尺，喷射火焰并留下一道火迹。加拿大横贯航空233号航班在1500英尺的较低高度观测到了5个物体。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生时，该地区约有15架加拿大皇家空军的F51和T3飞机在空中飞行。大多数驾驶这些飞机的飞行员报告称在飞行过程中看到了这些物体。尾迹持续时间长达1小时45分钟，被认为是此次事件的一个重要物理特征。这些报告汇集了来自多个空中交通管制中心、塔台操作员及平民目击者的信息，表明这是一场波及安大略省全境的广泛空中现象。

CA-FOIA-Part_20-p209-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. [redacted], his sister Mrs. [redacted], and two other individuals.

**Sighting:** On 22-5-50 at 6:30 p.m., witnesses observed a very white object travelling horizontally from north-west to south-west at approximately 2000 feet altitude and a speed of 500 miles per hour. The object made no noise, but appeared to explode in mid-air, with silver pieces fluttering toward the ground. A second sighting occurred on 23-5-50, where witnesses described a cigar-shaped object, approximately 30 feet in length, travelling north to south above the mountains. This object also made no noise, appeared to explode, and released silver fragments that fluttered toward the ground.

**Object:** A very white object, later described as cigar-shaped and approximately 30 feet long.

**Aftermath:** An immediate patrol was conducted by the RCMP with Mr. [redacted] to search the bush for the silver pieces, but none were located. A further patrol was not made regarding the second sighting because the ice on Atlin Lake was in poor condition.
CA-FOIA-Part_20-p209-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]先生、其胞姐[已删除]女士，以及另外两位人士。

**日期：** 1950年5月22日及1950年5月23日

**地点：** 加拿大阿特林湖（Atlin Lake）地区

**目击经过：** 1950年5月22日下午6:30，目击者观察到一个通体雪白的物体，正以约2000英尺的高度和每小时500英里的速度由西北向西南水平飞行。该物体全程无声，但在半空中似乎发生了爆炸，银色碎片随之飘落向地面。1950年5月23日发生了第二次目击事件，目击者描述称看到一个雪茄状物体，长度约30英尺，正从北向南飞越山脉。该物体同样没有发出任何声音，且再次出现爆炸并散发出飘向地面的银色碎片。

**物体描述：** 一个通体雪白的物体，后被描述为雪茄状，长度约30英尺。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）立即与[已删除]先生一同展开巡逻，在丛林中搜寻那些银色碎片，但一无所获。由于阿特林湖冰面状况不佳，针对第二次目击事件未再进行后续巡逻。

CA-FOIA-Part_20-p225-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The author (writer) and two other people residing at the location.

**Date / Time:** February 26, 1950, at approximately 1445 hours.

**Location:** Vancouver, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On Sunday, February 26, 1950, at approximately 1445 hours, the primary witness and two other individuals observed an unidentified object appearing from the eastern sky. The object traversed the clear sky from east to west at an angle of approximately 45 degrees. The total duration of the sighting was approximately three and a half minutes. The primary witness noted that the object moved quickly at first, then slowed down over the city, during which time he was able to observe it through 3.5-power binoculars for approximately two minutes. The other two witnesses were unable to use the binoculars due to the limited time available. After the period of slowing, the object gained speed and traveled west toward Vancouver Island, heading in a direction south of Parksville. The witness noted that the object’s motion was difficult to judge, but it exhibited a couple of distinct oscillations during the observation.

**Object:** The object was described as having a whitish color with a burnished bronze tint. It was estimated to be of "enormous proportion" and flying at a very high altitude, potentially measured in miles. The shape was described as resembling two wide-edged cigarette ashtrays placed face-to-face, with the bowl sections forming the body and the edges forming an equatorial ring. During the observed oscillations, the witness noted a slight ridge in the middle of the object, suggesting the presence of a cupola or dome; however, the witness acknowledged this might have been an optical illusion caused by sunlight flashing against the object during its movement. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The primary witness formally submitted his account to the Officer in Charge of Intelligence at the Department of Intelligence, Royal Canadian Air Force, in Vancouver, B.C. In his correspondence, the witness invited the recipient to advise whether the provided information was of interest or value to the department. He further offered to provide additional information if requested by the authorities. No specific weather data or official RCMP interrogation reports were included in the provided documentation, though the witness noted the sky was clear at the time of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Part_20-p225-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 作者本人及居住在当地的其他两人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1950年2月26日，约14:45。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华。

**目击经过：** 1950年2月26日星期日约14:45，主要目击者与其他两人观察到一个不明物体从东部天空出现。该物体以约45度的角度从东向西横穿晴朗的天空。目击持续时间总计约三分半钟。主要目击者指出，该物体起初移动迅速，随后在城市上空减速，在此期间他得以通过3.5倍双筒望远镜对其进行了约两分钟的观察。由于时间有限，另外两名目击者未能使用望远镜。减速过后，该物体再次加速，向西飞往温哥华岛方向，航向位于帕克斯维尔（Parksville）以南。目击者指出，该物体的运动轨迹难以判断，但在观察过程中表现出了几次明显的摆动。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为带有磨光青铜色调的白色。据估计其“比例巨大”，飞行高度极高，可能以英里计。其形状被描述为像两个边缘宽大的烟灰缸面对面扣在一起，碗状部分构成主体，边缘则形成了一个赤道环。在观察到物体摆动时，目击者注意到物体中部有一道轻微的隆起，暗示可能存在圆顶或穹顶；然而，目击者也承认这可能是由于物体移动时阳光反射造成的视觉错觉。未报告有任何声响。

**调查/后续：** 主要目击者正式向不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华的加拿大皇家空军情报部门负责人提交了他的陈述。在信函中，目击者询问对方所提供的信息对该部门是否有兴趣或价值。他并表示，如果当局有要求，他愿意提供更多信息。所提供的文档中未包含具体的气象数据或加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的正式审讯报告，但目击者指出当时天空晴朗。

CA-FOIA-Part_22-p121-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The page shows answers from one respondent completing a sighting questionnaire. No witness name is visible on this page.

**Sighting:** The respondent says the first indication of the object was that it “was a contrail.” They report that the object was seen as moving level, disappearing gradually, and that when first observed they were facing south; when they last saw it they were facing east.

**Object:** The object is described as having no sound, being a black round dot, about the same size as a fighter aircraft, with one light. The light is described as bright and clear blue. The speed is given as “fast, .9 Mach (Approx),” and the “other” description says “contrail as from a single engine.” Additional entries indicate the object changed direction about 180 degrees (approx), did not change speed, did not move behind something, did decrease in size, and did decrease in brightness.

**Aftermath:** This page appears to be page 2 of a typed questionnaire, stamped “UNCLASSIFIED” at the top and held in the Department of National Defence / Public Archives Canada file. No other outcome, follow-up, or date is visible on the page.
CA-FOIA-Part_22-p121-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 该页面显示了一位受访者填写的目击调查问卷。此页面上未显示任何目击者姓名。

**目击经过：** 受访者称，该物体最初的迹象是“一条凝结尾迹”。据报告，该物体呈水平移动并逐渐消失；初次观察时，目击者面向南方；最后一次观察时，目击者面向东方。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为无声，是一个黑色的圆点，大小与战斗机相当，带有一盏灯。这盏灯被描述为明亮且清晰的蓝色。速度被标注为“很快，约 0.9 马赫”，“其他”描述中提到“如同单引擎飞机产生的凝结尾迹”。补充条目显示，该物体改变了约 180 度的方向，速度未变，未移动到任何物体后方，尺寸有所减小，亮度也有所减弱。

**调查/后续：** 该页面似乎是一份打印调查问卷的第二页，顶部盖有“非机密”（UNCLASSIFIED）印章，现存于加拿大国防部/加拿大国家档案馆档案中。页面上未显示其他结果、后续行动或日期。

CA-FOIA-Part_22-p170-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian (a student in physical therapy and former tool-maker), their mother, and an unnamed correspondent (the primary author of the report).

**Date / Time:** February 19, 1954 (Note: Page 170 references April 23, 1953, but the case file title specifies February 19, 1954). Time: Evening, during dinner.

**Location:** Iberville, Quebec.

**Sighting:** While eating dinner, the primary witness observed a bright, fast-moving object approaching from the West. The witness alerted their mother, and both observed the object through a window. The witness then exited the house through a North-facing door, jumping three steps to continue observation. The object was seen moving at high speed, suddenly stopping, and remaining stationary for at least 15 seconds while hovering approximately 250 feet above the river. It then flew backward toward the Southwest at high speed before disappearing. The witness noted the sky was clear and sunny at the time. The total duration of the event was estimated at approximately one minute.

**Object:** The object was described as a "disc" or "saucer," round with a nearly flat bottom and a top dome. It was noted for being very bright and silent. It spun counter-clockwise while hovering. The witness compared its size to the Iberville town water tank (estimated at 28 feet in diameter). The witness compared its flight characteristics to a hummingbird (*oiseau-mouche*), noting it could fly forward and backward, with the backward speed being two to three times faster than its forward speed.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The file contains standard DND/RCAF reporting forms, including "Sketch C" (a circular disc with a dome) and instructions for mapping the object's trajectory. The witness provided detailed triangulation measurements, comparing the object’s position to the Iberville water tank (estimated 125 feet high, 300 feet from the observer). The witness verified the distance to the river (3,000–3,500 feet) the week following the sighting. The report includes an "Appendix B" translation certified by D.V. Lariviere. The witness expressed significant concern during the event and requested an official response from the authorities regarding the nature of the object. Some pages contain auxiliary sketches and notes referencing other locations (Sherbrooke, Red River) and measurements (3,000 feet).
CA-FOIA-Part_22-p170-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名平民（物理治疗专业学生，前工具制造工）、其母亲，以及一名未具名的通讯员（报告的主要撰写人）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1954年2月19日（注：第170页提及1953年4月23日，但案卷标题明确为1954年2月19日）。时间：傍晚，晚餐期间。

**地点：** 魁北克省伊贝维尔（Iberville）。

**目击经过：** 晚餐时，主要目击者观察到一个明亮且移动迅速的物体从西面靠近。目击者提醒了母亲，两人通过窗户观察该物体。随后，目击者从朝北的门走出屋子，跳下三级台阶继续观察。该物体以极高速度移动，突然停下，并在河面上方约250英尺处悬停了至少15秒。随后，它以极高速度向西南方向倒飞，随即消失。目击者指出，当时天空晴朗且阳光明媚。整个事件持续时间估计约为一分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为“圆盘”或“飞碟”，呈圆形，底部近乎平坦，顶部有圆顶。其特点是非常明亮且无声。在悬停时，它呈逆时针旋转。目击者将其尺寸与伊贝维尔镇的水塔（估计直径为28英尺）进行了对比。目击者将其飞行特性比作蜂鸟（*oiseau-mouche*），指出它能够向前和向后飞行，且倒飞速度比前进速度快两到三倍。

**调查/后续：** 档案中包含标准的国防部（DND）/加拿大皇家空军（RCAF）报告表格，其中包括“草图C”（带有圆顶的圆形盘状物）以及绘制物体轨迹的说明。目击者提供了详细的三角测量数据，将物体的位置与伊贝维尔水塔（估计高125英尺，距离观察者300英尺）进行了对比。目击者在目击事件发生后的那一周核实了到河流的距离（3,000至3,500英尺）。报告包含一份由D.V. 拉里维埃（D.V. Lariviere）认证的“附录B”译文。目击者在事件发生期间表现出极大的担忧，并要求当局就该物体的性质给予正式回应。部分页面包含辅助草图和提及其他地点（舍布鲁克、红河）及测量数据（3,000英尺）的笔记。

CA-FOIA-Part_24-p095-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Jesse Steele, a lightkeeper at Peckford's Island, and his assistant.

**Sighting:** On June 27th at 12:35 AM, the assistant sighted a light due south of the light station. It was visible for 10 minutes before disappearing. On June 29th at 3:30 AM, Jesse Steele sighted a similar object.

**Object:** The object seen on June 27th was described as the size of a tea cup, light red in color, and traveling at approximately 6 miles per hour in a northeasterly direction. The object seen on June 29th was described as the size of a tea plate, light red in color, located 2 feet above the horizon, and moving at 7 or 8 miles per hour in a northwesterly direction. The duration of the second sighting was approximately 65 seconds.

**Aftermath:** The weather conditions during the sightings were reported as fine and clear. The report was sent via intra-departmental correspondence to the District Marine Agent in St. John's, Newfoundland.
CA-FOIA-Part_24-p095-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 杰西·斯蒂尔（Jesse Steele），佩克福德岛（Peckford's Island）的灯塔看守人，以及他的助手。

**日期：** 6月27日和6月29日。

**地点：** 佩克福德岛（Peckford's Island）。

**目击经过：** 6月27日凌晨12:35，助手在灯塔正南方发现了一道光。该光持续可见10分钟后消失。6月29日凌晨3:30，杰西·斯蒂尔目击到了一个类似物体。

**物体描述：** 6月27日目击到的物体被描述为茶杯大小，呈浅红色，以每小时约6英里的速度向东北方向移动。6月29日目击到的物体被描述为茶碟大小，呈浅红色，位于地平线上方2英尺处，以每小时7到8英里的速度向西北方向移动。第二次目击持续时间约为65秒。

**调查/后续：** 据报告，目击期间天气状况良好且晴朗。该报告已通过部门内部信函发送至位于纽芬兰圣约翰斯（St. John's）的地区海事代理处。

CA-FOIA-Part_25-p191-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian family residing on Deepdale Road, several additional civilians from Deepdale and Inverness, and Cst. C.M. Campbell of the RCMP Inverness Detachment.

**Date / Time:** July 20, 1968, 11:15 PM to July 21, 1968, 12:30 AM.

**Location:** Deepdale, Inverness County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** Between 11:15 PM on July 20 and 12:30 AM on July 21, 1968, multiple civilian witnesses observed two unidentified flying objects. One object was positioned on the horizon, while the second was observed directly above a farm. The family residing on Deepdale Road reported that upon arriving at their home, they observed the objects at an altitude estimated between 8,000 and 10,000 feet. The objects were initially stationary; one then moved in a northerly direction at a high rate of speed before stopping and remaining stationary for approximately one hour. The lights from the object positioned above the farm were intense enough to illuminate the roof of the barn. The total duration of the sighting was approximately one hour and 15 minutes, concluding when the objects disappeared at 12:30 AM at a "terrific rate of speed."

**Object:** The objects were described as round in shape, though their exact form was difficult to discern due to the intensity of the light. They emitted brilliant, layered displays of red, green, and white colors. The objects were completely silent during all observed movements.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Cst. C.M. Campbell of the RCMP Inverness Detachment conducted an investigation and filed reports with the RCMP Sydney Division. Cst. Campbell personally patrolled the scene and observed a bright object in the sky for ten minutes, during which time it remained stationary. The weather at the time of the sighting was reported as clear. Cst. Campbell noted that the primary civilian witness appeared reliable and sincere; furthermore, this witness disclosed that they had observed a similar saucer-shaped object near their farm on a previous occasion. Despite inquiries at other farms in the immediate area, no other reports were received, and the investigation yielded no further sightings.
CA-FOIA-Part_25-p191-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 居住在迪普代尔路（Deepdale Road）的一户平民家庭，迪普代尔和因弗内斯（Inverness）的多名平民，以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）因弗内斯分局的C.M.坎贝尔警官（Cst. C.M. Campbell）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月20日晚上11:15至1968年7月21日凌晨12:30。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省因弗内斯县迪普代尔。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月20日晚上11:15至7月21日凌晨12:30期间，多名平民目击者观察到了两个不明飞行物。其中一个物体位于地平线上，另一个则被观察到悬停在一家农场正上方。居住在迪普代尔路的那户家庭报告称，当他们回到家时，观察到这些物体的高度估计在8,000至10,000英尺之间。这些物体起初处于静止状态；随后其中一个以极高的速度向北移动，接着停下并保持静止约一小时。位于农场上方的物体所发出的光芒非常强烈，足以照亮谷仓的屋顶。目击事件总持续时间约为1小时15分钟，最终于凌晨12:30以“极快的速度”消失。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为圆形，但由于光线过于强烈，难以辨别其确切形状。它们发出了红、绿、白三色交织的绚丽光芒。在整个观察过程中，这些物体完全处于静音状态。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警因弗内斯分局的C.M.坎贝尔警官进行了调查，并向皇家骑警悉尼分部提交了报告。坎贝尔警官亲自巡视了现场，并在天空中观察到一个明亮的物体长达十分钟，期间该物体一直保持静止。据报告，目击时的天气状况晴朗。坎贝尔警官指出，主要平民目击者看起来可靠且真诚；此外，该目击者透露，他们此前曾在自家农场附近观察到过类似的碟状物体。尽管对附近的其他农场进行了询问，但未收到其他报告，调查也未发现更多目击事件。

CA-FOIA-Part_25-p229-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unnamed male resident (ski-doo operator), unnamed female resident (woodcutter), A.E. Crosby (RCMP Constable), E. McPherson (Interpreter).

**Date / Time:** February 4, 1968, at 10:30 PM; February 14, 1968, at approximately 3:30 PM and 5:00 PM.

**Location:** Fort Norman, N.W.T. (Mackenzie River and Four Mile Creek, 3 miles east of the settlement).

**Sighting:** 
On February 4, 1968, at 10:30 PM, a male resident was traveling by ski-doo along the Mackenzie River. He observed a large, lighted object moving in an easterly direction at an altitude of 400–500 feet. The object descended toward the river, then rose rapidly and disappeared to the south. The witness, who confirmed he was sober and in good health, stated the sighting lasted 6–7 seconds and was definitely not an airplane.

On February 14, 1968, a female resident was cutting wood at Four Mile Creek, three miles east of Fort Norman. At approximately 3:30 PM, her dogs became terrified, barking and looking toward the C.N.T. line. She observed a reddish object moving slowly below tree-top level (approximately 20 feet off the ground) toward her. Fearing the object, she untied her dogs and fled by sleigh. She reported that the object followed her for approximately 5 minutes; she looked back three times to confirm it was still pursuing her before fleeing home. She stated she had never seen anything like it and confirmed it was not an airplane.

**Object:** 
The February 4th object was described as 30 feet long by 25 feet across, shaped like a "cigar cut in half" with a square tail end. It featured two rows of bright lights along its edges, suggesting a rounded bottom. It made no noise.

The February 14th object was described as round, yellowish-red in color, and approximately half the size of a 45-gallon drum. One account noted two flames spurting from its tail. It moved slowly below tree-top level and made no audible noise.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The RCMP, represented by Cst. A.E. Crosby, conducted interviews with the witnesses, assisted by interpreter E. McPherson. The RCMP noted that while the witnesses were considered reliable, it could not be definitively determined what the objects were. Official records confirm there were no known aircraft in the area at the time of the sightings. The female witness was noted as illiterate but highly reliable, and the male witness was noted as reliable and observant of the clear night conditions. Reports were filed for both incidents.
CA-FOIA-Part_25-p229-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 未具名男性居民（雪地摩托驾驶员）、未具名女性居民（伐木工）、A.E. 克罗斯比（A.E. Crosby，加拿大皇家骑警警员）、E. 麦克弗森（E. McPherson，口译员）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年2月4日晚上10:30；1968年2月14日下午约3:30及5:00。

**地点：** 西北地区诺曼堡（麦肯齐河及距离定居点以东3英里的四英里溪）。

**目击经过：**
1968年2月4日晚上10:30，一名男性居民驾驶雪地摩托沿麦肯齐河行驶时，观察到一个巨大的发光物体正以400至500英尺的高度向东移动。该物体向河面下降，随后迅速上升并向南方消失。目击者确认当时神志清醒且身体健康，他表示目击过程持续了6至7秒，并断定那绝对不是飞机。

1968年2月14日，一名女性居民在诺曼堡以东3英里的四英里溪伐木。下午约3:30，她的狗表现得非常惊恐，对着加拿大国家电信（C.N.T.）线路的方向吠叫。她观察到一个红色的物体在树梢高度以下（离地约20英尺）缓慢向她移动。由于感到恐惧，她解开了狗的绳索并乘雪橇逃离。据她报告，该物体尾随了她约5分钟；她在逃回家之前曾三次回头确认，发现它仍在追赶。她表示从未见过类似的东西，并确认那不是飞机。

**物体描述：**
2月4日的物体被描述为长30英尺、宽25英尺，形状像“被切成两半的雪茄”，尾部呈方形。其边缘有两排明亮的灯光，暗示底部呈圆形。该物体飞行时没有发出任何声音。

2月14日的物体被描述为圆形，呈黄红色，大小约为45加仑油桶的一半。其中一份记录提到其尾部喷出两道火焰。它在树梢高度以下缓慢移动，且未发出任何可听见的噪音。

**调查/后续：**
加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员A.E. 克罗斯比在口译员E. 麦克弗森的协助下对目击者进行了访谈。皇家骑警指出，尽管目击者被认为是可靠的，但仍无法明确断定这些物体究竟是什么。官方记录证实，在目击事件发生时，该地区没有已知的飞行器活动。报告中记录该女性目击者虽不识字，但非常可靠；男性目击者则被认为可靠且对晴朗夜空观察仔细。两起事件均已存档备案。

CA-FOIA-Part_25-p259-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted] (identified as a female civilian)

**Date / Time:** February 9, 1968, at approximately 8:05 AM

**Location:** Duncan, BC (southwest of the location)

**Sighting:** On the morning of February 9, 1968, the witness was standing outside her door facing southwest. The sky was described as cloudless, though the area at tree-top level was obscured by a fairly dense mist. The witness noted that the sun was shining brightly and directly into her eyes at the time of the observation. She reported that no other individuals were known to have witnessed the object. The object hovered at tree-top level for a duration of approximately 2 to 3 minutes before it moved and disappeared behind a mountain located to the west.

**Object:** The witness described the object as a single, cigar-shaped craft. It possessed no wings and exhibited a bright, silvery glow. Additionally, the object featured a halo-shaped ring that was observed to change colors.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was investigated by the Duncan Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). As part of the follow-up, officials conducted checks with the Patricia Bay Airport. These inquiries revealed that a twin-engine Beech aircraft, which was silver in color, had taken off at 7:58 AM—approximately seven to eight minutes prior to the sighting—and was heading in the direction of the Duncan area. The reporting officer calculated that this aircraft would have arrived in the vicinity of Duncan at approximately the same time as the reported sighting. Consequently, the investigating officer concluded that it was "almost certain" the object sighted was the Beech aircraft. The reporting officer also noted that the witness appeared "neurotic and unsure of herself" during the interview process. A formal report was slated to follow the initial investigation.
CA-FOIA-Part_25-p259-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]女士（身份为女性平民）

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年2月9日，上午约8:05

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省邓肯市（该地点的西南方）

**目击经过：** 1968年2月9日上午，目击者站在门外，面向西南方。据描述，当时天空万里无云，但树梢高度的区域被一层相当浓的薄雾遮蔽。目击者指出，观测时阳光明媚，且直射她的眼睛。她表示据她所知，没有其他人目击到该物体。该物体在树梢高度盘旋了约2到3分钟，随后移动并消失在位于西侧的一座山后。

**物体描述：** 目击者将该物体描述为一艘单一的雪茄状飞行器。它没有机翼，散发出明亮的银色光芒。此外，该物体还带有一个光环状的圆环，据观察会变换颜色。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）邓肯分队进行了调查。作为后续行动的一部分，官员向帕特里夏湾机场（Patricia Bay Airport）进行了核实。调查显示，一架银色的双引擎比奇（Beech）飞机于上午7:58起飞——即目击事件发生前约七到八分钟——并正朝邓肯地区方向飞行。负责报告的警官推算，该飞机抵达邓肯附近的时间与目击报告的时间大致吻合。因此，调查警官得出结论，所目击的物体“几乎可以确定”就是那架比奇飞机。负责报告的警官还指出，目击者在访谈过程中显得“神经质且对自己缺乏信心”。初步调查后，后续将提交一份正式报告。

CA-FOIA-Part_25-p274-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miss [redacted], Mrs. [redacted], Mrs. [redacted]’s sister-in-law, a female resident of 210 Weidner Dr., three unnamed civilians at/near the Dept. of Transport Pump House in Coxheath, several unnamed civilians on Coxheath Rd., Leeside Dr., and Weidner Dr., RCMP Constables D.W. Carver, D.G. McPherson, and J.C. Cowan.

**Date / Time:** December 23–24, 1967, at approximately 9:30 P.M.

**Location:** Sydney River, Coxheath (specifically the Pumping Station/Pump House area), and North Sydney, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** The event involved a series of reports occurring between December 23 and 24, 1967. On December 23, witnesses near the Dept. of Transport Pump House in Coxheath reported a loud, 5–10 second whistling noise—likened to a falling bomb—that grew in intensity before culminating in a powerful explosion. The blast was strong enough to shake nearby vehicles. One witness observed a white flash of light in an inverted cone shape rising approximately 100 feet into the air. 

On December 24 (with some reports conflating the date with the 23rd), residents on Weidner Drive and in North Sydney observed a fireball. One witness at 210 Weidner Drive saw a ball of light approaching from the east; it appeared as a small speck, grew larger and brighter, stopped momentarily, and then dropped straight down. Other witnesses described a round, red fireball with a tail moving at a 30-degree angle (right-to-left). Some observers noted the object appeared as bright as the moon, while others reported a disintegration burst. While some witnesses reported absolute silence, others noted the whistling and explosive force.

**Object:** The object was variously described as a "fireball," a "ball of light," and a "flash of light." Physical characteristics included a round shape (red or white), a bright tail, and an inverted cone shape. Sizes were reported as smaller than the moon but of comparable brightness. Movement ranged from a straight descent to a right-to-left trajectory. Sound reports were inconsistent, ranging from total silence to a 10-second whistling noise followed by a concussive explosion. The duration of sightings varied from 5 seconds to approximately two minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** RCMP officers D.W. Carver, D.G. McPherson, and J.C. Cowan conducted investigations, including taking formal statements on January 2, 1968. Officers searched the Coxheath area but found no physical evidence or impact craters. Seaboard Light and Power Co. explicitly refuted theories that the explosion resulted from electrical line failure. Investigators concluded that the various reports likely stemmed from a single event, with date discrepancies attributed to witness confusion. The file was handled according to operational protocols for meteors or fireballs and was officially closed on January 29, 1968, with the RCMP noting that delayed reporting may have led to distorted accounts.
CA-FOIA-Part_25-p274-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]小姐、[已删除]夫人、[已删除]夫人的嫂子/弟媳、韦德纳大道（Weidner Dr.）210号的一位女性居民、考克斯希思（Coxheath）交通部泵房及其附近的3名匿名平民、考克斯希思路（Coxheath Rd.）、利赛德大道（Leeside Dr.）和韦德纳大道上的多名匿名平民，以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员 D.W. 卡弗（D.W. Carver）、D.G. 麦克弗森（D.G. McPherson）和 J.C. 考恩（J.C. Cowan）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月23日至24日，约晚上9:30。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省悉尼河（Sydney River）、考克斯希思（特别是泵站/泵房区域）以及北悉尼。

**目击经过：** 该事件涉及1967年12月23日至24日期间的一系列报告。12月23日，考克斯希思交通部泵房附近的目击者报告称，听到了一声持续5至10秒的尖锐呼啸声——类似于炸弹坠落的声音——声音强度逐渐增强，最终引发了一次强烈的爆炸。爆炸威力巨大，足以震动附近的车辆。一名目击者观察到一道倒圆锥形的白色闪光升至约100英尺的空中。

12月24日（部分报告将日期与23日混淆），韦德纳大道和北悉尼的居民观察到了一个火球。韦德纳大道210号的一名目击者看到一个光球从东方靠近；它起初看起来像一个小点，随后变得越来越大、越来越亮，在短暂停留后垂直坠落。其他目击者描述称，这是一个带有尾迹的圆形红色火球，以30度角（从右向左）移动。一些观察者指出该物体亮度堪比月球，另一些人则报告称看到了物体解体时的爆裂。虽然部分目击者称现场绝对安静，但也有人提到了呼啸声和爆炸威力。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为“火球”、“光球”和“闪光”。其物理特征包括圆形（红色或白色）、明亮的尾迹以及倒圆锥形状。据报告，其尺寸小于月球，但亮度相当。运动轨迹从垂直下降到从右向左移动不等。关于声音的报告不尽相同，从完全寂静到持续10秒的呼啸声及随后的冲击性爆炸都有记录。目击持续时间从5秒到约两分钟不等。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警警员 D.W. 卡弗、D.G. 麦克弗森和 J.C. 考恩进行了调查，并于1968年1月2日获取了正式证词。警员们搜查了考克斯希思地区，但未发现任何物理证据或撞击坑。海博德电力公司（Seaboard Light and Power Co.）明确反驳了爆炸是由输电线路故障引起的说法。调查人员得出结论，认为各种报告很可能源于同一事件，日期上的差异归因于目击者的混淆。该档案按照针对流星或火球的操作规程处理，并于1968年1月29日正式结案。加拿大皇家骑警指出，报告的延迟可能导致了叙述的失真。

CA-FOIA-Part_26-p023-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Constable P. Thatcher (RCMP), Sergeant G.M.W. Bromley (Reporting Officer)

**Date / Time:** December 25, 1967, at approximately 6:11 p.m.

**Location:** Highway 28A, near Mallaig, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 25, 1967, Constable P. Thatcher was patrolling westbound on Highway 28A near Mallaig, Alberta, under clear sky conditions. At 6:11 p.m., Constable Thatcher observed an aerial phenomenon appearing behind him. The object traveled in a direct line from east to west, parallel to the highway. The witness first observed the object at an elevation angle of 40 degrees. The object continued its trajectory until it reached an angle of 15 degrees, at which point it appeared to burn up or explode in the sky. The entire duration of the sighting lasted between 5 and 10 seconds.

**Object:** The object was described as a round, bluish-white fireball. It emitted an intense light that was bright enough to illuminate the surrounding sky to near-daylight proportions. In terms of relative size, Constable Thatcher compared the object to the size of a golf ball held at arm's length relative to the moon. The object moved in a direct east-to-west path. No sounds were heard by the witness during the event, and the altitude of the object remained undetermined.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented by Constable P. Thatcher and submitted to RCMP Headquarters in Ottawa. The official report was concluded by Constable P. Thatcher and Sergeant G.M.W. Bromley. Based on the visual evidence and the nature of the object’s disappearance, the reporting officers concluded that the object was likely a meteorite or a fireball. No further anomalous activity was reported in connection with the event.
CA-FOIA-Part_26-p023-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** P. 撒切尔警官（加拿大皇家骑警），G.M.W. 布罗姆利警长（报告警官）

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月25日，下午约6:11

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省马拉格（Mallaig）附近的28A号公路

**目击经过：** 1967年12月25日傍晚，P. 撒切尔警官在晴朗的天气下，驾车沿阿尔伯塔省马拉格附近的28A号公路向西巡逻。下午6:11，撒切尔警官观察到身后出现了一种空中现象。该物体沿东西向直线飞行，与公路平行。目击者最初观察到该物体时，其仰角为40度。物体继续沿轨迹飞行，直至仰角降至15度时，在空中燃烧殆尽或发生爆炸。整个目击过程持续了5到10秒。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个圆形的蓝白色火球。它发出的强光足以将周围天空照亮至近乎白昼的程度。在相对大小方面，撒切尔警官将其比作手臂伸直时所见的高尔夫球与月球的比例。物体沿东西方向直线移动。目击者在事件过程中未听到任何声音，物体的飞行高度也无法确定。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件由P. 撒切尔警官正式记录，并提交至渥太华的加拿大皇家骑警总部。正式报告由P. 撒切尔警官和G.M.W. 布罗姆利警长共同结案。基于目击证据及物体消失的性质，报告警官推断该物体很可能是一颗陨石或火球。此后未再收到与该事件相关的异常活动报告。

CA-FOIA-Part_27-p212-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two brothers (names redacted), RCMP Cst. P. SHAW, B. A. MACKEIL.

**Date / Time:** February 3, 1969 (with one report erroneously noting March 2), between 10:00 P.M. and 10:40 P.M.

**Location:** 5.25 to 5.5 miles south of Yorkton, Saskatchewan, on Highway 9.

**Sighting:** At approximately 10:00–10:30 P.M., two brothers were driving south on Highway 9 when they observed a flashing reddish-orange light situated due west of the highway. The object appeared to be approximately 1.25 to 1.5 miles away. The witnesses followed the light in their truck for two miles until the road ended. During this pursuit, the light remained ahead of them; after they turned the truck around to head east, the light appeared to follow them for about one mile. 

The witnesses stopped their vehicle and observed the object for approximately five minutes as it hovered over a field. One account notes the object moved toward the witnesses, stopped in the middle of a field, and then hovered at an altitude of 20 to 150 feet above the ground. The object eventually moved away in a westerly direction, disappearing at high speed. The witnesses noted that the object disappeared behind trees at one point, only to be seen rising from the trees as they turned into their home lane. The witnesses explicitly stated that the object made no noise and they did not believe it was an aircraft.

**Object:** The object was described as a mass of light, 10 to 15 feet in diameter, with a misty, orange-red color that fluctuated in brightness. It exhibited a flashing quality and moved in a straight back-and-forth motion. While hovering, it maintained an altitude of 20 to 150 feet. When it departed, it traveled west at an estimated speed of 35–40 mph before accelerating to high speed.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** At 10:40 P.M., one of the witnesses contacted the RCMP office to report the sighting. An immediate patrol was conducted by the witnesses in conjunction with RCMP Cst. P. SHAW. A formal statement was taken from the witnesses at 11:15 P.M. by B. A. MACKEIL. The RCMP characterized the two brothers as reliable and honest individuals. Additionally, the RCMP contacted C.F.B. Whitespruce in Yorkton to inquire about radar data; the base reported that their radar did not detect any anomalous objects in the area at that time.
CA-FOIA-Part_27-p212-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两名兄弟（姓名已删减）、加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警员 P. 肖（P. SHAW）、B. A. 麦基尔（B. A. MACKEIL）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年2月3日（一份报告误记为3月2日），晚10:00至10:40之间。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省约克顿（Yorkton）以南5.25至5.5英里处的9号高速公路上。

**目击经过：** 晚10:00至10:30左右，两名兄弟正驾车沿9号高速公路向南行驶，此时他们观察到公路正西方有一个闪烁的红橙色光点。该物体距离他们约1.25至1.5英里。目击者驾驶卡车跟随该光点行驶了两英里，直到道路尽头。在追踪过程中，光点始终位于他们前方；当他们调转车头向东行驶时，光点似乎跟随了他们约一英里。

目击者停下车，观察该物体悬停在田野上空约五分钟。其中一份记录指出，该物体曾向目击者方向移动，停在田野中央，随后悬停在距离地面20至150英尺的高度。最终，该物体向西移动，并以极高的速度消失。目击者注意到，该物体曾一度消失在树木后方，但当他们转入自家车道时，又看到它从树丛上方升起。目击者明确表示，该物体没有发出任何声音，他们不认为这是某种飞行器。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一团光体，直径约10至15英尺，呈现出一种亮度波动的朦胧橙红色。它具有闪烁的特性，并以直线往复运动。悬停时，其高度保持在20至150英尺之间。离开时，它以约35至40英里/小时的预估速度向西飞行，随后加速至极高速度。

**调查/后续：** 晚10:40，其中一名目击者联系了加拿大皇家骑警办公室报告了此次目击事件。目击者随后与加拿大皇家骑警警员 P. 肖共同进行了即时巡逻。晚11:15，B. A. 麦基尔为目击者录制了正式口供。加拿大皇家骑警将这两名兄弟描述为可靠且诚实的人。此外，加拿大皇家骑警还联系了位于约克顿的怀特斯普鲁斯加拿大武装部队基地（C.F.B. Whitespruce）查询雷达数据；基地报告称，其雷达在当时并未探测到该区域有任何异常物体。

CA-FOIA-Part_27-p256-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A female driver, four other observers (various ages), and several passengers in the driver's vehicle.

**Date / Time:** October 11, 1971, at approximately 7:30 P.M.

**Location:** Highway 32, Hodges Cove, Trinity Bay, Newfoundland (traveling toward the Trans-Canada Highway).

**Sighting:** On the evening of October 11, 1971, under heavily overcast skies with frequent rain squalls and gale-force winds, a group of witnesses traveling from Hodges Cove toward Clarenville observed a series of anomalous lights. The primary witness, driving west on Highway 32, first noticed a brilliant white light appearing from a westerly direction. This was quickly joined by additional lights, totaling approximately six to nine in number. 

The witnesses described the lights as moving at a very fast rate of speed in a diagonal line across the sky from west to east. Once in formation, the lights reportedly broke their pattern and began "chasing each other." The observers noted that the lights appeared to be lower in altitude than a low-flying aircraft. The entire event lasted for approximately one minute before the objects disappeared out over the bay and into the clouds. All witnesses maintained that the lights were not stars, flares, fireworks, or conventional aircraft.

**Object:** The objects were described as brilliant, very bright white lights. They exhibited a flickering quality, varying in intensity like light bulbs turning on and off, similar to the appearance of aircraft landing lights. The objects moved at a high rate of speed and performed complex maneuvers, including formation flight and chasing behavior. No noise was heard by any of the witnesses during the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by the RCMP Clarenville Detachment. During the subsequent investigation, an official noted that the primary witness had passed five to six vehicles traveling in the opposite direction while returning to Clarenville. Based on this, the investigator concluded that the reported lights were likely reflections of headlights from these oncoming vehicles, an effect they suggested was exacerbated by the heavy rain and gale-force winds present at the time. Despite this official conclusion, the witnesses remained firm in their accounts that the phenomena were not terrestrial in origin.
CA-FOIA-Part_27-p256-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名女性驾驶员、四名其他观察者（年龄各异），以及驾驶员车上的几名乘客。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年10月11日，约晚上7:30。

**地点：** 纽芬兰省三一湾霍奇斯湾（Hodges Cove）的32号公路（正驶向横贯加拿大公路）。

**目击经过：** 1971年10月11日晚，在阴云密布、伴有频繁阵雨和强风的天气下，一群从霍奇斯湾前往克拉伦维尔（Clarenville）的目击者观察到了一系列异常光团。主要目击者在沿32号公路向西行驶时，首先注意到西方出现了一道耀眼的白光。随后，又有更多的光团加入，总数约在六到九个之间。

目击者描述称，这些光团以极快的速度呈对角线从西向东横穿天空。在编队飞行后，据称这些光团打破了队形，开始“互相追逐”。观察者们指出，这些光团的高度似乎比低空飞行的飞机还要低。整个事件持续了约一分钟，随后物体消失在海湾上空并隐入云层中。所有目击者都坚称这些光团既不是星星、照明弹、烟花，也不是常规飞行器。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为耀眼、极其明亮的白光。它们呈现出闪烁的特质，亮度如同开关灯泡般变化，类似于飞机的着陆灯。物体以极高的速度移动，并执行了复杂的机动动作，包括编队飞行和追逐行为。在观察过程中，没有任何目击者听到声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）克拉伦维尔分局记录在案。在随后的调查中，一名官员指出，主要目击者在返回克拉伦维尔的途中，曾与五到六辆迎面驶来的车辆擦肩而过。基于此，调查人员得出结论，认为所报告的光团很可能是这些迎面车辆前大灯的反射，并指出当时的大雨和强风加剧了这种视觉效果。尽管有此官方结论，目击者们仍坚持认为这些现象并非源于地球。

CA-FOIA-Part_27-p258-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** One male civilian (identified by the RCMP as a resident of Douglas, Manitoba).

**Date / Time:** October 27, 1971. There is a discrepancy in the recorded time: one report notes 8:30 A.M. C.S.T., while another report notes 3:30 A.M. C.S.T.

**Location:** Provincial Trunk Highway (PTH) #1, approximately 6 miles east of Brandon, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** A male witness driving west on PTH #1 observed an object while checking his rear and side-view mirrors. The witness reported that the object was traveling east, moving away from the highway. The witness described the object as being "very large" and "clearly visible." According to the account, the object maintained a climbing attitude before it lifted on its north side, leveled off, slowly faded, and then suddenly disappeared. The total duration of the sighting was approximately 2 minutes. The witness noted that there was other traffic on the road at the time, including a semi-trailer, but observed that other drivers did not appear to notice the object.

**Object:** The object was described as bright white in color and very large in size. Its structure was compared to two plates, with one inverted on top of the other, topped by a triangular-shaped object in the center. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted an investigation into the report, which included an interview with the witness. The interviewing officer noted that the subject appeared "quite in earnest" regarding his account. As part of the follow-up, the RCMP checked the witness’s background, noting he was unknown to the Brandon City Police but possessed a juvenile record from 1966. 

Official inquiries were made by the RCMP in the surrounding area, but no other sightings were reported, leading investigators to question why other east-bound traffic on the highway did not observe the object if it was as prominent as described. A telex message was forwarded by the RCMP in compliance with Op. Manual CO-Air, Para. #6. Additionally, the Brandon Municipal Airport was contacted to check for relevant weather data (noting the sky was heavily overcast) and air traffic records. The file was ultimately concluded with no further sightings or new information uncovered.
CA-FOIA-Part_27-p258-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名男性平民（加拿大皇家骑警将其确认为曼尼托巴省道格拉斯市的居民）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年10月27日。记录的时间存在差异：一份报告注明为中部标准时间上午8:30，而另一份报告则注明为中部标准时间凌晨3:30。

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省布兰登市以东约6英里处的1号省道（PTH #1）。

**目击经过：** 一名男性目击者在沿1号省道向西行驶时，通过后视镜和侧视镜观察到了一个物体。据目击者称，该物体当时正向东飞行，远离公路。目击者形容该物体“非常巨大”且“清晰可见”。据描述，该物体保持着爬升姿态，随后其北侧向上抬起，恢复水平飞行，缓慢变淡，最后突然消失。整个目击过程持续了约2分钟。目击者注意到当时公路上还有其他车辆，包括一辆半挂卡车，但他观察到其他驾驶员似乎并未注意到该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为亮白色，体积非常巨大。其结构被比作两个盘子，一个倒扣在另一个上面，顶部中心还有一个三角形物体。未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对该报告进行了调查，其中包括对目击者的访谈。负责访谈的警官指出，当事人对于自己的陈述表现得“相当诚恳”。作为后续调查的一部分，皇家骑警核查了目击者的背景，发现布兰登市警方对其并无记录，但他曾于1966年有过少年犯罪记录。

皇家骑警在周边地区进行了官方问询，但未收到其他目击报告。这使得调查人员产生质疑：如果该物体如描述般显眼，为何公路上其他向东行驶的车辆没有发现它。根据《行动手册》CO-Air第6段的规定，皇家骑警转发了一份电传信息。此外，调查人员还联系了布兰登市机场，核查了相关气象数据（记录显示当时天空阴云密布）及空中交通记录。该档案最终因未发现进一步的目击事件或新信息而结案。

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p025-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Maynard Rideout of Lower Woodstock, New Brunswick.

**Sighting:** On May 28, 1971, at 10:15 PM EDT, a UFO was reported near the Trans Canada Highway, 4 miles south of Woodstock, New Brunswick. The weather was clear.

**Object:** The witness observed three different spheres, each 50 to 100 feet in diameter, colored orange-yellow. The objects were stationary on the horizon for a period of over one hour.

**Aftermath:** Investigations conducted to date have failed to associate this observation with anything known in the Woodstock area. The object appeared in the Kilmarnock area.
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p025-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 新不伦瑞克省下伍德斯托克的梅纳德·赖道特 (Maynard Rideout)。

**日期：** 1971年5月28日，东部夏令时间晚上10:15。

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省伍德斯托克以南4英里处的横贯加拿大公路附近。

**目击经过：** 当时天气晴朗，目击者报告称在该区域发现了一个不明飞行物。

**物体描述：** 目击者观察到三个不同的球体，每个直径约为50至100英尺，呈橙黄色。这些物体在地平线上静止不动，持续时间超过一小时。

**调查/后续：** 迄今为止的调查未能将此次观测与伍德斯托克地区的任何已知事物联系起来。该物体曾出现在基尔马诺克 (Kilmarnock) 地区。

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p040-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two sons, a daughter, their mother, Melton, and two other unnamed individuals from the Saddle Lake Indian Reserve.

**Date / Time:** March 2, 1971, at approximately 10:15 P.M. MST.

**Location:** St. Paul / Saddle Lake, Alberta (near the Saddle Lake Indian Reserve).

**Sighting:** On the night of March 2, 1971, under a clear sky, a series of sightings occurred involving multiple witnesses. Melton, the primary witness, first spotted the object while outside and summoned two other individuals from the Saddle Lake Indian Reserve to observe it. Simultaneously, a mother and her three children (two sons and a daughter) observed the phenomenon. 

The object was observed for approximately three minutes in total. According to the accounts, the object remained stationary for about two minutes before proceeding in a westerly direction at a speed of approximately 15 mph. The witnesses noted that the craft maintained a low altitude, flying only 5 to 10 feet above the treetops. The mother reported a secondary visual effect, noting that blue and orange lights were reflecting into her bedroom, though she did not hear any noise. Conversely, the other witnesses reported hearing a distinct sound described as similar to a kitten’s purr, but significantly louder. All witnesses were adamant that the object was not a helicopter.

**Object:** The object was described as round or saucer-shaped. It featured three brilliant red and orange lights, with additional blue light reflections noted by one witness. The object moved at a slow speed of 15 mph at an altitude of 5–10 feet above the trees. It emitted a soft, purring sound, and the total duration of the observation was approximately three minutes.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The St. Paul RCMP detachment conducted lengthy interviews with all witnesses. The reporting officers concluded that the witnesses appeared sincere and that the sighting was not a figment of their imagination. The investigation noted that the location of the sighting is situated near the Saddle Lake Indian Reserve, in close proximity to several oil rigs, and directly within a known flight path for Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Cold Lake. Following the interviews, a telex message (STP 84) was dispatched to document the event.
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p040-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两个儿子、一个女儿、他们的母亲、梅尔顿（Melton），以及来自马鞍湖印第安保留地（Saddle Lake Indian Reserve）的其他两名未具名人士。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年3月2日，山区标准时间（MST）晚上10:15左右。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省圣保罗市 / 马鞍湖（靠近马鞍湖印第安保留地）。

**目击经过：** 1971年3月2日晚，在晴朗的天空下，发生了多名目击者参与的一系列目击事件。主要目击者梅尔顿在户外首次发现了该物体，并叫来马鞍湖印第安保留地的另外两人共同观察。与此同时，一位母亲和她的三个孩子（两个儿子和一个女儿）也观察到了这一现象。

该物体总共被观察了约三分钟。据描述，该物体先是静止悬停了约两分钟，随后以每小时约15英里的速度向西飞行。目击者指出，该飞行器保持着低空飞行，距离树梢仅5到10英尺。那位母亲报告了一种次要的视觉效应，称有蓝色和橙色的光反射进她的卧室，但她没有听到任何声音。相反，其他目击者报告称听到了一种独特的声音，描述为类似于小猫的呼噜声，但声音要大得多。所有目击者都坚称该物体绝非直升机。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形或碟形。它带有三盏明亮的红橙色灯光，其中一位目击者还注意到了额外的蓝色光反射。该物体以每小时15英里的慢速移动，高度位于树梢上方5至10英尺处。它发出柔和的呼噜声，整个观察过程持续了约三分钟。

**调查/后续：** 圣保罗皇家骑警（RCMP）分队对所有目击者进行了长时间的访谈。负责警官得出结论，认为目击者表现诚恳，此次目击事件并非凭空想象。调查指出，目击地点位于马鞍湖印第安保留地附近，靠近几处石油钻井平台，且正处于加拿大武装部队冷湖基地（CFB Cold Lake）的已知飞行航线上。访谈结束后，警方发送了一份电传信息（STP 84）以记录该事件。

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p046-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. [redacted], Mrs. [redacted], G.H. DONOVAN, E.C. WESLEY, and two additional individuals (names redacted).

**Date / Time:** February 23, 1971; sighting began at 8:30 P.M. CST and continued for 1.5 hours; RCMP received a call at 9:38 P.M.; additional observation noted at 10:37 P.M.

**Location:** 232 Deerwood Drive, Thompson, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On the evening of February 23, 1971, multiple witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the clear, cloudless skies over Thompson, Manitoba. The initial sighting began at 8:30 P.M. at 232 Deerwood Drive. Witnesses reported observing a single, solid object moving in a small circle while heading in a northerly direction. The object was observed for a duration of approximately 1.5 hours. 

At 9:38 P.M., the RCMP received a report from the residents at 232 Deerwood Drive. Upon the arrival of an RCMP patrol, the husband pointed out the object, which by that time had moved significantly further away, appearing as a distant star. A separate observation occurred at 10:37 P.M., where a witness initially hesitated to report the object but concluded it was not a star due to its movement and flashing nature. Cst. E.C. WESLEY and G.H. DONOVAN also observed the object, confirming it appeared as a star located in the north/northeast sky. Throughout the duration of the event, the object was seen slowly getting smaller as it appeared to move away from the Earth.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, solid, plate-shaped entity, estimated to be approximately the size of a full moon. It exhibited constant, rapid color changes, cycling through red, green, yellow, and blue. Witnesses noted a distinct red flash or flame emanating from the north side of the object. While the altitude remained unknown, the object’s movement was characterized by small circular patterns and a gradual recession into the distance. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Thompson City Detachment of the RCMP conducted an investigation, which included dispatching a patrol to 232 Deerwood Drive to obtain formal statements from the residents. Officers G.H. DONOVAN and E.C. WESLEY conducted their own visual verification of the object. Official records note that the sky was clear and cloudless during the event. The investigating officers explicitly documented that the witnesses appeared sober and showed no signs of intoxication at the time their statements were taken.
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p046-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]先生、[已删除]女士、G.H. 多诺万 (G.H. DONOVAN)、E.C. 韦斯利 (E.C. WESLEY) 以及另外两名人员（姓名已删除）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年2月23日；目击事件始于中部标准时间 (CST) 晚上8:30，持续了1.5小时；加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 于晚上9:38接到报警；晚上10:37有额外观测记录。

**地点：** 马尼托巴省汤普森市，鹿林大道 (Deerwood Drive) 232号。

**目击经过：** 1971年2月23日晚，多名目击者在马尼托巴省汤普森市晴朗无云的夜空中观察到一种不明空中现象。最初的目击事件始于晚上8:30，地点位于鹿林大道232号。目击者报告称，观察到一个单一的固体物体在向北移动的同时，进行着小范围的圆周运动。该物体的观测时长约为1.5小时。

晚上9:38，加拿大皇家骑警接到鹿林大道232号居民的报告。当骑警巡逻队抵达时，男主人指出了该物体，此时它已移动到相当远的地方，看起来像一颗遥远的恒星。晚上10:37发生了另一次观测，一名目击者起初对是否报告该物体感到犹豫，但最终断定它并非恒星，因为其具有移动和闪烁的特性。E.C. 韦斯利警员和 G.H. 多诺万也观察到了该物体，证实它看起来像位于北/东北方向天空中的一颗恒星。在整个事件过程中，该物体被观察到在缓慢变小，似乎正在远离地球。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的、固体的、盘状实体，估计大小约为满月。它表现出持续且快速的颜色变化，在红色、绿色、黄色和蓝色之间循环。目击者注意到从物体北侧发出明显的红色闪光或火焰。虽然高度未知，但该物体的运动特征为小圆周模式，并逐渐向远处退去。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警汤普森市分局进行了调查，包括派遣巡逻队前往鹿林大道232号获取居民的正式陈述。G.H. 多诺万警官和 E.C. 韦斯利警官进行了各自的目视核实。官方记录指出，事件发生时天空晴朗无云。调查警官明确记录道，在获取陈述时，目击者神志清醒，没有任何醉酒迹象。

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p051-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. [Redacted] (the observer and his wife)

**Date / Time:** February 17, 1971, at approximately 5:25 A.M. MST

**Location:** A residence along the Red Deer River, approximately 6 miles south of Wardlow, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On the morning of February 17, 1971, the witnesses observed an unidentified object while the sky was clear and the sun was beginning to rise. The object was positioned to the right of and above the sun, which had not yet crested the horizon. The witnesses observed the object for a duration of approximately 15 to 20 minutes. They viewed the object using both the naked eye and binoculars, noting that the object appeared clearer to the naked eye than through the binoculars. The object remained stationary throughout the duration of the sighting. After observing the object, the witnesses returned to bed; upon waking at 6:30 A.M., they noted that the object was no longer present.

**Object:** The object was described as large and round with a dull orange color. A distinct line was observed encircling the object; accounts vary slightly on the placement of this line, with one report placing it one-quarter of the way down from the top and another placing it three-quarters of the way down from the top. The object was estimated to be hovering approximately 400 feet above the ground. It exhibited no movement during the observation period and produced no reported sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) conducted an investigation into the report. The reporting officer documented that the witnesses were individuals of reputable character. During the investigation, it was noted that the lights at the witnesses' residence had been flickering or blinking on and off both prior to and following the incident. Despite the witnesses' testimony, the investigating officer and Sgt. Pinnock concluded that the object was likely a "sun dog" or a similar atmospheric phenomenon. No further physical evidence or alternative explanations were documented in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p051-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除] 夫妇（观察者及其妻子）

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年2月17日，大约凌晨5:25（山区标准时间）

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省沃德洛（Wardlow）以南约6英里处，红鹿河（Red Deer River）沿岸的一处住宅。

**目击经过：** 1971年2月17日清晨，在天空晴朗且太阳即将升起时，目击者观察到了一个不明物体。该物体位于尚未升出地平线的太阳的右上方。目击者观察该物体持续了约15至20分钟。他们分别用肉眼和双筒望远镜进行了观察，并注意到该物体用肉眼观察时比通过双筒望远镜观察时更为清晰。在整个目击过程中，该物体保持静止状态。观察结束后，目击者回到床上休息；当他们在早上6:30醒来时，发现该物体已消失不见。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的圆形物体，呈暗橙色。观察到有一条明显的线条环绕着该物体；关于这条线的位置，描述略有出入，一份报告称其位于顶部下方四分之一处，另一份报告则称其位于顶部下方四分之三处。据估计，该物体悬浮在离地面约400英尺的高度。在观察期间，它没有任何移动，也没有发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对该报告进行了调查。负责报告的警官记录称，目击者是信誉良好的人士。调查过程中还注意到，目击者住宅的灯光在事件发生前后曾出现闪烁或明灭不定的情况。尽管有目击者的证词，但负责调查的警官和皮诺克（Pinnock）警长仍得出结论，认为该物体很可能是一种“幻日”（sun dog）或类似的大气现象。所提供的档案中未记录任何进一步的物证或其他解释。

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p063-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. [Redacted], his wife, and his brother.

**Date / Time:** January 3, 1971, at 5:50 A.M. CST (Note: Page 72 contains a conflicting report citing March 1, 1971, at 5:00 A.M. CST).

**Location:** Resource, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On the morning of the sighting, the three witnesses were standing in their yard when they observed an unidentified object. The sky was clear and dark, with temperatures ranging between 5 and 10 degrees below zero. The witnesses observed the object to the east-south-east (or south-east) of their location. The object appeared to be positioned very low to the ground, though its exact distance was unknown; it was estimated to be several miles away. The witnesses monitored the object for approximately two hours.

**Object:** The object was described as being quite large. Its shape was initially reported as oblong, though it later appeared to change into a round shape. The object exhibited significant color changes, cycling through blue, red, and a very bright white. Once it reached the bright white state, it remained that color for the duration of the observation. The object appeared stationary throughout the two-hour sighting period. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to and filed by the Melfort Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). On January 4, 1971, the primary witness (Mr. [Redacted]) contacted the RCMP office again to provide an update. After observing that the object had not changed its position from the previous night, the witness concluded that the object was likely a star. The investigating RCMP members concurred with this assessment. The primary witness is noted in the file as being a reliable individual who is well-regarded within the community. 

*(Note: The discrepancy in dates between the two pages—January 3 vs. March 1—suggests either a clerical error in the filing of the report or conflicting documentation regarding the specific timeline of the event.)*
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p063-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]先生、他的妻子及其兄弟。

**日期 / 时间：** 1971年1月3日，中部标准时间（CST）凌晨5:50。（注：第72页包含一份相互矛盾的报告，称时间为1971年3月1日，中部标准时间凌晨5:00。）

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省，里索斯（Resource）。

**目击经过：** 目击当天清晨，三名目击者站在院子里时观察到了一个不明物体。当时天空晴朗且黑暗，气温在零下5到10度之间。目击者在他们所在位置的东南偏东（或东南）方向观察到了该物体。该物体看起来位置非常低，尽管无法确定其确切距离；据估计在几英里之外。目击者对该物体进行了约两个小时的观测。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体体积相当大。其形状最初被报告为长方形，但后来似乎变成了圆形。该物体呈现出显著的颜色变化，在蓝色、红色和非常明亮的白色之间循环。一旦达到明亮的白色状态，它在观测期间就一直保持该颜色。在两小时的目击过程中，该物体看起来是静止不动的。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已报告给加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）梅尔福特分遣队并存档。1971年1月4日，主要目击者（[已删除]先生）再次联系了皇家骑警办公室提供更新信息。在观察到该物体自前一天晚上以来位置没有改变后，目击者得出结论，认为该物体很可能是一颗恒星。负责调查的皇家骑警成员同意这一评估。档案中指出，该主要目击者是一位可靠的人，在社区中享有良好声誉。

*（注：两页报告之间日期上的差异——1月3日与3月1日——表明这可能是归档时的笔误，或者是关于事件具体时间线的记录存在冲突。）*

CA-FOIA-Part_28-p259-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two juvenile subjects (residing at a farm in the R.M. of St. Andrews/Parish of St. Clement)

**Date / Time:** July 31, 1972, at approximately 12:10 A.M.

**Location:** A farm in the R.M. of St. Andrews / Parish of St. Clement, approximately 1.5 miles west of the town of Selkirk, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** At approximately 12:10 A.M. on July 31, 1972, two juvenile witnesses residing at a farm near Selkirk were sleeping in a bunk house when they were awakened by a low-toned, throbbing noise. Upon exiting the bunk house and standing in their yard, they observed a bright, multi-coloured object in the sky. The witnesses reported that the sky directly above their residence was clear, despite thunderstorms occurring approximately 15 miles to the south. The witnesses observed the object moving in a southerly direction, performing a sharp, distinct zig-zagged flight pattern. The object then came to a complete stop for approximately 4–5 seconds before executing a 90-degree turn and proceeding in a westerly direction until it disappeared from sight. Both witnesses explicitly stated that the object was not a helicopter or a jet aircraft, noting their familiarity with the sounds and appearances of such conventional aircraft.

**Object:** The object was described as appearing like a bright star and was multi-coloured. Its altitude could not be determined by the witnesses. It was accompanied by a distinct, low-toned, throbbing sound. Its movement was characterized by sharp, zig-zagging patterns, a 4–5 second hover, and a sudden 90-degree directional change.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP Selkirk Rural Detachment conducted an investigation into the report. The reporting officers noted that the area is situated within a flight lane for commercial aircraft, leading some officials to suggest the object may have been a low-flying aircraft. However, the witnesses remained firm in their assessment that the object was not a conventional aircraft. The RCMP expressed skepticism regarding the validity of the report, noting that the witnesses appeared visibly shaken but describing their accounts as "vague" and questioning their overall reliability. The RCMP further noted that no other individuals within the district of 20,000 people reported a similar sighting. A copy of the official report was forwarded to the Meteor Centre on August 21, 1972, and additional copies were transmitted to RCMP Headquarters in Ottawa.
CA-FOIA-Part_28-p259-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 两名未成年人（居住于圣安德鲁斯农村自治市/圣克莱门特教区的一处农场）

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年7月31日，凌晨约12:10

**地点：** 曼尼托巴省塞尔柯克镇以西约1.5英里处，圣安德鲁斯农村自治市/圣克莱门特教区的一处农场。

**目击经过：** 1972年7月31日凌晨约12:10，两名居住在塞尔柯克附近农场的未成年目击者正在宿舍内睡觉，被一阵低沉的搏动声惊醒。他们走出宿舍站在院子里，观察到天空中出现了一个明亮且色彩斑斓的物体。据目击者称，尽管当时在南方约15英里处有雷暴，但他们住所正上方的天空却十分晴朗。目击者看到该物体向南移动，并呈现出一种急促、明显的“之”字形飞行轨迹。随后，该物体完全静止了约4至5秒，接着进行了90度转弯，并向西飞行，直至消失在视野中。两位目击者明确表示，该物体绝非直升机或喷气式飞机，并指出他们非常熟悉此类常规飞行器的声音和外观。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为看起来像一颗明亮的星星，且颜色多样。目击者无法确定其飞行高度。物体伴随着一种独特的、低沉的搏动声。其运动特征表现为急促的“之”字形飞行、4至5秒的悬停，以及突然的90度转向。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）塞尔柯克农村分队对此报告进行了调查。负责警官指出，该区域位于商业航班的航线上，因此一些官员认为该物体可能是一架低空飞行的飞机。然而，目击者坚持认为该物体并非常规飞行器。加拿大皇家骑警对该报告的真实性表示怀疑，指出目击者看起来明显受到惊吓，但形容他们的陈述“模糊不清”，并对他们的整体可靠性提出质疑。警方还指出，该地区两万名居民中没有其他人报告过类似的目击事件。官方报告的副本于1972年8月21日被转交至流星中心（Meteor Centre），其他副本也被发送至位于渥太华的加拿大皇家骑警总部。

CA-FOIA-Part_29-p001-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], Mr. [redacted], Mrs. [redacted]

**Date / Time:** May 1, 1972, at 12:15 A.M. ADST; May 2, 1972, from 12:40 A.M. to 1:00 A.M. ADST

**Location:** Maple Ridge, New Brunswick

**Sighting:** On May 1, 1972, at approximately 12:15 A.M. ADST, a group of witnesses—consisting of Mrs. [redacted], her husband Mr. [redacted], and Mr. and Mrs. [redacted]—observed an unidentified object in the northwest sky. The object remained visible for approximately 20 minutes before disappearing over the horizon. The night was noted as being clear with the moon shining in the eastern sky. A second sighting of an identical object occurred at the same location the following night, May 2, 1972, between 12:40 A.M. and 1:00 A.M. ADST.

**Object:** The object was described as being quite large and distinctively shaped like a cross. It featured a blinking red light. Regarding its movement, accounts vary slightly: one report notes the object moved vertically before disappearing, while another report states it moved continuously but did not move vertically. The object was observed at a high altitude, though the exact height could not be determined. It made no apparent sound during the sightings.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was investigated by the Fredericton Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). The RCMP initiated contact with the witnesses after a report regarding the event appeared in *The Daily Gleaner*. Following their interviews, the RCMP concluded that the witnesses were reliable. On May 4, 1972, a radio-gram detailing the event was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Centre. No further official action was taken by the authorities.
CA-FOIA-Part_29-p001-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** [已删除]女士、[已删除]先生、[已删除]先生、[已删除]女士

**日期 / 时间：** 1972年5月1日，大西洋夏令时间（ADST）凌晨12:15；1972年5月2日，大西洋夏令时间（ADST）凌晨12:40至1:00

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省，枫树岭（Maple Ridge）

**目击经过：** 1972年5月1日凌晨12:15左右，一组目击者（包括[已删除]女士、其丈夫[已删除]先生，以及[已删除]夫妇）在西北方向的天空中观察到一个不明物体。该物体持续可见约20分钟，随后消失在地平线以下。当晚天气晴朗，月亮悬挂在东方天空。次日，即1972年5月2日凌晨12:40至1:00之间，同一地点再次出现了同样的物体。

**物体描述：** 据描述，该物体体积相当大，形状呈独特的十字形，并带有闪烁的红灯。关于其运动方式，各方描述略有出入：一份报告称该物体在消失前曾垂直移动，而另一份报告则称其一直在持续移动，但并未进行垂直运动。该物体被观察到处于高空，但无法确定具体高度。在目击过程中，该物体未发出任何明显声响。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）弗雷德里克顿分局对此次目击事件进行了调查。在《每日拾穗者报》（The Daily Gleaner）刊登了相关报道后，加拿大皇家骑警主动联系了目击者。经过访谈，警方认为目击者证词可靠。1972年5月4日，一份详细记录该事件的无线电报被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心。此后，当局未再采取进一步的官方行动。

CA-FOIA-Part_29-p064-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A sentry at the Armouries, an unnamed officer, soldiers guarding power plants, and Superintendent Alex Collins of the city waterworks.

**Date / Time:** January 27th–29th, 1915, and February 4th, 1915; sightings occurred between 11:00 P.M. and 1:00 A.M., with one specific observation at 10:30 P.M. on February 4th.

**Location:** Along the Niagara River, specifically including the area over Victoria Park.

**Sighting:** During the period of January 27th to 29th, and again on February 4th, 1915, multiple reports were filed regarding an aeroplane flying at a low altitude along the Niagara River. The sightings consistently occurred late at night, primarily between 11:00 P.M. and 1:00 A.M. A sentry stationed at the Armouries reported hearing a distinct engine hum and observing a "grey shadow" moving through the night sky. These auditory reports of engine noise were corroborated by soldiers stationed at the local power plants, who also reported hearing the sound of engines during the same timeframe. On the night of February 4th, at approximately 10:30 P.M., Superintendent Alex Collins of the city waterworks observed a distant aeroplane flying over Victoria Park. Unlike the earlier reports, Collins noted that the aircraft was operating without any lights.

**Object:** The object was identified by witnesses as an aeroplane. Its physical appearance varied across the reported sightings: it was described as a "grey shadow" in some instances, while in others, it was noted to carry green and red navigation lights. During the February 4th sighting by Superintendent Collins, the object was observed to have no lights at all. The movement was described as low-altitude flight along the river, accompanied by a consistent engine hum.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The reports were treated with significant gravity by local authorities due to the sensitive nature of the power plants and the proximity to the international border. Official follow-up involved a coordinated effort between law enforcement agencies on both the Canadian and American sides of the border. These agencies were requested to assist in a formal investigation to identify the owner, origin, and purpose of the mysterious aircraft, though no definitive identification was recorded in the provided files.
CA-FOIA-Part_29-p064-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 军械库的一名哨兵、一名未具名的军官、负责守卫发电厂的士兵，以及城市水厂的负责人亚历克斯·柯林斯（Alex Collins）警司。

**日期 / 时间：** 1915年1月27日至29日，以及1915年2月4日；目击事件发生在晚上11:00至凌晨1:00之间，其中一次具体观测发生在2月4日晚上10:30。

**地点：** 尼亚加拉河沿岸，特别包括维多利亚公园上空区域。

**目击经过：** 在1915年1月27日至29日期间，以及2月4日，多份报告称有一架飞机在尼亚加拉河沿岸低空飞行。目击事件均发生在深夜，主要集中在晚上11:00至凌晨1:00之间。驻守在军械库的一名哨兵报告称，听到明显的引擎轰鸣声，并观察到一个“灰色阴影”在夜空中移动。这些关于引擎噪音的听觉报告得到了当地发电厂驻守士兵的证实，他们也在同一时间段听到了引擎声。2月4日晚约10:30，城市水厂负责人亚历克斯·柯林斯警司观察到一架远处的飞机飞越维多利亚公园。与之前的报告不同，柯林斯指出该飞行器在飞行时没有任何灯光。

**物体描述：** 目击者将该物体识别为飞机。其外观在各次目击报告中有所不同：有时被描述为“灰色阴影”，有时则被注意到带有绿色和红色的航行灯。在柯林斯警司2月4日的目击中，观察到该物体完全没有灯光。其飞行方式被描述为沿河流低空飞行，并伴有持续的引擎轰鸣声。

**调查/后续：** 由于发电厂的敏感性以及靠近国际边界，当地当局对这些报告给予了高度重视。官方的后续行动涉及加拿大和美国边境两侧执法机构的协调配合。这些机构被要求协助进行正式调查，以确定这架神秘飞行器的所有者、来源和目的，但在提供的档案中并未记录到任何明确的鉴定结果。

CA-FOIA-Part_29-p066-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mayor of Gananoque, Mayor Donaldson, Sir Robert Borden, Burke, Chief of the General Staff of the Militia, Sherwood, Constable Storey.

**Date / Time:** September 4, 1914; 11:15 P.M. (blackout initiation).

**Location:** Gananoque, Ottawa, and Brockville, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the night of September 4, 1914, a series of reports regarding "mysterious aeroplanes" triggered a significant security response across Eastern Ontario. The incident began when the Mayor of Gananoque contacted an individual named Burke to report that two unseen aeroplanes had been heard passing over the town. Recognizing the potential threat, Mayor Donaldson of Gananoque telephoned Prime Minister Sir Robert Borden to warn him that the aircraft were heading toward the nation's capital, Ottawa.

Upon receiving this intelligence, Sir Robert Borden immediately notified the Chief of the General Staff of the Militia and recommended that Sherwood be informed of the situation. Fearing that the illumination of the capital would serve as a beacon for the approaching aircraft, Sherwood ordered a city-wide blackout. At 11:15 P.M., the lights of Parliament Hill, the Royal Mint, and Rideau Hall were extinguished, followed by the rest of Ottawa’s city lights five minutes later. This event marked the first blackout of any Canadian city. Soldiers were deployed to rooftops throughout Ottawa with explicit orders to shoot down any aeroplanes that came into sight; however, despite the heightened alert, no aircraft were ever spotted.

**Object:** The objects were initially reported as two mysterious, unseen aeroplanes, identified primarily by the sound of their passage over Gananoque. Following the investigation, the objects were identified as paper balloons equipped with firecrackers and flares.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The investigation into the incident concluded that the "aeroplanes" were actually hot air balloons launched by American pranksters. The physical evidence was recovered by Constable Storey of the Brockville Police Department, who discovered the remains of one paper balloon near the Eastern Hospital. A second balloon was subsequently located east of the city. The incident, which caused widespread alarm and prompted newspaper headlines regarding a potential invasion, was ultimately dismissed as a hoax involving the firecracker-laden balloons.
CA-FOIA-Part_29-p066-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 加纳诺克市长、唐纳森市长 (Mayor Donaldson)、罗伯特·博登爵士 (Sir Robert Borden)、伯克 (Burke)、民兵总参谋长、舍伍德 (Sherwood)、斯托里警官 (Constable Storey)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1914年9月4日；晚上11:15（开始灯火管制）。

**地点：** 安大略省加纳诺克、渥太华及布罗克维尔。

**目击经过：** 1914年9月4日晚，一系列关于“神秘飞机”的报告在安大略省东部引发了重大的安全响应。事件始于加纳诺克市长联系了一位名叫伯克的市民，报告称听到两架看不见的飞机飞越该镇上空。意识到潜在威胁，加纳诺克市长唐纳森致电总理罗伯特·博登爵士，警告他这些飞行器正朝国家首都渥太华方向飞去。

收到情报后，罗伯特·博登爵士立即通知了民兵总参谋长，并建议将情况告知舍伍德。由于担心首都的灯光会成为来袭飞行器的指引目标，舍伍德下令在全市范围内实施灯火管制。晚上11:15，国会山、皇家铸币厂和里多厅的灯光被熄灭，五分钟后，渥太华其余地区的灯光也全部熄灭。这是加拿大城市首次实施灯火管制。士兵们被部署到渥太华各处的屋顶上，并接到明确命令：击落任何进入视野的飞机。然而，尽管处于高度戒备状态，却始终未发现任何飞行器。

**物体描述：** 这些物体最初被报告为两架神秘的、未被目击的飞机，主要通过它们飞越加纳诺克上空的声音来辨识。调查后确认，这些物体是装有鞭炮和照明弹的纸质气球。

**调查/后续：** 对该事件的调查结论显示，所谓的“飞机”实际上是由美国恶作剧者放飞的热气球。布罗克维尔警察局的斯托里警官发现了物证，他在东部医院附近找到了一个纸质气球的残骸。随后，第二个气球在城市东部被发现。这一事件在当时引起了广泛恐慌，并登上了关于“潜在入侵”的报纸头条，但最终被定性为一场涉及装有鞭炮气球的恶作剧。

CA-FOIA-Part_29-p067-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The page describes a report from a farmer named Cognac who said he heard an aeroplane near Sabrevois, Quebec, on March 27th. It also mentions that the story was repeated to Major Hector Bissonette and then communicated to the Military Secretary in Ottawa. A storekeeper in town apparently prompted Cognac to mention the incident, and F.G. Robinson of the Montreal office later reported on the matter.

**Sighting:** The text also refers to an aeroplane flying toward the Canadian border at an altitude between 2,500 and 3,000 feet. It is described as approaching from Lake Erie, passing over Buffalo, and then veering away before crossing to Fort Erie on the Canadian shore. Officials treated these reports as serious enough to send investigators to Sabrevois.

**Object:** The object is consistently described as an "aeroplane." The page does not give a detailed physical description beyond its flight path and altitude. Robinson reported that Major Bissonette was "extremely nervous" and feared German spies and secret bases of arms along the Quebec border. By contrast, Cognac was said to be "fairly intelligent" and later regretted having started trouble with his story.

**Aftermath:** Operatives of the Thiel Detective Service, assisting the Secret Service of the Dominion Police, were sent to investigate the reports. Robinson’s postscript says arrangements were made to prevent newspaper publicity about the rumour and to prevent despatches being sent.
CA-FOIA-Part_29-p067-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 该报告记录了一位名叫科尼亚克（Cognac）的农民的陈述，他称3月27日在魁北克省萨布雷瓦（Sabrevois）附近听到了飞机的声音。报告还提到，该事件被转述给了赫克托·比索内特（Hector Bissonette）少校，随后又传达给了渥太华的军事秘书。据称是镇上的一名店主促使科尼亚克提起了此事，蒙特利尔办事处的F.G.罗宾逊（F.G. Robinson）随后对此事进行了汇报。

**目击经过：** 文中提到一架飞机正以2,500至3,000英尺的高度飞向加拿大边境。据描述，该飞机从伊利湖方向驶来，飞越布法罗上空，随后在抵达加拿大岸边的伊利堡之前转向离开。官员们认为这些报告事态严重，因此派遣了调查人员前往萨布雷瓦。

**物体描述：** 该物体始终被描述为“飞机”。除飞行路线和高度外，文中未提供详细的物理特征描述。罗宾逊报告称，比索内特少校当时“极其紧张”，担心魁北克边境存在德国间谍和秘密武器基地。相比之下，科尼亚克被认为“相当理智”，后来对自己因讲述此事而引发麻烦感到后悔。

**调查/后续：** 蒂尔侦探社（Thiel Detective Service）的特工在协助自治领警察局（Dominion Police）特勤处调查这些报告。罗宾逊的附言中提到，当局已做出安排，以防止有关该传闻的报纸报道及相关电报的发送。

CA-FOIA-Part_29-p070-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The officer commanding the 21st Regiment of the First Division.

**Date / Time:** July 2, 1915; early morning.

**Location:** Windsor, Ontario.

**Sighting:** The officer commanding the 21st Regiment of the First Division reported the presence of an unidentified aerial craft, described as an "alien aeroplane," hovering in the vicinity of Windsor during the early morning hours of July 2, 1915. The sighting prompted immediate military concern regarding the nature and origin of the craft, leading the officer to initiate formal communication with higher command to address the potential security threat posed by the object's presence over the region.

**Object:** The object was identified by the witness as an "alien aeroplane." No further specific details regarding its size, color, sound, or specific flight maneuvers were documented in the provided records, other than the observation that it was "hovering." The duration of the sighting is noted only as occurring in the early morning.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the sighting, the officer commanding the 21st Regiment of the First Division dispatched an urgent telegram to the Military Secretary. In this communication, the officer formally requested that an "armoured aeroplane" be deployed from Toronto to Windsor to investigate or intercept the craft. The case file notes that, despite the urgency of the request and the official nature of the report, there is no evidence that any action was taken by the military authorities in response to the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Part_29-p070-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 第一师第21团指挥官。

**日期 / 时间：** 1915年7月2日；清晨。

**地点：** 安大略省温莎市。

**目击经过：** 第一师第21团指挥官报告称，1915年7月2日清晨，在温莎附近区域发现了一架不明飞行器，被描述为“外来飞机”（alien aeroplane）。此次目击事件引起了军方对该飞行器性质及来源的高度关注，促使该指挥官立即与上级指挥部进行正式沟通，以应对该物体出现在该地区所构成的潜在安全威胁。

**物体描述：** 目击者将该物体称为“外来飞机”。除观察到其处于“悬停”状态外，现有记录中未记载关于其尺寸、颜色、声音或具体飞行机动的详细信息。目击持续时间仅注明发生在清晨。

**调查 / 后续：** 目击事件发生后，第一师第21团指挥官向军事秘书发送了一封紧急电报。在电文中，该指挥官正式请求从多伦多调派一架“装甲飞机”前往温莎，以调查或拦截该飞行器。案卷记录显示，尽管请求十分紧急且报告性质正式，但并无证据表明军方当局针对此次目击事件采取了任何行动。

dow-65sec3-p0169-logan-followup-1947-09-.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from the SAC, Salt Lake City, to the Director, FBI, dated September 15, 1947, subject "Flying Discs," in Section 3 of case file 62-HQ-83894. The report is a field summary of local interviews and newspaper references; it carries office initials (SMK:LMS) and closes with the conclusion that no further investigation would be conducted. The two substantive rendered pages are parts of the same report, with page 0171 continuing the narrative from page 0169.

**Witnesses:** The principal named observers were Mr. and Mrs. Richard Anderson of Logan, who were interviewed by an FBI agent. The memo also references Mr. and Mrs. Gaylon Caldwell, Mr. and Mrs. Fred Thunell, Mr. and Mrs. Norman Hall, Keith Hughes, Joan Crookston, and others. Some names appeared in a newspaper account but later denied observing the objects because they had not had the opportunity; this suggests the local press report was at least partly inaccurate.

**Sighting:** The sightings occurred in Logan, Utah, on the evening of September 8, 1947, mainly between about 10:30 and 11:10 p.m. One account said approximately a dozen objects moved in group formation at 2,000-3,000 feet, were small like pigeons, white and illuminated, showed no wing movement, and disappeared to the north after circling the city for about 1-2 minutes. Another account described five groups of 35-60 small yellowish-white objects circling at high speed. A separate account said the objects traveled clockwise and looked like a group of moving stars.

**Investigation:** The memo treats the event as a composite of local reports rather than a single verified track. The varied descriptions, uncertainty about size and nature, and the possibility that some witnesses could have been seeing birds or lights are noted in the text. The final determination was that the information remained indefinite, and the Salt Lake City office ended active inquiry while informing military intelligence at Fort Douglas of the results.
dow-65sec3-p0169-logan-followup-1947-09-.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 来自犹他州盐湖城（Salt Lake City）负责人（SAC）致 FBI 局长的 FBI 办公备忘录，日期为 1947年9月15日，主题为“Flying Discs”，载于案卷 62-HQ-83894 第3部分。该报告是对当地访谈和报纸记载的现场汇总；文件上带有办公室缩写（SMK:LMS），并以“不再进行进一步调查”的结论结束。所展示的两页正文为同一报告的组成部分，其中第 0171 页承接第 0169 页的叙述。

**Witnesses:** 主要点名的目击者是来自 Logan 的 Richard Anderson 先生和夫人，他们接受了一名 FBI 特工的询问。备忘录还提到 Gaylon Caldwell 先生和夫人、Fred Thunell 先生和夫人、Norman Hall 先生、Keith Hughes、Joan Crookston 等人。部分姓名曾出现在报纸报道中，但后来否认曾看到这些物体，因为他们并没有机会目睹；这表明当地媒体报道至少有一部分不准确。

**Sighting:** 这些目击事件发生在 Utah 州 Logan，时间为 1947年9月8日晚，主要在晚上约 10:30 至 11:10 之间。一则说法称，大约十几件物体以编队方式移动，飞行高度为 2,000-3,000 英尺，体型像鸽子一样小，呈白色并发光，没有翅膀摆动迹象，在绕城约 1-2 分钟后向北消失。另一则说法描述有五组 35-60 个小型黄白色物体高速盘旋。另一个说法称这些物体按顺时针方向移动，看上去像一群移动的星星。

**Investigation:** 该备忘录将这一事件视为当地多份报告的综合，而非单一、经证实的轨迹。文中提到，各种描述彼此不同，对物体大小和性质也存在不确定性，而且有些目击者也可能看到的是鸟或灯光。最终认定信息仍然不明确，Salt Lake City 办公室在将结果告知 Fort Douglas 的军事情报部门后，结束了主动调查。

dow-65sec2-p0152-logan-teletype-1947-09-.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Salt Lake City teletype to the Director, marked "URGENT" and sent through the Communication Section on 10 Sep 1947 at 9:55 AM MST. The page is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, and states that the Bureau would be advised after a local inquiry. The text is a secondhand summary drawn from a Salt Lake Tribune item, not a signed witness statement.

**Witness:** The report says that eight different people in Logan, Utah, reported the incident. No names, occupations, or addresses are given on this page, so the witnesses cannot be individually identified from the document.

**Sighting:** According to the teletype, the Logan witnesses said they saw "three different flights of flying discs" between 10:40 and 11:10 PM on Monday, 8 Sep 1947. The page does not describe shape, color, size, altitude, direction, speed, sound, or duration beyond the reference to multiple flights.

**Object:** The objects are only identified as "flying discs," reflecting the 1947 terminology. No physical evidence, photographs, or technical data are mentioned here.

**Investigation:** FBI Salt Lake City notes that an investigation was already being conducted and that headquarters would be informed. Because this page only relays a press report, its evidentiary value is limited; however, it does preserve an early contemporaneous lead involving multiple alleged observers at Logan, Utah, on the night of 8 Sep 1947.
dow-65sec2-p0152-logan-teletype-1947-09-.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Salt Lake City发给Director的电传，标注“URGENT”，并于1947年9月10日上午9:55 MST通过Communication Section发送。该页属于FBI档案62-HQ-83894，第2部分，并说明在完成当地调查后将向Bureau通报。正文内容是根据《Salt Lake Tribune》的一则报道整理出的二手摘要，并非经过签字的证人陈述。

**Witness:** 报告称，犹他州Logan有八名不同的人报告了这一事件。此页未提供姓名、职业或地址，因此无法仅凭该文件逐一识别这些证人。

**Sighting:** 根据这份电传，Logan的目击者称，他们在1947年9月8日星期一晚上10:40至11:10之间看到了“three different flights of flying discs”。该页除提及多次飞行外，并未描述其形状、颜色、大小、高度、方向、速度、声音或持续时间。

**Object:** 这些物体仅被称为“flying discs”，反映了1947年的术语用法。此处未提及任何物证、照片或技术数据。

**Investigation:** FBI Salt Lake City注明，相关调查已经在进行中，且总部将被告知。由于这一页只是转述一则新闻报道，其证据价值有限；不过，它确实保留了一条早期的同时期资料线索，涉及1947年9月8日晚在犹他州Logan有多名据称目击者的事件。

dow-65serial130-p0109-boise-stevens-1947.report_summary:
**Witness:** Ralph Stevens, co-pilot of a DC-3 aircraft, interviewed at 2130 hours on 9 July 1947. Stevens corroborated statements made by pilot Smith regarding a UFO sighting.

**Sighting:** On 4 July 1947, eight minutes after departing from Boise, Idaho, Stevens spotted the first object at 2012 hours. While flying at approximately 8,000 feet altitude, he thought it was an oncoming aircraft similar to their DC-3 about five miles away. He turned on landing lights to signal the other plane, then mentioned this to Smith. Both pilots watched as four more objects appeared at the same altitude as the first.

**Objects:** The objects seemed to be at the same altitude as their plane, about 6,000 feet, heading about 290 degrees magnetic North. Stevens turned to follow them and watched for four or five minutes as all five objects merged as one and disappeared. He could not determine whether they merged in line of flight, went beyond vision range, or dissipated. Two minutes later, the large object reappeared with three smaller ones on its left and one smaller one at a great distance to the right. This second group remained in sight for about twelve minutes in that formation before disappearing into the sunset. When last seen, the objects appeared to have continued climbing after the plane leveled off at nine or ten thousand feet.

**Conditions:** Weather was clear and unlimited with no clouds. Wind was 230-10 (out of Southwest at 10 mph). Air speed approximately 135 MPH. Sun was below the horizon; objects were silhouetted against the sky with no distinguishable color or reflection. A bright red glow from the sunset was visible above the horizon.

**Additional Details:** Stevens stated there was a big difference in size between the large objects and smaller ones, and it was hard to distinguish their shape. He confirmed the objects were at the same altitude as their climbing plane. The crew radioed ahead to Ontario, Oregon weather station (about thirty miles distant) asking them to look outside and observe. The weather station radioed back confirming they could see the objects.
dow-65serial130-p0109-boise-stevens-1947.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** Ralph Stevens,一架DC-3飞机的副驾驶员,于1947年7月9日2130时接受访谈。Stevens证实了飞行员Smith关于UFO目击事件的陈述。

**Sighting:** 1947年7月4日,从爱达荷州博伊西(Boise, Idaho)起飞八分钟后,Stevens于2012时发现了第一个物体。当时飞行高度约为8,000英尺,他认为那是一架迎面而来的飞机,类似于他们的DC-3,距离约五英里。他打开着陆灯向另一架飞机发出信号,然后向Smith提及此事。两名飞行员一起观察时,又有四个物体出现在与第一个物体相同的高度上。

**Objects:** 这些物体似乎与他们的飞机处于同一高度,约6,000英尺,航向约为磁北290度。Stevens转向跟随它们,观察了四到五分钟,看到所有五个物体合并为一个并消失了。他无法确定它们是在飞行路线上合并、超出视野范围,还是消散了。两分钟后,那个大型物体重新出现,左侧有三个较小的物体,右侧远处有一个较小的物体。第二组物体保持该编队约十二分钟后消失在日落中。最后看到时,在飞机于九千或一万英尺高度平飞后,这些物体似乎继续爬升。

**Conditions:** 天气晴朗,能见度无限制,无云。风向风速为230-10(西南风,时速10英里)。空速约135英里/小时。太阳位于地平线以下;物体在天空中呈剪影状,无法辨别颜色或反光。地平线上方可见日落产生的明亮红色光芒。

**Additional Details:** Stevens表示大型物体与小型物体之间的尺寸差异很大,很难辨别它们的形状。他确认这些物体与他们正在爬升的飞机处于同一高度。机组人员通过无线电向前方约三十英里处的俄勒冈州安大略(Ontario, Oregon)气象站呼叫,要求他们到外面观察。气象站回复无线电确认他们能看到这些物体。
